sections.text: Defects, no need for sharp edges at corners to avoid stress concentration.
(4) Assembly

items: Hydraulic pump assembly shall follow assembly process specifications. Assembly shall not be affected by dust and other debris on the assembly surface. Special attention shall be paid to the sealing surface of the pump. The zero parts (including pumps, external coordination) on the assembly shall meet the quality requirements.

The heavy-duty fixed combined surface shall be tightly bonded. The pre-tightening force shall be used after the surface is cleaned. The allowable clearance shall not exceed 0.05 mm. The clearance measurement shall be performed, and the allowable clearance shall not exceed 1/4 of the contact surface width. The allowable clearance shall not exceed 1/10 of the circumference. The important fixed bonded surface shall be: ① The contact surface between the pump body and the shaft. The liquid pressure oil bonded surface below the lower guide surface of the pump. ③ The bushing surface and the moving ring turning head through the disk fixed bonded surface. ④ The pressure oil permanent tight state, the return pressure oil through the fixed bonded surface and the return pressure oil in the fixed bonded surface. ⑤ The moving work platform horizontal and lower bonded pressure oil platform fixed bonded surface, etc.

The pressure and moving work platform moving position difference should meet the design requirements. The pressure head return rotation work platform return rotation angle difference should meet the design requirements.
All oil passages, pipe joints, methods and other fixed and moving connection sealing parts, should be connected firmly, the seal should be good, should not have oil leakage phenomena.
The empty running time shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5.14.2 regulations. During the empty running time, the internal temperature (or the liquid inlet temperature) shall not exceed 60°C.
The hydraulic pump noise shall comply with GB 26484 regulations.
Electrical equipment shall comply with GB 5226.1 regulations.
The liquid pressure device quality shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 4.5 regulations.
The appearance shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 4.14 regulations.

The liquid pressure, lubrication, and cooling system work shall be recorded in the installation manual. Before installation, the hydraulic system shall be cleaned according to JB/T 9954—1999 Section 3.2.2 regulations. The method shall follow JB/T 9954—1999 Appendix A regulations.

sections.text: 3. Inspection Rules
(1) Inspection Conditions
The product shall be in a fully assembled state (except for oil seal coating) and can only undergo performance inspection after inspection.
(2) Inspection Method
The inspection method shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5 regulations.
4. Test Method
(1) General Regulations
The test method shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5.1 regulations.
(2) Performance Test
The performance test shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5.13 regulations.
(3) No-load Operation Test
The no-load operation test shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5.14, 3 regulations and the following regulations:

items: Check the power supply, start the motor, make the pump run at no-load. Check the motor current, motor oil pump starting characteristics and whether there is abnormal vibration and noise.
Observe each combination, make the pump work in the correct direction.
The no-load operation time shall not be less than 4h. The moving return rotation head shall be completed within the process. The lower operation shall not be less than 2h.
During operation, check whether the electrical and pressure system work is normal. Each seal shall not leak oil.
The pressure and work platform shall not have jamming, crawling and jumping phenomena.

The moving return pressure head and moving work platform moving position difference should meet the design requirements. Check the moving return pressure head and return work platform return rotation angle difference should meet the design requirements.

sections.text: (4) Load Operation Test

During the load operation test, the pressure head shall be in the left and right limit positions and the center position for load operation test. The load operation test shall comply with JB/T 3818—2014 Section 5.5 regulations and the following regulations:

items: Use liquid flow adjustment to adjust the liquid flow to 8MPa, 15MPa, 20MPa, 25MPa rated pressure. At each pressure level, continue 3a and repeat 3 times. The pressure recovery should not exceed ±1MPa.
At 25MPa load condition, conduct a working cycle test. Check whether the signal element is normal. The liquid and electrical system is not leaking.
During load operation, each liquid element, pipe and other dense parts shall not have oil leakage phenomena. The oil leakage shall not exceed the specified value.
During load operation, the moving position shall not have jamming, crawling and jumping phenomena.

During load operation, check the moving return pressure head and moving work platform moving position difference should meet the design requirements. Check the moving return pressure head and return work platform return rotation angle difference should meet the design requirements.
During load operation, the motor electrical current should comply with the regulations.
The hydraulic pump noise shall comply with GB 26484 regulations. After the above inspection is completed, continue the load operation test for 3.5h.

Hydraulic Cylinder Manual
Edited by Tang Yingda
Machinery Industry Press

This manual not only comprehensively and systematically introduces the common standards, formulas and data for hydraulic cylinder design, but also, based on the summary of relevant standards and the author's practical experience, provides technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their components, taboos for the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders, test methods for hydraulic cylinders, and a large number of product drawings of hydraulic cylinders that have been tested on actual machines (or empirical tests). Furthermore, through research and engineering tests (including some verification and re-inspection), it screens out new technologies for the design and (re)manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders with practical value or engineering application prospects.
This manual has the characteristics of novel content, large amount of information, wide range of sources, complete specifications, strong practicability, reliable data, and convenient use.

This manual can be used by personnel engaged in the selection, design, process, processing, assembly, testing, acceptance, on-site maintenance and upkeep, remanufacturing, and product marketing of hydraulic cylinders, hydraulic machinery, equipment, or devices, and can also be used as a reference by teachers and students of related majors in colleges and universities.

Foreword

In hydraulic transmission systems, power is transmitted and controlled through pressurized fluid circulating in a closed circuit. The hydraulic cylinder is one of the components in such systems, serving as a device that converts hydraulic power into linear mechanical force and motion. The hydraulic cylinder consists of several moving parts and assemblies, including a piston rod running within the cylinder barrel, or a piston rod and piston integrated coaxially and in parallel.

Among hydraulic transmission systems and components, aside from tanks and piping, the technical design that engineering technicians are most likely to encounter is the hydraulic cylinder. Although the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders are relatively simple and easy compared to other hydraulic components or devices, it is actually quite difficult to truly design and manufacture a good hydraulic cylinder. This is because its working conditions are more difficult to determine than those of hydraulic valves or pumps, and it may also be affected by unexpected factors. Moreover, hydraulic cylinders are often produced as single units or in small batches, making it difficult to achieve perfection in materials, heat treatment processes, process equipment, assembly, and inspection. Any small mistake can lead to major accidents. Taking hydraulic press cylinders as an example, if the sealing system design is unreasonable, or if the dimensions, geometric tolerances, or surface roughness of designed and manufactured parts are not properly handled, internal and external leakage will occur, and merely replacing seals can cause significant waste of manpower and materials. There have been incidents where cracks occurred at the flanged end of a piston rod due to heat treatment problems, leading to early fatigue fracture and causing hydraulic press slide blocks to fall off, resulting in personal injury. These firsthand experiences remind every designer that when designing hydraulic cylinders, one must consider all aspects carefully, be cautious, follow standards, and use calculation methods that have been proven and recognized through engineering practice.

Nowadays, manufacturing hydraulic cylinders is somewhat easier than in the past, as there are now commercial cylinder tubes that comply with JB/T 11718-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Tubes," precision seamless steel tubes with inner diameter that comply with GB/T 32957-2016 "Cold Drawn or Cold Rolled Precision Seamless Steel Tubes for Hydraulic and Pneumatic System Equipment," and seamless steel tubes that comply with YB/T 4673-2018 "Cold Drawn Seamless Steel Tubes for Hydraulic Cylinder Tubes." However, this brings about the problem of connecting and sealing the front and rear end caps. If not handled properly, it may result in batch scrap. Therefore, the manufacturing process of hydraulic cylinders is particularly important. It is necessary to correctly guide production and ensure product quality by designing and summarizing processing techniques and process equipment based on actual hydraulic cylinder production.

Large internal leakage and/or external leakage may be the primary and most intuitive manifestation of poor or deteriorating quality in a hydraulic cylinder. The actual service life of a hydraulic cylinder is often determined by the amount of leakage. At the same time, most of the content in current hydraulic cylinder standards is about sealing requirements or related to sealing, making the design of the hydraulic cylinder sealing device or sealing system particularly important.

The assembly of hydraulic cylinders requires specialized skills. Due to production batch sizes, hydraulic cylinder assembly generally cannot use complete interchangeability assembly method, and often requires grouping method, adjustment method, or repair assembly method. Therefore, operators need to be proficient not only in the drawings and assembly process of hydraulic cylinders, but also in measurement technology, assembly dimension chain calculation, and fitter technology. In this sense, a good hydraulic cylinder is not only designed but also assembled.

Whether it is the finalization (appraisal) of a hydraulic cylinder or its factory (acceptance) inspection, testing is required. Therefore, the comprehensiveness, correctness, and feasibility of hydraulic cylinder testing methods are particularly important. Moreover, the reliability, durability, and environmental adaptability of hydraulic cylinders are determined through testing, which is especially important for hydraulic cylinders used in ships, aerospace, and even military fields. To this end, this manual provides a relatively comprehensive introduction to laboratory environmental testing methods for military equipment.

Hydraulic cylinders are usually just one component in a hydraulic system, or one part in a hydraulic press (machinery), and must meet the technical conditions of the hydraulic press (machinery). Nowadays, the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders often neglect research and understanding of the entire hydraulic press (machinery), resulting in hydraulic cylinders that cannot well meet the technical requirements of the whole machine, making hydraulic cylinders one of the components with the shortest service life in the entire machine. This manual

This handbook provides an overview of hydraulic cylinder design and selection from the perspective of the entire hydraulic machine, based on relevant standards for hydraulic presses (machines) and the author's experience in designing and manufacturing hydraulic presses (machines). It also presents the author's views on content related to hydraulic cylinders in technical conditions for hydraulic presses, for reference and use by readers when designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses (machines).

Like other hydraulic components, hydraulic cylinders can only operate safely and reliably under certain conditions (such as specified operating conditions) to ensure a certain service life. Therefore, hydraulic cylinders need to be used correctly and maintained and serviced properly. Among these, the selection, use, and maintenance of hydraulic working media are particularly important. However, online testing (monitoring) of hydraulic working media not only requires necessary equipment but also requires relevant personnel to have certain practical experience.

In recent years, new standards, new materials, new structures, new processes, new products, new technologies, new design theories, and methods have emerged in the field of hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing. This handbook timely incorporates and summarizes the phased technical achievements, including aspects of green manufacturing and remanufacturing.

Worth promoting is a new design concept and method, which is to integrate the concept of remanufacturing into the design of new hydraulic cylinders, making new hydraulic cylinders remanufacturable. The specific approach is: during the design of new hydraulic cylinders, evaluate the remanufacturability of the hydraulic cylinder and its parts to meet the standards, and correct any problems found.

This handbook follows the new development concept and upholds the spirit of keeping pace with the times and innovation, striving to achieve the best combination of scientificity, advancement, practicality, and reliability, in order to maximize the rapid improvement of the ability of design personnel for hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic machinery, equipment, or devices with hydraulic cylinders as actuators to independently innovate, to meet the needs of building an innovative country.
This handbook has the following characteristics:
1. Comprehensive, New, and Accurate Standards

This handbook not only comprehensively and systematically cites and excerpts standards related to hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing published and implemented before December 31, 2018, such as GB/T 35023—2018 "Reliability Evaluation Method for Hydraulic Components", GB/T 36520.1—2018 "Hydraulic Transmission Polyurethane Seal Size Series Part 1: Dimensions and Tolerances of Piston Reciprocating Motion Seals", GB/T 36520.2—2018 "Hydraulic Transmission Polyurethane Seal Size Series Part 2: Dimensions and Tolerances of Piston Rod Reciprocating Motion Seals", GB/T 2348—2018 "Fluid Transmission Systems and Components Cylinder Diameter and Piston Rod Diameter", GB/T 37162.1—2018 "Hydraulic Transmission Monitoring of Contamination by Fluid Particles Part 1: General Provisions", and even includes GB/T 37400.10—2019 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery Part 10: Assembly" and GB/T 37400.16—2019 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery Part 16: Hydraulic Systems" published on August 30, 2019, and implemented on March 1, 2020, and based on the author's summary of application experience, explains matters that should be noted when citing these standards.
2. Practical and Reliable Content

This handbook includes standards, commonly used formulas and materials for hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing, technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their parts, etc., providing comprehensive, accurate, and practical reference standards, documents, and materials for engineering and technical personnel to design hydraulic cylinders, such as listing a large number of hydraulic cylinder drawings that have been tested on engineering prototypes (or empirical tests) in Section 4.9 and compiling Section 3.9 based on practical experience, providing truly useful references for engineering and technical personnel to design and manufacture hydraulic cylinders.
3. Adhering to Innovation and Pursuing Advancement

Innovation is the primary driving force for leading development. Some content in this handbook is given by the author for the first time, such as the failure modes of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system given according to GB/T 35023—2018. Taking Chapter 5 of this handbook as an example, not only are the test methods specified in GB/T 15622—2005 "Hydraulic Cylinder Test Method" and JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" innovated (including errata), but also the author's views on the test methods specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 2: Test Method" and GB/T 32216—2015 "Hydraulic Transmission Test Method for Proportional/Servo Control Hydraulic Cylinders" are presented and explanations are given.

In addition, this manual analyzes and compares the test methods in CB/T 3812—2013 "Hydraulic Cylinders for Ship Hatches", JB/T 11588—2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", and GB/T 24946—2010 "Digital Hydraulic Cylinders for Ships", and presents opinions.

During the compilation of this manual, we received strong support and help from many experts and professors, and we sincerely express our gratitude here! Due to the limited level of the authors and the incomplete research work, this manual must have some omissions and deficiencies, and we sincerely request criticism and corrections from readers.

1.1 Commonly Used Standard Catalogs for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing

A standard is a normative document, based on the comprehensive achievements of science, technology, and experience, formulated according to the principle of consensus and approved by a recognized institution, with the characteristics of common use and repeatability, in order to achieve the best order within a certain range. A document that clarifies requirements is called a specification. Normative documents are general terms for documents such as standards, technical specifications, procedures, and regulations.

The design and (re)manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders involve many current standards. According to these related standards, hydraulic cylinders can be designed and manufactured in a standardized manner, thereby obtaining unified, simplified, coordinated, and optimized hydraulic cylinders.

sections.text: 1.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing Common Standards Excerpts

Because standards have the characteristics of common use and repeated use, although this section excerpts the following standards, for the convenience of readers' reference and use, this manual may also repeatedly use these standards in other sections, such as GB/T 2348—2018 "Fluid Transmission Systems and Components Cylinder Bore and Piston Rod Diameter", GB 2350—1980 "Fluid Transmission Systems and Components Piston Rod Thread Form and Size Series" (a new standard is being developed), etc.
1.2.1 Excerpts of Commonly Used Basic Standards
1. GB/T 2346—2003 "Fluid Transmission Systems and Components Nominal Pressure Series" Standard Excerpts

In fluid transmission systems, power is transmitted and controlled through pressurized fluid (liquid or gas) in the circuit. Generally, systems and components are designed and sold for specified fluid pressure ranges.

The nominal pressure series of fluid transmission systems and components specified in the standard are shown in Table 1-9. This standard applies to the nominal pressure of fluid transmission systems and components, and also applies to the selection of pressure values in other related fluid transmission standards.

7. Excerpt from JB/T 7939—2010 "Area Ratio of Two Chambers in Single Piston Rod Hydraulic Cylinder"

The standard specifies the area ratio of two chambers in single piston rod hydraulic cylinders as shown in Table 1-18. This standard applies to the standard ratio of effective areas of the rodless chamber and rod chamber in hydraulic cylinders corresponding to single piston rod hydraulic cylinders.

For each value of D (cylinder bore diameter), the standard provides a series of standard values for d (piston rod diameter), which make the area ratio approximately equal to one of the following preferred numbers: 1.06, 1.12, 1.25, 1.32, 1.40, 1.60, 2.00, 2.50, and 5.00.

1.2.2 Excerpts of Scope and Normative References of Hydraulic Cylinder Product Standards

Product standards are standards that specify the requirements to be met by products to ensure their applicability. In the following excerpts of standards, the current standard date is added to the normative references that do not specify a date; for replaced standards, new standards are cited, and necessary corrections are made. When conducting quality assessment and accident arbitration based on the following standards, the original standard provisions shall still be followed, i.e., for all dated references, all subsequent amendments (excluding corrections) or revised versions are not applicable to the standard, but the parties who have reached an agreement based on the standard are encouraged to study whether to use the latest versions of these documents. For undated references, the current version of the referenced documents is applicable to this standard.

Another chapter in this manual specifically discusses JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", so this section does not excerpt it separately, but the following standard excerpts include excerpts of several hydraulic cylinder (component) technical conditions (specifications).

1.3 Common Standards for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing - Terms and Definitions and Their Explanations
1.3.1 Terms and Definitions Defined in Common Standards

Terms are the most basic subject of standardization. For terms and definitions, if there are no recognized standards, the formulation of other technical standards in a technical field will become a difficult and time-consuming task, which will ultimately lead to low work efficiency and a high probability of misunderstandings.

Terms are the linguistic (word) references to general concepts in specific professional fields. Terms should have the property of univocity, at least within a related discipline or a professional field, otherwise ambiguity, polysemy, and synonymy phenomena will occur.

Within a standard or a series of standards (or different parts of a standard), the same term should be used for the same concept. Synonyms should be avoided for defined concepts. Each selected term should have only one meaning as much as possible.

Before establishing terms and definitions for a concept in a certain standard, it should be checked whether terms and definitions for that concept have already been established in other standards. If they have been established, the standard that defines the concept should be cited, and there is no need to redefine it.

If it is necessary to repeat a term that has already been standardized, the standard from which the definition comes should be indicated. If an already standardized definition must be rewritten, a note should be added.
Terms should not contain requirements, nor should they be written in the form of requirements. The expression of a definition should be able to replace its term in context.

In the field of fluid power and control technology, terms have specific meanings. When formulating, modifying standards, writing journals, reports, and related technical documents, the terms specified in each standard should be used.

sections.text: 1.3.2 Explanation on Some Terms and Definitions
Terms (concepts) and definitions are the starting point of the life (service life) cycle of a product, and their importance is self-evident.
1. Proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder

In the current standards and some mechanical (hydraulic) design manuals and hydraulic technology monographs, terms such as cylinder, oil cylinder, hydraulic cylinder, servo cylinder, servo hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic booster, hydraulic actuator, hydraulic actuator, hydraulic servo actuator, and proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder have been used. Some of them have been defined in relevant standards. For example, "cylinder" and "servo cylinder" are defined in GB/T17446-2012, but the term "servo cylinder" is limited to only being related to pneumatic technology; in GB/T32216-2015, the term "proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder" is defined, which is a hydraulic cylinder used for proportional/servo control with dynamic performance requirements; in HB083-2005, there are names such as "hydraulic booster" and "hydraulic actuator", although there are no definitions, but there are explanations; "hydraulic servo actuator" is seen in reference [83], but its source is unclear; in QJ1495-1988, terms such as "actuator", "servo actuator", "electro-hydraulic servo actuator", and "servo hydraulic cylinder" are defined, which are applicable to aerospace product technical documents, and various papers, monographs, and civilian product technical documents can also refer to them; in DB44/T11691.1-2013 (already abolished, for reference only), the term "servo hydraulic cylinder" is defined, which is a hydraulic cylinder with static and dynamic index requirements. By cooperating with built-in or external sensors, servo valves or proportional valves, controllers, etc., it can form a hydraulic control system with high control accuracy and fast response speed. Static indexes include trial operation, pressure resistance, internal leakage, external leakage, minimum starting pressure, load starting friction force, eccentricity, leakage under low pressure, stroke detection, load efficiency, high temperature test, durability, etc.

Dynamic indicators include step response, frequency response, etc. According to the current standards, this manual uses "proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder", "servo controlled hydraulic cylinder", "servo hydraulic cylinder", or "hydraulic cylinder". According to or referring to some current standards, such as GB/T8129-2015, "servo hydraulic cylinder" is tentatively defined as a hydraulic cylinder whose cylinder advance, cylinder return movement and/or stop are operated according to instructions. The instruction may indicate the required next position value, or it may indicate the feed speed required to move to that position, or it may indicate the time, amplitude and/or frequency for which it remains at the predetermined position (nearby).
It should be noted here:

items: Do not call the hydraulic cylinder and servo valve integrated together a "servo hydraulic cylinder". If so, the definition of "servo hydraulic cylinder" in QJ1495-1988 cannot continue to be used.
In some fields, hydraulic vibration generators (or vibration generators, exciters, etc.) may also refer to servo controlled hydraulic cylinders. Please refer to standards such as GB/T22982-2010.

sections.text: It needs to be emphasized that at least the term "hydraulic cylinder" should be used in the field of hydraulic technology, because it needs to be distinguished from "air cylinder"; it is not advisable to use "servo cylinder" because it has been defined as a term only related to pneumatic technology.
2. Cylinder stroke

Terms such as "stroke", "cylinder stroke", "working stroke", and "full stroke" have been defined or used in relevant standards. For example, in GB/T17446-2012, "cylinder stroke" is defined as: the distance moved by its movable part from one limit position to another limit position; it also includes some expressions related to "cylinder stroke", such as "adjustable stroke cylinder (or adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder)" is defined as: the stroke stop position of which can be adjusted.

A cylinder whose position can be changed to allow variation in stroke length. Additionally, the term "full stroke" has been used in standards such as CB/T 3812—2013, JB/T 10205—2010, QC/T 460—2010, and DB44/T 1169.1—2013; while "maximum cylinder stroke" has been defined in reference [108].

If "stroke" is the distance between two extreme positions, then the stroke cannot be changed; if the extreme positions can be changed, then they are not extreme positions. Therefore, one of the definitions of extreme position and stroke must be negated (or ignored, or its meaning changed). If "stroke" can be varied, i.e., adjustable, then there would be no parameter in hydraulic cylinders that can be calibrated (represented) for basic parameters, thus there is a need to define the term "maximum cylinder stroke" and its definition.

In reference [108], "maximum cylinder stroke" is defined as the distance moved by its movable part from the cylinder's return (forward) dead center to the cylinder's forward (return) dead center. Since "maximum cylinder stroke" can be defined, "minimum cylinder stroke" can also be defined, thus "cylinder stroke" can be understood as having a certain range, or expressed as "cylinder stroke range". Further, "cylinder working stroke range" can be defined, and "maximum cylinder stroke" and "minimum cylinder stroke" should be included in the "cylinder stroke range". For servo hydraulic cylinders, defining "maximum cylinder stroke", "minimum cylinder stroke", "cylinder stroke range", and "cylinder working stroke range" is of great significance.

Because "cylinder forward dead center" is defined as the cylinder's forward limit position restricted by the cylinder structure, "maximum cylinder stroke" is determined by the cylinder structure, and is one of the characteristics that distinguishes this cylinder from other cylinders. This characteristic should be unique and have a definite meaning, i.e., the cylinder's forward dead center. The cylinder's forward dead center has only one (point) in a specific servo hydraulic cylinder, and it is also unique.

Under "cylinder working stroke range", "maximum working stroke" and "minimum working stroke" can be derived. Since "cylinder working stroke range" is included in "cylinder stroke range", "maximum working stroke" and "minimum working stroke" are also included in "maximum cylinder stroke" and "minimum cylinder stroke". Therefore, servo hydraulic cylinders can set "soft limits" through the control system they are in to avoid the moving parts colliding with other cylinder parts.
In GB/T 36484—2018 "Terminology for Forging Machinery", there are multiple terms related to stroke, all defined as: "... the maximum distance of movement."
3. Load-bearing Dynamic Friction Force and Dynamic Friction Force

"Load-bearing dynamic friction force" and "dynamic friction force" are related to servo hydraulic cylinders or proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinders. Whether they are synonyms or which one is more accurate is a problem that servo hydraulic cylinder designers need to consider.

In DB44/T 1169.1—2013, the term "load-bearing dynamic friction force" is defined as the motion resistance generated by the cylinder barrel, end cap, and sealing device to the piston rod under the condition of the servo hydraulic cylinder piston rod moving with load. In GB/T 32216—2015, the term "dynamic friction force" is defined as the motion resistance experienced by the piston and piston rod under the condition of the proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinder moving with load.
Whether it is "load-bearing dynamic friction force" or "dynamic friction force", there are certain problems with their terms and definitions, which are briefly explained as follows:

items: Although "load-bearing dynamic friction force" is slightly better than "dynamic friction force", both repeat the term "dynamic friction force" in tribology. Even if rewriting the already standardized definition, it should be explained.
In the definition of "load-bearing dynamic friction force", the statement "the motion resistance generated by the cylinder barrel, end cap, and sealing device to the piston rod" is questionable.

In the definition of "dynamic friction force", plunger hydraulic cylinders should not have a piston, so the definition "the motion resistance experienced by the piston and piston rod" is not rigorous enough.

Under unclear load conditions (not specified or limited in the term), whether it is possible to detect (test) or repeatedly detect (test) the "dynamic friction force" within a certain detection (test) accuracy range is debatable. What kind of influence do various loads have on the dynamic friction force and the static/dynamic characteristics of hydraulic cylinders, as well as the non-linear characteristics of dynamic friction essence, modeling uncertainty, etc. are all topics that hydraulic workers are currently researching.

sections.text: For hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T 10205—2010, dynamic friction force is part of the load efficiency test.

Based on the above brief analysis, the author believes that using the set of terms "running friction force", "no-load running friction force", and "loaded running friction force" to distinguish other hydraulic cylinders (specific) is more appropriate.
4. Leakage

In various standards, literature, and materials, it is very common to use "leakage" to describe the condition (phenomenon) of welds, parts, assemblies (devices). For example, in GB/T 241—2007, the term "leakage" is defined as the phenomenon of pressure transmission medium appearing on the outer surface of the metal tube base or weld under test pressure; at the same time, "destructive test" is also defined using "leakage", which is a test that continuously increases test pressure until the metal tube shows leakage or rupture. In GB 25974.1—2010, "external leakage" is defined as the leakage of hydraulic components, with more than one drop of working fluid leaking out within an average of 5 minutes; in GB/T 30206.2—2013, "leakage/seal leakage" is defined as a very small amount of fluid leakage on the surface of accessories, usually caused by the sealing parts undergoing periodic pressure loads resulting in compression expansion. For liquids, a thin oil film will form on the outer surface of the accessories, but no liquid droplets should form within the specified time. In JB/T 13141—2017, "leakage" is defined as

54.page_header: Chapter 1 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Manufacturing Fundamentals 43

sections.text: referred to as 'external leakage'. When the hydraulic oil, under a certain pressure and viscosity, flows from the hydraulic cylinder's internal chamber to the atmosphere, this is called external leakage.
There is also a definition of leakage, as defined in JB/T 13566—2018, which specifies that within 10 minutes if leakage exceeds one drop of oil, it is considered oil leakage, not oil seepage.

In reference document [102] it states: 'Leakage generally can be classified by form into: seepage, leakage, and blow-by. Leakage occurring in hydraulic cylinder seals is mainly blow-by (or leakage through). Due to the characteristics of blow-by classification, leakage through capillary tubes, and leakage through sealing components (substrates), while hydraulic cylinder seal product leakage is generally not caused by porosity in the sealing material, so it should not be called seepage but rather leakage.' The statement that leakage occurring in hydraulic cylinder seals is primarily blow-by is a classification standard for leakage.

What also needs to be noted is that leakage amount should not be used to distinguish between leakage and seepage. The specific verification can refer to GB/Z 18427—2001, which only applies to leakage caused by porosity in sealing materials (such as sealing components existing in substrates) and similar leakage, and should be called seepage.

For metal pipes (full pipes or pipe fittings), welds, etc., the definition of 'leakage' in GB/T 2247—2007 should be applied (for steel, cast iron and non-ferrous metal tubes at room temperature and below, as the basic type and standard).
5. Combined Seals

In GB/T 15242.1—2017, three types of combined seals are defined along with their terminology and definitions, categorized as 'hole type combined seal', 'shaft type stepped seal', and 'shaft type sliding lip seal'. However, this standard does not provide the terminology for 'coaxial seal' and its definition, while the standard's normative references cite GB/T 17446—2012, which also does not have the term 'coaxial seal'. This terminology has become an established convention without formal verification. For example, the term 'coaxial seal' has become a commonly used informal term. If this is considered a problem, reference document [102] notes that in JB/T 8241—1996, the term 'coaxial seal' was defined.

This term refers to plastic rings and rubber rings combined together to form a complete sealing component. At the same time, using 'coaxial seal' defines 'square ring seal', 'rectangular seal', 'mountain-shaped multi-component ring' and 'triangular multi-component ring' as four types of coaxial seals, and defines 'plastic ring' as a term, which means coaxial seals are composed of elastomeric sealing rings.

A combined seal (or ring) is composed of two or more of the above types of components, achieving the sealing function through different materials. The sealed components are combined into a single unit. Compared to single-material seals, the overall sealing performance of combined seals is better.

The 'coaxial' in the context of 'coaxial seals' does not refer to bore seals, but rather the distinction between combined seal types is characterized by differences. Bore seals reference bore types, while shaft seals reference shaft types. They share common features, as in the GB/T 10708.2—2000 standard, the 'ribbed rubber seal ring' and 'chevron rubber seal ring' both have
the characteristic that it is called 'bi-directional rubber seal ring' rather than 'coaxial seal'.

For the definition in GB/T 15242.1—2017 regarding this type of seal, its characteristic is that the structural component is called 'plastic ring' or 'plastic part'. Therefore, see JB/T 10205—2010 regarding the definition of 'sliding ring type combined seal'. There is a common issue, but overall, looking at GB/T 15242.1—2017, the combined seal is better. Further analyzing 'sliding ring type combined seal' as a seal classification and its relationship to elastic and flexible materials, seals operate through the seal body under applied force and stress to achieve actual deformation, allowing the elastic deformation capability to quickly restore to its initial close fit with the sealed surface, using elastic materials.

The above definition of 'elastic material' is derived from GB/T 17446—2012, while in GB/T 15242.1—2017 it is redefined as 'elastomer', and its normative reference states GB/T 9981—2008, while the former states GB/T 17446—2012, but GB/T 17446—2012 is the standard that should be referenced for normative citations, which does not comply with the standard's normative requirements.
In GB/T 15242.1—2017, 'seal carrier' is defined as: the cylinder bore piston or piston rod groove or similar fitting that relies on elastomeric force to achieve the sealed condition.
6. Sealing System
'Sealing system' is frequently found in various documents, materials, and notes. In standards such as GB/T 3217—2015, it is not yet formally listed with separate terminology and definition.

To introduce or establish 'hydraulic sealing system' as a formal terminology with authoritative definition, reference document [102] can be consulted. The main point is that it can be further understood by promoting design concept advancement. Hydraulic cylinder seal design should focus on the overall sealing concept, not just individual seal components, but rather the integration of seal components with the installation groove design, unified coordination. This promotes the concept of hydraulic cylinder seal and its design optimization.

Establishing a terminology that serves a clear purpose, establishing hydraulic cylinder 'sealing system' as a terminology serves this purpose. The establishment of hydraulic cylinder 'sealing system' terminology is beneficial for promoting hydraulic cylinder seal design concept advancement, and improving hydraulic cylinder sealing technology. But if only one seal (ring) is used, it cannot be called a sealing system.

Two seals configured together may not necessarily constitute a sealing system. For example, two independent seals configured by two or more seal components to form a sealing system have synergistic sealing effects. Therefore, it is a sealing system, not just a simple seal component configuration.

Hydraulic cylinder sealing systems must satisfy hydraulic cylinder sealing (performance) requirements; hydraulic cylinder sealing systems generally consist of piston sealing systems and piston rod sealing systems; hydraulic cylinder sealing systems emphasize (special) characteristics.

Coordination and unified configuration of all sealing components. The term "hydraulic cylinder sealing system" is defined as follows: A set of sealing components arranged in series according to hydraulic cylinder sealing requirements, designed to create sealing, control leakage, and/or prevent contamination.

It should be noted that the sealing components referred to here specifically include sealing rings, retaining rings, guide rings, and dust seals used on hydraulic cylinders. A sealing assembly consists of one or more sealing components and matching parts (such as retaining rings, springs, metal shells), combined with guide rings, support rings, and backing rings.

Definitions of terms such as "minimum starting pressure," "load efficiency," and "combined hydraulic cylinder" can be found in Section 5.1.1. For issues related to the naming of digital hydraulic cylinders, see Section 5.5.

1.6.3  Resistance Calculation Formulas

Actual fluids will cause energy loss due to viscous friction force (motion resistance) during flow. Generally, this energy loss due to motion resistance is divided into friction (pressure) loss along the path and local resistance (pressure) loss.
The energy loss of fluid on the calculated length of a pipe section is the sum of friction (pressure) loss along the path and local resistance (pressure) loss.
1. Calculation of Friction Loss Along the Path

Friction loss along the path is related to the flow state of the fluid. Under given conditions, the quantitative standard (index) used to indicate whether the flow is laminar or turbulent is the critical Reynolds number.
Calculation formulas for friction loss along the path in circular pipes are shown in Table 1-40.

3. Hydraulic Shock Calculation

In hydraulic system components, accessories and pipelines, the pressure rise caused by a sudden decrease in flow may cause hydraulic (pressure) shock. When the movement speed of the hydraulic cylinder changes drastically (such as starting, stopping or reversing), the hydraulic (pressure) shock caused by the inertial force due to the rate of change of momentum of the liquid in the cavity and moving parts is calculated using the formula in Table 1-51.

1. Calculation formula for thin-walled cylinder tube

Since thin-walled cylinder tubes are classified as axisymmetric problems, they can be calculated using the (thin) shell momentless theory. From the Laplace equation of uniformly thin shells under internal pressure: σt/r + σz/r = p/δ, and after assuming, simplifying, and omitting, the calculation formula for thin-walled cylinder tubes can be obtained.

sections.text: 3. Calculation Formula for Combined Cylinder

Since the stress at points r = ri and r = re (on the inner and outer cylindrical surfaces of the thick-walled cylinder under internal pressure) differs greatly, most of the material in the outer layer of the cylinder cannot be fully utilized. To make the stress distribution more uniform along the cylinder wall thickness, reduce the load on the inner wall, and effectively improve the load-bearing capacity of the cylinder while better utilizing the material of the outer layer, combined cylinders should be used for cylinders with very high internal pressure.

Combined cylinders are typically formed by a tight interference fit between an outer cylinder and an inner cylinder through the temperature difference method, or even by fitting two or more layers of outer cylinders onto an inner cylinder.
The load type and stress distribution of a one-layer combined cylinder subjected to internal pressure p are shown in Figure 1-6, and the calculation formulas are given in Table 1-66.

sections.text: 5. Calculation formula for rod stability

Hydraulic cylinder has at least one end that can move back and forth. Hydraulic cylinder can be simplified as a rod with uniform or non-uniform cross-section. For a rod (deformable body) in a deformed state, the balance between external load and elastic internal force it causes can be stable or unstable. The stability of the equilibrium state of a deformable body depends on the value of the compressive load applied on it. The extreme value of this load is called "critical load" Fkp.
For a rod (hydraulic cylinder) simplified as having uniform diameter d, when installation distance and stroke have a ratio greater than 10, i.e. l/d > 10, rod stability generally needs to be calculated or checked (or verified). See Table 1-67 for calculation formula.

sections.text: 1.7.3  Allowable Stress and Static Calculation of Hydraulic Cylinder
1. Allowable Stress

1) Allowable stress when the hydraulic cylinder is subjected to centric rated force. The normal stress of individual parts of the hydraulic cylinder shall not exceed 70% of the yield limit or the 0.2% residual deformation limit of the material (this also applies to the tangential stress caused by liquid pressure); the tangential stress shall not exceed 65% of the yield limit of the material.
The normal stress at the high-pressure end of the hydraulic cylinder shall not exceed 80% of the yield limit of the material.

2) Allowable stress when the column and the supporting jack are subjected to twice the centric rated force. When the column and the supporting jack are in the fully retracted state and subjected to twice the centric rated force, the stress shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.
Note: This requirement only includes mechanical loads and excludes liquid pressure.

3) Allowable stress when the column and the supporting jack are subjected to eccentric rated force. When subjected to eccentric rated force, the normal stress (boundary stress) of the bent parts of the column and the supporting jack shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.

When the eccentric rated force is also subjected to lateral loads (e.g., used for stabilizing the support frame), the normal stress of the bent parts of the column and the supporting jack shall not exceed the yield limit of the material.

4) Allowable stress of welds. Under the load conditions of 1) to 3), the stress of the welds shall not exceed the percentage values of the allowable stress of the parent material listed in Table 1-68.

3. General Thread Tolerances
The thread engagement length is divided into three groups: short group (S), medium group (N), and long group (L). The length ranges for each group should conform to the provisions of Table 1-74.

To reduce the number of cutting tools, thread tolerance classes should be selected according to Tables 1-75 and 1-76. The thread tolerance class is determined based on the thread tolerance accuracy (precision, medium, rough) and engagement length group (S, N, L). If the actual engagement length of the thread is unknown (such as for standard bolts), it is recommended to determine the thread tolerance class according to the medium group (N). According to the usage conditions, thread tolerance accuracy is divided into the following three levels: precision (used for precision threads), medium (used for general-purpose threads), and rough (used for situations where thread manufacturing is difficult, such as on hot-rolled bars and deep blind holes).

Unless otherwise specified, the recommended tolerance zones apply to threads before coating.
4. Thread Marking
A complete thread marking consists of a thread characteristic symbol, dimension symbol, tolerance zone symbol, and other necessary individual information for further explanation.
The characteristic symbol for ordinary threads is "M".
The dimension symbol for single-line threads is "Nominal Diameter × Pitch", with the numerical units of nominal diameter and pitch being millimeters.
Example 1: M8×1 indicates a single-line fine thread with a nominal diameter of 8 mm and a pitch of 1 mm.
For coarse threads, the pitch item can be omitted.
Example 2: M8 indicates a single-line coarse thread with a nominal diameter of 8 mm and a pitch of 1.25 mm.

The tolerance zone symbol consists of the pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol and the major diameter (for internal threads) or minor diameter (for external threads) tolerance zone symbol. The pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol is placed first, followed by the major/minor diameter tolerance zone symbol.

Each diameter's tolerance zone symbol is composed of a numerical value indicating the tolerance grade and a letter (uppercase for internal threads, lowercase for external threads) indicating the tolerance zone position.
If the pitch diameter tolerance zone symbol is the same as the major/minor diameter tolerance zone symbol, only one tolerance zone symbol is marked.
The thread dimension symbol and tolerance zone are separated by a hyphen "-".

Example 3: External thread: M10×1-5g6g indicates an external thread with a pitch diameter tolerance zone of 5g and a major diameter tolerance zone of 6g. M10-6g indicates a coarse external thread with both pitch diameter and major diameter tolerance zones of 6g. Internal thread: M10×1-5H6H indicates an internal thread with a pitch diameter tolerance zone of 5H and a minor diameter tolerance zone of 6H.
M10-6H indicates a coarse internal thread with both pitch diameter and minor diameter tolerance zones of 6H.
When indicating thread fits, the internal thread tolerance zone symbol is placed first, followed by the external thread tolerance zone symbol, separated by a slash "/".
Example 4: M6-6H/6g indicates a fit composed of an internal thread with a tolerance zone of 6H and an external thread with a tolerance zone of 6g.
M20×2-6H/5g6g indicates a fit composed of an internal thread with a tolerance zone of 6H and an external thread with a tolerance zone of 5g6g.
In the following cases, the tolerance zone symbols for medium tolerance accuracy threads can be omitted:
a) Internal thread: —5H for nominal diameters less than or equal to 1.4 mm; —6H for nominal diameters greater than or equal to 1.6 mm.
Note: For threads with a pitch of 0.2 mm, the tolerance grade is 4.
b) External thread: —6h for nominal diameters less than or equal to 1.4 mm; —6g for nominal diameters greater than or equal to 1.6 mm.

Example 5: M10 indicates a coarse external thread with pitch diameter and major diameter tolerance zones of 6g and medium tolerance accuracy, or a coarse internal thread with pitch diameter and minor diameter tolerance zones of 6H and medium tolerance accuracy.
Other necessary information in the marking includes the thread engagement length group and direction of rotation.

For threads with short and long engagement lengths, it is recommended to mark "S" and "L" symbols after the tolerance zone symbol, separated by a hyphen "-". For threads with medium engagement length, the engagement length group symbol (N) is not marked.
Example 6: M20×2-5H-S indicates an internal thread with short engagement length.
M6-7H/7g6g-L indicates internal and external threads with long engagement length.

Thread tolerance grade code: For external threads, mark with grades A and B; for internal threads, do not mark the tolerance grade code.
Marking example: The marking for a right-handed cylindrical internal thread with size code 2 is G2.

The marking for a B-grade right-handed cylindrical external thread with size code 4 is G4B.
When the thread is left-handed, add the notation "LH" after the tolerance grade code of the external thread or the size code of the internal thread.
Marking example: The marking for a left-handed cylindrical internal thread with size code 2 is G2LH.

1.7.5 Processability and Structural Elements of Cylinder Component Design
1. Review of Product Structure Processability

All newly designed products or improved design products should undergo a review of product structure processability during the design process. For incoming product drawings, a review of product structure processability must be conducted before trial production.

The purpose of reviewing product structure processability is to ensure that the product meets processability requirements under the premise of satisfying quality and user requirements, and can be manufactured using relatively economical and reasonable methods under existing production conditions. It also aims to reduce the negative impact on the environment during the manufacturing process, improve resource utilization, improve working conditions, reduce harm to operators, and facilitate use, maintenance, or recycling. Processability is divided into production processability and usage processability; the evaluation form is also divided into qualitative evaluation and quantitative evaluation. The evaluation of product structure processability mainly considers the following factors: 1) The type and complexity of the product. 2) The production volume or production type of the product. 3) Production efficiency and economy. 4) Existing production, usage, maintenance, and recycling conditions. (1) Basic Requirements for Processability of Casting, Forging, Stamping, Welding, Heat Treatment, Machining, and Assembly of Component Structures 1) Processability of Casting Component Structures: a. The wall thickness of castings should be appropriate and uniform. Under the premise of meeting component requirements, large wall thickness differences should be avoided as much as possible to reduce manufacturing difficulty. b. The casting fillets should be reasonable and no sharp corners should be present. c. The structure of the casting should be simplified as much as possible and have a reasonable draft angle for easy demolding. d. The thickness and distribution of ribs should be reasonable to avoid deformation or cracking of the casting during cooling. e. The material selection for castings should be reasonable. f. The internal cavity structure of the casting should minimize the number of cores and facilitate core fixing and venting. 2) Processability of Forging Component Structures: a. The structure should be as simple and symmetrical as possible. b. Die forgings should have a reasonable forging draft angle and fillet radius. c. The material and structure should have forgeability. 3) Processability of Stamping Component Structures: a. The structure should be as simple and symmetrical as possible. b. Sharp corners should be avoided in the outer shape and inner holes as much as possible. c. The size of the fillet radius should be conducive to forming. d. The material selection should meet process requirements. 4) Processability of Welding Component Structures: a. The materials used for welded components should have weldability. b. The arrangement of welds should be conducive to reducing welding stress and deformation, and minimizing energy and welding material consumption. c. The form, position, and size of the weld joint should meet the requirements for welding quality. d. The technical requirements for welded components should be reasonable. e. The component structure should be conducive to welding operation. f. Requirements for operational safety and reduction of environmental pollution should be met. 5) Processability of Heat Treatment Component Structures: a. The technical requirements for heat treatment should be reasonable. b. Heat-treated components should avoid sharp corners, sharp edges, and blind holes as much as possible. c. The cross-section should be as uniform and symmetrical as possible.

d. The material of parts should be compatible with the required physical and mechanical properties.
e. The heat treatment process of part materials should cause minimal environmental pollution.
6) Cutting processability of part structure:

a. Requirements for dimensional tolerances, geometric tolerances, and surface structure should be economical and reasonable.
b. Geometric shapes of machined surfaces should be as simple as possible.
c. Surfaces with mutual positional requirements should be machined in as few setups as possible.

d. Parts should have reasonable process datum and try to be consistent with design datum.
e. Structural elements of parts should be unified as much as possible, and try to use common equipment and standard tools for machining.
f. The structure of parts should facilitate simultaneous processing of multiple pieces.

g. The structure of parts should facilitate clamping, machining, and inspection.
h. The structure of parts should facilitate using less cutting fluid during machining.
7) Assembly processability:

items: a. Complex process equipment should be avoided as much as possible during assembly.
b. In the structure of assembly units or their components weighing more than 20 (or 15) kg, structural elements for lifting should be provided.
c. Intermediate disassembly and reassembly of related components should be avoided during assembly.
d. The connection methods of various components should ensure quick assembly and disassembly using the least tools as much as possible.
e. Various connection structural forms should facilitate mechanization and automation of assembly work.

sections.text: (3) Contents of processability review
To ensure good processability of the designed product, process review should be conducted at all stages of product design.
1) Review in preliminary design stage:

items: a. Analyze the rationality of structural schemes from a manufacturing perspective.
b. Analyze structural inheritance.
c. Analyze the degree of standardization, modularization, generalization, and serialization of the structure.
d. Analyze whether the various components of the product are conducive to assembly, adjustment, and maintenance.
e. Analyze whether the various components of the product are conducive to recycling and reuse after scrapping.
f. Analyze whether the selection of main materials is reasonable.
g. Possibility of processing main components in-house or outsourcing.

sections.text: 2) Review in technical design stage:

items: a. Analyze the feasibility of parallel assembly and inspection of various components of the product.
b. Analyze the feasibility of final assembly.
c. Analyze the feasibility of avoiding or reducing cutting machining during assembly.
d. Analyze the feasibility of manufacturing high-precision complex parts in-house.
e. Analyze the checkability of main parameters and the reasonableness of main assembly accuracy.
f. Analyze the feasibility of outsourcing special parts for processing.

sections.text: 3) Review in working drawing design stage:

items: a. Whether each component has assembly datum and is conducive to assembly.
b. The feasibility of splitting large components into smaller components for parallel assembly.
c. The feasibility of recycling and reusing components after scrapping.
d. Review the processability of casting, forging, stamping, welding, heat treatment, cutting machining, special machining, and assembly of parts.

sections.text: e. Review the possible harmful environmental impacts or safety hazards during the manufacturing process of parts, and whether these impacts or hazards can be avoided or reduced.

sections.text: 16. Classification and Codes for Metal Heat Treatment Processes
Metal heat treatment processes are classified into two main levels: basic classification and additional classification, with further subdivisions possible within each main level.

(1) Basic Classification: Based on the general name, type, and specific name of the process (classified according to the resulting microstructure or infiltrated elements), heat treatment processes are classified into three levels, as shown in Table 1-121.

(2) Additional Classification: Additional classification is a more detailed classification of certain process conditions within the basic classification. It includes the heating method and code for implementing the process, as shown in Table 1-122; annealing process and code, as shown in Table 1-123; and quenching cooling medium and cooling method and code, as shown in Table 1-124.

sections.text: 2. Technical Requirements for Electroplating of Hydraulic Cylinder Parts (Excerpt from GB/T 25974.2—2010)
(1) Basic Requirements

Before electroplating, the material, dimensional accuracy, and surface defects of the parts to be plated should be inspected. Parts that do not meet the requirements should not enter the electroplating process.
(2) Types of Plating Layers
1) Piston Rod. The piston rod should adopt one of the following composite plating layers:

items: a) Copper-tin alloy and hard chromium
b) Copper-tin alloy and white chromium
c) White chromium and hard chromium

sections.text: 2) Other Parts. Other parts are generally electroplated with zinc, and other plating types that effectively protect the surface of the parts are allowed.
(3) Thickness of Plating Layers
1) Composite Plating Layers. The thickness of composite plating layers:

items: a) Copper-tin alloy: 20–35μm; hard chromium: 30–45μm
b) Copper-tin alloy: 20–35μm; white chromium: 30–55μm
c) White chromium: 20–35μm; hard chromium: 30–45μm

sections.text: 2) Zinc Plating or Other Plating Layers. The thickness of zinc plating or other plating layers:
3) Special Plating Layers. The thickness of plating layers with special requirements shall be executed according to the provisions of the drawing documents.
(4) Hardness of Plating Layers

items: a) Copper-tin alloy and white chromium ≥500HV
b) White chromium and hard chromium ≥800HV
c) Copper-tin alloy and hard chromium ≥800HV

sections.text: (5) Appearance Quality of Plating Layers

items: 1) Inspection Environment. The appearance quality inspection should be conducted under natural scattered light or white light transmitted through light without reflected light.
2) Appearance Quality. The plating layer should be fine and uniform in crystallization, and should not have the following defects:
a) Surface roughness, particles, scorching, cracks, blistering, peeling, or falling off
b) Dendritic crystallization
c) Local absence of plating layer or exposure of intermediate layer
3) Allowed Defects. The plating layer is allowed to have the following defects:
a) Slight rough surface that does not affect assembly at the chamfer
b) Dark plating layer at the weld seam
c) Pitting or pinholes caused by defects in the base metal, sand holes, and the electroplating process, the diameter and quantity of which should meet the following requirements

sections.text: ① For zinc-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
② For chromium-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
③ For copper-plated parts, less than 5 points/dm², and the pore diameter should not be greater than 0.2mm.
4) Surfaces Not Assessed. Plating layer defects caused by welding-allowed defects are not assessed; the quality of the plating layer on the surface of the relief groove is not assessed.
5) Sand Marks on the Piston Rod Travel Surface. The sand marks on the piston rod travel surface are specified as follows:

items: a) There should not be more than two sand marks on the same circumferential line of the piston rod travel surface.
b) The length of sand marks should not exceed 6mm, and the depth should not be greater than 0.02mm
c) The interval between two sand marks should not be greater than 20mm
d) The number of sand marks should not exceed 10/m²

sections.text: 3. Specifications for Electroless Nickel-Phosphorus Alloy Plating Layer (Excerpt from GB/T 13913—2008)

Electroless nickel-phosphorus alloy plating layer is usually obtained by catalytic reduction of nickel metal ions in a hot weakly acidic solution using sodium hypophosphite as a reducing agent. Since the deposited nickel-phosphorus alloy is a catalyst for the reaction, the reaction proceeds automatically. As long as the electroless plating solution circulates freely through all surfaces of irregularly shaped parts, a uniform deposited layer of the plating layer can be obtained.

The obtained plating layer is a thermodynamic metastable alloy of nickel-phosphorus supersaturated solid solution with a phosphorus content of up to 14% (mass fraction). The structure, physical and chemical properties of electroless nickel-phosphorus depend on the composition of the plating layer, the chemical composition of the electroless nickel bath, the pretreatment of the substrate, and the post-plating heat treatment.

Electroless nickel-phosphorus plating layer can improve corrosion resistance and provide wear resistance. Generally, when the phosphorus content in the plating layer increases to more than 8% (mass fraction), the corrosion resistance will be significantly improved; while as the phosphorus content in the plating layer decreases to less than 8% (mass fraction), the wear resistance will be improved. However, through appropriate heat treatment, the microhardness of the high-phosphorus content plating layer will be greatly improved, thereby improving the wear resistance of the plating layer.

(1) Wear Resistance, Thickness, and Application Conditions of Nickel-Phosphorus Plating Layer. Table 1-133 lists the minimum thickness of nickel-phosphorus plating layer with sufficient wear resistance under different usage conditions. In order to obtain the best wear resistance with the minimum thickness of nickel-phosphorus plating layer, the surface of the substrate material should be flat and free of pores. The substrate material with a surface roughness value Ra < 0.2μm can be used as a template.

Since the electroless nickel-phosphorus deposition process can be controlled to obtain a nickel-phosphorus plating layer with characteristics that meet different usage requirements, engineering technicians can specify the characteristics of the plating layer according to special requirements. Table 1-134 lists the types and phosphorus contents of nickel-phosphorus plating layers recommended for use under different conditions.

(2) Marking of Substrate Metal, Coating, and Heat Treatment Conditions

The substrate metal, coating, and heat treatment conditions should be marked on engineering drawings, purchase orders, contracts, or product specification sheets. The marking should be made in the following order: substrate metal, special alloy (optional), stress relief requirements, thickness and type of underlying layer, phosphorus content and thickness of electroless nickel-phosphorus coating, type and thickness of coating (covering) layer applied on the electroless nickel-phosphorus coating, and post-treatment (including heat treatment). Double slashes (//) will be used to indicate that a step or operation has not been listed or has been omitted.
The marking includes the following contents:

items: a) The term "electroless nickel-phosphorus coating".
b) National standard number, i.e., GB/T 13913.
c) Hyphen.
d) Chemical symbol of substrate metal (see marking of substrate metal).
e) Slash separator (/).

f) Symbol of electroless nickel-phosphorus coating (see marking of coating type and thickness), and symbols of coatings before and after electroless nickel-phosphorus (see marking of coating type and thickness), with each level in the coating sequence separated by separators in the order of operations. The coating marking should include the thickness of the coating (μm) and heat treatment requirements (see marking of heat treatment requirements).

sections.text: Example of Marking:

An electroless nickel-phosphorus coating with phosphorus content of 10% (mass fraction) and thickness of 15μm is deposited on a 16Mn steel substrate, requiring stress relief treatment at 210℃ for 22h, followed by electroplating of 0.5μm thick chromium on its surface. After chromium plating, another heat treatment for hydrogen embrittlement relief is performed at 210℃ for 22h. The specific marking is as follows:
Electroless Nickel-Phosphorus Coating GB/T 13913-Fe<16Mn>[SR(210)22]/NiP(10)15/Cr0.5[ER(210)22]

items: Marking of Substrate Metal. The substrate metal should be marked with its chemical symbol, and if it is an alloy, it should be marked with its main components. For special alloys, it is recommended to mark them with their standard names. For example, fill in its steel number or corresponding national standard in the <> symbol. Fe<16Mn> is the national standard name for low-alloy high-strength steel.
Marking of Heat Treatment Requirements. Heat treatment requirements should be marked in brackets according to the following contents.

a) SR indicates stress relief heat treatment; HT indicates heat treatment to increase coating hardness or bonding force between coating and substrate metal; ER indicates hydrogen embrittlement relief heat treatment.
b) The minimum temperature (°C) of heat treatment should be marked in parentheses.
c) The duration of heat treatment (h) should be marked.

sections.text: (3) Marking of Coating Type and Thickness. Electroless nickel-phosphorus coating should be marked with the symbol NiP, and the phosphorus content value should be filled in parentheses immediately after it, followed by the minimum local thickness of the electroless nickel-phosphorus coating in μm.

The underlying layer should be marked with the chemical symbol of the deposited metal, followed by the minimum local thickness of the coating in μm. For example, the symbol Ni indicates a nickel electroplated layer.
Other coatings deposited on the electroless nickel-phosphorus coating, such as chromium,

(3) Technical requirements for nickel-phosphorus plating

1) Appearance of the coating. The appearance of the chemical nickel-phosphorus plating on the important surface of the coating should be bright, semi-bright or matte as specified by the demander, and there should be no pinholes, bubbles, peeling, spherical growths, cracks and other defects harmful to the final finishing when inspected by naked eyes (unless otherwise required).
Bubbles or cracks that are visible to the naked eye, as well as defects caused by heat treatment, should be regarded as waste products.

2) Surface roughness of the coating. If the demander specifies the requirements for the final surface roughness, its measurement method should be carried out in accordance with the provisions of GB/T 10061.

Note: The final surface roughness of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating is not necessarily better than the surface roughness of the substrate before plating. Unless the bottom layer of the plating is particularly smooth and polished.

3) Coating thickness. The specified coating thickness in the marking part refers to its minimum local thickness. In the absence of special instructions from the demander, the minimum local thickness of the coating should be measured at any point on the important surface of the workpiece (which can be tangent to a sphere with a diameter of 20 mm).

4) Coating hardness. If a hardness value is specified, it should be measured according to the method specified in GB/T 9790. The hardness of the coating should be within ±10% of the hardness value specified by the demander.

5) Adhesion of the coating. Chemical nickel-phosphorus coating can adhere to metals with and without coating layers. According to the requirements of the demander, the coating should be able to pass one or several adhesion tests specified in GB/T 5270.

6) Porosity of the coating. If required, the maximum porosity of chemical nickel-phosphorus coating should be determined jointly according to the requirements of the demander and the test method for porosity.

7) Corrosion resistance of the coating. If required, the corrosion resistance of the coating and its test method should be specified by the demander according to the standard consistent with GB/T 6461. The test methods of GB/T 10125, acetic acid salt spray test, copper accelerated salt spray test, etc. can be specified as the test methods to evaluate the spot corrosion resistance of the coating.

8) Heat treatment to eliminate internal stress before plating. When the demander specifically indicates [see 4.1 b) in GB/T 13913—2008], steel parts with a tensile strength greater than or equal to 1000 MPa, as well as parts containing tensile stress caused by processing, friction, straightening or cold processing, need to undergo heat treatment to eliminate internal stress before cleaning and depositing metal. The heat treatment process and type to eliminate internal stress shall be specially specified by the demander, or the demander shall select a suitable process and type according to GB/T 19349. The heat treatment process to eliminate internal stress shall be carried out before any acid or cathodic electrolysis.

9) Heat treatment to eliminate hydrogen embrittlement after plating. Steel parts with a tensile strength greater than or equal to 1000 MPa, as well as parts that have undergone surface hardening treatment, need to undergo heat treatment to eliminate hydrogenation after plating according to GB/T 19350 or the relevant process specified by the demander [see 4.1 b) in GB/T 13913—2008].

All heat treatments to eliminate hydrogen embrittlement after plating should be carried out in a timely manner, preferably within 1 hour after surface finishing and before grinding and other machining, and should not exceed 3 hours at most.

The effectiveness of the hydrogen embrittlement elimination treatment should be determined through the test method specified by the demander or the test method described in the relevant standard. For example, ISO 10587 describes a test method for hydrogen embrittlement of residual stress in threaded parts, while ISO 15724 describes a test method for the concentration of diffused hydrogen in steel.

10) Heat treatment to improve coating hardness. The provisions for using heat treatment methods to provide the hardness (and wear resistance) of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating are shown in Table 1-135 [see Section 12 below].

sections.caption: Table 1-135  Recommended heat treatment methods to improve hardness and adhesion

sections.text: If necessary, the heat treatment to improve the hardness (and wear resistance) of chemical nickel-phosphorus plating should be completed within 1 hour after mechanical plating and should be carried out before machining. The duration of heat treatment should be at least 1 hour after the part reaches the specific heat treatment temperature.

If the requirements specified in GB/T 19350 are met after the heat treatment process to improve the coating hardness, there is no need to carry out the heat treatment to eliminate hydrogen embrittlement separately.

11) Heat treatment to improve coating adhesion. The heat treatment process to improve the adhesion of chemical nickel-phosphorus coating on a certain metal substrate should refer to Table 1-135, unless the demander specifically specifies other process requirements.

12) Wear resistance of the coating. If required, the demander should specify the requirements for the wear resistance of the coating and specify the test method for detecting whether the wear resistance of the coating meets the requirements.

13) Weldability of the coating. If required, the demander should specify the weldability of the coating and specify the test method for detecting whether the weldability of the coating meets the requirements.

14) Coating chemical composition. The phosphorus content in chemical nickel-phosphorus coating should be specified in the identification [see identification of coating type and thickness and Table 1-124].

15) Shot peening of metal parts. If the buyer requires shot peening (shot blasting) before coating, the shot peening process should be performed according to the requirements of GB/T 20015 before any acidic or alkaline electrolytic treatment. This standard also specifies the method for measuring shot peening intensity.

16) The nickel underlayer for electroplating should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T 12332. The chromium coating applied over the chemical nickel-phosphorus coating should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T 11379.
(4) Information to be provided by the buyer to the manufacturer

1) Essential information. When the workpiece to be ordered requires coating according to the requirements of GB/T 13993-2008 standard, the buyer should provide the following information in writing in the engineering drawing, buyer's order, and detailed production schedule for all important items:

items: a) Coating name.
b) Tensile strength of the part and any heat treatment requirements before and after coating deposition.
c) Detailed description of the main surfaces, with appropriate markings on the drawing or sample.
d) Nature, state, and surface roughness of the base metal, if any of these factors affect the usability or appearance of the coating.
e) Location, type, and dimensions of defects.
f) Surface roughness requirements.
g) Any requirements for the underlayer.

sections.text: h) Sampling method, acceptance criteria, or other inspection requirements.
i) Standard methods and special test conditions for coating thickness, hardness, adhesion, porosity, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, and weldability testing.
j) Any special requirements for stress relief treatment, such as shot peening hardening before coating.
k) Special requirements for pretreatment or restrictions on pretreatment.
l) Special requirements for heat treatment or restrictions on heat treatment.

m) Special requirements for maximum coating thickness, especially for parts subject to wear or machining. These requirements must be strictly followed whether the thickness is measured before or after coating the part.
n) Special requirements for coating (plating) on chemical nickel-phosphorus coating.
2) Supplementary information. The following supplementary information should be specified by the buyer:

items: a) Steel parts should be demagnetized before coating to minimize the entry of magnetic particles or iron filings into the coating.
b) Final surface roughness of the coating.
c) Any special requirements for the chemical composition of the coating.
d) Any special requirements for repairing non-conforming products.
e) Any other special requirements.
