sections.text: Chapter 2 Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Components
2.1 Classification and Structure of Hydraulic Cylinders
2.1.1 Types and Classification of Hydraulic Cylinders
According to their purpose or task (function or effect), hydraulic cylinders provide mechanical energy for driving linear mechanical motion.

Further classification (subdivision) of hydraulic cylinders is very difficult. So far, only JB/T 10205-2010 contains a clear classification. Other standards, such as JB/T 2184-2007, list seven types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T 17446-2012 and GB/T 17446-1998 (which has been superseded) define more than 20 types of hydraulic cylinders; GB/T 9094-2006 stipulates 64 types of hydraulic cylinder mounting styles, etc.

GB/T 13342-2007 stipulates that commonly used marine hydraulic cylinders have the following two types: plunger-type hydraulic cylinders and double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinders. However, its scope of application should only be limited to marine reciprocating hydraulic cylinders, not all hydraulic cylinders. JB/T 12706.1-2016 stipulates round-head hydraulic cylinders and square-head hydraulic cylinders; JB/T 12706.2-2017 stipulates compact square-head hydraulic cylinders.

Hydraulic cylinders can be classified by working method into two categories: single-acting cylinders and double-acting cylinders. Single-acting cylinders are cylinders where fluid can only act on the piston (or piston rod) in one direction; double-acting cylinders are cylinders where fluid force can be applied to the piston in two directions.
Hydraulic cylinders that have been defined in various standards (including superseded standards) are shown in Table 2-1.

2.1.2  Basic Structure of Standard Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Model Representation Methods for Standard Hydraulic Cylinders

The model of a hydraulic cylinder usually consists of two parts, with the first part representing the name and structural characteristics, and the second part representing the pressure parameters, main parameters, and connection and installation methods. A third part can be added in the hydraulic cylinder model to represent other characteristics and detailed descriptions.

JB/T 2184—2007 stipulates that the main parameter of a hydraulic cylinder is the cylinder bore × stroke, with both units in mm; QC/T 460—2010 stipulates that the main parameter code of a hydraulic cylinder is expressed as bore × stroke, with both units in mm. The bore of a piston cylinder refers to the inner bore of the cylinder, the bore of a plunger cylinder refers to the plunger diameter, the bore of a sleeve cylinder refers to the diameter of the first-stage sleeve extended, and the stroke refers to the total stroke.

The standard hydraulic cylinders usually referred to at least include various hydraulic cylinders listed in Table 2-6. Examples of markings for some standard hydraulic cylinders are shown in Table 2-6.

sections.text: 2. Servo hydraulic cylinder model representation method

GB/T 32216—2015 is applicable to proportional/servo-controlled piston and plunger hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil as the working medium (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic cylinders or piston cylinders, plunger cylinders). Taking the piston cylinder as an example, its composition generally should include cylinder body (barrel), piston, piston rod, cylinder head, cylinder bottom, guide sleeve, sealing device, cushioning device, exhaust device, locking and anti-loosening device, built-in (type) or external (type) sensor, etc. If the electro-hydraulic servo valve is integrated on the piston cylinder, it should also include electro-hydraulic servo valve, manifold block and piping.

The model numbers of hydraulic components are uniformly formulated using Chinese phonetic letters and Arabic numerals. The servo hydraulic cylinder model is proposed to consist of three parts, with the front part indicating the name and structural characteristics of the servo hydraulic cylinder, the middle part indicating the parameters of the servo hydraulic cylinder, and the rear part indicating other characteristics and details of the servo hydraulic cylinder.
(1) Specific content of the front part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model

1) According to JB/T 2184—2007, the first part (number) uses Arabic numerals to indicate the number of piston rods of the servo hydraulic cylinder. For example, double rod servo hydraulic cylinder and constant velocity servo hydraulic cylinder use Arabic numeral "2" to indicate the number of piston rods, and the first number of single piston rod cylinder is omitted.

2) According to JB/T 2184—2007, the code DC※G is used to indicate the name of the servo hydraulic cylinder, with the specific meaning of electro-hydraulic servo control (DC)※ hydraulic cylinder (G). The specific meaning of ※G can refer to the provisions of JB/T 2184—2007.

3) According to JB/T 2184—2007, for servo hydraulic cylinders integrated with electro-hydraulic servo valves, the composite element composed is indicated by the code DC, separated by a slash from the servo hydraulic cylinder code. If there is no electro-hydraulic servo valve, it is omitted.

4) Referring to the provisions of JB/T 2184—2007 on structural codes, the piston rod sealing type is used as the structural characteristic. The gap seal code is specified as 01, the seal (ring) seal code is 02, and the code for other seal types is 03, but the current formulation does not follow the order of servo hydraulic cylinder finalization.
(2) Specific content of the middle part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model

1) According to JB/T 2184—2007, the rated pressure or nominal pressure value of the servo hydraulic cylinder should generally comply with GB/T 2346, and the code should follow JB/T 2184—2007, with special provision 21MPa indicated by code F1.

2) According to JB/T 2184—2007, the bore×stroke of the hydraulic cylinder is its main parameter. However, in the servo hydraulic cylinder numbering, the bore/piston rod diameter×maximum cylinder stroke value (Arabic numerals) is used to indicate, and it should generally comply with GB/T 2348 and GB 2349.

3) According to JB/T 2184—2007, the connection and installation method should be indicated by uppercase Chinese phonetic letters. However, in the servo hydraulic cylinder numbering, the installation code should generally follow GB/T 9094—2006, instead of JB/T 2184—2007.
(3) Specific content of other characteristics of the rear part of the servo hydraulic cylinder model

1) Referring to the provisions of JB/T 2184—2007 on the stroke end damping code, the code ZC is used to indicate that a fixed cushioning device is installed at the stroke end of the servo hydraulic cylinder, and the code ZT is used to indicate that an adjustable cushioning device is installed. If no cushioning device is installed at the stroke end of the servo hydraulic cylinder, it is omitted.

2) The Chinese phonetic letter NZ is used to indicate a servo hydraulic cylinder with a built-in (type) sensor, and the letter WZ is used to indicate a servo hydraulic cylinder with an external (type) sensor.

sections.text: 3. Hydraulic Cylinder Structural Features
Determined according to design requirements and manufacturer specifications.
(1) Hydraulic Cylinder Structural Features

In the first part of the hydraulic cylinder model composition, the first digit indicates the number of piston rods or the number of stages of a telescopic cylinder (omitted for single piston rod cylinders).

Hydraulic cylinders with the same name and main parameters but different structures are represented by sequential Arabic numerals based on the order of finalization. Generally including: 1) Cylinder end connection structure; 2) Piston structure and connection structure; 3) Piston rod structure; 4) Cylinder head structure; 5) Cylinder bottom structure; 6) Guide sleeve structure; 7) Sealing structure; 8) Cushioning structure; 9) Exhaust gas structure; 10) Locking and anti-loosening structure; 11) Connection and installation structure; 12) Oil port structure; 13) Other structures, such as travel (external extension) limit, positioning, adjustment, as well as integrated transmission, control, sensing, signal, medium pollution degree control, energy conversion and other components, accessories, assemblies or devices.

For hydraulic cylinders, its control mainly targets the working chamber (such as rodless and rod cavities) pressure, movable parts (such as pistons and piston rods) speed (including direction), cylinder stroke (such as maximum stroke and adjustable stroke) (or including direction) control; energy conversion includes gas-liquid and electro-hydraulic conversion.
More detailed structural features may also include material and mechanical properties, heat treatment, surface treatment, corrosion prevention, anti-pollution, etc.
(2) Drawing Design for Various Standard Hydraulic Cylinders

1) Drawing design for hydraulic cylinders in Appendix A (Normative Appendix) of JB/T 2162-2007. The standard drawing design for the circumferential distribution positions of oil inlet and outlet holes, fixed bolts, exhaust valves, gland plates, and brackets for hydraulic cylinders shall be in accordance with the provisions of Drawing A1 and Table A.1 of this standard. When selecting, except for the positions of the exhaust valve and fixed bolts which are fixed, the positions of oil inlet and outlet holes and their connecting threads can be determined through consultation with the manufacturer as needed.

2) Drawing design for hydraulic cylinders in JB/ZQ4181-2006. U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) with rear end clevis type (WE type) shall be in accordance with Drawing 1 of this standard, front flange type (TF type) U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) shall be in accordance with Drawing 2 of this standard, rear flange type (WF type) U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) shall be in accordance with Drawing 3 of this standard, intermediate fixed trunnion type (ZB type) U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) shall be in accordance with Drawing 4 of this standard, front fixed trunnion type (TB type) U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) shall be in accordance with Drawing 5 of this standard, end foot bracket type (JG type) U-type hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment (PN≤25MPa) shall be in accordance with Drawing 6 of this standard.

3) Drawing design for hydraulic cylinders in Appendix A (Normative Appendix) of JB/T6134-2006. The standard drawing design for the circumferential distribution positions of oil inlet and outlet holes, fixed bolts, exhaust valves, gland plates, and brackets for hydraulic cylinders shall comply with the following provisions: ① When the cylinder bore D=40~200mm, it shall be in accordance with Drawing A.1 and Table A.1 of this standard; ② When the cylinder bore D=220~320mm, it shall be in accordance with Drawing A.2 and Table A.2 of this standard; ③ When selecting, except for the positions of the exhaust valve and fixed bolts which are fixed, the positions of the buffer valve, check valve, oil inlet and outlet holes can be determined through consultation with the manufacturer as needed.
In addition to the above several hydraulic cylinder standards, there are also some drawings in standards such as JB/T11588-2013 and CB/T3812-2013 that can be referred to during design.
2.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Parameters and Parameter Calculation
2.2.1 Hydraulic Cylinder Parameters and Main Parameters
JB/T10205-2010 stipulates that the basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders should include cylinder bore, piston rod diameter (outer), nominal pressure, stroke, and installation dimensions.

In addition to the basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders stipulated in JB/T10205-2010, there are also standards for nominal pressure thrust and pull force, piston speed, rated pressure, minimum piston rod diameter (outer), plunger diameter for plunger type hydraulic cylinders, extreme or maximum stroke, area ratio of two chambers, threaded oil port and nominal diameter of oil port, piston rod and cylinder outer diameter, piston rod end connection type, piston structure, etc. in other hydraulic cylinder and related standards.

Strictly speaking, if the above formula is calculated using nominal pressure, it should be the theoretical output thrust of the cylinder under this nominal pressure value.
(2) Calculation Formula for Cylinder Motion Resistance

The actual output force of the cylinder is less than the theoretical output force of the cylinder, because the resistance caused by back pressure, friction, and the influence of leakage is ignored when calculating the theoretical output force of the cylinder. The calculation formula for cylinder motion resistance is:
F = F₁ + F₂ + F₃ ± F₄ ± F₅  (2-4)

Where: F — Total resistance of cylinder motion, or all external loads converted to the piston (piston rod), unit: N; F₁ — External load resistance including external friction force, mainly composed of the friction resistance of moving parts connected to the cylinder and the reaction force of the driven external load, with a value equal to the actual output force of the cylinder, unit: N; F₂ — Friction resistance of the sealing device or system of the hydraulic cylinder, generally estimated as 4% of the theoretical output force of the cylinder, unit: N; F₃ — Resistance caused by back pressure, including the buffering pressure generated when the hydraulic cylinder with buffer enters the buffering state, unit: N; F₄ — The gravity of the cylinder and the moving parts connected to the cylinder, converted to the cylinder axis line, in formula (2-4), when the gravity is opposite to the direction of motion, take '+'; when the gravity is the same as the direction of motion, take '−', F₄ = mg, unit: N; F₅ — When the hydraulic cylinder starts, brakes or changes direction, the inertia resistance of the cylinder and the moving parts connected to the cylinder, converted to the piston (piston rod), in formula (2-4), when accelerating and starting, take '+'; when decelerating and braking, take '−', F₅ = ma, unit: N.

Where: m — Mass of the cylinder and the moving parts connected to the cylinder, converted to the piston (piston rod), unit: kg; g — Acceleration of gravity, gₙ = 9.80665 m/s²; a — Acceleration, uniform motion a = 0, unit: m/s². (7) Cylinder output force efficiency calculation formula

The output force efficiency of the cylinder is the ratio of the actual output force of the cylinder to the theoretical output force. In hydraulic cylinders and their related standards, this quantity is also called "load efficiency".

where η — Cylinder output force efficiency or load efficiency; F₁ — Actual output force of the cylinder, unit: N; F — Theoretical output force of the cylinder, unit: N; p — Rated pressure including a nominal pressure value, unit: MPa; A — Effective area of the cylinder, respectively the effective area of the rodless chamber, the effective area of the rod chamber and the area of the piston rod, etc., unit: mm².
In hydraulic cylinders and their related standards, the load efficiency of hydraulic cylinders shall not be lower than 90%.
Note: The actual output force F₁ of the cylinder should generally be measured when the hydraulic cylinder is horizontally installed and the cylinder process moves at a constant speed (medium).
(8) Cylinder efficiency calculation formula

The hydraulic cylinder is a device that converts fluid energy into linear mechanical work, so there is an energy conversion (hydraulic transmission) efficiency problem. The total efficiency ηₜ of a general hydraulic cylinder consists of the following efficiencies:

items: Mechanical efficiency ηₘ. Energy loss caused by friction resistance generated by the sealing device of the hydraulic cylinder or the system, generally the mechanical efficiency ηₘ ≥ 90% of the hydraulic cylinder.

Volumetric efficiency ηᵥ. Due to the leakage of the sealing device or system of the hydraulic cylinder, especially when using piston ring sealing, the leakage is greater, generally the volumetric efficiency ηᵥ ≥ 98% of the hydraulic cylinder.

sections.text: 3) Hydraulic pressure efficiency ηᵧ. Due to the hydraulic pressure loss of the hydraulic cylinder, such as the hydraulic pressure acting on the effective area of the cylinder needs to overcome the resistance generated by the back pressure or cushioning pressure.
Taking the double-acting single piston rod hydraulic cylinder with back pressure p₁ as an example, its hydraulic (thrust) efficiency during the cylinder process is
ηᵧ = (pA₁ - p₁A₂)/(pA₁) × 100%    (2-17)
Its hydraulic (pull) efficiency during the cylinder return stroke is
ηᵧ = (pA₂ - p₁A₁)/(pA₂) × 100%    (2-18)

where ηᵧ — Hydraulic pressure efficiency; p — Nominal pressure (oil inlet pressure), unit: MPa; p₁ — Back pressure (oil outlet pressure), unit: MPa; A₁ — Effective area of the rodless chamber, A₁ = (π/4)D², unit: mm²; A₂ — Effective area of the rod chamber, A₂ = (π/4)(D² - d²), unit: mm²; D — Cylinder (inner) diameter, unit: mm; d — Piston rod diameter, unit: mm.
Then the total efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder is
ηₜ = ηₘηᵥηᵧ    (2-19)

Note: The total efficiency (value) of the hydraulic cylinder is definitely lower than the output force efficiency (value) of the cylinder, and it is not a parameter specified in the current hydraulic cylinder and its related standards, but it is necessary for the design of hydraulic systems with hydraulic cylinders as actuators.

a) When the piston rod is in a stable state and only bears axial load (ignoring its own gravity), it is calculated according to the simple tensile (compression) strength condition:

Where: σ — The maximum tensile (compressive) stress on the dangerous section under normal temperature and static load action, in MPa; σₚ — Allowable stress of material, in MPa; σₛ — Yield point, in MPa; n — Safety factor. Next, take the stability verification of the 6.3m shield advancing hydraulic cylinder piston rod given in reference [76] as an example.

When the supporting length LB of the hydraulic cylinder is ≥ (10~15)d, the bending stability of the piston rod needs to be checked. The schematic diagram of a straight rod under eccentric load is shown in Figure 2-1. According to the theory of material mechanics, a compressed straight rod will lose stability when its axial load F exceeds the critical load Fk. For hydraulic cylinders, the stability safety system nk also needs to be considered. Therefore, the stability condition for a compressed piston rod is:
F ≤ Fk/nk
Where: Fk — critical load of hydraulic cylinder; nk — stability safety factor, generally taken as nk = 2-4.

(5) Explanation

When choosing to comply with the "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard, the following explanation should be used in the test report, product catalog, and sales documents: "The hydraulic cylinder products of our company comply with the provisions of JB/T 10205—2010 'Hydraulic Cylinder'."

Note: 1) If possible, the GB 2880 standard should be eliminated from the technical requirements of the hydraulic cylinder, and standards such as GB/T 3452.3—2005, GB/T 15242.3—1994, etc. should be added. 2) The working medium temperature is preferably stipulated through the technical agreement as -20~65°C. 3) The factory test is preferably stipulated through the technical agreement to be conducted at room temperature. 4) Green manufacturing and remanufacturing should be appropriately added when drafting and revising the standard to adapt to environmental protection and circular economy requirements. 5) Hydraulic cylinders with special (product) standards are excluded. 6) The aforementioned documents are often used as one of the technical documents provided by the hydraulic cylinder manufacturer to the buyer.
2.3.2 Technical requirements for proportional/servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders
1. Product classification, marking, and basic parameters
(1) Classification

Electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders (hereinafter referred to as servo hydraulic cylinders or hydraulic cylinders) are classified into two types based on the working mode: single-acting servo hydraulic cylinders and double-acting piston-type servo hydraulic cylinders.
(2) Marking

items: Servo hydraulic cylinder model. See the servo hydraulic cylinder model representation method in Section 2.1.2.
Servo hydraulic cylinder marking example. See the servo hydraulic cylinder model representation method in Section 2.1.2.

sections.text: (3) Basic parameters

The basic parameters of the servo hydraulic cylinder should include the cylinder (bore) diameter, piston rod diameter, rated (or nominal) pressure, maximum cylinder stroke, mounting dimensions, etc., and may also include the minimum (temperature) speed, maximum speed, command rated value (such as rated current), sensor parameters, etc.
2. Structure

items: The connecting screws and bolts used for the connection parts of the cylinder body (barrel) in the servo hydraulic cylinder should not be lower than grade 8.8 specified in GB/T 3098.1—2000; the technical requirements for double-ended studs and nuts used for clamping and/or assembly between the cylinder head, cylinder body (barrel), and cylinder bottom are shown in Section 3.17.3 Cylinder assembly double-ended studs and tightening torque.
A cushioning device and a gas discharge device may be installed in the servo hydraulic cylinder as required.
The servo hydraulic cylinder should have anti-rotation features.
The strength of the weld seam should not be lower than that of the base material.

The sealing elements in the servo hydraulic cylinder should be able to withstand high temperature, corrosion, aging, hydrolysis, and have good sealing performance, with small static and dynamic friction forces, and can meet both the sealing requirements of the hydraulic oil and the application environment.

Servo hydraulic cylinders with a mass greater than 15 kg should preferably be equipped with lifting devices for lifting equipment, or the servo hydraulic cylinder should be provided with lifting points, and the set lifting points should be able to withstand a force of 4 times the lifting weight without damage.

sections.text: 3. Requirements
(1) Appearance requirements
The appearance quality of the servo hydraulic cylinder should meet the following requirements:

items: The servo hydraulic cylinder should not have defects such as burrs, bumps, scratches, rust, etc. The coating should not have defects such as pitting, blistering, peeling, or other defects harmful to the surface finish.
The surface of castings and forgings should be smooth and free of defects.
The weld seam should be flat, uniform, and beautiful, and should not have slag, spatter, etc.
For servo hydraulic cylinders with a flange structure, the radial misalignment of the two flange joint surfaces should not be greater than 0.1 mm.
External components should undergo anti-rust treatment, or be treated with anti-corrosion treatment such as coating, passivation layer, paint layer, etc.

The external surface of the servo hydraulic cylinder should be derusted or have the oxide layer removed before painting, and should not have rust pits; the paint layer should be smooth and uniform, and should not have defects such as pimples.

8) Appropriate sealing, dust-proofing, leak-proofing, and protection measures should be taken for oil inlet/outlet and external connection surfaces.
(2) Materials
The main component materials for servo hydraulic cylinders are shown in Table 2-22. Other materials with performance not lower than that specified in Table 2-22 can also be used.

The cylinder body (tube) should undergo 100% ultrasonic testing and should reach Grade I specified in NB/T 47013.3—2015.
(3) Environmental Conditions
Generally, the working environmental temperature of the servo hydraulic cylinder should be within -25 to 65°C, and the working medium temperature should be within -20 to 80°C.
(4) Contamination Level of Working Medium
The solid particle contamination level code of the working medium in the servo hydraulic cylinder cavity should not be higher than -/17/14 specified in GB/T 14039—2002.
(5) Pressure Resistance

The pressure cavity of the servo hydraulic cylinder should be able to withstand 1.5 times its rated (nominal) pressure, maintain pressure for at least 5 minutes, and all cylinder components should not have permanent deformation or damage. The outer surface of the cylinder body (tube) and welds should not have leakage.
(6) Sealing

The servo hydraulic cylinder should have no external leakage at all joint surfaces under 1.25 times the rated (nominal) pressure for at least 5 minutes. The leakage and low-pressure leakage of the servo hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of 6.2.2, 6.2.3, and 6.2.4 in JB/T 10205—2010.
(7) Starting Pressure
The starting pressure of the servo hydraulic cylinder should generally be less than or equal to 0.5MPa. Those with a starting pressure not exceeding 0.3MPa are low-friction servo hydraulic cylinders.
(8) Friction Force During Loaded Operation
Under simulated actual operating conditions, the maximum friction force during loaded operation of the servo hydraulic cylinder should be less than 2% of its rated load.
(9) Output Force Efficiency (Load Efficiency) The output force efficiency of the servo hydraulic cylinder should not be less than 90%.

(10) Minimum Speed When the cylinder diameter is less than or equal to 200mm, the minimum speed at which the servo hydraulic cylinder can run smoothly should not exceed 4mm/s; when the cylinder diameter is greater than 200mm, the minimum speed at which the servo hydraulic cylinder can run smoothly should not exceed 5mm/s; or refer to the relevant provisions in Section 3.3.2.

(11) Maximum Speed The maximum speed of the servo hydraulic cylinder is often limited by the piston rod and/or piston seal system and seal ring material. The maximum speed at which the servo hydraulic cylinder can run smoothly can be agreed upon by the manufacturer and user, or refer to the relevant provisions in Section 3.3.2.
(12) Durability The servo hydraulic cylinder should have a cumulative stroke of not less than 10⁵m under rated operating conditions.

(13) Frequency Response The frequency response index of the servo hydraulic cylinder (amplitude-frequency bandwidth and phase-frequency bandwidth, or the lower of the two indices) can be agreed upon by the manufacturer and user, or should meet the design requirements.
(14) Step Response The step response index of the servo hydraulic cylinder (step response time) can be agreed upon by the manufacturer and user, or should meet the design requirements.
2.3.3 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders Integrated with Electro-hydraulic Servo Valves

The exact meaning of a hydraulic cylinder integrated with an electro-hydraulic servo valve is an integrated combination mechanism of an electro-hydraulic servo valve, hydraulic cylinder, and other components/accessories. For details, refer to the definitions of "servo actuator" and "servo hydraulic cylinder" in QJ 1495.

The following technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders integrated with electro-hydraulic servo valves only include the contents different from the general technical requirements for electro-hydraulic servo valve-controlled hydraulic cylinders.
1. General Requirements
(1) Nominal Pressure or Rated Pressure The rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 2-23.

sections.text: (2) Thread Size of Oil Port Connection For newly developed servo hydraulic cylinders, the oil port should take anti-mistake measures in structural design, i.e., using pipe fittings with different calibers to prevent reverse installation (see GJB 1482—1992).

sections.text: (3) General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Components

1) The hydraulic components, piping, and oil passages integrated with the servo hydraulic cylinder should be able to withstand 1.5 times the rated (nominal) pressure of the servo hydraulic cylinder, maintain pressure for at least 5 minutes, and should not exhibit external leakage, permanent deformation, or damage. The outer surfaces of metal parts and weld seams should not show seepage. If no special requirements exist, the electro-hydraulic servo valve integrated with the servo hydraulic cylinder should not undergo a pressure test at 1.3 times its rated pressure again.

2) The hydraulic components and piping integrated with the servo hydraulic cylinder should preferably use products specified in current standards, and their (safety) technical requirements should comply with relevant standard regulations.

(4) Special Requirements: Products with special technical requirements should be negotiated between the user and manufacturer, such as impedance characteristics requirements, working mode requirements, electromagnetic compatibility requirements, reliability, maintainability and detectability requirements, quality assurance requirements, etc.
2. Dimensional, Weight, and Structural Requirements
(1) Dimensions

The external dimensions of newly developed hydraulic cylinders should be equal to or smaller than those of the same type and specification of hydraulic cylinders currently in service. When modifying the design of cylinder parts, structural elements for installation should not be arbitrarily changed. Connectors should be the same as those of electro-hydraulic servo valves currently in service. It is recommended to select plugs and sockets specified in GJB 599A.
The length of the servo hydraulic cylinder includes the length in the fully extended state, neutral position, and fully retracted state.
(2) Structure

1) Under the premise of meeting functional and performance requirements, the structural design of the hydraulic cylinder should be as simple as possible to ensure the safety and reliability of the host machine and minimize maintenance workload.

2) The piping between the electro-hydraulic servo valve and the hydraulic cylinder should be as short as possible and should preferably use rigid pipes; the pipe diameter should be as small as possible while meeting the maximum instantaneous flow rate requirements.
3) Pressure measurement points should comply with the provisions of 7.2 in GB/T 28782.2-2012.

4) When sensors, etc. have requirements for preventing relative rotation between the cylinder body and piston rod, the hydraulic cylinder and its installation and connection should be designed (arranged) with structures or mechanisms to prevent relative rotation between the cylinder body and piston rod.
3. Dynamic Performance Requirements
The response frequency of the servo valve should be more than 3 times the highest test frequency of the hydraulic cylinder.

The resonance frequency of the hydraulic cylinder used for dynamic testing of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should be more than 3 times the rated amplitude-frequency bandwidth of the tested electro-hydraulic servo valve.
2.3.4 Safety Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders

The design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders must provide basic safety assurance for users' use within the specified service life. Any hydraulic machinery may pose dangers during adjustment, use, and maintenance, so users can only adjust, use, and maintain the hydraulic cylinder according to the safety technical conditions or requirements of that hydraulic machinery to reduce or eliminate dangers.

The following requirements are proposed for hydraulic cylinders, some of which depend on the dangers of the machine in which the hydraulic system is installed. Therefore, the final technical specifications and structure of the required hydraulic system and hydraulic cylinder will depend on the risk assessment and the agreement between the manufacturer and user, but generally should follow:
1) Hydraulic cylinders used in special occasions should undergo risk assessment during design.
2) Measures should be taken to reduce risks during design and manufacture, such as reliable anti-loosening measures for various fasteners.

3) For unavoidable dangers in the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders, such as unexpected stroke and accidental falling of the slider driven by the hydraulic cylinder, the host manufacturer should take safety protection measures, including wind (danger) warnings.
4) More specific safety technical requirements (conditions) should be followed according to relevant standards.
1. Applicability

1) Anti-instability. To avoid bending or instability of the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder at any position, attention should be paid to the stroke length, load, and installation type of the hydraulic cylinder.
2) Structural design. The design of the hydraulic cylinder should consider the predetermined maximum load and pressure peak.

3) Installation rated values. When determining all rated loads of the hydraulic cylinder, its installation type should be considered. Because the rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder only reflects the pressure-bearing capacity of the cylinder body, it cannot reflect the force transmission capacity of the installation structure.

4) Loads caused by limit positions. When the hydraulic cylinder is used as a limiter, the size of the hydraulic cylinder and its installation type should be determined based on the maximum load caused by the limited component.

5) Impact and vibration resistance. Any components and accessories installed on or connected to the hydraulic cylinder should be installed or connected in a way that prevents loosening due to impact and vibration during use.

6) Accidental pressurization. Measures should be taken in the hydraulic system to prevent accidental pressure increase caused by the effective piston area difference, so that it does not exceed the rated pressure. Attention should also be paid to the fact that due to the area ratio of the hydraulic cylinder and the influence of pressure reduction, the maximum flow rate through the return oil filter of the hydraulic system where the hydraulic cylinder is located may be greater than the maximum flow rate of the pump.
2. Installation and Adjustment

The best installation method for the hydraulic cylinder is to have the reaction force generated by the load act along the centerline of the hydraulic cylinder. The installation of the hydraulic cylinder should minimize (reduce) the following situations:
1) Excessive deformation of the hydraulic cylinder structure due to thrust or tension of the load.
2) Causing lateral or bending loads.
3) The rotation speed of articulated installation types (which may force the adoption of
(Continuous external lubrication).
(1) Installation Position

The mounting face should not cause deformation of the hydraulic cylinder, and should allow for thermal expansion. The installation position of the hydraulic cylinder should be easily accessible for maintenance, adjustment of cushioning devices, and replacement of complete assemblies.
(2) Fastening Hardware

The selection and installation of fastening hardware for the hydraulic cylinder and its accessories should be able to withstand all foreseeable forces. For foot-mounted hydraulic cylinders, the mounting bolts may be subjected to shear forces. If shear loads are involved, consider using hydraulic cylinders with mechanisms designed to withstand shear loads. The fastening hardware used for installation should be sufficient to withstand overturning moments.
3. Cushions and Deceleration Devices
When internal cushioning is used, the design of the hydraulic cylinder should consider the effects of load deceleration on pressure increases.
4. Adjustable Stroke End Stops
Measures should be taken to prevent loosening of externally or internally adjustable stroke end stops.
5. Piston Stroke
The stroke length (including tolerances) should be specified according to the application of the hydraulic system if not prescribed in the relevant standards.
Tolerances for stroke length are given in JB/T 10205-2010.
6. Piston Rod
(1) Materials, Surface Treatment and Protection
Appropriate materials and surface treatments should be selected for the piston rod to minimize wear, corrosion, and foreseeable impact damage.
The piston rod should be protected from foreseeable damage such as indentations, scratches, and corrosion, which can be achieved using protective covers.
(2) Assembly
For assembly, piston rods with threaded ends should have a structure that allows a wrench to apply counterforce, as per ISO 4395. The piston should be reliably fixed to the piston rod.
7. Maintenance of Sealing Devices and Wearing Parts
Sealing devices and other wearing parts intended for scheduled maintenance should be easily replaceable.
8. Single-Acting Piston Hydraulic Cylinders
Single-acting piston hydraulic cylinders should be designed with a vent port, positioned appropriately to prevent ejected fluid from creating a hazard to personnel.
9. Replacement
Integral hydraulic cylinders should be avoided where possible, but when used, wear-prone parts should be replaceable.
10. Gas Venting
(1) Venting Position

When installing hydraulic cylinders on stationary industrial machinery, they should be positioned to allow automatic venting or provide an easily accessible external vent port. During installation, the vent port of the hydraulic cylinder should be in the highest position. If these requirements cannot be met, relevant maintenance and usage documentation should be provided.
(2) Vent Port
Hydraulic cylinders with a pressurized cavity should be designed or equipped with a vent port to prevent hazards. The hydraulic cylinder should be able to vent air safely through the vent port.
2.4 Design of Hydraulic Cylinder Barrel (Tube)

The barrel is the body of the hydraulic cylinder. In a broad sense, the hydraulic cylinder barrel refers to all pressure-bearing components that can form this special sealed pressure vessel, which almost includes all components that make up the hydraulic cylinder. In a narrow sense, the hydraulic cylinder barrel refers to the hollow pressure-bearing part in which the piston and/or piston rod moves reciprocally. The barrel can be closed at one end or open at both ends. The tubular body barrel that is open at both ends is called a cylinder tube.
The barrel is one of the main components of the hydraulic cylinder, and it must be processed using specified materials and meet specific technical requirements.

The barrel referred to in this manual is the narrow sense of the hydraulic cylinder barrel, with a circular inner hole, but not necessarily tubular. Both end faces must be perpendicular to the center (axis) of the inner hole.
Note: 1. It is more appropriate to understand the hydraulic cylinder barrel (tube) as a metal pressure shell. Refer to GB/T 19934.1-2005 for details.
2. In JB/T 12706.1-2016 and JB/T 12706.2-2017, the so-called "square head hydraulic cylinder" has a barrel cross-section that can be either square outer with round inner or cylindrical.
2.4.1 General Provisions

The hydraulic cylinder barrel (tube) should have sufficient strength, stiffness, plasticity, and impact toughness. For barrels (tubes) that require later welding of the bottom (end cap), the material (same steel or different steel as the bottom) should have good weldability (such as 35 steel), and the weld strength should not be lower than the strength of the base material. The weld quality should meet the requirements of Class II in GB/T 3323. The raised part of the hydraulic cylinder port (pipe connection) and the bottom (end cap) should be welded synchronously.
For hydraulic cylinders with requirements for wear resistance or corrosion resistance on the barrel bore, a liner structure made of suitable materials can be used inside the bore.
Various barrel (tube) structures are shown in Section 4.9 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection Reference Drawings.
Barrels (tubes) of hydraulic cylinders with the same model produced by the same manufacturer must have interchangeability.
During the design process, the barrel (tube) should be designed with remanufacturing capability, meaning the cylinder tube should have inherent remanufacturing capability.
For hydraulic cylinders used in special occasions, a risk assessment should be conducted on the barrel (tube) during the design phase.
2.4.2 Materials
For hydraulic cylinders or host machines with product standards, the materials should be specified in the product standards or host machine standards.

Due to the slightly lower mechanical properties of 20 steel and the inability to be quenched and tempered, it is less commonly used.

When conducting hydraulic cylinder pressure tests, the cylinder body (tube) should be guaranteed not to produce permanent deformation. Under the rated static pressure, any failure mode of the tested pressure cavity as specified in JB/T 5924-1991 "Test Methods for Rated Fatigue Pressure and Rated Static Pressure of Pressure Cavities of Hydraulic Components" (already repealed) should not occur.

For the cylinder body (tube) material of hydraulic cylinders operating in an environment with a temperature lower than -50°C, 35 and 45 steel that has been quenched and tempered or low-temperature steel must be selected.

For hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses, some standards stipulate the use of large carbon steel forgings or large alloy steel forgings. For example, JB/T 12510-2015 stipulates: The main cylinder and return cylinder are generally manufactured using carbon structural steel forgings as specified in JB/T 6397, or can also be manufactured using the method of welding split forgings. The forgings should be quenched and tempered, and appropriate materials and σs values should be selected based on calculated stress, with a safety factor not less than 3. The chemical composition and mechanical properties of the materials should comply with the provisions of the selected material standards, and the inspection items and sampling quantities should comply with the provisions of level V acceptance grouping of forgings in JB/T 5000.8-2007, and tangential mechanical properties σs, ReL, A, Z, and K should be tested piece by piece.

JB/T 5924-1991 "Test Methods for Rated Fatigue Pressure and Rated Static Pressure of Pressure Cavities of Hydraulic Components" was repealed on May 12, 2017, but so far there is no other standard that stipulates the failure mode of this "pressure cavity" or "pressure shell" of hydraulic cylinders, so it is temporarily expressed as above. In GB/T 19934.1-2005 "Fatigue Pressure Test of Metal Pressure Shells in Hydraulic Transmission - Part 1: Test Methods", the failure criteria are stipulated as: ① Any external leakage caused by fatigue; ② Any internal leakage caused by fatigue; ③ Material separation (such as cracks). However, whether it is completely applicable to hydraulic cylinders is a question.
2.4.3  Heat Treatment

Castings and forgings used to manufacture the cylinder body (tube) should adopt heat treatment or other methods to eliminate internal stress. Forgings of forged steel (cast steel), high-quality carbon structural steel, and alloy structural steel used to manufacture the cylinder body (tube) should be quenched and tempered before or after rough machining. 45 steel should be quenched and tempered to 250-280 HBW.

The heat treatment of the cylinder body (tube) can be expressed as: it should be quenched and tempered before or after machining. The cylinder tube that complies with the provisions of JB/T 11718-2013 should be given special instructions on the heat treatment state of the delivered cylinder tube by the supplier according to the requirements of the demander at the time of delivery, as agreed upon by both parties. Reference literature [115] and the previous edition give: Heat treatment: quenching and tempering, hardness 241-285 HBW.

In JB/T 8491.1-2008 "Heat Treatment Technical Conditions for Machine Tool Parts - Part 1: Annealing, Normalizing, Quenching and Tempering", the quenching and tempering hardness of 45 steel is stipulated as 200-230 HBW, 220-250 HBW, 250-280 HBW, and 270-300 HBW respectively.
Warning: The cylinder body (tube) must not undergo integral heat treatment with process codes 513 or 513- as specified in GB/T 12603 or GB/T 16924.

For cylinder tubes that use the cylinder tubes specified in JB/T 11718-2013 or other standards with the inner hole surface already finished, and for cylinder bodies (tubes) connected to the cylinder bottom (end cover) by welding, heat treatment cannot be used to eliminate internal stress. Methods such as vibration aging and static pressure stretching can be tried to eliminate internal stress, and the adopted method should be verified for process verification.
2.4.4  Geometric Dimensions and Geometric Tolerances
(1) Basic Dimensions

The basic dimensions of the cylinder body include the cylinder bore, the position of the cylinder inner hole, the outer shape of the cylinder body, the length of the cylinder body (inner hole), and the size of the oil port; for a tubular cylinder body with the inner hole and outer circle concentric, the basic dimensions of the cylinder tube include the cylinder bore, the outer diameter of the cylinder tube or the wall thickness of the cylinder tube (preferably the wall thickness of the cylinder tube), and the length of the cylinder tube.
(2) Cylinder Bore
1) The cylinder bore should prioritize the recommended sizes in Table 2-24.
For large hydraulic cylinders with a cylinder bore not less than 630 mm, the cylinder bore should prioritize the recommended sizes in Table 2-25.

2) The dimensional tolerance of the cylinder bore should preferably adopt H8 (or H7 or H6) as specified in GB/T 1801-2009; for cylinder tubes used in medium and low pressure or long cylinders, H9 or H10 as specified in GB/T 1801-2009 can also be used.
