4) Select the cross-sectional diameter d₂ of the O-ring according to the applicable range of the O-ring (see Table 2-75), and the O-ring selection is complete.
5) Decide whether to install a retaining ring and select the groove width based on pressure, clearance, etc., and determine the retaining ring thickness and tolerance.
6) Design the radial depth t of the groove according to the pressure condition and considering the compression rate of the O-ring (refer to Table 2-72, etc.).

7) Calculate the inner or outer diameter of the retaining ring according to the radial depth t of the groove, determine the inner and outer diameters and tolerances of the retaining ring, and the retaining ring design is complete.
8) Design and select the minimum chamfer length Zₘᵢₙ, groove bottom fillet radius r₁, groove edge fillet radius r₂, etc., according to the standard recommended groove dimensions.
9) Select the surface roughness values of the groove faces, mating part surfaces, and chamfer surfaces according to Table 2-78.

10) Design and determine the groove dimensional tolerances and geometric (concentricity) tolerances according to relevant technical requirements, calculate the limit dimensions of t' and g, and check the compression rate, and the groove design is complete.
11) Draw part and assembly drawings.
12) Overall evaluation and review of sealing performance. For further information on the design of O-ring grooves and retaining rings for O-rings, see Section 2.10.5.12.

(4) Selection of O-rings. The selection of O-rings should first consider the material of the O-ring according to the specified working conditions, taking into account the nature of the hydraulic transmission medium, working temperature range, sealing properties, sealing type, nominal pressure range, etc., and especially the reciprocating motion speed. If the selected O-ring is not used in petroleum-based hydraulic working media, or the working temperature is not within the range of -40~125°C, it may not be easily available on the market. For example, seals on hydraulic support (cylinder) and cylinders using phosphate ester flame-retardant hydraulic fluid in mines using emulsion require customization or purchase from the manufacturer.

When selecting the cross-sectional size of the O-ring, a larger cross-section O-ring should be preferred. Larger cross-section O-rings are less prone to twisting and extrusion. GB/T 3452.3-2005 "O-ring Groove for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Use" provides the applicable range of different cross-section O-rings for static and dynamic seals, see Table 2-75.

sections.text: 2. Y-shaped rubber seal rings and their grooves
(1) Sealing mechanism, classification and characteristics of Y-ring

1) Sealing mechanism of Y-ring. As shown in Figure 2-21, the natural state of Y-ring is that the sealing lip is open, and the lip part is large; after being installed into the sealing groove, the lip part becomes smaller, and the lip part is attached to the sealing surface, but the contact force is very small; when the sealed working medium is filled into the lip part, with the increase of pressure, the lip part and the sealing surface contact becomes wider, and the contact force increases, which is also the self-sealing ability of Y-ring mentioned earlier: that is, with the increase of the pressure of the sealed working medium, the sealing ability also increases accordingly. But it does not mean that the working pressure can be increased infinitely, generally the maximum working pressure of Y-ring does not exceed 25 MPa. With the increase of pressure, the friction force and wear are also increasing.

2) Classification of Y-ring. As shown in Figure 2-22, GB/T 10708.1-2000 "Rubber seal rings for reciprocating motion - Part 1: One-way seal rubber seal rings" specifies two types of Y-rings for L₁ sealing grooves, namely the piston L₁ sealing groove shown in Figure 2-22a and the rod L₁ sealing groove shown in Figure 2-22b.

Y-ring for L1 seal groove is an equal-lip Y-ring, while Y-ring for L2 seal groove is an unequal-lip Y-ring.

3) Characteristics of Y-ring. Compared with O-ring, the most significant feature of Y-ring is its small starting friction, and its service life and sealing performance are also higher than those of O-ring. Compared with V-ring, its friction is smaller than that of V-ring, and its sealing is better than that of V-ring. In summary, Y-ring has the following characteristics:

sections.text: (2) Sealing design of Y-ring. The sealing design of Y-ring is mainly the design of sealing groove. According to the working conditions and structural requirements, choose whether to use Y-ring for L1 seal groove or Y-ring for L2 seal groove, and whether to use retaining ring. In practice, Y-ring for L2 seal groove is used more often. There are no relevant standards for Y-ring for L1 and L2 seal grooves with retaining ring, and there are no corresponding standards for Y-ring grooves with retaining ring. Figure 2-23 shows the groove structure type of Y-ring with retaining ring, and the corresponding dimensions are shown in Tables 2-81 to 2-84.
3. Yx rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Yx ring and its characteristics
Yx ring is an unequal-lip narrow-section (cut) lip seal ring, which has been introduced before and will not be repeated here. Its sealing mechanism is the same as that of Y-ring.

(2) Sealing design of Yx ring. Since there are standards JB/ZQ4264-2006 "Yx seal ring for hole" and JB/ZQ4265-2006 "Yx seal ring for shaft", in the sealing design of Yx ring, as long as the sealing material of the sealing ring is selected correctly, the requirements of working medium, working temperature, working pressure and speed are met, and it is decided whether to install a retaining ring, the sealing groove can be designed according to the standard. The hole-type Yx seal ring has the following mark at the bottom: YxD50, which is the nominal outer diameter (cylinder inner diameter) D=50mm hole-type Yx seal ring, that is, the Yx seal ring used for piston seal. The shaft-type Yx seal ring has the following mark at the bottom: Yx d50, which is the nominal inner diameter (piston rod diameter) d=50mm shaft-type Yx seal ring, that is, the Yx seal ring used for piston rod seal.
The types of Yx ring and its groove are shown in Figure 2-24 and Figure 2-25. The groove dimensions of hole-type Yx seal ring are shown in Table 2-85.

5. V-shaped rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Sealing mechanism of V-shaped rubber sealing rings

V-shaped rubber sealing rings are also a type of lip seal. Their cross-section is V-shaped (or the cross-section is in the shape of the letter V, hereinafter referred to as V-ring), as shown in Figure 2-28. V-rings generally cannot be used alone; they must be used together with at least three components: a pressure ring and a support ring (or an elastic sealing ring) to form a combined seal, i.e., a V-shaped combined sealing ring. The included angle of V-rings is generally made 90°, with special cases at 60°. The pressure ring and support ring are also made 90° or slightly larger. Taking a V-ring for piston rod sealing as an example, when the V-ring is in its free state, its outer diameter is larger than the inner diameter of the sealing groove, and its inner diameter is smaller than the piston rod diameter. When the three components are assembled together and installed into the sealing groove, the V-ring undergoes initial deformation. Due to the action of the support ring, this deformation only occurs in the lip portion of the V-ring, generating pressure at the contact points. Even without applying pressure, the lip of the V-ring can seal the working medium with a certain pressure. This is the "self-sealing" effect possessed by V-rings. When the pressure of the working medium being sealed increases, the lip portion changes its contact shape and increases the contact stress. The lip portion and the contact surface fit more tightly, increasing the contact area between the sealing ring and the sealing surface, improving the sealing effect.

sections.caption: Figure 2-28 V-ring Structural Types

Part a) shows three variants: Pressure ring, V-ring, and Elastic seal ring with dimensions labeled h₁, D₁, and h₁. Part b) shows three variants: Pressure ring, V-ring, and Support ring with dimensions labeled h₂, h₁, d₁, and d₂. Each diagram shows cross-sectional views with hatched areas indicating material.

sections.text: a) Piston seal V-ring combination  b) Piston rod seal V-ring combination
Combined with tighter sealing, the sealing force is higher, and the sealing force increases with the V-ring's self-sealing effect.

When the pressure of the working medium is very high, several V-rings can be stacked together for combined use. Through the pressing of a set of V-rings by the pressure ring and support ring, their sealing capacity can be enhanced, and it can even reach 60 MPa or higher. The reason for the enhanced sealing capacity is that the working medium will be depressurized every time it passes through each V-ring until the leakage is prevented. After being pressed tightly, 3 to 4 V-rings can seal the ultra-high pressure of 60 MPa. The standard has a maximum of 6 V-rings stacked together as a group.

The V-ring is a one-way seal ring, and its V-ring notch end must face the high-pressure side. When used for the piston seal of a double-acting hydraulic cylinder, since two sets of V-rings must be arranged symmetrically, the length of the piston becomes too long, and the friction force also increases greatly. It is also relatively troublesome that the pressing force of the V-ring is not easy to adjust, and only an elastic seal ring is used to apply the pressing force. The friction force of the V-ring seal is greater than that of other seals. The minimum starting pressure reflected on the hydraulic cylinder is also large. In the JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard, for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with V-ring (combination) seal (both piston and piston rod seals are V-rings) with a nominal pressure ≤16 MPa, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 0.75 MPa; while for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with other seals, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 0.3 MPa. For double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure >16 MPa and V-ring (combination) seal (both piston and piston rod seals are V-rings), the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 9% of the nominal pressure; while for double-acting hydraulic cylinders with other seals, the minimum starting pressure is not allowed to be greater than 6% of the nominal pressure.

The material for manufacturing V-rings is most commonly nitrile rubber, and there are also those using cloth-reinforced rubber. Among them, cloth-reinforced fluorine rubber can be used for high temperature or other media (it should be checked according to the working medium when in use). The materials for manufacturing pressure rings and support rings (elastic seal rings) are generally
cloth-reinforced rubber, and there are also those using plastics and metals, but now few people make them by themselves, and there is no need to do so.
(2) Use and characteristics of V-ring seal

The V-ring was used earlier, but now it is used less. It is used on some agricultural plunger pumps because its lubrication is poor (water, pesticides or liquid fertilizers, etc.). It is occasionally used on hydraulic cylinders because of the harsh working conditions, and it is hoped that when there is a leak, the pressure cap (generally used to press the V-ring) can still be used after being tightened. When the V-ring is used, it can withstand a certain degree of eccentricity, but don't expect it to have a very long service life in occasions with large eccentricity. The number of V-rings in a group should not be too many. Sealing with 5 or 6 is not possible, and adding more will not be possible. In order to improve the sealing effect and service life, cloth-reinforced and non-cloth-reinforced V-rings can be mixed and installed, and generally the non-cloth-reinforced ones are placed in the middle.

items: Several V-rings can be stacked for use, and the sealing capacity generally increases with the increase of the number of stacks.
It has a certain ability to resist eccentricity.
Its service life can be improved by increasing the pressing force.
It is resistant to high pressure and has reliable performance.
When used in stacks, it can be cut and installed.
It can be used in occasions with poor lubrication or harsh working conditions.
It is especially suitable for use under heavy load conditions.

8) Good sealing effect at low temperatures.
9) Large friction resistance and large structural dimensions.
(3) Design and selection principles for V-ring seals
The main tasks in designing V-ring seals are: determining the installation structure for V-rings, selecting the material and quantity of V-rings, and selecting or designing the pressure ring and support ring for V-rings.
The maximum working pressure for V-rings can reach 60 MPa or even higher. The working temperature ranges from -30 to 100°C or higher, with a movement speed ≤0.5 m/s.
1) Determination of installation structure. The installation structure of V-rings differs from other seal groove structures in that it must have an adjustable groove length structure, which is necessary to apply pressure to the V-rings. The adjustable part is usually the pressure cover, which is typically pressed onto the pressure ring. Using adjustment shims is the most common method to adjust the pressure.
2) Material selection. V-ring materials are classified into three types: pure rubber, rubber with fabric insert, and rubber-plastic composite. Pure rubber V-rings have excellent sealing performance, while fabric-reinforced rubber V-rings have better pressure resistance and wear resistance than pure rubber V-rings. Some sources recommend that at least one pure rubber ring should be included in a group of V-ring seals under low-temperature conditions to ensure good sealing performance. Fabric-reinforced V-rings can be cut and assembled, while pure rubber V-rings cannot. When cutting fabric-reinforced V-rings, they should be cut at a 45° angle, and each V-ring can only be cut at one break.

When installing, the breaks should be staggered by 90° to 180°. This characteristic is very important; the author once used it when handling oil well seals in an oil field. Currently, V-rings are suitable for hydraulic oil and petroleum-based lubricants. If sealing other working media, it is necessary to communicate thoroughly with the seal manufacturer beforehand.
3) Selection of quantity. The number of V-rings in a group depends on the sealing pressure; the higher the pressure, the more rings are needed. However, when the number reaches a certain level, further increases do not significantly improve the sealing effect, while friction force increases sharply. The number of V-rings can be selected from 1 to 6, but 3 to 5 is most common. To improve the overall sealing performance, V-rings of different materials can be installed alternately, or spacer rings can be used.
4) Selection and design of pressure ring and support ring. V-rings sold in the market are usually supplied in sets, including the pressure ring, V-rings, and support ring (or elastic seal ring). Simply select according to the "Piston L3 Seal Groove V-ring, Pressure Ring, and Elastic Ring Dimensions and Tolerances" or "Piston Rod L3 Seal Groove V-ring, Pressure Ring, and Support Ring Dimensions and Tolerances" tables in GB/T10708.1-2000 "Reciprocating Rubber Seal Ring Structural Dimension Series Part 1: Unidirectional Rubber Seal Rings."

sections.text: If metal retaining rings and support rings are used, they may need to be designed by oneself. To ensure the correct position of the V-ring, the metal rings must be carefully designed and processed. However, the shape and dimensions of the V-ring will have errors, and the metal ring also needs to have a certain elasticity. Therefore, soft metals such as tin bronze and aluminum bronze are generally selected.

If the pressure of the hydraulic medium to be sealed is low and small friction force is required, the angle of the recessed part of the retaining ring can be designed to be slightly larger than the angle of the sealing ring. Some reference literature mentions that it can reach up to 96°.

Finally, it should be noted that the service life of V-ring combined seals (including sealing performance) is closely related to the adjustment of the pressing force. Theoretically, the V-ring will have a longer service life under the optimal pressing force. However, if the pressing force is adjusted to be very large at the first time, its service life will definitely be very low. When adjusting the pressing force on site, it is necessary to tighten it gradually and not be hasty. The author has had many on-site practice experiences in this regard.
6. U-shaped rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Characteristics and functions of U-ring

The U-shaped rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as U-ring) is a lip-shaped sealing element with a U-shaped cross-section. It has a pair of flexible sealing protrusions (sealing lips or lip edges, i.e., there is an inner lip and an outer lip, a pair of lips), as shown in Figure 2-30. According to the definition of the U-ring, the pair of sealing lips of the U-ring should be of equal height (symmetrical), and the bottom of the U-ring should be shorter than that of the Y-ring. However, there is no standard for how much shorter it should be to be called a U-ring instead of a Y-ring. In fact, this kind of sealing ring, which is frequently used for sealing hydraulic cylinders, had neither product standards nor sealing groove standards in China before July 13, 2018. However, it is common to see U-rings in the product samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers. In their product samples, the pair of sealing lips of the U-ring are either of equal height (symmetrical) or of unequal height (asymmetrical). The U-ring with equal height (symmetrical) lips is generally universal for shafts and holes (piston and piston rod seals), while the U-ring with unequal height (asymmetrical) lips is divided into piston seals and piston rod seals, which is similar to the Y-ring standard in China. However, Y-rings are rarely seen in the product samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers. Therefore, some reference literature points out that the U-ring in foreign countries is the same as the Y-ring in China.

As shown in Figure 2-31, in addition to a pair of (symmetrical or asymmetrical) sealing lips, the U-ring in the samples of foreign sealing ring manufacturers may also have another sealing lip on the side in contact with the mating part, which is called the second sealing lip.

sections.text: (2) Sealing mechanism of U-ring

As shown in Figure 2-34 and Figure 2-35, because U-ring has a pair of flexible sealing protrusions (sealing lips), the fluid pressure acting on one side of the lips keeps the other side in close contact with the mating surface to form a seal.

After the U-ring is assembled, the sealing groove and the mating surface radially compress the U-ring, make it contact with the mating surface and generate initial contact stress, block the assembly clearance, and form initial seal; after the working medium to be sealed pressurizes it, a pair of flexible lips radially expand, and the lips are further closely attached to the sealing surface. With the increase of working medium pressure, the sealing contact area and contact stress will also increase, and the sealing ability will be enhanced. Therefore, U-ring is a kind of seal ring with self-sealing effect (ability).
Compared with the extrusion seal, the typical U-ring has weak initial sealing ability. Therefore, it is generally not suitable for static sealing.

The atypical U-ring effectively overcomes the above disadvantages of U-ring because of the elastic body embedded in the U-shaped groove, so that the U-ring has almost the same initial sealing ability as the extrusion seal, and therefore can be used for static sealing.

The sealing mechanism of the atypical U-ring contains the sealing mechanism of the extrusion seal and the lip seal, but the elastic body embedded in the U-shaped groove may affect the excitation ability of the sealing lip, that is, it is insensitive to pressure impact or the self-sealing ability is weakened. The solution is to first vulcanize the bamboo joint-shaped O-shaped straight bar, then bond it into an O-ring, and then embed it into the U-shaped groove of the U-ring to form an atypical U-ring which does not affect the excitation ability of the sealing lip and has good initial sealing ability.

Another atypical U-ring has excellent static and dynamic sealing performance and can also be used for rotary sealing because of the metal spring (usually stainless steel) with U-shaped or oval cross-section embedded in the U-shaped groove. Due to its ability to accurately control the friction force within a wide working temperature range, it is used in switching elements such as pressure switches. This U-ring can be made of various materials and has excellent sealing performance.

For sealing applications such as PTFE + stainless steel, which can be used for food, medicine and other industries, reference can be made to Table 2-149 Figure 6 for non-standard U-shaped seals (with elastic metal springs) active seals.

sections.text: 7. Rhodoid rubber sealing ring and its groove
(1) Characteristics and function of rhodoid ring

As shown in Figure 2-38, the rubber sealing ring with a cross-section resembling a rhodoid is called rhodoid rubber sealing ring (hereinafter referred to as rhodoid ring). The rhodoid ring is a one-way sealing ring with standards, and the structure type, size, and tolerance of the rhodoid ring are specified in GB/T10708.1-2000 "Structure Size Series of Reciprocating Rubber Sealing Rings Part 1: One-way Rubber Sealing Ring".

The rhodoid ring is generally composed of two parts, the sealing part is made of rubber, and the supporting part is made of cloth-reinforced rubber, and the hardness of the cloth-reinforced rubber is higher than that of the sealing part rubber.

sections.caption: Figure 2-38  Structure type of rhodoid ring
sections.description: A cylindrical seal ring shown in cross-section with rubber material composition indicated. The figure shows the structural configuration of a rhodoid ring seal.

sections.text: According to relevant definitions, the rhodoid ring does not belong to lip seals. Because its sealing protrusion part (sealing lip or lip) does not have a connected flexible part. One-way sealing is because its structure is combined with a supporting part (ring), when the sealing part is pressurized by hydraulic oil on one side, the other side supporting part can only resist extrusion by leaning against the side of the sealing groove, and vice versa it cannot.

Due to its structural characteristics, when the piston seal of a double-acting hydraulic cylinder adopts a rhodoid ring, it is difficult to solve the pressure relief after oil trapping if it is installed back to back. Therefore, the rhodoid ring is mainly used for piston rod seals rather than piston seals of double-acting hydraulic cylinders.
Due to its structural characteristics, the rhodoid ring can be used for radial static sealing.
The use conditions of one-way sealing rhodoid ring for reciprocating motion are shown in Table 2-96.

sections.text: Compared with Y-shaped ring, the rhodoid ring has the following characteristics:

items: Reasonable structure type.
High sealing pressure and long life.
Good sealing performance.
Certain self-compensation ability.
Certain anti-eccentricity ability.
Universal with Y (unequal lip height) shaped ring groove.
Can be used for radial static sealing.

sections.text: When the hydraulic cylinder seal using Y (unequal lip height) shaped ring seal has problems, the rhodoid ring should be considered first, but it is not possible if the cylinder bore is scratched. Because its sealing material is generally NBR, its tear resistance and wear resistance are lower than AU or EU, and the author has practical field experience in this regard.
(2) Sealing Mechanism of U-ring

The sealing mechanism of U-ring is more similar to extrusion type sealing. Its structure can be understood as a combination of an irregular O-ring and a special retaining ring, i.e. the sealing part and supporting part mentioned above. The sealing material used for the sealing part of U-ring should be equivalent to that of O-ring, with hardness lower than 90 HA (or IRHD), generally around 75 HA; the hardness of cloth-inserted rubber used for the supporting part is generally higher than 90 HA, and it is usually molded into one piece with the same rubber. Due to the presence of the supporting part (special retaining ring), it can only be used in one direction, i.e. one-way sealing. After the U-ring is installed into the sealing groove, its sealing part is radially compressed, forming initial sealing against the mating surface and the bottom of the groove; when the sealing part is subjected to the action of hydraulic oil, i.e. under pressure, the supporting part leans against the side of the groove, and the sealing part undergoes further radial expansion and deformation, increasing the sealing contact area and enhancing the sealing capability; as the sealing pressure further increases, both the supporting part and the sealing part will deform together, further increasing the sealing contact area and further enhancing the sealing capability. Due to the presence of the supporting part, although the resilience of the sealing part is enhanced, it also limits the radial expansion and deformation of the sealing part. In addition, the anti-extrusion capability of the supporting part has a certain limit value, so the sealing pressure is also limited, but it is higher than that of Y-ring seal, possibly even twice as high.
Since the sealing capability of U-ring increases with the increase of sealing working medium pressure, U-ring has a self-sealing effect.

The main function of the supporting part is to enhance the strength of the sealing part, especially its anti-extrusion capability. However, the anti-extrusion capability of cloth-inserted rubber is not as good as that of plastic, so it is necessary to additionally install a plastic retaining ring when needed. After the U-ring is worn out by reciprocating motion, it still has a certain self-compensating effect because it is an extrusion type seal, which is also one of the reasons for its longer service life compared to Y-ring.

sections.text: 8. Drum-shaped and mountain-shaped rubber seals and their grooves
(1) Characteristics and functions of drum-shaped rings and mountain-shaped rings

Drum-shaped rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as drum-shaped ring) and mountain-shaped rubber seal ring (hereinafter referred to as mountain-shaped ring) are rubber seal rings suitable for installation on hydraulic cylinder pistons to provide bidirectional sealing. According to GB/T 10708.2—2000 (Structure and Dimensions of Reciprocating Rubber Seals Part 2: Bidirectional Sealing Rubber Seals), there are two structural forms. The first type consists of a drum-shaped ring and two L-shaped support rings (see Figure 2-40a); the second type consists of a mountain-shaped ring, two J-shaped rings, and two rectangular support rings (see Figure 2-40b). The sealing groove specified in GB/T 6577—1986 (Types, Dimensions, and Tolerances of Sealing Grooves for Hydraulic Cylinder Pistons with Support Rings) is adopted.

sections.text: When the reciprocating motion speed is not greater than 0.15 m/s, the working pressure range of the drum-shaped ring is 0.10–70 MPa, and the working pressure range of the mountain-shaped ring is 0–35 MPa; when the reciprocating motion speed is not greater than 0.5 m/s, the working pressure range of the drum-shaped ring is 0.10–40 MPa, and the working pressure range of the mountain-shaped ring is 0–20 MPa.

Drum-shaped rings and mountain-shaped rings are assembled bidirectional sealing rings for holes. In a drum-shaped sealing ring composed of a drum-shaped ring and two L-shaped support rings, the drum-shaped ring is generally made of rubber molded with fabric-wrapped rubber, and the two L-shaped support rings are made of plastic; in a set of mountain-shaped sealing rings composed of a mountain-shaped ring, two J-shaped rings, and two rectangular support rings, the mountain-shaped ring is generally made of rubber, and the two J-shaped rings and two rectangular support rings are made of plastic. Specifically, the two J-shaped rings are made of thermoplastic polyester plastic, and the L-shaped and rectangular support rings are made of reinforced phenolic plastic with glass fiber embedded.
This sealing structure has the following advantages:

items: Good sealing performance under low pressure conditions.
The piston length can be shorter, and some can be installed on an integral piston.
The special structure of the sealing assembly prevents the seal ring from twisting in the groove during installation.
High extrusion resistance of the seal ring, good piston guidance.
High temperature resistance and wear resistance.

9. Coaxial Sealing Elements and Their Grooves
(1) Characteristics and Functions of Coaxial Sealing Elements

The term "coaxial sealing element" is defined in JB/T 8241-1996 "Vocabulary of coaxial sealing elements", which refers to a combined sealing element composed of a plastic ring and a rubber ring, with the plastic ring serving as the friction sealing surface.

A coaxial sealing element typically consists of at least one sealing sliding ring (also called plastic ring or sliding ring) and an elastic body. Generally, the material of the sliding ring is made of polytetrafluoroethylene filled with bronze (or molybdenum disulfide, etc.) or high-hardness polyurethane, and the elastic body is made of rubber material. In GB/T 15242.1-2017, square coaxial sealing elements for holes, combined coaxial sealing elements for holes, and stepped coaxial sealing elements for shafts are respectively provided. The square coaxial sealing element for holes is a piston sealing element with a rectangular cross-section sliding ring and an O-ring or rectangular ring as the elastic body; the combined coaxial sealing element for holes is a piston sealing element composed of a sealing sliding ring, a mountain-shaped elastic body, and two retaining rings; the stepped coaxial sealing element for shafts is a piston rod sealing element with a stepped cross-section sliding ring and an O-ring as the elastic body.

Coaxial sealing elements are suitable for dynamic sealing of hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods using hydraulic oil as the working medium, with a working pressure ≤40 MPa, reciprocating motion speed ≤5 m/s, and a working temperature range of -40~200℃. After years of development and technological progress, its working pressure can reach 60 MPa, and the reciprocating motion speed can reach 15 m/s, but the working temperature range has not changed much, mainly because the performance of the elastic body (here referring to the commonly used O-ring material) has not changed much. It should be noted that it is not a single O-ring material that can be applied to the working temperature range of -40~200℃, but rather a comprehensive selection of low-temperature nitrile rubber (HNBR) with a working temperature range of -40~100℃, nitrile rubber (NBR) with a working temperature range of -30~120℃, fluoro rubber (FKM) with a working temperature range of -20~200℃, etc.
For special performance coaxial sealing elements, please refer to Section 2.10.5.1.4.
(2) Types and Working Characteristics of Coaxial Sealing Elements

Coaxial sealing elements are divided into double-acting and single-acting types, generally in combination of both, with the elastic body commonly being an O-shaped rubber sealing ring, and also rectangular (square) or mountain-shaped rubber sealing rings; the cross-section shape of the sliding ring is diverse, with square plastic rings and stepped plastic rings being commonly used. Coaxial sealing elements are not only used for piston and piston rod sealing, but also for dust sealing.
In coaxial sealing elements, there is a series of products with independent intellectual property rights in China, called "Che sealing elements".

Due to the significant changes in the structure of coaxial sealing elements, mainly in the sliding ring, several types of coaxial sealing elements are listed below for future unified naming, as shown in Figure 2-45.
From the various structural forms of the listed coaxial sealing elements, the following changes can be observed:

items: There are also bidirectional sealing structural forms for shaft seals, and lightweight structural forms have been developed.

There are also unidirectional sealing structural forms for hole seals, and coaxial seals composed of four parts with non-O-ring elastic bodies have been developed. At the same time, there are also lightweight structural forms for hole seals.

There are structural forms for rotary sealing for both shaft and hole seals. Based on the author's years of experience using coaxial sealing elements, the following characteristics of coaxial sealing elements are summarized:

sections.text: 1) Small friction force, easy starting at low pressure, smooth operation, no crawling.
2) Suitable for high-speed operation.
3) No danger of O-ring extrusion, long service life.
4) Wide range of applicable working media and working temperature if O-ring material is selected appropriately.
5) High pressure and high temperature resistant.
6) Compact seal structure.
7) Improved low-pressure sealing performance when sliding ring is made of polyurethane.
8) Relatively reliable performance when used in hydraulic joints and rotary joints. However, common coaxial seals have two disadvantages: 1) Difficult installation. 2) Poor sealing performance.

Special Note: For hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders, coaxial seals should be selected first, including coaxial combination dust seals. Compared with lip seals, the sealing performance of coaxial seals is lower, i.e., there is leakage, especially more obvious at low temperature and low pressure. Therefore, in places where internal leakage of hydraulic cylinders is strictly required, as well as in lifting (or lifting) machinery, coaxial seals are generally not used for sealing or must be used in series with lip seals.

10. Several Atypical Sealing Elements and Their Grooves
(1) Piston Rod Combination Seal Ring with Retaining Ring

The piston rod combination seal ring with retaining ring (hereinafter referred to as piston rod combination ring) is a sealing element composed of a sealing ring and a retaining ring made of two different materials.

As shown in Figure 2-51, the piston rod combination ring is a lip-type sealing element. The sealing ring is made of polyurethane rubber (93HA), and its cross-sectional shape is approximately trident-shaped; the retaining ring is made of plastic, with a hardness higher than that of the sealing ring.
Its main advantages are:

items: Excellent wear resistance.
Impact resistance.
Extrusion resistance.
Small axial compression deformation under medium pressure.
Can adapt to the harshest (demanding) working conditions.
Can be installed in an integral (closed) sealing groove.
Compact structure, suitable for installation in international standard grooves.

sections.text: The piston rod combination ring is suitable for mineral hydraulic oil, with a working temperature range of -35 ~ 110°C. The maximum working pressure can reach 50 MPa (pressure peak can reach 100 MPa), and the maximum speed is 0.5 m/s.

This piston rod combination seal ring with a special structure is mainly used for sealing hydraulic cylinders in walking machinery. Its application in the sealing system of hydraulic cylinders in construction machinery is mainly used as a buffer seal before the main seal, preventing the highest working pressure inside the hydraulic cylinder from directly acting on the main seal.

sections.text: (2) Piston Unidirectional Seal Ring with Support Ring and Its Groove

The piston unidirectional seal ring with support ring (hereinafter referred to as piston combination seal ring) is a sealing component composed of a seal ring and a support ring made of materials with different hardnesses.

As shown in Figure 2-52, the piston combination seal ring is a lip-shaped sealing component. The seal ring is made of fabric-reinforced rubber with slightly lower hardness, and its cross-sectional shape is approximately trident-shaped. The support ring is also made of fabric-reinforced rubber, with higher hardness than the seal ring.

The piston combination seal ring is installed back-to-back and can be used for piston sealing in double-acting hydraulic cylinders. Due to its sealing material and structural type, it can meet the requirements of harsh working conditions, such as pressure impact, vibration, and eccentricity. The maximum working pressure can reach 60 MPa.

Its outstanding performance characteristics are that the support ring can prevent extrusion and also produce a sealing effect under high pressure, forming a second sealing barrier. Therefore, it is suitable for heavy-duty working conditions.

sections.text: (3) Coaxial seal with retaining ring

The "coaxial seal with retaining ring" given in Reference [102] has the same structural form as the bore assembly coaxial seal given in GB/T15242.1-2017. However, in addition to providing reciprocating motion coaxial seals for hydraulic cylinder piston dynamic sealing devices suitable for water-based or oil-based hydraulic fluids as the transmission medium, GB/T15242.1-2017 has no other technical conditions available for selection and reference. It is also not as valuable as that given in GB/T15242.1-1994 (which has been superseded), which is suitable for reciprocating hydraulic cylinder pistons with hydraulic oil as the working medium, pressure ≤40 MPa, speed ≤5 m/s, and temperature range of -40~200°C.
Therefore, the following content is still of certain reference value.

The coaxial seal with retaining ring is different from the two structural forms of coaxial seals given in GB/T15242.1-1994 "Dimension series and tolerances for coaxial seals for dynamic sealing devices for hydraulic cylinder pistons and piston rods". Its elastomeric cross-section shape is not O-ring, but a special shape (such as mountain-shaped) elastomeric power element; its sliding ring is made of PTFE+bronze or PTFE+glass fiber, and there are also some made of hydrolytically resistant thermoplastic polyester TPE, and a POM or PA retaining ring is installed on each side of the sliding ring, as shown in Figure 2-53.

sections.text: The special-shaped elastomer has a greater squeezing (powering) ability to the sliding ring than the O-ring; the POM retaining ring installed on both sides of the sliding ring can enhance the extrusion resistance of the sliding ring, reduce pressure shock, and also has a certain dirt scraping and dirt holding capacity, which also plays a certain protective role on the sliding ring and elastomer.
This structural form of coaxial seal is mainly used for medium and heavy-duty hydraulic cylinders.

(4) TPU Coaxial Seal

A coaxial seal with sliding ring made of TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) is becoming increasingly popular, and has been successfully applied in hydraulic cylinders for construction machinery, hydraulic presses, elevators, agricultural machinery, machine tools, molds, booster cylinders, etc. According to a summary by a domestic manufacturer, compared to coaxial seals with sliding ring made of filled PTFE, it has the following characteristics:

items: Better conformity and higher dynamic and static sealing performance.
More convenient installation.
Better extrusion resistance.
The sealing surface of the TPU sealing sliding ring in contact with the inner wall of the cylinder or the outer surface of the piston rod is not sensitive to slight scratches.
The processing accuracy requirements for the inner wall of the cylinder or the outer surface of the piston rod can be reduced.
Better consistency of material properties for TPU sealing sliding ring.
TPU sealing sliding ring has an anti-O-ring extrusion design, which can better protect the elastomer.
TPU sealing sliding ring has an oil guide groove structure, which can effectively prevent through leakage.
TPU has comparable wear resistance to PTFE material.

sections.text: 10) TPU material coaxial seals have better economy. Compared to Y-rings or U-rings, TPU coaxial seals have the following characteristics:

items: Lower friction force.
Can effectively prevent or reduce the occurrence of crawling and/or abnormal noise in hydraulic cylinders.
Comparable pressure holding performance, but better dynamic sealing performance.
Better sealing performance at low pressure or low and high speed due to the force applied by the elastomer.
Ultra-high hardness TPU material is more pressure and extrusion resistant.
No occurrence of back pressure damaging the sealing lip, nor occurrence of burning the sealing lip due to trapped gas.
TPU material in polycarbonate system is more heat and working medium resistant than most foreign Y-rings or U-rings materials currently available.
Sealing ring with TPU+NBR material combination has lower compression set than single TPU material sealing ring.
Sealing groove is compatible with sealing grooves of other domestic and foreign seal manufacturers, making seal selection convenient.
Smaller sealing groove, saving space.
More convenient installation.
Better economy compared to imported sealing rings.

(5) Low Leakage Coaxial Seal

The elastomer of a general coaxial seal is an O-ring, and the friction sealing surface that contacts and seals the mating part is a plastic ring. The elastomer of a low leakage coaxial seal is two O-rings, and the friction sealing surface that contacts and seals the mating part is not only a plastic ring, but also an X-ring. This type of coaxial seal has better dynamic sealing performance because it adds a rubber seal to the metal and plastic friction sealing surface. At the same time, because it uses two O-rings to press the sliding ring against the mating surface, it has stronger energizing ability for the sliding ring, so its initial sealing (static sealing) performance is better.

The main features of the low-leakage coaxial seal are:
1) Excellent dynamic and static sealing performance.
2) Combining the advantages of combination seals and X seals.
3) High sealing pressure and small leakage.
4) Small structural size, safe and reliable.
5) Low friction, no crawling, long life.

Due to the above characteristics, low-leakage coaxial seals are mainly used in piston accumulators, synchronous control hydraulic cylinders, locking, positioning, support, suspension, servo, digital hydraulic cylinders, etc. With people's understanding and in-depth understanding of them, low-leakage coaxial seals will be applied to various hydraulic cylinders used under medium and heavy load conditions.

The sealing performance of low-leakage coaxial seals for piston seals is closely related to the guiding performance of the support ring of the piston and piston rod. In order to ensure the excellent sealing performance, high-quality support rings and more precise support ring installation grooves must be used.

sections.text: 11. Dust Seal Rings and Their Grooves
(1) Standard Rubber Dust Seal Rings and Their Grooves

Standard rubber dust seal rings refer to rubber dust seal rings (or simply called dust seals) adapted to GB/T 6578-2008 "Types, Dimensions, and Tolerances of Dust Seal Ring Grooves for Hydraulic Cylinder Piston Rods" cited in JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" and other hydraulic cylinder product standards.

Dust seals are sealing elements that function as wipers (scrapers) to prevent contaminants from entering, or devices installed on reciprocating piston rods to prevent contaminants from entering. Standard GB/T 10708.3-2000 "Dimension Series for Reciprocating Rubber Seals Part 3: Rubber Dust Seal Rings" specifies the types, dimensions, and tolerances of rubber dust seal rings for reciprocating motion. According to this standard, dust seal rings are classified into three basic types based on their structure and application:

sections.text: Types:

items: Type A dust ring: It is a single-lip rubber seal without a skeleton, suitable for installation in Type A seal structure, for dust prevention.
Type B dust ring: It is a single-lip rubber seal with a skeleton, suitable for installation in Type B seal structure, for dust prevention.
Type C dust ring: It is a double-lip rubber seal, suitable for installation in Type C seal structure, for dust prevention and auxiliary sealing.

12. Support ring, guide ring and its groove
(1) Support ring and its groove

Support rings or guide rings are not defined in GB/T 17446—2012 "Vocabulary for Fluid Power Systems and Components." Support rings are defined in GB/T 15242.2—2017 as rings that support the piston or piston rod of a hydraulic cylinder, prevent contact between moving metal parts, and provide a sliding surface between the seal ring and the cylinder bore or piston rod.

The split annular non-metallic guide element for radial supporting force. In JB/T 8241-1996, the supporting ring is also defined, which is a ring made of wear-resistant plastic material used to prevent collision between the piston and cylinder body, and serves a supporting and guiding function.

Both the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder must be guided during reciprocating motion. Although the piston's reciprocating motion is nominally guided by the inner diameter of the cylinder barrel, and the piston rod's reciprocating motion is nominally guided by the inner hole of the guide sleeve (or cylinder head), in modern hydraulic cylinders, guide rings (strips) are generally used to contact the cylinder barrel or piston rod. Since the guide ring moves reciprocally on the surface of the coupling part (cylinder barrel or piston rod), it must be wear-resistant. Therefore, it is also called a wear ring (strip).

Regarding the name of the supporting ring, in product catalogs of some domestic and foreign sealing manufacturers, it is rarely called a supporting ring, but more often called a guide ring (strip) or wear ring. There are also those called support rings.

The supporting ring and guide ring are two names for the same sealing element, which has practical significance for hydraulic cylinder seal design. In the composition of the V-ring rubber seal, when the retaining ring and guide ring are made into an integrated structure, it is more accurate to call it a "guide supporting ring." However, since the term "guide supporting ring" has not been defined in the current standard, this manual still uses the term "supporting ring" in its descriptions.
The plastic supporting ring can be considered as a non-metallic bearing to some extent. In the hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system, the supporting ring has the following functions:

items: It serves a supporting function, supporting the piston or piston rod and separating it from the metal surface with relative reciprocating motion.
It serves a guiding function, guiding the reciprocating motion of the piston and piston rod and resisting lateral forces.

sections.text: 3) When installed in front of the seal ring, it has the functions of impact resistance and decontamination.
4) It has centering and vibration suppression (absorption) functions.
5) The integral and flanged supporting rings have a certain sealing function.

Common materials currently used for manufacturing supporting rings include: polytetrafluoroethylene + bronze (or with molybdenum disulfide, graphite, etc.), glass fiber reinforced polyoxymethylene, glass fiber reinforced polyamide, fabric (cloth) reinforced polyoxymethylene, fabric (cloth) reinforced polyamide, etc. Their working temperature ranges, except for PTFE mentioned in the standard GB/T 15242.2, which is -40 to 200°C, the other two materials do not have such high usage temperatures, roughly around -40 to 130°C. Please carefully read the product catalogs of sealing manufacturers when selecting specific materials. However, some sealing manufacturers recommend in their product catalogs that the supporting rings used in high-speed light load or potentially crawling conditions can be used at temperatures of -180 to 250°C. Readers who want to adopt this should carefully consider it.

When there is a possibility of crawling, it is more suitable to use a supporting ring made of polytetrafluoroethylene + bronze material; under low-speed heavy load conditions, it is more suitable to use a supporting ring made of fabric reinforced polyoxymethylene or fabric reinforced polyamide (also called fabric reinforced plastic). The tolerance of the S dimension given in the current standard GB/T 15242.4-1994 is not very reasonable, and considerations for material swelling, thermal expansion (such as linear thermal expansion), etc. are not thorough. The S dimension tolerance should be given separately according to the usage temperature range. Although the materials selected for manufacturing guide supporting rings (strips) are all materials with low friction coefficients, if the S dimension tolerance is unreasonable, one situation is poor guidance, and more situations are excessive interference fit. Hydraulic cylinder manufacturers generally

During hydraulic cylinder factory testing, high-temperature tests specified in GB/T 15622—2005 are often not performed, which require inputting 90°C working oil into the tested hydraulic cylinder at rated pressure, reciprocating full stroke for 1h. Even the test oil temperature rarely reaches 50°C because hydraulic test benches generally cannot heat up the oil and there is no time for it. Therefore, some hydraulic cylinders may experience normal initial operation after field installation, but after running for a period of time, the cylinders may exhibit slower movement speed, crawling (vibration), or abnormal noise. Upon disassembly and inspection, the guide support ring may be severely squeezed or worn. GB/T 15242.2—2017 provides four specifications for guide support ring cross-sectional thickness: 1.55mm, 2.5mm, 3mm, and 4mm. However, other specifications such as 2.0mm and 3.5mm are also commonly used. Please refer to the seal manufacturer's product samples when using them.

The reasons why support rings without sealing function must have sufficient cut clearance b₂ or Z (Z₁) are:

items: During the operation of the hydraulic cylinder, the temperature will rise. The standard stipulates that the working temperature of the hydraulic cylinder can be ≤80°C. The high-temperature test of the hydraulic cylinder also requires that the hydraulic oil temperature be input into the hydraulic cylinder at 90°C and run back and forth for 1 hour. Because the temperature rises, the plastic support ring will elongate. That is, linear thermal expansion may cause the reciprocating motion part to be stuck (increased friction, rapid oil temperature rise) or even stuck.
If the support ring installed in front of the lip seal ring on the piston rod cannot relieve pressure on the "trapped oil," it may squeeze out the support ring (or lip seal ring).

sections.text: Plastic guide strips are currently the most commonly used material for making open (cut-type) guide rings. They have a rectangular cross-section with rounded or chamfered edges. Compared to closed (integral-type) guide rings, they have many advantages, especially the ability to be purchased in rolls and cut to any desired length, making installation simple and easy.

Guide strips have basically the same material as the aforementioned guide rings. However, it is easier to treat their surface structure to an ideal condition during the manufacturing process, such as a mesh structure, which improves their lubrication performance, wear resistance, and reduces static and dynamic friction coefficients. This allows hydraulic cylinders to operate at low speeds without crawling.

There are three supply forms of cut-type guide rings on the market: pre-processed tubular material formed into circular rings, spiral shape, and flat rolled guide strips. The cut types generally include three types: diagonal cut (Type A), straight cut (Type B), and lap joint or tongue-and-groove (Type C). Regardless of the cut type, the guide rings must have sufficient cut clearance b₂.

For "trapped oil" pressure, it is possible to squeeze out the support ring (or lip seal ring). Therefore, it is necessary to strive for the support ring to be balanced by the axial force of the hydraulic working medium, while ensuring that the seal ring (mainly the lip seal ring) and its groove are ventilated smoothly.
Guide strips (wear rings) from a company's product samples are listed in Tables 2-132 and 2-133.

sections.text: 3) Support and guide design. Support rings play an important role in the hydraulic cylinder sealing system. After preliminary selection, their relative positions to various sealing rings (including spacing, i.e. arrangement), the number of support rings used, and the matching of support rings made of different materials all require further design.

① Support and guide design for piston. For piston sealing systems using bidirectional sealing rings, a support ring should be arranged on each side of the sealing ring. A better arrangement is to add a filled PTFE support ring on each side of the fabric POM, fabric PA, or cotton fiber reinforced phenolic support rings arranged on both sides of the sealing ring. For piston sealing systems using unidirectional sealing rings, a wider support ring should be arranged between the two sealing rings. A better arrangement is to add a filled PTFE support ring on each side of the two sealing rings.

The added filled PTFE support rings have an absorbing (embedding) effect or a dirt-absorbing effect on solid particle contaminants in the hydraulic working medium that may damage the sealing rings and other guide rings, and also increase the guide length. Therefore, these sealing systems are more reasonable, as shown in Figure 2-70. There are more detailed explanations in the piston sealing system of coaxial seals in Table 2-149.

② Support and guide design for piston rod guide sleeve. For the piston rod sealing system arranged on the guide sleeve (or end cover), when a sealing system composed of coaxial seals + lip sealing ring + dust-proof sealing ring is used, support rings should generally be arranged on both sides of the coaxial seals. A better arrangement is to arrange a filled PTFE support ring or a filled PTFE support ring + coaxial seal + fabric POM, fabric PA, or cotton fiber reinforced phenolic support ring + lip sealing ring + fabric POM, fabric PA, or cotton fiber reinforced phenolic + dust-proof sealing ring in front of the fabric POM, fabric PA, or cotton fiber reinforced phenolic support ring arranged in front of the coaxial seal.

The filled PTFE support ring is arranged in front of the fabric POM, fabric PA, or cotton fiber reinforced phenolic support ring (on the side of the hydraulic cylinder working medium action), and its function is the same as above. The piston rod sealing system with only one filled PTFE support ring (three support rings in total) arranged in front of the coaxial seal has a longer supporting length for the moving parts of the hydraulic cylinder (including the piston and piston rod), so it is more reasonable, as shown in Figure 2-71. sections.text: 4) Groove design.
① Design principles for support ring installation grooves:

items: a. The radial depth of the groove should be as shallow as possible. Only in this way can the piston or piston rod be separated from the metal surface with relative reciprocating motion as much as possible to avoid collision. A thicker support ring should be used if necessary.
b. A wider support ring should be used as much as possible within the allowable length (width) of the piston or guide sleeve (cylinder head).

c. The tolerance level of the bottom dimension of the groove should be one level higher than that of the sealing groove bottom dimension of other sealing rings (excluding dust-proof rings) in the sealing system.

d. The side of the groove should be perpendicular to the bottom of the groove, and the fillet at the bottom of the groove should not be larger than the specified value to prevent it from "holding" here, causing the edge of the support ring to be tightly fitted or stuck with the mating part.

e. For multiple support rings, the bottom surfaces of their grooves must be coaxial, and one of the groove bottom surfaces can be used as the coaxiality reference for the groove bottom surfaces of other sealing elements.

f. The spacing between two adjacent support rings should be greater than the depth of their groove; the spacing with other sealing elements should be greater than the depth of the groove of this sealing element.

sections.text: ② Precautions for support ring installation groove design:

items: a. Both POM and PA materials have the problem of water absorption and expansion. During processing, storage, assembly, and use, serious problems may be caused by water absorption (or dimensional changes) due to water washing, moisture in the air, moisture absorption, etc., and mainly due to excessive water content in the hydraulic oil. The problem that occurs is that the relative reciprocating moving part is tightly fitted (expanded) or stuck (expanded to death).
b. The thickness tolerance of the support ring may be one of the main problems of domestic guide rings, and products from the same manufacturer in different batches may be different each time.
c. The length dimension and tolerance of the groove should also be designed and manufactured according to the standards or product samples.
d. The depth of the groove should not be less than the specified minimum depth.

sections.text: 13. Retaining ring and its groove
(1) Retaining ring and groove for O-ring

The O-ring is equipped with a retaining ring to increase the working pressure and service life of the O-ring and prevent the O-ring from being squeezed into the low-pressure side gap; when the pressure is further increased, the O-ring is squeezed out from the mating gap.

Damage. The installation of a retaining ring greatly increases the sealing pressure of the O-ring seal, with static sealing up to 63 MPa and dynamic sealing up to 35 MPa. When the working pressure of the dynamic seal exceeds 10 MPa (or when the static seal exceeds 16 MPa), consideration should be given to installing a retaining ring. The number of retaining rings to be installed is determined based on the pressure condition of the O-ring: one retaining ring for unidirectional pressure, installed on the side where the O-ring may be extruded; two retaining rings for bidirectional pressure, with the O-ring sandwiched between the two retaining rings. The author once used a single O-ring seal at the bottom of the two sets of 8 hydraulic cylinder barrels in a hydraulic tilter, and the seal almost completely failed during testing. After modifying the seal groove at the bottom of the cylinder and installing retaining rings, this problem was solved. The most commonly used material for processing retaining rings is polytetrafluoroethylene, but nylon 6 or nylon 1010 can also be used. It is generally believed that when the O-ring retaining ring is in contact with the mating part, installing a retaining ring for dynamic sealing may increase the friction force, and even on hydraulic cylinders of hydraulic presses, it may cause problems such as the slider being unable to move down quickly.

Here, it is emphasized once again that whether an O-ring needs to be equipped with a retaining ring, in addition to considering the working pressure or nominal pressure (rated pressure) of the hydraulic cylinder, factors such as the mating clearance or single-sided (maximum) clearance (extrusion clearance) should also be considered.

There is currently no standard for the size series and tolerances of O-ring retaining rings. Foreign products can be purchased as a set, while domestic hydraulic cylinder manufacturers generally design and manufacture them themselves.

Note: GB/T 3452.4-XXXX "Rubber O-rings for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Applications Part 4: backup rings (Retaining Rings)" is being developed, but the author has put forward some opinions on the submitted draft, including disagreement with determining the outer diameter size and tolerance of the O-ring retaining ring for pistons based on the piston diameter plus tolerance.

As shown in Figure 2-72, the cross-sectional shape of the O-ring retaining ring is usually rectangular; there are three types: integral, bevel-cut, and spiral. There is also a type of O-ring retaining ring as shown in Figure 2-72 d, which is called a concave retaining ring because it is concave with the O-ring extrusion surface, which can more favorably protect the O-ring.

sections.text: (2) Retaining ring for U-ring and its groove

In some seal product samples, the retaining ring for U-ring is also called a support ring. In order to distinguish it from the support ring that has been defined by the standard, it is uniformly referred to as the retaining ring for U-ring (or simply as a retaining ring) in the following description.

The retaining ring for U-ring is generally used in reciprocating motion and can refer to the type, size and tolerance of the retaining ring specified in the two standards JB/ZQ4264 or JB/ZQ4265 for design and manufacture.

The retaining ring for U-ring is generally made of engineering materials such as polytetrafluoroethylene (also known as fluoroplastic), polyamide or polyoxymethylene plastic. Due to its material properties, it is easy to be compressed and deformed under the pressure of the hydraulic working medium. Although the above materials have been improved, according to the above two standards,

According to the analysis of GB/T 3452.3-2005 "O-ring Grooves for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Applications", the thickness of the retaining ring with a cross-section of 1.80 mm, 2.65 mm, and 3.55 mm should be 1.4 mm, the thickness of the retaining ring with a cross-section of 5.30 mm should be 1.9 mm, and the thickness of the retaining ring with a cross-section of 7.00 mm should be 2.8 mm. Considering the tolerance of the seal groove width and the plastic material of the retaining ring, the thickness of the retaining ring can generally be determined as: 1.5 mm, 2.0 mm, 3.0 mm; there must be a clearance between the retaining ring and the moving mating surface, and the mating part must not be clamped (or expanded) or clamped (or expanded) to death, otherwise the friction force may increase greatly.

Principles for Selecting Retaining Ring Materials for U-rings:

items: The maximum extrusion gap appears when the maximum eccentricity occurs, and the ultimate extrusion resistance of the retaining ring material must meet the requirements of the maximum extrusion gap.
The ultimate extrusion resistance of a certain type of retaining ring material is closely related to the maximum working pressure, maximum working temperature, working time, etc.

In Table 2-138, the extrusion resistance of materials increases from top to bottom, among which 10FF, 34WF, and 31BF retaining ring materials are mainly used for U-rings made of NBR or FKM rubber materials. The ultimate extrusion resistance of a certain type of retaining ring material is expressed as the ultimate extrusion gap, which is obtained through theoretical calculation and experimental verification under certain conditions. When the maximum extrusion gap exceeds the ultimate extrusion gap, U-rings with retaining rings also do not have a long service life. As the working pressure, working temperature, and working time increase, the maximum extrusion resistance of the retaining ring decreases, and the service life is also shortened. Generally, the maximum eccentricity (allowable eccentricity) of the U-ring should be less than 20% of the pre-compression of the U-ring in the U-ring sealing groove; the maximum extrusion gap is the sum of the maximum unilateral fit clearance and the maximum eccentricity. In order to give full play to the respective characteristics of the above two materials, they can be combined or used in pairs, as shown in Figure 2-74.

sections.text: 14. Combined Sealing Gasket and Its Groove
(1) Sealing Gasket

The oil port sealing of hydraulic cylinders is also part of the hydraulic cylinder sealing design. Hydraulic cylinder oil ports generally have two types: threaded oil ports and flange oil ports, which use threaded connection and flange connection respectively. 15. High Temperature and High Pressure Sealing Ring

The hydraulic cylinder is an energy conversion device, and a part of energy will inevitably be lost, and most of this lost energy is converted into thermal energy. The (ultra) high-pressure hydraulic cylinder can convert higher (more) energy under the same volume and weight, so current hydraulic systems and components are pursuing high pressure or ultra-high pressure. High pressure is often accompanied by high temperature in many cases. In order to reduce the highest working temperature of hydraulic systems and components, a cooling system is generally required, but this also requires energy.

If hydraulic systems and components are allowed to operate at certain high temperatures and high pressures, at least the energy for the cooling system can be saved. As an actuator, the hydraulic cylinder not only generates heat by itself, but may also cause the temperature to be higher than the system temperature due to the transfer of thermal energy by the driven load and thermal radiation from the surrounding environment. Therefore, the sealing design of the hydraulic cylinder must predict the working temperature range. Now, the design of the sealing system for hydraulic cylinders with a highest working temperature of 150°C and a highest working pressure ≤35 MPa has become increasingly mature, but the design of the sealing system for hydraulic cylinders under higher temperatures and pressures must be cautious.
The non-typical U-shaped ring (with embedded metal spring) piston sealing system introduced in Table 2-149 may have a working temperature range of -60 to 150°C.

(1) Maximum Working Temperature of Sealing Material

In HG/T 2579—2008 "O-ring Rubber Seals for General Hydraulic Systems", O-ring rubber sealing materials with working temperature ranges of -40~100℃ and -25~125℃ are specified. In HG/T 2021—2014 "High Temperature Grease O-ring Rubber Seals", the sealing materials are classified into Class I, II, III and IV according to different media. Class I is represented by nitrile rubber NBR, suitable for petroleum-based grease, with a general working temperature range of -25~125℃, and can reach 150℃ for short periods. Class II is represented by low compression set fluoroelastomer FKM, suitable for synthetic ester lubricants, with a general working temperature range of -15~200℃, and can reach 250℃ for short periods. Class III is represented by acrylate rubber ACM and ethylene acrylate rubber AEM, suitable for petroleum-based lubricants, with a general working temperature range of -20~150℃, and can reach 175℃ for short periods. Class IV is represented by hydrogenated nitrile rubber HNBR, suitable for petroleum-based lubricants, with a general working temperature range of -25~150℃, and can reach 160℃ for short periods.

In HG/T 2810—2008 "Rubber Seal Materials for Reciprocating Motion", the sealing materials are classified into Class A and B. Class A is nitrile rubber material, with a working temperature range of -30~100℃. Class B is castable polyurethane material, with a working temperature range of -40~80℃.
(2) Maximum Working Temperature of Seal Ring

According to the high temperature test specified in JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder": Under rated pressure, 90℃ working oil is input into the tested hydraulic cylinder, and full-stroke reciprocating operation for 1h should meet the high temperature performance requirements agreed upon by the customer and manufacturer. At the same time, it is stipulated that under normal circumstances, the working environment temperature of the hydraulic cylinder should be within the range of -20~50℃, and the working medium temperature should be within the range of -20~80℃. In GB/T 7935—2005 "General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Components", it is stipulated that except for special provisions, the oil temperature during testing should be 50℃ (Class A ±1.0℃, Class B ±2.0℃, Class C ±4.0℃). In GB/T 15622—2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinder", it is stipulated that except for special provisions, type tests should be conducted at 50℃±2℃, and factory tests should be conducted at 50℃±4℃.

In GB/T 3452.1—2005 "O-ring Rubber Seals for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Use Part 1: Size Series and Tolerances", no provisions are made for working temperature. In JB/T 7757.2—2006 "O-ring Rubber Seals for Mechanical Seals", the working temperature range of nitrile rubber O-ring is specified as -30~100℃, and the working temperature range of fluoroelastomer is specified as -20~200℃.

In JB/T 10706—2007 "Fluoroplastic Coated Rubber O-ring for Mechanical Seals", the working temperature range is specified as -60~200℃ (FEP coated fluoroelastomer is -20~180℃, silicone rubber coated FEP is -60~180℃, fluoroelastomer coated PFA is -20~200℃, silicone rubber coated is -60~200℃).

In GB/T 15242.1—2017 "Size Series of Dynamic Sealing Devices for Hydraulic Cylinder Pistons and Piston Rods Part 1: Size Series and Tolerances of Coaxial Seals", no provisions are made for working temperature. In GB/T 15242.2—2017 "Size Series of Dynamic Sealing Devices for Hydraulic Cylinder Pistons and Piston Rods Part 2: Size Series and Tolerances of Support Rings", the working temperature range is specified as -30~100℃ (polyethylene).
Phenolic resin fabric bearing ring): -60 to 120°C (phenolic resin fabric bearing ring): -60 to 150°C [Filled polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) bearing ring].

GB/T 10708.1—2000 (Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 1: Unidirectional Rubber Seals), GB/T 10708.2—2000 (Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 2: Bidirectional Rubber Seals) and GB/T 10708.3—2000 (Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 3: Rubber Dust Seals) do not specify working temperatures.
In JB/ZQ 4264—2006 (YX-shaped Seals for Holes) and JB/ZQ 4265—2006 (YX-shaped Seals for Shafts), the working temperature range is -40(-20) to 80°C.
In MT/T 985—2006 (Technical Conditions for Polyurethane Seals for Mine Props and Jacks), the seal's suitable working temperature range is -20 to 60°C.
(3) Maximum Working Pressure of Seals

According to GB/T 10205—2010 (Hydraulic Cylinders), the pressure resistance test stipulates: the tested hydraulic cylinder piston shall be stopped at both ends of the formed stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at the stroke limit position), and hydraulic fluid with 1.5 times the nominal pressure shall be applied to the working chamber respectively. The type test pressure holding time is 2 min, and the factory test pressure holding time is 10 s. There shall be no external leakage or component damage.
GB/T 3452.1—2005 (O-rings for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Applications - Part 1: Size Series and Tolerances) does not specify the maximum working pressure.

GB/T 15242.1—1994 (Coaxial Seals for Dynamic Sealing Devices for Pistons and Piston Rods of Hydraulic Cylinders - Dimensions Series and Tolerances) (has been superseded) specifies the maximum working pressure as 40 MPa.

GB/T 10708.1—2000 (Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 1: Unidirectional Rubber Seals) specifies the maximum working pressure of Y-rings as 25 MPa, V-rings as 50 MPa, and V-combination rings as 60 MPa.

GB/T 10708.2—2000 (Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 2: Bidirectional Rubber Seals) specifies the maximum working pressure of drum-shaped rings as 70 MPa and mountain-shaped rings as 35 MPa.

GB/T 36520.1—2018 (Polyurethane Seals Dimensions Series - Part 1: Dimensions and Tolerances for Piston Reciprocating Motion Seals) specifies the maximum working pressure of single-body U-rings and single-body Y×D-rings as 35 MPa (medium: mineral oil, application field: engineering cylinders); single-body drum-shaped rings and single-body mountain-shaped rings as 45 MPa [medium: water-based emulsion (oil), application field: hydraulic supports]; T-groove combined drum-shaped rings and straight-groove combined drum-shaped rings as 90 MPa [medium: water-based emulsion (oil), application field: hydraulic supports].

GB/T 36520.2—2018 (Polyurethane Seals Dimensions Series - Part 2: Dimensions and Tolerances for Piston Rod Reciprocating Motion Seals) specifies the maximum working pressure of single-body U-rings and single-body Y×d-rings as 35 MPa (medium: mineral oil, application field: engineering cylinders); single-body V-rings as 45 MPa [medium: water-based emulsion (oil), application field: hydraulic supports]; combined type seals as 60 MPa [medium: water-based emulsion (oil), application field: hydraulic supports].
In JB/ZQ 4264—2006 (YX-shaped Seals for Holes) and JB/ZQ 4265—2006 (YX-shaped Seals for Shafts), the maximum working pressure is specified as 31.5 MPa.
In JB/T 982—1977 (Combined Gasket Seals), the maximum working pressure is specified as 40 MPa.

In MT/T 985—2006 (Technical Conditions for Polyurethane Seals for Mine Props and Jacks), the maximum working pressure of bidirectional seals is specified as 60 MPa, and that of unidirectional seals as 40 MPa.
(4) High Temperature and High Pressure Seals

Based on the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinder seals, existing seal materials, structural types, and working conditions, static seals (such as O-rings) and reciprocating motion seals with a maximum working temperature higher than 90°C and a maximum working pressure greater than 31.5 MPa are defined as high temperature and (ultra) high pressure seals.

It is difficult to predict the high temperature and high pressure sealing performance of seals, mainly because it is not only related to the sealing material and structural type, but also to the working conditions, such as the extrusion gap of the seal (including the maximum extrusion gap with eccentricity), which is difficult to determine accurately during design. Therefore, the sealing design of any hydraulic cylinder must be tested under actual working conditions (actual machine sealing performance test).

Here, readers are reminded that in GB/T 32217—2015 (Hydraulic Transmission - Sealing Devices - Test Methods for Evaluating the Performance of Hydraulic Reciprocating Motion Seals), the test medium temperature is specified as 60-65°C, and the (maximum) test pressure as 31.5 MPa.

1) High Temperature and High Pressure O-rings. As shown in Figure 2-76, high temperature and high pressure static seals using O-rings must be equipped with retaining rings. For bidirectional sealing, one (including paired) or two retaining rings (combined) are installed on both sides of the O-ring; for unidirectional sealing, one (including paired) or two retaining rings (combined) are installed on the side where the O-ring may be extruded.

A more serious problem is that some domestic seal manufacturers specify the working temperature range of coaxial seals as -55 to 260°C, which may require more sets of seals to adapt to the above temperature. Therefore, special attention must be paid when designing and using coaxial seals.

② Lip Seals. Although the working temperature ranges of polyurethane lip seals are different in various standards and product samples (see Table 2-146), it is still dangerous to use them for reciprocating motion seals in hydraulic cylinders with a maximum working temperature >90°C and a maximum working pressure >31.5 MPa.

Fluororubber lip seals with retaining rings can be used for high-temperature and high-pressure sealing in hydraulic cylinders, but some specifications and varieties need to be specially ordered from seal manufacturers.
Other lip seals made of high-temperature resistant sealing materials such as perfluoroelastomer (FFKM) and fluorosilicone rubber (FVQM) almost all need to be specially ordered.

③ Dust Seals. In the sealing system of hydraulic cylinders, dust seals not only have a dust-proof function but may also have an auxiliary sealing function; in addition, due to the heat conduction effect of metal parts, dust seals on high-temperature hydraulic cylinders also have to withstand high temperatures.

Due to the sealing material (generally nitrile rubber or polyurethane rubber) of rubber dust seals specified in GB/T10798.3-2000, they usually cannot meet the working conditions requirements of high-temperature and high-pressure hydraulic cylinders.
