2.10.6 Common Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Structure Types
1. Definition of Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing System

In hydraulic cylinder sealing and design, professional terms or vocabulary such as sealing components (rings), combined sealing components (rings), composite sealing rings, and sealing devices are often used. Nowadays, the term "hydraulic cylinder sealing system" is frequently used in domestic and foreign sealing component product samples, including in standards. However, this term has not been defined in any domestic standard so far.

The author attempts to give the following definition of the term "hydraulic cylinder sealing system", which is a configuration of sealing components arranged in series according to the requirements of hydraulic cylinder sealing to generate sealing, control leakage, and/or prevent pollution.

It should be noted that the sealing components here specifically refer to the general term for sealing rings, retaining rings, support rings (guide rings), and dust seals used on hydraulic cylinders. That is, the sealing device is a device composed of one or more sealing components and supporting parts (such as retaining rings, springs, metal shells), plus guide rings, support rings, and support rings.

The term "hydraulic cylinder sealing system" has its definite connotation and extension. Its connotation is:
1) It must be a configuration of two or more sealing components. A single sealing component cannot be called a sealing system.
2) Two or more sealing components used to seal the same leakage gap (or mating gap) can only be arranged in series (configured).

296.page_header: Chapter 2  Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Basic Components  285

sections.text: For back-to-back piston seals, strictly speaking, they cannot be called a sealing system. However, for convenience of expression, this manual sometimes also classifies the seal configurations described in 1) and 2) above as part of the piston seal system.
3) A hydraulic cylinder sealing system generally consists of two sub-sealing systems: the piston sealing system and the piston rod sealing system.
4) The hydraulic cylinder sealing system must meet the sealing (performance) requirements of the hydraulic cylinder.
5) The emphasis of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system (feature) is the coordination and unified configuration among various sealing elements.
Its extension is: applicable to cylinder seals. To express the sealing system in hydraulic cylinder sealing and its design, the following representation methods are established:

1) The piston sealing system is described starting from the oil port of the rodless chamber of the hydraulic cylinder, and the piston rod sealing system is described starting from the nearest seal to the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder (rod chamber).
2) For double-rod cylinders, the piston sealing system is described starting from the seal nearest to the oil port on the left side of the drawing.
3) Sealing elements with defined (symbol) are represented according to the definition; those without defined (symbol) are expressed in Chinese, and series configuration is indicated by the "+" sign.
4) Sealing elements assembled on the same component are generally described in one sealing system.

5) The applicable conditions for the sealing system are tentatively set as: maximum working pressure or pressure range, maximum working temperature or temperature range, and maximum reciprocating motion speed or speed range.
The applicable conditions for the sealing system can be further referenced in Table 2-157 "Summary of Rated Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Design."

6) The hydraulic working medium for hydraulic cylinders is generally hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with equivalent performance. If other working media are used, such as water-ethylene glycol, phosphate ester fire-resistant hydraulic fluids, etc., they need to be specifically noted.

sections.text: 2.10.7 Several Specific Issues in Hydraulic Cylinder Seal System Design
1. Groove Spacing Problem

Determining the minimum distance between (seal) grooves is a common problem encountered in hydraulic cylinder seal system design. Reasonable design of groove spacing can achieve the optimal structural dimensions of the hydraulic cylinder while ensuring reliable sealing, thereby achieving optimized design of the hydraulic cylinder seal system structure. Hydraulic cylinder seal system design not only includes the arrangement (configuration) of each sealing element, but also the determination of spacing between sealing elements. Only by ensuring the dimensional and shape stability of each (seal) groove can the sealing performance of the piston seal system or piston rod seal system be guaranteed.

The side wall of the groove on the part body is generally called the edge wall. If the strength and rigidity of the edge wall are insufficient, the groove side may bend, or even the edge wall may be sheared, leading to seal failure.

In the design of hydraulic cylinder piston rod seal system, for the spacing between seal grooves (including dust seal ring) of two coaxial sealing elements in the piston rod seal system, if only considering strength and rigidity, it should generally not be less than the depth of the deepest groove among them. In the design of hydraulic cylinder piston seal system, due to the action of alternating pressure, if the groove spacing between sealing elements is only considered from the perspective of strength and rigidity, it should be at least greater than 1.5 times the depth of the deepest groove among them.

The spacing between support ring and other sealing elements is generally 1.5 to 2 times the depth of the support ring installation groove. Under special circumstances, necessary strength calculations should be performed on the edge wall.

(2) Support Ring Arrangement Issues

The design of hydraulic cylinder sealing systems emphasizes holistic thinking and focuses on the coordination and unified configuration among various seals or sealing devices, including the arrangement of support rings.

Whether it is a piston sealing system or a piston rod sealing system, it is not possible to simply consider its own guidance and support, but should take the hydraulic cylinder as a whole and consider (design) it uniformly.
Under the premise that the hydraulic cylinder design should be as compact as possible, the arrangement of support rings should generally follow the following principles:

304.page_header: Chapter 2  Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Components  293

items: The piston seal system or piston rod seal system itself should have maximum guidance and support.
The piston or piston rod must have maximum guidance and support.
The sealing medium should preferably pass through a (anti-contamination) support ring before acting on other sealing elements.
It is best to have a support ring in front of the buffer seal ring as well.
It is best to have a support ring between other sealing elements, including between the dust seal and other sealing elements.

sections.text: When support rings are arranged in series, the one with lower material hardness should be subjected to the sealing medium first, i.e., placed in front.
3. Opening of leakage channels
As shown in Figure 2-79, if possible, it is best to open a leakage channel in front of the dust seal.

sections.caption: Figure 2-79 Opening of leakage channel in front of dust seal
sections.description: A cross-sectional technical diagram showing the positioning of a leakage channel before a dust seal in a hydraulic cylinder assembly.

sections.text: This is because: 1) A single-lip rubber dust seal only has a dust-proof function, and does not have an auxiliary sealing function. 2) Even when using a double-lip rubber dust seal, it is very difficult to achieve "zero" leakage. 3) Even if the external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder is "zero" under a certain specific working condition, once the working condition changes (such as an increase in oil temperature), external leakage may occur, only the amount of leakage varies.

Precisely because of this, only by channeling the "leaking oil" in front of the dust seal through a leakage channel directly into an open oil tank or other open container can the dust seal always seal the hydraulic oil at "zero" pressure, and its sealing performance can be maintained for a relatively long time. The external leakage at the piston rod can be guaranteed to be minimal or "zero" under changing working conditions.
If a leakage channel is opened in front of the dust seal, the dust seal used should be a double-lip nitrile rubber seal.

It should be noted here: ① In the schematic diagram of the test device specified in GB/T32217—2016, the setting position of the "leakage measurement port" has important reference value for the setting of other hydraulic cylinder leakage channels, and its specified "leakage collection area" (for a piston rod diameter of Φ36 mm and a length of (20 mm ± 5 mm)) is also very important. ② Some products now open the leakage channel in front of the second seal ring of the piston rod seal system, which is incorrect.
4. Selection of single and double lip dust seals
The dust seal is an important component of the piston rod seal system and should receive due attention.

GB/T10708.3—2000 "Rubber Seals for Reciprocating Motion - Part 3: Rubber Dust Seals" stipulates three basic types of dust seals, two of which are single-lip dust seals and one is a double-lip dust seal.

In the piston rod seal system, whether a single-lip or double-lip dust seal is used, it is very difficult to achieve "zero" leakage at the piston rod, only that the single-lip dust seal may be leaking continuously; while the double-lip dust seal may occasionally experience a large amount of leakage once.

In the piston rod seal system with coaxial sealing elements (the coaxial sealing element is close to the dust seal), regardless of whether this coaxial sealing element has a "rod return" function, a double-lip dust seal should be used.
In the piston rod seal system with lip seals (the lip seal is close to the dust seal), a single-lip dust seal should generally be used.

Single-lip dust seals and double-lip dust seals are also often referred to as single-acting dust seals and double-acting dust seals. During the return stroke of the cylinder (rod retraction), the dust seal has the function of scraping contaminants on the piston rod, such as mud, dust, and condensed water; the other function of the double-acting dust seal is to scrape off the oil film that leaks after being sealed by other sealing elements, further optimizing the sealing performance of the sealing system. However, regardless of whether it is a single-acting or double-acting dust seal, taking the dust seal specified in GB/T10708.3—2000 as an example, if the pressure it bears is too high, it may be squeezed out of the groove.
Dust seals generally do not have specified applicable pressures or rated pressures. Even double-lip dust seals mainly scrape oil rather than seal, or have an auxiliary sealing function.

Commonly used nitrile rubber dust seals and polyurethane rubber dust seals require lubrication. Because the sliding ring material of the sliding ring dust seal may be filled with polytetrafluoroethylene, the requirements for lubrication are not very strict. Dust seals lacking lubrication have a shorter service life, especially polyurethane dust seals, which may also produce abnormal noise during the reciprocating motion of the piston rod.
2.10.8 Preliminary determination of sealing conditions for hydraulic cylinders

The sealing conditions of a hydraulic cylinder are a set of characteristic values that the hydraulic cylinder experiences when performing its sealing function. The sealing performance of the hydraulic cylinder in testing and operation must meet the specified conditions, among which the rated conditions are the design basis to ensure that the hydraulic cylinder has sufficient sealing life.

When designing the seal for a hydraulic cylinder, the first step is to determine the specified conditions. The allowable leakage of the hydraulic cylinder seal is also given under the specified conditions. The actual working conditions of the hydraulic cylinder are generally difficult to determine, that is, the specified conditions and actual conditions are different. This is because the extreme conditions of the hydraulic cylinder seal are

(Extreme) operating conditions are difficult to predict, such as the instantaneous extreme velocity of piston and piston rod movement, sudden changes in hydraulic working medium and environmental temperature and conditions, sudden changes in external loads especially extreme side loads (eccentric loads) and pressure peak fluctuations, contamination caused by environmental changes, etc. These extreme operating conditions may occur for a very short time and be unrepeatable, but they can indeed cause hydraulic cylinder seal failure, and even develop into accidents.

Any sealing device or sealing system has the possibility of leakage and cannot adapt to all operating conditions, so it is very important to specify operating conditions in hydraulic cylinder seal design.
1. Specified operating conditions for hydraulic cylinder seals
Specified operating conditions are the operating conditions that the hydraulic cylinder must meet during operation or testing.
(1) Specified operating conditions in JB/T 10205-2010

JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" is applicable to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure below 31.5 MPa and hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium.
The basic parameters of the hydraulic cylinder include bore diameter, piston rod diameter, nominal pressure, stroke, installation dimensions, etc.

items: Pressure: ① The nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2346. ② The piston of the hydraulic cylinder is stopped at both ends of the stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder is at the extreme position of the stroke), and hydraulic oil with 1.5 times the nominal pressure is applied to the working chamber respectively. After a type test pressure retention of 2 min and a factory test pressure retention of 10 s, there should be no external leakage or component damage. ③ When the bore diameter of the hydraulic cylinder is greater than 32mm, under the minimum pressure of 0.5MPa; when the bore diameter of the hydraulic cylinder is less than or equal to 32mm, under the pressure of 1MPa, make the hydraulic cylinder reciprocate its full stroke more than 3 times, and stay at the end of the stroke for 10s each time. During the test process, it should comply with: a. The hydraulic cylinder should have no vibration or crawling. b. There should be no hydraulic oil leakage at the piston rod seal. At the end of the test, the oil film on the piston rod should be insufficient to form oil droplets or oil rings. c. There should be no hydraulic oil leakage at all static seals and welds. d. There should be no hydraulic oil leakage in the throttling and (or) cushioning components installed on the hydraulic cylinder.
Kinematic viscosity of hydraulic oil: When the oil temperature is 40°C, the kinematic viscosity should be 29-74mm²/s.

Working medium temperature: ① Generally, the working medium temperature of the hydraulic cylinder should be in the range of -20-80°C; ② Under the nominal pressure, input hydraulic oil at 90°C into the hydraulic cylinder, and reciprocate the full stroke for 1h, which should comply with the agreement between the manufacturer and the user.
Ambient temperature: Generally, the working ambient temperature of the hydraulic cylinder should be in the range of -20-50°C.

sections.text: 5) Speed: Under the nominal pressure, the hydraulic cylinder runs continuously at the highest speed required by the design, with a speed error of ±10%, and runs continuously for more than 8h each time. During the test, no adjustment shall be made to the components of the hydraulic cylinder, and the cumulative stroke or reversing times shall be recorded. After the test, all requirements shall comply with the durability requirements of the hydraulic cylinder.
(2) Specified operating conditions in the standards of various sealing elements

sections.text: 2. Extreme Operating Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Seals

Extreme operating conditions refer to the maximum and/or minimum operating conditions that components, piping, or systems are allowed to operate under extreme conditions specified for a given application for a given time. For example, the pressure test for hydraulic cylinders is: "Apply hydraulic oil at 1.5 times the nominal pressure to the working chambers respectively, and hold pressure for 10 s during factory testing, with no external leakage or component damage." Since overpressure may also occur during pressure testing, generally overpressure ≤10%. To describe this situation, the operating conditions that occur instantaneously under extreme conditions are temporarily referred to as extreme conditions.
Extreme conditions should include:

items: Pressure peak: A pressure pulse that exceeds the corresponding steady-state pressure and even exceeds the maximum pressure.
Pressure intensification: Pressure intensification caused by piston area difference exceeding the rated pressure limit.
Gravity velocity: The extreme velocity at which free fall (gravity) acceleration gn=9.80665 m/s² operates.

Ultra-low speed: When the inner diameter D of the hydraulic cylinder ≤200 mm, the lowest stable speed of the hydraulic cylinder is <4 mm/s; when the inner diameter D of the hydraulic cylinder >200 mm, the lowest stable speed of the hydraulic cylinder is <5 mm/s.

Excessive internal leakage during stroke: For hydraulic cylinders with a stroke exceeding 1 m, in addition to larger internal leakage at both ends of the stroke, the maximum internal leakage may occur at the middle position of the stroke.
Excessive leakage at low pressure: When the working pressure is lower than 0.5 MPa (or 1 MPa), the leakage at low pressure may exceed the standard.
Excessive operating temperature range: When the operating temperature is lower than -30°C or higher than 90°C.
Overload: In applications where overload or other external loads may be encountered, the design and installation of hydraulic cylinders should consider the maximum expected load or pressure peak.
Lateral or bending loads: Excessive deformation of the hydraulic cylinder structure due to structural design, installation, or alignment reasons.
Shock and vibration: Shock and vibration beyond the specified conditions of the hydraulic cylinder itself or its connecting parts.

sections.text: 3. Preliminary Determination of Rated Operating Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Seals

Rated operating conditions are the conditions indicated by the highest and lowest values (when necessary) of basic characteristics determined through testing. Components or piping are designed according to these conditions to ensure sufficient service life. However, in reality, some conditions, especially extreme conditions, are unrepeatable and therefore cannot be tested. The design of hydraulic cylinder seals must provide specified conditions, but the specified conditions are a relatively ideal condition, and it is difficult to accurately provide them in actual design. Rated conditions can be gradually corrected based on testing, although some conditions, such as extreme conditions, cannot be tested. However, if the rated operating conditions for hydraulic cylinder seals are not specified, the hydraulic cylinder cannot be designed. Therefore, based on years of experience in hydraulic cylinder design practice, the author has referred to relevant standards, literature, and a large number of product samples from seal manufacturers, and has designed Table 2-157 for reference by hydraulic cylinder seal designers when determining the rated operating conditions for hydraulic cylinder seals.

2.10.9  Comparison and Analysis of Sealing Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders and Selection of Seals for Servo Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Comparison and Analysis of Sealing Technical Requirements for Servo Hydraulic Cylinders

DB44/T 1169.1-2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinders Part 1: Technical Conditions" (has been abolished, for reference only) stipulates the technical requirements for single and double acting servo hydraulic cylinders. The technical requirements related to servo hydraulic cylinder seals mainly include: minimum starting pressure, internal leakage, load efficiency, external leakage, durability, pressure resistance, load-carrying dynamic friction force, and leakage under low pressure. Judging only from the technical requirements stipulated in this standard, the technical requirements for seals account for most of the content.

(3) Comparison and Analysis of Load Efficiency

Load efficiency is not specified in GB/T24946-2010. In GB/T13342-2007, JB/T10205-2010, and DB44/T11169.1-2013, the specified load efficiency requirements are that the load efficiency of hydraulic cylinders should not be less than 90%, the load efficiency of hydraulic cylinders should not be less than 90%, and the load efficiency of servo hydraulic cylinders should not be less than 90%, respectively.

In GB/T17446-2012, the general terminology related to efficiency is cylinder output force efficiency. Static pressure support structures for piston rods are frequently used in electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders. These structures incur certain hydraulic power losses whether using internal or external oil supply. Additionally, electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders may have holes drilled in pistons to improve system stability, which also causes certain hydraulic power losses. Therefore, an indicator should be provided to reflect or calibrate the (total) efficiency of electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders, providing a comprehensive evaluation of the utilization rate of input hydraulic power.
(4) Comparison and Analysis of External Leakage

External leakage is not specified in GB/T24946-2010, but sealing performance is specified, stating that when digital cylinders are subjected to 1.25 times the nominal pressure, there should be no external leakage at all mating surfaces. JB/T10205-2010 specifies that piston rods (plunger rods) should not leak when stationary; DB44/T11169.1-2013 specifies that other parts should not leak when piston rods (plunger rods) are stationary; GB/T13342-2007 specifies that hydraulic cylinders should not leak externally at all seals and during movement.

For hydraulic cylinder piston rods, when the piston rod is moving, it is very difficult to achieve "zero" leakage. The so-called "zero" leakage condition theoretically occurs when the amount of hydraulic oil carried out by the rod equals the amount carried back, and this condition disappears immediately when conditions change. Additionally, using "seepage" to describe the (external) leakage of hydraulic cylinder piston rods is not entirely appropriate. It is more suitable to express the leakage amount at the piston rod using Table 2-161.

sections.text: (5) Comparison and Analysis of Durability
In GB/T 24946—2010, the durability specified for digital cylinders is that the service life under rated operating conditions should have a total accumulated stroke of not less than 10^5m.

The durability indicators specified in JB/T 10205—2010 and DB44/T 1169.1—2013 are completely identical. In GB/T 13342—2007, the durability specified, except for single-acting piston cylinders or single-acting servo hydraulic cylinders, is the same as that specified in JB/T 10205—2010 and DB44/T 1169.1—2013 for other types, but the durability requirements for plunger hydraulic cylinders are different, being "the external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder should not exceed 2 times the specified value."

The specification in GB/T 13342—2007 for the "external leakage" of plunger hydraulic cylinders after durability testing is more reasonable, because whether it is a single-acting plunger hydraulic cylinder or a single-acting servo hydraulic cylinder, there cannot be any internal leakage or increase in internal leakage after durability testing or before durability testing. Therefore, the requirement in JB/T 10205—2010 and DB44/T 1169.1—2013 that "after durability testing, the increase in internal leakage should not exceed 2 times the specified value, and components should not have abnormal wear or other forms of damage" is not entirely reasonable.

GB/T 13342—2007 specifies the "external leakage" of plunger hydraulic cylinders after durability testing, which is also one of the reasons this manual references this standard. Otherwise, there would be no basis for determining the external leakage of plunger servo hydraulic cylinders after durability testing.
(6) Comparison and Analysis of Pressure Resistance

The pressure resistance requirement specified in GB/T 13342—2007 is that the hydraulic cylinder should withstand 1.5 times the nominal pressure without any component damage or permanent deformation, and without any leakage at gaskets and welds.

The pressure resistance requirements specified in GB/T 24946—2010 and DB44/T 1169.1—2013 are basically the same, being that the digital cylinder should withstand 1.5 times the nominal pressure (pressure holding for 5 min), without any component damage or permanent deformation, without any leakage at welds, and the cylinder body of the servo hydraulic cylinder should withstand 1.5 times the nominal pressure, without any external leakage, component deformation, or damage during pressure holding for 5 min.

In JB/T 10205—2010, during pressure testing, the tested hydraulic cylinder piston should be stopped at both ends of the stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at extreme position), and hydraulic fluid at 1.5 times the nominal pressure should be applied to the working chamber, with a pressure holding time of 2 min for type testing and 10 s for factory testing, without any external leakage or component damage.
Comparing the above four standards, the pressure resistance specified in JB/T 10205—2010 is more reasonable in terms of pressure holding time.
(7) Comparison and Analysis of Leakage at Low Pressure
GB/T 13342—2007 does not specify leakage at low pressure; GB/T 24946—2010 also does not specify leakage at low pressure.

The leakage at low pressure specified in JB/T 10205—2010 is: when the hydraulic cylinder bore is greater than 32mm, at the lowest pressure of 0.5MPa; when the hydraulic cylinder bore is less than or equal to 32mm, at a pressure of 1MPa, the hydraulic cylinder should reciprocate through its full stroke 3 or more times, with each end of the stroke held for at least 10s. During the test, it should meet the following requirements: b) no hydraulic fluid leakage at the piston rod seal, and at the end of the test, the oil film on the piston rod should not be sufficient to form oil drops or an oil ring; c) no hydraulic fluid leakage at all static seals and welds.

The leakage at low pressure specified in DB44/T 1169.1—2013 is: during testing of the servo hydraulic cylinder at a pressure of 3MPa, the oil cylinder should have no external leakage; at the end of the test, no oil drops or oil rings are allowed at the extended piston rod.

Comparing JB/T 10205—2010 and DB44/T 1169.1—2013, the requirements for leakage at low pressure specified in these two standards are basically the same, but the description of hydraulic cylinder piston rod leakage is better. Based on the above comparison and analysis, the main difference in the sealing technical requirements specified in DB44/T 1169.1—2013 compared to those specified in other standards is in the "minimum starting pressure."

Further analysis of this main difference: Since servo hydraulic cylinders have dynamic performance requirements, their step response and frequency response both specify technical requirements (indicators). If the starting pressure is too high, the response speed will definitely be low. However, except for piston clearance seals, the minimum starting pressure indicators for combined seals specified in DB44/T 1169.1—2013 are almost 1/10 or even lower than the indicators specified in current hydraulic cylinder standards, which raises questions about whether such a specification is reasonable from the perspective of servo hydraulic cylinder designers and manufacturers.
2. Selection of Seals for Servo Hydraulic Cylinders

Only referring to the products of a foreign seal manufacturer, based on the technical requirements for seals of servo (control) hydraulic cylinders, some piston combination seals are screened. However, if seals are selected according to the definition of "combination seal" in DB44/T 1169.1—2013, it will be very difficult because the definition of combination seal given in this standard lacks the most basic connotation.

Still according to the definition of "combination seal" in GB/T 17446—2012, which is "a sealing device consisting of two or more units of different materials," seals are selected as shown in Table 2-162.

Sealing and friction are two aspects of the same issue and mutually restrict each other. If good sealing is required, the friction force may be large. Excessive pursuit of a low minimum starting pressure (which should be starting pressure, see GB/T 17446—2012) has little significance in hydraulic cylinder sealing, and this is also true for servo hydraulic cylinders, because the ratio of minimum starting pressure to nominal pressure is very small.
The minimum starting pressure indicator specified in DB44/T 1169.1—2013 is too low, which is unscientific and unnecessary.

sections.text: 2.11 Design of Hydraulic Cylinder Piston Rod Hydrostatic Support Structure
1. General

The working principle of the piston rod hydrostatic support structure (hydraulic hydrostatic sliding bearing guiding the piston rod) is that the support force on the piston rod is mainly generated by external pressurized oil, rather than generated by the relative motion between the piston rod and its hydrostatic support sleeve (i.e., hydrodynamic effect).

The hydraulic hydrostatic bearing shaft in the sliding bearing guides the piston rod to reciprocate while bearing the loads acting on the piston rod. The piston rod hydrostatic support structure discussed in this manual includes the hydrostatic sliding bearing guiding the piston rod and its sliding contact components.

Generally, the design of piston rod hydrostatic support structures should follow these principles: under the maximum load that may be encountered, the minimum oil film thickness should at least maintain lubricating oil film thickness of 50%~60%.

In design, the eccentricity ratio (where the load eccentricity is the relative eccentricity ratio e = e/C₀) is limited to e = 0~0.5 in the range; the flow rate designed for the medium should be the set flow rate. This is because the hydrostatic support's ability to compensate for special eccentricity is at its strongest. It is also necessary to consider the hydrostatic support structure's load-bearing capacity, and there must be sufficient consideration for the forces acting in the oil cavity due to oil and the load acting on the oil cavity surface due to tightening, as well as the situation of reduced rigidity. It is especially important to note that one type of phenomenon is the eccentricity of the piston rod bending deflection leading to an offset from the center, and in the case of the piston rod hydrostatic support sleeve edge contact friction type hydrostatic support structure.

The design and calculation of the piston rod hydrostatic support structure is established on the basis of static (including front and boundary condition requirements). Whether enough determination of its operating parameters and operating conditions, geometry and shape, oil supply capacity, eccentricity ratio, load-bearing capacity, oil temperature and other functional relationships, as well as oil supply pressure, flow rate, friction power, temperature rise and other parameters, often needs to be verified by actual machines.
2. Structural Types

In common piston rod hydrostatic support bearing designs, the hydrostatic support sleeve has oil grooves between them, with 4 oil cavities or more (even number of cavities). The oil cavity depth is the groove depth (diameter direction C₀) 10 times or more, and the length-to-diameter ratio B/D is 0.3~1. This is the most commonly used structural type for this application.

This type, with and without oil return grooves, has a similar structure; under the same return oil pressure conditions, the type without oil return grooves requires a larger oil supply flow rate. The hydrostatic support sleeve is connected to the cylinder head by means of possible connections. As follows:
Using medium-type press-fit assembly, take necessary measures to prevent extreme working conditions from causing connection failure (loosening) or even total failure.
3. Basic Parameters

The basic parameters of piston rod hydrostatic support structure include: hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter D₁, outer diameter D₀, width B, number of oil cavities Z, axial oil seal strip width b₁, circumferential oil seal strip width b₂, oil return groove width, oil cavity depth, oil return groove depth (equivalent to the bearing return pressure), and throttle type (such as small orifice throttle type, capillary tube type, internal feedback type, etc.). Refer to page 5.
4. Materials

Hydrostatic support sleeve (i.e., bearing sleeve) material: cast alloy conforms to the requirements of GB/T 18324-2001; cast copper alloy conforms to JB/T 7921-1995 requirements; forged copper alloy conforms to JB/T 7922-1995 requirements.
5. Dimensions, Fits and Tolerances
In design, the hydrostatic support sleeve inner bore centerline is generally determined as the reference for the following requirements:
1) Hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter
The hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter D₀ should preferably be selected from Table 2-189 recommended values.

2) Hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter D₀ dimensional tolerances.
Hydrostatic support sleeve inner diameter D₀ tolerance zone should be selected according to GB/T 1801-2009 specified H7 or H8, which can be combined with the piston rod.
Select H7/h6, H8/h7, but ensure the designed clearance (equivalent to bearing clearance) through matching.
Refer to GB/T 28279.1—2012 for bearing clearance.

(2) Outer diameter D₀ of hydrostatic bearing sleeve. The wall thickness [(D₀-D_B)/2] of the hydrostatic bearing sleeve should be thick enough to ensure no excessive deformation during installation and use, especially within the specified environmental temperature and working medium temperature range.
The dimensional tolerance of the outer diameter of the hydrostatic bearing sleeve shall be determined according to the selected sealing requirements.
The symbol for the outer diameter D₀ of the integral metal bearing sleeve is specified in GB/T 27939—2011.

(3) Other parameters. Other parameters can be designed and calculated according to operating parameters, such as bearing capacity (load), reciprocating motion frequency (speed), working medium, oil supply pressure and temperature, etc. The design calculation results generally need to be verified on the actual machine.
(4) Geometric tolerances. 1) The cylindricity tolerance of the inner hole should not be lower than Grade 7 in GB/T 1184—1996.
2) The cylindricity tolerance of the outer circle should not be lower than Grade 7 in GB/T 1184—1996.
3) The concentricity (coaxiality tolerance) of the inner hole axis and the outer circle axis should not be lower than Grade 7 in GB/T 1184—1996.
4) The perpendicularity tolerance of the end face of the hydrostatic bearing sleeve to the inner hole axis should not be lower than Grade 7 in GB/T 1184—1996.
5) The runout of the outer end face of the hydrostatic bearing sleeve with flange to the inner hole axis should not be lower than Grade 7 in GB/T 1184—1996.
6. Surface quality. There should be no surface defects caused by processing and subsequent treatment processes, such as cracks, scratches, burrs, metal deposits and protrusions, etc.

The surface roughness of the inner hole should not be greater than Ra0.8μm; the surface roughness of the outer circle should not be greater than Ra1.6μm; if there is a flange, the surface roughness of the inner end face of the flange should not be greater than Ra2.5μm, and the surface roughness of the outer end face should not be greater than Ra3.2μm; burrs should be removed from the edges.
Only slight scratches are allowed on the outer circular surface, and they should not affect assembly and performance.
7. Other requirements. For dimensions without given tolerances, their allowable deviations should comply with the tolerance grade "m" specified in GB/T 1804—2000.

The edges of the ports and grooves on the inner hole of the hydrostatic bearing sleeve should also be chamfered and rounded, and the rounded corners at both ends of the inner hole should be smooth, with the radius of the rounded corners meeting the requirements of the drawing.
2.12 Design of Hydraulic Cylinder Buffer Device
Buffering is a means to decelerate when a moving part (such as a piston) approaches the end of its stroke.

There are mainly two types: fixed (type) or adjustable (type), which are collectively classified as cylinders with buffers. The design of cylinders with fixed-type (hydraulic cylinder) buffer devices is one of the difficult points in hydraulic cylinder design.

For servo hydraulic cylinders, since soft limits can be set through the control system to avoid impact between moving parts and other cylinder parts, i.e., the working stroke range of the cylinder can be controlled, for some hydraulic cylinders with low movement speed, small moving part mass, or considering that even in special cases, collision will not cause external leakage of the cylinder and damage to cylinder parts, etc., it can be considered not to install a hydraulic cylinder buffer device.

The technical requirements for hydraulic cylinder buffer devices are generally derived from the technical conditions (requirements) of hydraulic machines (equipment), and should be adapted to the technical conditions (requirements) of the host machine. For example, in JB/T 3818—2014 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Presses", the following specific provisions are made for hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses: hydraulic driving elements (such as pistons, columns, sliders, moving worktables, etc.) should not have vibration, crawling, and stagnation phenomena within the specified stroke and speed range, and should not have impact phenomena that affect normal operation during commutation and pressure relief.
2.12.1 Technical Requirements for Fixed-Type Buffer Devices for Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Technical requirements for fixed-type buffer devices specified in various standards

For cylinders with fixed-type buffer devices, their buffering performance cannot be adjusted online, and this does not include the situation where the buffering performance is changed by changing the viscosity of the working medium (hydraulic oil).
In the product standards for hydraulic cylinders, there are two standards that put forward technical requirements for fixed-type hydraulic cylinder buffer devices:

items: In CB/T 3812—2013 "Hydraulic Cylinder for Hatch Cover of Ships", it is stipulated that under the condition that the test hydraulic cylinder is input with a pressure of 50% of the nominal pressure, and tested at the designed highest speed, the buffering effect is that the piston should be smooth and slow when entering the buffer area.

In QC/T 460—2010 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders for Dump Trucks", it is stipulated that when the hydraulic cylinder is fully extended, the piston rod should extend and retract at a speed of 50~70mm/s, and there should be no impact sound when the hydraulic cylinder automatically stops.

sections.text: 2. General technical requirements for buffer devices

In addition to the above-mentioned performance requirements for fixed-type hydraulic cylinder buffer devices specified in the standards, the following basic performance requirements should be met as much as possible when designing fixed-type hydraulic cylinder buffer devices:

items: The buffer device should be able to absorb the maximum kinetic energy with a shorter buffer length of the cylinder (also called buffer stroke), that is, the kinetic energy of the moving parts (including various connecting parts or related parts) should be completely converted into thermal energy.
During the buffering process, pressure pulsation and excessively high peak pressure in the buffer cavity should be avoided as much as possible, so that the change in pressure is a gradual process.
The peak buffering pressure in the buffer cavity (rodless end) should be less than or equal to 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.

324.page_header: Chapter 2  Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Basic Components  313

sections.text: 4) When a buffer device is installed at the rodless end, the buffer pressure should avoid acting on the dynamic seal system of the piston rod.

5) The conversion of kinetic energy into thermal energy causes the hydraulic oil temperature to rise, and the maximum oil temperature should not exceed the maximum allowable operating temperature of the seal.

6) According to JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", when the hydraulic cylinder has requirements for buffer performance, it should be determined through negotiation between the user and the manufacturer.

7) The starting performance of the hydraulic cylinder should be considered, and the minimum starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the provisions of relevant standards; Abnormal situations such as delayed movement or abnormal movement, and abnormal noise should be avoided when the piston starts or leaves the buffer zone.
3. Ideal Buffer Performance Expected in Buffer Device Design

items: Adapt to working condition changes and can be adjusted within a certain range, such as changes in hydraulic oil viscosity, ambient temperature changes, changes in the speed of the piston at the beginning of buffering, changes in the return pressure of the hydraulic cylinder, changes in the gravity of related moving parts, etc.
During the buffering process, maintain a constant buffer pressure, and the deceleration of the piston is constant.
During buffering, the temperature rise of the hydraulic oil should not exceed 55°C, and the maximum temperature should not exceed 80°C.
If there is a pressure peak in the buffer cavity, it should not be greater than 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.
When the piston reaches the end of the cylinder return stroke, its moving speed should be zero, and there should be no abnormal noise or rebound.
There should be no abnormal noise or abnormal movement when the cylinder process starts, that is, there should be no excessive buffering problem.
The structure should be simple, easy to adjust, low manufacturing cost, and facilitate mass processing and manufacturing.

sections.text: 4. Design Principles of Hydraulic Cylinder Buffer Device

items: When the moving speed of the hydraulic cylinder piston is ≤100 mm/s, it can be considered not to install a buffer device; When the moving speed of the piston is >200 mm/s, a buffer device must be installed.

For double-acting hydraulic cylinders without a variable throttle buffer device at the rodless end, the most ideal buffer plunger is a concave parabolic shape. Therefore, efforts should be made to design and process the buffer plunger to be close to a concave parabolic shape (mainly using a conical or double-conical shape).
The end of the buffer plunger should not hit the cylinder bottom, and the buffer device should be protected during structural design.
The speed after buffering and restarting should not be too fast, and the buffer side (rodless end) should not be subjected to cavitation.
When a buffer device is installed at the rodless end, the buffer pressure should avoid acting on the dynamic seal system of the piston rod.
Comply with the general technical requirements for hydraulic cylinder buffer device design.

sections.text: 5. Basis for Hydraulic Cylinder Buffer Device Design
1) Moving speed of moving parts. If the cylinder is fixed and the piston rod is in the return stroke, the return speed of the piston rod is the basis for design.

2) Mass of moving parts. If the cylinder is fixed and the piston rod is in the return stroke, the mass of the piston rod is the basis for design; If the piston rod is connected to a slider, the mass of the slider should also be considered; If two (or more) cylinders control one slider, the mass conversion should also be included.
3) Load (gravity) and the direction of motion speed, such as whether it is an overload.
4) The (control) pressure and flow rate of the other cavity of the hydraulic cylinder during buffering.
5) Control method for buffering stop (end).
6) The situation (requirements) of restarting after buffering should not only consider the buffering effect but also the starting effect.
7) Temperature change range of hydraulic oil.
8) Expected design life of the buffer device.
2.12.2 Design Calculation of Fixed Buffer Device at Rodless End of Double-acting Hydraulic Cylinder
1. General Calculation of Buffer Pressure for Hydraulic Cylinder Buffer Device

As shown in Figure 2-80, a fixed constant throttle buffer device at the rodless end of a hydraulic cylinder is shown, which has just started to enter the buffer, and the hydraulic cylinder has started to brake.

sections.text: In the case of hydraulic cylinder buffer braking, the kinetic equation of the hydraulic cylinder piston is
A₁p₁×10⁶-A₂p₂×10⁶-Apc×10⁶±R=Gdv/gdt=G/g×a
Several points of explanation:

items: Dynamics foundation. The above formula is derived from the dynamics formula F=ma, that is, the force that acts on an object with a mass of 1 kg and causes it to produce an acceleration of 1 m/s² is 1 N, and F=d(mv)/dt, the resultant force acting on an object equals the rate of change of the object's momentum.

sections.text: 2) Explanations and Notes on the Terms in the Formula
A₁p₁—The return force acting on the piston, whose direction is the same as the piston movement (speed) direction, reducing the piston's buffer stroke.

A₂p₂—The pressure acting on the buffer plunger head, i.e., the hydraulic cylinder's exhaust pressure; its direction is opposite to the piston movement (speed) direction, having a braking effect, but usually very small, even zero.

Apc—The braking force acting on the piston, whose direction is opposite to the piston movement (speed) direction, varying with the instantaneous buffer pressure pc in the buffer cavity, playing a major braking role for the moving parts.
G/g—The mass of all related moving parts converted to the piston.
dv/dt—The acceleration of all related moving parts (equivalent mass) converted to the piston.
3) Precautions in Calculations

① p₁—The working pressure of the cylinder's return stroke generally changes during the buffering process. When using a hydraulic pump to provide hydraulic oil to the hydraulic cylinder causing the cylinder to return, the working pressure of the cylinder's return stroke may increase due to buffering and braking, and the highest working pressure of the cylinder's return stroke is set by the relief valve (or safety valve) installed on the hydraulic system; under certain conditions, the cylinder's return stroke buffering and braking can cause the piston to decelerate, which also requires the relief valve (or safety valve) to relieve; when using an accumulator to provide hydraulic oil to the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder causing the cylinder to return, the accumulator pressure continuously decreases.

② pc—The (instantaneous) buffer pressure in the buffer cavity, with its maximum value being the pressure peak value pcmax in the buffer cavity. The pressure peak value pcmax in the buffer cavity is generally considered to occur at the beginning of buffering, but with different buffer plunger shapes, the position where the pressure peak value occurs (in terms of buffer stroke) also differs, which generally needs to be obtained through machine testing. The fixed buffer devices currently designed almost all have buffer pressure peaks, it's just that they need to be limited to pcmax ≤ 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.

③ R—The external load converted to the piston, which is the most difficult to accurately determine in buffer design calculations, among which the external friction force of the hydraulic cylinder is almost never the same, fortunately it plays a braking role here.

④ In buffer design calculations, some assumptions are often needed, such as the hydraulic oil being incompressible; the flow coefficient of the throttle orifice being constant; the flow through the throttle orifice being turbulent; the working pressure of the cylinder's return stroke remaining unchanged during buffering; the internal friction force (loaded kinetic friction force) of the hydraulic cylinder being small and negligible, etc.
⑤ Thermal rise verification of the hydraulic oil must be performed.
2. Design Calculations for Constant Throttle Buffer Devices for Hydraulic Cylinders

The so-called constant throttle buffer device refers to a buffer device whose throttle area remains unchanged during the buffering process of the hydraulic cylinder, such as throttle valve buffer devices, buffer plunger being cylindrical (buffer hole being a cylindrical hole, see Figure 2-80) buffer devices, etc.
For buffering using a constant throttle buffer device, assuming the average acceleration of the piston is am = -v₀²/2sc, then the average buffer pressure in the buffer cavity is
pcm = [A₁p₁sc + (1/2 × G/g × v₀² ± Rsc)] × 10⁻⁶ / Asc (MPa) (2-61)

The maximum value of the buffer pressure in the buffer cavity, i.e., the pressure peak value pcmax in the buffer cavity, generally occurs at the moment when the piston just enters the buffer (the buffer plunger just enters the buffer hole), assuming the acceleration at this time is a₀ = amax = 2am = -v₀²/sc (or the maximum absolute acceleration amax = v₀²/sc), then the pressure peak value in the buffer cavity (approximate calculation) is
pcmax = [A₁p₁sc + (G/g × v₀² ± Rsc)] × 10⁻⁶ / Asc (MPa) (2-62)

1) Formulas (2-61) to (2-62) all originate from the dynamic equation of the hydraulic cylinder piston, only with certain assumptions made about a. For example, assuming a = am = -v₀²/2sc, the formula for calculating the average buffer pressure in the buffer cavity (2-61) is derived; assuming a₀ = amax = -v₀²/sc, the formula for calculating the pressure peak value in the buffer cavity (approximate calculation) (2-62) is derived.

Formulas (2-61) to (2-62) can not only be used for estimating calculations for throttle valve buffering, but also for estimating calculations for other throttle buffering, such as annular gap constant (variable) throttle devices.
2) When using an annular gap constant throttle buffer device, the approximate calculation formula for the annular throttle gap (single side) δ is
δ = √(12qvmμsc / (pcmdmπ)) × 10⁻² (m) (2-63)
Since qvm = Av₀/2, and dm ≈ d, the above formula can be rewritten as
δ = √(6Av₀μsc / (pcmdπ)) × 10⁻² (m) (2-64)

d = (-δ³pcm × 10⁶ + √(δ⁶p²cm × 10¹² + 9D²v₀²μ²s²c)) / (3v₀μsc) (m) (2-66)

(1) Factors to be considered when designing the annular throttling gap (single side) δ:

1) When designing the annular throttling gap (single side) δ for a constant throttling buffer device, the following factors should be considered:
① A—The effective acting area of the buffer pressure on the piston.
② v₀—The buffer speed of the piston at the beginning of buffering.
③ μ—The dynamic viscosity of the hydraulic oil.
④ s_c—The buffer stroke of the piston.
⑤ p_cm—The average buffer pressure in the buffer chamber.
⑥ d or d_m—The diameter of the buffer plunger or the average diameter of the annular gap.

2) The relationship between the annular throttling gap (single side) δ of the constant throttling buffer device and the related factors is as follows:
① A—The larger the effective acting area of the buffer pressure on the piston, the larger the annular throttling gap (single side) δ can be. This point is of great significance in the engineering design of hydraulic cylinders.
② v₀—The higher the buffer speed of the piston at the beginning of buffering, the larger the annular throttling gap (single side) δ should be. Otherwise, the maximum value of the buffer pressure in the buffer chamber, i.e., the pressure peak p_cm_max, may be > 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder. This point often appears in the opposite design in hydraulic cylinder design.
③ μ—The larger the dynamic viscosity of the hydraulic oil, the larger the annular throttling gap (single side) δ should be.
④ s_c—The longer the buffer stroke of the piston, the smaller the annular throttling gap (single side) δ can be. When the annular throttling gap (single side) δ remains unchanged, changing the buffer stroke of the piston can change the buffer effect. This point is the theoretical basis for the patent design of the author.
⑤ p_cm—The higher the average buffer pressure, the smaller the annular throttling gap (single side) δ should be.
⑥ d—The larger the diameter of the buffer plunger, the smaller the annular throttling gap (single side) δ should be. The significance of this point in the engineering design of hydraulic cylinders is the same as ①.

(2) Several explanations:

1) The calculation formula for the annular throttling gap (single side) δ is derived from the flow calculation formula for fluid flow in a fixed-wall concentric annular gap.

2) The actual situation is definitely not a concentric annular gap, but should be an eccentric annular gap, and it is also a moving-wall eccentric annular gap. Please refer to Table 1-50 for details. The formula in Table 1-50 is calculated with the aperture of the (buffer) hole as a parameter, which is different from the buffer plunger diameter d mentioned in the above formula.

3) The calculation formula for the annular throttling gap (single side) δ can only be used for approximate calculation, not only for the above reasons, but also because the reason for the formation of the gap flow is not only the pressure difference flow caused by the pressure difference, but also the shear flow caused by the movement of the buffer plunger.

4) The gap (annular throttling gap) δ between the buffer plunger and the buffer hole (single side) should not be designed too small. According to the size and tolerance of the hydraulic cylinder and its parts and the requirements of geometric accuracy, it is generally taken as δ ≥ 0.10 ~ 0.12 mm. If δ is designed and selected too small, it may also cause collision or rubbing between the buffer plunger and the cylinder head (the buffer hole set on the bottom of the cylinder) due to reasons such as the assembly of the hydraulic cylinder assembly, the processing quality of each component, and the wear of the guide sleeve (ring) that may cause eccentricity.

5) Since the buffer oil volume in the buffer chamber is V = As_c = π(D²-d²)s_c/4, and the buffer time is t_c = 2s_c/v₀, then q_Vc = V/t_c = Av₀/2. Among them, the buffer chamber volume at the beginning of buffering, i.e., the buffer oil volume V, is of great significance in the engineering design of the hydraulic cylinder buffer device.

The buffer valve is typically installed on the piston, and the throttle valve is installed on the piston rod. The buffer valve can be a throttle valve or a throttle hole, and the throttle valve can be a throttle valve, a throttle hole (for cylindrical holes), or a buffer device with non-cylindrical throttle holes.

2.12.3 Technical Requirements for Buffer Devices with Buffer Valves in Hydraulic Cylinders

For hydraulic cylinders with adjustable buffer devices, their buffer performance can be adjusted online, and the buffer valve buffer device is such a buffer device, but the buffer valve (group) here is different from the buffer valve usually used in hydraulic systems.
In the product standards for hydraulic cylinders, the following three standards have proposed technical (test) requirements for buffer valve hydraulic cylinder buffer devices:

items: In GB/T15622-2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated that all buffer valves in the working chamber of the tested cylinder should be fully loosened, the test pressure should be adjusted to 50% of the nominal pressure, and the cylinder should be moved at the designed maximum speed to detect the buffer effect when the buffer valve is fully closed.

In JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", it is stipulated that all buffer valves in the working chamber of the tested cylinder should be fully loosened, the test pressure should be adjusted to 50% of the nominal pressure, and the cylinder should be moved at the designed maximum speed. When the buffer valve is fully closed, the buffer effect should meet the requirements of 6.2.8, i.e., the buffer performance requirements for hydraulic cylinders should be determined by negotiation between the user and the manufacturer. At the same time, it is required that the installed throttling and (or) buffer components have no hydraulic oil leakage.

In JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated that all buffer valves in the working chamber of the tested cylinder should be fully loosened, the test pressure should be adjusted to 50% of the nominal pressure, and the cylinder should be moved at the designed maximum speed to detect the buffer effect when the buffer valve is fully closed.

sections.text: Author's note: In JB/T11588-2013, there are no requirements for buffer effect or performance. Although GB/T15622-2005 is not quoted in the normative references of JB/T11588-2013, the content of technical requirements for buffering in the above three standards is almost the same. Regardless of whether the installed buffer device is a fixed or adjustable type, it should comply with the requirements of JB/T10205-2010, i.e., the installed throttling and (or) buffer components have no hydraulic oil (external) leakage.
2.13 Design and Selection of Sensors (Switches) for Hydraulic Cylinders
2.13.1 General Technical Requirements for Sensors Used in Hydraulic Cylinders

A sensor is a device or apparatus that can sense the measured object and convert it into a usable output signal according to a certain rule. It is usually composed of a sensitive element and a conversion element. Among them, the sensitive element refers to the part of the sensor that can directly sense or respond to the measured object; the conversion element refers to the part of the sensor that can convert the measured object sensed or responded by the sensitive element into an electrical signal suitable for transmission or measurement. When the output is a specified standard signal, the sensor is called a

sections.text: Sensor. The sensor shall conform to the provisions of its general technical requirements and relevant product technical conditions (detailed specifications), and the requirements of product technical conditions (detailed specifications) shall not be lower than the general technical requirements. When the requirements of general technical requirements and product technical conditions (detailed specifications) are inconsistent, the product technical conditions (detailed specifications) shall prevail. For hydraulic cylinders with built-in sensors such as force sensors, pressure sensors, position sensors, displacement sensors, speed sensors, acceleration sensors, and temperature sensors, the performance indicators of the built-in sensors shall conform to the relevant technical requirements of the hydraulic cylinders.

1) The terms and definitions established in GB/T 7665—2005 "General Terms of Sensors" and various product standards are applicable to these requirements. 2) The naming method and code of sensors shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 7666—2005. Table 2-191 lists examples of the composition of typical sensor names and various modifiers, which can be referred to when naming sensors.

2.13.2  Technical Requirements for Force Sensors for Hydraulic Cylinders

A force sensor is a device that can sense force and convert the input force into an output quantity (usually an electrical parameter) that is proportional to it. GB/T 33010—2016 stipulates the technical requirements for force sensors.

Force sensors belong to physical quantity sensors. Weight (weighing) sensors are commonly used on hydraulic cylinders, while stress sensors or shear stress sensors are not commonly used. (1) Environmental and working conditions: Under the following environmental and working conditions, the force sensor shall be able to work normally: 1) The ambient temperature is -10～40°C, and the relative humidity is not greater than 80%. 2) In an environment without strong magnetic fields. 3) There are no corrosive media around. (2) Grading of force sensors: The grading and main technical indicators of force sensors are shown in Table 2-192. (3) Requirements for electrical characteristics of force sensors: 1) The insulation resistance of the force sensor shall not be greater than 2000MΩ. 2) The maximum allowable deviation of the input resistance of the force sensor is ±5% of its nominal value, and the maximum allowable deviation of the output resistance is ±1% of its nominal value. (4) Other requirements for force sensors: 1) Both ends of the force sensor should be equipped with connecting parts and accessories with appropriate structure and sufficient rigidity, and the accessories should not be replaced at will. 2) The surface quality of the force sensor and its accessories shall comply with the provisions of Chapter 10 of GB/T 2611—2007.

2.13.3  Technical Requirements for Pressure Sensors Used in Hydraulic Cylinders
Pressure sensors are sensors that can sense pressure and convert it into usable output signals. Technical requirements for pressure sensors are specified in JB/T 6170-2006.
Pressure sensors belong to physical quantity sensors. Pressure sensors, differential pressure sensors, and absolute pressure sensors are occasionally used in hydraulic cylinders.
1. Basic Parameters

(1) Measuring Range
The measuring range of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications). Unless otherwise specified, the measuring range of the sensor is recommended to be selected from the following numbers:
1×10ⁿ, 1.6×10ⁿ, 2×10ⁿ, 2.5×10ⁿ, 3×10ⁿ, 4×10ⁿ, 5×10ⁿ, 6×10ⁿ, 8×10ⁿ.
Where n is an integer, n=0, ±1, ±2, ±3....
The unit of measuring range is Pa, kPa, MPa, GPa.

(2) Type of Pressure Felt by the Sensor
1) Gauge Pressure Sensor (pg).
2) Absolute Pressure Sensor (pa).
3) Differential Pressure Sensor (pd).

(3) Type of Medium Being Measured
The type of medium in contact with the pressure chamber, such as gas, liquid, corrosive medium, non-corrosive medium, etc.

(4) Material in Contact with the Measured Medium
List the name and grade of the material in contact with the measured medium.

(5) Installation Effect
If the maximum installation force or torque affects the performance of the sensor, specific provisions should be made.

(6) Direction
The direction is determined based on the axial direction of the sensor pressure interface (i.e., the direction in which the measured medium enters the sensor), with the direction consistent with it being the Y-axis, and the rest being X and Z axes, with an outline drawing attached for explanation.

(7) Enclosure Sealing
When the sensor's enclosure needs to be sealed, the sealing material and sealing method should be specified, and the electrical connector should have the same requirements. When the sensor's enclosure has protection requirements, the protection level should be given, with the protection level specified according to GB/T 4208.

(8) Electrical Connection Method
The electrical connector model, electrical connection principle diagram, and necessary explanations should be provided.

(9) Excitation
The excitation of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications).

(10) Operating Temperature Range
The operating temperature range of the sensor should comply with the provisions of product technical conditions (detailed specifications), and it is recommended to select from the following five levels.
1) Commercial Grade: 0~70℃.
2) Industrial Grade: -25~85℃.
3) Automotive Grade: -30~100℃.
4) Military Grade: -55~125℃.
5) Special Grade: -60~350℃.

(11) Storage Temperature Range
The lower limit temperature of the storage temperature range is usually 10℃ lower than the lower limit value of the operating temperature, and the upper limit temperature is usually 15~20℃ higher than the upper limit value of the operating temperature.
2. Technical Requirements

(1) Product Technical Conditions (Detailed Specifications)
The sensor should comply with the provisions of this technical requirement and relevant product technical conditions (detailed specifications). When the requirements of this technical requirement and product technical conditions (detailed specifications) are inconsistent, the product technical conditions (detailed specifications) shall prevail.

(2) Appearance
The appearance of the sensor should be free from obvious defects, scratches, rust, and damage; the threaded parts should be free from burrs; the markings should be clear, complete, and accurate.

The overload of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
(12) Thermal Zero Drift
The thermal zero drift of the sensor within the working temperature range shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1). It is recommended to select the thermal zero drift of the sensor from the corresponding accuracy grade and higher grade range in Table 2-194.
(13) Thermal Full-Scale Output Drift
The thermal full-scale output drift of the sensor within the working temperature range shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1). It is recommended to select the thermal full-scale output drift of the sensor from the corresponding accuracy grade and higher grade range in Table 2-194.
(14) Long-Term Stability of Zero Point
Within the specified time (generally half a year or one year), the long-term stability of the zero point of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).

1) Frequency Response. The frequency response of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
2) Resonance Frequency. The resonance frequency of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
3) Natural Frequency (Ringing Frequency). The natural frequency of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
4) Damping Ratio. The damping ratio of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
5) Rise Time. The rise time of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
6) Time Constant. The time constant of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).
7) Overshoot. The overshoot of the sensor shall comply with the provisions of item 2(1).

2.13.4 Technical Requirements for Displacement Sensors for Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Metrological Characteristics of Typical Linear Displacement Sensors

Displacement sensors are sensors that can sense displacement (linear or angular) and convert it into a usable output signal. They can be used to measure displacement, distance, position, and elongation of length dimensions, and are widely used in engineering testing. Linear displacement sensors belong to the category of physical quantity sensors. On hydraulic cylinders, capacitive, eddy current, magnetostrictive displacement sensors, and grating displacement sensors are all used.

sections.text: 2. Grating Line Displacement Measuring Device

A grating line displacement measuring device is a measuring device that senses linear displacement using a grating line displacement sensor and displays its length using a grating digital display instrument. As stipulated in JB/T 10030-2012, the grating line displacement measuring device is suitable for coordinate linear displacement detection and measurement of machine tools, instruments, etc., and consists of a grating line displacement sensor and a grating digital display instrument connected together (hereinafter referred to as the measuring device).
(1) Requirements
1) Basic parameters. The basic parameters of the measuring device are shown in Table 2-202.

sections.caption: Table 2-202  Basic Parameters

sections.text: 2) Accuracy. The accuracy of the measuring device is expressed by half of the maximum interval error with a "±" sign, and is divided into 5 grades, as shown in Table 2-203.

sections.caption: Table 2-203  Accuracy Grades (Unit: mm)

sections.text: 3) Repeatability precision. The repeatability precision of the measuring device at any point within the effective range should comply with the provisions of Table 2-204.

sections.caption: Table 2-204  Repeatability Precision (Unit: μm)

sections.text: 4) Basic functions.

items: Counting. The measuring device should correctly count within the effective range and display the numerical value.
Zero setting. The measuring device should have a zero-setting function.

sections.text: 5) Appearance and interaction.

items: Appearance. The surface of the measuring device should not have obvious dents, scratches, cracks, or deformations. The surface coating or plating should not have defects such as bubbles, cracks, peeling, or rust.

Marking. The switches, buttons, lights, and sockets on the casing and panel of the measuring device should have markings indicating their functions. The markings should be firm, clear, beautiful, and durable.
Color. The colors of the connecting wires and their diameters, as well as the colors of the switches, buttons, and lights on the panel, should comply with the provisions of GB 5226.1-2008 (2019).

Interaction. All fastening and welding parts should be firm, the interface between the plug and socket should have reliable contact and appropriate tightness, and the moving parts of the sensor should be flexible and smooth, without sticking or looseness.

sections.text: 6) Protection level (IP). The measuring device should have protection capability. The protection level of an open-type grating line displacement sensor should not be lower than IP50, and the protection level of a closed-type grating line displacement sensor should not be lower than IP53.

The enclosure protection level of the grating digital display instrument should not be lower than IP43, and the panel protection level should not be lower than IP54 (according to the provisions of GB4208-2008).
7) Anti-interference capability

items: Anti-static interference capability. During the operation of the measuring device, anti-static interference capability test with contact discharge voltage of 4 kV and air discharge voltage of 8 kV shall be conducted on all parts frequently touched by operators. The measurement system should be able to work normally during the test.

Anti-fast transient electrical pulse group interference capability. a. During the operation of the measuring device, anti-fast transient electrical pulse group interference capability test shall be conducted by applying pulse groups (see Table 2-205) between the AC power supply terminal and the protective grounding. The measuring device should be able to work normally during the test. b. During the operation of the measuring device, anti-fast transient electrical pulse group interference capability test shall be conducted by applying pulse groups (pulse amplitude of 1 kV) to the sensor signal cable using a coupling clamp. The measuring device should be able to work normally during the test.

Anti-voltage surge interference capability. During the operation of the measuring device, anti-voltage surge interference capability test shall be conducted by superimposing pulse voltage (see Table 2-206) on the input power supply. The measuring device should be able to work normally during the test.

sections.text: 2.13.5  Technical Requirements for Speed Sensors for Hydraulic Cylinders
A speed sensor is a sensor that can sense speed and convert it into a usable output signal. Technical requirements for speed sensors are specified in GB/T 30242-2013.
Speed sensors belong to physical quantity sensors. Generally, linear speed (vibration speed) sensors, rather than angular speed (rotational speed) sensors, are used on hydraulic cylinders.
1. Environmental and Working Conditions

items: Environmental temperature: 15 to 35°C.
Relative humidity: not greater than 75%.
Electromagnetic field: there should be no electromagnetic field that affects the test results.

sections.text: 2. Technical Requirements
(1) Appearance
The appearance of the sensor should be intact without cracks or scratches; the markings should be clear, complete, and correct.
(2) Markings
The sensor should be fixed with the product markings in an obvious position on the body, and should be marked with the following contents:

items: Model and specifications.
Name.
Measurement range.
Name or trademark of the manufacturer.
Factory number.

Production date. When the product size is small, at least the model and specifications and factory number should be marked on the sensor body, and the remaining contents can be indicated on the product packaging.

sections.text: (3) Weight
The weight of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification, such as JB/T 9517-1999 "Magnetoelectric Speed Sensor".
(4) Shape and Installation Dimensions
The shape and installation dimensions of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(5) Output Resistance
The output resistance of the sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(6) Insulation Resistance
When a DC voltage of 500 V is applied, the insulation resistance of the sensor should not be less than 10 MΩ.
(7) Dielectric Strength
When an AC voltage of 500 V and a frequency of 50 Hz are applied, there should be no arcing, breakdown, or flickering on the surface of the sensor, and the test voltage should not have a sudden drop.
(8) Reference Sensitivity
The error of the reference sensitivity of the vibration speed sensor should be better than ±5%.
(9) Frequency Response (When Applicable)
The frequency response deviation of the vibration speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(10) Amplitude Linearity (When Applicable)
The amplitude linearity of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(11) Transverse Sensitivity Ratio (When Applicable)
The transverse sensitivity ratio of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(12) Sensitivity Time Drift (When Applicable)
The sensitivity time drift of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(13) Sensitivity Thermal Drift (When Applicable)
The sensitivity thermal drift of the amplitude speed sensor should meet the requirements of the product detailed specification.
(14) High Temperature Storage
The upper limit temperature and holding time for high-temperature storage are as follows:
Selection.

items: Upper limit temperature: 70°C, 85°C, 100°C, 125°C, 150°C.
Holding time: 48h, 72h, 96h, 168h.

sections.text: After the sensor undergoes high-temperature storage test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(15) Low-temperature storage
The lower limit temperature and holding time for low-temperature storage shall be selected from the following conditions.

items: Lower limit temperature: -55°C, -40°C, -100°C, -25°C, -10°C.
Holding time: 24h, 48h, 72h, 96h.

sections.text: After the sensor undergoes low-temperature storage test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(16) Temperature change
The temperature change shall meet the following conditions.

items: Extreme temperature: Select from the upper limit temperature and lower limit temperature specified in clauses (14) and (15).
Minimum test time at extreme temperature: Execute according to the provisions of the product detailed specification based on the weight of the sensor.
Conversion time: Not greater than 5min.
Number of cycles: 5 times, 10 times.

sections.text: After the sensor undergoes temperature change test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(17) Vibration

Under room temperature, apply vibration to the sensor along its three axes (X, Y, Z) respectively, with the vibration level and time conducted according to the provisions of the product detailed specification.

After the sensor undergoes vibration test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(18) Shock

Under room temperature, apply shock to the sensor along its three axes (X, Y, Z) respectively, with 12 shocks applied in each direction, acceleration of 1000m/s², waveform of half-sine pulse, pulse duration of 6ms, or conducted according to the provisions of the product detailed specification.

After the sensor undergoes shock test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(19) Constant humid heat
The constant humid heat test shall be selected from the following conditions.

items: Temperature: 40°C ± 2°C.
Relative humidity: 93% ± 3%.

sections.text: Test duration: 48h, 96h, 120h.

After the sensor undergoes constant humid heat test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), insulation resistance should meet the requirements of item 2.(6), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
(20) Salt spray
The salt spray test shall be selected from the following conditions.

items: Temperature: 35°C ± 2°C.
Salt water concentration: 5% ± 1% mass fraction.
Test time: 48h, 96h.

sections.text: After the sensor undergoes constant humid heat test, its appearance should meet the requirements of item 2.(1), insulation resistance should meet the requirements of item 2.(6), and the reference sensitivity of the vibration velocity sensor should meet the requirements of item 2.(8).
