2.13.6 Technical Requirements for Temperature Sensors for Hydraulic Cylinders

An integrated temperature sensor is a sensor that integrates a temperature sensor module installed in a junction box and connected to a temperature sensor probe, outputting a millivolt signal corresponding to the detected temperature with a linear relationship (i.e., having linearization capability). Temperature sensors can be classified according to the sensing element used, such as thermocouple integrated temperature sensors and thermal resistance integrated temperature sensors based on the detection element used.
1. Basic Parameters
(1) Measurement range
The recommended measurement range and its limits for integrated thermal resistance temperature sensors are shown in Table 2-212.
(2) Output parameters and signal transmission
The output parameters and signal transmission method of integrated temperature sensors are shown in Table 2-213.
(3) Normal working conditions
The normal working conditions of integrated temperature sensors include atmospheric conditions such as ambient temperature, relative humidity, and atmospheric pressure, as shown in Table 2-214.

For non-explosion-proof sensors, the surrounding air should not contain media that are corrosive to chromium, nickel plating, non-ferrous metals, and alloys, and should not contain flammable or explosive substances.
The normal working conditions of intrinsically safe explosion-proof sensors and explosion-proof sensors shall be implemented according to the provisions of JB/T 12599—2016.
2. Technical Requirements

items: The sensor should meet the provisions of this technical requirement and the relevant product technical conditions (detailed specification). When the requirements of this technical requirement are inconsistent with those of the product technical conditions (detailed specification), the product technical conditions (detailed specification) shall prevail.

2.13.7  Technical Requirements for Proximity Switches for Hydraulic Cylinders

Proximity switches are position switches that can operate without mechanical contact with moving parts. Proximity switches can be classified according to various basic characteristics, such as inductive type (I), capacitive type (C), ultrasonic type (U), diffuse photoelectric type (D), non-mechanical magnetic type (M), retroreflective photoelectric type (R), and through-beam photoelectric type (T).
Taking Hall proximity switch sensors as an example, the basic operating parameters and technical requirements are given below.
1. Basic Operating Parameters
(1) Operating Voltage
The nominal value of the sensor's operating voltage should comply with the product technical conditions.
(detailed specifications).
The recommended operating voltage of the sensor shall be selected from DC 2.5V to 40V.
(2) Output type
The output type of the sensor is usually single-pole type, all-pole type, bipolar type, and bipolar latch type.
(3) Maximum load current
The maximum load current of the sensor is recommended to be selected from the following values: 20mA, 50mA, 100mA, 200mA, 300mA, 500mA.
(4) Operating temperature range
The operating temperature range of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
The recommended lower limit value of the operating temperature range is: -55°C, -40°C, -25°C, -10°C.
The recommended upper limit value of the operating temperature range is: 70°C, 85°C, 100°C, 125°C, 150°C.
(5) Storage temperature range

The lower limit of the storage temperature range of the sensor is usually equal to or lower than the lower limit operating temperature by 10°C, and the upper limit of the storage temperature range is usually equal to or higher than the upper limit operating temperature by 15 to 20°C.
2. Technical requirements
(1) Appearance

The appearance of the sensor should be free from visible defects, corrosion, and damage; the threaded part should be free from burrs; the components should be intact; the markings should be clear, complete, and accurate.
(2) Appearance, installation dimensions, and lead connections
The appearance, installation dimensions, and lead connections of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(3) Operating point magnetic induction intensity
The operating point magnetic induction intensity of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(4) Reset point magnetic induction intensity
The reset point magnetic induction intensity of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(5) Hysteresis
The hysteresis of the sensor shall conform to the range specified in the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(6) Cut-off state current
The cut-off state current of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(7) On-state voltage drop
The on-state voltage drop of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(8) Operating frequency
The operating frequency of the sensor shall conform to the provisions of the product technical conditions (detailed specifications).
(9) Insulation resistance
Under the specified test conditions, the insulation resistance between the terminal and the housing of the sensor shall not be less than 20 MΩ.
(10) Insulation strength
Under the specified test conditions, the sensor shall be able to withstand a sinusoidal AC voltage with an amplitude of 1000V and a frequency of 50Hz for 1 minute without breakdown or arcing.
(11) Low-temperature storage

After low-temperature storage, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(12) High-temperature storage

After high-temperature storage, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(13) Temperature change

After the temperature change test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(14) Constant humidity and heat

After the constant humidity and heat test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5). The insulation resistance shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(9).
(15) Vibration

After the vibration test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(16) Shock

After the shock test, the appearance of the sensor shall conform to the requirements of item 2.(1), and the operating point magnetic induction intensity, reset point magnetic induction intensity, and hysteresis shall conform to the requirements of items 2.(3) to 2.(5).
(17) Electrostatic discharge immunity (when specified)
During the electrostatic discharge immunity test, the output state of the sensor shall not change.
(18) Electrical fast transient/burst immunity (when specified)
During the electrical fast transient/burst immunity test, the output state of the sensor shall not change.
(19) Service life
The service life of the sensor switch shall not be less than 1 million times.

3. BTL7 Series Rod-Type Magnetostrictive Micro-Pulse Displacement Sensor
(1) Product Introduction

Magnetostrictive displacement measurement system has been applied in factory engineering and automation technology. Magnetostrictive micro-pulse displacement sensor is used in applications requiring high reliability and precision. Built-in or compact sensors with measuring range of 25~7600 mm make the displacement measurement system widely used.

Non-contact, precise, and absolute measurement are its important characteristics, and linear magnetostrictive magnets are widely used in industrial applications. Non-contact, wear-free operation helps save high maintenance costs and avoids the trouble of failure downtime. This characteristic allows them to be installed in completely sealed housings, as current position information can be transmitted to internal sensor elements through the magnetic field without contact. Theoretically, a measurement system can measure multiple positions simultaneously. Convenient, lightweight, and reliable sealed design enables magnetostrictive displacement measurement systems to achieve IP67~IP67K protection level. Good shock and vibration resistance has enabled their rapid expansion in industrial applications to heavy machinery and system design fields. Many applications require obtaining measurement values and position values, which can be quickly provided in absolute terms after the measurement system is activated. Because reference runs are omitted, machine availability is greatly improved.

Rod-type micro-pulse displacement sensors are mainly used in hydraulic drive applications. When installed on the pressure part of a hydraulic cylinder, the displacement sensor must have the same pressure resistance as the hydraulic cylinder at that time. In fact, the sensor must be able to withstand pressures up to 1000 bar (1 bar = 10^5 Pa). The chip is integrated in an aluminum or stainless steel housing, the waveguide is installed in a high-pressure resistant non-magnetic stainless steel tube, and the front end of the tube is sealed with a welded plug. The high-pressure part is sealed by an O-ring on the flange mounting surface at the other end. The positioning magnet installed on the magnetic ring slides along the tube or rod with the built-in waveguide to mark the detected position.
(2) Technical Parameters

The BTL7 series rod sensors have characteristics of high pressure resistance up to 600 bar, high repeatability, non-contact, and durability, and can form a durable position feedback system in harsh environments, with a detection range of 25~7620 mm.

The measuring section of the sensor is installed in a high-pressure resistant stainless steel metal tube for reliable protection. This system is very suitable for position feedback of hydraulic cylinders, or for liquid level control of corrosive liquids in the food and chemical industries.

sections.text: 4. LWH Series Potentiometer Linear Displacement Sensor
(1) Product Introduction

Different from the rod-type magnetostrictive micro-pulse displacement sensor of the BTL7 series, the LWH series potentiometer linear displacement sensor is a contact-type linear displacement sensor. This series of sensors is used in measurement and control systems for direct and absolute measurement of displacement and length. The maximum working range is up to 900 mm, with high resolution (0.01 mm) providing accurate linear displacement measurement. The inner and outer surfaces of the sensor are specially treated, allowing it to work under high-speed and low-wear conditions. The flexible buffer bearing at the front end of the sensor can overcome some minor lateral stresses of the transmission rod, ensuring normal operation of the sensor. The structural design considers ease of installation and disassembly.

The fixing and structural design of the sensor's conductive material ensure reliable operation even under the harshest conditions. The sensor has mounting grooves on all four sides, which facilitates installation with the conductive material facing downward as much as possible, avoiding the presence of tiny impurities inside the sensor and thereby affecting its lifespan. This series of sensors has the following characteristics: a) Long service life of up to 10×10^7 cycles under different application conditions. b) Excellent linearity, up to ±0.04%. c) Resolution higher than 0.01 mm. d) High operating speed. e) Equipped with a DIN 43650 standard plug and socket (pressure connector). f) Protection class IP55. In addition, it should be noted that: a) The housing is made of anodized aluminum. b) The installation uses a crimped adjustable fixed clamp. c) The pull rod is made of stainless steel (1.4305), can rotate, and has an M6 external thread. d) The bearing uses a flexible buffer bearing. e) The resistance element uses conductive plastic. f) The brush assembly uses a precious metal multi-arm brush. g) The electrical connection is a 4-pole socket conforming to DIN 43650 standard.

sections.text: 2.14 Design of Hydraulic Cylinders for Air Release, Anti-Loosening, and Other Components and Devices
2.14.1 Technical Requirements for Air Release Devices of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Technical Requirements for Air Release Devices of Hydraulic Cylinders

Air release is the means of expelling air from a system or component. An air release valve is a component used to expel air or gas contained in the hydraulic system oil. The hydraulic system should be equipped with necessary air release devices (valves) as required and should allow for easy air discharge (release).

"Air release," "air release valve," and "air release" are all terms defined in GB/T 1746-2012. However, "air release" is defined as a term related only to pneumatics. Therefore, this manual often uses the expression "air (gas) release."
GB/T 13342-2007 stipulates that hydraulic cylinders should generally be equipped with air release devices.
GB/T 24946-2010 stipulates that digital cylinders can be equipped with air release devices as required.

GB/T 3766-2015 stipulates that when installing hydraulic cylinders on fixed industrial machinery, they should be able to automatically release air or provide easily accessible external air release ports. During installation, the air release port of the hydraulic cylinder should be positioned at the highest point.

When these requirements cannot be met, relevant maintenance and usage information should be provided; hydraulic cylinders with inflation chambers should be designed or equipped with air release ports to prevent danger. Hydraulic cylinders should be able to safely expel air through air release ports.

GB/T 3766-2001 (which has been superseded) stipulates that single-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinders should be equipped with air release ports, positioned appropriately to prevent danger from oil spray to personnel.

GJB 638A-1997 stipulates that wherever air that has been mixed in would interfere with the normal operation of the hydraulic system, appropriate methods such as installing manual air release valves should be adopted to expel it, rather than disconnecting pipelines or loosening tube nuts; requirements for automatic air release valves can be found in MIL-V-29592.
2. Air (Gas) Release Valves
The structural types of air (gas) release valves commonly used on hydraulic cylinders as specified in some standards are shown in Table 2-228.

The valve body and valve needle are integrated, connected to the cylinder barrel or cylinder head by threads, and sealed by the tapered surface at the head. When releasing air, loosen the threads, and the air inside the cylinder is squeezed out from the gap between the tapered surfaces and expelled outside the cylinder through the inclined hole. This type of air release plug has a simple and convenient structure, but has high requirements for the concentricity of the thread and tapered surface sealing. Otherwise, it cannot seal after tightening the air release valve, causing external leakage. According to reference [99], the valve material is 35 or 45 carbon steel, and the hardness of the tapered part after heat treatment is 38~44HRC.

sections.text: 2.14.2 Technical Requirements for Anti-Loosening Measures for Hydraulic Cylinders

According to GB/T 3766-2015, any components and accessories installed on hydraulic cylinders or connected to hydraulic cylinders should be able to prevent loosening caused by impact and vibration during use. At the same time, measures should be taken to prevent loosening of external or internal adjustable stroke terminal stoppers.

For hydraulic cylinders, anti-loosening of threaded connections or fasteners should adopt reliable methods, and various common anti-loosening methods for bolts, screws, studs, and nuts listed in Table 2-230 can be used.

sections.text: 2.14.3 Technical Requirements for Integrated Hydraulic Control Valves in Hydraulic Cylinders

Hydraulic cylinders with integrated hydraulic control valves, including those with cushioning valves, support valves, and proportional/servo valves, should preferably use cartridge valves and/or cartridge valves.

The nominal pressure and other performance indicators of the hydraulic control valves (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic valves) should not be lower than the technical requirements of the hydraulic cylinders; the mounting surfaces for valves or valve blocks installed on the hydraulic cylinders, or the cartridge mounting holes for cartridge valves, should comply with relevant standard specifications.

The protection level, operating voltage, and electrical connections of electrically controlled valves should comply with relevant standard specifications; generally, the electrically controlled valves themselves should also be equipped with manual override control devices.
1. General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Valves
(1) Selection of Hydraulic Valves

The selection of hydraulic valve types should consider correct functionality, sealing, maintenance and adjustment requirements, as well as the ability to withstand foreseeable mechanical or environmental impacts. In fixed industrial machinery, cartridge valves and/or cartridge valves should be preferred. When isolation valves are required, valves approved by the manufacturer for such safety applications should be used.
(2) Installation of Hydraulic Valves
When installing hydraulic valves, the following aspects should be considered:

items: Independent support, not relying on connected piping or fittings.
Ease of disassembly, repair, or adjustment.
Effects of gravity, impact, and vibration on the valve.
Sufficient space for wrenches, bolt removal, and electrical connections.
Avoidance of incorrect installation methods.
Prevention of damage from mechanical operating devices.
Installation orientation that prevents air accumulation or allows air discharge when used.

sections.text: (3) Valve Blocks

items: Surface Roughness and Flatness: On valve blocks, the surface roughness and flatness of valve mounting surfaces should meet the manufacturer's recommended requirements.
Deformation: During operation within the specified working pressure and temperature range, valve blocks or valve block assemblies should not fail due to deformation.
Installation: Valve blocks should be firmly installed.

Internal Flow Channels: Internal flow channels should have sufficient cross-sectional area at cross-flow areas to minimize additional pressure drops as much as possible. Cast and machined internal flow channels should be free of harmful foreign objects such as scale, burrs, and chips. Harmful foreign objects can obstruct flow or cause other components (including seals and packing) to malfunction and/or be damaged when moving with hydraulic fluid.
Identification: Valve block assemblies and their components should be labeled according to ISO 16874

sections.text: (i.e., GB/T 36997—2018) for marking. When not feasible, identification should be provided by other means.
(4) Electrically Controlled Valves

items: Electrical Connections: Electrical connections should comply with relevant standards (such as GB/T 5226.1 or the manufacturer's standard) and be designed with appropriate protection levels (such as GB/T 4208).
Solenoids: Appropriate solenoids (such as switching frequency, temperature ratings, and voltage tolerance) should be selected so that they can operate the valve under specified conditions.

Manual or Other Override Control: When power is unavailable, if operation of electrically controlled valves is necessary, an override control method should be provided. When designing or selecting an override control method, the risk of accidental operation should be minimized; and after the override control is released, automatic reset should be implemented unless otherwise specified.

sections.text: (5) Adjustment
When allowing adjustment of one or more valve parameters, the following provisions should be considered as appropriate:

items: Safe adjustment methods;
Methods to lock adjustments if unauthorized changes are not permitted;
Methods to prevent adjustments beyond safe ranges.

sections.text: 2. Technical Requirements for Pressure Control Valves
Valves whose function is to control pressure are called pressure control valves.

Pressure control valves specified in standards include proportional pressure pilot valves, hydraulic relief valves, hydraulic solenoid relief valves, hydraulic unloading relief valves, hydraulic solenoid unloading relief valves, hydraulic reducing valves and one-way reducing valves, internally controlled hydraulic sequence valves and one-way sequence valves, externally controlled hydraulic sequence valves and one-way sequence valves, electrically modulated (proportional) relief valves, electrically modulated (proportional) reducing valves, digital relief valves, hydraulic pressure relays, as well as other types such as bidirectional relief valves (groups) (brake valves) and balance valves.

Different from hydraulic control of hydraulic control valves, this is a control method that operates by changing the hydraulic pressure in the control circuit, but it itself does not have the ability to control the hydraulic pressure in the control circuit.
(1) Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Relief Valves and Solenoid Relief Valves
1) General Requirements

items: The nominal pressure of relief valves should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2346 "Nominal Pressure Series for Hydraulic Transmission Systems and Components."

The mounting surfaces of plate-connected relief valves should comply with the provisions of GB/T 8101 "Hydraulic Relief Valve Mounting Surfaces," and the connecting mounting surfaces of stacked relief valves should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2514 "Hydraulic Four-Port Directional Control Valve Mounting Surfaces."
Other technical requirements should comply with the provisions of GB/T 7935 "General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Components."
Manufacturers should indicate the applicable conditions and environmental requirements of their products in product samples and related materials.
Performance requirements.
Pressure oscillation should comply with JB/T 10374—2013 "Hydraulic Relief Valves."

sections.text: 3. Technical Requirements for Flow Control Valves

Valves whose main function is to control flow are called flow control valves. The flow control valves specified in the standard include hydraulic speed control valves and one-way speed control valves, hydraulic overflow throttle valves, hydraulic throttle valves and one-way throttle valves, hydraulic stroke throttle valves and one-way stroke throttle valves, hydraulic throttle shut-off valves and one-way throttle shut-off valves, electro-hydraulic proportional flow direction composite valves, manual proportional flow direction composite valves, etc.
(1) Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Speed Control Valves
1) General requirements.

items: The nominal pressure of the speed control valve shall conform to the provisions of GB/T2346 "Nominal Pressure Series for Hydraulic Transmission Systems and Components".

The installation surface of the plate-connected speed control valve shall conform to the provisions of GB/T8098-2003 "Installation Surface for Flow Control Valves with Compensation in Hydraulic Transmission", and the connection installation surface of the stacked speed control valve shall conform to the provisions of GB/T2514 "Installation Surface for Four-port Directional Control Valves in Hydraulic Transmission".
Other technical requirements shall conform to the provisions of 4.10 in GB/T7935 "General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Components".
The manufacturer should indicate the applicable conditions and environmental requirements of the product in the product samples and relevant materials.

sections.text: 2) Performance requirements.

items: The working pressure range shall conform to the provisions in Table A.1 of JB/T10366-2014 "Hydraulic Speed Control Valves".

sections.text: 4. Technical Requirements for Directional Control Valves

A valve whose main function is to control the direction of oil flow, connecting or blocking one or more flow paths, is called a directional control valve. The directional control valves specified in the standard include hydraulic ordinary (straight-through, right-angle) check valves and hydraulic control check valves, hydraulic solenoid directional valves, hydraulic manual and roller directional valves, hydraulic electro-hydraulic directional valves and hydraulic directional valves, hydraulic solenoid directional seat valves, hydraulic multi-way directional valves, electro-modulated (proportional) three (four-way) directional flow control valves, dual-speed directional combination valves, as well as high-pressure manual ball valves, hydraulic control shut-off valves, shut-off check valves, butterfly valves, ball valves, etc. The minimum control pressure of hydraulic electro-hydraulic directional valves and hydraulic directional valves, as well as the minimum control pressure for reverse opening of hydraulic control check valves, are defined differently from the minimum control pressure of flow control valves.
(1) Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Multi-way Directional Valves
1) General Requirements

items: The nominal pressure of the multi-way valve should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2346 "Hydraulic Transmission Systems and Components - Nominal Pressure Series".
The nominal flow rate of the multi-way valve should comply with the relevant provisions of JB/T 8729—2013 "Hydraulic Multi-way Directional Valves".

The form and dimensions of threaded oil port connections should preferably comply with the provisions of GB/T 2878.1 "Hydraulic Transmission Connections - Oil Ports and Stud End with Metric Threads and O-ring Seals, Part 1: Oil Ports".

In addition to marking technical parameters in the product catalog, pressure loss characteristic curves, internal leakage characteristic curves, relief valve and other pressure characteristic curves can be drawn as reference curves for users to refer to when selecting.
Other technical requirements should comply with the provisions of Section 4 in GB/T 7935 "Hydraulic Components - General Technical Conditions".
Manufacturers should state the applicable conditions and environmental requirements of the product in the product catalog and related materials.

5. General Technical Requirements for Electrohydraulic Servo Valves

An electrohydraulic servo valve is a servo valve whose input is an electrical signal and output is hydraulic energy. Among them, the flow control electrohydraulic servo valve is an electrohydraulic servo valve whose main function is to control the output flow.

The current standard GB/T 10844—2007 stipulates marine electrohydraulic servo valves, GB/T 13854—2008 stipulates jet pipe electrohydraulic servo valves, GJB 3370—1998 stipulates aircraft electrohydraulic servo valves, GJB 4069—2000 stipulates ship electrohydraulic servo valve specifications, and QJ 504A—1996 stipulates flow electrohydraulic servo valves, etc.
(1) Types, Main Parameters and Interfaces of Electrohydraulic Servo Valves

1) Types. Electrohydraulic servo valves can be classified into single-stage, two-stage (or secondary, double-stage), three-stage or four-stage electrohydraulic servo valves according to the number of hydraulic amplifier stages.
2) Main parameters. The main parameters of electrohydraulic servo valves should include the rated current, rated pressure and rated flow of the electrohydraulic servo valve.

3) Interfaces.

items: Hydraulic Interfaces. Except as otherwise specified, the mounting surface dimensions of electrohydraulic servo valves shall comply with the relevant standards or the manufacturer's regulations.

Electrical Interfaces. Except as otherwise specified, the connection method of the coil, the marking of the terminal, the color of the external lead wire and the polarity of the input current shall comply with the provisions of item 3.(1) of this requirement.

sections.text: (2) Mechanical Design Requirements for Electrohydraulic Servo Valves

1) Design Layout. According to the different requirements of the controlled object, electrohydraulic servo valves can be designed in different types. It is recommended to adopt two-stage electrohydraulic servo valves, whose pre-stage hydraulic amplifiers can adopt some frictionless variable orifice amplifiers, such as double-nozzle baffle type, jet pipe type or jet deflection plate type, etc., and whose output-stage hydraulic amplifiers usually adopt four-way spool valve structures.
2) Interchangeability requirements.

items: Installation Requirements. The external outline dimensions of newly developed electrohydraulic servo valves shall be equal to or smaller than those of electrohydraulic servo valves of the same type and specification that are currently in service. When modifying the design of the valve's parts or components, the structural elements of the installation shall not be arbitrarily changed.
The electrical connector shall be the same as that of the electrohydraulic servo valve currently in service. It is recommended to select the plug socket specified in GJB 599A.

sections.text: ② Mounting Surface Dimension Requirements.

a. Symbol Requirements. The installation surface of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should use the following symbols:
a) Use A, B, P, T, X, and Y (L) to mark each oil port according to GB/T17490.
b) Use F1, F2, F3, and F4 to mark the threaded holes of the fixing screws.
c) Use G to mark the positioning pin holes.
d) Use rmax to mark the edge radius of the installation surface.

b. Installation Surface Precision Requirements. The precision of the installation surface of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should comply with the following regulations:
a) The tolerance for flatness of the installation surface is 0.025 mm.
b) The surface roughness value Ra should be less than or equal to 0.8 μm.
c) The tolerance for the position of the installation surface holes is 0.2 mm.
c. Installation Surface Dimension Requirements. The dimensions of the installation surface of the electro-hydraulic servo valve should comply with the relevant standards.

d. Installation Surface Fixing Requirements. If the electro-hydraulic servo valve is installed on an iron mounting base, it is recommended:
a) The minimum thread length for the fixing screws that can be screwed into the threaded holes of the iron mounting base should be at least 1.5D (D is the screw diameter).
b) The depth of the threaded holes on the iron mounting base should be at least (2D+6) mm.
The maximum working pressure of the iron mounting base (baseplate, oil passage block) with the installation surface of the electro-hydraulic servo valve will be specified by the manufacturer.
e. Positioning Pin Dimension Requirements. The recommended dimensions for the positioning pins protruding from the installation surface are given in Table 2-234.

③ Material. All materials should comply with the requirements of Section 3.4 in GJB1482.
④ Locking. All threaded connecting parts should be firmly locked with locking wire according to HB0-2.
⑤ Structural Strength. All parts of the product should have sufficient strength and rigidity to withstand various loads and load combinations generated by hydraulic pressure, temperature, transmission, and transportation, and to withstand the torque loads acting during installation and operation under rated conditions.
⑥ Standard Parts and General Parts. Standard parts and general parts should be given priority where applicable.
⑦ Seals. The materials of the sealing rings and gaskets should be nitrile rubber material specified in GJB250A or other materials compatible with the working medium of the system. The dimensions of the sealing rings and their installation groove dimensions should comply with HB/Z4 and HB4-56-57. The sealing structure of threaded connections should comply with HB4-59. In special cases where there are specific requirements for structural dimensions and weight, non-standard parts may be used.
Alternatively, it can be stated as: The rubber material of the sealing rings used in hydraulic systems and their components should be verified to be compatible with the hydraulic oil used; unless there are special requirements for the sealing material, the dimensions of the sealing devices should comply with the requirements of HB4-56-57, HB4-59, or SAEAS4716C; when the rated working pressure of the hydraulic system exceeds 10.5 MPa (1500 psi), a backup ring should be installed at the O-ring, and the dimensions of the backup ring should comply with the requirements of HB4-58.
⑧ Appearance Quality. The surface of the product should not have rust, dents, burrs, cracks, or other defects.
⑨ Surface Treatment. No plating should be used on internal metal parts. The surface treatment of other parts should comply with the regulations in GJB/Z594A. The surface treatment of external metal parts should be suitable for the environmental conditions where the product is located.
⑩ Quality. The mass of the electro-hydraulic servo valve excluding the hydraulic oil (such as filled hydraulic oil) and the bottom cover, expressed in kg, should comply with the regulations in the detailed industry specifications.

2) Rated current. Unless otherwise specified, the rated current should generally comply with the provisions of Table 2-231. The pressure oil port P, working oil ports A, B and (external) pilot supply port X should be able to withstand 1.3 times the rated supply pressure (return port T open); the return port T should be able to withstand 1.3 times the rated supply pressure of the return port T. Under the application of positive and negative rated currents, each maintained for 2.5 minutes, the valve should not have obvious external leakage (moistening allowed, dripping not allowed) and permanent deformation. During and/or after the test, the valve's rated flow, hysteresis, and zero offset should comply with the requirements of detailed industry specifications. Pressure resistance testing should not be performed on the valve's (external control) drain port Y.
Note: Regarding external leakage, reference can be made to the provisions of GB/Z 18427—2001, which is expressed as not worse than Grade 3 (fluid formation without dripping droplets).

3) Destructive pressure. Apply 2.5 times the rated supply pressure to the pressure oil port P, working oil ports A, B (return port T open); apply 1.5 times the rated supply pressure to the return port T, each maintained for 30s. The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not be damaged, and there is no requirement for the valve to restore working performance. Valves that have undergone destructive pressure testing cannot be used as products again.

4) Pressure pulse. If detailed industry specifications require pressure pulse testing of the electro-hydraulic servo valve, the electro-hydraulic servo valve should be able to withstand 2.5×10⁵ cycles of pulse under rated pressure at positive and negative rated currents. After the test, its performance should comply with the requirements of detailed industry specifications.

5) Working medium. Should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications. Generally, petroleum (mineral) based hydraulic oil conforming to GB 11118.1 should be used, or aviation hydraulic oil No. 10, No. 12, and No. 15 conforming to SH 0358, Q/SY 11507, GJB 1177A. The oil used for filling and the oil filled in protective packaging generally should be consistent with the actual working medium of the electro-hydraulic servo valve.

6) Working medium temperature. The working medium temperature class should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications. For example, meeting the requirements of GJB 456 -55 (54)~135℃.

Note: 1. The temperature class III in GJB 456 is different from the temperature class III in GB/T 30206.3. 2. The operating temperature range of petroleum-based aviation hydraulic oil specified in GJB 1177A is -54~134℃. 3. In ISO 10770-1: 2009, the output flow or valve core position - oil temperature

sections.text: 8) Coil impedance and inductance. Should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications.

9) Excitation (tremor) vibration. Should comply with the provisions of detailed industry specifications. Generally, the excitation or tremor frequency is 400Hz, with a peak-to-peak value of 10% of the rated current.
(4) Hydraulic Design Requirements for Electro-Hydraulic Servo Valve
1) Working pressure. The rated supply pressure and return pressure should comply with the provisions of Table 2-232 and meet the pressure class specified in GB/T 2346—2003 or GJB 456—1988.

2) Pressure resistance. The pressure oil port P, working oil ports A, B (return port T open); apply 1.5 times the rated supply pressure to the return port T, each maintained for 30s. The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not be damaged, and there is no requirement for the valve to restore working performance. Valves that have undergone pressure testing cannot be used as products again.
Temperature characteristic test: The oil temperature should reach 70°C.
7) Contamination resistance: The electro-hydraulic servo valve should operate normally when the solid particle contamination level of the oil is no worse (higher) than GB/T 14039 grade 17/14.

In GJB 3370-1998, for nozzle flapper servo valves, the acceptance level of solid contamination in the working fluid used for performance testing, acceptance testing, and internal oil seals should be no higher than class 6/A specified in GJB 420, and the control level should be no higher than 7/A; for other tests, the solid contamination level of the working fluid should be no higher than 8/A. For jet pipe and direct drive servo valves, the requirements may be appropriately reduced, and should comply with the detailed specifications.

8) Filtration precision: When the electro-hydraulic servo valve is used conventionally, a filter with nominal filtration precision of no less than 10μm should be installed before the oil inlet (pressure oil port).
When the electro-hydraulic servo valve is used for long life, a filter with nominal filtration precision of no less than 5μm should be installed before the oil inlet (pressure oil port).

During electro-hydraulic servo valve testing, it is recommended to install a filter with nominal filtration precision of 3μm as close as possible to the oil inlet (pressure oil port) of the electro-hydraulic servo valve.

9) External sealing: The electro-hydraulic servo valve should not have obvious external leakage under all specified operating conditions and throughout the entire working period (moistening is allowed, but oil droplets dripping is not allowed).

(6) Environmental Requirements for Electro-hydraulic Servo Valves

1) Low temperature starting: When the environmental temperature and working medium temperature are both -30°C, the electro-hydraulic servo valve should be able to start with ±50% of the rated current, and there should be no obvious external leakage at the seals (moistening is allowed, but oil droplets dripping is not allowed).

2) High and low temperature: When the environmental temperature and working medium temperature are both in the range of -30~135(90)°C, the deviation of rated flow should not exceed ±25%, the resolution should not exceed 2%, or the hysteresis should not exceed 6%. At high temperatures, the insulation resistance should not be less than 5MΩ, and there should be no obvious external leakage at the seals (moistening is allowed, but oil droplets dripping is not allowed).
In GB/T 13854, the environmental requirements (high and low temperature) for servo valves are -30~60°C environmental temperature and -30~90°C working fluid temperature.
In JB/T 10205, the working oil temperature for high temperature testing is 90°C.

3) Temperature shock: After the electro-hydraulic servo valve undergoes the temperature shock shown in Figure 2-101 for 3 cycles, the insulation resistance should not be less than 5MΩ, and the zero drift should not exceed 2% (zero drift for jet pipe should not exceed 1.5%).

sections.caption: Figure 2-101 Temperature Shock Diagram
sections.description: A temperature-time graph showing temperature shock test profile. The y-axis shows temperature from -30±3 to 90±5°C, and the x-axis shows time in minutes. The profile shows rapid transitions between high temperature (90±5°C) and low temperature (-30±3°C) with hold periods of approximately 5 minutes at each extreme, connected by ramp transitions of approximately 5 minutes each. The cycle shows transitions at approximately 60-minute intervals.

sections.text:
4) Damp heat. Under the damp heat conditions of 95% humidity and 35°C temperature specified in GB/T 4000-2000 Table 072-8, the insulation resistance and dielectric strength of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall meet the requirements of items 3.(6) and 3.(7). The appearance quality shall meet the following requirements:
① The color shall not be significantly darkened.
② The corrosion area of the coating shall not be greater than 3%.
③ The main metal shall not be corroded (the surface that is difficult or impossible to plate under normal plating conditions is generally not calculated for corrosion area).

5) Salt spray. Under the salt spray conditions specified in GB/T 4000-2000 Table 072-16, the insulation resistance of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall meet the requirements of item 3.(6). The appearance quality shall meet the following requirements:
① The color shall not be significantly darkened or the coating shall have a uniform and continuous light film-like corrosion.
② The corrosion area of the coating shall be less than 6%.
③ The main metal shall not be corroded (the surface that is difficult or impossible to plate under normal plating conditions is generally not calculated for corrosion area).

6) Mold. Under the mold conditions specified in GB/T 4000-2000 Table 072-14, the mold level of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall not be worse than level 2, and the insulation resistance shall meet the requirements of item 3.(6).

7) Vibration. Under the Class 3 vibration conditions specified in GB/T 4000-2000 Figure 074-1, there shall be no resonance that affects the working performance, and no loosening or damage of components. The zero drift shall not be greater than 2% (the zero drift of the jet pipe electrohydraulic servo valve shall not be greater than 5%).

8) Shock. Under the shock level 2 conditions specified in GB/T 4000-2000 Table 072-23, there shall be no loosening or damage of components. The insulation resistance shall not be less than 5MΩ, the rated flow tolerance shall not be greater than ±10%, the hysteresis shall not be greater than 5%, and the zero drift shall not be greater than 2% (the zero drift of the jet pipe electrohydraulic servo valve shall not be greater than 5%).

9) Acceleration. The acceleration value of the electrohydraulic servo valve in each main shaft direction shall be based on the requirements proposed by the user or as specified in the detailed technical requirements of the industry.
The acceleration values are divided into three levels:
① Level I, 10×9.8m/s².
② Level II, 20×9.8m/s².
③ Level III, 30×9.8m/s².
The acceleration action time is 5 minutes.
During the acceleration test, the zero drift of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall not be greater than 3%. After the test, there shall be no loosening or damage of components, and the zero position change shall not be greater than 2% of the rated current.
Generally, for every 1g change in acceleration, the zero drift (acceleration) shall not be greater than 0.3%.

10) Impact. Under the Class A conditions specified in GB/T 4000-2000 074.4, there shall be no loosening or damage of components. The insulation resistance shall not be less than 5MΩ, the rated flow tolerance shall not be greater than ±10%, the hysteresis shall not be greater than 5%, and the zero drift shall not be greater than 2%.

(7) Durability requirements for electrohydraulic servo valves
Under the designed rated operating conditions, the service life of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall not be less than 10⁷ cycles. During the service life, the rated flow tolerance of the electrohydraulic servo valve shall be ±25%, the hysteresis shall not be greater than 6%, and the zero drift shall not be greater than 5%.
Note: 1. The definition of "rated operating conditions" can be found in GB/T 17446-2012.
2. "Durability test" and "service life test" are synonymous, see GB/T 2900.99-2016.
2.14.4  Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Filters

To maintain the required hydraulic oil contamination level, the hydraulic system and circuit should provide filtration. If the main filtration system (such as supply or return line filters) cannot achieve the required hydraulic oil contamination level or there are higher filtration requirements, a bypass filtration system can be used. Filters should be installed as needed in the pressure line, return line, and/or auxiliary circulation circuit to achieve the system's required oil contamination level. All filters should be equipped with indicators to provide indication when the filter needs maintenance. The indicator should be easily observable by the operator or maintenance personnel. If this requirement cannot be met, the operator's manual should specify regular replacement of the filter. The filter should be installed in an easily accessible location, with sufficient space left for replacing the filter element. Due to the area ratio of the hydraulic cylinder and the influence of decompression, the maximum flow through the return line filter may be greater than the maximum flow of the pump. When the maximum pressure difference generated by the system across the filter may cause damage to the filter element, a filter bypass valve should be installed. In the pressure circuit, the bypass flow of contaminants through the filter should not cause harm downstream. It is not recommended to install a filter in the pump's suction line, and it is not advisable to use it as the main system filtration. A suction strainer or coarse filter can be used. Malfunction of proportional valves or servo valves caused by contamination may lead to danger, so it is advisable to install an additional full-flow filter with a non-bypass and easily observable clogging indicator near the proportional valve or servo valve in the supply line. The burst pressure rating of the filter element should exceed the highest working pressure of the system. The blockage of the liquid flow through the non-bypass filter should not cause danger.
1. Basic Technical Parameter Requirements

1) The filtration accuracy of the filter should meet the requirements of the product technical documentation.
The filtration accuracy (μm) should be selected from 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 40. When the filtration accuracy is greater than 40μm, it should be determined by the manufacturer.
2) The rated flow (L/min) of the filter should be selected from the following grades: 16, 25, 40, 63, 100, 160, 250, 400, 630, 800, 1000. When the rated flow is greater than 1000L/min, it should be determined by the manufacturer.
3) The nominal pressure of the pressure line filter should be in accordance with GB/T 2346
of the standard selection.
4) The dirt-holding capacity of the filter under rated flow should be specified in the technical file of the product.
5) For filters equipped with an indicator, the pressure drop of the indicator should be indicated in the technical file of the product.

6) For filters equipped with a bypass valve, the opening pressure drop should be marked in the technical file of the product. When the pressure drop of the bypass valve reaches 80% and the specified opening pressure drop of the bypass valve, the leakage should comply with the provisions of Table 1 in GB/T 20079-2006. The closing pressure drop of the bypass valve should not be less than 65% of the specified opening pressure drop. When the flow through the bypass valve reaches the rated flow of the filter, its pressure drop should not be greater than 1.7 times the opening pressure drop.

7) When the filter is equipped with both an indicator and a bypass valve, it should meet the following formula requirement, i.e., 65% of the opening pressure drop of the bypass valve ≤ the pressure drop of the indicator ≤ 80% of the opening pressure drop of the bypass valve.
8) The initial pressure drop of the filter under rated flow should be specified in the technical file of the product.
9) The flow-pressure drop characteristic curve of the filter under test conditions should be provided in the technical file of the product.
2. Material Requirements

items: The materials selected for the filter should comply with the relevant material standards or technical agreements.
The selected materials should be compatible with the working medium.
Metal materials should be corrosion-resistant or protected to ensure that the filter has good resistance to salt spray, humidity, and other harsh conditions during normal storage and use.

sections.text: 3. Performance Requirements

items: Low-pressure sealing: There should be no oil leakage on the outside of the filter under a pressure of 1.5 kPa.
High-pressure sealing: There should be no oil leakage or permanent deformation on the outside of the filter under 1.5 times the nominal pressure.
Burst pressure: The filter should not burst under 3 times the nominal pressure.
Pressure drop flow characteristics: The pressure drop flow characteristics of the filter should be specified in the technical file of the product.

sections.text: 4. Connection Dimensions
When there are no technical specifications, the connection dimensions between the filter and the pipeline should be selected from Table 2 in GB/T 20079-2006 according to the connection method.
5. Design and Manufacturing

items: The filter should be manufactured according to the product drawing and technical file, and its technical requirements should comply with the provisions of GB/T 20079-2006.
The filter should be designed in a structural form that allows the filter element to be replaced without disassembling the pipe fittings or fasteners.

sections.text: 3) The filter should be designed in a structural form that can effectively prevent incorrect installation of the filter element.
4) When the filter is equipped with a bypass valve, the design structure should prevent pollutants deposited from directly passing through the bypass valve.
5) The surface of the filter should not have defects such as dents, cracks, corrosion, and burrs. The surface coating should not crack, peel, or flake during normal storage, transportation, and use.
6) The cleanliness index of the filter should be specified, and all oil ports should be equipped with dust caps when leaving the factory.
6. Instructions

items: When choosing to comply with GB/T 20079-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Filters", it is recommended that manufacturers use the following instructions in test reports, product samples, and sales documents: The hydraulic filter complies with GB/T 20079-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Filters".
Hydraulic filters with special (product) standards are excluded.
The above documents are often used as one of the technical documents for exchanging information between the supply and demand parties of hydraulic filters.

sections.text: 2.1.4.5 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Isolated Accumulators

In hydraulic systems and circuits with inflatable accumulators, when the system is shut down, the hydraulic system should automatically release the liquid pressure of the accumulator or completely isolate the accumulator. In special cases where pressure is still required after the machine is shut down or the potential energy of the hydraulic accumulator will not cause any danger (such as clamping devices), it is not necessary to comply with the requirements for pressure release or isolation. Inflatable accumulators and any matching pressure-bearing components should be used within the rated limits of pressure, temperature, and environmental conditions. In special cases, protective measures may be needed to prevent overpressure on the gas side. If damage to components and pipe fittings in the inflatable accumulator system may cause danger, appropriate protection should be taken for them. The inflatable accumulator and all matching pressure-bearing components should be supported according to the instructions of the accumulator supplier. The inflatable accumulator should not be modified by machining, welding, or any other means without authorization. The output flow of the inflatable accumulator should be related to the predetermined working requirements and should not exceed the rated value specified by the accumulator manufacturer.
1. Scope of Application

Applicable to accumulators with a nominal pressure not exceeding 63 MPa, a nominal volume not exceeding 250 L, a working temperature of -10 to 70°C, and nitrogen/petroleum-based hydraulic oil or emulsion as the working medium.
2. Technical Requirements
(1) General Technical Requirements

items: The nominal pressure and nominal volume (series) of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2352.
The type of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of JB/T 7035 or JB/T 7034.
The type and size of the bladder of the accumulator should comply with the provisions of HG 2331.

sections.text: 4) After the test is completed, the accumulator capsule should maintain a residual pressure of 0.15-0.30 MPa.
5) The accumulator should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T 7935.
(2) Technical requirements and indicators

items: After the airtightness test, there should be no air leakage.
During the sealing performance test and pressure test of the accumulator, there should be no air or oil leakage at all seals.
After the accumulator's repeated action test, the decrease in inflation pressure should not be greater than 10% of the pre-charge pressure, and there should be no oil leakage at all seals.
After the accumulator undergoes repeated action tests, a gas leak check test should be conducted, and there should be no air leakage.

Oil seepage check: After the accumulator undergoes repeated action tests and gas leak checks, the oil seepage at the valve seat of the inflation valve should not be greater than the specified value in Table 1 of JB/T 7036-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Isolated Accumulators."

Disassembly inspection of the accumulator: The capsule or diaphragm should not exhibit peeling, swelling, cracking, or aging; all parts should not be damaged, and the mating accuracy should not decrease.

Cleanliness check: The mass of contaminants inside the accumulator should not be greater than the specified value in Table 2 of JB/T 7036-2006 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Isolated Accumulators."

items: A safety valve should be installed in the hydraulic system using the accumulator, and its discharge capacity must be greater than or equal to the accumulator's discharge capacity. The opening pressure should not exceed the accumulator's design pressure.
The isolation gas inside the accumulator can only be nitrogen, and the inflation pressure should not be greater than 0.8 times the nominal pressure value.
The design, manufacturing, and inspection of the accumulator should comply with the relevant provisions of the "Safety Technical Supervision Regulations for Pressure Vessels."

The accumulator should undergo regular inspections. The inspection cycle should be in accordance with the provisions of the "Safety Technical Supervision Regulations for Pressure Vessels," the inspection method should be in accordance with the provisions of the "Inspection Regulations for Pressure Vessels in Use," and the inspection results should comply with the relevant provisions of the "Safety Technical Supervision Regulations for Pressure Vessels."
When the accumulator is in storage, transportation, or long-term disuse, the internal residual stress should be below 0.3 MPa.

2.14.6  Technical requirements for other devices integrated on hydraulic cylinders
1. Technical requirements for stroke adjustment devices

The positioning accuracy and repeatability of the control position of the adjustable stroke cylinder and other stroke adjustment devices or mechanisms in hydraulic cylinders should comply with the requirements of relevant standards, and their operation should be sensitive and reliable.

In GB/T 24946-2010 "Marine Digital Hydraulic Cylinders," it is stipulated that the repeatability of the digital cylinder (stroke) should not exceed 3 pulse equivalents, i.e., it should not exceed 0.03 mm.

In JB/T 9834-2014 "Technical Conditions for Double-Acting Cylinders for Agricultural Use," it is stipulated that the operation of the stroke adjustment mechanism of the cylinder should be sensitive and reliable.
2. Technical requirements for setting test ports

In JB/T 3018-2014 "Hydraulic Press - Technical Conditions," it is stipulated that when hydraulic components such as cartridge valves or stacked valves are used, a pressure test port should generally be set between the actuator (such as hydraulic cylinder) and its corresponding flow control element. In the outlet throttling system, a test port should generally be set at the inlet of the relevant actuator (such as hydraulic cylinder).

For measuring the average steady-state pressure of a closed circuit with an inner diameter greater than 3 mm, an average flow velocity less than 25 m/s, and an average steady-state pressure less than 70 MPa when transmitting hydraulic power, the selection and setting of pressure measurement points are specified in GB/T 28782.2-2012 "Hydraulic Transmission Measurement Technology - Part 2: Measurement of Average Steady-State Pressure in Closed Circuits."

sections.text: 2.15.2  Installation and Connection Forms of Hydraulic Cylinders for Hydraulic Presses

In hydraulic presses, hydraulic cylinders are installed in two ways: some have the cylinder body directly set on the crossbeam, such as in rubber vulcanizing hydraulic presses. However, most hydraulic cylinders are designed as independent hydraulic components or units, serving as functional parts of the hydraulic transmission system.

Although installing the hydraulic cylinder as an independent unit in the hydraulic press may reduce the strength and stiffness of the crossbeam, it also has its advantages: a) The hydraulic cylinder can be manufactured by specialized factories, and the main machine manufacturer can purchase it externally. b) It reduces the difficulty of processing and manufacturing the hydraulic press frame. c) The design, manufacturing, testing, acceptance, and replacement of hydraulic cylinders are simple and convenient. d) It better meets the requirements of standardization, serialization, and modular design for hydraulic presses.
There are various installation forms of hydraulic cylinders in hydraulic presses. Although GB/T 9094-2006 specifies 64 installation forms, it still does not cover all existing hydraulic cylinders.
1. Installation Forms with Flange or Boss on Cylinder Body

The front or rear flange or boss for installation of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses is generally directly set (designed) on the cylinder body, rather than on the cylinder end cover. Although the following description still uses front or rear flange or boss, it differs from general hydraulic cylinders and those specified in GB/T 9094-2006.

The cylinder body of hydraulic cylinders has three installation forms: front flange, rear flange, and intermediate flange. The flanges also have three types: circular flange, square flange, and rectangular flange. The flange connection holes are generally through holes, and threaded holes are less common.
(1) Front Circular Flange Installation Form

The far datum face of the front flange is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam, and the hydraulic cylinder is fastened to the crossbeam through bolts. During operation, since the two fixed mating surfaces usually squeeze each other, the flange needs to transmit force, resulting in stress concentration at the transition between the flange and the cylinder body (tube), which is prone to fatigue failure. Additionally, the presence of connecting holes in the flange also accelerates this type of failure.

There are also designs where the near datum face of the front flange is tightly fitted to the outer surface of the crossbeam. During operation, the two fixed mating surfaces usually tend to separate, causing a significant increase in the force on the connecting bolts, a decrease in the ability to resist eccentric loads, and no improvement in the stress condition of the cylinder body (tube).
(2) Rear Circular Flange Installation Form

The far datum face of the rear flange is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam, and the hydraulic cylinder is fastened to the crossbeam through bolts. During operation, although the two fixed mating surfaces usually squeeze each other and the flange needs to transmit force, the force direction is different from the front flange installation form. Therefore, there is generally no stress concentration problem at the transition between the flange and the cylinder body (tube) for rear flange installation.
(3) Front Boss Installation Form

The far datum face of the front boss is tightly fitted to the inner surface of the crossbeam. A pressure ring fixes the boss, a large nut at the far end of the datum point fastens the cylinder tube, and the pressure ring is fastened to the cylinder bottom through bolts or other forms to ensure this tight fit.

This installation form is the most common and is widely used in medium and small hydraulic presses. However, it is not given in GB/T 9094-2006. The stress condition of this installation form is similar to that of the front flange installation form, but it is generally slightly improved due to the absence of flange connecting holes. However, the stress concentration problem at the transition between the boss and the cylinder body (tube) still exists.
2. Connection Forms between Piston Rod and Slide Block

GB 28241-2012 and JB/T 4174-2014 define the term "slide block," which is the main component of a hydraulic press that completes the stroke movement and installs the upper die. The piston rod connects to the slide block to transfer energy to it.

GB 2350-1980 specifies three forms of piston rod threads (one internal thread, two external threads). GB/T 9094-2006 provides the end dimensions of piston rods with external threads, the end of piston rods with wrench faces (with internal threads), the end of piston rods with pin holes, the end of piston rods with flanges, and the end dimensions of piston rods with internal threads. However, the length of the external thread at the end of the piston rod differs from the length of the (external) thread of the piston rod specified in GB 2350-1980.

In some designs, a spherical surface is made at the end of the piston rod, and it is fastened by screws through the central threaded hole at the end of the piston rod, the side threaded holes, or a pressure ring. A spherical pad is clamped between the end of the piston rod and the slide block, forming a ball joint connection between the piston rod and the slide block.
(1) Rigid Connection
The rigid connection between the piston rod and the slide block is the most common connection form. Generally, the piston rod is connected to the slide block through accessories.

Due to the different types of piston rod ends and the variety of accessories, there are also various connection forms between the piston rod and the slide block of hydraulic presses. However, it must be ensured that the connection is safe, reliable, and has a long service life. Any components or parts connected to the hydraulic cylinder should be firm to prevent loosening due to impact and vibration. Especially for slide blocks with the risk of accidental falling, a risk assessment should be conducted.
The rigid connection forms between the piston rod and the slide block are as follows:

a) Connection through threaded flange.
b) Connection composed of key and pressure ring.
c) Direct fastening connection with screws.
d) Positioning sleeve connection.
In GB/T 9094—2006, the threaded flange is also called piston rod flange.
(2) Swivel Connection

When the connection between piston rod and slide block is in the form of pin, clevis and universal joint bearing, the piston rod and slide block can swing or rotate. This connection form is also relatively common. However, due to the high precision requirements and large nominal force of general hydraulic presses, the above-mentioned swivel connections are not actually used much in hydraulic presses for metal cold working. Instead, a ball joint bearing connection is widely used in hydraulic presses.
The ball surface at the end of the piston rod of the ball joint bearing connection is generally a concave ball surface with material removed, and a center hole with internal thread is generally made in the center; The ball surface at the end of the piston rod and the ball pad block form a pair of ball joints, which should be in a compression state during the working stroke of the hydraulic press. The ball joint bearing connection mainly aims to minimize the eccentric (load) force transmitted from the slide block to the piston rod, or to adapt to the small amount of position change of the slide block during the working stroke.
There is also a special structure of double ball joint bearing connection for hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses, which is characterized by the fact that the piston rod does not directly transmit force to the slide block, but uses an intermediate connecting rod, that is, the piston rod transmits force to the intermediate connecting rod through a ball joint bearing connection, and the other end of the intermediate connecting rod transmits force to the slide block through the ball joint bearing surface. Therefore, there are two double ball joint bearing connections between the piston rod and the slide block. This connection has better elimination of eccentric (load) force effect than a single ball joint bearing connection, so the service life of the hydraulic cylinder is longer.
2.15.3  Installation Dimensions of 16MPa Series Single Rod Hydraulic Cylinder

The installation dimensions of 16MPa series single rod hydraulic cylinder are specified in JB/T 12706.1—2016 to meet the interchangeability requirements of common hydraulic cylinders, which are applicable to round head hydraulic cylinders with cylinder diameters of 25~500mm and square head hydraulic cylinders with cylinder diameters of 200~500mm.
JB/T 12706.1—2016 only provides a basic principle. In order to not limit technical applications, hydraulic equipment manufacturers are allowed to flexibly apply it in the design of 16MPa hydraulic cylinders.

2. In the JB/T 12706 "Installation Dimensions of 16MPa Series Single Rod Cylinders" series of standards, Part 3 is missing: Compact series with cylinder diameters of 250mm~500mm.

The installation type identification codes and dimensional letter codes including installation dimensions listed in this manual according to the GB/T 9094-2006 standard are mainly for standardizing, serializing and modularizing the design of electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders, and are also beneficial for adopting group technology to conduct more in-depth research on servo hydraulic cylinders.

The cylinder assembly should not use pull rods or steel pull rods, but should use double-ended studs. For electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinders, double-ended studs are mainly used for clamping between cylinder head, cylinder body and cylinder bottom, that is, the installation and connection of the hydraulic cylinder itself. This type of hydraulic cylinder with pull rod is still widely used. The existing standards stipulate that the length of double-ended studs (Grade B) generally does not exceed 500 mm, and lacks necessary technical conditions. If spring washers or elastic washers are used, it is also difficult to determine the tightening torque of the nut.
2.15.8 Double-ended stud and tightening torque for cylinder assembly

The cylinder assembly pull rod installation defined in GB/T 17446-2012 is a cylinder installation method that uses the extended part of the cylinder assembly pull rod parallel to the outer side of the cylinder body and is installed from one end or both ends of the cylinder. However, the cylinder assembly should not use pull rods or steel pull rods, but should use double-ended studs. As shown in Figure 2-161, it is a double-ended stud with a transition fit thread at the end screwed into the cylinder head or cylinder bottom end and a fine ordinary thread at the end screwed into the nut, which is for reference only during design. The dimensions of the double-ended stud shown in Figure 2-161 are shown in Table 2-313, and the technical conditions are shown in Table 2-314.

To ensure the reliability of the threaded connection and realize its designed function, the pre-tightening force should be determined by actual usage conditions and strength calculations; during installation and use, the initial pre-tightening force must be ensured. Therefore, it is necessary to select an appropriate tightening method and be able to accurately control the tightening torque to the required value.

The relationship between the tightening torque and pre-tightening force in the elastic zone is shown in equations (2-78) to (2-81), but it is not applicable to threaded connections with spring washers or elastic washers:
Tt = Ts + Tw = KFfd  (2-78)
Ts = (Ff/2)(P/π + μsd₂secα')  (2-79)
Tw = (Ff/2)μwDw  (2-80)
When the contact bearing surface is an annular ring:
Dw = (2/3) × (d³w - d³h)/(d²w - d²h)  (2-81)
Where: Tt—tightening torque;

items: Ts—thread torque;
Tw—bearing surface torque;
K—torque coefficient;
Ff—initial pre-tightening force or pre-tightening force;
d—thread nominal diameter;
P—pitch;
μs—thread friction factor;
d₂—thread pitch diameter;
α'—thread flank angle;
μw—bearing surface friction factor;
Dw—equivalent diameter of bearing surface friction torque;
dw—outer diameter of contact bearing surface;
dh—inner diameter of contact bearing surface.

According to usage requirements, double-ended studs can be made of materials such as 30Cr, 40Cr, 30CrMoSi, 35CrMoA, 40MnA, and 40B, and their performance is determined through negotiation between the supplier and the demander.
The transition fit thread screwed into the cylinder head or cylinder bottom end and/or the fine thread ordinary thread screwed into the nut end can use the pre-applied adhesive layer anti-loosening and locking specified in GB/T35480-2017.
For double-ended studs with a performance grade equal to or lower than 10.9, nuts conforming to GB/T6171 grade 10 can be selected; for double-ended studs with a performance grade higher than 12.9, nuts conforming to GB/T6176 grade 12 should be selected.
When adding spring washers or elastic washers in the threaded connection pair, it may change the effective contact area of the support surface, change the friction coefficient of the support surface, and generate additional axial force, which may affect the pre-tightening force obtained by applying the same torque.
Unless otherwise specified, for the tightening of a single nut, the tightening speed should be 10-40 r/min for nuts of M16 and below, and 5-15 r/min for nuts greater than M16-M39; others should be in accordance with the assembly technical requirements of hydraulic cylinders.
When using the "torque method" for tightening, since only the tightening torque is controlled, although the operation is simple, about 90% of the tightening torque may be consumed by the thread and bearing surface friction torque. The dispersion of the initial pre-tightening force varies with the degree of control of factors such as friction consumption. Therefore, the tightening accuracy level is low (the torque dispersion increases).

sections.text: 2.15.9 Special No-Gap Ball Joint Series for Servo Hydraulic Cylinder

In the electro-hydraulic servo valve controlled hydraulic cylinder system, there is often relative motion between the hydraulic cylinder and the load it drives. The hinge or ball joint connecting them may have gaps, which can cause poor dynamic performance of the system, increased overshoot, and even induce system oscillation, which are serious problems. Therefore, it is very necessary to eliminate or reduce these gaps as much as possible.

As shown in Figure 2-162 and Figure 2-163, these are external view diagrams of rod end flange type ball joints and cylinder bottom end ball joints for servo hydraulic cylinders with built-in displacement sensors and push-pull column type force sensors. The size codes, code meanings, and dimensions of the rod end flange type ball joint are shown in Table 2-318.

The cylinder bottom end ball joint (or adjustable clearance rear clevis) has basically the same structural principle as the rod end flange type ball joint (or adjustable clearance front clevis). It is mainly composed of a single clevis bracket, a cylinder bottom end single clevis with adjustable clearance spherical bearing, a pin shaft for spherical bearing, a radial spherical bearing, and structures for bearing positioning, clearance adjustment, and pin shaft locking plate. During use, the bearing clearance, i.e., the cylinder bottom end connection clearance, can also be appropriately adjusted through the bearing clearance adjustment structure according to on-site conditions.

sections.text: 2.15.10 Threaded Oil Port
1. Standard Oil Port

(1) Oil port with metric thread and O-ring seal. For metric threaded oil ports used in hydraulic transmission connections as specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011, which are applicable to stud end connections as specified in GB/T 2878.2-2011 and GB/T 2878.3-2017. The maximum working pressure for oil ports specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 is 63 MPa (630 bar). The allowable working pressure should be determined based on factors such as oil port dimensions, material, structure, operating conditions, and application. The types and dimensions of oil ports specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 are shown in Figure 2-164 and Table 2-320.

(2) Threaded oil port for hydraulic tube fittings (excerpted from GB/T 19674.1-2005). The maximum working pressure for oil ports specified in GB/T 19674.1-2005 is 63 MPa. The allowable working pressure should be determined based on factors such as oil port dimensions, material, process, operating conditions, and application. 2. Oil Port Standards Reference and Oil Port Thread Issues

In GB/T 3766—2015, clause 5.3.23 "Note" on the use of standard parts states: When more than one standard type of threaded oil port connection is used in a system, there may be mismatches between certain stud end series and oil ports of different connection series, which may cause leakage and connection failure. When using them, the matching can be confirmed based on the markings of the oil port and stud end. The above problem is also pointed out in reference [108].

In JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", it is stipulated that the threaded connection dimensions of the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2878—1993 "Threaded Connection of Hydraulic Components - Oil Port Types and Dimensions". However, this standard has been replaced by GB/T 2878.1—2011 "Hydraulic Transmission Connection - Oil Ports and Stud Ends with Metric Threads and O-ring Seals - Part 1: Oil Ports", so when designing hydraulic cylinder oil ports now, GB/T 2878.1—2011 should be followed.

The corresponding joint standard adopted by GB/T 2879.1—2011 is JB/T 966—2005 "Metal Tube Joints for Fluid Transmission and General Use - O-ring Flat Face Seals", and the original JB/T 984—1977 "Welded Straight Through Tube Joint Body" (the joint standard is JB 966—1977) has been superseded.

The "Welded End Straight Pipe Joint" has been replaced by the "Cylinder End Straight Through Joint ZZ J" (standard figure 17) in JB/T 966-2005. The main difference between the two is whether there is a cylindrical step on the fixed cylinder end side. The joint body specified in the original JB/T 984-1977 has no cylindrical step, while the cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005 has a cylindrical step.

When using the joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 and sealing with the "Combination Sealing Washer" specified in JB/T 982-1977, the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 is small, and the combination sealing washer may not fit or there may be interference between the joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 and the upper plane of the aperture of the oil port, making it impossible to seal at the oil port connection. When using the cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005, although there is generally no interference problem with the upper plane of the aperture of the oil port, some specifications of the combination sealing washer may still not fit, causing the same problem, i.e., it is impossible to seal at the oil port connection.

Therefore, if the combination sealing washer specified in JB/T 982-1977 is used to seal the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011, the corresponding cylinder end straight through joint ZZ J specified in JB/T 966-2005 should be used, and the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of some oil ports should be increased; if the welded straight through pipe joint body specified in JB/T 984-1977 or the welded end straight pipe joint specified in JB/T 966-1977 is still used, the aperture (countersink) plane diameter of the oil port specified in GB/T 2878.1-2011 must be increased. Please refer to Table 2-323 for details.
