In practice, in addition to using fine-pitch ordinary threads (M) for port threads, 55° unsealed tube threads specified in GB/T 7307—2001 "55° Unsealed Tube Thread" are also commonly used for hydraulic cylinder port threads. The following statement is given in reference [99]: "55° unsealed tube threads or fine-pitch ordinary threads are used in medium and high-pressure systems with nominal pressures of 16-31.5 MPa." The 60° sealed tube threads (NPT) specified in GB/T 12776—2011, the metric sealed threads (Mc or Mp/Mc) specified in GB/T 1415—2008, and the 55° sealed tube threads (Rp/R1 and Rc/R2) specified in GB/T 7306.1—2000 and GB/T 7306.2—2000 can all be used when the nominal pressure is less than or equal to 16 MPa.
2.16 Design of Nameplates for Hydraulic Cylinders

Nameplates for various electromechanical equipment, instruments, meters, and various component products, including nameplates, operation prompt plates, instruction plates, circuit diagram plates, design data chart plates, and safety signs, are collectively referred to as nameplates. Nameplates for hydraulic cylinders need to be designed and may vary for different users, but should comply with the provisions of GB/T 13306—2011 "Nameplates".

sections.text: 2.16.2 Technical Requirements for Nameplates Used in Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Type and Dimensions
(1) Shape of the nameplate and its code: 1) Rectangular (including square), code J. 2) Circular, code Y. 3) Oval, code T. 4) Fan-shaped, code Sh. 5) Triangular, code S.

(2) Characteristics of text, symbols, and lines on the nameplate: 1) Raised type: text, symbols, and lines are raised above the nameplate surface (excluding recessed printed characters). 2) Recessed type: text, symbols, and lines are recessed into the nameplate surface. 3) Flat type: text, symbols, and lines are flush with the nameplate surface. The text, symbols, and lines of nameplates of any shape can be of any of the above three types, or a combination of two or three types.

(3) Type and dimensions of the nameplate: 1) The type and dimensions of rectangular nameplates should comply with the provisions of Figure 1 and Table 1 in GB/T 13306—2011. For rectangular nameplates with two holes, the ends may be made into rounded heads, as shown in Figure 1 e) and Figure 1 f) in GB/T 13306—2011. The width (B) to length (L) ratio of rectangular nameplates is generally 1:1, 1:1.25, 1:1.6, 1:2, 1:2.5, 1:3.2, 1:4, and 1:5, among which 1:1, 1:1.6, 1:2.5, and 1:4 are recommended for priority selection; when B≥32 mm, the number of fixing holes is 4. 2) For other types of nameplates, refer to the relevant provisions in GB/T 13306—2011.

sections.text: (2) Content, characters and symbols on nameplates
1) The content and arrangement as well as colors on nameplates should follow relevant regulations or be determined by the nameplate designer.

2) The Chinese characters on nameplates generally use simplified Chinese characters officially promulgated and implemented by the state, and traditional Chinese characters are allowed when there are special needs. It is recommended to use fonts such as bold, extended imitation Song and imitation Song for Chinese characters, and other clear, beautiful and easily recognizable fonts are allowed for product names and manufacturer names.
3) When placing trademarks (factory marks) and quality product marks on nameplates, their requirements should conform to relevant regulations.
4) The names, units and unit symbols of quantities used in nameplates should conform to the provisions of GB 3100.
(3) Materials
1) The following materials are recommended for nameplates:

items: a) Industrial pure aluminum 1070A, 1060, 1050A and 1050.
b) Stainless steel 06Cr19Ni10, 12Cr18Ni9 and 10Cr17.
c) Cast steel, rolled thin steel plates, etc.
d) Thermosetting and thermoplastic plastics.
e) When there are special needs, brass plates H62, H68 and other materials can be selected.

sections.text: 2) The adhesive material for adhesive nameplates should be able to firmly adhere the nameplate to a smooth, clean, oil-free metal or non-metal surface without using activation (such as using solvents or heating).
3) The recommended thicknesses of metal materials such as aluminum plates for nameplates are: 0.3mm, 0.4mm, 0.5mm, 0.6mm, 0.8mm, 1.0mm, 1.2mm, 1.5mm, 2.0mm, 3.0mm, 4.0mm.
(4) Appearance requirements
1) For nameplates with borders, the border lines around the fastening holes are allowed to be made into arcs.
2) Nameplates using adhesives do not need to have fastening holes made.
3) The edges of the nameplate should not have obvious burrs, teeth or waves. The front should be flat and smooth. The border lines should be uniform, smooth, continuous and not broken.
4) The size and line thickness of characters and symbols should be neat and eye-catching, arranged uniformly, and should not be missing or unclear.

5) The surface should not have cracks and obvious scratches, as well as rust spots, spots, shadows that affect clarity. The coating should not have pinholes, bubbles, fog, stains, wrinkles, peeling or signs of peeling and obvious particle impurities.
6) Adhesive nameplates should not have phenomena such as creases, wrinkles, self-rolling, tearing and adhesive seepage.

7) The color of the nameplate should be clear and eye-catching, with uniform color and should not have color deviation. For nameplates with two or more colors overprinted, the edges between colors should be neat and clear, and there should be no gaps at the junction of two colors.
8) The surface can be matted according to product needs to make it matte or semi-matte.
(5) Performance requirements
1) The coating adhesion should not be lower than level 4 specified in GB 1720.
2) The lightfastness of colors should conform to the provisions of GB/T 730:
Indoor use shall not be lower than level 4; outdoor use shall not be lower than level 6.
3) For aluminum anodized nameplates with dark-colored front anodized film, the thickness shall not be less than 10μm; for those with light-colored film, it shall not be less than 5μm.
4) The sealing quality of the anodized film on aluminum anodized nameplates shall comply with the provisions of Article 4.4 "Sealing Quality" in GB/T 8013.1-2007.
5) When wear resistance testing is required for aluminum anodized nameplates, the evaluation method for wear resistance shall be agreed upon by both the supplier and the demander.
6) Salt spray resistance: After a 48-hour test, it shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 4159.
7) Damp heat resistance: After a 10-day test, it shall comply with level 2 specified in JB/T 4159.
8) Mold resistance: After a 28-day test, it shall comply with level 2 specified in GB/T 2423.16.
2.17 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly

Hydraulic cylinder assembly is the process of combining parts that constitute a hydraulic cylinder into components, subassemblies, and assemblies according to the technical requirements (conditions) and precision requirements of the hydraulic cylinder design, until the hydraulic cylinder product is formed. Hydraulic cylinder assembly is a later-stage work in hydraulic cylinder manufacturing and is a key link in forming the hydraulic cylinder product. A good hydraulic cylinder is not only designed but also assembled.

The assembly of servo hydraulic cylinders should refer to relevant standards such as QJ 1499A and QJ 2478, and the environment of the (servo) hydraulic cylinder assembly site should meet cleanliness requirements.
2.17.1 General Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly
1. Technical requirements for assembly in GB/T 7935-2005 "Hydraulic Components - General Technical Conditions"

items: Components should be assembled using qualified parts and purchased parts according to the provisions and requirements of relevant product standards or technical documents. Parts and purchased parts that are deformed, damaged, or rusted shall not be used for assembly.
Parts should be cleaned before assembly and should not contain any contaminants such as iron filings, burrs, or fibrous debris.

When assembling components, cotton yarn, paper, and other fibrous materials that are prone to shedding should not be used to wipe the inner cavity of the housing, mating surfaces of parts, and inlet/outlet passages.
When assembling components, sealing elements that are defective or have exceeded their effective service life shall not be used.
Symbols indicating the function of oil ports should be marked near all connecting oil ports of the component.

sections.text: 6) The coating of the exposed non-machined surface of the component should be uniform and consistent in color. Putty shall not be applied before spraying.
7) After the component passes factory inspection, all oil ports should be sealed, dust-proof, and leak-proof. Here it should be noted that:

1) Articles 4.4 to 4.10 in GB/T 7935-2005 are cited by standards such as JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", JB/T 11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", and DB 44/T 1169.1-2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinders Part 1: Technical Conditions".
2) Generally, sealing elements should not be cleaned.
3) Except for hydraulic cylinders with special structures and special purposes, oil port symbols and reciprocating motion arrows are generally not marked on ordinary hydraulic cylinders.
2. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 1829-2014 "Press Machinery - General Technical Conditions"

items: When assembling subassemblies or the entire assembly, gaskets not specified in the technical document are not allowed to be installed.
The cleanliness of press machinery assembly should comply with the provisions of the technical document.
During the assembly process, machined parts should not be bumped, scratched, or rusted.

After assembly, the heads of screws and bolts and the end faces of nuts should be in uniform contact with the plane of the fastened part, without tilting or gaps. The lengths of screws installed in the same position should generally be the same. There should be no loosening of fastened screws, bolts, and nuts, and the fastening force of screws that affect precision should be consistent.

Sealing elements should not have damage. Before assembly, sealing elements and sealing surfaces should be coated with grease. When assembling overlapping sealing rings, the rings should be pressed tightly against each other.

sections.text: 3. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 3818-2014 "Hydraulic Press - Technical Conditions"

items: The hydraulic press should be assembled according to the assembly process specification. Parts and their surfaces, as well as the lips of seals, should not be damaged due to assembly. All assembled parts (including purchased parts and outsourced parts) should meet the requirements.

Important fixed mating surfaces should fit tightly. After being securely fastened, they should be inspected with a 0.05mm feeler gauge, and the depth to which the feeler gauge can be inserted should not exceed 1/4 of the contact surface. The total length of the areas where the feeler gauge can be inserted on the contact surface should not exceed 1/10 of the circumference.

For hydraulic cylinders with support ring sealing structures, the support ring should be moderately tight and securely locked. Moving parts that slide down quickly by their own weight (including pistons, movable crossbeams, or sliders) should not have any obstruction during rapid downward movement.
All pipelines, pipe joints, flanges, and other fixed and movable connection sealing points should be reliably connected, well sealed, and should not have any external leakage of oil.

sections.text: 4. Technical requirements for assembly in JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders"

items: Cleanliness requirements: The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic oil inside the hydraulic cylinder body shall not be higher than Grade -/19/16 specified in GB/T 14039-2002.

The assembly of hydraulic cylinders should comply with the provisions of Articles 4.4 to 4.7 in GB/T 7935-2005. After assembly, the hydraulic cylinder should move freely, and there should be no damage to all external connecting threads, edges of oil ports, etc.

430.page_header: Chapter 2  Hydraulic Cylinder and Basic Component Design  419

sections.text: After assembly, the piston stroke length tolerance of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of Table 9 in JB/T 10205.
3) Appearance requirements: The appearance should comply with the provisions of 4.8 to 4.9 in GB/T 7935—2005.
The appearance inspection of the cylinder should meet the following requirements:

items: a) For cylinders with flange structure, the radial misalignment of the mating surfaces of the two flanges should be ≤0.5 mm.
b) The surface of cast and forged parts should be smooth and free of defects.
c) The welding should be flat, uniform, and aesthetically pleasing, without welding slag, spatter, etc.
d) Nameplates should be fixed at the positions specified in the drawing.
e) Dust and protective measures should be taken for the inlet and outlet ports and external connections.

sections.text: 4) Coating adhesion: The adhesion of the paint coating on the surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be controlled between level 0 and level 2 as specified in GB/T 9286—1998.
5. GB/T 37400.10—2019 (Heavy Machinery General Technical Conditions Part 10: Assembly) Assembly Technical Requirements
(1) General Requirements for Assembly

items: 1) Parts and components (including outsourced and purchased parts) entering the assembly process must have a qualification certificate from the inspection department before assembly can proceed.
2) Parts should be cleaned and washed before assembly, and should be free of burrs, flash, oxide scale, corrosion, chips, oil stains, colorants, rust preventive oil, and dust.

3) Before assembly, the main fitting dimensions of parts and components, especially the interference fit dimensions and related accuracy, should be rechecked. The fitting dimensions that have been trimmed by a fitter should be reinspected by the inspection department.
4) The machining process during assembly should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T 37400.9; the welding process should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T 37400.3.
5) Except for special requirements, sharp corners and edges of parts should be blunted before assembly.
6) Parts should not be bumped, scratched, or corroded during the assembly process.
7) The holes for conveying the medium should be checked for smoothness using the light transmission method or the air flow method.
8) Components that cannot be accessed after assembly should be coated with primer and topcoat first. Parts with wet paint should not be assembled.

9) The base, body, and other foundation parts of the machine should be leveled (or vertically aligned) during assembly. The calibration accuracy should be at least 0.1 mm/m for simple-structured and low-precision machines, and at least 0.05 mm/m for complex-structured and high-precision machines.
10) After assembly, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil (or grease) should be injected into each lubrication point on parts and components with relative motion.

(3) Assembly connection method—screw and bolt connection

1) When tightening screws, bolts, and nuts, striking or using inappropriate tightening tools is not allowed. After tightening, the screw slots, nuts, and heads of screws and bolts should not be damaged.

2) For fasteners with specified torque requirements on drawings or process documents, torque wrenches should be used and tightened according to the specified torque; for fasteners without specified torque requirements, the tightening torque can refer to Table 2-332. When using torque wrenches to tighten bolts, the following steps can be followed:

items: Tighten to TA/3 value.
Tighten to TA/2 value.

sections.text: d) Check all bolts with TA value.

3) When multiple screws (bolts) are used to fasten the same component, the screws (bolts) should be tightened in a crisscross, symmetrical, gradual, and uniform manner. If there are positioning pins, start from the screw (bolt) near the pin.
4) After tightening screws, bolts, and nuts, their bearing surfaces should be in contact with the fastened components.

5) When double nuts are used for fastening, if the two nuts have different thicknesses, the thinner nut should be placed inside the thicker nut. The thinner nut should be tightened according to the specified torque requirements, while the thicker nut should be subjected to a larger tightening torque.

6) After tightening the nut, the end of the bolt or screw should protrude 2-3 threads beyond the nut face; for bolts tightened using tension preloading, the length of the bolt end protruding beyond the nut face after tightening should be according to the design drawing requirements or not less than 1 nominal diameter (d) of the bolt.
7) After tightening the countersunk screw, the countersunk part should be 1-2 mm below the surface or according to the design drawing requirements.

8) Fasteners should be assembled strictly according to the performance grades specified on drawings and technical documents. Lower performance fasteners are not allowed to replace higher performance fasteners.
9) For large diameter, heavy-duty bolts, anti-seize compound should be applied to the threaded engagement area during assembly.

1) When assembling parallel keys, they should not be fitted into a stepped shape.

(2) Pollution Control Requirements

1) The requirements for measurement, assembly and test site are as follows: a. On-site pollution control shall be carried out according to the cleanliness level requirements in Table 2-333. b. It is forbidden to dry sweep the ground or perform processing that produces chips in the room. If brazing wires are required in Class I and II environments, a special isolation room should be set up. c. Staff entering the room should wear long fiber textile work clothes, hats and soft soled work shoes. Staff entering Class I and II environments should remove dust from their bodies beforehand. They should not wear work clothes, hats and shoes after going outdoors. d. Use rolled edge silk cloth or other long fiber textiles as wiping cloth, and do not use cotton yarn to wipe parts, components and products. e. Measuring tools, tools and fixtures used for assembly and debugging of non fully enclosed products should have a firm rust prevention layer to prevent rust chips, delamination, spalling, etc. f. Regularly sample and analyze the properties and sources of pollutants, and take targeted measures.

2) All parts and components put into assembly and purchased finished parts should be carefully cleaned, especially the cavities, channels and parts installed in the cavities of hydraulic systems of hydraulic products should be strictly and thoroughly cleaned. The cleaning effect is guaranteed by the cleaning method and procedure. Finally, visually inspect the parts and cleaning liquid to ensure that there are no visible chips, dust, hair and fibers. The cleaning procedures, methods and requirements are as follows: a. According to the characteristics of the parts, clean them according to the main cleaning procedures specified in Table 2-334. b. The nominal filtration precision of the system should be better than 10μm. The oil tank should be equipped with a dust cover. (3) Rust prevention requirements

items: Requirements for the site where measurement, assembly, debugging and parts/components are stored.
① Strictly control the relative humidity as required in Table 2-333.
② No acid, alkali and other chemical substances should be stored in the site, and it should be as far away as possible from all places where corrosive gases may be released.

③ Where purified compressed air is needed, an oil-water separator should be installed, and oil and water should be drained regularly; before each work shift, it should be checked with white paper, and it can only be used if there is no water or oil. Generally, the felt and activated carbon of the oil-water separator should be replaced at least once every six months.
2) Requirements for assembly and debugging.
① Steel precision parts/components without coating should not be exposed for more than 2h after being unsealed.

② When taking parts/components during measurement, cleaning, assembly and debugging, silk gloves should be worn. If it is inconvenient to operate with gloves, they can be omitted, but hands must be washed before operation and kept dry and clean.

③ After being unsealed, if parts/components are stored for more than 3d, they should be temporarily sealed with oil or sealed, and the requirements are as follows: a. Parts/components should be carefully cleaned and fully dried as specified in 6.(2) 2) of 2.17.1 (blown dry with hot compressed air at 60~70℃ or dried in an oven at 50~60℃ for 30~40min), and then sealed with oil or sealed. b. Small precision parts/components can be sealed with oil by immersion, that is, immersed in a container filled with the working liquid after dehydration, and covered and sealed, and the oil sealing period is 3d. Other parts/components should be immersed in anti-rust oil at 55~60℃ for 5~10s, and the oil sealing period is 3d. Short-term oil sealing can be cold immersed in anti-rust oil with a ratio of 1:4 of anti-rust oil to kerosene for 5~10s, and the oil sealing period is 3 months; c. Electrical parts/components that are not suitable for oil sealing should be sealed in a dry box. At the same time, moisture-proof sand (1kg/m³) that has been dried and a moisture-proof sand indicator (or indicator paper) should be placed in the container.
④ Anodized aluminum alloy parts, stainless steel parts, chrome-plated or nickel-plated steel parts, and all metal parts with coating do not need to be sealed with oil within 3 months.

⑤ During the assembly and debugging of hydraulic products, the storage time when the oil cavity is in an oil-free state shall not exceed 24h. After the assembly and debugging of hydraulic products are completed, new working liquid should be injected in time for sealing. Other parts that need to be sealed with oil should be temporarily sealed with oil or sealed as specified in Article ③.

⑥ Parts/components that have been unsealed and cleaned should be immersed in gasoline containing 3%~7% working liquid (or the last cleaning medium containing 3%~7% working liquid) for 5~10s, and other parts/components (except bearings and parts/components that do not allow oil) should be immersed in gasoline containing 3%~7% anti-rust oil for 5~10s after cleaning, and then blown dry with clean compressed air or air-dried naturally.

sections.text: 4) Assembly requirements
1) Before assembly, the following inspection should be performed:

items: a. The manufacturing of parts and components should comply with the requirements of QJ1499 and should be free of bumps, scratches, and damage to the surface treatment layer.
b. After washing, parts and components should be visually inspected and should be free of any visible dirt.
c. Rubber seals and rubber-metal parts should be free of delamination, degumming, cracking, blistering, impurities, and scratches.

d. The certificate of conformity should be consistent with the actual product. The storage period of parts and components and the calibration period of sensors should be within the specified time limit.

sections.text: 2) Rubber parts should be soaked in working fluid for 24 h before assembly. During assembly, measures should be taken to prevent seals from being scratched and cut.

Although "rubber parts should be soaked in working fluid for 24 h before assembly" is stipulated in QJ2478-1993, the author believes that its applicability is problematic. It is suggested not to apply this process in hydraulic cylinder assembly.

items: 3) When assembling hydraulic products and their components, the surfaces of parts should be pre-coated with working fluid.
4) During assembly, threaded connection parts (except those in contact with working medium) should be coated with special No. 12 grease conforming to SY1510 on the outer thread surface.

5) During assembly test, it is allowed that the surface treatment layer of the assembly may be slightly damaged locally due to the fixture, jig, or thread engagement, but the base metal should not be damaged.

6) Springs, spring washers, saddle-shaped elastic washers, wave-shaped elastic washers, and seals (including fluoroplastic retaining rings and gaskets) disassembled from products are not allowed to be used again when reassembled and must be replaced with new parts.

7) Product matching should ensure that parts and components are interchangeable (except those marked as selective matching in the drawing), and cutting processing is not allowed on the product after assembly.

sections.text: 8) The assembly, test, brazing, and installation of electronic products should comply with the provisions of QJ165 and special technical conditions.

9) The wire harness inside the electrical connector should be tightly tied with nylon or hemp thread. When the wire harness has a metal wave shield, the shield should be reliably connected to the metal base.
10) The moving parts of the product should move smoothly without sticking, hesitation, or crawling.
11) Dynamic balancing and overspeed test should comply with the provisions of special technical requirements.
2.17.2 Specific Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Assembly
1. Assembly Preparation

items: 1) According to the production order, prepare drawings, technical documents, and job guidance documents.
2) According to the assembly batch, prepare all parts and components once according to the detailed list or detailed table in the assembly drawing.

3) Recheck the main matching dimensions of parts and components. When using the grouping selection assembly method, parts and components can be grouped at this time; check the certificates of conformity of outsourced and purchased parts and components to ensure that all parts and components entering the assembly are qualified products within the effective service life.
4) The working of the stroke adjustment mechanism of the adjustable stroke cylinder should be sensitive and reliable and meet the accuracy requirements.

5) The working surfaces and mating surfaces of the main parts and components are not allowed to have defects such as rust, scratches, and knocks. All seals (including dust seals, retaining rings, support rings, etc.) should not have any damage.
6) Before assembly, burrs should be removed from each part, and sharp corners and edges not shown in the drawing should be rounded and blunted.
7) Clean each part and component carefully and achieve the cleanliness requirements, but generally do not include seals.

8) The cleaned parts and components should be dried before assembly and should be assembled in time; parts and components that cannot be assembled in time should be wrapped or covered with plastic cloth (film).
9) Make a good inventory and registration of tools, process fixtures, and low-value consumables used for assembly.

sections.text: 2. Assembly
(1) General technical requirements for seal assembly
The function of seals is to prevent leakage or make the leakage amount meet the design requirements. Reasonable assembly process and method can ensure the reliability and durability (life) of seals.

1) Check each part and component according to the drawing, especially the chamfers, lead-in chamfers, and fillets (blunting). There should be no burrs, flashes, etc., and the surfaces of grooves on mating (matching) parts and seals should not have tool marks (such as spiral marks, cross-cutting marks, trembling-cutting marks, etc.), scratches, knocks, or rust.
2) Before assembly, each part and component must be carefully and thoroughly cleaned.
Cleaning, and drying or wiping, especially the grooves of each seal must not retain cleaning liquid (oil) or other residues.
3) After cleaning, each component should be assembled in time; if it cannot be assembled in time, it should be wrapped or covered with plastic cloth (film).

4) Check the specifications, dimensions, and surface quality of the seals according to the drawing, and take them out in the required quantity at one time; seals contaminated on the surface (such as with oil stains, debris, dust, or sand, etc.) cannot be directly used for assembly.

5) Seals that have been disassembled or used generally cannot be used again for assembly, especially O-rings, coaxial seals, dust seals, and support rings (except for pre-assembly), retaining rings, etc.
6) An appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the mating surfaces of each matching (mating) part before assembly.

7) The lubricating oil (grease) applied during assembly must not contain solid particles or mechanical debris, including graphite, molybdenum disulfide grease, etc. It is best to use the special lubricating oil (grease) specified by the seal manufacturer.

8) Rubber seals are best assembled at a temperature of 23°C±2°C to 27°C±2°C; seals stored at low temperature must reach room temperature before assembly; seals (or parts with grooves) that need to be heated for assembly should be heated with hydraulic oil not exceeding 90°C, and should be assembled after returning to room temperature and cooling to shrink and set.

9) Various seals must not be overstretched during assembly, nor rolled for installation, or subjected to local strong pulling, pressing, twisting (rotating), folding, or strong compression (squeezing), etc.
10) For repairing surface damage of components, sandpaper (cloth) must not be used for grinding. Fine oilstone can be used for grinding, and it should be cleaned after repair.
11) Seals must not be omitted or over-installed. The installation direction and position of the seals must be correct, and the assembled components should be assembled as a whole in time.

12) During final assembly, if the piston or cylinder head (guide sleeve) needs to pass through oil (flow) holes, key slots, threads, or tool withdrawal slots, necessary protective measures must be taken to protect the seals (parts) from damage.

13) After final assembly, dust plugs (caps) should be used to seal the oil ports of each component, and seals, installation tools, including special tools and other low-value consumables, such as wiping cloths, should be counted.
(2) Technical requirements for O-ring assembly
1) Ensure that the shaft and hole of the mating parts have good coaxiality, so that the clearance around the circumference is uniform.

2) During the assembly process, prevent the O-ring from being scratched, abraded, or cut. When inserting it into the hole or the end of the shaft, there should be a sufficiently long guide cone (incline chamfer), and the intersection of the cone surface and the cylindrical surface should be rounded and smoothly transitioned.

3) If the O-ring needs to pass through oil holes, threads, tool withdrawal slots, elastic retaining ring grooves, or other seal grooves that may scratch, cut, or squeeze it during assembly, necessary protective measures must be taken, such as plugging, filling, shielding, or isolating, to ensure that the O-ring is not damaged during the assembly process. If necessary, special assembly tools should be designed, manufactured, and used.

4) An appropriate amount of grease should be applied to the groove first, and then the O-ring should be installed. Before assembly, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the mating surfaces of each mating (mating) part; after assembly, the mating parts should be able to move freely, and prevent the O-ring from twisting or rolling.

5) For O-rings installed in a stretched or compressed state, in order to restore the cross-section to a circular shape after pre-stretching or pre-compression, after the O-ring is installed in the groove, it should be left for a proper time before assembling the mating (mating) parts.

6) When installing and removing O-rings, installation and removal tools should be used. The material and style of the installation and removal tools should be selected appropriately, and the end and cutting edge should be blunt. It is forbidden to use sharp and hard tools such as steel needles to pry the O-ring to avoid damaging its surface.
7) O-rings and retaining rings that have been installed, removed, or used must not be used again for assembly.
8) Ensure that the retaining ring for the O-ring and the O-ring are in the correct relative position.
(3) Technical requirements for lip seal assembly

1) Check the specifications, dimensions, and surface quality of the seal, especially the lips (seal edges) must not have defects such as damage; at the same time, check the dimensions and tolerances of each component, surface roughness, chamfers (guide) angles, and fillets, and there must be no burrs or flashes. It is particularly emphasized that the piston seal and piston rod seal must be clearly distinguished, especially the YX-shaped seal ring for holes and the YX-shaped seal ring for shafts.
2) When assembling the lip seal, the direction must be correct; for the lip seal with a retaining ring, the relative position of the retaining ring and the seal must be correct.

3) Before installation, an appropriate amount of lubricating oil (grease) should be applied to the surface of the mating parts, an appropriate amount of grease should be applied to the seal groove, and the groove at the end of the lip seal should also be filled with grease, and the air should be discharged.

4) Special tools are generally required to install lip seals, and they can be made according to the type recommended by the seal manufacturer. If the lip seal needs to pass through oil holes, threads, tool withdrawal slots, or other seal grooves during installation, special measures must be taken to protect the seal from damage. The usual practice is to first install a special sleeve at the through part, or install 3 (4) petal retaining rings in the seal groove.

5) Lip seals (or parts with grooves) that need to be heated for assembly should be heated with hydraulic oil not exceeding 90°C, and should be assembled with the mating (mating) parts after returning to room temperature and cooling to shrink and set; water must not be used to heat lip seals, especially seals made of polyurethane and polyamide materials.

6) The pressure ring of the V-shaped seal, the V-shaped ring (with or without fabric), and the support ring (elastic seal ring) must be arranged and combined correctly, and must not be adjusted too tightly during initial adjustment.

7) Generally, a pre-assembly should be carried out after only the support ring is installed to check the coaxiality of the mating parts and the assembly of the support ring, and check the movement of the piston and piston rod if possible to avoid

436.page_header: Chapter 2  Design of Hydraulic Cylinders and Basic Components  425

sections.text:
To prevent rigid interference.
8) After assembly, there should be no jamming or uneven resistance during the reciprocating motion of the piston and piston rod throughout their full stroke.
(4) Technical Requirements for Assembling Coaxial Seals
Coaxial seals are composite seals composed of a plastic ring and a rubber ring, with the plastic ring providing the entire friction sealing surface. Therefore, they need to be assembled in steps.
The rubber ring must be assembled first. Please refer to the technical requirements for assembling O-rings mentioned above.
1) For piston seals, coaxial seals generally require heating for assembly. It is advisable to heat the plastic ring in hydraulic oil at a temperature not exceeding 90°C until it becomes highly elastic and stretchable. It may be necessary to heat the piston as well, which facilitates the cooling, shrinking, and shaping of the plastic ring.
2) For piston seals, coaxial seals generally require specialized installation tools and shrinking/shaping tools, which can be manufactured and used according to the type recommended by the seal manufacturer.
If it needs to pass through other seal grooves, relief grooves, etc., it is best to consider them in the installation tool.
The surface roughness of the contact surface between the shaping tool for the plastic ring and the plastic ring should be comparable to the surface roughness of the mating part.
3) Coaxial seals assembled after heating must be cooled to room temperature together with the piston before being assembled into the cylinder (tube). If coaxial seals for piston rods are installed using heating, they must also be cooled to room temperature before being assembled with the piston rod.
4) For piston rod seals, coaxial seals can also be assembled after heating, but the plastic ring needs to be bent into a concave shape before assembly. After assembly, a tapered mandrel shaping tool is generally used for shaping. Common issues include forgetting to install the rubber ring and incorrect installation direction of the plastic ring. For example, stepped coaxial seals are unidirectional seals and have specific directional requirements during installation.
5) Before installing the piston into the cylinder (tube) or the piston rod into the guide sleeve or cylinder head, the angle and length of the chamfer at the end of the cylinder (tube) and piston rod must be checked. The intersection between the tapered surface and the cylindrical surface must be rounded and smoothly transitioned, and the surface roughness must meet the requirements specified in the drawing.
6) Generally, coaxial seals should be installed first in a set of seals.
7) Pay attention to lubrication and strictly prohibit dry assembly.

(5) Technical Requirements for Assembling Support Rings
The support rings commonly used now are made of wear-resistant plastic materials and serve to support the piston or piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, preventing direct contact and collision between moving metal parts, and providing radial support and (axial) guiding functions.
In a certain sense, support rings can be considered as non-metallic bearings.
1) Check the dimensions and tolerances of the groove according to the drawing, especially the fillet at the bottom and edge of the groove. If possible, perform a pre-assembly to inspect the concentricity and movement of each component.
If the end of the hydraulic cylinder is equipped with a cushioning device, it is necessary to check whether the cushioning plunger interferes or collides with the cushioning hole.
2) Support rings with cut-type notches need to be cut and trimmed according to Appendix A of the GB/T15242.2-2017 standard, but the width of the cut notch of the support ring generally cannot be less than the specified value.
3) For batch products, a pre-shaping tool for the support ring should be made.
4) Generally, the support ring should be installed last in a set of seals. If there are multiple support rings in a set of seals, their notch positions should be staggered during installation.
5) Fix the support ring in the groove by applying an appropriate amount of grease. Note that applying too much grease is not conducive to fixing the support ring.
6) Before installing the piston into the cylinder (tube), the angle and length of the chamfer at the end of the cylinder (tube) must be checked. The intersection between the tapered surface and the cylindrical surface must be rounded and smoothly transitioned, and the surface roughness must meet the requirements specified in the drawing. Otherwise, the most likely issue during piston installation is the support ring falling out of the groove.
7) The support ring should be installed with the same precision as a bearing, and methods such as hammering, pressing, or using sandpaper (cloth) to grind and reduce the thickness of the support ring are not allowed. Additionally, using thin sheets (films) between the bottom of the groove and the support ring to reduce the fitting clearance is not allowed.
8) Support rings that have been used for pre-assembly should not be used again for assembly in other situations.
(6) Other Assembly Technical Requirements
1) Ensure the correct positioning of each component of the hydraulic cylinder according to the drawings and technical documents.
2) All threaded connections should be tightened according to the torque specified in the design. For those with specified requirements, follow the regulations, such as the tightening torque of screws for the CD250 and CD350 series heavy-duty hydraulic cylinders (see Table 2-337); for those without specified requirements, refer to Table 2-316 (fine-pitch bolts or nuts) and Table 2-332 (coarse-pitch bolts, screws, and nuts).
3) Important fixed mating surfaces should fit tightly; any components installed or connected to the hydraulic cylinder should be secure.
4) After assembly, ensure that the hydraulic cylinder moves freely, especially for those designed with end cushioning plungers, there should be no interference or collision during movement; there should be no damage to external threaded connections, port edges, etc.
5) Unless otherwise specified, the tolerance for the stroke length of a general hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 9 of JB/T10205.
6) For hydraulic cylinders with stroke positioning or limit devices, the deviation of the stroke positioning or limit should comply with the technical (accuracy) requirements or relevant standard regulations.
7) The surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be clean, with smooth and natural rounded corners, flat welds, and no burrs or sharp edges.
8) The nameplate should be clear and correct, and the installation should be secure and flat.
9) The painting of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of JB/T5673, and the color of the topcoat can be determined according to user requirements. The surface of the piston rod and positioning valve rod should not be painted.

sections.text: 2.18  Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Operation
The technical requirements for trial operation and/or operation of hydraulic cylinders are expressed differently in the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinders, as shown in Table 2-338.

For hydraulic presses (machines), technical requirements are generally provided for no-load operation. For example, JB/T 12996.2—2017 states: "There should be no sticking, crawling, or jumping phenomena during the operation of the ram and worktable."

Considering the above standards comprehensively, the starting and operating states of hydraulic cylinders that have passed factory tests should be described according to Table 2-339. If conditions permit, high-temperature, high-pressure, and their combined operating conditions should also be tested according to the standard. The test results should comply with the standard requirements.

Hydraulic cylinders are usually just a component in a hydraulic system or a part in a hydraulic press (machine). The trial operation and/or operation of hydraulic cylinders must meet the technical conditions of the hydraulic press (machine). Please refer to Chapter 4 for details.

After assembly of moving and rotating parts, the movement should be smooth, flexible, and light, without any jamming phenomenon.

The hydraulic cylinder driven by hydraulic pressure should not have vibration, crawling, or stagnation within the specified stroke and speed range (during operation). There should be no impact phenomenon that affects normal operation during commutation and pressure relief. For hydraulic cylinders with support ring seal structure, the support ring should be properly tight and reliably locked. The moving parts (including pistons, movable crossbeams or sliders, etc.) that slide quickly by their own weight should not have jamming phenomenon during rapid descent.
When the hydraulic cylinder is running unloaded or loaded, the movement of the piston should be smooth, without crawling or other abnormal phenomena.
During trial operation, the piston movement should be uniform, without crawling, external leakage, or other abnormal phenomena.
During the low-pressure test process, the hydraulic cylinder should not have vibration or crawling.
The dynamic load test of the hydraulic cylinder is conducted on-site at the user's location, observing whether the operation is smooth and flexible.

Chapter 3 Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders
3.1 Commonly Used Machine Tools and Equipment for Manufacturing Hydraulic Cylinders
3.1.1 Overview

This section mainly introduces metal cutting machine tools, which can be classified into general-purpose machine tools, specialized machine tools, dedicated machine tools, and combined machine tools. Commonly used metal cutting machine tools for manufacturing hydraulic cylinders include lathes, milling machines, drilling machines, boring machines, grinding machines, sawing machines, thread processing machine tools (pipe thread lathes), and machining centers. CNC machine tools are now widely used. CNC machine tools are machine tools that process workpieces according to digital information instructions issued by the control system based on pre-programmed programs. They mainly include CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes, CNC scraping and rolling lathes, CNC deep hole honing machines, vertical internal cylindrical honing machines, external cylindrical grinding machines, their types and parameters, technical conditions, and accuracy inspections. The types and parameters of machine tools determine their main purposes and generally limit the workpieces that can be processed, as well as their sizes, shapes, and even surface accuracy. They are the main basis for selecting workpiece manufacturing methods and determining workpiece machining processes, and also an important guarantee for the feasibility and economy of workpiece manufacturing. The technical conditions of machine tools are not only the basis for machine tool manufacturing and acceptance, but also the basis for troubleshooting when machine tools or products have problems. The geometric accuracy, positioning accuracy and repeatability, working accuracy requirements, inspection methods, and corresponding tolerances of machine tools are the main basis for judging whether the mechanical machining process of workpieces is reasonable. The accuracy of workpiece machining generally cannot exceed the accuracy that can be achieved by the test pieces during the accuracy inspection of the machine tool's working accuracy. Some machine tools are hydraulically driven, and their technical conditions clearly specify requirements for hydraulic systems and hydraulic cylinders, etc., so they can be used as the basis for designing and manufacturing hydraulic cylinders for these machine tools. The positioning accuracy and repeatability of the linear axes of these hydraulic transmission manual or automatic control machine tools can also be used as a reference for inspecting proportional/servo control hydraulic cylinders.
3.1.2 CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe

JB/T 13092.1-2017 "CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe Part 1: Accuracy Inspection" stipulates the geometric accuracy, positioning accuracy and repeatability, working accuracy requirements, inspection methods and corresponding tolerances of CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes; JB/T 13092.2-2017 "CNC Hydraulic Cylinder Lathe Part 2: Technical Conditions" stipulates the manufacturing and acceptance requirements of CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes, applicable to CNC hydraulic cylinder lathes with a maximum turning diameter of the bed body up to 1250 mm and a maximum workpiece length up to 5000 mm (hereinafter referred to as the machine tool).

7. No-load test
(1) Temperature rise test

The main moving mechanism of the machine tool shall start from the lowest speed and run at each level of speed in turn (run at low, medium and high speeds for stepless speed change mechanism). The running time at each speed shall not be less than 2 min, and the running time at the highest speed shall not be less than 1 h, so that the spindle bearing reaches a stable temperature. Check the temperature and temperature rise of the spindle bearing. The temperature shall not exceed 70°C, and the temperature rise shall not exceed 40°C.
(2) Inspection of main motion and feed motion

1) For the moving parts on each linear axis, carry out no-load test at low, medium, high and fast feed speeds respectively. The motion shall be stable and reliable, with no vibration at high speed and no obvious crawling at low speed.
2) The actual deviation of spindle speed and feed speed shall not exceed ±5% of the instruction value or the value indicated on the nameplate.
(3) Function test
1) Use buttons, switches or manual operation to carry out the following action tests on the machine tool to test the flexibility and reliability of the actions.

items: Select any spindle speed to start the spindle for forward rotation, reverse rotation, stop (including braking) continuous operation test, with no less than 10 times of continuous operation.
The spindle shall be tested for speed conversion at low, medium and high speeds.

Select any feed speed (or feed amount), and continuously operate the start, feed and stop actions. On the full stroke of Z axis and X axis, carry out work feed and fast feed tests. The fast feed test of Z axis and X axis can be carried out on more than 1/2 of the full stroke. The continuous operation in forward and reverse directions shall not be less than 7 times.
On the full stroke of Z axis and X axis, carry out the conversion test of low, medium and high feed speeds (or feed amounts).
Use a hand pulse generator or single-step to test the feed of the slide plate and slide plate.
Use manual or automatic operation to test the movement of the tailstock and tailstock sleeve on its full stroke.

For the moving parts with locking mechanism, carry out the locking test at any position on the full stroke. The slide plate of inclined and vertical guide rails shall not fall after cutting off the power.

sections.text: ⑧ Carry out the operation test of the chip removal device.
⑨ Carry out the function test of various indicator lights, control buttons, DNC communication transmission equipment and temperature regulating device of the numerical control device.
⑩ Carry out the function test of the safety, insurance and protection devices of the machine tool.

⑪ Carry out the sealing, lubrication and cooling performance test of the hydraulic, lubrication and cooling systems, which should be easy to adjust, flexible in action, well lubricated, well cooled, and no leakage in each system.
2) Use numerical control instructions to carry out the following action tests on the machine tool to test the flexibility and reliability of the actions.

① Carry out the forward rotation, reverse rotation, stop and speed change test of the spindle (for mechanical stepped speed change, carry out the speed conversion test at each level of speed; for stepless speed change, carry out the low, medium and high speed change test).
② Carry out the low, medium and high feed speed (feed amount) and fast feed change test of the feed mechanism.
③ Carry out various positioning tests of the rotary tool post.

④ Test the reliability and flexibility of the functions of overtravel protection of feed coordinates, manual data input, coordinate position display, return to reference point, program sequence number indication and retrieval, program pause, program end, program elimination, individual part feed, linear interpolation, circular arc interpolation, linear cutting cycle, taper cutting cycle, thread cutting cycle, circular arc cutting cycle, tool position compensation, pitch compensation, gap compensation, etc.

sections.text: 9. Minimum setting unit feed test
(1) Test method

First use rapid movement to move the moving part of the linear axis in the positive (or negative) direction for a certain distance and then stop, then give several instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, then stop, and use this position as the reference position. Then still give 1 instruction each time in the same direction for a total of 20 instructions for the minimum setting unit, so that the moving part moves and stops continuously, and measure its stopping position under each instruction. Then from the above final position, continue to give several instructions for the minimum setting unit in the same direction, so that the moving part moves and stops. From this position, give several instructions for the minimum setting unit in the negative (or positive) direction, so that the moving part approximately returns to the above final measurement position. The stopping positions of the moving part under these positive and negative instructions for several minimum setting units are not measured. Then starting from the above final measurement position, still give 1 instruction each time in the negative (or positive) direction for a total of 20 instructions for the minimum setting unit, continue to make the moving part move and stop continuously, and approximately return to the reference position, and measure its stopping position under each instruction, as shown in Figure 3-2.

sections.text: Measure at least at three positions in the middle and near both ends of the stroke. Each linear axis should be inspected. The error is calculated based on the maximum error value at the three positions.

10. Return-to-Origin Test

1) General requirements. When testing a particular axis, other moving parts should, in principle, be positioned at the midpoint of their stroke. For machine tools equipped with pitch error compensation and backlash compensation devices, the test should be conducted with these devices in use.

2) Test method. Make the moving parts of each linear axis move from any point on the stroke in the same direction at high speed, performing a 5-time return-to-origin test to a set origin Po. Measure the difference between the actual position Pi of the moving part each time and the theoretical origin position Po, which is the return-to-origin deviation Xi (i=1, 2, 3, 4, 5), as shown in Figure 3-3.

sections.text: 3.1.3 CNC Scraping and Rolling Machine Tools for 500–1500mm (hereinafter referred to as scraping and rolling machine)

In JB/T 13405–2018 "CNC Scraping and Rolling Machine Tools", the classification, naming, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation, and storage of CNC scraping and rolling machine tools are specified, which are suitable for metallurgical, aerospace, construction machinery, petroleum, coal, and other industries processing various metal cold drawn (rolled) pipes and hot rolled pipes with hardness of 170–310HBW, processing diameter of 50–630mm, processing length of 500–1500mm.
1. Classification and Naming
(1) Structural Composition of the Product
The scraping and rolling machine consists of four main parts: the main mechanical system, CNC electrical system, cutting fluid filtration system, and special composite cutting tools.
(2) Model and Marking
1) Model Representation Method

sections.caption: CNC Scraping and Rolling Machine Tool Classification Diagram
sections.description: Hierarchical diagram showing CNC scraping and rolling machine tool classification with the following structure: GGJ at top level, branching to blade machining method (1W—single blade scraping method—one-time processing; 2W—double blade scraping, return pressure; CR—dual blade scraping method—workpiece and blade simultaneous rotation; single blade rotation workpiece rotation, blade rotation does not rotate). Below shows maximum machining diameter (unit: mm), maximum machining length (unit: mm), and bed series: D—bed guide rail side clearance 500mm, E—bed guide rail side clearance 600mm, F—bed guide rail side clearance 800mm, G—bed guide rail side clearance 1000mm. Final level shows CNC Scraping and Rolling Machine Tool.

sections.text: 2) Marking Example

For a scraping and rolling machine tool with a bed rail outer side width of 600mm, maximum processing inner diameter of 300mm, maximum processing length of 3000mm, and double rotation processing method, with scraping and rolling simultaneously processed on one path, the marking is: GGJE3000/300–CR1W
(3) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of the scraping machine should comply with the provisions of Table 1 in JB/T 13405–2018. The accuracy of the processed products can be respectively:

items: Dimensional accuracy of IT7–IT8 grade
Surface roughness Ra value of 0.03–0.20μm
Roundness ≤0.03mm

sections.text: Based on the author's experience, it is difficult to achieve a surface roughness value of Ra0.03μm for the inner hole of pipes processed by a scraping machine. Specific usage should be consulted with the machine tool manufacturer.
2. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

Welded parts of the product should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.3; forgings should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.8; assembly should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.10; piping should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.11; painting should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.12. The series of standards GB/T 37400.1–2019 "General Technical Conditions for Heavy Machinery" including 16 parts has been implemented since March 1, 2020, and the corresponding parts can be correspondingly matched with the above industry standards.
(2) Performance Requirements
The load test run of the product should meet the following requirements:

items: All components operate normally, with flexible movement and no abnormal noise
The overall noise should not exceed 85dB(A)
Overload shutdown protection function should be available during processing
High and low liquid level alarm function for cutting fluid
High and low pressure protection for cutting fluid
Low air pressure protection
Low lubricating oil pressure alarm protection
8) Filter element clogging alarm protection.
9) The axial and radial runout of the spindle of the machine tool power head should be less than 0.02mm.
10) For equipment with a machining length greater than 5000mm, a vise clamping device should be installed.
11) Controllable timed automatic lubrication system.
12) Programmable control cooling system.

sections.text: (3) Technical requirements for main components
1) Requirements for hydraulic system components are as follows:

items: ① The design of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766.
② All used hydraulic components should comply with the provisions of GB/T 7935.

③ The technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders should comply with the provisions of JB/T 10205. When installing the hydraulic cylinder, if the structure allows, the inlet and outlet positions should be on the top or other easy-to-install surfaces.

sections.text: 2) Technical requirements for hydraulic stations are as follows:

items: ① The pump and motor spindle should rotate flexibly without any jamming.

② The hydraulic station should be tested in conjunction with the electrical device, and the actions of all hydraulic components should be correct and without jamming. A pressure test should be conducted at 1.5 times the working pressure, and the sealing condition of all hydraulic components should be good.
③ The hydraulic station should operate smoothly without any abnormal sounds, noise, or vibration.

sections.text: 3) Requirements for mechanical structure components are as follows:

items: ① The selected high-quality carbon structural steel and carbon structural steel materials should comply with the provisions of GB/T 699 and GB/T 700 respectively; the selected low-alloy high-strength steel should comply with the provisions of GB/T 1591; the selected cast carbon steel parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T 11352; the selected alloy tool steel should comply with the provisions of GB/T 1299.

② The chemical composition content and porosity of the bed casting should comply with the provisions of GB/T 9439; the surface hardness of the guide rail after high-frequency induction hardening should reach 50-55HRC, and the effective hardness depth should be 1.5-2.5mm. The casting should undergo annealing treatment and comply with the provisions of JB/T 7711.
③ The straightness error of the bed guide rail in the height direction and front-rear direction (with the operator's side as the front) should not be greater than 0.01/1000.
④ The saddle of the spindle box should be lined with plastic and scraped.

⑤ After installing the workpiece head, pressure head, and spindle box, the position tolerance of their centers relative to the bed guide rail surface should be less than 0.02mm, and the concentricity tolerance between the three centers should be less than ф0.01mm.
⑥ After installing the ball screw and trapezoidal screw, the position tolerance of their centers relative to the bed guide rail surface should be less than 0.02mm.
⑦ The oil tank should not have any leakage.
⑧ The lubrication system piping should not be blocked, and the joints should not have any oil leakage.

sections.text: 4) Requirements for electrical control components are as follows:

items: ① The operating mechanism and its accessories should operate flexibly, and the contacts of various auxiliary switches should be correctly and reliably closed and opened; before use, a simulated operation test should be conducted, and the actions of all electrical components (including electromagnets) should be correct and reliable.

② The continuity of the protective grounding circuit of the electrical control components should comply with the provisions of 18.2.2 in GB 5226.1-2008 (2019); the insulation resistance should comply with the provisions of 18.3 in GB/T 5226.1-2008 (2019); the withstand voltage should comply with the provisions of 18.4 in GB/T 5226.1-2008 (2019).

sections.text: (4) Requirements for installation foundation
The ground foundation should be flat, with a flatness error less than 2cm/10m, and the thickness of the cement foundation should be greater than 200mm.
(5) Safety protection

items: Couplings and exposed rotating parts should be equipped with protective covers.
Cables and wires should be equipped with protective conduits.

The mechanical equipment should be equipped with an emergency automatic shutdown switch for fault states; the electrical equipment should be equipped with an automatic alarm signal and an automatic power-off shutdown program for emergency states.
The program should include overload protection and interlock protection.
Warning signs should be posted on moving parts.

sections.text: (6) Appearance requirements

items: The coating should be flat, smooth, and uniform in color, without sagging, peeling, missing coating, scratches, or other defects.
Hydraulic components and electrical components should have clear and durable markings.
The surface of the weld seam should be flat and smooth, without defects such as incomplete welding, missing welding, or slag inclusion. Important parts should undergo non-destructive testing.

sections.text: 3.1.4 CNC Deep Hole Honing Machine

The geometric accuracy, positioning accuracy, and working accuracy requirements and inspection methods of CNC deep hole honing machines are specified in JB/T 12403.1-2015 "CNC Deep Hole Honing Machine Part 1: Accuracy Inspection"; the manufacturing and acceptance requirements of CNC deep hole honing machines are specified in JB/T 12403.2-2015 "CNC Deep Hole Honing Machine Part 2: Technical Conditions", which applies to CNC deep hole honing machines with a honing diameter of 20-500mm and a maximum honing depth of up to 16000mm (hereinafter referred to as the machine tool).
1. Structural type
The machine tool has two structural types: workpiece fixed type and workpiece rotating type.

items: Workpiece fixed type, with main components as shown in Figure 1 of JB/T 12403.1-2015, including: grinding rod box, grinding rod bracket, grinding rod guide frame, grinding head bracket, chip discharge hopper, workpiece bracket, bed, and saddle.

Workpiece rotating type, with main components as shown in Figure 2 of JB/T 12403.1-2015, including: grinding rod box, grinding rod bracket, grinding rod guide frame, grinding head bracket, chip discharge hopper, workpiece bracket, spindle box, bed, and saddle.

sections.text: 2. General requirements
When accepting the machine tool according to JB/T 12403.2-2015, the requirements in Chapter 3 "Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders" on page 734 should also be met simultaneously.

GB/T 9061—2006 "Metal Cutting Machine Tools - General Technical Conditions", GB/T 25373—2010 "Metal Cutting Machine Tools - Assembly General Technical Conditions", GB/T 25376—2010 "Metal Cutting Machine Tools - Mechanical Processing Parts General Technical Conditions" and other relevant acceptance items not specifically defined in JB/T 12403.2—2015 shall be inspected.
3. Accessories and Tools
1) Accessories and tools that should be supplied randomly to ensure the basic performance of the machine tool are shown in Table 3-10.
