sections.text: 3.4.2 Methods to Meet the Closed Loop Tolerance Requirements of Assembly Dimension Chains

According to product design requirements, structural characteristics, tolerance sizes, and production conditions, different methods can be adopted to meet the closed loop tolerance requirements. Commonly used methods include interchangeability, grouping, repair fitting, and adjustment.
1. Interchangeability Method
Depending on the degree of interchangeability, it can be divided into complete interchangeability and large number interchangeability.
(1) Complete Interchangeability Method

During assembly of all products, the component rings do not need to be selected or their sizes or positions changed. After assembly, the closed loop tolerance requirements can be met. This method uses the extreme value formula for calculation.
(2) Large Number Interchangeability Method

In the vast majority of products, the component rings do not need to be selected or their sizes or positions changed during assembly. After assembly, the closed loop tolerance requirements can be met. This method uses the statistical tolerance formula for calculation.

The large number interchangeability method is based on a certain confidence level. Generally, the closed loop tends to follow a normal distribution, with a confidence level P = 99.73%. At this time, the relative distribution coefficient k₀ = 1. Under certain production conditions, if it is required to appropriately enlarge the component ring tolerance, a lower P value can be taken. The relationship between confidence level and relative distribution coefficient is shown in Table 3-57.

sections.caption: Table 3-57 Relationship between Confidence Level and Relative Distribution Coefficient

sections.text: When using the large number interchangeability method, appropriate process measures should be taken to exclude individual products that exceed the tolerance range or limit deviation.
2. Grouping Method

The component rings are divided into several groups according to their actual sizes, and corresponding groups are assembled together. Parts in the same group have interchangeability. This method usually uses the extreme value tolerance formula for calculation.
3. Repair Method

During assembly, remove part of the material from the compensation ring to change its actual size, so that the closed ring meets its tolerance and limit deviation requirements. This method typically uses the extreme value tolerance formula for calculation.
4. Adjustment Method

During assembly, use adjustment methods to change the actual size or position of the compensation ring, so that the closed ring meets its tolerance and limit deviation requirements. Generally, bolts, inclined surfaces, retaining rings, shims, or clearances in hole-shaft connections are used as compensation rings. This method typically uses the extreme value tolerance formula for calculation.

In the assembly process of adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinders (see Figure 3-4), "using the repair method to trial-assemble the adjusting shim 15" includes dimensional chain calculation. Due to space limitations, this example calculation process is omitted in this manual.
3.5 Design and Use of Process Equipment for Hydraulic Cylinders
3.5.1 Significance of Using Process Equipment for Cylinder Processing

Professional cylinder manufacturers produce honed, rolled, cold-drawn seamless steel pipes or cylinders that meet the requirements of JB/T11718-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder Cylinders." These are frequently used by hydraulic cylinder manufacturers for hydraulic cylinder body manufacturing. For the manufacturing of single-piece or small-batch hydraulic cylinders, they have the advantages of being simple, fast, and low-cost, so they have been widely used in recent years.
Cylinders processed on CNC scraping and rolling machines using combined tools (rough boring, scraping, and rolling) can be classified as rolled cylinders.

In cylinder body manufacturing, since the purchased seamless steel pipes have only the inner hole precision machined, the outer circle and both end faces are generally not machined or precision machined. Moreover, the connections between the cylinder and the cylinder bottom, cylinder cap, etc. (including welding bevels) have not been machined either. Therefore, secondary machining is required to meet the various design and process requirements for hydraulic cylinder bodies.

The above-mentioned seamless steel pipes with honed, rolled, cold-drawn (or hot-rolled) inner holes or cylinders are semi-finished products for hydraulic cylinder bodies. They are collectively referred to as cylinders below.

To ensure the coaxiality, perpendicularity, and other geometric tolerance requirements of each machining surface to the cylinder's inner hole axis during secondary machining, it is now generally necessary to turn a section of outer cylindrical surface on the cylinder's outer circle that is coaxial with the cylinder's inner hole. Then, use a center frame to support this section of the outer circle for further machining.

The processing of this section of the outer circle is purely a process requirement for the process datum, not a product design datum. However, if this section of the cylinder's outer circle is not machined, it would be almost impossible to complete the subsequent processes. Machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle not only affects the appearance of the product but also weakens the cylinder's strength. Therefore, some users explicitly require that this section of the cylinder's outer circle must not be machined.

Machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle also faces difficulties in clamping and alignment, such as using a self-centering chuck to expand and clamp one end of the inner hole, then aligning the other end's inner hole. Although this clamping and alignment method is widely used, it is very difficult to implement in practice, time-consuming, and the quality is not guaranteed. Using a single-action chuck to clamp the outer circle and aligning the other end's inner hole also faces the same problems. Moreover, since it is necessary to simultaneously determine the centers of the two end inner holes coinciding with the machine tool's centerline, the alignment is even more difficult. The above two clamping and alignment methods share a common problem, that is, the chuck jaws must be in line contact with the workpiece; otherwise, it will be impossible to align the other end. Regardless of how this clamping may damage the inner hole, in terms of machining, line contact clamping has very low resistance to cutting forces and other external forces.

To improve resistance to cutting forces and other external forces, it is often necessary to first machine the cylinder's end face, then use the tailstock center to support the cylinder before machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle. However, machining also faces the same problem, that is, low resistance during end face machining.

The most reliable method for machining this section of the cylinder's outer circle is to use a cylindrical mandrel, especially using a centering clamping mandrel for machining, which is most reasonable in theory. However, it has the following problems in practice: 1) Although seamless steel pipes of the same inner hole diameter have different lengths, different lengths of centering clamping mandrels are needed. 2) Because the centering clamping mandrel must pass through the entire length of the seamless steel pipe's inner hole, it is very difficult to ensure that it does not damage the inner hole surface. 3) Due to its structural reasons, large-diameter centering clamping mandrels are too heavy.

There is also a simple centering clamping mandrel, but the problem is that the inner hole surface is almost damaged after clamping. Sometimes, it cannot be removed after clamping. Moreover, different lengths of simple centering clamping mandrels are also needed.
The centering expansion sleeve designed by the author is to solve the above problems and provide a kind of process equipment for turning processing centering fixtures for cylinder processing.

This centering expansion sleeve can process the other end of the cylinder according to the hydraulic cylinder design requirements under the conditions of one end of the cylinder's inner hole being expanded and clamped by a self-centering chuck and the tailstock extended center supporting and positioning the centering expansion sleeve. It does not need to process an additional process datum, that is, it does not need to machine a section of the outer cylindrical surface on the cylinder's outer circle that is coaxial with the cylinder's inner hole and use a center frame to support and position this section of the outer circle for further machining. Instead, it can directly machine to meet the hydraulic cylinder design requirements, and the same inner hole diameter cylinders can use one (type) of centering expansion sleeve, which can be reused.

Using the centering expansion sleeve as process equipment for cylinder processing is not only because using process equipment can ensure product quality, improve productivity, reduce costs, accelerate production cycles, and increase economic benefits, but also because it is necessary in some cases. For example, for the hydraulic cylinders of RAS series gate-type hydraulic shearing machines produced by a certain company, when the host manufacturer does not allow processing the process datum on the cylinder's outer circle, it is almost impossible to ensure the coaxiality or perpendicularity of the machined part of the cylinder to the cylinder's axial direction by aligning the inner hole. At the same time, without the support and positioning of the center frame, turning machining of the cylinder's end is also very difficult. Moreover, when the outer shape of the cylinder body is not circular (such as square or rectangular cylinder bodies, etc.) and has a certain length, even if the headstock end of the cylinder body is positioned using a center plug and tightened with threads, it is still difficult to perform turning machining on the other end due to excessive overhang length, especially for long cylinders, or even impossible. Therefore, using the centering expansion sleeve as process equipment for cylinder processing is necessary in this case.
3.5.2 Design and Use of Centering Expansion Mandrel
1. Structural Design of Centering Expansion Mandrel

The centering expansion mandrel for cylinder boring is shown in Figure 3-11. The outer surface of the mandrel's locating seat 5 is a cylindrical surface that mates with the double-cone sleeve 3 and the movable plate 10's inner hole. The right end of the locating seat 5's inner hole (upper and lower, left and right as marked in Figure 3-11) is equipped with a standard 60° C-type center hole 22, with a threaded hole in the middle and a through hole at the left end. Each end face of the double-cone sleeve 3 is provided with an O-ring rubber seal groove, with O-ring rubber seals 2 and 15 installed (install 15 first). The double-cone sleeve 3 is inserted from the left end of the mandrel's locating seat 5 into the sleeve on the mandrel until the O-ring rubber seal 15 axially contacts the left end face of the locating seat 5's seat portion. Hexagon socket head cap screws 23 (with thread-locking adhesive applied to the screw end) connect the locating seat 5 and double-cone sleeve 3, ensuring a designed clearance between the left end face of the locating seat 5's seat portion and the right end face of the double-cone sleeve 3.

2. Working Principle of Centering Expansion Mandrel

During the process of tightening the threaded end hexagon adjustment rod 6 with an extended hexagon wrench through the hexagon socket wrench hole 21, the movable plate 10 and a group of steel balls 1 and 13 push the steel balls along the left conical surface of the double-cone sleeve 3 to the right, generating radial displacement and expanding the left end diameter of the thin-walled sleeve 14. Simultaneously, the locating seat 5 and another group of steel balls 16 and 24 push the steel balls along the right conical surface of the double-cone sleeve 3 to the left, generating radial displacement and expanding the right end diameter of the thin-walled sleeve 14. Since both ends of the thin-walled sleeve 14 are expanded, the centering expansion mandrel automatically centers and expands (tightens) within the cylinder bore.
3. Use of Centering Expansion Mandrel

After cleaning the cylinder bore to be processed, the centering expansion mandrel is lifted into the cylinder bore using two lifting eye bolts 20, leaving sufficient length (depth) for processing. Using an extended hexagon wrench through the hexagon socket wrench hole 21 to tighten the threaded end hexagon adjustment rod 6, the centering expansion mandrel automatically centers and expands (tightens) within the cylinder bore. After removing the lifting device and lifting eye bolts, the cylinder with the centering expansion mandrel is lifted onto the lathe for clamping. The cylinder end without the centering expansion mandrel uses a self-centering chuck to expand and clamp the bore. When using an extended center to tighten the 60° C-type center hole 22, the cylinder is clamped with a self-centering chuck, completing the cylinder tube clamping for the boring process.

Note that pads or wooden blocks should be placed on the machine tool guideways beforehand to prevent the cylinder from accidentally falling and causing injury to personnel and damage to the machine tool. Before clamping the cylinder, the pads or wooden blocks should not be removed, and the lifting device should not be released. Before processing after clamping, the pads or wooden blocks and lifting device must be removed and released. After completing this process, the centering expansion mandrel is removed following the above process in reverse. However, note that when the cylinder is placed vertically with the top end removed, the centering expansion mandrel is removed.

When centering the expansion mandrel, the lifting tool must be installed first and the centering expansion mandrel must be in a suspended state before loosening the internal hexagonal adjustment rod 6. Otherwise, the centering expansion mandrel may slip and fall, causing damage to the cylinder tube and the centering expansion mandrel.
4. Characteristics of the centering expansion mandrel
The centering expansion mandrel has the following characteristics in cylinder tube processing:

items: There is no need to manufacture centering clamping mandrels or simple centering clamping mandrels for individual products, which reduces the difficulty of cylinder body processing, saves manufacturing costs, and shortens the manufacturing cycle.

There is no need to machine an outer circle on the outer surface of the cylinder tube as a process reference, which eliminates one process step and avoids introducing process reference errors into subsequent processing steps, while also improving the appearance quality, strength, and stiffness of the cylinder tube.
A centering expansion mandrel can be used to process cylinder tubes with the same inner diameter, without any requirements on the length of the cylinder tube, and has good versatility.

Two centering expansion mandrels can be used simultaneously to clamp and expand a cylinder tube for double-end processing, which not only further reduces working hours and improves efficiency, but also expands the application range of the centering expansion mandrel.
Using the centering expansion mandrel can maximize the elimination of the influence of human factors on product quality, ensuring the consistency of the geometric accuracy of the cylinder tube.
According to relevant standards, the centering expansion mandrel can be designed and manufactured in a standardized and serialized manner.

sections.text: In summary, the application of the centering expansion mandrel in cylinder tube processing can make single-piece and small-batch cylinder tube processing easier, improve the structural processability of the cylinder tube, and may further transform special process equipment into general-purpose process equipment, or even standard process equipment.
3.6 Several Process Issues in Rolling and Honing of Cylinder Tubes
3.6.1 Process Quality Issues in Rolling Holes

Rolling holes is generally arranged as the final finishing process for the inner diameter of hydraulic cylinder tubes, but poor surface quality is found after rolling the inner diameter of the cylinder tube, and only then do people think of pursuing the quality of the inner hole before rolling, which happens frequently.

Rolling is a processing method that applies pressure to a metal blank or workpiece using a rolling tool to cause plastic deformation, thereby forming the blank or rolling the surface of the workpiece. Rolling holes is a chip-free finishing processing method that utilizes the plasticity of the material, uses a rolling head to roll the processed surface, causing plastic deformation on the surface to form a hardened layer and produce residual compressive stress.
The plastic deformation in rolling follows three principles: the yield principle, the flow principle, and the strengthening principle.
Note: In GB/T 4863—2008, the definition of the term "rolling holes" is: "Processing the holes of a workpiece using the rolling method."

(1) The role of rolling holes
Rolling holes generally has the following roles:
1) Reduce the surface roughness value. Rolling can improve surface quality, i.e., surface integrity. Generally, the surface roughness value can be reduced by at least two levels, for example: carbon steel (45 steel) has a roughness of Ra3.2μm before rolling → about Ra0.2μm after rolling; cast iron (HT150～HT330) has a roughness of Ra3.2μm before rolling → about Ra0.8μm after rolling.
2) Correct the roundness. If the process parameters are selected correctly, the roundness of the hole after rolling is improved.
3) Improve surface hardness. Generally, it can improve the surface hardness by 15% to 30%, for example: carbon steel (45 steel) has a hardness of 197HBW before rolling → 240HBW after rolling; cast iron (HT150～HT330) has a hardness of 180HBW before rolling → 198HBW after rolling.
4) Improve wear resistance. Generally, the wear resistance of the surface can be improved by about 15% after rolling.
5) Improve fatigue strength. Generally, the fatigue strength of the surface can be improved by about 30% after rolling, and the notch fatigue strength (45 steel sample) can be improved by 78% to 121%.

3.6.2 Issues with Honing Texture of Cylinder Tubes
Vertical internal cylindrical honing machines are mainly used for honing cylinders. If used for hydraulic cylinder tubes,

The honing of hydraulic cylinder tubes, how to choose the process parameters and honing effect, even some honing machine manufacturers can't explain clearly, mainly because of the cross-hatch pattern problem. This is still a test question that some hydraulic cylinder manufacturers often use to examine whether engineering technicians are proficient in the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders.

Honing is a method of finishing by applying a certain pressure to the surface of the workpiece using a honing tool, while the honing tool performs relative rotation and linear reciprocating motion, and cuts off an extremely small amount of excess on the workpiece. Honing is a special form of grinding, belonging to finishing. The principle of honing is that under a certain pressure, a complex relative motion is generated between the abrasive strip and the machined surface of the workpiece, and the abrasive particles of the abrasive strip play the roles of cutting, scraping, and squeezing, cutting off a very thin metal layer from the machined surface.

During honing, the abrasive strip expands and contracts radially, and contacts the hole surface with a certain pressure; the abrasive strip has three movements: rotational movement, reciprocating movement, and radial movement under pressure; the rotational movement and reciprocating movement make the cutting trajectory of the abrasive particles on the hole surface form a cross-shaped and non-repeating mesh pattern, which is conducive to storing lubricating oil and reducing the wear of the part surface. In order to prevent the motion trajectory of the abrasive particles of the abrasive strip from repeating, the number of revolutions per minute of the honing head and the number of reciprocating strokes per minute of the honing head should be mutually prime.

Honing can be divided into three stages: the first stage is the falling cutting stage; the second stage is the broken cutting stage; the third stage is the blocked cutting stage (equivalent to polishing). Honing can be divided into constant pressure honing and constant quantity honing.

Honing can improve the dimensional accuracy, roundness, straightness, cylindricity, and surface roughness of holes. For small and medium-sized hydraulic cylinder tubes, cold drawing-floating boring-rolling-honing is the most economical, efficient, and reasonable.
Honing has the following characteristics:

items: The abrasive particles of the abrasive strip have a small load and a long service life.
The speed is low, generally below 100 mm/min.

A large amount of cutting fluid is injected during honing, which can wash away the fallen abrasive particles, fully cool the machined surface, generate little heat in the workpiece, and have an extremely thin deformation layer, thereby obtaining a better surface quality.
Honing can generally obtain holes with IT6~IT7 accuracy, Ra0.025~Ra0.2μm, and shape error is generally less than 0.005 mm.

sections.text: The process elements of honing processing mainly include the number of honing times, cross-hatch angle α, working pressure, the length of the abrasive strip extending out of the hole, the type and particle size of the abrasive material of the abrasive strip, honing fluid, etc.
The honing of cylinder tubes can be selected according to the following process elements:

items: Honing is divided into rough honing, fine honing, and super fine honing. The honing allowance after boring is 0.05~0.08 mm, the honing allowance after reaming is 0.02~0.04 mm, and the honing allowance after grinding is 0.01~0.02 mm. For allowances that are large or require high accuracy, it can be divided into three times of rough honing, fine honing, and super fine honing.

The rotational speed is generally vr=14~48 m/min, and the reciprocating feed speed va=5~15 m/min. The cross-hatch angle α=2arctan(va/vr), and the cross-hatch angle is generally 30°~60°, with 45° being the best.
The working pressure of honing is selected as follows: 0.5~2.0 MPa for rough honing, 0.2~0.8 MPa for fine honing, and 0.05~0.1 MPa for super fine honing. Generally, 0.2~0.5 MPa can be taken.

During honing, the abrasive strip must extend beyond both ends of the hole, which is usually called the "cutting out" length. Some data suggest that a length of 1/3 of the abrasive strip is most suitable.

Abrasive materials suitable for grinding carbon steel and ductile iron include brown corundum A (GZ) and microcrystalline corundum MA (GW), etc. Honing abrasive strips should use ceramic binder (V), the hardness of the honing abrasive strip should be selected as K~P, and the particle size of the abrasive strip should be selected as F80 or above.

sections.text: The honing process for cylinder bore platforms is now very mature and has relevant standards, and its process can be referenced to meet the technical requirements of hydraulic cylinder tubes.
The honing of cylinder bore platforms is generally divided into three processes:

items: The first process is mechanical expansion knife constant quantity honing, which is to eliminate the geometric errors produced by boring the cylinder, so that the roundness and cylindricity of the cylinder meet the requirements, and provide appropriate surface roughness and machining allowance for the next process.

The second process is also mechanical expansion knife constant quantity honing, but the feed speed and feed amount are smaller than the first process, which is to form a clear, symmetrical, and uniform mesh pattern on the cylinder bore surface, that is, the groove pulling process.

The third process is the fine honing process, which uses constant pressure honing, divided into two levels of pressurization, which is to form a platform, that is, to remove the peaks and retain the valleys, forming a certain width and number of platforms, and retaining a certain depth of grooves.

sections.text: Three standards have been used for cylinder bores: ZBJ92011-1989 is the mirror honing standard; JB/T9768-1999 is the ordinary honing standard; DIN4776-1990 is the platform honing standard. The current standard is JB/T5082.7-2011 "Internal Combustion Engine Cylinder Liners Part 7: Platform Honing Cross-hatch Technical Specifications and Testing Methods".

Comparing the honing of the inner hole of the cylinder tube with the honing of the cylinder bore, it can be concluded that the main difference is that the honing of the inner hole of the cylinder tube does not have the groove pulling process, and it is not necessary (not allowed) for the inner hole surface of the cylinder tube to form a "clear, symmetrical, and uniform mesh pattern".
3.6.3 The problem of choosing the process of rolling holes and honing holes

What should be the difference between rolling the inner hole of the cylinder tube and honing the inner hole of the cylinder tube (requirements), and under what circumstances (or conditions) should the process of rolling holes or honing holes be chosen for the cylinder tube of the hydraulic cylinder? This is a problem that is often faced.

Rolling holes or honing holes are both methods of finishing the inner hole surface. Without considering other factors (requirements or problems) for the time being, the pros and cons of the above two methods of finishing the inner hole of the cylinder tube are weighed only from the perspective of ensuring the service life of the sealing element, that is, durability.
Note: This section mainly involves the relationship between the surface microstructure (or texture) of the cylinder bore and the tribological performance of seals including support rings.

In JB/T 11718-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders", the processing method for the inner bore of the cylinder is not specified. Only the tolerance grade for cylinder diameter, roundness of the inner bore, straightness of the bore axis, and surface roughness of the inner bore are specified. In common piston sealing devices, the standards do not specify the processing methods for components (cylinder parts, such as cylinder tubes) that contact seals (including support rings), and even do not specify the surface roughness of the cylinder bore. For example, in GB/T 2879-2005 "Dimensions and Tolerances of Dynamic Sealing Grooves for Hydraulic Cylinder Pistons and Piston Rods", it is stipulated: "The surface roughness of components contacting seals depends on the application and requirements for seal life, and should be determined through consultation between the manufacturer and user."

Based on the understanding of hydraulic sealing technology, it is insufficient to represent (require) the surface structure parameters of the cylinder bore only by the arithmetic mean deviation Ra and maximum height Rz of the profile. It should also include the relative bearing ratio Rmr. For sealing purposes, the Rmr of cylinder parts in contact with seals should be between 50% and 70%.
Therefore, some finishing processes for piston or piston rod sealing groove bottom surfaces can also consider using rolling processes.

Comprehensively considering the requirements of sealing, friction, and lubrication, and from the perspective of the applicability of sealing materials, the finishing processing method for the cylinder bore should be selected as follows:
1) Honing or honing plus polishing can be successively applied to nitrile rubber or fluorine rubber, polyurethane rubber, polytetrafluoroethylene (filled) plastic, and polyamide (filled) plastic.
2) Rolling can be successively applied to polytetrafluoroethylene (filled) plastic and polyamide (filled) plastic, polyurethane rubber, fluorine rubber, or nitrile rubber.
3) From the perspective of ensuring the relative bearing ratio Rmr alone, rolling is superior to honing because rolling can achieve an Rmr of up to 70%.
Polishing after honing may not significantly improve the relative bearing ratio Rmr, but it can significantly reduce seal wear including micro-movement wear. Therefore, polishing should be performed after honing the bore, and polishing can also be performed after rolling.
There are doubts about the claims by some scraping and rolling machine manufacturers that scraping and rolling surfaces have the same oil storage capacity as honed surfaces.
For cylinder parts such as guide sleeves or support rings made of metal materials such as cast iron and copper alloys, the inner bore that directly contacts the piston rod and serves guiding and supporting functions can use rolling as one of its finishing processing methods.
3.7  Common Surface Treatment Processes for Piston Rods
3.7.1  Polishing and Inspection Issues Before and After Chrome Plating of Piston Rods

Spiral patterns were found on the surface after chrome plating of piston rods, which was finally determined to be caused by belt polishing before plating by the electroplating factory; roundness, cylindricity, and straightness problems were also found on the workpiece after plating, which was also considered to be caused by belt polishing before and/or after plating. Improper polishing may further increase the waviness of the piston rod surface.

Polishing is a processing method that uses mechanical, chemical, or electrochemical action to obtain a bright and smooth surface on the workpiece. Its characteristic is to reduce the surface roughness value of the polished surface using free abrasive and soft polishing tools to obtain or improve the surface finish. Polishing before chrome plating of piston rods is mainly to improve the brightness of the surface after plating.
Therefore, it is judged that the term "belt polishing" is problematic and should be called "belt grinding".

Belt grinding or polishing cannot be used for piston rod surfaces before chrome plating, especially belt grinding on belt grinding equipment modified from old lathes without strict belt grinding process specifications, because it is very likely to damage the geometric accuracy and surface finish of the surface that has already formed on the external cylindrical grinder.

In order to ensure the surface finish or brightness after plating, the surface roughness value of the piston rod surface must not be higher than Ra0.8μm after external cylindrical grinding, and should be Ra0.4μm or below.

Polishing or grinding must be performed after plating, but the polishing allowance should not be too large; generally, the unilateral allowance should be between 0.01 and 0.02mm. After polishing after plating, straightness, roundness, cylindricity, and surface finish should be inspected.
The polishing or grinding after plating should also pay attention to improving the relative bearing ratio Rmr of the surface structure, because it affects the sealing performance of the piston rod.

Due to the possible unevenness of the chromium coating, there is now also a process of grinding the outer circle and then polishing or grinding after chrome plating with a coating thickness ≥0.10mm, but if the coating is too thick, it will not only increase the cost, but also there is a risk of defects such as peeling or delamination of the coating. Therefore, it is not recommended to use a process with a coating thickness exceeding 0.10mm.

The minimum (maximum) thickness of the hard chromium coating, the hardness of the hard chromium coating, the measurement method, and the inspection rules should be negotiated and determined according to the relevant regulations of the electroplating factory. If necessary, the adhesion strength, dimensional accuracy, and geometric tolerances of the hard chromium coating can also be included.

For the outer surface of the piston rod chrome-plated with hard chromium, the hardness of the hard chromium coating should be greater than or equal to 800HV0.2, and the thickness of the hard chromium coating should be between 0.04 and 0.10mm.

Special reminder: The hard chromium layer is very sensitive to impact, and is easily damaged by local hammering, impact, or knocking, etc. Even if the hard chromium layer is not visibly damaged by impact, it may still affect its performance.

The chrome coating on the piston rod surface may crack or peel off quickly, causing further damage to the sealing device, system, and contacting metal parts. Therefore, it is essential to protect the piston rod surface during post-plating polishing or grinding. The method of using a hammer (small sheet metal hammer) to repair the damaged hard chrome layer on the piston rod is not recommended, as it will inevitably cause local out-of-roundness of the piston rod and may lead to large-scale cracking or peeling of the hard chrome layer, resulting in seal damage and external leakage at the piston rod seal.
3.7.2 Technical Requirements for Thickness and Hardness of Chrome Coating on Piston Rod Surface

A 630T hydraulic press hydraulic cylinder piston rod was scratched, causing external leakage at the piston rod seal. Upon on-site inspection, besides finding problems with the cleanliness of the hydraulic oil used, it was also considered that there were issues with the thickness and hardness of the hard chrome layer (chrome coating) on the piston rod surface, i.e., the coating was too thin and the hardness was too low.

Since some hydraulic cylinder manufacturers do not have professional instruments and equipment to check the thickness and hardness of the chrome coating on the piston rod surface, and some electroplating factories even polish the electroplated surface after plating the piston rod, the piston rod after outsourcing electroplating has become a finished product. Therefore, hydraulic cylinder manufacturers only check the appearance of the chrome coating on the piston rod surface (such as unevenness, darkness, roughness, delamination, peeling, or blistering defects) and neglect the most basic inspection of coating thickness and hardness.
There is now a fast hard chrome plating method in electroplating factories, which has problems when used to plate the piston rod surface.

According to the technical requirements proposed in this manual and referring to the provisions of GB/T 25974.2-2010 and JB/T 5082.5-2018 "Engine Cylinder Liners Part 5: Technical Conditions for Steel Plated Chrome Cylinder Liners," the outer surface of the piston rod should be plated with hard chrome, and the hardness of the chrome coating should be greater than or equal to 800 HV0.2; before polishing or grinding, the thickness of the chrome coating should be between 0.04-0.10 mm, and after polishing or grinding, the chrome coating should generally be within the range of 0.03-0.05 mm.

For some servo hydraulic cylinders (such as high-frequency, short-stroke reciprocating servo hydraulic cylinders) or some hydraulic cylinders with special requirements (such as special environmental requirements), the chrome coating after polishing or grinding should be thicker.
The hardness of the chrome coating can be tested according to the provisions of GB/T 9790-1988 "Vickers and Knoop Microhardness Tests for Metallic Coatings and Other Related Coatings."
Note: In YB/T 017-2017, it is stipulated that the detection of coating hardness shall be carried out in accordance with GB/T 4340.1.

The minimum (maximum) thickness of the chrome coating can be obtained by measuring the difference in dimensions before and after plating, or by using GB/T 6462-2005 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic and Oxide Coatings - Microscope Method," GB/T 4955-2005 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic Coatings - Coulometric Method by Anodic Dissolution," GB/T 31563-2015 "Measurement of Thickness of Metallic Coatings - Scanning Electron Microscope Method," etc.
3.8 Typical Mechanical Processing and Assembly Processes for Hydraulic Cylinders

The mechanical processing process is a processing method and process that transforms various raw materials and semi-finished products into products that meet the drawings and technical requirements by using mechanical force to process them, according to the drawings and technical requirements, etc.

The assembly process is a method and process of assembling and connecting parts or components to make them into semi-finished products or finished products that meet the drawings and technical requirements, according to the drawings and technical requirements, etc.

The mechanical processing process and assembly process generally need to be specific, i.e., documented and standardized. One of the commonly used process documents - the process card, is a process document that briefly explains the processing (or assembly) process of a product or component in terms of work steps. The following mechanical processing and assembly processes are given in the form of process cards, but also include materials and their heat treatment, some surface engineering technologies, such as rolling holes, surface quenching, and surface rust prevention (coating), etc.

In order to standardize the mechanical processing process and assembly process, typical processes can be formulated, i.e., according to the structure and process characteristics of the product or part, they are classified or grouped, and unified processing (assembly) methods and processes are formulated for products or parts of the same type or group. It is very necessary to formulate typical processes for hydraulic cylinders.

Note: In GB/T 4863-2008 "Basic Terms of Mechanical Manufacturing," there are no terms such as "mechanical processing process" and "assembly process," only the term "mechanical manufacturing process," i.e., a general term for various methods and processes of manufacturing machinery.
3.8.1 Mechanical Processing and Assembly Processes for Adjustable Stroke Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Mechanical Processing Process for Cylinder Parts of Adjustable Stroke Hydraulic Cylinder

An adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder for a hydraulic upper-type sheet metal bending machine (see Figure 3.4) has mechanical processing processes for the cylinder end cover, piston end cover, trapezoidal thread shaft, and stop block that do not have typical significance in other hydraulic cylinders, and also involve the design and processing accuracy of trapezoidal threads. Therefore, only the mechanical processing process of the cylinder (see Figure 3.5) and piston rod (see Figure 3.7) and the processing process of trapezoidal threads are given below, while the process drawings are omitted.

(3) Trapezoidal Thread Machining Process

items: Trapezoidal Thread Turning Method.
The general methods for thread turning include radial feed, oblique feed, axial feed, improved oblique feed, and double-edged alternating feed, with the latter

sections.text: Both are mainly used for CNC machining; the choice of cutting method primarily considers factors such as material, pitch, thread accuracy, and machine tool performance.

② For trapezoidal threads with a pitch P≤8, rough turning followed by finish turning is required. Rough turning can use radial cutting with a tool whose tooth angle is 2° smaller than the thread angle and cut to the minor diameter; finish turning can use a forming tool with the same tooth angle for radial cutting, or use a tool with the same tooth angle but thinner than the forming tool for axial cutting.

③ The tooth angle of the cutting tool is critical, and tool installation is also very important. Radial cutting produces higher thread accuracy but generally results in larger surface roughness values; axial cutting may affect the tooth shape but can produce threads with smaller surface roughness values.

④ On CNC lathes, alternating cutting with double-edged tools results in uniform wear on both cutting edges and can achieve good tooth shapes and lower surface roughness values, but the programming is complex.
2) Thread cutting tools.
① Rough turning can use high-speed steel single-tooth flat thread cutting tools or hard alloy thread cutting tools.
② Finish turning generally uses hard alloy thread forming cutting tools (indexable thread cutting tools).
3) Tool installation methods.
① Rough turning tools can generally be installed perpendicularly, but cutting may produce tooth angle errors.
② Finish turning must use special fixtures to hold the thread cutting tool.
③ Hard alloy tools should be higher than 1% of the thread outer diameter, while high-speed steel tools can be slightly below the workpiece axis.
④ The protrusion of the thread cutting tool from the tool holder should not exceed 1.5 times the height of the tool shank cross-section.
4) Selection of process parameters. Trapezoidal thread process parameters can refer to Tables 3-62 to 3-64.

sections.text: 5) Lead screw cutting. The process requirements for lead screw cutting are as follows:

① The semi-finished blank of the lead screw to be cut should have internal stress fully eliminated to ensure stable internal structure. The blank can be spheroidized annealed with a hardness of 180～210 HBW.

② The center holes at both ends of the lead screw to be turned must be on the same straight line, and the center holes must be ground before finish turning, with a surface roughness value Ra≤0.2μm, and when matched with standard center points, the contact surface should be no less than 85%; before finish turning, the outer circle should be finely ground to ensure the outer circle cylindrical error ≤0.01mm; the gap between the outer circle and the follower rest ≤0.01mm.
③ During rough turning, a large amount of emulsion should be poured, and during finish turning, fine cutting fluid should be used.
Cutting fluid. It can use 30% soybean oil + 20% kerosene + 50% high-speed all-loss system oil (high-speed spindle oil).

④ For precision turning, high-vanadium cobalt or super-hard high-speed steel turning tools can be selected. Fine-grained hard alloy (such as YG6X) forming turning tools should be selected, with high grinding support amount. It is not allowed to have burns, nicks, or burrs on the cutting edge. The blunt radius of the cutting edge R should not be greater than 0.005 mm, and the surface roughness of the cutting edge Ra should be ≤0.1 μm.

⑤ The machining environment should be clean, and the room temperature should be constant. Generally, for machining a 1000 mm long lead screw with 7-level precision, the temperature change should be ≤±1°C.
⑥ Cutting speed. Rough turning: high-speed steel turning tool, 10 m/min; hard alloy turning tool, 30-50 m/min. Semi-precision turning: 8-10 m/min. Precision turning: cutting speed ≤1 m/min.

⑦ Cutting amount. For rough turning, the cutting amount per pass is about 0.4 mm. For precision turning, the cutting amount per pass is about 0.2 mm (related to material and hardness), but the cutting amount should be gradually reduced.

⑧ Tool geometric parameters. For precision turning tools, the front angle is 0°, the side cutting edge angle is 10°-12°, and the tool edge angle is taken as 1/4 to 1/3 of the tolerance of the lead screw thread angle.
2. Assembly process of adjustable stroke hydraulic cylinder
(1) Preparation
1) According to the production task schedule, receive and further familiarize with the assembly drawings and related process documents.
2) According to the schedule and the parts list in the assembly drawing, receive the parts, and the quantity received should match the actual assembly quantity required.
3) Check the support condition of each part, especially pay attention to check the type, specification, size, and appearance support of the seals. If any problems are found, report them in time.

3.9 Taboos for Design and Manufacturing of Hydraulic Cylinders

Taboos for design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders refer to the prohibitions, dangers, disapprovals, non-allowances, impossibilities or impossibilities expressed by "should not (or should not, not allowed)", "not suitable (or not recommended, not suggested)", "not necessary (or not necessary, not needed)", "cannot (or cannot)", "impossible (or impossible)" in the general manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders, etc. The behaviors or things that are tabooed are actually violations of the provisions, recommendations or suggestions in the relevant elements requirements, verification methods, rules, procedures or guidelines contained in the relevant standards of hydraulic cylinders.
In Appendix A of GB/T 3766-2015, as long as they are suitable and may cause serious hazards, they are all taboos for the design, manufacturing, installation and maintenance of hydraulic cylinders.
3.9.1 Taboos for Design and Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders

Since the hydraulic cylinder is a hydraulic actuator that provides linear motion, it is the simplest and most convenient to directly use the hydraulic cylinder to achieve reciprocating linear motion of the machine.

The selection of the type of hydraulic cylinder is one of the prerequisite conditions for the design calculation of the hydraulic cylinder. First, it should be determined whether to use a double-acting piston cylinder, a single-acting piston cylinder, a plunger cylinder, a single or double-acting telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder, or other types of hydraulic cylinders.

There are many factors to consider in the design and selection of hydraulic cylinders. For example, if the reciprocating motion speed needs to be the same, it is easier to use a double (output) rod cylinder; if the return speed of the cylinder needs to be greater than the moving speed of the cylinder, it is more appropriate to use a single piston rod piston cylinder; if only one-way drive of the external load is required, and the return trip can be reliably achieved by external force, a plunger cylinder can be selected; if it is necessary to drive the load to rotate, a swing hydraulic cylinder (combined hydraulic cylinder) can also be selected, etc.

Taking the design and selection of the plunger cylinder as an example, because the plunger cylinder usually only has one oil port, it can only drive the resistance load and cannot return by liquid pressure. That is, the plunger cylinder can only be used in occasions where there is external force (such as gravity, overload or a return cylinder) during the return trip, otherwise it cannot return. In addition, the plunger cylinder is not suitable for horizontal placement. Since it can only bear pressure, considering the stiffness, the diameter of the piston rod is relatively large, and its radial support point is also different from that of the piston cylinder, resulting in a relatively large volume and support of the plunger cylinder. If installed horizontally, the piston rod is prone to press on one side, causing unilateral wear of the guide sleeve and seal ring. If it is necessary to install it horizontally, a plunger bracket needs to be installed to prevent the plunger from sagging, causing bending and increasing initial deflection to cause jamming.

The selection of hydraulic cylinders should first be selected from standard hydraulic cylinders. There are now standard hydraulic cylinders, including hydraulic cylinders for metallurgical equipment, dump (low-speed) truck hydraulic cylinders, marine (reciprocating) hydraulic cylinders, marine hatch cover hydraulic cylinders, marine digital hydraulic cylinders, servo hydraulic cylinders (as specified in local standards), double-acting agricultural hydraulic cylinders, tractor steering hydraulic cylinders, large hydraulic cylinders, hydraulic cylinders for mining machinery, hydraulic support columns and jacks for coal mines, etc.

For products within the scope of product standards, it is taboo to design and use non-standard hydraulic cylinders; for products without product standards, it is also taboo to design and use them in violation of JB/T 10205-2010.

It is inappropriate for some literature to recommend the use of double piston rod cylinders for occasions requiring the same reciprocating motion speed. In addition, if a symmetrical electro-hydraulic servo valve is used to control an asymmetric servo hydraulic cylinder (differential cylinder), the servo hydraulic cylinder can only withstand pressure and cannot withstand tension, and phenomena such as pressure out of control, cavitation and pressure shock may occur.

Not only are there no current product standards for the HSG type engineering hydraulic cylinders designed by the joint design group of engineering machinery hydraulic cylinders in the various editions of the (Modern) Machinery Handbook, but HSG type engineering hydraulic cylinders are generally not the hydraulic cylinders used on some engineering machinery.

Due to the different working conditions of engineering machinery compared to stationary machinery, the requirements for hydraulic cylinders also differ. Ordinary hydraulic cylinders generally cannot meet the requirements for small mass, limited installation space, generally large impact forces, and high safety and reliability of hydraulic cylinders used on engineering machinery, and therefore should not be used.
3.9.2 Taboos in Hydraulic Cylinder Parameter Design

The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders in various hydraulic cylinder standards are not completely identical. In JB/T 10205—2010, it is stipulated that: "The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders should include the cylinder bore, piston rod diameter (outer), nominal pressure, stroke, and installation dimensions."

In addition to the basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders specified in the above standards, there are also those in other hydraulic cylinder and related standards that list the thrust and pull force at nominal pressure, piston speed, rated pressure, minimum piston rod diameter (outer), plunger diameter for plunger-type hydraulic cylinders, limit or maximum stroke, area ratio of two chambers, threaded ports and nominal bore of ports, piston rod thread type and size, mass, installation type, and connection dimensions as basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders.

In JB/T 2184—2007, the main parameters of hydraulic cylinders are specified as: Cylinder bore × Stroke, with the unit being mm. Since the nominal pressure or rated pressure of a hydraulic cylinder generally depends on the hydraulic system of the host machine, it is taboo for the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to be higher than the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic system and hydraulic pump of the host machine; if it is necessary to use the hydraulic system of the host machine to perform pressure resistance testing on the hydraulic cylinder, the pressure should not exceed the maximum allowable pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.
The nominal pressure or rated pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should be less than 2/3 of the nominal pressure or rated pressure of the host hydraulic system and hydraulic pump during testing.

The basic parameters, structural form, dimensions, and tolerances of the hydraulic cylinder components should comply with relevant standards, such as the nominal pressure should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2346, the inner diameter of the cylinder and the diameter of the piston rod should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2348, the thread size of the oil port connection should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2878.1, and the sealing groove should comply with the provisions of GB/T 2879, GB/T 3452.1, GB 6577, GB/T 6578, 15242.3 and other standards, and taboo to adopt non-standard structural forms or dimensions.

If the hydraulic cylinder is not designed according to relevant standards, it may cause problems with matching the hydraulic pump, and it may also make it difficult to select seals and accessories for the hydraulic cylinder. The dimensions such as the cylinder diameter and piston rod diameter calculated according to the load and nominal (rated) pressure must be rounded to the values specified in the standard, otherwise it may be impossible to select suitable seals. When determining the wall thickness of the cylinder, taboo to ignore the additional dimensions that should be added to the cylinder due to structural elements such as thread processing, grooves, and oil port settings, as well as processability requirements, so as not to cause the actual dimensions to be reduced or stress concentration, resulting in a decrease in the pressure bearing capacity, strength, and stiffness of the hydraulic cylinder.

Taboo to have too small a safety factor for the hydraulic cylinder. In order to ensure sufficient load-bearing capacity of the hydraulic cylinder and consider the influence of factors such as the uniformity of the material and stress concentration, the hydraulic cylinder must have sufficient safety factor, which should generally be above 5. At the same time, under the condition of meeting the force and stroke requirements of the driving load, taboo to have an excessively large external contour size of the hydraulic cylinder.
3.9.3 Taboos for Metal Material Selection and Structural Design of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Taboos for Metal Material Selection of Cylinder Components

The reference [99] points out: "When there is severe impact during work, the cylinder and end cover of the hydraulic cylinder cannot use brittle materials such as cast iron." However, it should also be noted that the reference [115] points out: "Low and medium carbon carbon steel and alloy steel have high multiple impact strength after quenching and low and medium temperature tempering. The comprehensive mechanical properties of quenching + high temperature tempering (i.e. quenching and tempering) are the best, although it can withstand a high strength of a single impact, but the strength of small energy multiple impacts is very low."

When the cylinder needs to be welded with the cylinder bottom, cylinder head, pipe joint (connecting pipe), or clevis, etc., 35 steel with good weldability should be used, and quenched and tempered after rough machining.

For the cylinder (tube) material of a hydraulic cylinder that works in an environment with a temperature lower than -50°C, 35 steel, 45 steel, or low-temperature steel that has been quenched and tempered must be selected. The piston rod that works under corrosive conditions should be made of stainless steel as much as possible.
2. Taboo to use a tie-rod structure for hydraulic cylinders under long stroke, large cylinder diameter, and high pressure

Considering the strength and stiffness of the threaded connection, in order to reduce the tensile force and stress amplitude on the bolt, the stiffness of the bolt can be reduced or the stiffness of the connected parts can be increased. A measure to reduce the stiffness of the bolt is given in reference [54], as shown in Figure 3-14.

In reference [110], it is pointed out: "Although the tie-rod hydraulic cylinder has the characteristics of good processability and maintainability, when the length of the hydraulic cylinder is 1500-2000mm, due to the action of hydraulic force, it is easy to cause the tie-rod to elongate and deform, resulting in leakage. The troubleshooting method: Avoid using a tie-rod structure for long hydraulic cylinders and choose a flange connection instead."

sections.text: 3. Taboo to have poor stability of the piston rod

Reference [110] lists a case where the hydraulic cylinder is improperly designed, resulting in poor stability of the piston rod. The cause of the failure: The length of the piston rod guide sleeve is too small, resulting in poor guiding ability. The troubleshooting method: The length L of the guide sleeve generally varies depending on the size of the hydraulic cylinder, the type of piston rod seal, and the purpose, but it should generally be more than 3/5 of the piston rod diameter to ensure that the piston rod has sufficient stability.

Reference [99] points out: "When using a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder, it is necessary to comprehensively consider selecting a piston rod with sufficient stiffness and installing an intermediate spacer ring."
This manual requires that under normal circumstances, taboo to have a guide sleeve guiding length or supporting length B < 0.7d (d is the piston rod diameter).
4. Other taboos in the structural design of hydraulic cylinders

items: Reference [110] points out: "The end cover of the hydraulic cylinder should not be too thin. The end cover of the hydraulic cylinder bears a large liquid pressure. If the end cover is too thin, gaps are likely to occur, leading to leakage; if the bolt spacing is too large and the bolt preload torque is different, gaps are also likely to occur locally under the action of hydraulic force, thereby leading to leakage."
If a vent (discharge) valve is installed on the hydraulic cylinder, taboo to not be in the highest position and not easily accessible during installation.
If it can be foreseen that the piston rod may be crushed, scratched, and corroded, taboo to not install a protective cover.
Taboo to not design or configure a vent (discharge) port for a hydraulic cylinder with an air cavity; taboo that venting through this vent (discharge) port may cause danger.

Taboo to not have an anti-loosening design for the adjustable stroke terminal stop installed inside or outside the hydraulic cylinder; taboo to install a safety valve on the hydraulic cylinder or hydraulic system that cannot automatically reset.

sections.text: 3.9.4 Design Taboos for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Devices
1. Design Taboos for Sealing Grooves
Do not use sealing grooves specified outside the declared compliant hydraulic cylinder product standards or JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" for hydraulic cylinder product design.
Generally, sealing grooves listed in Table 3-71 should not be selected for hydraulic cylinder product design.

However, considering current standards, since the sealing grooves provided in JB/T 10205—2010 cannot meet the requirements of most hydraulic cylinder seals and their design, if sealing grooves outside these product standards are used, the hydraulic cylinder cannot declare compliance with any product standard, including JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", and the designed hydraulic cylinder product will be a non-standard product.

In summary, to avoid designing and manufacturing non-standard products, referring to the provisions on seal and groove selection in GB/T 13342—2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinders", the design taboos for sealing grooves should be further stated as follows: priority should be given to using seals and grooves specified in national standards for hydraulic cylinder product design; non-standard seals and grooves, i.e., those without current international, Chinese, or foreign standards, should not be used for hydraulic cylinder product design.

Hydraulic cylinders designed with non-standard sealing grooves are most likely to fail to find matching seals. Using seals specified outside standard regulations may result in unguaranteed sealing performance; designing and manufacturing seals independently may also have problems with sealing performance including reliability and durability regardless of cost; self-made seals cannot be stored for extended periods, and urgent maintenance and replacement of seals may face situations where no seals are available for replacement.

Various types of standard grooves are composed of various geometric elements, such as dimensional and tolerance elements, geometric tolerance elements, and surface structure elements, etc. Grooves that meet these groove composition elements and are within the applicable range of the groove are standard grooves. Excessive requirements for various elements may also lead to non-standard groove design, such as unrealistically reducing dimensional tolerances to 1/5 or 1/10 of the original tolerance, etc.
Non-standard sealing grooves do not refer to modifications to sealing grooves made to adjust seal compression, adapt to seal material swelling values, and install thicker retaining rings, etc.
2. Taboos for Seal Material Selection
Sealing elements or devices incompatible with the working medium should not be selected for hydraulic cylinders.
Common working media for general hydraulic cylinders are shown in Table 3-72.

sections.text: Special attention should be paid to the fact that hydraulic cylinders using phosphate ester flame retardant oil and phosphate ester hydraulic oil (fluid) as the working medium should not use sealing rings made of neoprene rubber, nitrile rubber and other sealing materials. In DL/T571—2014 "Guidelines for Operation and Maintenance of Phosphate Ester Flame Retardant Oil in Power Plants", it is recommended to use sealing rings made of silicone rubber, (ternary) EPDM rubber, fluorine rubber and other sealing materials.

In addition, polyurethane material dustproof sealing rings should not be selected in environments prone to mold growth. Because certain types of polyurethane (such as polyester and certain polyethers) are non-mold-resistant materials.
3. Taboos in Selection of Structural Types of Sealing Components (Rings)

At present, most hydraulic cylinder sealing systems contain polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings. However, with the progress of hydraulic cylinder sealing technology and the improvement of customers' requirements for product quality, their limitations (or defects) have also become increasingly prominent.
From the perspective of material properties, compared with NBR, it has the following limitations:

items: Large permanent deformation under compression. At high temperatures, the permanent deformation under compression of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings is 1-2 times that of NBR rubber sealing rings.

Severe hydrolysis at high temperatures. During the use of hydraulic oil, it is generally inevitable that it is contaminated by water (such as moisture, humidity invasion). The increase of water content and the rise of oil temperature will make the hydrolysis effect on general polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings more serious, and this hydrolysis is irreversible and fatal damage. However, polyurethane materials resistant to hydrolysis have poor elasticity and are rarely used to make Y-rings or U-rings.

Large leakage under low pressure or high-speed conditions. Now, when selecting polyurethane materials to make Y-rings or U-rings, there are generally: (1) Polyurethane materials resistant to high temperatures are often not resistant to low temperatures. (2) If the material hardness is selected to be high, the sealing ring has poor elasticity; if the material hardness is selected to be low, the sealing ring is severely squeezed out. (3) Polyurethane materials with high elasticity have poor high-temperature resistance. (4) Polyurethane materials resistant to hydrolysis have problems with elasticity and low-temperature resistance.

sections.text: Therefore, manufacturers of sealing components are often in a dilemma of being unable to take care of both sides.
From the perspective of structural type, it has the following defects:

items: Compared with NBR rubber, it has poor conformity and low-temperature follow-up.
The large contact area leads to large friction force.
It is prone to crawling and abnormal noise problems.
Air is easily trapped in the groove at the end of the lip, which may lead to burning of the sealing lip.
Insufficient material hardness may lead to extrusion of the base of the sealing ring.
When two lip-shaped sealing rings are installed back-to-back, the back pressure generated may damage the lip of the sealing ring.
Large-section sealing rings have large friction force, are difficult to install, and have high cost.
Small-section sealing rings are prone to flipping and have poor pressure resistance.

sections.text: Due to the above limitations (defects) of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings, the problems of hydraulic cylinder sealing systems nowadays are mostly concentrated on them. Therefore, the following taboos (not suitable) are proposed:

items: Hydraulic cylinder sealing systems should not prioritize the selection of polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings.
Polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings should not be selected in high-temperature or humid-heat environments.
Polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings should not be selected under low-pressure or high-speed conditions.
Hydraulic cylinders with low-friction (or dynamic characteristic) requirements should not select polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings.
When two lip-shaped sealing rings are installed back-to-back, polyurethane Y-rings or U-rings without pressure relief grooves should not be selected.

sections.text: The above main viewpoints have been proved by a large number of comparative bench tests on hydraulic cylinder sealing performance conducted by Suzhou Meifurui New Material Technology Co., Ltd.
4. Taboos in Determining Sealing Conditions

Hydraulic cylinder sealing devices or systems whose environmental temperature, working medium temperature, reciprocating motion speed, sealing gap, working pressure range, and working temperature range do not meet the requirements of the standards should not be selected or designed.

Generally speaking, reciprocating motion speed, sealing gap, working pressure range, and working temperature range are performance parameters of hydraulic cylinder sealing components (rings), devices or systems, and all should contain a range expressed by high (large) or low (small), or the highest (large) or lowest (small) (value). The lowest environmental temperature or the lowest value of the environmental temperature should be equal to the lowest working medium temperature or the lowest value of the working medium temperature. In various current standards, the highest values of the temperature of the hydraulic oil input to the hydraulic system or hydraulic cylinder are not the same. Now, some excerpts are listed in Table 3-73 to avoid violating the taboos of the design of hydraulic cylinder sealing devices (systems).
