It should be particularly noted that the use conditions of general seals should include the applicable seal clearance size and changes; the use conditions of each seal component (device) selected in a specific seal system should be consistent with the seal clearance.
5. Taboos in Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Design Based on Sealing Performance
1) Hydraulic cylinder seal devices or systems that may cause external leakage when the hydraulic cylinder is stationary should not be selected or designed.

Generally, seals (seal devices) for reciprocating motion that are not specified by standards or have not been verified should not be used for static sealing of hydraulic cylinders. In practice, the author has not only seen seals (rings) specified in JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" used for static sealing, but also seen rotary (shaft) seals used for static sealing.

It should be particularly noted that lip packings (various forms such as V-shaped, U-shaped, L-shaped, Y-shaped, etc.) specified in JB/T 6612—2008 "Terms for Static Seals and Packing Seals" are mostly not suitable for static sealing of hydraulic cylinders. This is not only because the standard's scope of application does not explicitly include hydraulic cylinder seals, but also because the seal types and sealing mechanisms specified in the standard are more suitable for complex reciprocating motion seals rather than static seals.
2) Hydraulic cylinder seal devices or systems whose internal leakage does not meet the standard requirements should not be selected or designed.

In the JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" standard, the internal leakage difference between "double-acting" hydraulic cylinders and "single-acting" hydraulic cylinders is more than 1 times. If the "single-acting hydraulic cylinder internal leakage" is the same, then the double-acting hydraulic cylinder sealing system should be "no excess design".

3) Hydraulic cylinder seal devices or systems whose external leakage does not meet the standard requirements under the specified pressure level or pressure direction changes should not be selected or designed.

The corrosion resistance of hydraulic cylinder seals determines to a certain degree the durability of the hydraulic cylinder. In cases of insufficient corrosion resistance, long-life (pre-service life) sealing elements, sealing devices or systems should be selected and designed to avoid misalignment and combination of sealing elements (sealing devices), so that the sealing system has a long service life.
4) Hydraulic cylinder seals that cannot provide support and guidance should not be selected or designed.
Reciprocating seals or sealing elements should have support and guidance functions. Seals without support and guidance cannot be expected to have good, stable, long-life sealing performance.

General sealing elements used to seal hydraulic cylinders without support and guidance, with single reciprocating sealing surfaces, mostly have contact between the reciprocating sealing surface and the cylinder surface during operation.
Also, asymmetric sealing elements should not be designed to be fixed in systems with support and guidance.
5) Hydraulic cylinder seals without dust prevention sealing should not be selected or designed.

Hydraulic cylinders without dust prevention sealing should not be designed, nor should dust prevention sealing rings unsuitable for the specified working pressure be selected or designed. Similarly, hydraulic cylinders without covers (caps) to prevent dust at each outlet should not be designed, and furthermore, reciprocating seals with protective covers but without sealing should not be designed.
Hydraulic cylinder seals without dust prevention rings are not quality-safe designs.
When the cylinder returns to the extreme position, having the reciprocating sealing element installation surface (circular surface) enter the dust sealing ring is also a dust sealing design taboo.

6) Hydraulic cylinder seal systems whose external leakage and internal leakage after low temperature, corrosion resistance, continuous impact, high temperature and other tests do not meet the standard requirements should not be selected or designed.

Hydraulic cylinder factory test items are divided into inspection items and sampling items. Among the test items, low temperature, corrosion resistance, continuous impact, high temperature and other tests are generally sampling items. Generally, hydraulic cylinders that have external leakage or internal leakage exceeding the standard after one sampling test item should have their sealing elements (rings) inspected and replaced for each batch, and hydraulic cylinders that undergo one sampling test item for each batch should have their sealing elements (rings) inspected and replaced.
Hydraulic cylinder leakage inspection is based on the test conditions in the test, and the sealing element (system) design should also be based on these sealing element performance requirements.
Note: In JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" standard, "grade test" is defined as a sampling item.
6. Taboos in Hydraulic Cylinder Seal Design Based on Wear-Resistant Damping Force
Hydraulic cylinders generate wear-resistant damping force during reciprocating motion, and due to the support environment for each

Frictional resistance caused by the friction between the dynamic sealing device and the mating parts (couplings), and even the metal friction between the piston rod and the guide bushing (cylinder head), and between the piston and the cylinder barrel, results in reduced output force efficiency of the cylinder, increased temperature of the hydraulic oil, and wear of cylinder components. Except for using metal (such as tin bronze) as guide rings or support rings, metal friction between other cylinder components should be avoided as much as possible during the reciprocating motion of the hydraulic cylinder.

items: Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements. A suitable sealing device or system should be selected or designed, especially for hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders. Although the standard stipulates the use of V-ring seals on hydraulic cylinders for lifting purposes, when selecting or designing a sealing device or system containing V-ring seals, the (minimum) starting pressure should be estimated to see if it exceeds the standard. Excessive "redundant design" of the sealing system should be avoided, including excessive support and guidance.

Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes insufficient guidance and support for the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder. When driving the load with the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder extended, especially when the piston rod of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is near the limit extension, the piston rod may bend or become unstable. If the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, the possibility of the piston rod bending or becoming unstable is greater. The load driven by the hydraulic cylinder may have lateral component forces. In this case, if the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, severe wear of the cylinder components may occur. If the support length or guidance length of the piston and piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder is insufficient, it may also cause an increase in the eccentricity of the hydraulic cylinder, resulting in local wear of the cylinder components. All these situations may increase the friction force of the hydraulic cylinder when carrying a load to varying degrees.
Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the output force efficiency (load efficiency) of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements.

sections.text: The friction force when carrying a load directly reduces the output force efficiency of the cylinder. According to the definition and calculation formula of the output force efficiency of the cylinder, if the tested hydraulic cylinder maintains a uniform motion state at different pressures to detect the output force efficiency of the cylinder, then the formula pA=W+F₂+F₃ must be true, where pA is the theoretical output force of the cylinder, W is the actual output force of the cylinder, F₂ is the friction resistance generated by friction, and F₃ is the resistance generated by back pressure.

According to the provisions of JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", the output force efficiency of the cylinder should be η=W/(pA)×100%≥90%. If the back pressure is limited or ignored, the friction resistance generated by friction will be limited.
7. Taboos for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Design Based on Hydraulic Cylinder Operating Performance

items: Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes vibration, sticking, or crawling of the hydraulic cylinder. There are many factors that cause the hydraulic cylinder to vibrate, stick, or crawl. Even hydraulic cylinders that pass factory tests and inspections may exhibit these conditions during use. However, the probability of the sealing system's "redundant design" and the design of sealing rings, support rings, or retaining rings with excessive interference fit may be very high.
In a reciprocating motion sealing system, do not select or design a sealing device or system with a large difference between the static and dynamic friction coefficients.

sections.text: If the static and dynamic friction coefficients of the sealing device or system in the hydraulic cylinder differ too much, it may cause the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder to exceed the standard, crawling, or sudden jumping (instantaneous jumping) of the hydraulic cylinder when starting. The possible reasons for this are:

items: Inappropriate selection of sealing materials, including support ring and guide ring materials.
Problems with the sealing material during use, such as deformation of polyamide when exposed to water.
The working environment temperature of the hydraulic cylinder exceeds the allowable use temperature of the sealing components.
Unreasonable design or installation of the sealing system, resulting in dry friction.
Unreasonable selection of sealing components, including support rings, or quality problems with the components themselves.
Unreasonable design of the sealing groove.
Inappropriate selection of surface roughness of mating parts or lack of demagnetization.
Inconsistent surface roughness or surface hardness of mating parts.

Other reasons such as unreasonable structural design of the hydraulic cylinder, unreasonable design or adjustment of the cushioning device, bending or instability of the piston rod, air in the working medium, or piston seal leakage.
Do not select or design a hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system that causes the dynamic characteristics of the hydraulic cylinder to not meet the standard requirements.

sections.text: One of the technical requirements for assembly quality in the JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard is that "after assembly, the hydraulic cylinder should be guaranteed to move freely." Digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders have further requirements for dynamic characteristics (dynamic indicators), such as step response and frequency response for servo hydraulic cylinders. Taking DB44/T 1169.1 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 1: Technical Conditions" as an example, the required "minimum starting pressure" value is so small that it cannot be achieved by merely improving the assembly quality level. Instead, the selected or designed hydraulic cylinder sealing device or system should first have performance that meets the relevant standard requirements.
3.9.5  Taboos for Hydraulic Cylinder Cushioning Device Design
The cushioning of a cylinder with a cushioning device is a means of deceleration when the moving parts are approaching the end of their motion. There are mainly two types: fixed and adjustable.
There are several taboos in the design of fixed hydraulic cushioning devices:

items: Taboo for excessive cushioning length. The cushioning device should be able to absorb the maximum kinetic energy with a shorter cushioning length (also known as cushioning stroke) of the cylinder.

sections.text: The goal is to completely convert the kinetic energy of the moving parts (including all connecting parts or related parts) into heat energy.

items: During the buffering process, it is forbidden to have excessively high pressure pulses or excessively high peak pressure in the buffering chamber. The change in pressure should be a gradual process.
It is forbidden for the peak buffering pressure in the buffering chamber (at the cylinder head end) to exceed 1.5 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder.
For hydraulic cylinders with buffering devices installed at the rod end, it is forbidden for the (excessively high) buffering pressure to act on the piston rod dynamic sealing system.

It is forbidden for the oil temperature to be too high. The conversion of kinetic energy into heat energy causes the temperature of the hydraulic oil to rise, and the maximum temperature of the oil should not exceed the maximum allowable operating temperature of the sealing elements.

It is forbidden to install unnecessary buffering devices. According to JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", "For hydraulic cylinders that require buffering performance, it shall be determined through consultation between the user and the manufacturer." For hydraulic cylinders that do not require buffering devices, do not add them unnecessarily; for cases where the buffering device of the hydraulic cylinder alone cannot convert all kinetic energy, other deceleration and braking measures should be taken, such as designing braking circuits in the hydraulic system.

It is forbidden for the designed buffering device to affect the starting performance of the hydraulic cylinder. The starting performance of the hydraulic cylinder should be considered, and the (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the requirements of relevant standards; abnormal situations such as delayed movement or surging (abnormal movement) and abnormal noise should be avoided when the piston starts or leaves the buffering area.

It is forbidden for the nominal flow rate of the check valve in the buffering valve buffering device to be too small. If the designed check valve has too small a nominal flow rate, it may cause the hydraulic cylinder to suddenly stop or retreat when starting.

sections.text: A case is listed in reference [110]: When the hydraulic cylinder moves at a high speed, it is prone to produce great impact and noise when suddenly stopping at the end of the stroke, causing damage to the hydraulic cylinder, and even damaging various valves, pipes and related mechanical parts. The cause of the fault: As shown in Figure 3-15a, due to the large mass of the load, hydraulic cylinder piston and piston rod itself, the momentum of the movement is very large, so when it suddenly stops at the end of the stroke, it is prone to produce great impact and noise, causing damage to the hydraulic system. The troubleshooting method: In order to eliminate this impact, corresponding components can be installed in the hydraulic circuit to control the speed of the hydraulic cylinder. A buffering device should be installed for the fast-acting hydraulic cylinder, such as a fixed or adjustable hydraulic cylinder buffering device, as shown in Figure 3-15b.

The current problem is that if the speed of the hydraulic cylinder during the entire stroke can be reduced, it can fundamentally solve the impact and noise problems when the hydraulic cylinder reaches the end of its stroke, and the hydraulic cylinder itself may not need to be equipped with a buffering device. However, the example in reference [110] is neither the buffering device design of the hydraulic cylinder itself nor the buffering design of the hydraulic system where the hydraulic cylinder is located.

sections.description: Two diagrams labeled a) and b) showing hydraulic cylinder configurations. Diagram a) shows a basic hydraulic cylinder setup. Diagram b) shows an improved configuration with additional cushioning components.

sections.text: Figure 3-16 shows an example of a throttling valve buffering circuit given in the book "Analysis and Design of Hydraulic Circuits" by the author, for readers' reference.

sections.caption: Figure 3-16  Throttling valve buffering circuit
sections.description: A hydraulic circuit diagram showing a throttle valve cushioning system with numbered components: 1—Hydraulic source, 2—Three-position four-way solenoid directional valve, 3, 9—Two-position two-way solenoid directional valve, 4, 5, 7, 8—One-way throttle valve, 6—Hydraulic cylinder.

sections.text: In Figure 3-16, when the three-position four-way solenoid directional valve 2 is in the left position, the hydraulic oil supplied by the hydraulic source 1 flows through the three-position four-way solenoid directional valve 2, the two-position two-way solenoid directional valve 3, the check valve in the one-way throttle valve 4, and the check valve in the one-way throttle valve 5 into the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder 6. The hydraulic oil in the rod cavity of the hydraulic cylinder 6 flows back to the oil tank through the throttle valve in the one-way throttle valve 8, the two-position two-way solenoid directional valve 9, the throttle valve in the one-way throttle valve 7, and the three-position four-way solenoid directional valve 2, and the hydraulic cylinder performs high-speed cylinder movement; when the cylinder movement reaches a certain position, the travel switch (not shown in the figure) sends a signal, the solenoid of the two-position two-way solenoid directional valve 9 is energized and changes direction, disconnecting the oil circuit where the one-way throttle valve 8 is located. At this time, only the throttle valve in the one-way throttle valve 7 works, the return oil of the hydraulic cylinder is reduced, that is, the hydraulic cylinder realizes secondary deceleration, and the hydraulic cylinder performs low-speed cylinder movement.

Similarly, the return stroke of the cylinder can also achieve deceleration. Since the throttling (deceleration) setting is on the hydraulic return line, there are no problems such as cavitation in the intake line, so the specifications of the one-way throttle valves 5 and 7 can be smaller, that is, the speed of the hydraulic cylinder can be reduced to a very low level, achieving the purpose of buffering.

In reference [99], the principles for selecting buffering mechanisms are given as: It is generally believed that for ordinary hydraulic cylinders, when the working pressure is greater than 10 MPa and the piston speed is greater than 0.1 m/s, a buffering device or other buffering methods should be used. This is only a reference condition, mainly depending on the specific situation.
3.9.5 Selection of Cushioning Mechanisms

The selection of cushioning mechanisms should be comprehensively considered based on the working requirements of the hydraulic cylinder, cushioning type, cushioning form, cushioning method, cushioning performance, cushioning mechanism type, and the purpose of the hydraulic cylinder. For example, for hydraulic cylinders that require slow speed changes, when the piston speed is 0.05-0.12 m/s, a cushioning device should also be used.
For external braking mechanisms, when vm ≥ 1 m/s, the internal cushioning mechanism cannot absorb all the kinetic energy, and an external braking mechanism must be installed, as described below:

items: Install an external travel switch. When entering the cushioning stage, the switch cuts off the oil supply, making the hydraulic energy equal to zero, but it can still form pressure pulses.
Install a damper between the piston rod and the load.
Install a hydraulically controlled throttle valve at the hydraulic cylinder outlet.

sections.text: In addition, the type of cushioning mechanism can be determined according to the requirements of the working process for piston linear speed changes, as described below:

items: For deceleration transition processes that require very smooth operation, such as sand molding operations, fragile item pallet operations, precision grinding feed, etc., it is advisable to select approximately constant deceleration type cushioning mechanisms, such as multi-hole cylinder type or multi-hole plunger type as well as automatic throttling type.
For deceleration mechanisms that allow slight pulses, such as ordinary machine tools, rough rolling mills, etc., milled groove type or stepped type cushioning mechanisms can be used.
For deceleration mechanisms that can withstand certain pulses, conical type or double conical type, or even cylindrical plunger cushioning mechanisms can be used.

sections.text: 3.9.6 Configuration Selection and Oil Circuit Design Taboos for Throttle Valves on Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Configuration Selection Taboos

items: Prohibit the use of connection threads other than M, G, R and NPT, and ordinary fine pitch (M) threads should be preferred.
Prohibit the selection of pipe fitting types that cannot meet the working pressure or nominal pressure of the hydraulic system, or that do not have corresponding specifications or products.

Prohibit pipe fittings and connected pipes whose maximum working pressure or nominal pressure exceeds the specified pressure and temperature requirements. Pipe fittings are only safe to use within the specified pressure and temperature range. The connected pipe wall thickness should be sufficient. For special applications such as hydraulic systems on ships, connecting pipes (seamless carbon steel pipes) should consider corrosion allowance.
Prohibit pipe fittings and connected pipes whose flow capacity is lower than the hydraulic system requirements.

Prohibit pipe bending radius and deviation, pipe bending roundness tolerance and corrugation depth from exceeding the provisions of JB/T 5000.3. The wall thickness reduction rate of cold bent pipes must not exceed 15%.

Prohibit piping cleanliness from exceeding standards. Except for galvanized steel pipes, all carbon steel pipes (including prefabricated formed pipelines) must undergo acid washing, neutralization, cleaning, blow drying and rust prevention treatment.

Prohibit leakage. All welded parts of prefabricated pipes must undergo pressure testing at 1.5 times the working pressure, maintaining pressure for 10 min with no leakage or other abnormal phenomena; for assembled pipelines, conduct pressure testing according to hydraulic system (pipe) technical requirements.

Prohibit the use of pipe fitting connections for hard pipe assemblies in larger diameters or some special applications. Generally, flange connections should be used for hard pipe assemblies when the nominal diameter ≥40 mm; for piping in some special applications such as severe vibration, swaying and impact situations, flange connections can be used when the nominal diameter ≥25 mm.

Prohibit the application of flexible hose assemblies in some special situations. For some special applications or equipment with technical requirements or safety technical standard provisions, flexible hose assemblies cannot be used.

sections.text: 2. Oil Circuit Block Design Taboos

Oil circuit blocks can be used for installing cartridge valves, stack valves and plate valves, and according to hydraulic circuit diagrams, connect valve ports through oil passages to form cubic base plates, belonging to piping. In various standards and reference documents, oil circuit blocks are also called integrated blocks, oil circuit plates, mounting plates, bases, bottom plates, bottom plate blocks, foundation plates or valve blocks.
Oil circuit block design should follow certain principles. Based on relevant standards and practical experience summary, the following oil circuit block design taboos are listed for reader reference.

items: (1) Oil circuit block material selection taboos. Be very careful when selecting cast iron to manufacture medium, high pressure and larger sized oil circuit blocks. First, larger sized cubic castings cannot be cast qualified by any foundry; second, once problems occur during machining, repair is difficult. Usually Q235, Q345, 20, 35 or 45 carbon steel plates or forgings can be selected to manufacture oil circuit blocks. When using steel plates to manufacture oil circuit blocks, attention should be paid to the different mechanical properties in each direction and possible quality defects. For marine two-way cartridge valve oil circuit blocks, medium carbon steel forgings are recommended, and the blanks should eliminate internal stress and undergo non-destructive testing. Oil circuit blocks used for pipe fitting testing are specified to have no plating, and hardness values should be 35-45 HRC as specified in GB/T 230.1. Prohibit using cast iron to manufacture medium, high pressure or medium, large sized oil circuit blocks as well as those used in vibrating applications.

(2) Oil circuit block type determination taboos. Oil circuit blocks can be designed as square or rectangular hexahedrons. Generally, designing oil circuit blocks with flanges on four sides should be prohibited. Oil circuit block dimensions should not be too large, otherwise manufacturing is difficult; generally the three determined reference surfaces should be mutually perpendicular, and design datum, process datum and measurement datum should coincide, with the three reference surfaces leaving about 0.3 mm for precision grinding. Prohibit hydraulic valve mounting surfaces from extending beyond the oil circuit block.

sections.text: In complex hydraulic systems with many hydraulic valves, multiple oil circuit blocks can be stacked. The upper and lower surfaces of stacked oil circuit blocks generally should have common P oil passages, common T oil passages and L oil passages, as well as at least four screw (through) holes for connection (the bottom layer
Threaded holes, generally the topmost one is a counterbore for cylindrical head screws.
The dimensional tolerance of the manifold's external shape should generally not exceed the requirements for JS grade in GB/T 1804.
The external oil ports of the manifold should be uniformly arranged on one surface; manifolds weighing more than 15 kg should have lifting facilities.

Under the pressure test pressure (or rated pressure) of the manifold and within the specified time, after 1 hour of immersion in 90°C hydraulic oil, no deformation should occur that would cause hydraulic valve malfunction (or stated as "should not cause malfunction due to deformation").
Note that the edges of the hexahedron should be chamfered at 2×45° or 1.5×45°, and the surface can be treated with bluing or chemical nickel plating.
Reference materials suggest that the maximum edge length of the manifold should not exceed 600 mm, otherwise it would be considered too large.

Generally, the precision grinding allowance for a plane should be around 0.2 mm, but since the manifold surface may be scratched during processing, the grinding allowance should be increased for safety.
(3) Taboos in dimension marking for manifolds

The dimension marking for a certain surface of the manifold can be marked in the form of dimensions starting from the same reference, or it can be listed in coordinate form. This common reference is generally selected as the lower-left corner of the main view of the manifold as the coordinate origin.
The dimensions of the hydraulic valve mounting surface can be marked as reference dimensions at the same time according to its marking method.
Taboo dimension markings that are not conducive to inspection and verification.
(4) Taboos in the design of flow channel cross-sectional area and minimum spacing for manifolds

Reference literature suggests that for medium and low-pressure hydraulic systems, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should not be less than 5 mm, and for high-pressure hydraulic systems, it should be larger. Other reference literature suggests determining the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold based on the flow channel diameter, i.e., when the diameter is less than or equal to φ2.5 mm, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should not be less than 5 mm; when the diameter is greater than φ2.5 mm, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) in the manifold should generally not be less than 10 mm.

For steel manifolds without product standard specifications, the minimum spacing between flow channels (oil passages) (actual) can refer to the wall thickness of corresponding nominal pressure hard pipes (steel pipes), but generally should not be less than 5 mm in design.

The cross-sectional area of the manifold flow channel should be at least equal to the flow area of the relevant components. The recommended pipe flow rate for the nominal diameter of the pressure oil passage can refer to the design of the flow rate limit for oil in system metal piping, such as the recommended oil flow rate values for system metal piping in Table 4-151.
For a flow channel hole drilled from both ends (counter-drilling), the maximum deviation at the joint point should not exceed 0.4 mm.
Taboos include designing the cross-sectional area of flow channels and the spacing between oil passages in the manifold too small.
(5) Taboos in plugging holes in manifolds

Generally, there may be process holes on the manifold, and plugging holes means blocking these process holes according to process requirements. There are three common methods for plugging holes on steel manifolds: welding, ball expansion, and screw plugs.

When using the welding method to plug holes, a cylindrical plug should generally be pre-installed inside the hole, made of low-carbon steel, about 5 mm in length, and tightly fitted with the hole; a welding (seam) thickness of more than 5 mm should be left, and sealed welding should be performed according to the plug welding process, but there should be a certain weld bead height (excess height).

The author disagrees with the suggestion in some reference literature that process holes with a diameter of φ5 mm and below can be directly welded and plugged without pre-installing a cylindrical plug; also disagrees with using steel balls as pre-installed plugs for welding.

When using hydraulic pneumatic ball expansion plugs to plug holes, as long as the dimensions and tolerances of the mounting holes are processed and assembled strictly according to JB/T 9157-2011 "Dimensions and Tolerances for Hydraulic Pneumatic Ball Expansion Plugs", they can generally be used under a maximum working pressure of 40 MPa, and the manifold material can be gray cast iron, ductile iron, carbon steel, or alloy steel.
Note: If there are no technically skilled operators and strict process guarantees, try not to use hydraulic pneumatic ball expansion plugs to plug holes, especially in military products.
When using screw plugs to plug holes, pressure oil passages can only use hexagonal screw plugs specified in GB/T 2878.4-2011 (external and internal).

For test (permanent blocking) oil ports, M14×1.5 hexagonal screw plugs are preferred for plugging. Process holes on marine two-way cartridge valve manifolds should be blocked using removable methods such as plugs or flanges as much as possible.
For manifolds with pressure passages and process holes, using tapered screw plugs to plug holes is now taboo.
(6) Taboos in surface flatness and surface roughness of manifolds

In addition to ensuring the design and manufacture of corresponding holes on the manifold according to the dimensions and tolerances, position tolerances, etc. specified by the components (hydraulic valves), ensuring the verticality tolerance of threaded (screw) holes is also particularly important.

The flatness tolerance for the contact surface (mounting surface) between the current components (hydraulic valves) and the manifold is generally required to be 0.01 mm/100 mm, and the surface roughness value Ra should be ≤0.8 μm, but should comply with the requirements of the hydraulic valve manufacturer you choose.
Taboos include surface quality defects such as bumps, scratches, scribe marks, nicks, indentations, rust spots, and peeling plating on the component mounting surface.
(7) Taboos in the design of holes and threaded oil ports on manifolds

Try to avoid designing long holes, inclined holes, intersecting holes, and half-intersecting holes. Generally, when the hole depth exceeds 25 times the hole diameter or more, processing becomes difficult; when the eccentricity between two holes of equal diameter exceeds 30%, both the flow area and local resistance will have problems.

Threaded oil ports used for external connections should ensure their verticality. Generally, the verticality tolerance for threaded oil ports with M22×1.5 mm and below is φ0.10 mm, and for threaded oil ports with M22×1.5 mm and above is φ0.20 mm; the thread tapping length for threaded oil ports should be sufficient; the thread accuracy should comply with GB/T

522.page_header: 第 3 章  液压缸的制造  511

sections.text: 193. Provisions for Grade 6H in GB/T 196 and GB/T197. Considering the assembly and disassembly of pipe joints, sufficient wrench space should be left between adjacent threaded oil ports and between them and other components. Considering the strength and rigidity of oil ports, the minimum center distance between adjacent threaded oil ports should be 1.5 times the oil port diameter. It is prohibited to design flow channels in hydraulic blocks that are difficult to process or have poor flow characteristics; it is also prohibited to design piping that cannot be assembled or disassembled.
(8) Taboos for Marking Hydraulic Blocks

The marking of valve mounting surfaces on hydraulic blocks generally used for mounting plate valves and stack valves can be carried out according to the relevant regulations of hydraulic systems. However, GB/T14043-2005 "Identification Symbols for Hydraulic Valve Mounting Surfaces and Cartridge Valve Valve Holes" stipulates the identification symbols for hydraulic valve mounting surfaces and cartridge valve valve holes that comply with national and international standards. Further reference can also be made to the provisions of GB/T17490-1998 or ISO16874 (i.e., GB/T36997-2018). Identification marks should be made on the side of each external oil port at a position not less than 6 mm from the edge of the hole and not affecting the sealing. It is prohibited to omit identification marks on external oil ports of hydraulic blocks. Using computer-aided three-dimensional software to model hydraulic blocks can display the relative positions of each hole in its internal space and the connection status of each hole, allowing for a three-dimensional and intuitive check of the design results. However, the above taboos are of great significance for the design of hydraulic blocks using computer-aided three-dimensional software.
3.9.7  Taboos for Installation and Connection of Hydraulic Cylinders

Regardless of whether the installation posture of hydraulic cylinders is horizontal, vertical, or inclined, the effects of the weight of the piston rod and its connecting parts, as well as the lateral forces applied externally, on their guidance, support, and movement cannot be ignored, especially for horizontally installed hydraulic cylinders.

For large horizontally installed hydraulic cylinders and long-stroke solid piston rod hydraulic cylinders, the weight of the piston rod and the moving parts it drives can cause an increase in the eccentricity between the piston and piston rod and the cylinder barrel and guide sleeve, resulting in local wear, increased internal and external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder, and a shortened service life of the hydraulic cylinder. If necessary, additional guidance and support should be provided for the piston rod or moving parts.

For vertically installed hydraulic cylinders with a top-mounted configuration, the weight of the piston, piston rod, and the moving parts it drives is an overrunning load during the cylinder's stroke, affecting the deceleration, braking, stopping, and locking of the hydraulic cylinder; for bottom-mounted installations, it affects the return stroke motion and stopping.

For heavy-load, hollow piston rod, long-stroke, rear lug-mounted piston rod end pin hole or lug-connected hydraulic cylinders, and plunger cylinders, special attention should be paid to their rod stability (instability) issues. Hydraulic cylinders with inclination and swing requirements should be able to work normally under certain inclination and swing conditions. It is prohibited to install and connect hydraulic cylinders in an unstable or unreliable manner.

1) It is prohibited to determine the installation and connection method of the cylinder without considering the structural layout of the host machine, installation conditions, motion form, and requirements. Whether the installation and connection method of the hydraulic cylinder is appropriate has a significant impact on the service life and efficiency of the cylinder, and in severe cases, it can lead to abnormal motion.

2) It is prohibited to ignore the geometric tolerances of the hydraulic cylinder barrel, lugs, and pin shafts. In order to reduce the starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder and ensure that there is no "binding" phenomenon during motion, sufficient attention should be paid to the geometric tolerances of the barrel. Generally, the roundness and cylindricity errors of the inner diameter of the barrel should not be greater than half of the diameter tolerance of the barrel; the straightness error of the barrel axis should not be greater than 0.03 mm per 500 mm length; the axial circular runout error of the end face of the barrel should not be greater than 0.04 mm per 100 mm. For lug-type hydraulic cylinders, the position tolerance error of the lug holes relative to the barrel axis should not be greater than 0.03 mm; for pin-type hydraulic cylinders, the position tolerance error of the pin axis should not be greater than 0.1 mm, and the perpendicularity error should not be greater than 0.1 mm per 100 mm length.
3) Try to avoid the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder bearing the maximum load in a compressed state to prevent instability of the piston rod.
The installation method and load guidance will directly affect the bending stability of the piston rod. The specific requirements given in reference [99] are as follows:

items: Lug installation: The force acts within a plane, and if the lug is equipped with a ball joint, it can be deflected within a cone angle of ±4°.

Pin installation: The force acts within a plane, and the most commonly used types are front pin and intermediate pin. Rear pin is only used for small, short-stroke hydraulic cylinders because of its large support length, which affects the bending stability of the piston.

Flange installation: The force and support center are on the same axis, and the connection between the flange and the support seat should allow the flange surface to bear the force, rather than the fixing screws. For example, for front flange installation, if the force is a thrust, the type shown in Figure 3-17a should be adopted, avoiding the type shown in Figure 3-17b; if the force is a pull, the opposite is true; for rear flange installation, if the force is a thrust, the type shown in Figure 3-18a should be adopted, avoiding the type shown in Figure 3-18b; if the force is a pull, the opposite is true.

sections.text: Chapter 4 Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection for Hydraulic Press (Machine)

The hydraulic cylinder in the hydraulic system of a hydraulic press (machine) should comply with the corresponding standard provisions or with the product (design) drawings and technical documents (such as technical conditions, technical requirements) that have been reviewed, approved, and implemented by the relevant departments. The main content of this chapter is to provide a basis for the design and selection of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic press (machine).
4.1 Design and Selection Basis for Hydraulic Cylinders in Construction Machinery

Construction machinery products specified in JB 6030—2001 "General Safety Technical Requirements for Construction Machinery" include bulldozers, loaders, excavators, backhoe loaders, scrapers, and graders, which are now all classified as earthmoving machinery. Other construction machinery products may also include cranes and hoisting machinery, road construction and maintenance machinery equipment, building construction machinery and equipment, etc.

Earthmoving machinery is wheeled, tracked, or walking self-propelled or towed machinery, equipped with working devices or auxiliary devices (work tools), or both, mainly used for excavation, loading, transportation, drilling, paving, compaction, or trenching operations of soil, rock, or other materials. Hydraulic working devices and auxiliary devices in earthmoving machinery generally contain hydraulic cylinders, and the technical conditions of the entire machine serve as the basis for the design and selection of these hydraulic cylinders.

According to the principle of "Reference documents without a specified date shall be the latest version applicable to this document," the documents cited in the following sections have been updated to current standards. For revoked standards, they have been noted, and some new standards adopted should include the 2018 edition of construction machinery series standards, etc.

Note: Earthmoving machinery includes the following machine families: bulldozers, loaders, excavators, trenchers, dump trucks, scrapers, graders, backfilling compactors, road rollers, pipe-laying machines, horizontal directional drills, etc.
4.1.1 Track-Type Bulldozer

The track-type bulldozer discussed in this section is a self-propelled tracked machine, whose working device can be equipped with a bulldozer attachment, performing earth shoveling, pushing, and leveling of materials through the forward movement of the machine, or equipped with auxiliary devices to generate thrust or traction. GB/T 35213—2017 "Earthmoving Machinery - Track-Type Bulldozer - Technical Conditions" stipulates the terms and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, as well as markings, packaging, transportation, and storage of track-type bulldozers, applicable to crawler-type bulldozers (hereinafter referred to as bulldozers) with engine net power of 60~400kW that are mechanically driven, hydromechanical, or hydrostatic, derivatives of bulldozers (such as bulldozer rakes), variant products, as well as bulldozers with net power greater than 400kW, which can also be referenced.
1. Classification
(1) Type and Model
1) Type. Bulldozers can be classified into three types based on the transmission method: mechanically driven bulldozers, hydromechanical bulldozers, and hydrostatic bulldozers.
2) Model. The model of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T 9725—2014 "Product Model Compilation Method for Earthmoving Machinery."
(2) Parameters
1) Main Parameter. The engine net power is used as the main parameter for bulldozers.

2) Basic Parameters. The basic parameters of bulldozers can be found in Table A.1 of Appendix A of GB/T 35213—2017. The dimensions and symbols of basic parameters should comply with the provisions of GB/T 18577.1—2008 "Definitions of Dimensions and Symbols for Earthmoving Machinery - Part 1: Host" and GB/T 18577.2—2008 "Definitions of Dimensions and Symbols for Earthmoving Machinery - Part 2: Working Devices and Auxiliary Devices."
2. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: The engine net power of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of GB/T 16936—2015 "Engine Net Power Test Specification for Earthmoving Machinery."
The assembly quality of a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5945—2018 "General Technical Conditions for Assembly of Construction Machinery."
The appearance quality of the paint coating on a bulldozer should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5946—2018 "General Technical Conditions for Coating of Construction Machinery."
The structural design of a bulldozer should ensure safety and convenience during use, maintenance, and upkeep.

sections.text: (2) Performance and Quality Requirements

items: A bulldozer should be able to start and operate normally under environmental temperatures of -15 to 40°C and altitudes not exceeding 2000 m, with smooth starting. If special requirements are needed, they can be specified in the contract between the supplier and the demander.

The specific power of a bulldozer should not be less than 5.6 kW/t. Note: The term "specific power" is defined in GB/T 35213—2017 as "the ratio of the engine net power of a bulldozer to the working mass of the entire machine."
The side slip of a bulldozer should not exceed 0.5%.
The maximum traction force of a bulldozer should not be less than 78% of its own working mass (the ground adhesion coefficient should be greater than 0.81).

The maximum traction efficiency of a mechanically driven bulldozer should not be lower than 75%, and the maximum traction efficiency of hydromechanical and hydrostatic bulldozers should not be lower than 70%.

sections.text: The traction efficiency shall not be less than 65%.

items: After the bulldozer completes a 1000 h reliability test, the reliability evaluation index shall meet the following requirements: ① The mean time between failures (MTBF) shall not be less than 300 h; ② The availability shall not be less than 90%.

The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic system of the bulldozer's working device shall meet the following requirements: ① The contamination level of the plunger pump system shall not be higher than -/18/15; ② The contamination level of the gear pump system shall not be higher than -/20/17.
The bulldozer shall be able to climb up a longitudinal slope of 30° smoothly.
The sealing performance test of the bulldozer shall be conducted immediately after the bulldozer stops working for 3 h, and no oil or water leakage shall occur at the sealing joints within 15 min.

When the bulldozer is on a 30° longitudinal slope, it shall be able to stop reliably when braking uphill; when braking after the vehicle starts sliding down the slope from zero speed and travels 1 m by itself, it shall be able to stop reliably within the ground contact length of the track (except for hydrostatic bulldozers with neutral gear braking).
When the bulldozer turns at low speed, the driven wheel on the braking side shall not rotate (except for bulldozers with in-situ turning function).

The thermal balance performance achieved during bulldozer operation shall meet the following requirements: ① The outlet temperature of the torque converter shall not be greater than 120°C; ② The oil temperature of the final drive shall not be greater than 100°C; ③ The oil temperature of the working device (hydraulic system) shall not be greater than 90°C.
The effective capacity of the fuel tank shall ensure that the entire machine can work continuously for more than 10 h.
The lifting speed of the bulldozer's blade shall not be less than 0.3 m/s, and the natural sinking amount of the bulldozer's blade within 15 min shall not be greater than 120 mm.
The electrical system of the bulldozer shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 35213—2017.
The hydraulic system shall be safe and reliable, operate smoothly, and shall not have phenomena such as impact, stagnation, crawling, or vibration. The arrangement of various pipelines shall be neat.

sections.text: (3) Safety and environmental protection requirements
The safety and environmental protection requirements for bulldozers are specified in GB/T 35213—2017.
3. Test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage
The test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of bulldozers are specified in GB/T 35213—2017.

For material or item handling (transportation), the terms and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of hydraulic excavators are specified in GB/T 9139—2018 "Earth-moving Machinery - Hydraulic Excavator - Technical Conditions", applicable to wheeled and tracked hydraulic excavators (hereinafter referred to as excavators) with a working mass not exceeding 200000 kg as specified in GB/T 8498—2017 "Earth-moving Machinery - Basic Types - Identification, Terms, and Definitions".
4.1.2 Hydraulic excavator

This section involves hydraulic excavators, unless explicitly marked as mechanical excavators, excavators usually refer to hydraulic excavators. Excavators are self-propelled tracked, wheeled, or walking mechanical equipment with a rotatable upper structure that can carry the working device, mainly using a bucket for excavation operations, and the chassis does not move during its working cycle. The working cycle of an excavator usually includes excavation, lifting, rotation, and unloading of materials, and excavators can also be used for handling (transporting) items or materials.
1. Classification
(1) Types
According to the walking mode, they are divided into: ① Tracked excavators; ② Wheeled excavators; ③ Walking excavators.
(2) Models
The product model of the excavator shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 9725—2014 "Earth-moving Machinery - Product Model Compilation Method", or be determined by the manufacturer.
(3) Main parameters
The working mass is used as the main parameter for excavators.
(4) Main parameters
The main parameters of the excavator are shown in Table 4-1.

sections.text: 2. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: The excavator driver's manual should be prepared according to GB/T 25622—2010 (Earth-moving Machinery Driver's Manual Content and Format) regulations.
The excavator should be able to operate normally in an environment with an ambient temperature of -15~+40°C and an altitude not exceeding 2000m.
The painting quality of the excavator should meet the requirements of JB/T 5946—2018 (General Technical Conditions for Painting of Construction Machinery) regulations.
The operating device of the excavator should meet the requirements of GB/T 8595—2008 (Earth-moving Machinery Operating Device for Drivers) regulations.
The fuel tank capacity of excavators with a working mass of 6000kg and above should ensure that the entire machine can operate continuously for no less than 10h.

sections.text: (2) Performance Requirements

items: The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic system of the excavator should not exceed -/18/15 specified in GB/T 14039—2002.

Under the test conditions specified in GB/T 7586—2008 (Test Method for Hydraulic Excavators) (now GB/T 7586—2018 version), the displacement caused by internal leakage of the boom hydraulic cylinder piston rod should not exceed 25mm/10min.
No leakage should occur when the new machine leaves the factory.
The climbing ability of tire-type excavators should not be less than 35%, and that of crawler-type excavators should not be less than 50%.
The deviation of straight-line travel of crawler-type excavators should not exceed 5% of the measured distance.

Under the conditions specified in GB/T 36693—2018 (Reliability Test Method, Failure Classification and Evaluation of Earth-moving Machinery Hydraulic Excavators), the reliability of the excavator should meet the following requirements: ① The mean time between failures of excavators with a working mass of 6000kg and below should not be less than 300h, and that of excavators with a working mass of 6000kg and above should not be less than 600h. ② The operational availability should not be less than 90%.

sections.text: (3) Safety Requirements

items: The excavator should be affixed with safety labels, which should meet the requirements of GB 20178—2014 (General Provisions for Safety Labels of Earth-moving Machinery) regulations.

The driver's field of view should meet the requirements of GB/T 16937—2010 (Test Method and Performance Criteria for the Driver's Field of View of Earth-moving Machinery) regulations. Excavators can be equipped with corresponding auxiliary equipment, such as rearview mirrors and monitoring devices, to supplement the inadequacy of the direct field of view. The field of view of rearview mirrors and monitoring devices should meet the requirements of GB/T 25685.2—2010 (Field of View of Mirrors and Rearview Mirrors for Earth-moving Machinery Part 2: Performance Criteria) regulations.
The front window of the driver's cab should be equipped with a wiper and washer.
The electrical control system should have an overload protection device to ensure safety.

sections.text: 5) The excavator should meet the requirements of the mandatory provisions applicable in GB 25684.5—2010 (Safety of Earth-moving Machinery Part 5: Requirements for Hydraulic Excavators).
6) The excavator should preferably meet the requirements of the recommended provisions applicable in GB 25684.5—2010.
(4) Environmental Protection and Comfort Requirements

items: If equipped with a fully enclosed driver's cab, the environment of the driver's cab should meet the requirements of GB/T 19933.2—2014 (Driver's Cab Environment of Earth-moving Machinery Part 2: Air Filter Test Method), GB/T 19933.4—2014 (Driver's Cab Environment of Earth-moving Machinery Part 4: Test Method and Performance of Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC)), and GB/T 19933.5—2014 (Driver's Cab Environment of Earth-moving Machinery Part 5: Test Method for Defrosting System of Windshield) regulations.

The exhaust pollutants of the diesel engine of the excavator should meet the requirements of GB 20891—2014 (Emission Limits and Measurement Methods for Exhaust Pollutants of Diesel Engines for Non-road Mobile Machinery (China Stage III and IV)) regulations.

The fuel consumption rate of the diesel engine of the excavator should meet the requirements of GB 28239—2012 (Limits and Test Methods for Fuel Consumption Rate and Oil Consumption Rate of Off-road Diesel Engines) regulations.

If the excavator is equipped with an air conditioner, the refrigerant of the air conditioner should meet the requirements of GB/T 18826—2016 (Industrial 1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a)) regulations.

The sound power level of the excavator's external sound emission and the sound pressure level of the sound emission at the driver's position should meet the requirements of GB 16710—2010 (Noise Limits for Earth-moving Machinery) regulations.

Except for small excavators, the vibration reduction capability of the driver's seat of the excavator should meet the requirements of class EM6 input spectrum in GB/T 8419—2007 (Laboratory Evaluation of Vibration of Driver's Seat of Earth-moving Machinery).

sections.text: 3. Test Method
The test method should be carried out according to GB/T 7586—2008 (Test Method for Hydraulic Excavators) (now GB/T 7586—2018 version) regulations.
4. Inspection Rules
(1) Factory Inspection

items: Each excavator should be inspected and qualified by the quality inspection department of the manufacturer before leaving the factory.
The inspection items of the excavator leaving the factory should be in accordance with Table 4-2 regulations.
The indicators of the factory inspection items should all reach the requirements to be qualified.

sections.text: (2) Type Inspection
In the type inspection items, the key items specified in Table 4-2 should all reach the requirements, and the number of nonconforming important items should not exceed 2 to be qualified.
5. Marking, Packaging, Transportation and Storage
The marking, packaging, transportation and storage of the excavator can be found in GB/T 9139—2018.

4.1.3 Mining Hydraulic Excavator

The mining hydraulic excavators mentioned in this section are suitable for material excavation or earthwork engineering in open-pit mines, mainly driven by hydraulic systems, with material excavation, rotation, unloading, and walking functions, and with a working mass exceeding 200 t. GB/T 13011—2017 "Mining Hydraulic Excavator" specifies the terms and definitions, types and main parameters, technical requirements, test methods and inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of mining hydraulic excavators (hereinafter referred to as excavators), applicable to hydraulic excavators with a working mass exceeding 200 t used for open-pit mining or earthwork engineering.
1. Types and Main Parameters
(1) Types

Excavators can be divided into two types based on the prime mover: electric motor driven and diesel engine driven.
Excavators can be divided into two types based on the working device: front shovel type mining hydraulic excavator (see Figure 1 in JB/T 13011—2017) and backhoe type mining hydraulic excavator (see Figure 2 in JB/T 13011—2017).
(2) Model
The excavator product model is based on working mass as the main feature. The model representation method is shown in JB/T 13011—2017.
(3) Main Parameters
The main parameters of excavators should comply with the provisions in Table 4-3.
2. Technical Requirements (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)
(1) General Technical Requirements

items: The excavator should comply with the provisions of JB/T 13011—2017 and be manufactured according to drawings and technical documents approved through the prescribed procedures.
The manufacturing and inspection of excavators should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.
The design of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766.
The solid particle contamination level code of hydraulic system oil should comply with the provisions of GB/T 14039.

items: Safety signs should be set on the excavator, and the safety signs and danger diagrams should comply with the provisions of GB/T 25517.

sections.text: 3. Test Method and Inspection Rules (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)
(1) Overall Assembly No-Load Test
1) Before the overall assembly no-load test, a detailed test procedure should be formulated for the excavator.
2) The overall assembly no-load test of the excavator should include the following two steps:

items: Inspection and adjustment after overall assembly.
Overall assembly no-load performance test.

sections.text: 3) The inspection and adjustment after overall assembly of the excavator should include the following contents:

Before the test run, the hydraulic system should first check the leakage of hydraulic pipelines. Adjust the hydraulic pump and hydraulic valve to their positions, increase the pressure step by step, and conduct a no-load trial operation to determine that the pressure at the main test points is normal.
4) The overall assembly no-load test should include the following contents:

items: Test the actions of each working device separately. Operate the boom, arm and bucket separately to check whether the actions are normal.

sections.text: Hydraulic cylinders, boom cylinder, bucket cylinder and bucket-opening cylinder shall be tested for boom, arm, bucket and bucket-opening movements respectively. Each movement shall be tested for no less than 3 times in full stroke without any abnormal phenomenon.
② Simulate different excavation processes to test the combined movements of the working device. Each combination of movements shall be tested for no less than 3 times without any abnormal phenomenon.

③ Test the maximum working dimensions of the machine, including the maximum digging radius, maximum digging height and maximum unloading height. The test point for the maximum digging radius and maximum digging height shall be the farthest point of the middle bucket tooth tip, and the test point for the maximum unloading height shall be the lowest point at the rear of the bucket. The maximum working dimensions shall meet the performance requirements of the machine.

(2) Factory Inspection 1) Each excavator shall be inspected and qualified by the inspection department of the manufacturer before leaving the factory, and shall be accompanied by a document certifying the product's qualification. 2) The factory inspection items of the excavator include component inspection, assembly inspection and no-load test of the complete machine. For the standard product, at least one machine shall be randomly selected for no-load test of the complete machine in each batch, and the no-load test shall meet the requirements of the no-load test. (3) Type Inspection See JB/T13011-2017 for type inspection of excavators.
4. Marking, Packaging, Transportation and Storage
See JB/T13011-2017 for marking, packaging, transportation and storage of excavators.
4.1.4 Tire Type Loader

The loader is a self-propelled tracked or tire type machine, with a working device mainly used for loading operations (with a bucket) at the front end, and loads or excavates by moving the machine forward.
Note: The working cycle of the loader usually includes loading, lifting, transportation and unloading of materials.

The tire type loader involved in this section is specified in GB/T35199-2017 "Technical Conditions for Tire Type Loader of Earth-moving Machinery" in terms of terms and definitions, models, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation and storage, and is applicable to the tire type loader (hereinafter referred to as loader) specified in GB/T8498-2017 "Basic Types, Identification, Terms and Definitions of Earth-moving Machinery". Other types of loaders can also be used as reference.
1. Model
The model of the loader shall comply with the provisions of JB/T9725-2014 "Model Preparation Method for Earth-moving Machinery", or be determined by the manufacturer.
2. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: The loader shall be able to work normally in an environment with ambient temperature of -15 to 40°C and altitude not greater than 2000m.

sections.text: 2) The structure of the loader shall consider the possibility of replacing various working devices and auxiliary devices.
3) The assembly quality of the loader shall comply with the provisions of JB/T5945-2018 "General Technical Conditions for Assembly of Construction Machinery".
4) The appearance quality of the painting of the loader shall comply with the provisions of JB/T5946-2018 "General Technical Conditions for Painting of Construction Machinery".
5) The driver's manual of the loader shall comply with the provisions of GB/T25622-2010 "Driver's Manual for Earth-moving Machinery - Content and Format".
6) The capacity of the fuel tank of the loader shall ensure continuous operation for no less than 10 hours under normal working conditions.
7) The calibration of the bucket capacity of the loader shall comply with the provisions of GB/T21942-2008 "Calibration of Bucket Capacity for Loaders and Backhoe Excavators".
8) See Appendix A of GB/T35199-2017 for the basic parameters of the loader.
9) Special requirements of the loader can be determined through negotiation between the supplier and the demander.
(2) Performance Requirements

items: The hydraulic system of the loader shall comply with the provisions of GB/T3766, and the maximum temperature rise and the highest temperature of the hydraulic oil shall be within the normal working allowable range of the loader.

sections.text: 2) The solid particle contamination level of the hydraulic oil in the hydraulic system of the loader shall not be greater than the level specified in Table 4-4.
3) The solid particle contamination level code of the hydraulic oil in the torque converter and transmission system of the loader shall not be greater than —/20/17 specified in GB/T14039-2002.
4) During the entire factory inspection or type inspection (excluding reliability test), the whole machine shall not leak oil or water.
5) The settling amount of the hydraulic cylinder of the loader shall comply with the provisions of Table 4-5.

4.1.5  Graders

The graders referred to in this section are self-propelled wheeled machinery equipped with an adjustable blade between the front and rear axles. This machinery can be configured with a blade (push plate) or ripper mounted at the front, and the ripper can also be mounted between the front and rear axles. GB/T 14782—2010 "Technical Conditions for Graders" specifies the terminology and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation, and storage for self-propelled graders. It applies to self-propelled graders with integral or articulated frames.
Note: Graders mainly perform leveling, slope cutting, trenching, and loosening of materials through forward movement.
1. Classification
1) Graders are classified by frame type into integral or articulated; by transmission type into mechanical, hydraulic, or hydrostatic; by drive type into rear axle drive or all-wheel drive.
2) The model numbering method for graders follows the provisions of JB/T 9725—2014 "Product Model Numbering Method for Earthmoving Machinery".
2. Requirements (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)
(1) General requirements

1) The grader shall meet the requirements of GB/T 14782—2010 standard and be manufactured according to drawings and technical documents approved through the prescribed procedures. 2) Raw materials, purchased parts, and outsourced parts shall have markings and quality certificates from the supplier. The manufacturer shall sample and test them, and use them only after confirming they are qualified.

items: 3) Welded parts shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 5943—2018 "General Technical Conditions for Welded Parts of Construction Machinery".
4) The appearance coating shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 5946—2018 "General Technical Conditions for Coating of Construction Machinery".

sections.text: (2) Performance requirements
1) The main performance requirements for graders shall comply with the provisions of Table 4-6.

items: 2) The hydraulic system shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766, hydraulic components shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 7935, and the maximum temperature and maximum temperature rise of hydraulic oil shall be within the normal operating allowable range of the grader.
