4.1.6 Mobile Crane

A mobile crane is a type of crane that has its hoisting machinery mounted on a general-purpose or special-purpose automobile chassis, providing mobility performance similar to that of a heavy-duty vehicle. The terms, definitions, technical requirements, inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation, and storage of mobile cranes are specified in JB/T 9738-2015 "Mobile Crane". This standard applies to hydraulic cranes powered by internal combustion engines (hereinafter referred to as cranes), and other types of cranes may also refer to its implementation.
1. Technical Requirements
(1) Operating Conditions

items: The ground where the crane is parked should be firm, and no sinking should occur during operation. If necessary, measures should be taken to meet the bearing capacity requirements. The bearing capacity of the ground (road) during travel should not be less than the ground pressure and axle load of the crane.

During testing, outriggers should be extended, all tires should be lifted off the ground, the entire machine should remain level, and the inclination of the slewing bearing installation plane should not exceed 1%.
The working pressure of the crane tires should comply with the regulations in the product manual, with an allowable error of ±5%.
The ambient temperature should be -20～40℃. If it is below -20℃, it should be stated in the purchase contract.

The wind speed at the work site should not exceed 14.1m/s. When the wind speed exceeds 15.5m/s, the auxiliary arm should be retracted; when the wind speed exceeds 20.0m/s, the entire boom should be retracted to the travel state.
When the boom length exceeds 50m and the user specifies the wind speed, the working wind speed shall be executed according to the contract.
The altitude should generally not exceed 2000m.

sections.text: (2) Overall Machine (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)

items: The design calculation of the crane should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3811-2008 "Crane Design Specification".
The crane should meet the requirements for market access such as national mandatory certification and mandatory inspection of motor vehicles.
The maximum lifting capacity of the crane should comply with the provisions of GB/T 7835-2013 "Lifting Machinery - Basic Types of Rated Lifting Capacities".
The stability of the crane as a whole should comply with the provisions of GB/T 19924-2005 "Mobile Crane - Determination of Stability".
The rated lifting capacity table and working range should comply with the provisions of GB/T 21458-2008 "Mobile Crane - Rated Lifting Capacity Chart".
The setting and debugging of safety devices for the crane should comply with the requirements of JB 8716-1998 "Safety Regulations for Mobile Cranes and Tire Cranes" (already repealed).
Cranes with a maximum rated total lifting capacity greater than or equal to 8t should be equipped with an optional fixed auxiliary arm.

The operational reliability and travel reliability indicators of the crane should comply with the provisions in the product technical documents. The operational reliability test should comply with the provisions of JB/T 4030.1-2013 "Test Specification for Mobile Cranes and Tire Cranes - Part 1: Operational Reliability Test", and the travel reliability test should comply with the provisions of JB/T 4030.2-2013 "Test Specification for Mobile Cranes and Tire Cranes - Part 2: Travel Reliability Test".

The gas and liquid pipelines and electrical lines should be installed firmly and arranged neatly, and should not detach, loosen, or rub against each other during travel and hoisting operations; where mechanical damage may occur, they should be laid in grooves or pipes, and protective devices should be installed at the outlets to prevent wear.

Each control device should be easy to operate, flexible, and reliable, and should have indicator signs or markings. The signs or markings should comply with the provisions of GB 4094-2016 "Signs for Vehicle Control Devices, Indicators, and Signal Devices", GB 15052-2010 "Crane - Safety Signs and Hazard Symbol Diagrams - General Principles", and GB/T 25195.2-2010 "Crane - Symbol Diagrams - Part 2: Mobile Crane".
Edges of parts that can be touched during normal use should be rounded (minimum radius of 2mm) or chamfered (minimum 2mm×2mm).

The paint should be smooth and uniform, without defects such as missing paint, peeling, falling off, or inconsistent color; the main exposed surfaces should be free of defects such as flow marks and bubbles. The adhesion of the paint film should meet the requirements of first-class quality specified in GB/T 9286-1998 "Paints and Varnishes - Cross-cut Test for Film Adhesion".
Exposed pin shafts, valve blocks, and other metal surfaces should be treated for corrosion and rust prevention.
The maximum working speed of the crane's hydraulic pump should be limited according to design requirements, and its value should not exceed the rated speed of the hydraulic pump.
The operating parameters of the crane should meet the design values provided by the manufacturer.
The main dimensions and weight of the crane should not be greater than their limit values, and the deviation of the mass parameter should not be greater than 3%.
The manufacturer should clearly state in the instruction manual whether the crane has the capability of telescoping with load.
For cranes with special requirements, they may be executed according to the contract.

sections.text: (3) Mechanisms and Components (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)
1) Luffing Mechanism

items: The luffing mechanism should be able to reliably support the boom and make the boom stop smoothly at any position under the control of the operator; when the operator does not operate, it should be able to support the boom and the rated load.

When a hydraulic luffing mechanism is used, the design of the connecting device between the two hydraulic cylinders that perform synchronous actions should be able to avoid overload of one of the hydraulic cylinders.

sections.text: 2) Telescoping Mechanism

items: The telescoping mechanism should be able to reliably support each extended boom section, make the crane boom extend and retract smoothly to the predetermined boom length under the control of the operator, and effectively control the rated load.
A holding device (such as a

532.page_header: Chapter 4  Hydraulic Machine (Jack) Hydraulic Jack Design and Selection  521

sections.text: balance valve), in case of accidental failure of hydraulic system (such as pipe rupture), to prevent uncontrolled retraction of boom.

3. Telescopic mechanism of single-cylinder pin-insertion type. The length of each section of boom should not be less than 2 arm positions. The telescopic mechanism of single-cylinder pin-insertion type should be able to control the working pressure of hydraulic cylinder according to the load state of telescopic cylinder. Hydraulic cylinder, arm pin and cylinder pin should have mechanical interlocking device.

(4) Hydraulic System
1) The design, manufacture, installation and piping of hydraulic system should conform to the provisions of GB/T 3766.
2) Hydraulic components should be able to work normally without failure under the maximum working pressure (including the pressure during overload test) and maximum running speed. Hydraulic components should conform to the provisions of GB/T 7935.
3) Hydraulic pump and hydraulic motor should be able to withstand the change of various loads in operation. Hydraulic system should be equipped with limit load adjustment function. The starting point of variable motor should be at the maximum displacement. The automatic switching from small displacement to large displacement should be possible.
4) During the stability test of hydraulic circuit, the operation should be stable without vibration. Each hydraulic circuit should be equipped with a device showing pressure or a detection port. The accuracy of pressure gauge should not be lower than Class 1.6.
5) When the hydraulic pump is at the rated speed (flow rate), the pressure of hydraulic system should conform to the design requirements. When the hydraulic pump is running stably at the designed speed (flow rate), the actual working pressure of each hydraulic circuit should not be greater than the rated working pressure of hydraulic pump. The set pressure of safety relief valve should not be greater than 110% of the rated working pressure of system.
6) Anti-wear and viscosity-temperature hydraulic oil should be selected for crane, and it should be clearly specified in the product manual. The pollution grade, measurement method, selection and replacement of hydraulic oil solid particles should conform to the provisions of JB/T 9737-2013 "Hydraulic Oil Solid Particle Pollution Grade, Measurement and Selection for Mobile Crane".
7) During the operation of hydraulic system, the highest oil temperature in hydraulic oil tank should not exceed 80°C. When the temperature rise test is finished, the relative temperature rise of hydraulic oil in oil tank should not be greater than 45°C.
8) During the normal operation of crane (including the performance test process), there should be no oil leakage in hydraulic system. During the sealing performance test, after 15 minutes, the retraction amount of luffing hydraulic cylinder and vertical leg hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than 2mm, and the sinking amount of heavy object should not be greater than 15mm; the fixed joint surface of crane should not seep oil, and the relative moving parts should not drip oil. No oil film can be felt by hand or no oil stain can be seen by naked eye is regarded as no oil seepage; the area of oil stain oozing out should not be greater than 100cm² or no oil drop should appear is regarded as no oil dripping.
9) The safety factor of hydraulic steel pipe and joint should not be less than 2.5.
10) Hydraulic hose should conform to the provisions of JB/T 8727. The safety factor should not be less than 4. When the working pressure of hydraulic hose is greater than 5MPa or the temperature is higher than 50°C, and the distance from operator is less than 1m without any other shelter, protective measures should be taken to prevent the operator from being injured by the bursting of hose.
11) The vacuum degree at the suction port of gear pump should not be greater than 0.03MPa. The vacuum degree at the suction port of piston pump should not be greater than 0.02MPa.

12) Hydraulic cylinder should be equipped with a device which can stop its action when the hydraulic pipeline bursts accidentally (such as hydraulic lock, balance valve, etc.). The device should be as close to hydraulic cylinder as possible and adopt rigid connection. If the welded or ferrule joint is installed between hydraulic cylinder and hydraulic valve, the safety factor of the whole structure should not be less than 2.5.

13) A safety warning sign should be marked on the accumulator or at a prominent position near the accumulator.
14) Filter should be equipped with blocking detection or alarm device.
15) Hydraulic oil tank should be equipped with liquid level indicator, and the "highest" and "lowest" marks allowed by the system should be made.
2. Test Methods and Test Rules
The test method and inspection rules of crane should be carried out according to the provisions of GB/T 6068-2008 "Test Code for Truck Crane and Tyre Crane".
3. Signs, Packaging, Transportation and Storage
See JB/T 9738-2015 for signs, packaging, transportation and storage of crane.
4.1.7 Impact Roller

The impact roller involved in this section is a self-propelled or towed mechanical equipment with one or more metal compacting wheels whose outline surface is composed of several curves as generatrix, which generates impact force when rotating, and is used to compact crushed stone, concrete, soil or sand and gravel materials. GB/T 25626-2018 "Impact Roller" stipulates the terms and definitions, classification, requirements, test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation and storage of impact roller, which is applicable to towed impact roller (hereinafter referred to as roller). Other types of impact roller can be used for reference.
JB/T 13786.1-2020 "Earth-moving Machinery Oscillating Roller Part 1: Technical Conditions" will be implemented on January 1, 2021, which can be referred to.
1. Classification

(1) Model
The model of roller should be compiled according to the provisions of JB/T 9725-2014 "Product Model Compilation Method for Earth-moving Machinery", or determined by the manufacturer.

(2) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of roller should conform to the provisions of Table 4-7.

sections.caption: Table 4-7 Basic Parameters of Roller
rows: Buffer hydraulic cylinder filling oil pressure/MPa

sections.text: 2. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: The structural layout of the roller should facilitate convenient and safe use, maintenance, servicing, and adjustment.
All parts requiring lubrication should be equipped with reliable and easily maintainable lubrication devices.
The roller should have good cushioning and vibration reduction; when traveling between sites, the impact wheel should be able to be lifted and have a reliable locking device.
The assembly quality of the roller should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5945—1991 (2018) "General Technical Conditions for Assembly of Construction Machinery."
The painting quality of the roller should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5946—1991 (2018) "General Technical Conditions for Painting of Construction Machinery."

sections.text: (2) Performance Requirements

items: The operating mass of the roller should meet the requirements in Table 4-7, with an allowable deviation of ±3% of the design value.
The impact potential energy of the roller should meet the requirements in Table 4-7, with an allowable deviation of ±5% of the design value.
The operating speed of the roller should meet the requirements in Table 4-7.
The roller should not exhibit any oil leakage.
The roller should have good compaction effectiveness, achieving a compaction degree of at least 95% when meeting the effective compaction degree.

sections.text: (3) Safety Requirements

items: The roller should comply with the mandatory provisions applicable in GB 25684.1—2010 "Earth-Moving Machinery - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements" and GB 25684.13—2010 "Earth-Moving Machinery - Safety - Part 13: Requirements for Rollers." Recommended provisions should be followed as appropriate.
The safety labels attached to the roller should comply with the provisions of GB 20178—2014 "Earth-Moving Machinery - Safety Labels for Machinery - General Rules."

sections.text: (4) Reliability Requirements

items: During the 300h reliability test, the average time to first failure should be no less than 120h; the average time between failures should be no less than 150h; the operational availability should be no less than 95%.
The reliability test for the roller may alternatively be replaced by a 300h industrial test, with indicators meeting the requirements of 2.(4)1).

sections.text: 3. Test Methods
(1) Leakage Detection

items: Parts of the test machine that may exhibit leakage should be wiped clean before the test.
After the test machine operates continuously for 1.5h, stop and immediately perform the following detection:
① Place white paper under parts that may exhibit leakage to facilitate observation.
② Check for oil leakage within 10min after shutdown.
③ Record the inspection results in the Leakage Detection Record Form (see Table B.6 in GB/T 25626—2018).

sections.text: (2) Failure Determination Rules
Determine failures according to the following rules:

items: Only failures caused by the test machine's inherent potential factors and inherent defects should be counted in the failure count; failures caused by external factors or violation of operating procedures should not be counted in the failure count. When reliability testing is interrupted due to such causes, resampling and retesting are allowed.

When two or more failures occur simultaneously and there is a direct relationship between them, calculate based on the most severe failure category without cumulative calculation; when there is no direct relationship between failures, calculate separately.
Each failure occurrence should be determined as one failure count and can only be classified into one failure category.
Random spare parts should be replaced according to the time specified in the product manual, which should not be considered as a failure, but should be recorded and explained in the test report.

sections.text: (3) Reliability Index Calculation

items: Time to First Failure (MTTFF) is shown in equation (4-1).
Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) is calculated according to equation (4-2).
Operational Availability A₀ is calculated according to equation (4-4).

sections.text: MTTFF = t    (4-1)
Where t—the numerical value of time to first failure, in h.
MTBF = t₀ / rᵦ    (4-2)

Where t₀—the numerical value of accumulated product operating time, in h; rᵦ—the equivalent number of failures occurring in the product, calculated according to equation (4-3). When rᵦ < 1, let rᵦ = 1.
rᵦ = Σ kᵢ εᵢ    (4-3)
Where kᵢ—the number of occurrences of the i-th type of failure in the product; εᵢ—the hazard coefficient for the i-th type of failure (see Table D.1 in GB/T 25626—2018).
A₀ = t₀ / (t₀ + Σ trᵢ + Σ tmᵢ) × 100%    (4-4)
Where A₀—operational availability; trᵢ—the total repair time required for the i-th level of failure, in h; tmᵢ—the time required for the i-th maintenance, in h.
4. Inspection Rules, Marking, Packaging, Transportation, and Storage
The inspection rules, marking, packaging, transportation, and storage of the roller are specified in GB/T 25626—2018.
4.1.8 Asphalt Concrete Paver
The asphalt concrete paver discussed in this section adopts a floating screed/automatic leveling screed method to distribute and

sections.text: Pre-compaction, a mobile machine that forms the set road surface shape. GB/T 16277—2008 "Asphalt Concrete Paver" stipulates the classification, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, signs, packaging, transportation and storage of asphalt concrete pavers, and is applicable to self-propelled asphalt concrete pavers (hereinafter referred to as pavers).
1. Classification
(1) Type
Paving machines are classified according to their walking type:

items: Crawler paver.
Tire paver.

sections.text: (2) Basic Parameters
The basic product parameters of the paver are shown in Table 1 of GB/T 16277—2008.
(3) Model

The product model of the paver can be composed of a group code, a type code, a main parameter code, and an update and variant code, or it can be composed of enterprise information and product code, please refer to GB/T 16277—2008 for details.
2. Technical Requirements (Only Related to Hydraulic Cylinders)
(1) Basic Requirements

items: The paver should be manufactured according to the drawings and technical documents approved by the prescribed procedures.

The normal working conditions of the paver should comply with the following regulations: ① The working environment temperature of the paver should generally be within the range of 4 to 35°C; the altitude should be below 500 m.

sections.text: ② The asphalt pavement base course, asphalt mixture, etc. used by the paver should comply with the provisions of GB 50092—1996 "Technical Specifications for Asphalt Pavement Construction and Acceptance".

The paver should be able to pave the surface layer of asphalt mixture pavement in various working combination states under the condition of receiving materials from the supporting equipment specified by the product.

items: The paver should be equipped with a special device, tool box, special tools, common spare parts and accessories for hoisting and transportation.
The outer boundary dimensions in the transportation state should comply with the relevant regulations on transportation and transportation.

Reliability requirements for pavers: The reliability test time for the whole paver is 300 h; the working time before the first failure is not less than 100 h; the average trouble-free working time is not less than 100 h; the reliability is not less than 85%.

sections.text: (2) Automatic Leveling System

items: The automatic leveling system should adopt mechanical contact or non-contact sensors, and the response characteristics of the electro-hydraulic control system should meet the requirements of paving surface smoothness.

(3) Hydraulic System

The electronic management system should be able to set and store the relevant data of the working process, and output statistical data.
The electronic management system should have optional functions of wireless data transmission and remote control.
The electronic management system can provide instructions and help for the use, maintenance and maintenance of the paver as needed.

4.1.9 Hydraulic Pile Hammer

The hydraulic pile hammer uses an engine (motor) to drive a hydraulic pump that delivers stable high-pressure oil to the hydraulic cylinder. 4.2  Design and Selection Basis for Hydraulic Cylinders Used in Hydraulic Presses

A hydraulic press is a general term for presses driven by hydraulic transmission, or can be described as a general term for presses that use hydraulic transmission to drive the slider or working components. It is divided into hydraulic presses and hydraulic presses according to the medium. Usually, a hydraulic press refers to a press driven by hydraulic pressure. For some hydraulic presses specified in standards, see Table 4-10. Although there are various differences, the hydraulic system and hydraulic cylinder are components of the hydraulic presses specified in the standards. A CNC hydraulic press is a hydraulic press that mainly uses digital quantities for information transmission and control, has a man-machine interface, and adopts digital control for main parameters (at least including pressure and displacement parameters). However, its type should comply with GB/T 28761-2012 "Forging Machinery Type Designation Method". In various hydraulic press standards, the type and basic parameters, (technical) requirements, etc., of hydraulic presses are generally given, which are the basis for designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses. Some detailed (or specific) technical requirements are even mandatory for hydraulic cylinders specially designed for that type of hydraulic press. In order to standardize the design and selection of hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses, the following excerpts from the current various hydraulic press standards, and provides necessary annotations and explanations for the requirements (including type and parameters) of hydraulic cylinders in them.

This includes technical requirements for the hydraulic cylinder's "starting pressure," "static friction force with load," and "operation," etc.

4.2.2 Single Column Hydraulic Press

In GB/T 36484-2018, a 'single column hydraulic press' is defined as: 'A hydraulic press whose body is a C-shaped single column structure.' In JB/T 9958.1-1999, the types and basic parameters of single column hydraulic presses are specified, applicable to medium and small single column hydraulic presses for calibration pressing, stretching, and general purposes.
1. Types
1) Single column hydraulic presses are classified by their ram speeds into:

items: Type I—Low speed type, with a removable calibration worktable and precision calibration device, generally suitable for manual control.

Type II—Medium speed type, with structures for adjusting the ram's no-load and working stroke speeds, and adjusting the working force and stroke of the ram and lower ejection device, generally suitable for semi-automatic control.

Type III—High speed type, in addition to having the structures required for the medium speed type, should also be able to achieve the possibility of automatic production lines, generally suitable for automatic control.

sections.text: 4.2.4 Electrode Extrusion Hydraulic Press

The electrode extrusion hydraulic press is mainly used in the carbon industry to extrude the raw material paste mixed and kneaded in a hot state into the required specifications after cooling. JB/T 1808—2005 stipulates the types and basic parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, and signs, packaging, transportation, and storage of electrode extrusion hydraulic presses, applicable to electrode extrusion hydraulic presses (hereinafter referred to as extruders).
Note: The terms and definitions of "carbon electrode hydraulic press" are found in GB/T 36484—2018 and JB/T 4174—2014.
1. Types and Basic Parameters
(1) Types

The type of extruder is a carbon electrode forming extrusion hydraulic press with a high-position oil tank and direct drive of the oil pump. The material chamber is divided into fixed and rotating types. The structures of fixed and rotating material chambers extruders are shown in Figures 1 and 2 of JB/T 1808—2005, respectively.
(2) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of the extruder should comply with the provisions in Table 4-17.

sections.caption: Table 4-17 Basic Parameters of Extruders

sections.text: 2. Technical Requirements

The design and manufacture of the extruder should comply with the provisions of JB/T 1808—2005 standard and be manufactured according to the approved design drawings and technical documents (or the contract and agreement signed by the user and the manufacturer).
(1) General Requirements

The cutting, machining, welding, casting, forging, piping, and painting of the extruder, in addition to meeting the requirements of the design drawings and technical documents, should also comply with the relevant provisions of JB/T 5000.

544.page_header: Chapter 4  Design and Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders for Hydraulic Presses (Machinery)  533

sections.text: 2) In addition to meeting the requirements of drawings and technical documents, the electric power transmission and control system shall also comply with the relevant provisions of GB 5226.1.
(2) Structural requirements

items: The rotating material chamber shall be able to rotate 90° as specified, and ensure the positioning requirements of the material chamber in horizontal or vertical positions.
Nozzles and nozzle sleeves of various specifications shall be interchangeable.
The heating device for the nozzle sleeve and nozzle type shall be able to reach the required working temperature.
The vacuum chamber shall be tightly combined with the material chamber, and the sealing structure shall meet the specified vacuum degree requirements during vacuum extraction.
The extruded electrode shall be cut to the required length and the corresponding cooling time shall be selected according to different specifications of the electrode.
The flatness of the cut electrode end face shall be less than 6mm.

The operation program compiled by the PLC programmable controller shall meet the requirements for normal and safe operation of the equipment. Signals from misoperations shall not be responded to (except for the emergency stop button).
The impact of electrode specification changes on production capacity can be compensated by changing the extrusion parameters.

sections.text: (3) Safety requirements

items: The extruder shall be equipped with mechanical safety devices to ensure the personal safety of operators.
Both the electrical control and hydraulic systems shall have overload and interlock safety protection devices.

The heating elements of the nozzle, material chamber and extrusion head shall be safe and reliable. Pipes and joints heated with heat transfer oil shall not leak. Heating elements heated electrically shall be reliably insulated. When measured with a 500V megohmmeter, the insulation resistance value shall not be less than 0.5MΩ.
The noise value of the extruder during operation shall not be greater than 85dB(A).

sections.text: (4) Assembly precision requirements

items: After assembly, the flatness of the upper plane of the extruder base shall be 0.1/1000.

The shoulder of the main cylinder, the nut of the tension rod and the end faces of the front and rear crossbeams shall be tightly fitted. When checked with a 0.08mm feeler gauge, the insertion depth shall not exceed 10mm, and the cumulative insertion length shall not be greater than 10% of the circumference.

When the extrusion head moves within the full length of the material chamber, there shall be no rubbing against the sides. The allowable gap in the vertical direction can be adjusted to be tight on top and loose on bottom at the outer end of the material chamber, and tight on bottom and loose on top at the bottom of the material chamber, but the minimum single-sided gap shall be greater than 0.2mm.

sections.text: (5) Completeness

1) The extruder shall include the main body, hydraulic station, cutting device, electrical control system, vacuum extraction device, etc. The cylindrical cooling machine, nozzle replacement machine, and cooling roller conveyor can be optionally configured. The scope of supply shall be as specified in the purchase contract.
2) Supporting parts (including motors, hydraulic pumps, vacuum devices, hydraulic and electrical components, and sealing parts, etc.) shall comply with the current relevant standards and have obtained their qualification certificates.
3) Spare parts shall be provided as specified in the contract.
(6) Reliability and service life

1) The service life of the extruder under specified usage conditions shall not be less than 3000h.
2) The cumulative working time from the start of use to the first major overhaul of the extruder shall not be less than 15000h.
Note:
1) Before designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses, it is essential to clearly and accurately understand the usage conditions of the hydraulic cylinders. The adjustment range of the hydraulic cylinder and the slide block it drives is very important.
2) The durability requirement for hydraulic cylinders may differ from the reliability and service life requirement for hydraulic presses, but generally the service life of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses should be comparable to that of the hydraulic press.
3) The completeness of hydraulic presses is specified, and the sealing parts of hydraulic cylinders in the supporting parts are very important.
4.2.5 Powder metallurgy hydraulic press

In GB/T 8541—2012, GB/T 36484—2018, JB/T 4174—2014 and JB/T 12519.1—2015, there is no term or definition for "powder metallurgy hydraulic press". JB/T 12519.1—2015 specifies the types and basic parameters of 1000~25000kN powder metallurgy hydraulic presses, which are applicable to general-purpose powder metallurgy hydraulic presses (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic presses).
1. Types

According to the structural type of the machine body, hydraulic presses can be divided into two basic types:
1) Four-column type (see Figure 1 in JB/T 12519.1—2015).
2) Frame type (see Figure 2 in JB/T 12519.1—2015).
Note: In Figures 1 and 2 of JB/T 12519.1—2015, the installation types of the hydraulic cylinders for both basic types are MF7 with rear centering and front end round flange. However, it should be noted that Figures 1 and 2 do not determine the structure of the hydraulic press.

items: The main parameter of the hydraulic press is the nominal force.
The type of the hydraulic press shall comply with the provisions of Figures 1 and 2 in JB/T 12519.1—2015.
The basic parameters of the hydraulic press shall comply with the provisions of Table 4-18.

sections.text: 4.2.6 Powder product hydraulic press

items: The working table surface is the reference plane for the overall assembly accuracy test.

sections.text: 4.2.7 Hydraulic Press for Plastic Products

Hydraulic press for plastic products is a hydraulic press for pressing plastic products. JB/T 3820-2015 stipulates the accuracy inspection of hydraulic press for plastic products, which is applicable to hydraulic press for plastic products (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic press), but not applicable to injection molding machine.
1. Inspection Instructions

items: The working table surface is the reference plane for the overall assembly accuracy inspection of the hydraulic press.
Before the accuracy inspection, the hydraulic press should be leveled, and the longitudinal and transverse level deviation of its working table surface shall not exceed 0.20 mm/1000 mm.
For the hydraulic press equipped with a movable working table, the working table shall be placed in the working position of the hydraulic press and locked firmly.
The accuracy inspection should be carried out separately after no-load operation and load operation, and the value of accuracy inspection after load operation shall prevail.
The accuracy inspection shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 10923-2009, and other equivalent inspection methods may also be adopted.
L is the maximum length of the surface to be tested, and l is the length not tested. When L ≤ 1000mm, l is L/10; when L > 1000mm, l = 100mm.
The flatness of the upper plane of the working table and the lower plane of the slider may be inspected before assembly.

Before the overall assembly accuracy inspection, the adjustment principle of the clearance between the slider and the guide rail: under the premise of ensuring the overall assembly accuracy, the guide rail shall not generate heat, be not pulled, and be able to form an oil film. The recommended total clearance value of the guide rail in Table 4-21 is only for reference.

2. Measure the total clearance of the upper and lower parts of the guide rail with a feeler gauge at the extreme position of the slider's movement, or push the slider to one side of the fixed guide rail to measure its total clearance on one side.

sections.text: (3) Selection principles for relevant parameters and dimensions of hydraulic press
1) Only one hydraulic cushion force parameter is selected for one nominal force (specification).

2) The opening height of tensile slider, stroke of slider and stroke of hydraulic cushion can be adopted correspondingly according to the parameters listed in Table 4-25, or cross-selection can be made.

3) The opening height and stroke of blank holder slider should be consistent with those of tensile slider in principle. In special cases, the opening height and stroke of blank holder slider can be slightly smaller than those of tensile slider (but the last two digits should be rounded to hundreds).

4) The dimensions of tensile slider, distribution dimensions of ejector pins of hydraulic cushion, and dimensions of blank holder slider and worktable can be adopted correspondingly according to the dimensions listed in Table 4-25, or cross-selection can be made.
5) Speeds.
① Speed of tensile slider.
a. Only one empty stroke descending speed and one working speed parameter are selected for one product with nominal force (specification).
b. The return speed should be greater than or equal to 2/3 of the empty stroke descending speed parameter.
② Speed of blank holder slider. The empty stroke descending speed and return speed of blank holder slider should be greater than or equal to 2/3 of the corresponding parameters of tensile slider.

6) In case of special situations, when the dimensions of worktable, slider and distribution dimensions of ejector pins of hydraulic cushion specified in JB/T 8493-1996 standard are insufficient, the dimensions recommended in Appendix A of JB/T 8493-1996 can be referred to.
2. Precision of hydraulic press
(1) Inspection description
1) The worktable surface is the reference surface for the overall assembly precision inspection of hydraulic press.

2) Before the precision inspection, the hydraulic press should be adjusted to be level, and the longitudinal and transverse level deviation of its worktable surface shall not exceed 0.20/1000. The front side is the position of the main operator of the hydraulic press, and the right side is the right side.
3) For the hydraulic press equipped with a movable worktable, the worktable should be in the working position of the hydraulic press and locked firmly.

4) The precision inspection should be carried out respectively after the empty operation test and load operation test, and the value of precision inspection after the load operation test shall prevail.
5) The precision inspection should comply with the provisions of GB/T 10923-2009, or other equivalent inspection methods can be adopted.
6) L is the maximum length of the surface to be inspected, and l is the length not to be inspected. When L≤1000 mm, l=0.1L; when L>1000 mm, l=100 mm.
7) The flatness of the upper plane of the worktable and the lower plane of the slider can be inspected before assembly.

8) Before the overall assembly precision inspection, the principle for adjusting the clearance between the slider and the guide rail should ensure that the guide rail does not heat up, does not roughen, and can form an oil film on the premise of ensuring the overall assembly precision. The recommended total clearance values of guide rails listed in Table 4-26 are only for reference.

2. Accuracy
(1) Basic Requirements
1) Accuracy Inspection Reference. The workbench surface serves as the reference plane for hydraulic press accuracy inspection.
2) Conditions for Accuracy Inspection.
① Before accuracy inspection, the hydraulic press should be adjusted to a level position, and the flatness of its workbench surface should not exceed 0.20/1000.

② The accuracy inspection of hydraulic presses should be conducted separately after empty running and full load running tests, with the measured values after full load running tests recorded in the qualification certificate.

3) Requirements for Inspection Methods. Manufacturers or users may employ other equivalent methods for accuracy inspection, but arbitration should strictly follow the provisions of JB3864-1985 standard.
4) Requirements for Measuring Tools. See JB3864-1985 for details.

5) Provisions for Accuracy Inspection Using Pressure Test Blocks. For hydraulic presses for other types of abrasive products that cannot be inspected according to the methods specified in JB3864-1985 standard, the pressure test block method may be used for inspection. The tolerance and method for accuracy inspection should comply with the provisions of Appendix A of JB3864-1985.

6) Calculation Methods for Tolerances and Rounding of Decimals. The tolerance values for each inspection item must be calculated according to the specified formulas. For calculation structures, decimal values less than 5 are counted as 5, and those greater than 5 are counted as 10.
7) Codes in Standards. See JB3864-1985 for details.
(2) Given Tolerance Values and Inspection Methods
See JB3864-1985 for details. However, this standard is quite outdated, and whether to adopt it is to be negotiated between the manufacturer and the user.
4.2.11 Hydraulic Press for Magnetic Materials

The terms "hydraulic press for magnetic materials" and their definitions are not found in GB/T8541-2012, GB/T36484-2018, JB/T4174-2014, and JB/T6584-1993. JB/T6584-1993 specifies the technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, packaging, marking, and transportation for hydraulic presses for magnetic material products (hereinafter referred to as magnetic material presses).
1. Technical Requirements
(1) Drawing and Technical Document Requirements
Magnetic material presses should be manufactured according to the approved drawings and technical documents.
(2) Type and Basic Parameters
The type and basic parameters of magnetic material presses should comply with the corresponding standards.
(3) Complete Set Requirements
1) Magnetic material presses are generally equipped with corresponding auxiliary devices.
① Auxiliary devices for wet forming. Including automatic slurry delivery device, magnetizing/demagnetizing device, vacuum water extraction device, and universal mold frame.
② Auxiliary devices for dry forming. Including powder feeding device, magnetizing/demagnetizing device, and universal mold frame.

2) Magnetic material presses should be equipped with necessary tools, accessories, and wearing parts, ensuring their performance and interchangeability. The supply of special accessories is to be negotiated between the supplier and the demander.
(4) Requirements for Purchased Supporting Parts

The quality of purchased supporting parts for magnetic material presses should comply with the provisions of the corresponding standards. They should undergo running tests simultaneously with the whole machine upon leaving the factory.
(5) Safety and Protection
1) Magnetic material presses should have reliable safety and protection devices for operators. Protection devices should comply with the requirements of JB3915 (already abolished).
2) Magnetic material presses should have reliable overload and overtravel protection devices.
3) Magnetic material presses should be equipped with emergency stop and devices to prevent power-driven operation when unexpected voltage returns.
(6) Performance of the Press
1) Magnetic material presses should have floating pressing and bidirectional pressing process actions.
2) The pressure and stroke of magnetic material presses can be adjusted according to process requirements.
3) The pressing speed of magnetic material presses should be adjustable within the range specified in the design documents.
4) The sliding friction pairs of magnetic material presses should take wear-resistant measures and have a reasonable hardness difference.

5) The operation of magnetic material presses must be sensitive, reliable, and stable. Hydraulic actuators (such as pistons and plungers) should not exhibit vibration, crawling, or jamming phenomena within the specified stroke speed range. Reversing should not have impact phenomena affecting normal operation.
6) Magnetic material presses should have continuous pressing capability, and the continuous pressing time should be adjustable.
7) The coordinated and reliable operation of the press and its supporting auxiliary devices should be ensured.
8) The rigidity of magnetic material presses should comply with relevant standards or design requirements.

9) The noise limit of magnetic material presses should comply with the provisions of ZBJ62006.1 (already abolished), and the measurement method should follow the provisions of JB3623 (already abolished).
10) The accuracy of magnetic material presses should not be lower than the provisions of GB/T9166-2009.
(7) Performance of Supporting Devices
1) Automatic slurry delivery device.
2) Automatic powder feeding device.
3) Vacuum water extraction device.
4) Magnetizing/demagnetizing device.
5) Requirements for universal mold frame.

(8) Castings, Forgings, Welded Parts and Their Quality

1) All castings, forgings, and welded parts on the magnetic material press shall comply with the provisions of the standards and the technical requirements of the drawings and process documents. Defects in castings that do not affect use and appearance are allowed to be repaired according to the provisions of relevant standards, provided that quality is ensured.
2) The working surfaces of important castings shall not have defects such as pores, shrinkage cavities, sand holes, slag inclusions, and segregation.
3) Important castings, forgings, and welded parts shall be subjected to stress relief treatment.
4) The hardness of the same guide rail surface after machining shall be uniform, and the hardness difference shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 3818—2014.

5) After machining, parts shall comply with the requirements of the design drawings, process documents, and relevant standards; the machined surfaces shall not have burrs, scratches, or other mechanical damage; sharp edges and corners shall not be present, except as otherwise specified.
6) The scale lines, numbers, and markings on the scale parts of parts shall be accurate, uniform, and clear.
(9) Assembly Quality

1) The magnetic material press shall be assembled according to the assembly process specifications. No damaged parts, their surfaces, or the lips of seals shall be assembled. After assembly, the actions of each mechanism shall be flexible, accurate, and reliable.

2) Important fixed mating surfaces shall be tightly fitted. After being firmly pre-tightened, they shall be inspected using a 0.05 mm feeler gauge. Local insertion is allowed, and the cumulative insertion portion shall not exceed 10% of the inspectable length.
Important fixed mating surfaces include:

items: The fixed mating surface between the column shoulder and the worktable.
The fixed mating surface between the column adjustment nut, locknut, and the upper beam and worktable.
The fixed mating surface between the hydraulic cylinder locknut and the upper beam.
The fixed mating surface between the piston shoulder and the slider.

4) All pipelines, pipe joints, flanges, and other fixed and movable connections shall be reliably connected, well sealed, and free from leakage.
(10) Quality of Hydraulic, Pneumatic, and Electrical Devices
1) Hydraulic Device Quality:

items: The hydraulic device shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 3818—2014.

When designing the hydraulic system, the heat generation shall be minimized, and the hydraulic oil shall be able to dissipate heat effectively. The oil temperature in the oil tank (or the oil temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump) shall not exceed 60°C.
A magnetic filter shall be installed in the hydraulic system of the magnetic material press.
The cleanliness of the hydraulic system of the magnetic material press shall comply with the provisions of ZBJ 6200.1 (now obsolete).

sections.text: 2) The pneumatic device shall comply with the provisions of Article 5.3 in JB/T 1829—2014.

4) Appearance Quality:

items: The appearance quality of the magnetic material press shall comply with the provisions of JB/T 3818—2014.
The painting of the magnetic material press shall comply with the provisions of ZBJ 5001 (now obsolete).

sections.text: 2. Testing Methods
(1) Testing Conditions for the Magnetic Material Press

items: Before testing, the press shall be leveled, and the levelness of the worktable in the longitudinal and transverse directions shall not be greater than 0.20/1000.
The matching auxiliary devices shall be tested together with the press.
Testing shall be conducted under normal conditions of voltage, hydraulic pressure, air pressure, and lubrication.

sections.text: (2) Performance Testing

items: Starting and Stopping Test. It shall be conducted continuously for no less than 3 times, and the action shall be sensitive and reliable.
Sliding Operation Test. It shall be conducted continuously for no less than 3 times, and the action shall be stable and reliable.
Slider Stroke Adjustment Test. It shall be adjusted to the maximum stroke length, and the action shall be accurate and reliable.
Slider Stroke Limiter Test. It can generally be combined with the slider stroke adjustment test, and the action shall be accurate and reliable.

Slider Stroke Speed Test. It shall be tested at the maximum empty stroke speed, and the action shall be accurate and reliable. The stroke speed shall comply with the provisions of relevant standards or technical documents.
Pressure Adjustment Test. The pressure shall be debugged in stages from low pressure to high pressure, and the pressure at each stage shall be stable and reliable.

Matching Auxiliary Device Test. The actions of the slurry automatic delivery device, vacuum water absorption device, magnetizing and demagnetizing device, universal mold frame, and other matching auxiliary devices shall be coordinated, accurate, and reliable.
Sustained Pressure Test. The pressure shall be maintained for 10 s at the rated system pressure, the pressure shall be stable, and the pressure deviation shall not be greater than ±0.8 MPa.
Safety Device Test. It shall be combined with the machine performance test, and the action shall be safe and reliable.
Safety Valve Test. It shall be combined with the load test, and the action test shall be conducted for no less than 3 times. The action shall be sensitive and reliable.

4.2.12 Six-sided top hydraulic press for superhard materials

The terms and definitions of "six-sided top hydraulic press for superhard materials" are not included in GB/T 8541-2012, GB/T 36484-2018, JB/T 4174-2014, and JB/T 8779-2014. JB/T 8779-2014 stipulates the model and basic parameters, accuracy, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, packaging, transportation, and storage of the six-sided top hydraulic press for superhard materials, which is applicable to six-sided top hydraulic presses for superhard materials with mineral oil as the transmission medium, driven by a single pump (or with a booster), hereinafter referred to as the press.
1. Model and basic parameters

items: The model name of the press should comply with GB/T 28761.
The parameters and dimensions of the press should adopt the parameters and dimensions approved through the prescribed procedures.

sections.text: 2. Accuracy

items: The accuracy inspection of the press should comply with GB/T 10923.

Before the accuracy inspection, the installation level of the press should be adjusted. On the flange surface of the lower hydraulic cylinder of the press, a level should be placed along two perpendicular directions, and the reading of the level should not be greater than 0.20/1000.
Special inspection tools and accuracy inspection can be found in JB/T 8779-2014.

sections.text: 3. Technical requirements

items: General requirements: 1) The press should comply with JB/T 1829, and should be manufactured according to the drawings and technical documents approved through the prescribed procedures. 2) The design and layout should consider the requirements of process aesthetics, the appearance should be beautiful, and it should be convenient for use, maintenance, assembly, disassembly, and transportation. 3) Spare parts and accessories should be interchangeable and should comply with the relevant standards and technical documents. 4) The accompanying technical documents include the product inspection certificate, packing list, and product instruction manual. The product instruction manual should comply with GB/T 9969, and its content should include an introduction to performance and structure, installation, transportation, storage, use, and safety. 5) The disassembled parts and hydraulic components should have corresponding identification marks. The pipe ports and channel ports of hydraulic components should have dust-proof measures.
Stiffness: The press should have sufficient stiffness and should comply with the provisions of the technical documents.
Wear-resistant measures: Important friction pairs (such as cylinders, sleeves, pistons) should take necessary wear-resistant measures and comply with the provisions of the technical documents.

Safety protection: 1) The safety protection of the press should comply with GB 28241. Whether it is the design and selection of the structure, components, and hydraulic system, as well as their application, configuration, adjustment, and control, consideration should be given to ensuring personal safety under various usage and maintenance conditions. 2) On the main machine and its molds (top hammers) in the ultra-high-pressure working area, the buyer should set up personal safety protection devices, such as protective plates (walls). If the supplier needs to provide them, it should be noted in the contract or agreement. 3) The buyer should formulate a regular inspection, replacement, and scrapping system for the ultra-high-pressure parts of the press to ensure the safe operation of the press. 4) An over-travel protection device should be installed on the main machine and the booster to prevent accidents. 5) The exposed windows on the main machine should have protective plates, and the exposed couplings should have protective covers. 6) Parts that may automatically fall off, such as pins, should have anti-falling-off devices. 7) Single-direction rotating motors should mark arrows indicating the direction of rotation in obvious places. 8) The selection of all hydraulic components should not exceed the technical specifications specified for those components. 9) The relevant components affecting safety in the hydraulic system should be equipped with safety protection devices such as overload protection and over-travel protection [such as safety valves, over-travel buzzers, warning indicator lights, and automatic power-off devices for the electrical system, etc.]. 10) The hydraulic circuit and electrical circuit should prevent uncontrolled movement and abnormal action sequences under conditions such as the starting, stopping, idling, adjustment, and hydraulic faults of the executing elements. 11) When the press is shut down, it should be able to automatically release the hydraulic pressure or reliably cut off from the hydraulic system. For gas accumulators, they should be filled with nitrogen or other inert gases, kept away from heat sources, and installed vertically. 12) The noise should not exceed the provisions of GB 26484.

sections.text: (5) Cast and forged parts

items: The cast steel parts of the press should comply with the provisions of the technical documents. Defects that do not affect safe use, service life, and appearance can be repaired according to relevant regulations, provided that the quality is guaranteed.
Important cast and forged parts (such as hinge beams, working cylinders, booster cylinders, ultra-high-pressure cylinders, and working pistons) should undergo stress relief treatment.

(6) Machining: 1) The quality of machined parts should comply with the provisions of the design drawings and technical documents, and there should be no defects that reduce the safe use of the press or affect its appearance. 2) The machined surfaces should not have defects such as rust, burrs, bumps, and scratches. 3) The quality grade of non-planar defects on the hinge ear side of cast steel parts is Grade 1 as specified in GB 7233.2-2010, and the quality grade of non-planar defects on the remaining parts and other cast steel parts is Grade 2 as specified in GB 7233.2-2010.

4) The safety technical requirements for the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of safety protection.

① When the rated pressure is less than or equal to 20 MPa, the pressure test pressure should be 1.5 times the rated pressure.

sections.text: 4. Test Methods
(1) General Requirements

items: The press should be installed and adjusted before inspection, and its installation level should comply with the accuracy requirements.
During the inspection process, structural parts and components that affect the performance and accuracy of the press should not be adjusted. Otherwise, the test should be repeated.

The inspection should be carried out on the assembled whole machine. Except for the parts specified in the standard or technical document that need to be disassembled during the inspection, other parts should not be disassembled.
The power supply should be normal during the inspection.
All actuators of the press should be connected during the inspection.

sections.text: (2) Basic Performance Inspection
It should be carried out in combination with the no-load test and load test. The general performance inspection methods are as follows:

items: Starting and stopping inspection. It should be carried out continuously for no less than three times, and the action should be sensitive and reliable.
Operation test of the main engine and booster piston. It should be carried out continuously for no less than three tests, and the action should be flexible and reliable.
Limit adjustment test of the main engine piston stroke. It should be adjusted within the piston stroke range, and the action should be accurate and reliable.

Main engine piston stroke speed adjustment test. It should be adjusted according to the maximum no-load stroke speed specified, and the action should be accurate and reliable, and comply with the relevant standards or technical documents.

Pressure adjustment test. According to the provisions of the technical document, it should be measured in stages from low pressure to high pressure. The pressure test results at each pressure level should be stable and reliable.

Safety device test. Action tests such as emergency stop and emergency pressure relief, and prevention of automatic connection of electric drive devices when unexpected voltage is restored should all be safe and reliable.
Safety valve test. It should be combined with overload test, and the number of action tests should be no less than three times. The results should be flexible and reliable.

sections.text: (3) No-load Test

items: The press piston should undergo a no-load test with full reciprocating motion. The continuous no-load test time should be no less than 4 hours. During type inspection, the continuous no-load test time for each test should be no less than 8 hours, and the cumulative continuous no-load test time should be no less than 68 hours.

After the no-load test, measure the oil temperature in the oil tank (or the temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump). Record the temperature when it reaches a stable value. The temperature should not be higher than 60°C.

During the no-load test process, check the working conditions of each mechanism: ① Check the correctness and smoothness of the actuator movement. ② Check all high-pressure and low-pressure hydraulic systems, cooling systems, etc. The pipes, joints, flanges, and other connecting seams should be well sealed, and there should be no oil or water leakage or mutual mixing. ③ Check whether all indicating devices are accurate and reliable.

sections.text: (4) Load Test

items: After the press passes the no-load test, it should undergo a full load test.

Pressure regulation test: Increase the pressure in stages according to the specified pressure levels, and the operation should be stable and reliable. Check the temperature rise and leakage to comply with the regulations.

Under the rated pressure, the continuous operation test should be no less than 15 hours. Check the temperature rise of the system, leakage, nominal force, and the current of the main motor, which should comply with the regulations.
Perform a pressure holding test under the rated pressure, and the pressure drop should comply with the provisions of Table 4-34.
The work of each mechanism should be normal during the load test.

sections.text: (5) Overload Test

The overload test should be carried out with the safety valve adjusted to 1.1 times the rated pressure, and the number of times should be no less than three times. The parts of the press should not have any damage or permanent deformation, and the hydraulic system should not have leakage or other abnormal phenomena.
Explanation:

items: Although the pressure test pressure for hydraulic cylinders in JB/T 8779-2014 is contradictory to the pressure test pressure for the shells of self-made hydraulic components, it has important reference value for hydraulic cylinders used in hydraulic presses with a nominal (or rated) pressure greater than 31.5 MPa.

In JB/T 8779-2014: "When designing a hydraulic system, necessary measures should be taken to ensure that the oil temperature in the oil tank (or the temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump) is 15-60°C." This is more explicit than the statements in other standards.
The pressure holding performance (pressure holding accuracy) of the press in JB/T 8779-2014 also has certain reference value.

4.2.14 Single-Action Thin Plate Stamping Hydraulic Press

The single-action thin plate stamping hydraulic press is a thin plate stamping hydraulic press with one slider. JB/T8492-1996 specifies the basic parameters and dimensions of single-action thin plate stamping hydraulic presses, applicable to the Y27 series single-action thin plate stamping hydraulic presses.

The general requirements for welded parts should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.3.
The welding of pipelines should comply with the provisions of JB/T 5000.11.
The upper crossbeam, slide, base, and worktable are made of cast steel parts and should not be lower than the requirements of ZG270-500 in GB/T 11352-2009.
The upper crossbeam, slide, base, and other main components are made of welded structures, with the following requirements:

sections.text:
① The material shall comply with the provisions of GB/T700 and GB/T1591, and shall not be lower than Q235.

8) Columns (columns in a column-and-beam hydraulic press) and tie rods (tie rods in a prestressed frame press):
① Columns and tie rods shall not be lower than the requirements for 45 steel in JB/T6397-2006, and the forgings shall comply with the requirements for Group V in JB/T5000.8-2007.
② The hardness of the working surface (guideway surface) of the columns in a column-and-beam press shall not be lower than 280 HBW.

9) Working cylinder, with the following requirements:
① For working cylinders made of casting, forging, or welding, mechanical properties such as ReL, Rm, A, Z, and KU2 (with a notch depth of 2 mm) shall be inspected piece by piece.
② For working cylinders made of casting, forging, or welding, intermediate pressure test shall be conducted at 1.5 times the working liquid pressure for a pressure test with a duration of 10 min. External leakage test shall be conducted at the highest working liquid pressure. For welded working cylinders, if the manufacturer has corresponding forged parts (split forgings) and corresponding non-destructive testing specifications for the weld seams, etc., as process assurance, the pressure test may not be conducted.
③ For integral forged working cylinders, the mechanical properties and non-destructive testing results shall prevail, and the intermediate test may not be conducted.

10) The hardness of the working surface of the plunger and piston rod shall not be lower than 40 HRC, and the hardened layer shall not be less than 3 mm. For medium and large parts, hardfacing is recommended for the hardened layer.
(4) Quality of machined parts

1) The general requirements for machining of parts shall comply with the provisions of JB/T5000.9.
2) Machining requirements for major parts:
① Machining requirements for the upper crossbeam, slide block, base, frame, and working table are as follows:
a. The surface roughness value Ra of the major working surfaces shall be 6.3 μm.
b. The major geometric tolerances shall not be lower than grade 7.
c. The tolerance for the center distance of the holes in the columns of a column-and-beam press shall be ±0.15 mm.
② Machining requirements for the plunger and piston rod are as follows:
a. The surface roughness value Ra of the working surfaces shall be 1.6 μm.
b. The major geometric tolerances shall not be lower than grade 7.
③ Machining requirements for the working cylinder are as follows:
a. The surface roughness value Ra of the inner bore of the piston cylinder shall be 1.6 μm.
b. The surface roughness value Ra of the bottom R and the flange shoulder of the cylinder shall be 3.2 μm.
c. The major geometric tolerances shall not be lower than grade 7.
④ Columns (columns in a column-and-beam press):
a. The surface roughness value Ra of the stressed surface of the thread and the surface R shall be 3.2 μm.
b. The surface roughness value Ra of the guideway surface shall be 1.6 μm.
(5) Assembly quality

1) The general technical requirements for assembly shall comply with the provisions of JB/T5000.10.
2) After fastening, the important joint surfaces shall fit closely, and the clearance between them shall not be greater than the requirements specified in Table 4-42. The cumulative length of the out-of-tolerance part shall not be greater than 10% of the inspection length, and the depth of insertion shall not be greater than 10 mm. The important joint surfaces are:
① The joint surface between the large nut and the crossbeam (upper beam or base).
② The joint surface between the upper beam or base and the frame (i.e., the columns in a frame press).
③ The joint surface between the flange shoulder of the hydraulic cylinder and the crossbeam.
④ The joint surface between the end face of the piston rod or plunger and the slide block.
⑤ The joint surface between the working table and the base.

items: Technical requirements and connection dimensions of purchased and self-made hydraulic components shall conform to the provisions of GB/T 7935.

Hydraulic cylinder shall be subjected to overall assembly pressure test, with test pressure being 1.25 times of working pressure. The pressure holding time shall not be less than 10 min, with no leakage or any sign affecting strength.

The integrated block of hydraulic valve shall be subjected to pressure resistance test, with test pressure being 1.25 times of working pressure. The pressure holding time shall not be less than 10 min, with no leakage. Meanwhile, the performance test of opening/closing and pressure regulation shall be conducted.
The kerosene leakage test and opening/closing performance test shall be conducted on the sealing parts of hydraulic control check valve, liquid filling valve, gate valve, etc.

items: ① When designing single-action thin plate stamping hydraulic press, the standard shall be confirmed.

4.2.17  Baler Hydraulic Press

Metal baler hydraulic press and non-metal baler hydraulic press both have terms and definitions in GB/T 36484-2018 and JB/T 4174-2014. Metal baler hydraulic press is a hydraulic press used to compress scrap metal sheets, wire, etc. into blocks, while a hydraulic press used to compress metal chips into blocks is called a metal chip briquetting hydraulic press; non-metal baler hydraulic press is a hydraulic press used to compress non-metallic products, materials, or scrap into blocks.
1. Hydraulic Cotton Baler

GB/T 19820-2005 stipulates the structural form, product classification and basic parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules and marking, packaging and storage requirements of the MDY type hydraulic cotton baler (hereinafter referred to as the baler), which is applicable to the design, manufacture and quality inspection of the hydraulic cotton baler.

2) Performance and Quality of the Whole Machine.
① The nominal force of the baler shall comply with the provisions in Table 4-49, and the size of the bale and the mass of the cotton bale shall comply with the provisions of GB/T 6975-2013 "Cotton Packaging".

② If the main structural parts have welding processes, stress relief treatment shall be carried out. The stress welds of the main hydraulic cylinder body need to be subjected to non-destructive testing, and the results shall meet the Class II requirements in JB 4730 (already repealed).

④ The mechanical properties of the piston rod or piston of the main hydraulic cylinder: the tensile strength shall not be lower than 200MPa. The tolerance of metal cutting processing shall not be lower than 9-level precision, the cylindricity tolerance shall not be lower than 9-level precision, and the surface roughness value shall not be greater than Ra0.8μm.
⑤ The surface of the piston rod or plunger of the main hydraulic cylinder should be treated for wear resistance.

4) Assembly quality.

items: Parts entering the assembly (including purchased parts and outsourced parts) shall be inspected and qualified before assembly.
Parts should be cleaned and washed before assembly, without burrs, flash, chips, or weld slag. Parts should not be bumped or scratched during assembly.
The diagonal tolerance of the cross-section of the box shall be less than or equal to 5mm.
The symmetry of the piston rod or plunger of the main hydraulic cylinder to the axis of the inner wall of the box in the full stroke shall be less than or equal to 6mm.
The perpendicularity of the axis of the piston rod or plunger of the main hydraulic cylinder to the pressure beam in the full stroke shall be less than or equal to 1.5/1000.

The installation of hydraulic components and pipelines should prevent the sealing elements from being scratched, ensure no external leakage, and the exposed pipelines should be arranged neatly and firmly.
The electrical system should have a reliable grounding device, and the insulation resistance of components should not be less than 1MΩ.
The laying of electrical lines should be neat, beautiful, and reliable.

sections.text: 5) Appearance quality.

items: The outer surface of the whole machine should be flat, without burrs, flash, or weld slag.
The exposed machined surfaces of parts should be treated for rust prevention.

sections.text: 6) Painting quality.

items: Before painting, the rust, oxide scale, weld slag, and dirt on the surface of all steel parts that need to be painted should be removed.
The coating should be smooth, uniform, without wrinkles, bubbles, bottom exposure, obvious flow marks, and other defects.
The color of the topcoat should be consistent in the same area.

sections.text: (3) Test method.

items: No-load test. After the baler is installed and adjusted according to the instruction manual, a no-load test is conducted. The running time should not be less than 20min. After reaching the normal working requirements, check the provisions in Table 4-50.

items: Hydraulic system inspection. The main hydraulic system is subjected to a pressure test at 1.25 times the rated pressure, with no abnormal conditions.
Use a thermometer to measure the oil temperature before starting up and 8h after the baler is working normally in the oil tank.

Overload test and deflection inspection of the pressure beam. The overload test and the deflection inspection of the pressure beam are carried out synchronously. sections.text: Explanation:

items: In Table 8 of GB/T 19820-2005, the technical requirements for the processing quality of main parts (such as the hole of the main pressure cylinder or the hole of the cylinder guide sleeve, the plunger or piston of the main pressure cylinder) are given. However, requirements such as "the processing size tolerance value of the main pressure cylinder hole or the cylinder guide sleeve hole is not lower than IT10 precision, the roundness tolerance value is not lower than IT10 precision, and the surface roughness value Ra is not greater than 1.6μm" are the lowest requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their parts that can be seen in current standards. Whether they are appropriate remains to be discussed.

It is debatable to determine "the main hydraulic system is subjected to a pressure test at 1.25 times the rated pressure" and "the deflection inspection of the pressure beam (overload test) is carried out at 1.25 times the rated pressure" as one pressure value, but it can be referred to for the design and manufacture of hydraulic cylinders for hydraulic presses.

sections.text: 2. Metal baler hydraulic press
In JB/T 8494.2-2012, the metal baler hydraulic press is specified.

Technical Requirements, Inspection or Testing Methods, Inspection Rules, Marking, Packaging, Transportation and Storage, Applicable to Various Types of Light and Thin Production and Living Waste Steel, Various Types of Plastic Strong Non-Ferrous Metals (Such as Aluminum Alloy, Copper Material) Compression Metal Compression Hydraulic Press (hereinafter referred to as the compressor).
(1) Technical Requirements
1) General Requirements

items: The compressor should meet the provisions of JB/T 1829—1997 (2014) and JB/T 8494.2—2012 standards, and be manufactured according to the drawings and technical documents approved by the prescribed procedures.

The compressor should have sufficient rigidity, and should not have any damage or permanent deformation after overload test, and the deflection of the press beam under pressure should not be greater than 1/600.

The density of the compressed blocks of the compressor should meet the provisions of GB/T 4223—2017 "Scrap Steel", and the density of the compressed blocks based on steel material should be 1200~2500kg/m³. If the user has special requirements, it can be negotiated with the manufacturer.

The parameters of the compressor should meet the provisions of the technical documents. If the user has special requirements for the nominal compression force, it can be customized by negotiating with the manufacturer.

The random technical documents of the compressor should include the product's quality certificate, packing list and instruction manual. The content of the instruction manual should meet the provisions of GB/T 9969.

sections.text: 2) Supporting Equipment

items: When the compressor leaves the factory, it should ensure its integrity, and be equipped with special accessories, spare parts and wearing parts specified in the technical documents. Special accessories are determined by the user and the manufacturer, or supplied with the machine or ordered separately.

The manufacturer should ensure that the purchased parts of the compressor (such as hydraulic, electrical components) meet the standards, and should be accompanied by the producer's qualification certificate before use, and must be installed on the main machine and tested at the same time.

sections.text: 3) Safety

items: The compressor should have reliable safety protection devices, and meet the provisions of JB 3915 (has been abolished).
The operating mechanism of the compressor should be safe and reliable, and there should be no continuous action of the next cycle when the compressor performs a single cycle action.
The cover of the compressor should have measures to prevent automatic falling.

After the emergency stop of the compressor, the inertial descent value of the cover should be calculated based on the inertial extension amount of the piston rod of the pushing cylinder, and should not exceed 20mm within 3min.
The operating force of the hydraulic system of the compressor should meet the provisions of GB/T 3766.
The safety and protection of the electrical equipment of the compressor should meet the provisions of GB 5226.1.

sections.text: 4) Castings, Forgings, Welded Parts

items: Cast iron parts, cast steel parts, forgings, welded parts and non-ferrous metal parts should meet the provisions of the technical documents. Gray cast iron should meet the provisions of JB/T 5775, and welded parts should meet the provisions of JB/T 8609. For defects in castings, forgings and welded parts, repairs are allowed according to the provisions of the technical documents under the condition of ensuring the use requirements and appearance quality.
Important castings, forgings and welded parts of the compressor should be subjected to stress relief treatment.
The wear-resistant measures should be taken for the wear-resistant plate in the high-pressure chamber and the wear-resistant plate of the press head.

sections.text: 5) Processing

items: The processing quality of the parts of the compressor should meet the requirements of the design drawings and process specifications; the processed surfaces should not have burrs, spots and other mechanical damage, and all sharp corners should be blunted except for special provisions.
For cutting processing dimensions without dimensional tolerance requirements marked on the drawings, the limit deviation should meet the provisions of the technical documents.

The processing precision of the inner diameter of the hydraulic cylinder, the main part of the compressor, should reach H9 or above; the processing precision of the outer circle of the piston rod should reach f8 or above.

sections.text: 6) Assembly

items: The compressor should be assembled according to the assembly process specifications, and parts such as gaskets and sleeves not specified on the drawings are not allowed to be installed.
All supporting parts (including purchased and outsourced parts) should meet the provisions of the technical documents.

The bonding surfaces of the tie rod nuts of the machine body, the fixing and bonding surfaces of the hydraulic cylinder should be well bonded. A 0.05mm feeler gauge is used for inspection, and only local insertion is allowed. The insertion depth should generally not exceed 20% of the radial bonding width, and the cumulative length of the insertable parts should generally not exceed 10% of the circumference that can be inspected.

The sum of the gaps between the side guard plates of the press heads at all levels of the compressor and the guard plate of the compression chamber should meet the provisions in Table 1 of JB/T 8494.2—2012.
Anti-rust and decontamination treatments should be carried out on the pipeline channels and oil tank surfaces of the hydraulic system and cooling system before assembly.
All pipelines, pipe joints, flanges and other fixed connections, sealing parts should be reliably connected, well sealed, and should not have leakage.

sections.text: 7) Hydraulic System and Lubrication System

items: The hydraulic system of the compressor should meet the provisions of GB/T 3766 and JB/T 3818.
The working pressure of the hydraulic system should generally not be greater than 20MPa.
The hydraulic transmission parts should not have crawling, vibration, stagnation and significant impact phenomena in various ranges.
A filter should be installed in the hydraulic system.
The cleanliness of the hydraulic system should meet the provisions of JB/T 9954.
The compressor should have a lubrication device to ensure the lubrication of each rotating part. The lubrication pipelines and lubrication points should be consistent with the product manual.

sections.text: 8) Electrical System
The electrical system of the compressor should meet the provisions of GB 5226.1.
9) Appearance

items: There should be no protrusions, depressions, roughness and other damage on the outer surface of the compressor that are not specified on the drawings.
The joints of the base, side frame, front frame, rear frame, door beam, and support beam should be flat, and there should be no obvious gaps and misalignments.

3. Technical conditions for heavy-duty hydraulic scrap metal balers

JB/T 11394-2013 stipulates the structural types and main technical parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection and inspection rules, painting, packaging, storage and transportation, and signs for heavy-duty hydraulic scrap metal balers (hereinafter referred to as balers), applicable to heavy-duty hydraulic scrap metal balers with a main (or final-stage) extrusion force of 8000-20000 kN. (1) Structural types and main technical parameters 1) Structural type. An automatic production equipment that completes the extrusion and baling of scrap metal into blocks (cubic or rectangular) composed of body, multi-stage hydraulic cylinders and pressing heads, hydraulic system, pipeline system, automatic lubrication system, hydraulic oil heating and cooling system, and electrical control system. It adopts three-way extrusion method, and the density of the produced scrap steel bales is 2.5-3.5 t/m³, which should comply with the provisions of Class I scrap steel baling blocks in GB/T 4223-2017 (Scrap Steel). 2) Machine model. The baler model is executed according to the product classification spectrum of national forging machinery. 3) Main technical parameters are shown in Table 4-53.
