4.4.3 Six-roll Cold Rolling Mill

The six-roll mill is a mill with six horizontal rolls arranged vertically in the same window, with two supporting rolls arranged on the left and right of the upper and lower work rolls, mainly used for rolling non-ferrous metal plates and cold-rolled steel strips. JB/T 11593-2013 "Six-roll Cold Rolling Mill" stipulates the structural types, basic parameters, technical conditions, test methods, inspection and packaging of six-roll cold rolling mills, applicable to six-roll cold rolling mills with automatic thickness control, intermediate roll lateral movement, and hydraulic roll bending (hereinafter referred to as six-roll mills).
1. Structural Type and Basic Parameters

(1) Structural Type
The six-roll mill is a fully hydraulic mill, with a closed frame structure frame. The intermediate roll can be driven laterally by a hydraulic cylinder, and the work roll has positive and negative bending roll devices, while the intermediate roll has a positive bending roll device. The rolling line elevation adjustment adopts a worm gear pair electric pressure reduction or a hydraulic cylinder (or hydraulic motor) driven wedge adjustment mechanism; It is a six-roll mill with hydraulic pressure reduction, automatic thickness AGC system, tension closed-loop and speed closed-loop control (see Figure 1 in JB/T 11593-2013).

4.5.1  Hydraulic System for Metal Cutting Machine Tools

GB/T 23572—2009 "General Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Systems of Metal Cutting Machine Tools" stipulates the technical requirements, assembly requirements, safety requirements, test methods, inspection rules and other requirements for hydraulic systems of metal machine tools. It is applicable to hydraulic transmission and control systems of metal cutting machine tools that use hydraulic oil as the working medium.
1. Technical Requirements

items: Basic Requirements: The design, manufacture and use of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766, and should ensure long service life of the equipment and convenient maintenance.

Hydraulic Components and Parts: Hydraulic components used in the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 7935, and other parts should comply with the requirements of the corresponding standards.

Hydraulic Oil: 1) The hydraulic oil used in the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766 and GB 7632—1987 "Selection and Use of Lubricants for Machine Tools". The hydraulic system should be equipped with a liquid filter device in a position convenient for replacement and maintenance. The oil should be fully filtered before being injected into the hydraulic system oil tank. 2) The oil used in the hydraulic system and the oil used in the guide rail or other mechanical parts should be separated from each other.

Pipelines, Joints and Channels: 1) The material of the pipe joints in the hydraulic system is generally metal. The material of the pipeline is generally metal, oil-resistant rubber braided hose, resin high-pressure hose and other materials compatible with the working medium. The pipe wall should be able to work normally when subjected to 1.5 times the maximum working pressure of the system. 2) There should be no leakage at all joints and exposed joints of the hydraulic system. Sealing packing or sealing glue can be used at joints and other joints, but miscellaneous materials such as hemp and silk should not be used instead. 3) The bent part of the oil pipe should be smooth, and there should be no obvious dents or bias (flattening). The ratio of the short and long axes should not be less than 0.75. 4) Before assembly, the joints, pipelines, channels (including cast core holes, machined holes, etc.) and oil tanks of the hydraulic system should be cleaned.

sections.text: 5) The oil channels of the hydraulic system should have sufficient flow area.

6) The pipeline should be set safely and reasonably, and the arrangement should be neat, which is convenient for adjusting, repairing and replacing components. In order to avoid vibration and collision of the pipeline, there should be a certain gap between the pipelines. When the pipelines are long or the pipelines vibrate and collide, resulting in noise, pipe clamps should be used for fixing. The distance between the pipe clamps can refer to the value in Table 4-166.

sections.caption: Table 4-166  Distance Between Pipe Clamps
headers: Distance between pipe clamps L (Unit: mm)

items: 7) The pipe clamp should not be welded to the pipe, nor should it damage the pipeline.
8) Generally, the pipeline should not be used to support components or support the oil circuit board.

9) The hose is generally used between movable parts and is convenient for replacing parts, suppressing the transmission of mechanical vibration or noise. Its length should be as short as possible to avoid severe bending and deformation of the hose during equipment operation. If necessary, a hose protection device should be installed.
10) When the pipeline needs to be suspended and crossed, its height should be convenient for maintenance and ensure the safety of personnel, and the support should be reliable.
11) The pipeline should be marked. Pressure pipelines, control pipelines, oil return and leakage pipelines should use different signs.
12) There should be signs at both ends of the pipeline connection to facilitate recovery after disassembly.

13) Hydraulic System Oil Tank: 1) The nominal volume of the oil tank of the hydraulic system should comply with JB/T 7938—2010 "Hydraulic Pump Station Oil Tank Nominal Volume Series" (already abolished). 2) During the entire working cycle, the oil level in the oil tank should be kept at a safe working height. The oil tank should have sufficient space to allow thermal expansion of the oil and separation of air. Under normal circumstances, the oil tank should be able to accommodate all the oil returned from the system. Spills or leaks of contaminated oil should be prevented from flowing directly back into the oil tank. 3) Where conditions permit, the bottom of the hydraulic station can be raised 150 mm above the installation surface to facilitate handling, oil discharge and heat dissipation. 4) The detachable cover plate should be able to prevent impurities from entering the oil tank in its structure. 5) Use baffles or other measures to separate the return oil from the inlet of the hydraulic pump. The adopted measures should not hinder the cleaning of the oil tank. 6) The shape of the bottom of the oil tank should allow the hydraulic oil to be drained. The oil tank should be equipped with an oil drain hole, a sampling hole, an oil filling port and a cleaning port. The oil drain hole should be located at the lowest position of the bottom of the oil tank. The sampling hole can also be set on the working pipeline. The oil tank should be equipped with one or more cleaning ports to clean the entire interior of the oil tank.

sections.text: 7) Tubes passing through the tank top cover should be sealed, and the terminal of the return oil line should be below the lowest liquid level of the tank.
8) A level gauge should be installed next to the oil filling port, and an air filter should be provided on the upper part of the vented tank.

9) The tank material should be compatible with the oil. For tanks made of ordinary steel plates, the inner surface can be treated with methods such as phosphating after pickling, shot peening or sandblasting followed by spraying, which have excellent chemical and physical stability, or it can be coated with a rust-proof coating that does not peel off and is compatible with the oil.
(6) Pressure Gauge

items: Pressure gauges installed in hydraulic systems should be installed in conspicuous and easily observable positions.
The range of the pressure gauge should be 1.5 to 2 times the pressure being tested.
Pressure gauges should generally be equipped with a pressure relief device, or use shock-resistant pressure gauges with dampers added externally.
When measuring multiple pressures, a multi-point measurement device consisting of one pressure gauge and one selector valve can be used.

sections.text: 2. Assembly Requirements

items: The interfaces between the separated parts of the hydraulic system pipeline and the host should be numbered and marked, and the pipeline numbering, marking, and relevant technical documents should be consistent.

When installing the hydraulic pump, ensure that the pump shaft is concentric with the drive motor transmission shaft. For rigid coupling, the concentricity tolerance is φ0.05 mm; for flexible coupling, the concentricity tolerance is φ0.1 mm.
Other assembly and trial operation requirements should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766.

sections.text: 3. Safety Requirements

items: The safety requirements for the design, manufacture, and use of hydraulic systems should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3766.

The action sequence between moving parts should be equipped with interlocking safety devices. When using a static pressure device, to ensure that the hydraulic system or other mechanical movements can only be driven after establishing static pressure, interlocking safety devices should generally also be provided.
When the hydraulic system of the machine tool loses normal pressure and may cause unsafe factors, necessary alarm devices, indication signals, and protective measures should be set in the system.
When the connection between the hydraulic pump and the drive motor is exposed, a safety guard should be installed.

When the machine tool is stopped, the hydraulic circuit equipped with an accumulator should be able to automatically release the pressure in the accumulator, or reliably isolate the circuit from the accumulator.

When the machine tool is stopped, if the hydraulic circuit still needs to use the pressurized oil in the accumulator to work, safety usage instructions should be marked on the accumulator or in a conspicuous place near the accumulator, including the words "Caution, Pressure Vessel".
All components or equipment with a mass exceeding 15 kg should be easily liftable or equipped with lifting devices.

sections.text: 4. Test Methods

items: Preparations Before the Test: Before the test, the hydraulic system should be circulated and filtered. During circulating filtration, servo valves, proportional valves, accumulators, etc. in the hydraulic system should be short-circuited.

Performance Test: Considering operability, the performance test of the hydraulic system is conducted within the range of the hydraulic pump station. The test items, test methods, and technical requirements are shown in Tables 4-167 to 4-170.

1) The hydraulic pump station operates in an unloaded state, adjust the pressure to 0.1-0.2 MPa, and conduct the no-load test after there are no abnormal sounds.
2) No-load test: Cooperate with electrical equipment, appropriately adjust the pressure, and check the correctness of the action sequence and operation of each hydraulic component.

1) The installation and connection of components and auxiliary components in the hydraulic pump station should comply with the design requirements.
2) The working cycle and action sequence should comply with the design requirements.

1) Gradually increase the pressure to the rated load, and the test time should not be less than 0.5 h.
2) Check the rated pressure, rated flow, and pressure fluctuation value.

1) The rated pressure and rated flow should comply with the design requirements (tolerance value less than 5%).
2) The pressure fluctuation should be within ±0.2 MPa.

Apply a pressure resistance test pressure to the hydraulic pump station (excluding components with limited test pressure in the design); the pressure resistance test pressure is 1.5 times the rated pressure of the hydraulic pump station (1.25 times when the rated pressure > 16 MPa); increase the pressure uniformly, and after reaching the pressure resistance test pressure, maintain it for 5 min.
No external leakage or other abnormal phenomena should occur.

When operating at rated load, use a sound level meter to measure at 4 points on a sphere with a radius of 1 m from the hydraulic pump station (in different directions); the measurement method should comply with the provisions of GB/T 16769-2008 (already repealed).

sections.text: 4.5.2 Hydraulic Slideway for Modular Machine Tool

In JB/T 9885-2013 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Slideway for Modular Machine Tool", manufacturing and acceptance requirements for hydraulic slideway for modular machine tool are specified, applicable to hydraulic slideway for modular machine tool with nominal size of 100-800mm (including long table type, hereinafter referred to as hydraulic slideway or slideway).
1. General Requirements

When accepting slideway according to JB/T 9885-2013 standard, inspection should also be conducted for other acceptance items not specifically defined in JB/T 9885-2013 standard for GB/T 9061-2006 "General Technical Conditions for Metal Cutting Machine Tools", GB/T 25373-2010 "General Technical Conditions for Assembly of Metal Cutting Machine Tools", GB/T 25376-2010 "General Technical Conditions for Mechanical Processing Parts of Metal Cutting Machine Tools", JB/T 1534-2006 "General Technical Conditions for Modular Machine Tools" and other standards.
2. Random Accessories
1) Manufacturer should provide easily damaged seals, the quantity of accessories is 2 times the usage number of this slideway.
2) Finished parts should be equipped with fastening screws and positioning pins for installation.
Note: Seals and standard parts should generally be marked with corresponding markings or specifications.
3. Manufacturing Quality
(1) General Requirements

items: The contact dimensions of the hydraulic slide should comply with GB/T3668.4-1983 "Standard Parts for Modular Machine Tools - Slide Dimensions". For long table type hydraulic slides, the contact dimensions should comply with JB/T2462.8-2017 "Standard Parts for Modular Machine Tools - Part 8: Slides (Long Table Type) - Parameters and Dimensions" (JB/T2462.8-1999 has been superseded) and the relevant technical documents.
The technical conditions for gray cast iron parts should comply with JB/T3997-2011.
After passing the test, all exposed oil ports on the parts should be sealed with oil-resistant plugs (paper, cotton yarn, wooden plugs and other debris are prohibited).

sections.text: Note: GB/T3668.4-1983 specifies the interchangeability dimensions for modular machine tool slides.
(2) Slide Saddle Guide Rail

The performance of the coating material or plastic guide rail plate on the slide saddle guide rail should comply with JB/T3578-2007 "Technical Specifications for Epoxy Coating Materials for Sliding Guide Rails". The performance and requirements of the coated guide rail should comply with JB/T3579-2007 "General Technical Conditions for Epoxy Coated Sliding Guide Rails".
(3) Slide Base Guide Rail
The straightness of the upper surface of the slide base guide rail in the vertical plane along its length should not be concave.
(4) Feed Hydraulic Cylinder
1) Test Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder
The hydraulic cylinder must be tested separately on the corresponding test bench and should comply with the relevant test conditions.
2) Test Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder

items: Test Equipment Oil (Liquid) should meet the following requirements: a. Oil Temperature: During the test, the temperature of the oil entering the feed hydraulic cylinder being tested should be maintained within the range of 50°C±5°C; b. Viscosity: The kinematic viscosity of the oil should be 17-23 mm²/s; c. Filtration Accuracy: Should not be lower than 50μm; d. The oil should have anti-rust capability.

Pressure Gauge for Test should meet the following requirements: a. Accuracy: The error during the test should be less than ±1.5%; b. Range: The pressure gauge for the test is a direct-reading pressure gauge, and its range should be 140%-200% of the test pressure.

Installation Position: When measuring pressure fluctuations, the inner diameter of the pressure gauge connecting pipe should be 4 mm, and the length should be less than 300 mm. It should be connected to the working pipe at a distance of about 10d (d is the inner diameter of the working pipe) from the inlet of the component being tested and about 30d from the outlet (should not be installed at bends). When measuring pressure fluctuations, the pressure gauge should not be equipped with a damper.

sections.text: 3) Test Items for Hydraulic Cylinder. ① Trial Operation and Stroke Measurement. Install the hydraulic cylinder to be tested on the corresponding test bench. Under no-load conditions, perform reciprocating motion for 7 full strokes. There should be no abnormal phenomena such as external leakage or impact. At the same time, stop the piston of the hydraulic cylinder at both ends of the stroke and measure the length of the full stroke, which should comply with the design requirements.

② Detection of Resistance to Piston and Piston Rod Movement. With no load on the piston rod, introduce pressure oil into the advance chamber of the hydraulic cylinder to make the piston rod move at a certain feed speed, and measure the required pressure, which should not exceed the data listed in Table 4-171.

sections.text: Note: 1. The values in the table are only applicable to seals in the form of O, U, X, Y. 2. The pressures referred to in the table are gauge pressures.

③ Internal Leakage Test. Introduce pressure oil into the advance chamber of the hydraulic cylinder, unscrew the pipe joint at the retract chamber, and turn the external leakage port upward. Gradually increase the pressure of the incoming oil to 6.3 MPa (the pressure in the advance chamber of the hydraulic cylinder for long table type slides should reach 4 MPa), maintain the pressure for 30 s, and then measure the oil flow at the external leakage port as the leakage per minute. The piston should stop at two positions of the hydraulic cylinder (the following positions).

First Position: The piston is located in the middle of the hydraulic cylinder. Second Position: The piston is located 60 mm from the end cover of the retract chamber (long table type slides do not perform this position test).
The internal leakage of the hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the values listed in Table 4-172.

sections.caption: Table 4-172 Internal Leakage of Hydraulic Cylinder

sections.text: ④ External Leakage Test. Make the piston move at a certain speed, and perform reciprocating motion for more than 30 full strokes. At this time, there should be no oil leakage at the pipe joints and seal of the hydraulic cylinder cover, and the external leakage at the seal between the piston rod and the cylinder cover should not form droplets.

The test should be conducted separately under pressures of 0.5 MPa and 6.3 MPa in the retract chamber of the hydraulic cylinder; for the hydraulic cylinder of long table slides, the test should be conducted separately under pressures of 0.5 MPa and 4 MPa in the advance chamber.

⑤ Stability Test of Piston Rod Movement. With no load on the piston rod, introduce pressure oil into the advance chamber of the hydraulic cylinder to make the piston rod move at the minimum feed speed specified for the component. At this time, the movement of the piston rod should be stable. Touch the end of the piston rod with a dial indicator to check the stability of the piston rod's movement.

4. No-load Running Test
1) The hydraulic system matched with the slide should comply with GB/T 23572-2009 requirements.

2) The slide should be placed on the corresponding test bench and run for no less than 2h no-load trial operation. During this period, all specified working procedures must be completed. The actions should be sensitive and reliable, and all operating handle transitions should be accurate, smooth, and without obvious impact phenomena.

3) The maximum stroke length, fast advance speed, fast return speed, and working feed speed range of the slide should all comply with the provisions of the slide design. Within the working feed speed range, the movement of the slide saddle should be smooth without crawling.
5. Load Test

1) Perform a load test according to the specified maximum feed force to check the stability of the feed force. Measure using a hydraulic cylinder and force gauge on the centerline of the front end of the slide saddle, at a distance of B/2 (B is the width of the slide saddle) from the working surface.

2) Adjust the feed speed of the slide saddle to the minimum working feed speed to test the change in feed speed under maximum feed force and no-load conditions. The change rate (see formula (4-11)) should not exceed ±15%. Measure continuously 30 times in 10 cycles. During this time, the feed of the slide saddle should be smooth. Use a dial indicator to check the movement of the slide saddle by touching the front face of the slide saddle. The pointer should rotate smoothly, and the fluctuation should not exceed 0.01mm.
Where: δ — feed speed variation rate; S₀ — average feed speed without load, unit: mm/min; S — limiting feed speed under specified load, unit: mm/min.
Other instruments with detection effects not lower than the dial indicator can be used for measurement.

3) Under a hydraulic system pressure of 7MPa (4MPa for long slide surfaces) and at a certain feed speed, let the slide saddle rest against a fixed stop for 5min. There should be no oil leakage at the hydraulic pipe joints, various valve connections, or hydraulic cylinder seals. There should be no pressure drop phenomenon in the hydraulic system.

The accuracy of the hydraulic slide should be tested according to JB/T 9889-2013 "Accuracy Test for Slide of Modular Machine Tools" and the test results should be recorded in the product quality certificate.
4.5.3  Machine Tool (High Speed) Rotary Hydraulic Cylinder

In the typical structure of hydraulic cylinders in reference [15], general hydraulic cylinder typical structures, special-purpose hydraulic cylinder typical structures, and piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinder typical structures (including gear-rack rotating hydraulic cylinders, parallel piston gear-rack hydraulic cylinders, roller rotating hydraulic cylinders, ball screw rotating hydraulic cylinders, and single screw rotating hydraulic cylinders) are listed respectively. It is pointed out that: "Piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders are a combination of hydraulic cylinders and rotating mechanisms. The rotating mechanism is usually a gear-rack pair or a screw-nut pair. This is an element that lies between hydraulic cylinders and hydraulic motors and possesses the function of oscillating motors. Because its output is torque, the rotation angle is a limited ±θ° oscillating angle."

According to the definition of cylinders or hydraulic cylinders, some hydraulic cylinders listed in the typical structures of piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders in reference [15] do not belong to hydraulic cylinders, but some belong to combined hydraulic cylinders, such as gear-rack rotating hydraulic cylinders and parallel piston gear-rack hydraulic cylinders.

The machine tool rotating hydraulic cylinders listed in this section differ in principle from the typical structures of piston-type rotating hydraulic cylinders listed in reference [15]. The rotational motion between the cylinder body and piston of these hydraulic cylinders is driven by an external force rather than produced by the hydraulic cylinder itself.

sections.text: (3) Test Method
1) Test Conditions
① The hydraulic accumulator can be installed on the machine tool, or it can be tested on a test bench.
② During the test, the initial oil temperature should be within the range of 5 to 40°C.
③ The hydraulic oil should preferably use hydraulic oil with ISO viscosity grade 32 or 46 in GB/T 3141—1994.
④ The hydraulic oil should have anti-wear, anti-foaming, and anti-rust capabilities.
⑤ The hydraulic system should be equipped with a filter with a filtering accuracy of 20μm.
⑥ The range of the pressure gauge should not be less than 1.5 times the maximum working pressure.
⑦ The maximum residual unbalance of the connecting device used for balance testing shall not be greater than 20% of the maximum allowable residual unbalance of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested.

2) Starting pressure. When the oil temperature is not lower than 25°C, the pressure when the piston of the hydraulic cylinder starts to move should comply with the provisions of (2)3). After the piston reciprocates several times, it should move smoothly and without crawling throughout the entire stroke.

3) Temperature rise. When the hydraulic cylinder runs continuously and reaches thermal equilibrium (thermal equilibrium refers to the state where the temperature rise of the hydraulic cylinder changes no more than 1°C within 10 minutes), measure the external surface temperature of the oil distribution valve body of the hydraulic cylinder, which should comply with the provisions of (2)4).

4) Leakage. When the pressure is 75% of the maximum working pressure and the oil temperature is 50°C, the leakage per minute measured with a measuring cup from the return oil port should comply with the provisions of (2)5).

5) Maximum thrust and maximum tension. Under static conditions and maximum working pressure, measure the maximum thrust and maximum tension of the hydraulic cylinder with a force gauge, which should comply with the provisions of (2)7). Alternatively, it can be calculated according to the calculation method given below.
The maximum thrust of the hydraulic cylinder is calculated according to formula (4-12).
FTmax = (pmax - 0.25) × ST    (4-12)
Where FTmax — maximum thrust, in N; pmax — maximum working pressure, in MPa; ST — effective area of the piston push side, in mm².
The maximum tension of the hydraulic cylinder is calculated according to formula (4-13).
FLmax = (pmax - 0.25) × SL    (4-13)
Where FLmax — maximum tension, in N; pmax — maximum working pressure, in MPa; SL — effective area of the piston pull side, in mm².

6) Balance. Before conducting the dynamic balance test of the hydraulic cylinder, the installation accuracy of the positioning surface of the hydraulic cylinder of the connecting device should be pre-tested to ensure that the radial and axial circular runouts do not exceed 0.01 mm.

When the hydraulic cylinder undergoes a dynamic balance test, remove the non-rotating parts such as the oil distribution valve at the rear end of the hydraulic cylinder, and install the hydraulic cylinder on the spindle of the testing machine through the connecting device.

The residual unbalance amount measured during the dynamic balance test of the hydraulic cylinder shall be calculated according to the requirements of GB/T 9239.1—2006 to obtain the dynamic balance quality grade, which should comply with the provisions of (2)8).
7) Running test.

① The hydraulic cylinder should run continuously at low, medium, and high speeds under the maximum working pressure. During operation, no less than 10 speed levels should be selected, and each speed level should not be less than 2 minutes.
② Under the maximum working pressure, run continuously at the limit speed for 1 hour, which should comply with the provisions of (2)9).
Connect the piston rod to a force gauge to observe the changes in the thrust and tension of the hydraulic cylinder. The thrust and tension should remain unchanged.
(4) Inspection
1) The product should be inspected and qualified by the inspection department before leaving the factory.
2) The inspection items for leaving the factory include balance, operation, accuracy inspection, and marking content.
(5) Marking, packaging, and accompanying documents
1) Marking. The product should have permanent marking, with clear and neat handwriting, including the following content:

items: ① Name or trademark of the manufacturer.
② Model or factory number.
③ Maximum working pressure.
④ Maximum speed.

sections.text: 2) Packaging. The product packaging should comply with the provisions of JB/T 3207—2005.
3) Accompanying documents

items: ① When the product leaves the factory, it should provide accompanying documents, including product instruction manual, quality certificate, and packing list.
② The accompanying documents should comply with the provisions of JB/T 9935—2011.

items: The external surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be smooth and aesthetically pleasing, without sharp edges, burrs, pores, and other defects. The unprocessed surface should be coated for protection.

sections.text: 2) Maximum working pressure p_max: The maximum working pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should not be less than 4.0 MPa.

7) Maximum thrust F_Tmax and maximum pull F_Lmax: The manufacturer should provide the maximum thrust and maximum pull at the maximum working pressure.
8) Balance: The balance quality grade of the hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than G2.5.

9) Operation: During operation, the valve body of the distributing valve should rotate flexibly without any jamming. There should be no leakage at all sealing parts, and the hydraulic cylinder should not exhibit any abnormal phenomena such as shaft seizing.
10) Accuracy inspection.
① General description

items: When using JB/T13101-2017, the accuracy inspection method and the accuracy of inspection tools should comply with the provisions of GB/T17421.1-1998.

The accuracy inspections of G1 and G2 can be performed in any order according to the principle of convenience.
The units of linear dimensions and tolerances in the accuracy inspection are mm.

② Accuracy inspection. The radial circular runout inspection of the hydraulic cylinder body is shown in Table 4-183. The radial runout inspection of the valve body or return cover of the hydraulic cylinder is shown in Table 4-184.

sections.text: 11) Pressure retention performance: When the hydraulic system is in an abnormal state and the oil supply pressure is suddenly interrupted, and the pressure in the hydraulic cylinder can still be maintained at more than 85% of the original pressure after 1 minute of interruption.

12) Pressure relief performance: When the hydraulic system is in an abnormal state and the oil supply pressure reaches 1.05 times the maximum working pressure, the relief valve should open to relieve pressure.

items: The hydraulic cylinder can be installed on the machine tool or tested on a test bench.

④ The hydraulic oil should have anti-wear, anti-foaming, and anti-rust capabilities.
⑤ The hydraulic system should be equipped with a filter with a filtering accuracy of 20μm.
⑥ The pressure gauge range should not be less than 1.5 times the maximum operating pressure.
⑦ For the connecting device used for balance inspection, the maximum residual unbalance should not exceed 20% of the maximum allowable residual unbalance of the hydraulic cylinder being tested.

2) Starting pressure. When the oil temperature is not lower than 25°C, test the pressure when the hydraulic cylinder piston starts to move. After reciprocating the piston several times, it should move smoothly throughout the entire stroke without crawling.
3) Temperature rise. Operate the hydraulic cylinder continuously until thermal equilibrium is reached (thermal equilibrium means the temperature rise of the hydraulic cylinder within 10 minutes is not greater than 1°C). Then measure the temperature of the external surface of the valve body, which should meet the requirements.

4) Oil leakage. Under a pressure of 75% of the maximum operating pressure, operate the hydraulic cylinder continuously at 75% of the highest speed until the oil temperature reaches 50°C. Measure the oil leakage per minute using a measuring cup and timer from the return oil port, which should meet the requirements.
5) Maximum thrust and maximum pull force. Under static conditions and maximum operating pressure, measure the maximum thrust and maximum pull force of the hydraulic cylinder using a force gauge, which should meet the requirements. The approximate calculation methods for maximum thrust and maximum pull force are as follows:
FTmax = (pmax - 0.25) × ST  (4-14)
FLmax = (pmax - 0.25) × SL  (4-15)
6) Balance

① Before performing dynamic balance testing on the hydraulic cylinder, pre-inspect the installation positioning accuracy of the positioning surface of the connecting device to ensure that the radial runout and axial runout do not exceed 0.01mm.
② When performing dynamic balance testing on the hydraulic cylinder, remove the non-rotating parts such as the valve body at the rear end of the hydraulic cylinder, and install the hydraulic cylinder on the spindle of the testing machine through the connecting device.
③ Calculate the dynamic balance quality grade according to the requirements of GB/T 9239.1—2006 based on the measured residual unbalance during the dynamic balance test of the hydraulic cylinder, which should meet the requirements.
7) Operation test. Operate the hydraulic cylinder continuously for 1 hour at low, medium, and high speeds under maximum operating pressure, with the highest speed operation not less than 30min, which should meet the requirements.
8) Pressure retention performance. The test can be conducted using any of the following methods, and the results should meet the requirements.
① Adjust the system pressure to the maximum operating pressure, operate the hydraulic cylinder at the highest speed normally, then cut off the oil circuit. After 1min, observe the change in the chuck clamping force, which should not be less than 85% of the original clamping force.
② Connect a force gauge to the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, adjust the system pressure to the maximum operating pressure, operate the hydraulic cylinder at the highest speed normally, then cut off the oil circuit. After 1min, observe the change in the force gauge, and the output thrust/pull force should not be less than 85% of the original thrust/pull force.
9) Pressure relief performance. The test can be conducted using any of the following methods, and the results should meet the requirements.
① When the system oil pressure reaches 1.05 times the maximum operating pressure, observe the change in the chuck clamping force, which should remain unchanged.
② Connect a force gauge to the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, observe the change in the thrust/pull force of the hydraulic cylinder, which should remain unchanged.
(4) Inspection
1) The product can only be shipped after passing inspection by the inspection department.
2) The inspection items before delivery include balance, operation, accuracy inspection, and
Content of markings.

items: Name or trademark of the manufacturer.
Model or serial number.
Maximum working pressure.
Maximum speed.

sections.text: 4.6 Hydraulic cylinders for mining machinery: design and selection criteria
4.6.1 Hydraulic parts for coal mining machinery

In MT/T 459—2007 'General technical conditions for hydraulic parts for coal mining machinery', the technical requirements, safety requirements, test requirements, markings and packaging for hydraulic components of coal mining machinery are stipulated, applicable to all kinds of hydraulic components (hereinafter referred to as 'components') for coal mining machinery using hydraulic oil (liquid) as the working medium, and also applicable to hydraulic auxiliary parts for coal mining machinery.
1. Technical requirements

items: Basic parameters, graphic symbols and installation and connection dimensions of the components shall generally comply with the provisions of the relevant national standards. However, when the main machine of coal mining machinery has special requirements, the basic parameters and installation and connection dimensions may also be determined according to the requirements of the main machine.

All parts shall be manufactured according to the prescribed drawings and technical documents, and their materials shall comply with the provisions of the drawings. The performance of materials shall comply with the provisions of the relevant standards. Materials may be replaced on condition that the product quality is not reduced.

The shell of the component shall be treated accordingly to eliminate internal stress. The shell shall be free of process defects affecting the use of the component and meet the strength requirements of the component. The surface of the shell shall be flat and smooth, and shall not have process defects affecting the appearance quality. The casting shall be cleared of sand, and there shall be no residue in the internal channels and cavities. The inspection of flaws shall be carried out for complex castings.

The components shall be assembled according to the provisions of the relevant product standards or technical documents. All parts and purchased parts shall be products inspected and qualified by the quality inspection department.

sections.text: 5) Parts shall be cleaned before assembly, and shall not contain any contaminants (such as iron filings, burrs, fibrous impurities, coal chips, coal ash, etc.).

6) During the assembly of the component, cotton yarn, paper and other fibrous materials that are easy to fall off shall not be used to wipe the inner cavity of the shell, the mating surfaces of the parts and the inlet and outlet flow channels.
7) During the assembly of the component, seals with defects and beyond the effective service life shall not be used.
8) Symbols indicating the function of the oil port shall be clearly marked near all oil connection ports of the component. Except for special provisions, the symbols of oil ports are as follows:

items: P — Pressure oil port
T — Return oil port
A, B — Working oil ports
L — Drain oil port
X, Y — Control oil ports

sections.text: 9) The coating of the exposed non-machined surface of the component shall be uniform with consistent color. No putty shall be applied for pretreatment before spraying.
10) After the component passes the factory inspection, sealing, dustproof and leakage prevention measures shall be taken for all oil ports.
2. Safety requirements

items: All kinds of light metal, light alloy materials and non-metallic materials shall comply with the relevant provisions of GB 3836.1—2000 (2010) 'Explosive atmospheres—Part 1: Equipment—General requirements'.
Explosion-proof components shall comply with the relevant requirements of GB 3836.2—2000 (2010) 'Explosive atmospheres—Part 2: Equipment protected by flameproof enclosures "d"'.
Intrinsically safe components shall comply with the relevant requirements in GB 3836.4—2000 (2010) 'Explosive atmospheres—Part 4: Equipment with type of protection "i"'.

Components with explosion-proof requirements shall be provided with 'product qualification certificate', 'explosion-proof certificate' issued by the national designated explosion-proof inspection station and 'mark certificate for coal mine products' issued by the authorized institution of the national safety production supervision department.

sections.text: The GB 3836—2000 series of standards have been abolished. The above-mentioned names of standards are the names of the current (2010 edition) standards, and some standards have been updated to the 2017 edition.
3. Test requirements

items: When the components are tested, the requirements for the accuracy grade of measurement, the system error of the measurement system, measurement, test oil and the test of special hydraulic components shall comply with the provisions of Chapter 5 of GB/T 7935—2005.

When the components are tested, they shall be tested according to their respective relevant standards and test reports shall be issued. Tests with measurement accuracy requirements of Class A and Class B shall be undertaken by the national (or provincial) hydraulic parts product quality supervision center, and tests with measurement accuracy requirements of Class C shall be undertaken by the test department of the component manufacturer.

sections.text: 4. Markings and packaging
1) A product nameplate shall be set in an obvious part of the component, and the content of the nameplate shall include:

① Product name, model, factory number.
② Main technical parameters.

2) For components with directional requirements (such as the rotation direction of hydraulic pumps, etc.), directional arrows or corresponding symbols should be clearly marked on the obvious parts of the component.
3) When components are packed at the factory, the following documents should be included:
① Certificate of conformity.
② Instruction manual (including component name, model, external drawing, installation and connection dimensions, structural diagram, main technical parameters, usage conditions and maintenance methods, as well as a parts list, etc.).
③ Packing list.
4) When packaging components, the specified accessories should be packaged together with the components and fixed inside the box.
5) For components with adjustment mechanisms, the adjustment spring should be in a relaxed state when packaging, and exposed parts such as threads and keyways should be protected.
6) The packaging should be firm and reliable, with measures to prevent vibration and moisture.
7) On the obvious position of the outer wall of the packaging box, the following contents should be clearly marked with text:
① Product name, model.

③ External dimensions of the packaging box (length, width, height).
④ Manufacturer name.
⑤ Packing date.
⑥ User name, address, and station name.
⑦ Transportation precautions or operation signs.
4.6.2 Hydraulic Cylinders for Mining Machinery

MT/T 900-2000 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders for Mining Machinery" specifies the scope and normative references.
1. Technical Requirements
(1) General Requirements
1) The inner diameter and piston rod diameter of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with GB/T 2348.
2) The stroke of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with GB 2349.
3) The thread type and dimensions of the piston rod should comply with GB 2350.
4) The groove dimensions and tolerances for piston and piston rod seals should comply with GB/T 2879, GB 2880 and GB/T 15242.3.
5) The dimensions and tolerances of support rings for pistons should comply with GB 6577 and GB/T 15242.4.
6) The groove type and dimensional tolerances for dust seals on piston rods should comply with GB/T 6578.
7) The installation type and dimensions of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with GB/T 9094.

8) The dimensions and installation dimensions of the end clevises on the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with GB/T 14036 and GB/T 14042.
(2) Minimum Starting Pressure
The (minimum) starting pressure of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 2-67.
(3) Internal Leakage
Under rated pressure, the internal leakage of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 1 of MT/T 900-2000, see Table 2-159 for details.
(4) Load Efficiency
Under rated pressure, the load efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder should not be less than 90% (qualified products ≥90%, first-class products ≥92%).
(5) Pressure Resistance Performance
No abnormal phenomena should occur during the pressure resistance performance test.
(6) Stroke
The stroke of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the requirements of the drawing.
(7) External Leakage
The external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 1 of MT/T 900-2000, see Table 2-67 for details.
(8) High-Temperature Performance
No abnormal phenomena should occur during the high-temperature performance test.
(9) Durability
Under rated pressure, the durability of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions in Table 1 of MT/T 900-2000, see Table 2-67 for details.
(10) Machining Quality
According to the provisions of JB/T 5058-2006 "Guidelines for Grading the Importance of Quality Characteristics of Products in the Machinery Industry", the importance level of machining quality characteristics should be determined.
(11) Assembly Quality
The assembly quality of qualified hydraulic cylinders should comply with:
1) The main parts of components such as piston rod, cylinder barrel, piston, guide sleeve, etc. should not be bumped or have obvious scratches.
2) The seal rings should not have scratches, twists, curling, or extrusion.
3) No corrosion should occur on the key parts of the main components.
4) The chrome plating layer on the surface of the piston rod should be uniform and dense, and should not have cracks, peeling, or shedding defects; under the designed maximum load, the chrome plating layer should not have cracks.
— The assembly quality of first-class hydraulic cylinders should comply with:
1) Components such as piston rod, cylinder barrel, piston, guide sleeve, etc. should not be bumped or have obvious scratches.
2) The seal rings should not have scratches, twists, curling, or extrusion.
3) No corrosion should occur on all parts inside the cylinder.
4) The chrome plating layer on the surface of the piston rod should be uniform and dense, and should not have cracks, peeling, or shedding defects; under the designed maximum load, the chrome plating layer should not have cracks.
There shall be no cracks on the coating.
(12) Internal Cleanliness
The internal cleanliness index shall conform to the provisions of Table 1 in MT/T 900-2000, as shown in Table 5-15 specifically.
2. Test Method
The test method for hydraulic cylinders shall be as specified in MT/T 900-2000.
3. Inspection Rules
The inspection rules for hydraulic cylinders shall be as specified in MT/T 900-2000.
4. Marking, Packaging, and Storage
(1) Marking
The marking for hydraulic cylinders shall be as specified in MT/T 900-2000, with the nameplate of the product as shown in Table 2-324.
(2) Packaging
The packaging for hydraulic cylinders shall be as specified in MT/T 900-2000.
(3) Storage
The storage for hydraulic cylinders shall be as specified in MT/T 900-2000.
4.7 Marine Hydraulic Cylinders: Design and Selection Basis
4.7.1 Marine Hydraulic Systems

CB/T 1102-2008 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Hydraulic Systems" stipulates the requirements for marine hydraulic systems, the application of components and accessories, piping and cleaning, etc., and is applicable to the design and manufacture of hydraulic transmission and control systems for ship machinery and equipment, including the hydraulic systems of the entire ship and supporting equipment.
1. Design
(1) Design Principles
1) The design of hydraulic systems should consider personnel safety and possible accidents, and take the following safety measures:

items: ① Pressure, position, and speed limits.
② Overload protection.
③ Reduction of system impact pressure, which should not cause danger due to impact pressure.
④ Provision of system back pressure.
⑤ Guarantee of hydraulic pump suction conditions.
⑥ The filtration accuracy of the hydraulic oil should meet the requirements of various components in the system.
⑦ Provision of alarm signals, such as low oil level, high or low oil temperature, filter blockage, pressure loss, overload, etc.
⑧ Clear specification of the quality and performance of the recommended working oil.
⑨ Safety protection when the hydraulic energy source or pipeline of the system suddenly fails. Such as setting hydraulic lock valves, anti-burst valves, hydraulic brakes or locking mechanisms, etc.
⑩ Formulation of safe operating procedures and setting of operating procedure nameplates.

sections.text: 2) The working temperature of the system should match the allowable operating temperature of the components.
Matching requirements:

items: 3) The system design should consider avoiding heat generation.
4) When the oil temperature in the system is too high, an oil cooler (air-cooled or water-cooled) set in the system should be used.
5) When the oil temperature in the system is too low, an oil heater (electric heating or steam heating) set in the system should be used.

6) When starting under low ambient temperature conditions, methods such as oil circulation, throttling, and overflow should be used for warm-up. The system can only be put into operation after warming up to a certain temperature.
7) The installation of components and pipelines should consider reducing the generation and transmission of noise.
8) Noise reduction measures should be taken, such as elastic through-cabin pipe fittings, accumulators, hoses, etc.
9) Collection facilities should be set up for parts prone to oil leakage, and oil pollution collection work should be done well to prevent oil pollution from harming the environment.

10) Equipment layout should consider the following disassembly and installation measures: ① When disassembling individual components or pipelines in the system, adjacent components or parts should not be disassembled in large quantities. ② When carrying out maintenance work, a large amount of working oil loss should not be caused. ③ Unless the system needs to replace the working oil, the maintenance oil tank generally does not need to drain oil.
11) Components that need debugging, replacement, and regular cleaning should be arranged in easily operable locations.
12) Vent or drain points should be set at appropriate parts of the system, paying attention to not causing air accumulation.
13) Components, parts, or equipment weighing more than 15 kg should be easy to lift or have lifting devices.

sections.text: (2) Components and Accessories
1) Hydraulic Cylinders

items: ① The load, stroke, and installation of hydraulic cylinders should not subject them to abnormal lateral forces.
② The exhaust port of the hydraulic cylinder should be arranged upward.
2) Working Hydraulic Oil

① The type and characteristics of the working hydraulic oil used should be suitable for all components and accessories in the system. The solid particle contamination level code of the working hydraulic oil should meet the requirements of GB/T 14039.
② When extracting liquid samples from the working system pipeline for hydraulic particle contamination analysis, it should be carried out according to the provisions of GB/T 17489.
③ When the working oil is filled into the system, it should be filtered, and the filtration accuracy should not be lower than the system requirements.
3) Seals and Sealing Elements
① The seals of components and accessories should adopt pressure sealing seals.
② Mechanical seals should meet the requirements of GB/T 6556.
③ O-ring rubber seals should meet the requirements of GB/T 3452.1.

676.page_header: Chapter 4  Hydraulic Machine (Pump) Hydraulic System Design and Selection  665

sections.text: 4) Block. The block shall not deform under the specified working pressure and temperature.

(3) Piping
1) Flow velocity in pipelines. The general flow velocities are: 1 m/s for suction pipelines, 3 to 6 m/s for pressure pipelines, and 1.5 to 2.5 m/s for return oil pipelines.
2) Pipeline strength. The strength of the pipeline system should be able to withstand the highest peak pressure that may occur in the system.
3) Pipeline and its fittings.
① Galvanized pipes or joints should not be used, nor should brass pipes be used.
② The welds between pipes and joints, flanges, etc. should be subject to non-destructive testing.
4) Pipeline layout.
① The routing and layout of the pipeline should minimize the number of elbows and joints.
② Where small diameter pipes for remote control or braking are relatively weak, protective measures such as baffles or protective covers should be installed.
③ The pipeline layout should not interfere with the adjustment, repair, disassembly, and assembly of components or equipment.
④ Fittings should be easy to disassemble and assemble, without affecting other fittings or components, and without requiring special tools.
⑤ Where pipeline deformation may occur due to changes in oil temperature and air temperature, larger elbows or expansion joints should be installed.
⑥ The highest points in different areas of the pipeline system should be equipped with venting points. At the same time, venting points should be provided at the lowest positions.
⑦ Deck pipelines should be laid along the hatch coaming, and should be protected from sunlight exposure or equipped with sunshades.
⑧ Pipelines in cabins should be kept away from heat sources and have improved ventilation.
⑨ Leaking oil, return oil from pilot control, and return oil pipelines should be separately connected to the oil tank.
⑩ Fittings should not be used to support equipment or oil blocks.
⑪ Pipelines should not pass through freshwater tanks. If unavoidable, they should pass through oil-tight tunnels or sleeves. When passing through fuel oil tanks, the pipe wall should be thickened and should not have detachable joints.
⑫ When pipelines pass through watertight or airtight structures, they should be equipped with through fittings or base plates.
5) Pressure measurement interfaces.
① If there is no pressure measurement interface on the pressure control component, a pressure measurement interface should be installed on the corresponding pipeline.
② A pressure measurement interface for the supply oil pressure should be installed between the actuator and its corresponding control component.
③ When using a multi-point pressure gauge switch and a pressure gauge to form a pressure measurement device, each pressure measurement point should be marked.
2. Process
(1) Bending pipes

items: The bending radius of pipes should generally be greater than 3 times the outer diameter of the pipe. At the same time, bending should start at a distance greater than 0.5 times the outer diameter of the pipe from one end of the pipe.
No creases should appear when bending the pipe. The ratio of the minor axis to the major axis of the elliptical cross-section at the flattened area of the bent pipe should not be less than 0.75.
The sand-filled hot bending process should not be used.
Flanges or pipe joints should be installed near elbows and branch pipes.
Heat treatment and non-destructive testing should be performed after bending the pipes.

Attention should be paid to the following when configuring hoses:
① The arrangement of hoses should avoid twisting.
② Hoses should be fixed in position or protected.
③ If the weight of the hose may cause tension, supports should be installed and brackets or drag chains should be configured.
④ If a hose rupture would endanger safety, the hydraulic system should be protected with a cover.

sections.text: (2) Support of pipeline systems

items: Supports should be installed at both ends of the pipeline system and along its length.
The support of the pipe should be close to the elbow.
If there are no special requirements for the spacing of pipeline system supports, it should be less than the recommended values in Table 4-185.
Supports such as brackets, hangers, and pipe clamps should not be welded to the pipe, nor should they damage the pipe.

sections.caption: Table 4-185 Spacing of Pipeline System Supports

items: 5) Vibration-damping pads should be installed between the pipe clamp and the pipe.

sections.text: (3) Cutting and drilling of pipes

items: Pipes should be cut and drilled using machining methods, avoiding gas cutting.
Burrs and chips should be removed after cutting and drilling pipes.

sections.text: (4) Welding

items: Pipes should not be lengthened by butt welding. Welding is only applicable to the connection of pipes with flanges, pipe joints, branch pipes, etc.
After welding, the inside of the pipe in the welded area should be cleaned of welding slag, spatter, and oxide scale.
The distance from the weld to the open end of the pipe should not exceed 5 times the inner diameter of the pipe.
There should be no dead corners at any welded joint.
Electric welding should not be used for welding construction, and argon arc welding should be used instead.

sections.text: 3. Requirements
(1) Marine environmental conditions

items:
Atmospheric environment. The hydraulic system should be able to work normally under the following atmospheric environmental conditions:
① The temperature range for ships sailing unlimited sea areas is -25 to 55°C.
② The relative humidity of the air is 95%, with dew formation.
③ There is salt spray, oil mist, and mold.

sections.text: 2) Inclination and rocking: After being subjected to the inclination and rocking specified in Table 4-186, the hydraulic system should be able to work normally.

sections.caption: Table 4-186 Inclination and rocking values

sections.text: 3) Vibration: After being subjected to the vibration specified in Table 4-187, the hydraulic system should be able to work normally.

sections.caption: Table 4-187 Vibration values

sections.text: 4) Impact: After being subjected to the impact specified in Table 4-188, the hydraulic system should be able to work normally.

sections.caption: Table 4-188 Impact values

sections.text: (2) Product marking

items: The graphic symbols used in the simplified schematic diagram of the hydraulic system should comply with the requirements of GB/T 786.1.
Each component should have a code, such as a number or letter, and should be marked near the corresponding component on the equipment.
The oil ports of each component, such as the working oil inlet and outlet, pilot control port, test port, drain port, etc., should all have markings.
The control valve should have markings for its operating form and function.
Integrated or assembled components, such as cartridge valves, combination valves, etc., can be marked as a whole.
The marking of electric actuators should be consistent with the marking on the electrical and hydraulic system diagrams.
The identification symbols and colors of pipelines should comply with the requirements of GB 3033-1982 (which has been invalidated).

sections.text: 4. Testing
(1) Test pressure

The hydraulic test should be conducted before and after the installation of the pipelines. The system pressure test pressure should not be lower than 1.5 times the design pressure, and the sealing test pressure should be 1.25 times the design pressure, but should not exceed the design pressure plus 7 MPa.
(2) Test requirements

items: The hydraulic test of pipelines should comply with the requirements of CB/T 3616-1994 (2017) "Requirements for Hydraulic Test of Pipelines".
The installation and sealing test of pipelines should comply with the requirements of CB/T 3619-1994 "Quality Requirements for Installation and Sealing Test of Ship Systems and Power Pipelines".
During the test, the pressure should be increased in steps of 25% of the nominal pressure until the test pressure is reached, and the holding time should not be less than 5 min.
The hydraulic system of ship machinery and equipment should be tested together with the corresponding equipment.
The hydraulic system of the whole ship should be tested together with the mechanical equipment being driven or controlled.

The following matters should be noted during the hydraulic test: ① Pressure gauges with a pressure range exceeding the effective range, automatic control components, and pressure valves that have been adjusted should be isolated or removed. ② Before pressurizing, the air stored in the system should be fully eliminated. ③ During the test, the pressure should be increased to the test pressure in steps of 25% of the nominal pressure, and the holding time for each level should generally be 10 min.

sections.text: (3) Test content: The main contents of the hydraulic system test are as follows: ① The function of transmission or control. ② Performance parameters, such as working oil pressure, speed of the actuator, etc. ③ The effectiveness of safety protection measures. ④ Overload capacity, etc.
5. Cleaning
(1) General requirements

items: Blind plates, plugs, etc. should be installed at all oil ports of hydraulic components and auxiliary parts in the system. If any problems are found, they should be disassembled and maintained in a timely manner.
The oil tank (cabinet) is usually not filled with hydraulic oil when it is installed on the ship. Before filling with oil, its internal cleanliness should be rechecked.
All pipelines (including cross-connected pipelines for cleaning) should be chemically cleaned.

If the pipelines after chemical cleaning are not cleaned with oil in time, oil filling should be used to form a complete oil film on the inner surface of the pipelines, and pipe plugs should be used to seal the ports. The oil used should be compatible with the working oil.
When installing the hydraulic system on the ship, operations such as air cleaning, grinding, or painting that may pollute the system should not be carried out nearby.
Equipment (including integrated blocks) and pipeline systems that are assembled as a whole and shipped should be cleaned in advance, and the open oil ports should be sealed.
The pipeline system should be cleaned with oil after being installed on the ship.
Special equipment should be used for hydraulic pumps, filters, oil tanks, etc. for cleaning.

Temporary cross-connected pipes should be set up to short-circuit the pipeline system into a loop, without allowing the cleaning oil to flow through hydraulic pumps, control components, and actuator components, etc.
When setting up cross-connected pipes, the pipeline system can be short-circuited into one or several loops as needed and for convenience.
For pipelines that do not constitute a loop, such as expansion oil pipes and drain pipes, they should be handled separately.

678.page_header: Chapter 4  Design and Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders for Hydraulic Presses (Machines)  667

sections.text: , they should be connected into loops for cleaning. Otherwise, anti-pollution measures should be taken during installation.
(2) Cleaning of piping systems by filling with oil

1) Flow rate of hydraulic pump set for cleaning. The flow rate of the hydraulic pump set for cleaning should be the same as or slightly greater than the working flow rate of the hydraulic system. However, it is recommended that the flow rate of the hydraulic pump set for cleaning should ensure that the Reynolds number in the pipe fittings is not less than 4000.
2) Filters for cleaning.

items: ① The accuracy of the filter can be determined according to the actual situation. At the beginning of cleaning, a coarse filter of 150-200 mesh is usually used, and then the accuracy is gradually increased. Finally, its accuracy should be consistent with or slightly higher than the requirements of the hydraulic system.
② The filter for cleaning should be full-flow.
③ The filter for cleaning should be easy to disassemble, inspect, or replace the filter element.

sections.text: 3) Oil for cleaning.

items: ① The oil for cleaning should have the same oil base as the working oil.
② The oil for cleaning is usually of low viscosity.
③ If the working oil is used for cleaning, the oil after cleaning is generally not suitable for use as working oil again.
④ Soluble chemical cleaning agents should not be used.

sections.text: 4) Temperature of cleaning oil.

items: ① It is recommended to use hot oil for cleaning. When the oil temperature is limited by the cleaning equipment and the oil used, the maximum oil temperature should not exceed the specified value, and the recommended oil temperature is 50°C.
② The oil temperature can be increased by using an oil heater or throttling.
③ Oil pipes should not be directly heated.

sections.text: 5) Operational requirements.

items: ① The cleaning by filling with oil should be carried out continuously, and the pipes should be lightly tapped with a wooden hammer (or other effective methods) along the pipeline multiple times, especially at welded parts or pipe joints.

② After the pipe fittings are cleaned by filling with oil, the time interval for inspecting the filter should not be too long. It is recommended to perform the first inspection 10 minutes after cleaning.
③ The time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter can be gradually extended according to the actual situation, and the maximum recommended interval is 1 hour.
④ The total cleaning time should be determined according to the length and complexity of the piping system loop. Generally, each loop requires 10-24 hours.
⑤ After the cleaning meets the quality requirements, the piping system can be purged with clean and dry compressed air or nitrogen to remove the cleaning oil from the piping system.

sections.text: (3) Cleaning of the system by filling with oil

1) The system cleaning by filling with oil is carried out after the installation of the hydraulic system and mechanical equipment is completed. The system cleaning by filling with oil usually uses the working oil.
2) The oil filling and air exhaust should be operated according to the following requirements:

items: ① During the oil filling process, the hydraulic oil should be prevented from being stirred.
② The oil filling process should be continuous, and air should not be filled in at the same time.
③ The new oil injected into the system should be filtered.

sections.text: 3) The control elements and actuator elements should be operated one by one in steps. It is recommended that each element should be operated no less than 6 times, and the duration should be no less than 15min.

4) During the system cleaning by filling with oil, the actuator elements are usually in an unloaded state. If cleaning is carried out under load, it should be operated according to the requirements of equipment trial operation.
5) The cleaning process should be operated according to the following requirements:

items: ① The oil temperature during the cleaning process should be below 60°C.
② There should be no leakage during the cleaning process.

③ After the system starts cleaning by filling with oil, the time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter should not be too long. It is recommended to perform the first inspection 30 minutes after cleaning.
④ The time interval for inspecting the cleaning filter can be gradually extended according to the actual situation.
⑤ The oil level in the oil tank should be checked frequently. When the oil level reaches the minimum allowable level, oil should be added to the oil tank in time.

sections.text: (4) Quality inspection of cleaning
1) Quality inspection of cleaning should be carried out after cleaning of the piping system by filling with oil and cleaning of the system by filling with oil.

2) According to the importance and composition of the mechanical equipment, the components of the system should meet the following requirements for the contamination level of solid particles in the oil:

items: ① For general medium and low-pressure hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/20/16 in GB/T14039-2002, and the contamination level code of solid particles in high-pressure hydraulic systems should not be higher than --/18/15 in GB/T14039-2002.

② For general medium and low-pressure proportional hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/17/14 in GB/T14039-2002, and the contamination level code of solid particles in high-pressure proportional hydraulic systems should not be higher than --/16/12 in GB/T14039-2002.
③ For servo hydraulic systems, the contamination level code of solid particles should not be higher than --/15/12 in GB/T14039-2002.

sections.text: 3) The following inspection methods are recommended:

items: ① Inspect the filter.
② Inspect the quality of the oil.
③ Analyze and determine the contamination degree of the oil.

sections.text: 4) The oil sample for oil quality inspection should be taken according to the following regulations:

items: ① When used for inspecting the oil quality, the sample should be taken from the oil tank or the release point of the system 6 hours after the cleaning work is stopped.
② When used for determining the contamination degree of the oil, three samples should be taken continuously and randomly during the cleaning process, with a time interval of 10 seconds.

sections.text: 5) Other matters.

items: ① When the hydraulic system is officially put into use, the filter should be replaced with a new or clean filter element.
② After completing the above work, the outer surface of the pipe fittings that need to be protected from rust should be coated with oil-resistant paint.

sections.text: The use instructions, packaging, and transportation of the hydraulic system can be found in CB/T11102-2008.
4.7.2 Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinder
The scope and normative references of GB/T 13342—2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinder" are shown in Table 1-30.
1. Classification
(1) Type
There are two common types of marine hydraulic cylinders:

items: Plunger-type hydraulic cylinder: The plunger only extends outward in one direction, and the reverse retraction is completed by external force.
Double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder: The piston moves in both directions, and both extension and retraction strokes are realized by fluid pressure.

sections.text: (2) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of hydraulic cylinders can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-14.
(3) Graphic Symbols
The graphic symbols of hydraulic cylinders shall be in accordance with the provisions of GB/T 786.1.
2. Requirements
(1) Appearance

items: The hydraulic cylinder shall be free from defects such as burrs, bruises, and rust, and the coating shall be free from peeling and bubbles.
The outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder shall be free from defects such as folds, obvious waves, and cracks.
Exposed components shall be treated for rust prevention, and may also be protected by coatings, passivation layers, paint layers, etc. When painting, apply anti-rust primer first, then topcoat.
The outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder shall be free from oxide scale and rust pits before painting. The paint layer shall be free from defects such as blisters.

sections.text: (2) Materials
1) The materials selected for the main parts of the hydraulic cylinder are shown in Table 4-189, and materials with performance higher than those specified in Table 4-189 may also be selected.

sections.caption: Table 4-189 Main Parts Materials

sections.text: 2) After 100% non-destructive testing of the cylinder barrel, it should reach Grade I specified in JB/T 4730.3—2005 (already obsolete).
(3) Structure

items: The hydraulic cylinder should generally be equipped with a buffer device, and there should be no metal impact sound when the stroke reaches the end.
The connecting screws and bolts used in the hydraulic cylinder shall not be lower than Grade 8.8 specified in GB/T 3098.1—2000.
The hydraulic cylinder should generally be equipped with an exhaust device.
The hydraulic cylinder, piston rod or plunger should have anti-corrosion measures.

sections.text: 5) The strength of the weld seam should not be lower than the strength index of the parent material, and the quality of the weld seam should reach Grade II specified in GB/T 3323—2005.
6) The performance of seals, the design and manufacture of each sealing ring and groove can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.
(4) Temperature: The temperature requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.
(5) Working Medium: The solid particle contamination degree code of the working medium in the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder shall not be higher than that specified in GB/T 14039—2002 —/19/16.
(6) Pressure Resistance: The pressure resistance requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.

(7) Sealing: Under 1.25 times the nominal pressure, the internal leakage between the cylinder barrel and the piston should comply with the values specified in Table 2 or Table 2-159 of GB/T 13342—2007, and there should be no external leakage at other mating surfaces.
(8) Internal Leakage: The internal leakage of a double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 2 or Table 2-159 of GB/T 13342—2007.
(9) External Leakage: The external leakage requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.

(10) Minimum Starting Pressure: 1) The minimum starting pressure of the plunger-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 3 or Table 2-67 of GB/T 13342—2007. 2) The minimum starting pressure of the double-acting piston-type hydraulic cylinder should not be greater than the value specified in Table 4 or Table 2-158 of GB/T 13342—2007.
(11) Minimum Stable Speed: The requirements for the minimum stable speed of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.
(12) Load Efficiency: The load efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder should not be lower than 90%.
(13) Pressure Resistance: The pressure resistance requirements of the hydraulic cylinder can be found in GB/T 13342—2007 or Table 2-67.

(14) Internal Cleanliness: The quality of internal pollutants in the hydraulic cylinder (when the stroke is 1 m) should be lower than the limit value in Table 5 of GB/T 13342—2007, as detailed in Table 5-15.
3. Test Methods
The test methods for hydraulic cylinders can be found in GB/T 13342—2007.
4. Inspection Rules
The inspection rules for hydraulic cylinders can be found in GB/T 13342—2007.
5. Marking, Packaging, Transportation and Storage
(1) Marking
The marking requirements for hydraulic cylinders can be found in GB/T 13342—2007, and the product nameplate is shown in Table 2-324.
(2) Packaging
The packaging requirements for hydraulic cylinders can be found in GB/T 13342—2007.

(3) Transportation and Storage
The requirements for transportation and storage of hydraulic cylinders are specified in GB/T 13342—2007.
4.7.3 Marine Digital Hydraulic Cylinders
The scope and normative references of the standard GB/T 24946—2010 'Marine Digital Hydraulic Cylinders' are listed in Table 1-31.
1. Product Classification

(1) Structure of Digital Cylinders
The typical structural diagram of digital cylinders is shown in Figure 1 of GB/T 13342—2007.

(2) Basic Parameters
The basic parameters of digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.

(3) Marking
The marking of digital cylinders is specified in GB/T 24946—2010.

(4) Structure
1) The connecting screws and bolts used for connecting parts with the cylinder body in digital cylinders should comply with grade 8.8 specified in GB/T 3008.1—2000.
2) Hydraulic cylinders can be equipped with gas charging devices as required.
3) Hydraulic cylinders should have anti-corrosion structure.
4) Welding strength should not be lower than the base material strength.
5) The sealing components of digital cylinders should function properly, and the design and manufacture of each sealing ring groove should comply with GB/T 24946—2010.
2. Requirements

(1) Appearance
1) Digital cylinders should not have cracks, bruises, scratches, casting defects, rust, or bubbles.
2) External surfaces should be smooth and clean, and may also use multi-layer coating or other surface treatments.
3) Oil should be removed from the external surfaces of digital cylinders before rust removal. The surfaces should be smooth and bright, without wrinkles or cracks.

(2) Material
1) The main material for digital cylinders should be Table 4-190, or materials with performance higher than Table 4-190 specifications may also be used.

sections.caption: Table 4-190  Main Component Materials

sections.text: Note: Due to the low strength of 20 seamless steel tube, all digital cylinders should use 20 seamless steel tube with appropriate fit.
2) Cylinders should undergo 100% ultrasonic flaw detection and should meet level 1 requirements of JB/T 4730.3—2005 (already obsolete).

(3) Environmental Conditions
The environmental conditions for digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.

(4) Working Fluid Contamination Level
The solid particle contamination level in the working fluid of digital cylinders should not exceed the equivalent number specified in GB/T 14039—2002 -19/16.
The contamination level of working fluid in digital cylinders specified in GB/T 24946—2010 should be low.

(5) Fatigue Strength
Digital cylinders can withstand 1.5 times the rated pressure, all components should not have fracture or permanent deformation, and welding should not leak.

(6) Sealing
The sealing performance requirements for digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.

(7) Minimum Starting Pressure
The minimum starting pressure requirements for digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.

(8) Pulse Flow
The deviation between the actual pulse flow of digital cylinders and the specified value should be less than 5%.

(9) Minimum Stable Speed
The minimum stable speed of digital cylinders should not be greater than 20 pulses per minute, with the unit of minimum stable speed being mm/s.

(10) Maximum Speed
The maximum speed during operation of digital cylinders should not be less than 2000 pulses per minute, with the unit of maximum speed being mm/s.

(11) Repeat Positioning Accuracy
The repeat positioning accuracy of digital cylinders should not exceed 3 pulses per minute.

(12) Resolution
The resolution of digital cylinders should not be greater than 30 pulses per minute.

(13) Hysteresis
The hysteresis of digital cylinders should not exceed 30 pulses per minute.

(14) Pulse Frequency
The minimum pulse frequency of digital cylinders is 10Hz, and the maximum pulse frequency is 3000Hz within the range specified in the manual.

(15) Durability
Digital cylinders should meet the following conditions: continuous operation stroke should not be less than 10⁶ m.

(16) Internal Cleanliness
The internal cleanliness of working fluid (for 1m stroke) in digital cylinders should be lower than the limits specified in GB/T 24946—2010.
3. Test Method
The test methods for digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.
4. Test Rules
The test rules for digital cylinders are specified in GB/T 24946—2010.
5. Marking, Packaging, Transportation and Storage

(1) Marking
The marking of digital cylinders is specified in GB/T 24946—2010, and the product nameplate is shown in Table 2-324.
(2) Packaging: Refer to GB/T 24946–2010 for packaging of digital cylinders. (3) Transportation and Storage: Refer to GB/T 24946–2010 for transportation and storage of digital cylinders.
