4.8.1 Dump (Low-Speed) Vehicle Hydraulic Cylinders
4.8.1.1 Dump vehicle hydraulic cylinders
QC/T 460—2010 "Technical Conditions for Dump Vehicle Hydraulic Cylinders" stipulates the scope and normative references shown in Table 1-30.
1. Composition and main parameter selection of hydraulic cylinder product model

The hydraulic cylinder product model consists of level code, hydraulic cylinder type code, pressure level code, main parameter code, connection and installation code, and product serial number, as shown in Figure 1 of QC/T 460—2010.
(1) Level code
Indicates the extension level of the hydraulic cylinder, represented by a single Arabic numeral 1, 2, 3..., and the first level can be omitted.
(2) Hydraulic cylinder type code
The hydraulic cylinder type code is represented by two Chinese Pinyin letters. The hydraulic cylinder type codes are shown in Table 4-196.
(3) Pressure level code
The pressure level code consists of a single uppercase Chinese Pinyin letter.
See Table 4-197 for pressure grade codes.

sections.caption: Table 4-196 Hydraulic Cylinder Type Code
rows: Double-acting final-stage telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder

sections.text: Note: In JB/T 2184-2007, "SG" represents a double-acting single piston rod hydraulic cylinder, and "MG" represents an electro-hydraulic stepping hydraulic cylinder. Moreover, plunger cylinders can only be single-acting cylinders; double-acting cylinders do not have double-piston types.

sections.caption: Table 4-197 Pressure Grade Code (Unit: MPa)

sections.text: (4) Main parameter codes: Main parameter codes are expressed by multiplying the bore diameter by the stroke, with the unit being mm. For piston cylinders, the bore diameter refers to the inner diameter of the cylinder; for plunger cylinders, the bore diameter refers to the plunger diameter; for sleeve cylinders, the bore diameter refers to the diameter of the first-stage sleeve that extends out; the stroke refers to the total stroke.

(5) Connection and mounting type codes: Connection and mounting type codes are composed of one or two uppercase Pinyin letters. When the upper and lower mounting types are the same, a single letter can be used to represent them; when the upper and lower mounting types are different, the first letter represents the upper mounting type, and the second letter represents the lower mounting type. Specific codes are shown in Table 4-198.

sections.caption: Table 4-198 Connection and Mounting Type Code

sections.text: Note: In GB/T 9094-2006, some connection and mounting types listed in the above table are not included, such as ball joint type and insertion type.

(6) Product serial number: The product serial number is expressed by Arabic numerals representing the design sequence number of the product. The product serial numbers are used in sequence as 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on.
(7) Model example: Examples of hydraulic cylinder models can be found in QC/T 460-2010 or Table 2-6.
2. General Requirements

items: The hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of the QC/T460-2010 standard and be manufactured according to the drawings and technical documents approved by the prescribed procedures.
All parts must be inspected and qualified by the quality inspection department before assembly and use.
All parts should be deburred and cleaned before assembly.
The non-machined surfaces of the exposed parts of the hydraulic cylinder should be painted according to the requirements of TQ 6 in QC/T484.
All exposed oil ports of the hydraulic cylinder should be sealed with plugs.

sections.text: 6) The limit of solid particle contamination in the hydraulic oil inside the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of QC/T 29104.
7) The operating temperature range of the hydraulic cylinder should be -20~40°C.
8) The surface roughness of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the requirements of JB/T 5943 specifications.
9) The surface hardness of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with QC/T 625 specifications.
Note: In GB/T 37400-2019, sections 6, 7, 10 specify: "each sealed cavity, dust, skin and other sealing devices should prevent oil leakage" can be referenced.
3. Performance Requirements
(1) Test Operation Requirements
During test operation, the hydraulic cylinder must be stable and free from external leakage. It must comply with the starting force specified in Table 4-199.
(2) Starting Force
Starting force should comply with Table 4-199 specifications.

sections.text: (3) Durability Performance

During durability testing, the hydraulic cylinder must not produce permanent deformation, component damage, or external leakage; after durability testing, the hydraulic cylinder must not show signs of performance degradation or failure.
(4) Oil Leakage
Hydraulic cylinder external oil leakage and internal leakage requirements are specified in QC/T 460-2010 or Table 2-67.
(5) Full-Process Testing
Full-process testing must be conducted. The stroke length must comply with Table 4-200 specifications.

(6) Buffering Effect
Hydraulic cylinders equipped with buffering devices must undergo buffering effect testing.

sections.text: When the hydraulic cylinder automatically stops, the stroke length should comply with the provisions of Table 4-196.
(7) Limit Effect
For hydraulic cylinders equipped with limit devices, during the limit effect test, when the hydraulic cylinder automatically stops, the stroke length should comply with the provisions of Table 4-196.
(8) Load Efficiency
Under rated pressure, the load efficiency η of the hydraulic cylinder should be greater than or equal to 90%.

4.8.1.2 Hydraulic Cylinder for Dump Slow-Speed Vehicle

JB/T 13514-2018 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinder for Dump Slow-Speed Vehicle" specifies the model composition, technical requirements, testing, inspection rules, product label, user manual, packaging, transportation, and storage for hydraulic cylinders used in the lifting system of dump slow-speed vehicles (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic cylinders) using hydraulic oil as the working medium.
1. Model Composition
(1) Basic Structure
The product model of the hydraulic cylinder consists of category code, stage code, pressure level code, main parameter code, connection and installation method code, and product sequence number.

sections.caption: Product sequence number composition diagram
sections.description: A hierarchical diagram showing the composition of hydraulic cylinder product codes, with boxes indicating: product sequence number, connection and installation method code, main parameter code (diameter × stroke), pressure level code, category code, and stage code

sections.text: (2) Category Code
The category code of the hydraulic cylinder is represented by two uppercase Chinese pinyin letters:

ZG——Single-acting plunger hydraulic cylinder. HG——Single-acting piston hydraulic cylinder. TG——Single-acting telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder. SG——Double-acting single-piston hydraulic cylinder. According to the provisions of JB/T 2184-2007 standard, SG should be the code for double-acting single piston rod hydraulic cylinder.
(3) Stage Code
The output stage of the hydraulic cylinder is represented by a single Arabic numeral 1, 2, 3, … 1 can be omitted.
(4) Pressure Level Code
Different pressure levels are represented by a single uppercase Chinese pinyin letter:
D——10MPa. E——16MPa. F——20MPa.
(5) Main Parameter Code

The main parameter code is expressed as cylinder diameter multiplied by stroke in mm, where the piston cylinder diameter refers to the inner diameter of the cylinder, the plunger cylinder diameter refers to the plunger diameter, and the sleeve cylinder diameter refers to the diameter of the first-stage sleeve extended, and the stroke refers to the total stroke.
(6) Connection and Installation Method Code

The connection and installation method code consists of one or two uppercase Chinese pinyin letters. When the upper and lower installation methods are the same, a single letter can be used; when they are different, the first letter represents the upper installation method, and the second letter represents the lower installation method:
E——clevis type. L——Threaded type. Q——Ball joint type. R——Insert type. Z——Hinge shaft type.
(7) Product Sequence Number
The product sequence number is sequentially represented by Arabic numerals 1, 2, 3, 4, … indicating the design sequence number of the product.
2. Technical Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: All parts should be deburred and cleaned before assembly.
All exposed oil ports of the hydraulic cylinder should be sealed with plugs.
The welding surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be flat and free of rust, and the weld should be uniform, without burn marks, residual slag, or splashes.

The coating quality of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of TQ-2-3 in JB/T 5673-2015 "General Technical Conditions for Painting of Agricultural and Forestry Tractors and Implements".
The surface coating quality of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of JB/T 11223-2011 "Appearance Quality Requirements for Three-Wheeled Vehicles and Low-Speed Trucks".
The restriction of solid contaminants in hydraulic oil inside the hydraulic cylinder should comply with QC/T

sections.text: 29104—2013 "Hydraulic Oil Solid Particle Contamination Limits for Special Purpose Vehicle Hydraulic Systems" provisions.
(2) Performance Requirements
1) During trial operation test, the hydraulic cylinder should move smoothly without abnormal phenomena such as external leakage, and should comply with the starting pressure specified in 2.(2)2).
2) Starting Pressure. The starting pressure should meet the requirements of Table 4-201.

sections.text: 3) Pressure Resistance Performance. During pressure resistance test, the hydraulic cylinder should not produce loosening, permanent deformation, component damage or external leakage; after pressure resistance test, the hydraulic cylinder should not exhibit disconnection or failure.
4) Leakage.

① External Leakage. External leakage should meet the following requirements: During external leakage test, there should be no external leakage at the joint surfaces. During internal leakage test and pressure resistance test, the hydraulic cylinder should not have external leakage.
② Internal Leakage. Under rated pressure, the internal leakage of piston-type hydraulic cylinder should not exceed the limits specified in Table 4-202 or Table 4-203.

8) Load Efficiency. Under rated pressure, the load efficiency η of the hydraulic cylinder should not be less than 90%.

9) Reliability. Under rated pressure, the hydraulic cylinder can reciprocate 30,000 times or move reciprocally 30 km. Before the hydraulic cylinder reciprocates 5,000 times or moves reciprocally 5 km, there should be no external leakage. Afterwards, for every 50 reciprocations or 50 m of movement, for hydraulic cylinders with piston rod, plunger and sleeve diameter less than 50 mm, the external leakage should be less than or equal to 0.2 mL; for hydraulic cylinders with piston rod, plunger and sleeve diameter greater than 50 mm, the external leakage should be less than or equal to 0.004 dL. During testing, there should be no loosening, permanent deformation or abnormal wear at any part of the hydraulic cylinder.

items: After hydraulic cylinder passes factory inspection, oil should be drained, and all oil ports should be sealed with oil-resistant plugs to ensure sealing, dust prevention, and leak prevention. Exposed machined surfaces, threads, etc. should have protective measures applied.

items: The mechanical properties of the cylinder body material, specifically the yield strength, should not be lower than the specified 280MPa.

sections.text: 2) The cylinder head should meet the following requirements:

sections.text: 3) The piston should meet the following requirements:

The scope and normative reference documents specified in GB 25974.2—2010 "Hydraulic Support Part 2: Technical Conditions for Columns and Jacks" are shown in Table 1-3.
1. Requirements
(1) General Requirements

items: Unmarked tolerances. The tolerance limits for unmarked dimensions on the drawing of machined metal parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T 1804—2000 grade M, and those without assembly relationship should comply with the provisions of GB/T 1804—2000 grade C.
Pressure-bearing welds. Welds subjected to liquid pressure should be able to withstand 200% of the rated working pressure of the hydraulic cylinder, and should not leak after a 5-minute test.
Cast and forged parts. Cast steel parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T 11352. Forged parts should comply with the provisions of GB/T 12361.

Other components. Hydraulic cylindrical helical springs should comply with the provisions of JB/T 3338.1. Ordinary threads should comply with the provisions of GB/T 197—2003 grades 6 and 7 (grade 6 for external threads and grade 7 for internal threads). The quality of the coating on the piston rod should comply with the provisions of Appendix A of GB 25974.2—2010 unless there are special requirements. The dimensions of O-ring seals and grooves should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3452.1 and GB/T 3452.3.
Lifting points. Hydraulic cylinders should be equipped with lifting points, and the lifting points should be able to withstand a force of 4 times the lifting weight without damage.

Valves and safety devices. Support columns and supporting hydraulic jacks should be equipped with safety devices to prevent the pressure from exceeding the allowable value. Valves and safety devices that are fixedly installed should not malfunction accidentally.
Working fluid. The working fluid of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with the provisions of MT 76.
Welding. Welding operations and quality requirements should comply with the provisions of GB 12467 (all parts).
Allowable stress and static force calculation. The allowable stress and static force calculation for parts can be found in Appendix B of GB 25974.2—2010 or in Section 1.7.3.

sections.text: (2) Assembly Quality Requirements

If any of the above phenomena occur, they should be replaced immediately. ③ After the hydraulic cylinder is assembled, it should be retracted to the shortest state, and all liquid inlet and outlet ports should be sealed with plastic plugs. ④ After assembly, the outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder (except for the outer surface of the piston rod) should be sprayed or painted with anti-rust primer and topcoat according to the drawing requirements. sections.text: 2) Plating Layer: The quality of the plating layer without special requirements should comply with the provisions of Appendix A of GB/T 25974.2-2010 or Section 1.7.6. All galvanized parts should be passivated after plating.
(5) Performance Requirements
1) Sealing Performance

During the hydraulic cylinder loading sealing test, with the lock pressure cavity closed, the pressure in the pressure cavity should not drop more than 10% within the first 1 minute or the length of the hydraulic cylinder should change less than 1%. In the following 5 minutes, the pressure or length should remain unchanged. In the next 5 minutes, the pressure drop should not exceed 0.5% or the length change should not exceed 0.05%.
2) No-Load Operation: The hydraulic cylinder should operate smoothly without sticking, crawling, or external leakage when unloaded throughout the entire stroke.

3) Minimum Starting Pressure: The starting pressure of the piston cavity for the column under no-load, no-back-pressure conditions should be less than 3.5 MPa. The starting pressure of the piston rod cavity should be less than 7.5 MPa. The starting pressure of the piston cavity and piston rod cavity for the jack under no-load, no-back-pressure conditions should be less than 3.5 MPa.
4) Sealing Performance of Piston Rod Cavity: The piston rod cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should not leak externally under a pressure of 2 MPa and 1.1 times the supply pressure.

5) Pressure Relief Performance: The column and supporting jack should have bearing capacity while moving and possess pressure relief characteristics: ① The force measured during central pressure relief should be less than 1.1 times the rated force and not less than the rated force. ② The force measured during eccentric pressure relief should not exceed 110% of the maximum force measured during central pressure relief and should not be less than the rated force.
Note: In GB/T 25974.2-2010, the term "pressure relief" is defined as: "The process of the hydraulic cylinder length change caused by external forces exceeding the safety valve opening pressure."

6) Overload Performance in Center: The overload performance in center includes: ① The column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure when subjected to a static load of 1.5 times the rated force and a dynamic load from mechanical impact reaching 1.5 times the rated working pressure. The residual deformation of the cylinder barrel expansion should be less than 0.02% of the cylinder diameter. ② The column and supporting jack that have not been subjected to mechanical impact dynamic load should be able to withstand a static load pressure of 2 times the rated force. After the loading test, the function of the column and supporting jack should no longer be considered, but the base material should not produce cracks, nor should weld seam cracks occur. ③ The supporting jack that has not been subjected to mechanical impact dynamic load should be able to withstand a static tensile force of 2 times the rated force. ④ The column and supporting jack in a fully retracted state should be able to withstand 2 times the rated force, and there should be no plastic deformation after the test. ⑤ The jack should not experience functional failure when loaded with 1.5 times the rated tensile force or rated working pressure. 7) Eccentric Loading Performance: After being subjected to eccentric force and lateral force, the column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure. The deflection at the transition between stages should be less than 0.1% of the test length. 8) Durability: After 21,000 loading cycles, the column (including the extension section) and supporting jack should not experience functional failure. After 10,000 loading cycles, the jack should not experience functional failure. 9) External Extension Limit: The column and supporting jack should extend once towards the internal stop block under rated working pressure, remain stationary for at least 3 minutes, and the internal stop block should not be damaged. The column and supporting jack should extend towards the external stop block using at least 0.8 times the rated working pressure.

sections.text: The internal stopper should not be damaged after extending 100 times. If the hydraulic system experiences a pressure higher than 1.8 times the rated working pressure, the column and support jack should extend 100 times under higher pressure, and the internal stopper should not be damaged.
When the support jack under tension is pulled out against the internal stopper with 1.5 times the rated tension, the support jack should not be damaged.

When the piston of the jack extends outward and contacts the internal stopper, the jack should be able to withstand 1.25 times the rated working pressure, and there should be no functional failure after the test.
Note: The internal stopper refers to the limit part such as the guide sleeve.

10) Function. After completing the above performance tests, the column and support jack should be able to retract the full stroke under external load starting from the fully extended position. The measured force should not be less than the rated force and not more than 1.1 times the force measured in the center pressure test; it should be able to retract completely under 0.8 times the rated working pressure, and meet the sealing performance requirements in 1.5.1).

11) Hydraulic cylinder connection points. The connection between the hydraulic cylinder (including the extended section) and the force transmission component should be able to withstand 1.5 times the rated force without functional failure.

12) Cylinder body burst performance. ① Cylinders that meet any of the following conditions should undergo a burst test: a. The cylinder body uses new materials. b. The cylinder diameter series is used for the first time. The material, nominal wall thickness, and nominal inner and outer diameters of the burst test specimen should be the same as those required for the hydraulic cylinder cylinder barrel, but the length can be shortened, but should not be less than the requirements in Table 4-213.

sections.text: ② After the cylinder body bursts, there should be no brittle fracture. (6) Material performance 1) Steel. ① General performance. When the calculated stress reaches 90% of the allowable stress, the tensile strength of the steel used in the hydraulic cylinder should not be less than 1.08 times the material's yield limit or 0.2% residual deformation limit. The fracture elongation δ5 of the steel used should not be less than 10%. Note: According to the provisions of GB/T 699-2015, the mechanical properties are expressed as the percentage elongation after fracture A(%); when A>10% is required, it excludes steel grades such as 65 and 70, because the A value of 60 steel is 10%, and the A value of 70 steel is 9%.

② Steel for welded parts. The grain size grade of steel measured according to GB/T 6394-2002 (2017) "Method for determining the average grain size of metals" should not be lower than grade 6; at -20°C, the Charpy impact absorption energy should not be less than 27 J.

③ Steel for non-welded parts. The steel used for the hydraulic cylinder barrel of non-welded parts should meet the requirements of 1.6.1)① and 1.6.1)②. Other steel for non-welded parts should have a Charpy impact absorption energy of not less than 25 J at 20°C. 2) Light metals. The outer surface of hydraulic cylinders used in mines with gas hazards should not use light metals or light metal alloys as described in Chapter 8 of GB 3836.1-2000 (2010) "Explosive atmospheres Part 1: Equipment - General requirements", including coatings and platings. 3) Other materials. Other materials used to manufacture hydraulic cylinder parts should meet the requirements of 1.6.1)①; non-metallic materials should meet the requirements of Chapter 7 of GB 3836.1-2000 (2010).

4.9 Reference Drawings for Hydraulic Cylinder Design and Selection

All the hydraulic cylinder drawings involved in this section are hydraulic cylinder product drawings designed, reviewed, approved, (re)manufactured, used, tested, accepted and repaired by the author in the past decade or so. The original drawings have been deleted according to relevant requirements including the protection of patent technology.

Due to the large time span, the author's cognition and understanding of hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing technology, the update of standards, the progress of technology, the improvement of design and manufacturing level, as well as the accumulation and summary of experience, these drawings are not perfect when examined with the current perspective. However, the actual service life of the hydraulic cylinders designed and manufactured by the author has been verified by practical machine verification (or demonstrative test).

Only some common and representative hydraulic cylinder drawings are selected in this section, and some products produced by professional manufacturers are not selected, such as automobile full hydraulic steering gear, coal mine hydraulic support, etc. designed and manufactured by the author.
This manual does not involve the so-called hydraulic cylinder or hydraulic device in which the piston and piston rod move spirally.

The focus of this section is to describe the structural design characteristics of hydraulic cylinder, and the seals in all drawings are simplified, and the nameplates, marks, etc. of each hydraulic cylinder are deleted.

(1) Basic Parameters and Working Conditions
This hydraulic cylinder is the main cylinder of the 8000 kN plastic products hydraulic press designed and manufactured by the author.

sections.text: The hydraulic cylinder is installed in an upper position, the boss stop of the cylinder head cooperates with the mounting hole of the body for positioning, and is locked on the upper crossbeam by the installation round nut; the connecting flange at the end of the piston rod is connected to the slider. The hydraulic cylinder has fast descending (cylinder process) and pressure holding requirements, but the hydraulic system is equipped with a special pressure supplementing system.

This hydraulic press is installed and used indoors, but the environment has a certain amount of dust pollution; it generally operates continuously for 24 hours, and the hydraulic system is equipped with an automatic temperature control device.
(2) Structural Design Features

As shown in Figure 4-6, the cylinder body 1 and piston rod 5 of this hydraulic cylinder are both forged parts made of 45 steel, which undergo rough machining followed by quenching and tempering treatment. The piston and piston rod are of an integrated structure, with the piston rod 5 being a solid rod. A filling valve is directly installed on the cylinder bottom for controlling filling during rapid descent of the slider. The piston sealing system 4 consists of bearing ring I (PTFE) + bearing ring II + bearing ring II + coaxial sealing element + bearing ring II + lip seal ring + bearing ring II + bearing ring I (PTFE), maximally ensuring bearing and guiding, while preventing pollution, withstanding impact, and reducing settling.

The cylinder head 8 (integrated with the guide sleeve) was originally designed with gray cast iron, but was later changed to nodular cast iron. The cylinder head 8 is connected to the cylinder body 1 by a flange connection, fastened with screws. The piston rod sealing system 7 consists of a coaxial sealing element + lip seal ring + dust seal ring; the inner bore of the cylinder head matches the diameter of the piston rod for bearing and guiding; the cylinder head 8 and cylinder body 1 are sealed with an O-ring + retaining ring.

The end of piston rod 5 is connected to flange 9 by threaded connection with piston rod 5, and is connected and fastened to the slider by screws, but only the end face of piston rod 5 is in close contact with the mounting surface of the slider. Both oil ports of the hydraulic cylinder are connected by flanges (2 and 6), with the diameter design of the flow channel holes in the two oil ports being particularly reasonable.

This hydraulic cylinder has sufficient strength and rigidity, reliable installation and connection, and strong guiding and bearing capacity for the piston and piston rod, capable of withstanding a certain amount of eccentric load. This hydraulic cylinder is not allowed to undergo pressure testing when the piston contacts the cylinder head (i.e., at the extreme dead point or maximum stroke position), meaning it cannot be tested or used when the stroke is >1200 mm, nor can the cylinder head be used as an actual stopper.

Due to the relatively large area of the two chambers (φ=3.6), a safety valve is installed in the rodless chamber of the hydraulic cylinder to prevent overpressure beyond the rated pressure limit caused by the area difference of the piston.
The designed stroke in the drawing is 1230 mm.

Cover 9, piston 4, and piston rod 7 are all made of 45 steel, with a metal support ring 8 installed in the cylinder cover 9. This hydraulic gate shearing machine main cylinder is a double-acting hydraulic cylinder with a nominal pressure of 25 MPa, a cylinder bore of 180 mm, a piston rod diameter of 100 mm, and a stroke of 200 mm. Since the main and auxiliary cylinders need to be connected in series to form a synchronous circuit to ensure that the (upper) tool holder and blade driven by the main and auxiliary cylinders do not change or change as little as possible during operation, the effective area of the rod cavity of the main cylinder needs to be equal or close to the effective area of the rodless cavity of the auxiliary cylinder, otherwise, the shearing angle is always in a changing state during the operation of the (upper) tool holder and blade.

This hydraulic upper-moving sheet metal bending machine hydraulic cylinder is a double-acting hydraulic cylinder with a nominal pressure of 25 MPa, a bore diameter of 180 mm, a piston rod diameter of 160 mm, and a stroke of 180 mm.

This hydraulic cylinder is fixedly installed to the frame through the stepped side surface of the cylinder body with threaded holes and fastened with screws. The piston rod end is connected with a spherical washer screw connection or a special pin double screw connection.

This hydraulic cylinder is adapted to a nominal force of 1000 kN torque shaft synchronous hydraulic upper-moving sheet metal bending machine, and consists of a pair of left and right cylinders with the same basic parameters except for the installation type and dimensions (mainly the direction and position of the oil port and stroke adjustment device). (2) Structural Design Features

As shown in Figure 4-14, all self-manufactured metal machined parts of this hydraulic cylinder are made of 45 steel. The cylinder body 7 has a square (rectangular) cross-section, and its side surface is generally equipped with a positioning step or keyway, so that the reaction force of the load acts on the mounting plate of the host machine body, ensuring that the mounting screws are free from shear force. The built-in stop block (or stopper) 5 is adjusted by a trapezoidal threaded shaft (or shaft) 12, and abuts against the piston end cover 9 during the cylinder process, thus positioning (limiting) the piston and piston rod.

Although the stroke adjustment devices of the left and right cylinders are controlled by one input shaft of the stroke adjustment device, the geometric accuracy and working accuracy of the host machine largely depend on the stroke positioning accuracy and stroke repeat positioning accuracy of a single hydraulic cylinder.

sections.text: Sealing system 3 of the piston rod consists of lip seal ring + support ring (2 rings) + lip seal ring + dust seal ring. The dust seal groove is set on the cylinder head (pressure cover) 1, while other seal ring grooves are set on the guide sleeve 2. The upper piston seal (system) 8 is a bidirectional seal rubber seal ring; static seals are all O-ring + retaining ring.

The piston rod sealing system 3, static seals, and rotating shaft seal 10 all adopt "redundant design". Both ports are generally threaded ports, using combined seal washers for sealing. This hydraulic cylinder generally cannot perform pressure tests when the piston contacts the guide sleeve, i.e., at the dead point of the cylinder process limit or maximum cylinder stroke. In other words, it cannot be tested or used when the stroke > 180 mm, and the guide sleeve cannot be used as an actual limiter. Since the areas of both chambers are relatively large (φ≈4.765), the hydraulic system should be equipped with a safety valve in the rod cavity of the hydraulic cylinder to prevent overpressure caused by the piston area difference from exceeding the rated pressure limit. However, some hydraulic up-moving plate bending machines currently do not have a safety valve installed in the rod cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.

This hydraulic cylinder is suitable for a CNC synchronous hydraulic up-moving plate bending machine with a nominal force of 1000kN. The CNC synchronous hydraulic plate bending machine was originally a type of bending machine specified in DB34/T2036-2014 (now repealed) and should now be called a CNC plate bending machine. (2) Structural Design Features

As shown in Figure 4-15, the self-made metal machined parts of this hydraulic cylinder are all made of 45 steel. Its piston rod sealing system 3 is a lip seal ring + support ring + lip seal ring + support ring + dust seal ring; the piston seal (system) 6 is a coaxial seal component + support ring (2 rings); static seals are O-ring + retaining ring. The piston rod sealing system adopts "redundant design". This hydraulic cylinder has the following features: 1) The piston rod sealing system 3 uses a lip seal ring instead of the coaxial seal component commonly used in general CNC hydraulic cylinders. 2) An insertion valve (charging valve) valve hole is set inside the cylinder body 4, and an oil passage block (cover plate) mounting surface is designed on the cylinder body 4. 3) The oil tank port uses flange connection, but this is not advisable. 4) The area ratio between the two chambers is super large (φ=8.258), allowing for faster cylinder return speed.

Due to the super large area ratio between the two chambers, this hydraulic cylinder cannot perform pressure tests when the piston contacts the cylinder head, i.e., at the dead point of the cylinder process limit or maximum cylinder stroke. In other words, it cannot be tested or used when the stroke > 120mm, and the cylinder head cannot be used as an actual limiter.

As shown in Figure 4-16, this hydraulic cylinder is a light-duty tension rod type hydraulic cylinder. The cylinder barrel 3 is made of 20 steel, while other self-made metal mechanical parts are made of 45 steel. Both ends of the cylinder stroke have buffer devices, which are a combination of fixed buffer devices and buffer valve buffer devices. The buffering performance can be adjusted through the throttle valve 10. The check valve 11 is used to prevent the cylinder from being immobile, sluggish, or suddenly jumping at startup, as well as to prevent possible abnormal noises. This is a common design for buffer valve buffer devices.
This buffer device only works when the buffer sleeve 5 or buffer plunger (integrated with the piston rod) enters the buffer chamber, and it has a certain buffering effect during the entry process.

The piston seal (system) 6 consists of a support ring + coaxial seal; the piston rod seal (system) 1 consists of a support ring + lip seal + dust seal, and all static seals are O-ring seals. The piston 7 is connected to the piston rod 4 by threads, and an elastic retaining ring is used for anti-loosening. The tension rod assembly should also adopt appropriate anti-loosening measures (not shown in the figure). Both oil ports are threaded ports sealed with combination sealing washers. There are also other non-fine threaded (M) oil ports. It should be noted that in the connection structure between the piston and piston rod, despite many references introducing or recommending the use of elastic retaining rings, based on the author's practical experience, elastic retaining rings (for holes) are neither necessarily reasonable nor necessarily reliable for preventing loosening of threaded connections or stopping (positioning) cylinder parts. They should be used as little as possible, as the author has repeatedly seen and handled cases where hydraulic cylinders were damaged or even scrapped due to elastic retaining rings detaching or breaking when this structure was used.

This is a booster, which is a hydraulic component that can convert the inlet pressure of a fluid into a higher secondary fluid outlet pressure. It is essentially a combined hydraulic cylinder.

Since the sealing material of this booster is selected as polytetrafluoroethylene and fluororubber, hydraulic oil and other working media compatible with the sealing material can be used, and two different fluids can also be used.
Rear-end circular flange installation.

(2) Structural design features: As shown in Figure 4-25, except for the metal support ring 13, which is made of tin bronze (such as ZQSn5-5-5), etc., all other self-made metal mechanical processing parts are made of 45 steel. The threaded flange I4 is connected to one end of the cylinder barrel 7 by threads, and the low-pressure cylinder bottom 3 is clamped between the rear-end circular flange 1 and the threaded flange I4, and the three are fastened together with screws; the threaded flange II9 is connected to the other end of the cylinder barrel 7 by threads, and the flange cylinder sleeve 10 is clamped between the threaded flange II9 and the high-pressure cylinder body 15, and fastened together with screws; the piston 6 and the piston rod 14 are an integral structure; both ends of the cylinder stroke are designed with fixed buffer devices; the booster is equipped with a lifting ring screw 16 for lifting. The piston seal (system) 5 is a support ring + support ring + coaxial seal + support ring + support ring; the piston rod seal system 12 is a support ring + support ring + coaxial seal + coaxial seal + metal support ring; static seals are all O-ring seals.

This booster also has the following features in structure: 1) The design and installation of two metal support rings is beneficial to reduce the sealing pressure that the coaxial seal bears during the boosting process. 2) The fixed buffer device designed and installed at both ends of the stroke can meet the frequent reversing of the low-pressure hydraulic cylinder to reduce or avoid impact on other parts. 3) The installation of proximity switches at both ends of the stroke can monitor or control the working or operation of the booster cylinder. 4) The design and installation of pressure test joints 2 and hexagon socket screw plugs 11 can be used to detect pressure, exhaust, etc. respectively. 5) The secondary fluid can be other fluids other than hydraulic oil, but it must be compatible with the sealing material and cannot cause corrosion of carbon steel. There are also some other features, such as the design to prevent the high-pressure joint from bursting out. However, fluids that are flammable, explosive, etc. and dangerous cannot use this booster for pressurization.

The piston seal and its design of this hydraulic cylinder are quite special. Generally, single-acting piston hydraulic cylinders do not use lip seal rings installed back to back for bidirectional sealing, nor do they use O-rings for reciprocating motion sealing. Its piston rod seal (system) only has dustproof, guiding and supporting functions, but not the function of sealing the working medium in the rod cavity.

Another feature of this hydraulic cylinder is the oil supply at the end of the piston rod. The piston rod is of hollow welded structure, with oil ports set on the single clevis at the end of the piston rod. The hydraulic oil acts on the piston and the end face of the through hole through the through hole, making the piston rod move in the cylinder process.

When the cylinder moves forward, the air in the rod cavity is discharged through the muffler 15; when the cylinder moves backward, the air in the rod cavity is sucked in through the muffler 15. It is feasible to consider using cold-drawn high-frequency welded pipe as part of the blank of the cylinder 9, because the technology of using cold-drawn high-frequency welded pipe as the cylinder tube below medium and high pressure is now very mature, especially when used as an ultra-long cylinder tube, which has more advantages. One of the advantages is that it can reduce the cost. The inner hole of the piston rod metal support ring 12 made of nodular cast iron can be rolled as a finishing process; the piston split metal support ring 4 made of tin bronze can also be rolled as a finishing process for the outer circle, and then cut into two halves after overall rolling.

The fixed buffer device of this hydraulic cylinder has certain characteristics. Since the structure of the buffer sleeve 3 is simple and the processing and measurement are relatively convenient and accurate, it can be modified or replaced according to the actual situation during trial or use. Therefore, the buffer performance of the return stroke of this hydraulic cylinder can be appropriately adjusted within a certain range; in addition, a one-way valve (not shown in the figure) is also set in the return stroke buffer device, and its function has been explained in the previous text.

As shown in Figure 4-46, the tandem cylinder is a cylinder with two pistons moving in the same separated chamber inside the same cylinder barrel, connected by piston rod I9 and piston rod II17 threads. (2) Structural and Process Characteristics

As shown in Figure 4-49, the cylinder body 3 and piston rods I and II of this hydraulic cylinder are all made of alloy steel. The piston rod I, piston rod II, and piston (not individually numbered in the figure) form an integral structure, and the piston diameter is equal to the outer diameter of piston rod I.

To prevent external leakage of the hydraulic cylinder and to provide a reliable lubricating oil film for the lip seal ring, leakage channels are opened between the piston seal and the sealing system of piston rod I, and between the coaxial seal component of piston rod II and the lip seal component, and they are interconnected.
The hydraulic cylinder is supplied with oil through the piston rod and is in a normally pressurized state.

The blank of the cylinder body of this hydraulic cylinder is a forging, with a relatively low material utilization rate. It is advisable to use die forging, but the one-time investment is large. Due to the large batch size, further research is necessary.

In addition, a special processing process for the cylinder body of this hydraulic cylinder is introduced: because the batch of this hydraulic cylinder is large, in order to achieve the interchangeability requirement for cylinder bodies (barrels) of the same model produced by the same manufacturer, although the cylinder body does not directly contact the piston rod, the inner hole coupled with the outer circle of the piston rod still adopts rolling as its finishing processing process.

5.1 Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders
5.1.1 Summary and Application of GB/T15622-2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders"
1. Summary

GB/T15622-2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders" was issued on July 11, 2005 and implemented from January 1, 2006, replacing GB/T15622-1995 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders". This standard is not only normatively referenced by JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" but also normatively referenced by other hydraulic cylinder product standards. To apply this standard well, the following is a summary of some of its contents.

items: Scope: This standard specifies test methods for hydraulic cylinders.
This standard applies to type tests and factory tests for hydraulic cylinders (including double-acting and single-acting hydraulic cylinders) using hydraulic oil (liquid) as the working medium.
This standard does not apply to combined hydraulic cylinders.

sections.text: 2. Normative References

The following documents contain provisions that, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. For dated references, subsequent amendments to, or revisions of, any of these publications do not apply. However, parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the normative documents indicated below. For undated references, the latest edition of the normative document referred to applies.

items: GB/T14039-2002 Hydraulic Fluid Power - Fluids - Code for Levels of Contamination by Solid Particles
GB/T17446 Fluid power systems and components - Vocabulary (GB/T17446-1998)

sections.text: 3.1 Minimum Starting Pressure
The minimum pressure at which a hydraulic cylinder starts to move.
3.4 Load Efficiency
The ratio of the actual output force of a hydraulic cylinder to its theoretical output force. The symbols and units used in this standard are shown in Table 5-1.
6.7 Load Efficiency Test

sections.text: 2. Application

As a normative reference document of JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", most of the contents of GB/T15622-2005 (including the summary contents above) are cited in JB/T10205-2010; however, the following points should be noted when applying this standard.
(1) Combined Hydraulic Cylinders

The research on the term and definition of "combined hydraulic cylinder" is to determine the scope of application of this standard. GB/T17446-1998 "Fluid Power Systems and Components - Vocabulary" is normatively referenced in the normative references of this standard but without a date, indicating that GB/T17446-2012 "Fluid Power Systems and Components - Vocabulary" applies to this standard. Neither GB/T17446-1998 nor GB/T17446-2012 contains the term and definition of "combined hydraulic cylinder", and this term and definition are not found in other hydraulic cylinder-related standards, nor is this term defined in this standard.
Further consultation of five manuals related to hydraulic cylinder classification yielded the following:

sections.text: To determine the scope of application specified in the standard GB/T 15622—2005, it is necessary to define the term "combined (type) hydraulic cylinder." Here is a tentative definition of the term "combined hydraulic cylinder": a hydraulic cylinder composed of two or more hydraulic cylinders assembled together as a single unit.

Based on this definition, a spring-return single-acting cylinder is not a combined (type) hydraulic cylinder; while a swing hydraulic cylinder is a combined (type) hydraulic cylinder, but does not include devices or parts that convert the reciprocating linear motion of the hydraulic cylinder into the reciprocating rotary motion of gears, etc.

There are also cases where combined (type) hydraulic cylinders are referred to as compound hydraulic cylinders. In some literature, the definition of compound hydraulic cylinder has been proposed, i.e., a compound hydraulic cylinder is a hydraulic cylinder assembled from different hydraulic cylinders or other hydraulic components. If this definition is followed, the same servo hydraulic cylinder, if the servo valve is installed on its cylinder body, can be called a compound hydraulic cylinder after being assembled into a single hydraulic cylinder; while if the servo valve is connected to it through pipelines, this type of hydraulic cylinder cannot be called a compound hydraulic cylinder, which obviously presents a problem.
For the types and classification of hydraulic cylinders, please refer to Section 2.1.1 of this book.
(2) Minimum Starting Pressure and Load Efficiency

The study of the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" is to enable non-professional personnel who have not participated in the compilation of the standard to clearly understand, correctly apply, and cite the national standard GB/T 15622—2005.
In both GB/T 15622—2005 and JB/T 10205—2010, the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" are defined.

In the normative references of GB/T 15622—2005, GB/T 17446—2012 (1998), there are two terms: "starting pressure" and "cylinder output force efficiency," which are defined as the minimum pressure required to initiate motion (action) and the ratio between the actual (effective) output force of the cylinder and the theoretical output force, respectively. Comparing the definitions of "minimum starting pressure" with "starting pressure" and "load efficiency" with "cylinder output force efficiency" in GB/T 15622—2005 and GB/T 17446, the following can be found:

items: Using "minimum" to define "minimum," the concept and term are the same, which is equivalent to not defining it.
Different terms but the same definition do not conform to the uniqueness of terms.
It violates the statement: "The following terms and definitions given in GB/T 17446 as well as the following are applicable to this standard."

sections.text: In GB/T 15622—2005, the term "minimum starting pressure" and its definition do not follow the method of selecting terms and writing definitions as "terms expressing more specific concepts can usually be composed of terms expressing more general concepts"; "load efficiency" not only does not conform to the requirement that terms should have uniqueness but also does not comply with the principle of not repeating the definition of terms that have been defined in other authoritative vocabularies. Therefore, it is unnecessary to reselect and define the terms "minimum starting pressure" and "load efficiency" in GB/T 15622—2005.

GB/T 1.1—2009 "Guidelines for Standardization Part 1: Structure and Drafting of Standards" stipulates that synonymous terms should be avoided for concepts that have already been defined. Further references can be made to GB/T 20000.1—2002 "Guide to Standardization Part 1: General Vocabulary of Standardization and Related Activities," GB/T 10112—2019 "Terminology Work Principles and Methods," and GB/T 15237.1—2000 "Terminology Work Vocabulary Part 1: Theory and Application" and other related standards.
(3) Effective Area of Piston Rod
The study of the name and symbol of the "effective area of piston rod" is mainly to solve the calculation problem of load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency.
In the normative references of GB/T 15622—2005, GB/T 17446, there is no term and definition of "effective area of piston rod," but there is the term and definition of "piston rod area."
In GB/T 17446—1998 and GB/T 17446—2012, the term "piston rod area" is defined as "the cross-sectional area of the piston rod" and "the cross-sectional area of the piston rod," respectively.

As a normative reference file of GB/T 15622—2005, although JB/T 10205—2010 is consistent with the referenced file in "quantity, symbol, and unit," it later changes "effective area of piston rod" to "numerical value of effective area of piston" in "load efficiency test," with the symbol still being "A."
The term "effective area of piston" only appears in GB/T 17446—1998, with its definition being: the area that generates mechanical force under the action of fluid force.

It seems that neither GB/T 15622—2005 nor JB/T 10205—2010 can calculate the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of single-acting and double-acting hydraulic cylinders specified in the standard scope.
(4) Calculation and Test of Load Efficiency

If the issues of the name and symbol of the "effective area of piston rod" mentioned above are not resolved, the calculation of load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of double-acting hydraulic cylinders and single-acting hydraulic cylinders specified in GB/T 15622—2005 cannot be carried out.

items: According to "symbols and units" and "load efficiency test" in GB/T 15622—2005, only the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of plunger cylinders can be calculated, while the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of double-acting piston cylinders and single-acting piston cylinders cannot be calculated.

According to "quantity, symbol, and unit" and "load efficiency test" in JB/T 10205—2010, due to inconsistency before and after, the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency cannot be calculated.

According to "load efficiency test" in JB/T 10205—2010, only the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of piston cylinders can be calculated, while the load efficiency or cylinder output force efficiency of plunger cylinders cannot be calculated.

sections.text: The load efficiency of a cylinder or the output force efficiency of a cylinder cannot be calculated.

Based on the above analysis, in the "Symbols and Units" or "Quantities, Symbols and Units" of GB/T 15622—2005 or JB/T 10205—2010, "Piston (Effective) Area" can be added, or "Piston Rod Effective Area" can be deleted, and "Cylinder Effective Area" can be added. Otherwise, the load efficiency of single and double-acting piston cylinders specified in the standard range cannot be calculated.

It should be noted that if the hydraulic cylinder type test hydraulic system given in Figure 4 of GB/T 15622—2005 is used for load efficiency testing, some small-sized hydraulic cylinders may not be able to proceed due to the maximum speed during testing exceeding the designed maximum speed and/or excessive back pressure; general hydraulic cylinders will also fail to achieve the purpose of verifying the load-bearing static friction force of the hydraulic cylinder through load efficiency testing due to the inability to limit the back pressure.

In addition, there are issues of confusion and misuse of terms such as trial operation and trial running, nominal pressure and rated pressure, double-rod cylinder and double piston rod (hydraulic) cylinder, leakage and seepage, stroke and maximum stroke, etc. in GB/T 15622—2005, as well as some other issues, which are worth further discussion.
5.1.2 JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Summary and Its Application

JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" was issued on February 11, 2010 and implemented on July 1, 2010, which has been over 10 years. Compared with other hydraulic cylinder product standards, it has a wider applicable range, so it is widely followed by other hydraulic cylinders without product standards in design and manufacturing.
The study of JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard is to better comply with this standard, and to design and manufacture better hydraulic cylinders by applying or referring to this standard.
1. Scope
(1) Summary
1 Scope

This standard specifies the classification and basic parameters, technical requirements, test methods, inspection rules, packaging, transportation and other requirements for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders.

This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure of 31.5 MPa or less, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium. For hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure higher than 31.5 MPa, this standard may be referred to. Special requirements other than those specified in this standard shall be negotiated between the hydraulic cylinder manufacturer and the user.
(2) Application
Based on the writing characteristics of the standard, the standard lacks hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure of 31.5 MPa.

According to the provisions of GB/T 8170—2008, the correct statement should be: This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure less (lower) than or equal to 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium.

It can also be expressed as: This standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure not greater (higher) than 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as the working medium.

(1) Summary

(2) Application

JB/T10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" replaced JB/T10205—2000 "Technical Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders" which was first published in August 2000. In JB/T10205—2000, the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders (Table 5) and the internal leakage of single-acting hydraulic cylinders (Table 6) differ from Tables 5-7 and 5-8 only in the "Notes", indicating that there has been no change in the performance indicators for internal leakage of piston-type single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders in factory tests over the past 20 years.

In JB/JQ20301—1988 "Grading of Product Quality for Medium and High-pressure Hydraulic Cylinders (Trial Implementation)", Table 1 lists the inspection items and key items for quality grading. The internal leakage indicators for medium and high-pressure hydraulic cylinders with cylinder bores of 40-250 mm are also the same as in Table 5-7, but there is no distinction made between the internal leakage of piston-type double-acting and single-acting hydraulic cylinders, nor are there any "Notes" regarding checking internal leakage by settling amount.

Based on the above summary and the distribution of versions of this standard that it has replaced, the following points should be noted when applying the performance indicators for internal leakage of piston-type single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders in JB/T10205—2010: 1) Internal leakage of piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders. In Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010, the internal leakage (values) listed for piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders is twice or more than that listed in Table 6 for double-acting hydraulic cylinders. Table 6 of JB/T10205—2010 can be traced back at least to JB/JQ20301—1988, and its evolution is clear, indicating industry consensus; however, Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010 is not in JB/JQ20301—1988 and can only be traced back to JB/T10205—2000.

Considering factors such as the sealing structure and mechanism of hydraulic cylinders and test conditions, the internal leakage (values) listed for piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders in Table 7 of JB/T10205—2010 are not entirely reasonable. 2) Checking internal leakage of piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders by settling amount. Since internal leakage of piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinders can be checked (measured) by settling amount, then piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders should also be able to use settling amount to check (measure) their internal leakage. In standards such as JB/T9834—2014 "Technical Conditions for Agricultural Double-acting Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T11588—2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated that the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders can be measured or calculated by settling amount.
When using settling amount to measure or calculate the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders, testing (trial) methods should be specified.

There is a one-to-one correspondence between settling amount and internal leakage, and the values are basically equivalent after conversion, as shown in Table 5-7 above. If it is confirmed that the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders given in Table 6 of JB/T10205—2010 is reasonable, then the settling amount of double-acting hydraulic cylinders can only be around 0.025 mm/min. 3) Internal leakage of hydraulic cylinders and technological progress. Despite the JB2146—

744.page_header: Chapter 5 Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders 733

sections.text: 1977 "Hydraulic Component Factory Test Technical Indicators" and JB/JQ20301-1988 "Medium and High Pressure Hydraulic Cylinder Product Quality Classification (Trial)" and JB/T10205-2000 "Hydraulic Cylinder Technical Conditions" and JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" have no substitution or reference relationship, but because it is stipulated in JB2146-1977 that the allowable value of internal leakage is calculated based on the cylinder sinking amount of 0.5mm/5min (0.1mm/min). This not only shows that the sinking amount can be used to detect the internal leakage of piston-type double-acting hydraulic cylinders, but also shows the technical progress of the internal leakage performance index of hydraulic cylinders.

Standards should fully consider the latest technical level and provide a framework for future technological development. In terms of the internal leakage of double-acting hydraulic cylinders, a performance index of hydraulic cylinders, JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" has not changed since JB/JQ20301-1988 "Medium and High Pressure Hydraulic Cylinder Product Quality Classification (Trial)" implemented in October 1988, and the standard cannot reflect that it is based on a summary of modern science, technology and experience.

Technology is always progressing. In Table 7 of JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinder", there is a note: "For special specifications of hydraulic cylinders, the internal leakage is calculated based on the displacement of 0.01mm/min when the rodless chamber is pressurized." The above statement in JB/T11588-2013 is not entirely correct. For further reference, see Table 5-10 in Section 5.1.3 of this chapter and JB/T9834-2014 "Agricultural Double-Acting Cylinder Technical Conditions".

A sealing form composed of a sliding ring (made of a material with a low friction coefficient and self-lubricating properties) and an O-ring, etc.
3.2 Load efficiency
The percentage of the actual output force of the hydraulic cylinder to the theoretical output force.
3.3 Minimum starting pressure
The minimum pressure for the hydraulic cylinder to start.
2) Application. In JB/T8241-1996 "Coaxial Seal Vocabulary", the terms and definitions of coaxial seals have been determined, namely
2 Terms
2.1 Coaxial seal
A combination seal composed of a plastic ring and a rubber ring, with the plastic ring as the entire friction sealing surface.
2.2 Plastic ring
A plastic seal ring that acts as a friction sealing surface in a coaxial seal.
2.3 Rubber ring
A rubber seal ring that provides sealing pressure in a coaxial seal and compensates for the wear of the plastic ring.
In GB/T17446-2012 (1998), the following two terms have been defined (determined), namely
3.2.82 (2.2.4.12) Starting pressure - The minimum pressure required to start movement.
3.2.164 (3.5.3.7.1) Cylinder output force efficiency (output force efficiency) - The ratio between the actual output force and theoretical output force of the cylinder.
There is no need to redefine terms (vocabulary) that have been determined (defined) in other current standards. Moreover, after comparison, there are some problems with the redefined terms:

items: For the sliding ring in the sliding ring combination seal, it is not clearly stated that it should be a plastic ring.
In the sliding ring combination seal, O-rings, etc., one of the components is not only O-rings, but also square (rectangular) rings; secondly, the expression of O-rings, etc. is prone to ambiguity.
The percentage in load efficiency is inaccurately expressed.
The two words "minimum" in minimum starting pressure are redundant.

items: Terms. The following terms or vocabulary are defined in GB/T 17446: Bore diameter: The inner diameter of the cylinder body. Cylinder stroke: The distance moved by its movable part from one extreme position to the other. Cylinder output force: The force generated by the pressure acting on the piston. Cylinder output force efficiency: The ratio between the actual output force of the cylinder and the theoretical output force. External leakage: Leakage from the inside of a component or pipe to the surrounding environment. Internal leakage: Leakage between internal cavities of a component. Effective area of cylinder: The area on which fluid pressure acts to provide usable force. The following terms or vocabulary are not defined in GB/T 17446: Cylinder bore, sleeve diameter, piston rod diameter, plunger diameter, external leakage (amount), effective area of piston rod, actual output force, load efficiency.

In GB/T 2348—1993 "Cylinder Bore and Piston Rod Outer Diameter for Hydraulic and Pneumatic Systems and Components", the cylinder bore and piston rod diameter for hydraulic cylinders and pneumatic cylinders used in hydraulic and pneumatic systems and components are specified.

In Table 5-9 (Table 1 of JB/T 10205—2010), W is the actual output force, while in Abstract 7.2.7, W is the actual output force, which is inconsistent.

1) Abstract.
7.3.3  Pressure Resistance Test
The specific content is shown in item (1) of this article.

2) Application. In GB/T 17446—2012, there is no term "stroke", only "cylinder stroke". Judging from the subsequent "single-acting hydraulic cylinder in the extreme position of the stroke" and the definition of cylinder stroke, the "two ends of the stroke" in the above text should be the extreme positions of the cylinder stroke respectively.

The terminal position of the return stroke. In general hydraulic cylinders, the piston of single and double-acting piston cylinders and the piston rod head of single-acting plunger cylinders are often used as limiters. When the piston or piston rod head contacts other cylinder parts, it is one end of the cylinder stroke (the terminal position of the cylinder process or the terminal position of the cylinder return stroke). In high-pressure and high-speed (high-speed return stroke of the cylinder) hydraulic cylinders, the piston diameter (or cylinder bore) and piston rod diameter, and the piston rod head diameter and piston rod diameter are not much different. In this case, if the working chamber is subjected to hydraulic oil with a pressure of 1.5 times the nominal pressure for a pressure test at the terminal position of the cylinder process, the cylinder parts may be damaged. Therefore, in some other hydraulic cylinder product standards, there are: "During the pressure resistance test of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested, the piston of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested should be stopped at both ends of the stroke (cannot contact the cylinder cover)" or "(During the pressure resistance test of the double-acting piston hydraulic cylinder) When pressurizing from the rodless end, fix the piston near the end of the stroke for the test; when pressurizing from the rod end, fix the piston near the starting position of the stroke for the test". About the stroke of the cylinder, see Section 1.3.2.
(6) Factory Inspection
1) Summary
10.1.2 Factory Inspection

Factory inspection refers to the inspection that must be performed on each unit when the product is delivered, which is divided into mandatory inspection items and sampling inspection items. For the performance inspection items and methods of mandatory inspection items in factory inspection, refer to the regulations in 7.1-7.3, among which the test items are 7.3.1, 7.3.2, 7.3.3, 7.3.5, 7.3.6, 7.3.9; the performance requirements should respectively comply with the regulations in 6.2.1, 6.2.7, 6.2.2, 6.2.3.1, 6.2.3.2, 6.2.4, 6.2.8, 6.1.6.
2) Application. In JB/T 10205-2010, there is no clause "6.1.6" at all, and its "performance requirements should comply with the provisions of 6.1.6" points to nothing.
(7) Buffer Test
1) Summary
6.2.8 Buffer
The buffer performance of the hydraulic cylinder shall be determined through consultation between the user and the manufacturer if required.
7.3 Buffer Test

All buffer valves in the working chamber of the hydraulic cylinder to be tested shall be loosened, the test pressure shall be adjusted to 50% of the nominal pressure, and the movement shall be carried out at the highest designed speed. When all buffer valves are closed during operation, the buffer effect shall meet the requirements of 6.2.8.

2) Application. Buffering is a means for moving parts (such as pistons) to decelerate when approaching the end of their movement. There are mainly two types: fixed (type) and adjustable (type). Obviously, the test method for fixed (type) buffering (device) is missing in GB/T 10205-2010. The buffer valve buffer (device) is generally composed of a one-way valve and an adjustable throttle valve. The "buffer valve loosening" mentioned in GB/T 10205-2010 should be the loosening of the throttle valve, but the adjustment of the throttle valve is generally not based on the buffer stroke, that is, the buffer valve cannot automatically close during the operation of the hydraulic cylinder.
This can be evidenced by "The throttle and (or) buffer elements installed on the hydraulic cylinder have no hydraulic (external) leakage" in JB/T 10205-2010.

(8) Other Precautions. In addition to the specific matters that should be noted when selecting and applying JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" as mentioned above, the following points should also be noted: 1) The normative reference documents do not have the groove for the sealing ring used for the static sealing of the hydraulic cylinder. 2) There is no GB/T 15242.3-1994 in the normative reference documents. In its terms and definitions, the sealing type of "sliding ring combined seal" does not have a corresponding installation groove and cannot be used. 3) There are no model marking regulations and marking examples in the classification, marking and basic parameters. 4) The safety technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders are missing. 5) The provisions on pressure resistance and pressure resistance test lack theoretical basis and are inconsistent with other standards, such as JB/T 3818-2014. 6) The provisions on the working medium temperature of the hydraulic cylinder lack theoretical basis and are inconsistent with other standards, such as JB/T 3818-2014. 7) At least one group of values of the internal leakage (specified value or allowable value) of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder and the internal leakage (specified value or allowable value) of the piston-type single-acting hydraulic cylinder are worth discussing. 8) The low-temperature performance, stroke positioning performance, half-stroke internal leakage, piston (rod) runout and durability under certain lateral forces of the hydraulic cylinder are missing in the JB/T 10205-2010 standard. 9) Other issues, such as the lack of auxiliary verbs in clause expressions or many situations that do not comply with the rules for using auxiliary verbs given in GB/T 1.1-2009.

Up to now (October 2020), there has been no amendment sheet for JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder", including the errata sheet. In short, in order to be able to design and manufacture hydraulic cylinders that meet the standard requirements by complying with the "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard, the "Hydraulic Cylinder" standard itself should first be rigorous and accurate, and should be a summary of science, technology and experience, and at the same time, it should provide a framework for the future technical development of hydraulic cylinders.
5.1.3 Comparison and Application of Hydraulic Cylinder Test Methods in Current Standards

3. Application of Test Items and Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders
When applying or referencing test items and methods in various standards, the following points should be noted.
(1) Pressure Test (Test) Pressure
In the pressure test, the pressure test (test) pressure is specified differently in various standards, such as nominal pressure, rated pressure, nominal working pressure, and rated working pressure.
Only "Nominal Pressure" and "Rated Pressure" are defined in GB/T17446—2012.
The pressure test represented by nominal pressure or rated pressure has a specific meaning, while others may be ambiguous.

In the standards listed in Table 5-10, the highest is "1.5 times the nominal pressure" for the pressure test (test) pressure. In hydraulic transmission systems and components, the pressure test pressure is second only to the burst pressure. Generally, only the pressure test (performance) test can be conducted under the pressure test pressure, and other performance tests cannot be performed. The pressure test is a static pressure test.

This point is particularly important for cylinders. In pressure tests, the specification of "holding pressure for 10 seconds during factory testing" is the most scientific. Other specifications such as holding pressure for 2 minutes (or even 5 minutes in some cases) at 1.5 times the nominal pressure, even if the hydraulic cylinder being tested passes the test, may cause irreparable damage to the cylinder.

"Nominal pressure" and "rated pressure" are also used in sealing tests. In any case, the test pressure for hydraulic cylinder sealing tests should not be higher than or equal to the pressure test pressure, and the corresponding holding time for static sealing factory tests should also be reasonably specified. Otherwise, after factory testing, the hydraulic cylinder being tested will be scrapped.
(2) Piston and Piston Rod
The piston and piston rod are cylinder components that can perform reciprocating motion relative to the cylinder body (barrel), and the piston and piston rod are coaxial and connected as one unit.

In some hydraulic cylinder test standards, the states of hydraulic cylinder operation and stopping are often described by the relative position between the piston and the cylinder body (barrel). Such descriptions are mostly necessary, but since the piston is hidden inside the cylinder body (barrel) and cannot be directly observed, only the exposed piston rod can be visually judged during hydraulic cylinder testing. Therefore, the descriptions of piston position during hydraulic cylinder operation and stopping lack simultaneous descriptions of the piston rod.

In DB44/T1169.2-2013, regardless of whether the specified test methods are correct and feasible, only in the general provisions for eccentricity test "detecting the eccentricity of the piston rod during piston movement for hydraulic cylinders with piston diameter greater than 500mm under loaded conditions," the word "所" (meaning "during") in "piston movement 所 piston rod" is difficult to understand.

Even for hydraulic cylinders with built-in displacement sensors or servo hydraulic cylinders, there is still the issue of simultaneous description of the piston and piston rod when the hydraulic cylinder is running and stopping. Additionally, plunger cylinders do not have pistons, only piston rods, so describing the state of the hydraulic cylinder using the piston rod is more accurate.
(3) Placement of Hydraulic Cylinder

GB/T 15622-2005 provides two placement methods for hydraulic cylinder testing: horizontal placement and inclined placement. During hydraulic cylinder testing, it is generally impossible to simulate actual working conditions, i.e., it is impossible to simulate the installation type, connection type, and force conditions on the host machine. Therefore, the tested hydraulic cylinder generally does not bear lateral loads or perform lateral force loading.
Different placements of the tested hydraulic cylinder may directly affect test results, and some performances may not even be testable, such as the settlement of the hydraulic cylinder.
JB/T 10205-2010 also stipulates: "The test device for hydraulic cylinders should generally adopt a plane device with a horizontal foundation as the standard."
(4) Internal Leakage Test

Most hydraulic cylinder tests require "stopping the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at both ends of the stroke" respectively, and measuring the leakage amount leaking through the piston to the unpressurized chamber. Without discussing whether the two ends are the (stroke) limit positions or other positions, but conducting internal leakage tests by "stopping the piston at both ends and the middle of the hydraulic cylinder respectively" is more reasonable, especially for hydraulic cylinders with a stroke exceeding 1000mm, this specification is even more reasonable.

During internal leakage testing, the temperature of the hydraulic oil (fluid) input to the tested hydraulic cylinder cannot be lowered, otherwise the test measurement values will be inaccurate. More importantly, the viscosity of the test hydraulic oil must comply with regulations or be agreed upon by the manufacturer and user. Otherwise, internal leakage tests conducted at the user's site, including settlement tests, may exceed standards.
(5) Settlement Measurement Method

The internal leakage factory test method given in Table 6 of JB/T 9834-2014 is not entirely reasonable (see Table 5-10). For example, oil supply to both chambers of the tested cylinder is required, but it should be stipulated that the hydraulic cylinder cannot operate at high speed; closing the shut-off valve on the supply oil chamber can only be a shut-off valve installed in the rodless chamber, not a shut-off valve installed in the rod chamber; using a loading cylinder to make the supply chamber oil pressure reach the test pressure, but it must be stipulated that it is the rodless chamber.

The correct method for settlement testing to check internal leakage should be: supplying oil to both chambers of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder respectively, allowing it to run at low speed; under the condition of ensuring the rodless chamber is free of air, and the amount of air mixed in the test oil meets the regulations, closing the shut-off valve near the oil port of the rodless chamber, making the piston and piston rod stop at a certain distance from the cylinder return stroke limit position or a specified position (generally should include the cylinder stroke limit position and the middle position of the cylinder stroke), and opening the oil port of the rod chamber, allowing it to communicate directly with the atmosphere; through external loading (force), the pressure in the rodless chamber should always be maintained at the test pressure (nominal pressure), and the displacement of the piston (piston rod) should be measured after 1 minute.

According to the settlement measurement method given by the author above, the hydraulic system schematic diagram for type testing of hydraulic cylinders shown in Figure 5-1 and the hydraulic system schematic diagram of the loading device for digital hydraulic cylinder type testing shown in Figure 5-2 do not have the function of active loading with fixed direction and fixed pressure, and cannot be used to complete this test.
5.1.4 Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Test

Except for hydraulic cylinders with product standards, other hydraulic cylinders (including those with special technical requirements, special structures, and hydraulic cylinders) can perform sealing performance tests according to this. For sealing performance test items missing in various product standards, tests can also be conducted by referring to this method and rules.
