sections.text: 2. Test Equipment

The factory test equipment for hydraulic cylinder sealing performance should generally consist of a loading test equipment and a hydraulic cylinder test operation table (including hydraulic system, testing instruments, meters, devices, and/or electrical control, operating devices, and other control equipment).

756.page_header: Chapter 5 Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders 745

sections.text: Composition of the device.
According to the relevant standards for hydraulic cylinder testing, the factory sealing performance test device of hydraulic cylinders should have the following performance:

items: It should be equipped with a device for applying external loads to the tested hydraulic cylinder, and the load should act along the centerline of the hydraulic cylinder. It should be able to generate a pressure greater than or equal to 1.5 times the nominal pressure in each working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, and can serve as an actual stopper for the tested hydraulic cylinder at various positions of the stroke, including the two extreme positions of the hydraulic cylinder stroke (i.e., the so-called stroke ends). It can also be equipped with a device for applying lateral force (load) to the tested hydraulic cylinder. The installation, connection, and placement of the hydraulic cylinder (type) test should be consistent with the actual working conditions.

The hydraulic system should be equipped with a relief valve to prevent the tested hydraulic cylinder from bearing a pressure exceeding 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure, especially to prevent the pressure increase in the rodless cavity of the hydraulic cylinder due to the piston area difference from exceeding the above-mentioned pressure; a manual pressure relief device for each chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder should be set up; necessary safety devices should be set up, and reliable protective measures should be adopted to ensure the safety of equipment and personnel.

The hydraulic system should be able to apply a pressure of 0 to 1.5 times the nominal pressure or higher to the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to make the hydraulic cylinder run continuously (reversing) stably at the nominal pressure (or rated pressure) and 0 to the highest design speed; it should be able to apply a back pressure of 0.2 MPa to the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to make the oil temperature in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder reach and maintain +50℃±4℃ or +90℃±4℃; the solid particle contamination level code of the oil in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder should not be higher than 19/15 or —/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039.

Both chambers (oil ports) of the tested hydraulic cylinder should be able to be connected to the system, cut off from the system, and also open to the atmosphere after being cut off from the system; the pressure measurement point should be set at a distance of about 2d to 4d from the oil port of the tested hydraulic cylinder (d is the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline), and the temperature measurement point should be set at a distance of 2d to 4d from the pressure measurement point (d is the same as above).

The allowable system error of the measurement system and the allowable variation range of the average display value of the controlled parameters should be specified according to the relevant standards. It should be able to detect a pressure of 0.03 MPa (the minimum starting pressure of the servo hydraulic cylinder) up to 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure, and the range of the (pressure gauge) should generally be (1.5 to 2.0)×1.5×nominal pressure; it should be able to detect an input flow rate of 0.02 mL/min up to the flow rate that enables the tested hydraulic cylinder to run at the highest design speed; it should be able to detect a force greater than or equal to the theoretical output force of the tested hydraulic cylinder; it should be able to detect the stroke and deviation of the tested hydraulic cylinder; or it should be able to accurately detect the cylinder stroke positioning accuracy and stroke repeated positioning accuracy of the tested hydraulic cylinder with special technical requirements or special structures. It should also be able to automatically accumulate the number of reversals (counting), timing, ambient temperature measurement, etc. The measurement of the inclination, rocking, vibration, and eccentricity of the hydraulic cylinder should be carried out according to the relevant standards.
The electrical control voltage should be DC 24V, and it should be equipped with reliable grounding connection. The electrical operation device (station) should be set independently and can be moved.

sections.text: The environmental pollution degree, background noise level, power capacity and quality, fire protection facilities, safety protection measures, etc. of the installation site of the test device should all comply with the relevant standards.

Taking the "Figure 3 Factory Test Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram" (see Figure 5-1) given in GB/T 15622-2005 "Hydraulic Cylinder Test Method" as an example, according to the mandatory inspection items, rules (methods or steps) for hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" and the corresponding mandatory test items and rules for the sealing performance of hydraulic cylinders, the following points should be noted when applying GB/T 15622-2005 "Figure 3 Factory Test Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram":

items: (1) Oil Tank: Since there is no heat exchanger designed and installed in the oil tank shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, the oil temperature in the oil tank and the input port of the hydraulic cylinder cannot be guaranteed to reach and maintain the specified temperature and allowable variation range. Therefore, all the mandatory inspection items specified in JB/T 10205 and all the mandatory test items specified in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test cannot obtain accurate test measurement values and converted values, that is, they do not meet the test conditions specified in JB/T 10205.

(2) Filter: Since only a coarse filter is allowed on the hydraulic pump suction pipeline, the filter shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005 can only be a coarse filter. The oil filtered by the coarse filter cannot guarantee that it meets the test oil contamination level specified in JB/T 10205 and in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test, that is, the solid particle contamination level code of the oil in the input port of the hydraulic cylinder should not be higher than 19/15 or —/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039, that is, it does not meet the test conditions specified in JB/T 10205.

(3) Hydraulic Pump: Since there is only one fixed displacement hydraulic pump and one relief valve in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, and it is a return throttling, no bypass throttling speed control system, this system cannot achieve (obtain) stable operation (condition) under no-load conditions with low pressure and low speed, that is, it cannot carry out the mandatory inspection items specified in JB/T 10205 and the mandatory test items "test run" specified in the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance test, that is, "starting pressure characteristic test"; or it cannot carry out the test items of "low pressure and low speed test" and "leakage under low pressure".

(4) Relief Valve: Since there is only one relief valve in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622-2005, if the hydraulic system is to be able to adjust out a stable pressure condition between less than 0.3 MPa (or 0.03 MPa) and greater than or equal to 1.5×31.5 MPa (or 1.1×1.5×nominal pressure), it is almost impossible in terms of the performance (such as pressure regulating range) of the existing relief valve. Moreover, to prevent the pressure increase in the rodless cavity of the tested hydraulic cylinder due to the piston area difference, a relief valve should be set in the rodless cavity.
(5) Loading Device

sections.text: Because the loading device is not shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622—2005, while the "Schematic Diagram of Hydraulic System for Type Test" shown in Figure 4 of GB/T includes a loading device, it is determined that the "Schematic Diagram of Hydraulic System for Factory Test" shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622—2005 does not include a loading device.

Without a loading device, not only can the settling amount not be inspected, but the mandatory inspection item "7.3.3 Pressure Test" specified in JB/T 10205 may also not be possible to perform. Because not all tested hydraulic cylinders allow the piston to stop at both ends of the stroke (limit positions) (single-acting hydraulic cylinders are in the advancing position) and be subjected to pressure test pressure, if the tested hydraulic cylinder has the above requirements, the hydraulic system will not be able to pressurize to the pressure test pressure, and thus cannot apply hydraulic fluid with 1.5 times the nominal pressure (or rated pressure) to the working chamber, so the pressure test cannot be performed.
Similarly, without a loading device, it is also impossible to perform cylinder thrust efficiency or load efficiency tests.
(6) Pressure Gauges, Flowmeters, and Others

Pressure gauges and flowmeters are similar to the above-mentioned relief valves, mainly because the range and accuracy of a single pressure gauge or flowmeter cannot meet the requirements specified in the relevant standards. The temperature measurement point cannot be set only on the oil tank, as the relevant standards stipulate that the temperature measurement point should be set near the pressure measurement point. Since there is no bypass throttling speed regulation (circuit) in the hydraulic system shown in Figure 3 of GB/T 15622—2005, it is difficult for this system to meet the various speed requirements during the testing of the hydraulic cylinder under test, such as the designed maximum speed. The current standards do not require all hydraulic cylinders to be equipped with exhaust devices, so the hydraulic system should be equipped with exhaust devices to minimize the amount of air entering the pipelines, components, and accessories (such as the oil tank). In summary, it is necessary to provide a schematic diagram of the hydraulic system for the hydraulic cylinder sealing performance factory test device, as shown in Figure 5-3.

5.1.4.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Test Method and Inspection Rules
1. Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance
In all the following tests, there should be no damage to any components (including sealing elements).

In all the following tests, except for the piston rod seal, there should be no external leakage or seepage at other locations; there should be no external leakage when the hydraulic cylinder is stationary at the piston rod; there should be no seepage on the outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder body (barrel).
In low-pressure, low-speed tests and internal leakage tests, the internal leakage should not exceed the standard specified values.
When checking (measuring) the internal leakage amount by the settlement method, the settlement amount should not exceed the standard specified value.
During operation, the hydraulic cylinder should not exhibit vibration, abnormal noise, sudden rushing, jamming, or crawling.
If necessary, environmental adaptability tests are recommended.
The operating conditions should generally include combinations of high and low pressure, high and low temperature, and high and low speed.
For hydraulic cylinders with lateral deviation performance requirements, the lateral deviation value should not exceed the specified value.
For the description of the starting and operating states of hydraulic cylinders, refer to Section 2.18 of this manual.
2. Factory Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance
(1) Trial Operation (Mandatory Test)
The hydraulic cylinder is started under no-load conditions and reciprocated several times along the full stroke to completely expel air from the hydraulic cylinder.
(2) Low-Pressure, Low-Speed Test (Mandatory Test)

items: Pressure adjustment range: 0 to 0.5 MPa or 0 to 1.0 MPa.
Speed adjustment range: 0 to 4.0 (8.0) mm/s or 0 to 5.0 (10.0) mm/s.

sections.text: Adjust the pressure and speed, and finally select a pressure of 0.5 MPa or 1.0 MPa and a speed of 4.0 (5.0) mm/s or 5.0 (10.0) mm/s. The cylinder should reciprocate along the full stroke at least 3 times (6 times), with each end of the stroke being held for at least 10 s.

The minimum stable speed index should be determined through agreement with the user and should be stipulated in the contract. Additionally, the two groups of minimum speed indexes are specified in GB/T13342 and CB/T3812, respectively.
(3) High-Speed Test (Sampling Test)

Under the rated pressure, the hydraulic cylinder operates continuously at the design-required highest speed (highest speed index should be determined through agreement with the user and should be stipulated in the contract) under the specified conditions or rated conditions, with a speed error of ±10%. Each test should run continuously for more than 8 hours.
The high-speed test (sampling test) is also known as the durability test.
(4) Pressure Resistance Test (Mandatory Test)

Except for hydraulic cylinders where the technical requirements explicitly prohibit using cylinder components as actual limiters, for other hydraulic cylinders undergoing the pressure resistance test, the hydraulic cylinder piston should be stopped at both ends of the stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at the extreme position of the stroke), and hydraulic oil at 1.5 times or 1.25 times the rated pressure should be applied to the working chamber. The factory test should maintain pressure for 10 s.
(5) Internal Leakage Test (Mandatory Test)

The hydraulic cylinder should be stopped at both ends of the stroke or at a position 10 mm from the end of the stroke (endpoint), and hydraulic oil at the rated pressure (or rated pressure) should be applied to the working chamber for testing.

For hydraulic cylinders with a stroke exceeding 1 m, in addition to the internal leakage test (mandatory test), the hydraulic cylinder should also be stopped at the middle of the stroke for the aforementioned internal leakage test (mandatory test).
It is recommended to determine through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user that the internal leakage test pressure uses the "rated pressure."
(6) High-Temperature Test (Sampling Test)
Under the rated pressure, hydraulic oil at 90°C is input into the hydraulic cylinder, which should reciprocate along the full stroke for 1 hour.

The high-temperature test should only be conducted on hydraulic cylinders if high-temperature performance is required for the product. Whether to disassemble and inspect or replace sealing elements after the test should be determined through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user.
(7) Buffer Test (Sampling Test)

Under a pressure of 50% of the rated pressure or the highest working pressure, the hydraulic cylinder should operate several times at the highest speed required by the design (under the specified conditions or rated conditions).

The buffer test should only be conducted on hydraulic cylinders if buffer performance is required for the product. This test mainly examines the sealing performance of the hydraulic cylinder under the action of "buffer pressure" or "peak buffer pressure."
(8) Dynamic Characteristics Test (Sampling)

For hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristic requirements, the dynamic characteristics test shall be conducted according to the provisions of their product standards, such as digital hydraulic cylinders and servo hydraulic cylinders. For hydraulic cylinders without product standard provisions but with dynamic characteristic requirements, inspection shall be conducted at least according to the special technical requirements (conditions or indicators) agreed upon between the manufacturer and the user.

It is recommended that manufacturers draft and formulate product enterprise standards based on their products. During dynamic characteristics testing, extreme conditions beyond the specified operating conditions may occur.
(9) External Leakage Test (Mandatory)
The external leakage test is included in all the above tests; at the end of the above tests, the oil film on the piston rod should be insufficient to form oil droplets or oil rings.

For hydraulic cylinders that have not undergone sampling test items, the external leakage should be checked after reciprocating the full stroke more than 20 times under nominal pressure (or rated pressure), with the same requirements as above. The installation positions (surfaces) of the inlet and outlet ports, exhaust (relief) devices, cushioning (valve) devices, stroke adjustment devices (mechanisms), input devices (including speed reduction devices and drive devices, etc.), hydraulic valves or manifold blocks, and instruments, sensors, etc., should not have external leakage.
3. Inspection Rules for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Factory Test

Hydraulic cylinders must undergo individual sealing performance factory tests before leaving the factory. The inspection results (test measurement values) of mandatory inspection items and sampling inspection items agreed upon with the user shall comply with the relevant standard provisions.
For hydraulic cylinders that have passed type tests and are already standardized or in mass production, sampling inspection items should also be conducted periodically.
4. Precautions for Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing Performance Testing

items: The hydraulic cylinder test should be operated by specially trained personnel with professional knowledge.

There are dangers in hydraulic cylinder testing, such as possible cylinder body rupture, connection (including welding) failure, piston rod disconnection (ejection), and seal device (system) failure, etc. Necessary protective measures should be taken, including installing and using protective covers, etc., to avoid possible injuries to personnel caused by high-pressure and/or high-temperature oil splashing or spraying.

For hydraulic cylinders designed with exhaust (relief) devices, the air in the hydraulic cylinder should be completely expelled during trial operation, and the danger of oil splashing or spraying to personnel caused by exhaust should be avoided.

For hydraulic cylinders (including test systems) without exhaust (relief) devices, the full stroke should be reciprocated several times during trial operation to completely expel the air in the hydraulic cylinder, and then placed for a period of time before conducting other test items, so that the air mixed in can be separated from the oil in the oil tank.

The oil used for hydraulic cylinder sealing performance testing should be consistent with the type and viscosity grade of the working medium of the hydraulic system or host it is matched with; otherwise, it may cause batch non-conformance of the product.

sections.text: 6) Except for high and low temperature tests, other hydraulic cylinder sealing performance inspections should be conducted when the working medium temperature in the working chamber is 52°C ± 4°C (considering the system error allowed by the measurement system); otherwise, it may cause batch non-conformance of the product.

7) In the single-acting hydraulic cylinder specified in JB/T 10205, the settling amount refers to the displacement of the cylinder (piston and piston rod) in the return direction caused by the leakage of the oil in the rodless cavity through the piston seal device (system) to the rod cavity. The settling (amount) of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder installed on the host may be either the displacement (amount) of the cylinder in the return direction or the displacement (amount) in the advance direction. Therefore, attention should be paid to the conversion relationship between the settling amount of the double-acting hydraulic cylinder in the advance direction and the internal leakage amount, and at the same time, attention should be paid to the fact that the settling amount of the hydraulic cylinder is caused by external loading, and the test bench without loading test devices cannot detect this item.

8) During testing, the hydraulic cylinder should be loaded (pressurized) and unloaded (depressurized) slowly and in stages. During the pressure test, the holding time specified in the standard should not be exceeded (10 s for factory test holding).

9) In JB/T 10205, the internal leakage amount (specified value) of double-acting hydraulic cylinders and the internal leakage amount (specified value) of single-acting hydraulic cylinders have at least one group of questionable values, and further consultation with the user should be conducted before testing to determine.
10) When visually checking the external leakage at the piston rod, it is advisable to wipe it clean again after trial operation and then check to avoid false "leakage" being misjudged as leakage.

11) For checking seepage or external leakage, the method of attaching clean absorbent paper (for fixed cylinder parts surface, such as cylinder body surface) or laying white paper along the path (for moving cylinder parts along the path, such as piston rod reciprocating path) can be used to check, with oil traces or oil spots on the paper indicating seepage or external leakage.

12) All sampling test items may cause certain damage to the hydraulic cylinder seal. It is recommended that the first hydraulic cylinder that has undergone sampling test items be disassembled and inspected after the test.
5.2 Test Method for Marine Hatch Cover Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Comparison and Application of Test Methods for Marine Hatch Cover Hydraulic Cylinders

There are many differences between the test methods for marine hatch cover hydraulic cylinders specified in CB/T 3812—2013 "Marine Hatch Cover Hydraulic Cylinders" and the test methods for hydraulic cylinders specified in GB/T 13342—2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Reciprocating Hydraulic Cylinders", GB/T 15622—2005 "Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinders", and JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders". The following points should be noted when applying them.
(1) Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram
In CB/T 3812—2013, the hydraulic system schematic diagram for hydraulic cylinder testing is specified according to GB/T 13342. GB/T 13342—

760.page_header: Chapter 5  Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders  749

sections.text: As stipulated in GB/T 15622-2005, Figure 1 (Hydraulic System Principle Diagram for Type Inspection of Double-Acting Piston Hydraulic Cylinder) and Figure 4 (Hydraulic Principle Diagram for Type Test) have certain technical progress, but also have some unreasonable aspects:

items: In the tested hydraulic cylinder circuit, the hydraulic principle diagram given in GB/T 13342-2007 has additional items such as a thermometer at the oil port of the tested hydraulic cylinder, a cooler and a filter in the return oil line.

In the loading hydraulic cylinder circuit, the hydraulic principle diagram given in GB/T 13342-2007 adopts a bridge-type rectifier circuit with a one-way valve, which can adjust speed or back pressure through a throttle valve. Compared with the circuit given in GB/T 15622-2005, it can reduce a relief valve.
The positions of the thermometer and pressure gauge at the oil port of the tested hydraulic cylinder are reversed, which does not comply with the relevant standard regulations.
The return oil line composed of a flowmeter + cooler + filter and piping has a certain back pressure, which has a great impact on the hydraulic cylinder test.
The proportions of graphic symbols are incorrect in many places, and the drawing method is wrong.
The nominal names of all filters (1, 27, 29 - filter) should be (hydraulic) filters.

sections.text: (2) Material Test, Cleanliness Test and Environmental Adaptability Test

The test method in CB/T 3812-2013 includes material test, cleanliness test (test) and environmental adaptability test (test), which are not included in GB/T 15622-2005 and JB/T 10205-2010. Specifically:

items: Material Test. Check the material certificates of each part.

Cleanliness Test. Clean the inner cavity of the hydraulic cylinder, then slowly pour the cleaning liquid onto the filter membrane (accuracy 0.8μm) placed on the funnel orifice for filtration. After filtration, dry and weigh it. The difference between the weight of the filter membrane after filtration and before filtration is the weight of pollutants in the inner cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.

sections.text: 3) Environmental Adaptability Test. When the ambient temperature is 65°C ± 5°C, keep the temperature of the test hydraulic fluid at 70°C ± 2°C. The hydraulic cylinder runs continuously with full stroke at a speed of 100-120 mm/s for 1 hour. When the ambient temperature is -25°C ± 2°C, keep it warm for 0.5 hours, then supply hydraulic oil with a temperature of -15°C for about 10 minutes.

"Test" has a clear definition. Checking the material certificates of each part cannot be called a "material test". However, before the hydraulic cylinder test, it is necessary to check and verify the grades and material specifications of the materials used.

Although this standard provides a cleanliness test method, which is feasible and may facilitate the use of the standard, it must be complete, accurate, and comply with the relevant standard regulations. The cleanliness requirements and cleanliness test method given in this standard are derived from JB/T 7858-2006, but there are big problems, as detailed below.
(3) Hydraulic Cylinder Performance Test Method

1) Compared with the other two standards (GB/T 15622-2005 and JB/T 10205-2010), CB/T 3812-2013 adds two test items, minimum stable speed and disassembly inspection, in the hydraulic cylinder performance test method, and omits the stroke inspection. The disassembly item is only carried out during type inspection. Stroke should be a basic parameter of the hydraulic cylinder. It is also included in the product identification specified in CB/T 3812-2013, but this standard has neither technical requirements nor inspection methods for stroke.

items: The technical requirements and test methods for "load efficiency" are included in these standards, but the test method given in CB/T 3812-2013 is: Install a dynamometer on the piston rod of the tested hydraulic cylinder, gradually increase the pressure in the working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, and calculate the efficiency of each point according to formulas (2) and (3). This is different from the other three standards, lacking the test condition of "keeping the tested hydraulic cylinder moving at a constant speed" or "keeping the tested hydraulic cylinder moving at a constant speed", that is, it may not measure and record various parameters under steady-state operating conditions. Therefore, there are deficiencies in the test method for "load efficiency" given in CB/T 3812-2013.
In addition, the calculation formula (2): η=W/F×100 given by it is wrong and should be η=W/F×100%.

sections.text: 3) The technical requirements and test methods for buffering are not included in GB/T 13342-2007, but are included in the other three standards. In CB/T 3812-2013, the test method for "buffering effect" is: Test the tested hydraulic cylinder at a designed maximum speed when the input pressure is 50% of the nominal pressure, and observe the movement of the piston. Compared with the "buffering test" given in GB/T 15622-2005, which is to fully loosen the buffer valve in the working chamber of the tested hydraulic cylinder, adjust the test pressure to 50% of the nominal pressure, run at the designed maximum speed, and detect the buffering effect when the buffer valve is fully closed, its applicable range may be wider.
However, the piston is not visible, and it is impossible to determine the buffering effect by "observing the movement of the piston".

4) The test method for "durability" given in CB/T 3812-2013 is different from the other three standards. It is to continuously operate the test for a cumulative reciprocating motion of 5000 times under nominal pressure, requiring normal operation, no replacement of parts (including seals), and checking external and internal leakage; and it gives the continuous operation time based on the working temperature of the hydraulic oil entering the hydraulic cylinder being 50°C ± 2°C. The test shall be stopped when the oil temperature is lower or higher than this temperature, and the test shall be continued after the temperature returns to normal until the 5000 times are completed, but the continuous operation time for each time shall not be less than 6 hours.

It is not a problem to check the "durability" of the hydraulic cylinder by cumulative reciprocating motion times of continuous operation, but if there is no specified speed for the reciprocating motion of the hydraulic cylinder, disputes may arise in the inspection results. In addition, there are also some problems in the expression of continuous operation time in this standard.

5) In the "disassembly inspection" given in CB/T 3812-2013, there is a provision for "checking the appearance... and the outer diameter of the guide plug...", but the "guide plug" is not defined in GB/T 17446-2012.
Other items such as operation and operation, load, oil pressure, and horizontal safety position are also involved.
This section has been omitted as it has been described elsewhere or modified in Table 5-10.
2. Test Methods for Cleanliness and Environmental Adaptability of Hydraulic Cylinders for Ship Hatch Covers
(1) Cleanliness

1) Cleanliness Index. The cleanliness requirements in CB/T 3812-2013 are as follows: The mass of contaminated particles in the hydraulic cylinder cavity (calculated for a stroke of 1 m) shall comply with the provisions of Table 5-14 (Table 13 in CB/T 3812-2013). The cleanliness requirements in JB/T 10205-2010 are as follows: The cleanliness control during the manufacturing and installation process of all components shall be in accordance with the requirements of GB/Z 19848, and the cleanliness index of hydraulic cylinders shall comply with the provisions of Table 5-15 (Table 8 in JB/T 10205-2010, i.e., Table 2 in JB/T 7858-2006).

In GB/T 13342-2007 and GB/T 24946-2010, it is also stipulated that: for hydraulic cylinders with an inner diameter of 25-32 mm, the extreme value of the mass of contaminants is 18 mg; for hydraulic cylinders with an inner diameter of 630-800 mm, the extreme value of the mass of contaminants is 416 mg. Comparing only the cleanliness indexes of double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a 1 m stroke in the two tables, the index of the mass of contaminated particles in the hydraulic cylinder cavity given in CB/T 3812-2013 far exceeds the cleanliness index given in JB/T 10205-2010, with the highest exceeding more than four times. GB/T 13342-2007 is included in the normative references of CB/T 3812-2013, and JB/T 7858-2006 is included in the normative references of GB/T 13342-2007, but CB/T 3812-2013 does not give the cleanliness index according to JB/T 7858-2006.
2) Cleanliness Test Method. The detection procedure and single filter membrane mass analysis procedure given in JB/T 7858-2006 are as follows:

items: Measure and record the magnetism of the tested component, and demagnetize to 12 Gs (Gauss, 1 Gs=10⁻⁴T) or below if necessary.
Clean the outer surface of the tested component.
Determine the wet volume of the inner cavity of the tested component.
Disassemble the tested component (components with process plugs and interference fits are not disassembled).

Remove the sealing elements on the mating surfaces (except for the piston sealing elements of hydraulic cylinders), and wipe the parts of the sealing surfaces that do not contact the working medium with white silk cloth.
Put all the internal parts after disassembling the component into a clean container.

Spray wash the parts that contact the working medium with clean washing liquid. For the parts that partially contact the working medium, only wash the parts that contact the working medium. For the parts that do not contact the working medium (such as the flange of the pump), only wipe the parts that contact the working medium with clean cloth.

762.page_header: Chapter 5 Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders 751

sections.text: Parts, valve handles, cylinder clevises, etc.) are not cleaned. The amount of clean cleaning solution used is 2-5 times the wet volume of the inner cavity of the component being tested.
⑧ Collect the cleaning solution from step ⑦ into a container that meets the cleanliness requirements and mark the container number (e.g., sample No. 1).
⑨ Repeat steps ⑥-⑧, with the container numbers being sample No. 2 and sample No. 3 in sequence.
⑩ Perform mass analysis on samples No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3 according to the single filter membrane or double filter membrane mass analysis procedure.

Note: Single filter membrane and double filter membrane mass analysis methods are two selectable mass analysis methods. When it is certain that the filter membrane can be sufficiently rinsed, the single filter membrane analysis method can be selected.

⑾ Single filter membrane mass analysis procedure: a) Take an appropriate amount of spare filter membrane (0.8μm) and place it in a Petri dish, cover it halfway, and put it into a drying oven. Keep it at a constant temperature of 80℃ (or the temperature specified for the filter membrane) for 30 min. After taking it out, cover it and cool for 30 min. During this process, the filter membrane should remain flat and undeformed. b) Take out one filter membrane that has been dried from the Petri dish and weigh its initial mass GA. c) Fix the filter membrane on the filtration device. After fully stirring the sample to be tested, pour it into the filtration device. Then use 50 mL of clean cleaning solution to rinse the sample container and pour it into the filtration device. Cover the funnel lid and perform vacuum filtration. When there is about 2 mL of residual liquid left in the filtration, remove the funnel lid and rinse the side wall of the funnel with clean cleaning solution, then cover the funnel lid and continue vacuum filtration until the cleaning solution on the filter membrane is completely filtered. d) Use a syringe to draw clean cleaning solution and inject it along the wall of the funnel for rinsing until there is no cleaning solution on the filter membrane. e) Stop vacuum filtration. Carefully remove the filter membrane and place it in a Petri dish. Place the Petri dish with the lid half-open into a drying oven and keep it at a constant temperature of 80℃ (or the temperature specified for the filter membrane) for 30 min. Take it out, cover it, and cool for 30 min, then weigh the mass GB. f) The mass of contaminants in the sample being tested is Gn=GB-GA. Comparing the testing procedures and single filter membrane mass analysis procedures given in JB/T7858-2006 with the cleanliness test methods given in CB/T3812-2013, the problems are obvious at a glance. Tests that are not conducted according to the procedures or methods specified in the standard are invalid.
(2) Environmental Adaptability

1) Environmental adaptability indicators. The environmental adaptability requirements in CB/T3812-2013 are: the environmental temperature, etc. should comply with the relevant provisions of GB/T13342. In GB/T13342-2007, the temperature requirements are specified as: 5.4.1 When the ambient temperature is -25-65℃, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to work normally. 5.4.2 When the working medium temperature is -15℃, the hydraulic cylinder should have no jamming phenomenon. 5.4.3 When the working medium temperature is 70℃, there should be no leakage at the mating surfaces of the hydraulic cylinder. In CB1146.2-1996 "Environmental Test and Engineering Guide for Ship Equipment - Low Temperature", the severity level (test temperature) of low-temperature operation test is specified; in CB1146.3-1996 "Environmental Test and Engineering Guide for Ship Equipment - High Temperature", the severity level (test temperature) of high-temperature operation test is specified. Among them, the requirement in CB/T3812-2013 that "when the ambient temperature is 65℃±5℃, the temperature of the test hydraulic oil should be maintained at 70℃±2℃" does not comply with the provisions of CB1146.3-1996, and it is also very difficult to achieve in actual operation.

2) Environmental adaptability test method. Taking the high-temperature operation test - intermediate inspection (excerpt) specified in CB1146.3-1996 as an example: "5.2.4.3 For communication navigation equipment, navigation equipment, and radar equipment installed on the open deck of ships, when the temperature rises to 70℃±2℃ and is maintained for 10 h, the various temperature control devices equipped by the test specimen itself can be turned on, and within 30 min, the temperature of the test box (chamber) should be reduced to 55℃±2℃ at the specified rate [not greater than 1℃/min (average value within 5 min)], then start the test specimen to work continuously for 2 h, and perform relevant performance tests under the environmental conditions of 55℃±2℃, and the performance should be within the specified range." Compared with the environmental adaptability test method specified in CB/T3812-2013, there are significant differences. a) The ambient temperature and the working medium temperature are the same, both are 70℃±2℃. b) The test specimen (hydraulic cylinder) does not work under the environmental conditions of 70℃±2℃. c) The operation test - intermediate inspection is conducted under the environmental conditions of 55℃±2℃. d) The continuous working (continuous reciprocating operation) time is 2 h. In summary, the author believes that when formulating standards, it is necessary to consider the requirements related to health and safety, such as whether it is appropriate to conduct environmental adaptability inspection when the ambient temperature is 65℃±5℃. Environmental testing should follow the standards, otherwise the test results may not be valid.
5.3 Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Comparison of Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders

The test methods for large hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders" differ from the test methods for hydraulic cylinders specified in GB/T15622-2005 "Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" in many aspects, mainly including: 1) JB/T11588-2013 does not provide a test device. 2) JB/T11588-2013 states: "The ambient temperature for the test is room temperature." The other two standards do not directly state this. 3) JB/T11588-2013 lacks a title like "Test Hydraulic Oil", so the description (requirements) about the test hydraulic oil below may be misunderstood. The other two standards all provide the description about hydraulic oil under the title "Test Hydraulic Oil".

items: In JB/T 11588-2013, the statement "Cleanliness: The internal cleanliness should not be higher than 19/15 or -/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039-2002" (requirement) contains errors. See section 6.1.2, item 15 for the citation and application of GB/T 14039-2002 standard.

JB/T 11588-2013 specifies the accuracy of the test pressure gauge: 0.5 grade for type testing; 1.0 grade for factory testing; range is 140%-200% of the maximum test pressure. Unlike the other two standards, it does not specify the allowable error of the measurement system and the allowable variation range of the average display value of the controlled parameter.
JB/T 11588-2013 divides the test into static pressure test (method) and dynamic load test for hydraulic cylinders, while the other two standards do not make such test classification.

The issue of mixed use of "trial operation" and "trial run" exists in all three standards, but in JB/T 11588-2013, it states "Before the test, preparation operation should be performed first. Start under no-load condition, and reciprocate the full stroke several times to completely eliminate air in the hydraulic cylinder, and the operation should be normal." Such statement (requirement) at least has problems of inconsistent use of terms (trial operation and trial run), non-standard use of terms (such as state, load), and putting forward performance requirements (such as operation should be normal) under the title of test method.

In JB/T 11588-2013, "Minimum starting pressure: Without load, the hydraulic pressure is gradually increased from zero until the piston rod moves smoothly, measure the minimum starting pressure at three points near the two ends and the middle of the piston in the cylinder, and take the maximum value." Such statement is different from the other two standards in several aspects. "When the piston rod moves smoothly, measure the minimum starting pressure at three points of the piston" does not conform to the definition of "minimum starting pressure" in the other two standards, nor does it conform to the definition of "starting pressure" in GB/T 17446-2012; "Hydraulic pressure" is generally not an abbreviation of liquid pressure, and cannot be used interchangeably with "pressure".

The internal leakage and external leakage in JB/T 11588-2013 are also different from the other two standards, such as explicitly mentioning "holding pressure for 30 min", and conducting internal leakage test and external leakage test separately.

JB/T 11588-2013 provides a cleanliness test method for hydraulic cylinders, which is to pressurize one cavity and drain oil from the other cavity, and use an oil contamination detector to detect the oil discharged from the hydraulic cylinder. The other two standards do not provide this.

JB/T 11588-2013 requires "Dynamic load test of hydraulic cylinder should be conducted at the user's site" and requires "Observe whether the action is smooth and flexible." This still has the problem of inconsistent use of terms (such as action).

In "Stroke test" of JB/T 11588-2013, since there is no requirement for "stroke" in this standard, it cannot perform the so-called "stroke test"; and in "Stop the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at the extreme positions at both ends of the stroke,...". "Extreme positions at both ends of the stroke" appears again, which is inconsistent with the previous multiple expressions of "both ends of the stroke".

Compared with the other two standards, JB/T 11588-2013 does not have regulations and requirements for "steady-state operating conditions", requirements and test methods for "durability", requirements and test methods for "load efficiency", requirements and test methods for "high-temperature performance", etc.

sections.text: JB/T 11588-2013 does not have regulations and requirements for "environmental test".
2. Application of Test Methods for Large Hydraulic Cylinders
(1) Standard Citation

JB/T 11588-2013 does not normatively cite the two standards GB/T 15622-2005 "Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders" and JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders", but through the above comparison, it is found that the content of "test methods" in JB/T 11588-2013 is basically similar or identical to the other two standards.
Without normatively citing the above two standards, the following problems cannot be solved:

items: GB/T 15622-2005 was published and implemented earlier, and a large amount of content from GB/T 15622-2005 is cited in JB/T 11588-2013, but GB/T 15622-2005 is not listed as a normative reference document, so that people who have not participated in the drafting of the standard may have many objections to this standard, or cannot use more authoritative normative reference documents to clarify these objections.

At least the schematic diagram of the hydraulic system for factory test is no longer available for reference. If a "test method" does not have a test device and a schematic diagram of the test device, it is indeed difficult to clearly describe or provide the test method, and it is very prone to problems.
Standards can be revised and trimmed, but they must develop towards a more standard and more applicable direction, not the opposite.

sections.text: (2) Pressure Resistance

The "pressure resistance" test specified in JB/T 11588-2013 is: Stop the piston of the tested hydraulic cylinder at both ends of the stroke respectively, and apply 1.5 times the nominal working pressure to the working chamber respectively, hold pressure for 2 min for type test, and hold pressure for 10 s for factory test. The biggest difference between the "pressure resistance test" in this standard and the "pressure resistance test" in the above two standards is "nominal working pressure".

The "nominal working pressure" is used multiple times in this standard, such as in internal leakage and external leakage tests, and is different from "nominal pressure", because this standard also uses "nominal pressure" in the cushioning test. It is not important whether "nominal working pressure" is first used in this standard, but what pressure it is has not been clearly defined. Because in GB/T 17446-2012, there are only "nominal pressure" and "maximum working pressure".

764.page_header: Chapter 5  Test Methods for Hydraulic Cylinders  753

sections.text: The terms "nominal working pressure" and "maximum pressure" are defined, which may lead to a series of problems:

1) The standard lacks normative references for terms and vocabulary, and does not specify the terms and definitions used in the standard. It is impossible to determine this "nominal working pressure," and consequently, it is also impossible to perform a "pressure test."

2) If "nominal working pressure" and "nominal pressure" are treated as synonyms, then due to the special structure of large hydraulic cylinders, performing a pressure test at the extreme position of the cylinder stroke may pose a risk of damaging the hydraulic cylinder.

3) If "nominal working pressure" and "maximum working pressure" are treated as synonyms, then performing a pressure test at the extreme position of the cylinder stroke may pose a slightly lower risk of damaging the hydraulic cylinder.
(3) Operating State

The operating state of the hydraulic cylinder is one of the technical requirements for the hydraulic cylinder, as mentioned in Section 2.18 on the technical requirements for the operation of hydraulic cylinders.

There are multiple descriptions of operation in JB/T 11588-2013, such as "operation should be normal," "smooth movement," "whether there is vibration or crawling," "whether the movement is smooth and flexible," etc.

The current problem is how to determine whether "the piston rod moves smoothly" during the minimum starting pressure test. Generally, a lower starting pressure is better, especially for hydraulic cylinders with dynamic characteristics. The following issues may exist with this standard's provisions:
1) Under the same test conditions, different testers and both parties may obtain inconsistent test results, and it is easy to raise objections to the test results.

2) For large hydraulic cylinders, the attitude of the hydraulic cylinder during the test will have a significant impact on the starting pressure. If the attitude of the hydraulic cylinder during the test is not specified, it may lead to greater controversy.
3) For large hydraulic cylinders, the minimum starting pressure may be related not only to the type of seal used in the hydraulic cylinder but also to the cylinder bore and piston rod diameter.
Additionally, it is unclear where the definitions of "M type as standard seal" and "T type as low-friction seal" originate.
5.4 Test Method for Proportional/Servo-Controlled Hydraulic Cylinders
5.4.1 GB/T 32216-2015 "Test Method for Proportional/Servo-Controlled Hydraulic Cylinders in Hydraulic Transmission"

GB/T 32216-2015 "Test Method for Proportional/Servo-Controlled Hydraulic Cylinders in Hydraulic Transmission" (issued on December 10, 2015, and implemented on January 1, 2017) specifies the scope as follows: This standard specifies the test methods for type testing and factory testing of proportional/servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders. This standard applies to piston-type and plunger-type hydraulic cylinders (hereinafter referred to as hydraulic cylinders or piston cylinders, plunger cylinders) that use hydraulic oil as the working medium and are controlled by proportional/servo control.

sections.text: 2) Safety requirements. The test device should fully consider the safety of personnel and equipment during the test process, should comply with the relevant requirements of GB/T37666, and have reliable measures to prevent personal injury accidents such as electric shock, mechanical injury, or high-pressure oil injection in case of failure. 3) Test proportional/servo valve. The response frequency of the test proportional/servo valve should be more than 3 times the highest test frequency of the hydraulic cylinder under test. The rated flow of the test proportional/servo valve should meet the maximum movement speed of the hydraulic cylinder under test. 4) Hydraulic source. The hydraulic source of the test device should meet the pressure requirements for testing, ensure stable oil supply pressure for the proportional/servo valve, and meet the instantaneous flow requirements for dynamic testing; it should have temperature adjustment, control, and display functions; it should meet the cleanliness level requirements for hydraulic oil, see 2.(3). 5) Pipeline and pressure measurement point location. ① In the test device, the pipeline between the test proportional/servo valve and the hydraulic cylinder under test should be as short as possible, and hard pipes should be used as much as possible; the pipe diameter should be as small as possible under the premise of meeting the maximum instantaneous flow. ② The pressure measurement points should comply with the provisions of 7.2 in GB/T28782.2-2012. 6) Instruments. ① The automatic recording analyzer should be able to measure the amplitude ratio and phase shift between sinusoidal input signals. ② The signal generator with adjustable amplitude and frequency should be able to output sinusoidal signals, and can perform sweep frequency between 0.1 Hz and the highest frequency required by the test; it should also be able to output forward step and reverse step signals. ③ The test device should have the function of real-time sampling of parameters such as speed, displacement, and output force of the hydraulic cylinder under test, and the sampling speed should meet the needs of test control and data analysis. 7) Measurement accuracy. According to the provisions of 4.1 in JB/T7033-2007, type testing adopts Grade B, and factory testing adopts Grade C. The allowable system error of the measurement system should comply with Table 5-16.

sections.text: (2) Hydraulic oil for testing

items: Viscosity. The kinematic viscosity of the test hydraulic oil at 40°C should be 29-74 mm²/s.

Temperature. Unless otherwise specified, type testing should be conducted at 50°C±2°C; factory testing should be conducted at 50°C±4°C. Factory testing can be conducted at a lower temperature, in the range of 15-45°C, but the detection indicators should be adjusted accordingly according to temperature changes to ensure that the performance indicators specified in the product standard can be achieved at 50°C±4°C.
Cleanliness. For servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder testing, the test hydraulic oil should have a cleanliness level of NAS 1638 grade 6 or better, or ISO 4406 cleanliness code of 18/16/13 or better.

sections.text: The contamination level of solid particles in hydraulic oil should not exceed the level specified in GB/T 14039-2002 as -/17/14; for proportional control hydraulic cylinder tests, the contamination level of solid particles in the hydraulic oil used for the test should not exceed the level specified in GB/T 14039-2002 as -/18/15.
4) Compatibility. The hydraulic oil used in the test should be compatible with the seals of the hydraulic cylinder under test and other parts that come into contact with the hydraulic oil.
(3) Steady-state Conditions

During the test, when the average displayed values of the controlled parameters vary within the range specified in Table 5-17, it is considered to be in steady-state conditions. Measurements and records of each parameter should be taken under steady-state conditions.

sections.text: 2. Test Items and Test Methods
(1) Test Run
Conduct the test according to GB/T 15622-2005 paragraph 6.1.
(2) Pressure Resistance Test

Make the tested hydraulic cylinder extend and stop at the position of the working stroke (single-acting hydraulic cylinder at the working stroke position), apply 1.5 times the rated pressure to the working cavity, type test pressure holding time 10min, outlet test pressure holding time 5min, observe that the tested hydraulic cylinder has no leakage and no damage.
(3) Starting Pressure Test

Test at no load condition. If the load is insufficient, adjust the temperature of the hydraulic oil. The pressure of the tested hydraulic cylinder rises until the cylinder starts to move, at which time record the pressure change during the test process. The maximum pressure value is the minimum starting pressure. For double-acting hydraulic cylinders, this test is conducted in both forward and reverse directions.
(4) Output Force Test

Under load condition, make the tested hydraulic cylinder rise to a pressure of 1 MPa, at which time the cylinder starts to move and maintains constant speed. Record the pressure and flow rate at the cylinder inlet. For double-acting hydraulic cylinders, this test is conducted in both forward and reverse directions. This test item test results are affected by load conditions, should note load method and installation method in test report. Output force test formula (5-1):

Where: Fd—output force, unit is N; p1—inlet pressure, unit is MPa; p2—outlet pressure, unit is MPa; A1—inlet cavity effective area, unit is mm²; A2—outlet cavity effective area, unit is mm²; F—load force, unit is N.
(5) Step Response Test

Adjust the hydraulic oil pressure to test pressure, test pressure range can be set to 10%-100% of the tested hydraulic cylinder rated pressure. Within the stroke range of the hydraulic cylinder, set the distance between the two end limit switches to 30% of the stroke in the middle area to set the maximum measurement point; adjust the signal to occur at the amplitude and frequency, so that the output stroke signal, according to the working procedure to determine the stroke value (amplitude range 5%-100%); use automatic data recording to record the test data, draw the step response characteristic curve, according to the curve to determine the tested hydraulic cylinder step response time. For double-acting hydraulic cylinders, this test is conducted in both forward and reverse directions. For two cavity surface area consistent double-acting hydraulic cylinders, use supplementary compensation, calibration, reverse direction stroke position relative to each other. This test item test results are affected by load conditions, should note load method and installation method in test report.
(6) Frequency Response Test

Adjust the hydraulic oil pressure to test pressure, test pressure range can be set to 10%-100% of the tested hydraulic cylinder rated pressure. Within the stroke range of the hydraulic cylinder, set the distance between the two end limit switches to 30% of the stroke in the middle area to set the maximum measurement point; adjust the signal to occur at the amplitude and frequency, so that the output stroke signal, according to the working procedure to determine the stroke value (amplitude range 5%-100%); frequency from 0.1Hz step increase to the tested hydraulic cylinder response value reduced to -3dB, or phase lag after 90°, use dynamic analysis to record the test data, draw the frequency response characteristic curve, according to the curve to determine the tested hydraulic cylinder frequency response index. For two cavity surface area consistent double-acting hydraulic cylinders, use supplementary compensation, calibration, reverse direction stroke position relative to each other. This test item test results are affected by load conditions, should note load method and installation method in test report.
(7) Durability Test

Under the specified working pressure, make the tested hydraulic cylinder operate continuously at the designed maximum speed, speed deviation is ±10%. One continuous operation 8h or more. During the test period, the hydraulic cylinder components should not be damaged. Record the amount of leakage during operation.
(8) Sealing Test
According to GB/T 15622-2005 paragraph 6.5 separately conduct external sealing and internal sealing test.
(9) Buffer Test
When the tested hydraulic cylinder has a buffer device installed, follow GB/T
GB/T 15622-2005 6.6 pressure test.

items: (10) Load efficiency test: According to GB/T 15622-2005 6.7 conduct load efficiency test.
(11) High temperature test: According to GB/T 15622-2005 6.8 conduct high temperature test.
(12) Stroke inspection: According to GB/T 15622-2005 6.9 conduct stroke inspection.

2) Pressure test.

sections.text: 5. Environmental Test (Content not specified in GB/T 32216-2015)

For the tests specified in this standard, they should be conducted under the conditions specified in the standard. However, as the actual applications of hydraulic devices in different environmental conditions continue to increase, it may be necessary to conduct other tests to verify the characteristics of hydraulic cylinders in different environments. In such cases, the requirements for environmental tests should be agreed upon by the supplier and the user.
Environmental tests include the following:

items: 1) Ambient temperature range.
2) Oil temperature range.
3) Vibration.
4) Shock.
5) Acceleration.
6) Explosion-proof performance.
7) Fire resistance performance.
8) Corrosion resistance performance.
9) Vacuum level.
10) Ambient pressure.
11) Heat radiation resistance.
12) Water immersion resistance.
13) Humidity.
14) Electrical sensitivity.
15) Air dust content.
16) EMC (electromagnetic compatibility).
17) Pollution sensitivity.

sections.text: 6. Several Notes

items: 1) Since servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders need to be used in conjunction with electro-hydraulic servo valves, if their test conditions are inconsistent with those of the electro-hydraulic servo valve, their test results, including characteristic curves, may have some problems. The author believes that, in general, the hydraulic cylinder should be tested under the standard test conditions of the matched electro-hydraulic servo valve, and does not agree with the statement and/or practice of "factory test can reduce temperature".

2) It should be particularly noted that the requirement of "for servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder test, the solid particle contamination degree of the test hydraulic oil should not be higher than that specified in GB/T 14039-2002 -/17/14" is too low. It should be in accordance with the standard test conditions for electro-hydraulic servo valves (see Reference [118]) to specify the contamination degree grade of the test hydraulic oil for servo hydraulic cylinders, i.e., the solid particle contamination degree grade code of the test hydraulic oil should not be worse than -/15/12 in GB/T 14039-2002 (ISO 4406:1999, MOD) (equivalent to level 6 specified in NAS 1638).

3) Regarding the issue of starting friction force of servo hydraulic cylinders, it has been discussed in Section 2.10.8, and it is believed that: the proposal that the electro-hydraulic servo valve-controlled hydraulic cylinder with a starting pressure not exceeding 0.3 MPa is a low-friction hydraulic cylinder is more appropriate. The current problem is that if the test is conducted according to "for double-acting hydraulic cylinders, this test (starting pressure characteristic test) should be performed in both forward and reverse directions", then for differential servo hydraulic cylinders (single-rod cylinders), is it the starting pressure of the rodless chamber or the starting pressure of the rod chamber, and after how many trial operations can the test be conducted. For single-rod cylinders, it is better to take the starting pressure of the rodless chamber as the standard, and it is advisable to conduct the inspection after 20 trial operations.

4) Regarding the test of dynamic friction force under load, since the load condition will affect the test results, this test may have great problems. Providing an eccentric load curve during the test is a solution, and specific details can be found in Reference [99], pages 22-421.

sections.text: 5) Internal or external sensors are important components that are generally equipped with servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders. Their performance directly affects or indicates the quality or level of the servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder. This should be reflected in the servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder tests, but the current standards lack technical requirements and test methods related to sensors. At least the model and accuracy (grade) of the sensors equipped with the servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder should be reflected in the test report.

6) The installation and connection of servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders are very important. The author has discussed the connection in reference [118]. It is not enough to only "record the loading method and installation method in the test report" during the tests of dynamic friction force, step response, and frequency response, as the aforementioned two items still have the problem of being "not conducive." For servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders with specific applications, it is advisable to have bench tests that simulate actual installation and connection, including the installation posture. Otherwise, the hydraulic cylinder may have many problems in actual use.

7) The hydraulic natural frequency of the servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder is a very important parameter, especially for servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders applied in situations with high dynamic performance requirements. It is necessary to verify the lowest hydraulic natural frequency of the hydraulic cylinder during the test.

8) The format of the test report for proportional/servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders is given in Annex A of GB/T 32216—2015; for servo-controlled hydraulic cylinders with hydraulic protection modules, the test report can be prepared using the format shown in Table 5-18.

5.4.2 DB44/T 1169.2—2013 Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 2: Test Methods

In DB44/T 1169.1—2013 (already obsolete, for reference only), servo hydraulic cylinders are defined as: hydraulic cylinders with requirements for static and dynamic indicators. Through cooperation with built-in or external sensors, servo valves or proportional valves, controllers, etc., it can form a hydraulic control system with high control accuracy and fast response speed. Static indicators include trial operation, pressure resistance, internal leakage, external leakage, minimum starting pressure, load friction force, deflection, leakage under low pressure, stroke detection, load efficiency, high temperature test, durability, etc. Dynamic indicators include step response, frequency response, etc.

The author believes that there are certain problems with the above definition of servo hydraulic cylinders, which should be the expression of the concept of servo hydraulic cylinders, reflecting the essential characteristics of servo hydraulic cylinders and the distinguishing features from other hydraulic cylinders, and should not include requirements, and should be able to replace the term in the context.

Despite this, according to the test methods specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013 "Servo Hydraulic Cylinder Part 2: Test Method", the above-mentioned static and dynamic indicators (items) of servo hydraulic cylinders should also be able to be tested (inspected).

Figure 5-7 shows the schematic diagram of the hydraulic system for performance test of servo hydraulic cylinder given in DB44/T 1169.2—2013 (drawn according to Figure 2 in DB44/T 1169.2—2013, but the basic elements of component graphic symbols and their relative positions may be modified).

According to GB/T 3766—2015, GB/T 15622—2005, GB/T 17446—2012, JB/T 10205—2010, DB44/T 1169.1—2013 and DB44/T 1169.2—2013 and other relevant standards, the following points should be noted when applying the test methods specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013.
1. Trial Operation
Regarding the test circuit, setting and test steps specified in Article 4.1 of DB44/T 1169.2—2013:

items: Once the oil port D in the test hydraulic system is connected to the oil port E of the tested hydraulic cylinder 19, it is impossible to start the tested hydraulic cylinder 19 under no-load conditions.

sections.text:
2) The graphic symbol of the servo valve 11 is incorrect, and generally it is understood that one of the switching functions in the left or right position cannot be realized.
3) It is very unscientific to decide the length of the hydraulic cylinder stroke in the form of adding or not adding a regulating shim 20, and it is too difficult to implement.
4) The test hydraulic system is not equipped with a degassing device. If the tested hydraulic cylinder itself is not equipped with a degasser, it is difficult to degas (discharge) the test hydraulic system and the tested hydraulic cylinder 19.
5) No protective measures have been taken for the pressure gauges in the test hydraulic system, and only one pressure gauge is installed on each pressure pipeline of each hydraulic source. It is impossible to detect or indicate all pressures between 0 and 40 MPa within the allowable error range of the measurement system.
6) The placement posture of the tested hydraulic cylinder should be explained, and its test steps are not detailed enough.
2. Pressure Resistance Performance Test
Regarding the test circuit, setting and test steps specified in Article 4.2 of DB44/T 1169.2—2013:

items: Although the basic technical parameters or main technical parameters of the servo hydraulic cylinder are not specified in DB44/T 1169.1—2013, "nominal pressure" cannot be excluded from the basic parameters, and it is a problem to determine the basis for the pressure resistance test based on what pressure, such as nominal pressure, rated pressure or rated working pressure.
The pressure holding time specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013 has no theoretical basis, which may cause the hydraulic cylinder to be scrapped.
It is not clear whether the servo hydraulic cylinder is allowed to perform a pressure resistance test at the end of the cylinder stroke as an actual positioning device of the hydraulic cylinder.
The pressure resistance test is not only a test of the cylinder body of the hydraulic cylinder, but also includes tests of other cylinder parts.
The test steps are not detailed enough.

sections.text: 3. Internal Leakage and External Leakage Tests
Regarding the test circuits, settings and test steps specified in Articles 4.3 and 4.4 of DB44/T 1169.2—2013:

items: For a double-acting hydraulic cylinder, dividing "internal leakage in the rodless cavity" and "internal leakage in the rod cavity" and "external leakage in the rodless cavity" and "external leakage in the rod cavity" is not necessarily scientific, and there are also errors in the test steps (requirements) specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013.

sections.text: 5. Load-carrying dynamic friction force test
For the test circuit, setting, and test steps specified in 4.6 of DB 44/T 1169.2—2013:

items: In DB 44/T 1169.2—2013, the loading test device shown in Figure 1 cannot load the servo hydraulic cylinder during its movement, i.e., it cannot achieve "the test hydraulic cylinder 19 moving from Sa to Sb under loaded condition, and then back from Sb to Sa".

Under the condition of "the piston rod of the test hydraulic cylinder 19 pressing against the upper beam of the frame 21", what is being detected (tested) is not the load-carrying dynamic friction force.

sections.text: 3) The steps (methods) of the test and the purpose to be achieved are inconsistent with the term "load-carrying dynamic friction" defined in DB44/T 1169.1—2013.
4) There are doubts about the principle of testing the load-carrying dynamic friction of servo hydraulic cylinders.
5) According to the test method specified in DB44/T 1169.2—2013, there are doubts about the load-carrying dynamic friction curve shown in Figure 4 of DB44/T 1169.2—2013.

Due to the limited space of this manual, other tests such as step response test (4.7), frequency response test (4.8), eccentricity test (4.9), leakage test under low pressure (4.10), stroke detection (4.11), load efficiency test (4.12), high-temperature test (4.13), durability test (4.14), etc. will not be explained one by one.

The author also has some views on the definition of "servo hydraulic cylinder" in this standard, the name "servo hydraulic cylinder", and the classification of hydraulic cylinders. If a hydraulic cylinder in a hydraulic system and circuit equipped with a servo valve or proportional valve can be named a servo hydraulic cylinder, then according to this logic, a hydraulic cylinder in a hydraulic system and circuit equipped with an "electronic control valve" can also be called an "electronic control hydraulic cylinder", which is obviously inappropriate; or a hydraulic cylinder in a hydraulic system and circuit equipped with a proportional valve can also be named a proportional hydraulic cylinder, rather than a servo hydraulic cylinder, which is also contradictory to the above definition of servo hydraulic cylinder.
5.5 Test Method for Digital Hydraulic Cylinders

According to the definition of digital hydraulic cylinders in GB/T 24946—2010, digital hydraulic cylinders are hydraulic cylinders that control position, speed, and direction through electric pulse signals.

GB/T 24946—2010 provides a typical structural diagram of digital hydraulic cylinders (drawn by the author according to Figure 1 in GB/T 24946—2010, but with added port identifications), as shown in Figure 5-8.

sections.text: At the same time, GB/T 24946—2010 also provides a hydraulic system schematic diagram for type testing of digital hydraulic cylinders (drawn by the author according to Figure 2 in GB/T 24946—2010, but with possible modifications to the basic elements and relative positions of component graphic symbols, and with added port identifications), as shown in Figure 5-9.

Based on Figures 5-8 (Figure 1 in GB/T 24946—2010) and 5-9 (Figure 2 in GB/T 24946—2010), the following two points should be noted when applying the hydraulic system schematic diagram for type testing of digital hydraulic cylinders specified in this standard (Figure 2 in GB/T 24946—2010).

(1) Name of Digital Hydraulic Cylinders: After comparison, the typical structural diagram of digital hydraulic cylinders shown in Figure 5-8 was also found in reference [15] published in 1990, but its name is the schematic diagram of electro-hydraulic stepping (hydraulic) cylinders (Figure 9.3.24). Electro-hydraulic stepping hydraulic cylinders are one of the seven types of hydraulic cylinders specified in JB/T 2184—2007 (and replaced by JB 2184—77). Based on the above situation, the author believes that the "digital hydraulic cylinder" specified in GB/T 24946—2010 is the "electro-hydraulic stepping hydraulic cylinder" specified in JB/T 2184—
2007 (1997). It needs to be further explained that GB/T 17446—2012 does not have the terms "digital hydraulic cylinder" or "digital cylinder".

(2) Typical Structural Diagram and Hydraulic System Schematic Diagram of Digital Hydraulic Cylinders: According to Figure 5-8, the hydraulic energy amplifying element should be a double-sided cylindrical slide valve (three-way valve), rather than the four-way valve shown in Figure 5-9, that is, the typical structural diagram of digital hydraulic cylinders does not match the hydraulic system schematic diagram.

Although the four-way valve is also a common hydraulic energy amplifying element and is applied in electro-hydraulic stepping motors, due to the fact that electro-hydraulic stepping hydraulic cylinders mostly use differential circuits (connections), a three-way valve can be used.

Due to the limited space of this manual, other issues in Figure 5-9 will not be explained one by one here, such as the loading hydraulic cylinder being unable to move back on its own. sections.text: Please refer to the explanation of Figure 5-3 to understand the various components in Figure 5-10. A digital hydraulic cylinder, as commonly understood, is a type of hydraulic power component (or hydraulic power mechanism) that generally consists of a hydraulic power amplification element (hydraulic control element), a hydraulic cylinder (hydraulic actuator), and a stepper motor, etc. A feedback control system using this as a driving device is a type of hydraulic servo control system. From this perspective, the problems in the definition of "digital hydraulic cylinder" in GB/T 24946—2010 are obvious.
5.6  Environmental Test Method for Hydraulic Cylinder

A servo-controlled hydraulic cylinder is typically controlled by an electro-hydraulic servo valve. Current electro-hydraulic servo valve standards, such as GB/T10844—2007 "General Technical Conditions for Marine Electro-hydraulic Servo Valves" and GB/T13854—2008 "Jet Pipe Electro-hydraulic Servo Valves," include "Environmental Requirements." Servo hydraulic cylinders, especially those integrating servo valves, generally have the same environmental requirements as servo hydraulic valves. In GB/T15623.1—2003 (which has been superseded) "Hydraulic Transmission - Electro-modulated Hydraulic Control Valves - Part 1: Four-way Directional Flow Control Valve Test Methods" and GB/T15623.2—2003 (which has been superseded) "Hydraulic Transmission - Electro-modulated Hydraulic Control Valves - Part 2: Three-way Directional Flow Control Valve Test Methods," there are "Environmental Tests," but in GB/T15623.1—2018 and GB/T15623.2—2017, the "Environmental Test" content is no longer present. Similarly, GB/T32216—2015 also lacks "Environmental Test" content. Electro-hydraulic servo valves (servo hydraulic cylinders) have different environmental requirements and test methods in different usage environments or application fields. The environmental test methods for marine electro-hydraulic servo valves are shown in Table 5-19.
