sections.text: (2) Principle of Comprehensive Benefits

items: The optimal design of the hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing engineering should be carried out in combination with existing technical means, equipment guarantee, performance requirements of the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder, etc.

The hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing engineering should be designed as a whole technically, so that the dismantling, cleaning, inspection, processing, assembly, packaging, and other technical processes can achieve overall optimization.

The economic design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing requires that the remanufacturing of waste hydraulic cylinders can obtain the maximum benefit. It should consider the comprehensive costs of design, production, transportation, storage, etc. of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing, as well as the comprehensive costs of environmental pollution caused by the production and economic activities of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing, etc.

The environmental design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing requires that the environmental impact of the processing of waste hydraulic cylinders and the use of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders should be less than the environmental impact caused by the production and use of prototype new products.
The resource design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing requires making full use of the resources of the original waste hydraulic cylinder and renewable resources as much as possible.

sections.text: (3) Principles of Compliance with Laws and Regulations
The engineering design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing should be implemented within the framework of laws, regulations, and mandatory standards, for example:

items: Restrictive requirements and responsibilities of international regulations.
Requirements of our country's laws, regulations, policies, and mandatory standards.
Technical standards and voluntary agreements.
Other relevant requirements.

sections.text: (4) Principles of Stakeholder Requirements
The engineering design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing should consider stakeholder requirements, for example:

items: Rights claims of all parties regarding the original hydraulic cylinder and the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder.
Market or consumer needs, development trends, and expectations.
Expectations of society and investors, etc.
Other relevant requirements.

sections.text: 2. Work Procedures and Contents
(1) Basic Work Procedures

The basic procedure for the engineering design of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing is: based on hydraulic cylinder drawings and technical requirements, production program, relevant laws, regulations, policies, and standards, and hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing database, etc., with the purpose of improving production quality, reducing production costs and resource consumption, and reducing environmental pollution, etc., through the application of reasonable technical approaches and process optimization, selection of auxiliary materials, etc., to carry out the design of reverse logistics for remanufacturing-oriented hydraulic cylinders, remanufacturing production process, remanufacturing management, and market marketing and service of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, etc., to propose the most optimized hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing scheme, thereby providing specific support for the development planning, remanufacturing production scheme, remanufacturing guarantee scheme, remanufacturing management, etc., of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing enterprises.
(2) Main Work Contents

1) Design of Waste Hydraulic Cylinder Recycling. The design of waste hydraulic cylinder recycling mainly considers the recycling, transportation, warehousing, classification, etc., of waste hydraulic cylinders, in order to achieve the maximum economic benefit of recycling and the minimum environmental pollution. It mainly includes the following aspects:

items: a) Reverse Logistics. Design and formulate the recycling model and approach of waste hydraulic cylinders, and determine necessary recycling nodes.
b) Organizational Management. Design and formulate the management method and setting of waste hydraulic cylinder recycling, etc.
c) Inspection and Classification. Design the node position of inspection in the recycling of waste hydraulic cylinders, and the standards and methods of inspection and classification, etc.

d) Ecological Environment Protection. Reduce the damage of hydraulic cylinders and environmental pollution during the recycling process, and strengthen the recycling use of logistics packaging materials, etc.

sections.text: 2) Design of Remanufacturing Production Process. The design of remanufacturing production process mainly optimizes and designs the establishment of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing production model and process standards based on the quality requirements of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing, and provides an executable hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing production scheme. It mainly includes the following aspects:

items: a) Disassembly Process. Design and determine the contents of disassembly process, disassembly steps, disassembly tools, and site, etc.
b) Cleaning Process. Design and determine the cleaning parts, cleaning process flow, cleaning quality standard, cleaning equipment, and site, etc.
c) Inspection Process. Design and determine the inspection parts, inspection process flow, inspection quality standard, inspection equipment, and site, etc.
d) Machining Process. Design and determine the machining surface, machining technical standard, machining equipment, and site, etc.

e) Surface Technology Process. Design and determine the parts, process flow, technical standard, equipment, materials, and site, etc., for the restoration or performance upgrade of surface technology.
f) Assembly Process. Design and determine the assembly flow, assembly standard, assembly equipment, and site, etc., of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.
g) Inspection Process. Design and determine the factory inspection (test) standard, test method, test equipment, and environmental conditions, etc., of the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder assembly.

sections.text: Generally, the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder should be subject to factory inspection (test) according to the standard followed by the prototype new product, but it is also allowed to carry out factory inspection of the whole machine (assembly) according to the requirements of the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder or the items agreed upon by both parties.

items: h) Painting Process. Design and determine the painting parts, painting flow, painting standard, painting equipment, materials, and site space, etc., of the remanufactured hydraulic cylinder.
i) Factory Layout. Design and determine the scheme contents of the layout of the hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing workshop, equipment layout, workstation layout, and production line layout, etc.

sections.text: 3) Design of Remanufacturing Management Scheme. Based on the quality requirements of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders and the characteristics of the remanufacturing production process, the reasonable and feasible hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing management scheme should be planned and designed. It mainly includes the following aspects:

items: a) Quality Management. Design and determine the remanufacturing process of different hydraulic cylinders and quality management standards, etc.
b) Production Management. Design and determine the management contents, personnel, and scheme, etc., of the hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing production process.

c) Information Management. Design and determine the statistics and management of relevant information such as the quantity of waste hydraulic cylinders, production output planning, production technology, quality standard, personnel, equipment, and spare parts in the whole remanufacturing process.
d) Equipment Management. Design and determine the management scheme of the use, maintenance, and repair of the production equipment for hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing.
e) Personnel Management. Design and determine the human resource management system and method for remanufacturing, etc.
f) Safety Management. Design and determine the safety management system for the site, equipment, personnel, etc., facing the whole process of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing.
g) Environmental Protection Management. Design and determine the clean production management system for production, equipment, resources, etc., facing environmental protection.
h) Product Identification Management. Design and determine the marking and statistical management method of the identification and information of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.

sections.text: 4) Marketing and service design for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders. It is necessary to study the market demand for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, customer expectations for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, as well as the marketing and service of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, to improve the benefits and market competitiveness of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders. It mainly includes the following aspects:

items: a) Market marketing. Determine the marketing plan and strategy for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, and guide green consumption of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.
b) Service model. Determine the service plan for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.
c) User analysis. Predict and determine users' expected demand for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, and design service plans for remanufactured hydraulic cylinders that meet users' needs.
d) Greenization. Taking green as the goal, determine the green implementation plan for the sales, use, and guarantee processes of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.

sections.text: 3. Comprehensive Evaluation
According to the needs of the remanufacturing project, the remanufactured hydraulic cylinders can be evaluated by referring to relevant methods.
6.4 Technical Specifications for Remanufacturing Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Parts
6.4.1 Technical Specifications for Evaluating the Remanufacturability of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. General Provisions

items: The object of remanufacturability evaluation can be either the hydraulic cylinder assembly or the parts of the hydraulic cylinder.
The remanufacturability evaluation of waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts (i.e., remanufacturing blanks) should be conducted before remanufacturing.

The purpose of evaluating the remanufacturability of hydraulic cylinders and their parts is to determine the remanufacturability of waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts; to assess whether the remanufacturability of hydraulic cylinders and their parts at the design stage meets the standards, and to correct the exposed problems.

The remanufacturability evaluation should be carried out based on the remanufacturing plan, combined with the actual conditions such as the guarantee equipment, technical means, and remanufacturing product performance requirements provided by the remanufacturing enterprise.
The remanufacturability evaluation of hydraulic cylinders and their parts has individuality.
The remanufacturability evaluation of hydraulic cylinders and their parts consists of two parts: qualitative evaluation and quantitative evaluation.

The remanufacturability of hydraulic cylinders and their parts is comprehensively determined by the technical feasibility, economic feasibility, environmental feasibility, and serviceability after remanufacturing.

The technical feasibility of remanufacturing hydraulic cylinders and their parts requires that the remanufacturing and processing of waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts be technically and technologically feasible, i.e., it can restore, upgrade, or improve the performance of the original product. Its common parameter indicators include disassembly rate, cleaning satisfaction rate, and fault detection rate.

The economy of remanufacturing hydraulic cylinders and their parts requires that the input (capital) cost of remanufacturing waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts is less than the economic benefits obtained from the output, and the profit rate meets the enterprise's requirements.

The environmental reliability of remanufacturing hydraulic cylinders and their parts requires that the environmental pollution caused by the remanufacturing and processing process and use process of waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts is less than the environmental pollution caused by the production and use process of the original product.

sections.text: 2. Qualitative Evaluation

items: For remanufacturing waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts, qualitative evaluation of remanufacturability should be conducted first. Remanufacturability should generally meet the conditions of functionality, economy, marketability, and environmental protection.
Qualitative conditions for remanufacturability are as follows:

a) There are mature remanufacturing restoration or upgrading technologies that can meet the remanufacturing process requirements such as transportation, disassembly, cleaning, inspection, processing, and assembly of remanufacturing blanks.
b) The remanufacturing blanks can meet the needs of batch processing for remanufacturing.
c) The remanufacturing blanks have high residual value and can be restored through remanufacturing.
d) The remanufacturing blanks can achieve standardized production, the parts have interchangeability, and spare parts are easily available in the market.
e) There is a clear market demand for remanufactured products.
f) The remanufacturing process should comply with relevant regulations in China regarding intellectual property rights and environmental protection.

sections.text: 3. Quantitative Evaluation
(1) Parameters for Evaluating the Technical Remanufacturability

items: Disassembly rate: The disassembly rate (Rd) is the ratio of the number of cylinder parts that can be disassembled without damage to the total number of cylinder parts contained in the hydraulic cylinder, i.e.,

sections.text: where Qnd — the number of cylinder parts that can be disassembled without damage; Qrd — the total number of cylinder parts contained in the hydraulic cylinder. The disassembly rate needs to comprehensively consider factors such as the value of the corresponding cylinder parts, disassembly time, disassembly cost, and disassembly equipment. During specific disassembly, analysis and selection should be made according to the actual situation, and clear explanations should be provided.

items: 2) Cleaning satisfaction rate: The cleaning satisfaction rate (Rc) is the ratio of the number of cylinder parts that can meet the requirements after cleaning to the number of cylinder parts that need cleaning in the hydraulic cylinder, i.e.,

sections.text: where Qnc — the number of cylinder parts that can meet the requirements after cleaning; Qrc — the number of cylinder parts that need cleaning in the hydraulic cylinder. The cleaning satisfaction rate needs to comprehensively consider factors such as cleaning time, cleaning cost, cleaning equipment, and environmental impact. During specific cleaning, analysis and selection should be made according to the actual situation, and clear explanations should be provided.

items: 3) Fault detection rate: The fault detection rate (Ri) is the fault detection rate for remanufacturing

sections.text: The ratio of correctly detected faults to the total number of actual faults that occurred in the same test unit during the specified working time T under specified conditions, i.e.,
Ri = Nd/NT × 100%

Formula (6-3): Where Nd is the number of faults correctly detected in the test unit; NT is the total number of faults that actually occurred in the same test unit. The fault detection rate needs to comprehensively consider factors such as detection time, detection cost, and detection equipment. During specific detection, analysis and selection should be conducted according to actual conditions, and clear explanations should be provided.
(2) Parameters for Evaluating the Economics of Remanufacturing
1) Profit Margin
The profit margin (Rc) is the ratio of the profit obtained from selling a single remanufactured product to the cost invested in remanufacturing the product, i.e.,
Rc = Rb/Rc × 100%
Formula (6-4): Where Rb is the net profit obtained from selling the remanufactured product; Rc is the cost invested in remanufacturing the product.
2) Value Recovery Rate
The value recovery rate (Rcb) is the ratio of the value of recovered hydraulic cylinders and their parts to the total value of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders, i.e.,
Rcb = Rrc/Rpc × 100%
Formula (6-5): Where Rrc is the value of recovered hydraulic cylinders and their parts; Rpc is the total value of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders.
3) Environmental Benefit Rate

The environmental benefit rate (Rec) is the ratio of the sum of direct environmental economic benefits and indirect environmental economic benefits obtained from remanufacturing to the net profit obtained from selling the remanufactured product, i.e.,
Rec = (Rdc + Rjc)/Rb × 100%
Formula (6-6): Where Rdc is the direct environmental economic benefits; Rjc is the indirect environmental economic benefits; Rb is the net profit obtained from selling the remanufactured product.
4) Processing Efficiency

Processing efficiency (Rm) is an indicator of the time aspect of the remanufacturing processing stage, expressed as the ratio of the average processing time for remanufacturing waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts to the average processing time required for manufacturing the prototype new product of the hydraulic cylinder, i.e.,
Rm = Tr/Tm × 100%

Formula (6-7): Where Tr is the average processing time for remanufacturing waste hydraulic cylinders and their parts; Tm is the average processing time required for manufacturing the prototype new product of the hydraulic cylinder. Processing efficiency needs to consider factors such as corresponding production equipment, product performance, and cost price. During specific evaluation of processing efficiency, analysis and selection should be conducted according to actual conditions, and clear explanations should be provided.
(3) Parameters for Environmental Assessment
1) Material Saving Rate
The material saving rate (Rma) is the ratio of the sum of the mass of remanufacturable parts and the mass of directly usable parts to the mass of the hydraulic cylinder assembly, i.e.,
Rma = (Wrm + Wru)/Wp × 100%
Formula (6-8): Where Wrm is the mass of remanufacturable parts; Wru is the mass of directly usable parts; Wp is the mass of hydraulic cylinder assembly.
2) Energy Saving Rate
The energy saving rate (Rre) is the ratio of energy saved through remanufacturing to the energy consumed in disposing of waste hydraulic cylinders, calculated as shown in equation (6-9):
Rre = (PWmd - PWrm)/PWmd × 100%

Formula (6-9): Where PWmd is the energy consumed in disposing of waste hydraulic cylinders; PWrm is the energy consumed in remanufacturing the hydraulic cylinder. Advanced and applicable hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing technologies should be selected to improve the energy saving rate.
3) CO2 Emission Reduction Rate

The CO2 emission reduction rate (Rrq) is the ratio of the amount of CO2 emissions reduced through remanufacturing to the amount of CO2 emissions generated from disposing of waste hydraulic cylinders, i.e.,
Rrq = (Emd - Er)/Emd × 100%

Formula (6-10): Where Emd is the CO2 emissions generated from disposing of waste hydraulic cylinders; Er is the CO2 emissions generated from remanufacturing the hydraulic cylinder. Advanced and applicable hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing technologies should be selected to improve the CO2 emission reduction rate.
4. Flow of Remanufacturability Evaluation
(1) Failure Mode Analysis of Waste Hydraulic Cylinders
1) Remanufacturability evaluation should be conducted based on the failure mode of waste hydraulic cylinders and feasible remanufacturing schemes.

2) The failure mode analysis of waste hydraulic cylinders should consider the following reasons: the product has developed irreparable faults (fault scrap), the cost-effectiveness ratio is too high during product use (economic scrap), the product performance is outdated (functional scrap), the pollution of the product does not meet environmental protection standards (environmental scrap), and the product style and other aspects do not meet people's preferences (preference scrap).
(2) Analysis of Factors Affecting the Remanufacturability of Hydraulic Cylinders

1) The remanufacturability of hydraulic cylinders should comprehensively consider the effects of factors such as technical feasibility, economic feasibility, environmental feasibility, and product service life, as well as their combined effects.
2) The effects of different technological process routes on the economics, environment, and service life of hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing should be considered.

3) Serviceability of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders refers to the inherent usage performance of the remanufactured hydraulic cylinders themselves, which should be able to meet corresponding market needs. The serviceability of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders is determined by the remanufacturing technology scheme adopted and directly affects their environmental and economic performance.

4) According to actual needs, production guarantee conditions meeting the requirements should be provided. These guarantee conditions include equipment status, personnel technical level, technology application status, and production conditions.

5) Based on the requirements of technical, economic, and environmental performance, a method combining failure mode prediction analysis and physical testing should be used to determine the quantitative evaluation parameters of the items in 3(1) and 3(2).
(3) Quantitative Evaluation Process for Remanufacturability

1) The quantitative evaluation process for remanufacturing used hydraulic cylinders and their components is shown in Figure 6-3. First, a remanufacturing scheme should be selected based on the service performance requirements and failure modes of the used hydraulic cylinders and their components. Then, an economic and environmental evaluation of the remanufacturing scheme should be conducted. Finally, through multiple rounds of evaluation and comparison, the optimal remanufacturing scheme should be determined.

2) For used hydraulic cylinders and their components with remanufacturing value, various factors in the evaluation process should be used to optimize factors and formulate the most optimized remanufacturing scheme.
6.4.2  Disassembly Technology Specifications for Remanufactured Hydraulic Cylinders

The disassembly of remanufactured hydraulic cylinders (disassembly objects) is divided into destructive disassembly, partially destructive disassembly, and non-destructive disassembly based on the degree of disassembly damage.
1. General Requirements
(1) Pre-disassembly Requirements

items: Register the disassembly objects and mark information labels in prominent positions.
Store the disassembly objects properly to avoid damage such as corrosion and deformation caused by improper storage.
Necessary cleaning and preliminary inspection should be conducted to check the product's

sections.text: Sealing and Damage Inspection

items: 4) Relevant drawings and documents should be consulted to understand the structure and assembly relationship of the object to be disassembled, and suitable disassembly methods and tools should be designed or selected based on the connection form and size specifications of the components.
5) Measure the assembly clearance between disassembled parts and their relative positions to related components, and make markings and records.
6) Skill training should be provided to disassembly personnel.
7) Special plans should be formulated for hazardous disassembly operations.

sections.text: (2) Requirements for the disassembly process

1) Components that can ensure the performance of the hydraulic cylinder after remanufacturing do not need to be completely disassembled. Necessary tests or diagnostics should be conducted to ensure there are no hidden defects.
2) When disassembling sealed joints, it is advisable to use vibration or pushing methods to avoid damaging the joint surfaces.
3) For difficult-to-disassemble components such as broken bolts or seized joints, care should be taken to avoid damaging other components during disassembly.
4) For complex hydraulic cylinders or cylinder components, remanufacturing assembly drawings should be made or markings should be made during disassembly.
5) For shaft-hole fitted components, priority should be given to the principle of using the same force for disassembly as for assembly.
6) Avoid destructive disassembly to ensure the reusability of cylinder components and the recyclability of materials. If destructive disassembly is necessary, the principle of protecting high-value cylinder components should be followed.
7) For disassembly objects containing hazardous substances, the hazardous substance disassembly plan should be followed.
(3) Requirements after disassembly

1) State identification should be performed on disassembled cylinder components, categorizing them into direct use, remanufacturable, and scrap parts for storage, and recording relevant information.
2) Coupled parts and non-interchangeable parts after disassembly should be grouped and stored with proper markings.
3) For components containing harmful substances, the types of harmful substances should be indicated.
4) For components containing harmful waste, they should be collected and stored separately by category, with hazardous waste warning signs, and handed over to qualified institutions for disposal.
5) Storage of waste after disassembly should comply with the requirements of GB 18597 and GB 18599.

2. Safety and Environmental Requirements
1) The disassembly site should be equipped with ventilation, dust removal, and anti-seepage facilities.
2) Environmentally friendly disassembly equipment and tools should be used to avoid impacts on human health and the environment.
3) Harmful solid, liquid, and gaseous wastes generated during disassembly should be classified and collected, and disposed of according to relevant laws, regulations, and standards of China.
4) Disassembly noise should meet the requirements of GB 12348.
5) Necessary labor protection should be provided to disassembly personnel.

sections.text: 6.4.3  Technical Specifications for Cleaning Re-manufactured Hydraulic Cylinders

Cleaning of re-manufactured hydraulic cylinders and their parts (i.e., re-manufactured blanks) can be classified in different ways, such as according to the re-manufacturing process, which can be divided into pre-disassembly cleaning, post-disassembly cleaning, re-manufacturing processing cleaning, pre-assembly cleaning, pre-coating cleaning, and post-testing cleaning; according to the cleaning object, which can be divided into part cleaning, component cleaning, and assembly cleaning; according to the type of surface contaminants, which can be divided into oil cleaning, carbon deposit cleaning, scale cleaning, coating cleaning, impurity cleaning, rust cleaning, and other contaminant cleaning; according to the cleaning technical principle, which can be divided into physical cleaning, chemical cleaning, and electrochemical cleaning; according to the cleaning technical means, which can be divided into thermal cleaning, ultrasonic cleaning, vibration grinding cleaning, shot blasting cleaning, sandblasting cleaning, dry ice cleaning, high-pressure water jet cleaning, laser cleaning, ultraviolet cleaning, and solution cleaning.
1. General Requirements

items: Based on the characteristics of the cleaning object and its surface contaminants, combined with the requirements of subsequent re-manufacturing processing technology, formulate a reasonable cleaning plan and process guidelines to ensure the economy, environmental protection, and safety of cleaning, and avoid damage to the cleaning object, operators, and external environment.

The cleaning of re-manufactured blanks should not affect subsequent re-manufacturing evaluation testing, processing, assembly, and coating, as well as the quality and performance of the re-manufactured hydraulic cylinder and its parts.

sections.text: 2. General Requirements
(1) Cleanliness Requirements

items: For pre-disassembly cleaning, the accumulated dust, oil, sand, and other contaminants on the exterior of the re-manufactured hydraulic cylinder should be basically removed to facilitate subsequent disassembly and avoid bringing contaminants into the factory process interior.
For cleaning before re-manufacturing processing, it should meet the subsequent re-manufacturing requirements.

sections.text:
manufacturing process requirements.
3) For cleaning before assembly, it should meet the requirements of subsequent assembly processes.
4) For cleaning before surface coating, it should meet the requirements of surface cleanliness as specified in GB/T 8923.1, GB/T 8923.2, etc.
(2) Requirements for the Surface State and Structural Organization of Remanufactured Blanks

items: The surface corrosion state and surface roughness of remanufactured blanks should be reasonably controlled according to the type of remanufactured blanks, cleaning methods, and remanufacturing processes. For remanufactured blanks using remanufacturing processes such as thermal spraying, the surface roughness requirements can be relaxed on the condition that subsequent processing requirements are met.

The cleaning process should avoid causing changes in the structural organization of the remanufactured blank surface, stress deformation, and surface damage to prevent affecting subsequent remanufacturing processes and assembly.

During the cleaning process, necessary protective measures should be taken to prevent damage, destruction, and corrosion to non-cleaning surfaces, and to avoid hard particles and corrosive media entering the internal cavity of the remanufactured blank or mating surfaces that do not require cleaning.
After cleaning, measures should be taken to prevent contamination, corrosion, and other damage to cylinder parts during storage or transportation.

sections.text: (3) Site, Labor Safety, and Environmental Protection Requirements

items: The cleaning site should be equipped with necessary facilities such as ventilation, noise reduction, dust removal, and anti-seepage according to different cleaning process requirements.
Necessary labor protection should be provided for cleaning operators to prevent injuries.
Environmentally friendly cleaning processes, equipment, materials, and methods should be given priority.
Various harmful solid, liquid, and gaseous waste generated from cleaning should be classified and collected, and disposed of according to relevant laws, regulations, and standards of China.

sections.text: 6.4.4 Surface Repair Technology Specifications for Remanufactured Cylinder Parts

The surface repair technology of remanufactured cylinder parts refers to a series of surface engineering technologies involved in the process of repairing the surface of remanufactured cylinder parts (remanufactured blanks) to restore their geometric parameters and performance to those of the original new products, including additive manufacturing technology.

The surface repair technology of remanufactured cylinder parts can be classified in different ways. For example, according to the bonding principle between the repair layer and the blank substrate, it can be divided into metallurgical bonding repair technology, mechanical bonding repair technology, semi-metallurgical/semi-mechanical bonding repair technology, chemical bonding repair technology and physical bonding repair technology; according to the degree of damage to the remanufactured blank, it can be divided into surface damage repair technology and volume damage repair technology; according to the repair technology means, it can be divided into welding repair technology, surface deposition repair technology, surface coating repair technology and adhesive repair technology, etc.
1. Design and Selection Principles
(1) Adaptability Principle

1) The repair layer should have good matching with the remanufactured blank material in physical, chemical and mechanical properties, and the influence of the repair process on the shape, size, performance, etc. of the remanufactured blank should meet the relevant drawings and technical requirements.

2) Based on the original service environment, stress state, working medium and failure mode of the remanufactured blank, the mechanical properties, physicochemical properties, environmental characteristics and organizational structure that the repair layer should have should be comprehensively considered, and appropriate surface repair technology and materials should be selected.
(2) Economic Principle

On the premise of meeting the quality and performance requirements of remanufactured cylinder parts, comprehensive consideration should be given to technical input cost, process flow complexity and remanufacturing economy and other indicators, priority should be given to low-cost and low-pollution repair materials and technologies, automated repair processes should be given priority, and the process flow should be simplified as much as possible.
(3) Environmental Protection Principle

When selecting surface repair technology, consideration should be given to reducing resource consumption, energy consumption and environmental pollution; in repair process design and material selection, conditions should be created for realizing multiple remanufacturing, recycling or extending the service life of cylinder parts.
2. Requirements
(1) Basic Requirements
1) For surface repair of remanufactured cylinder parts, environmentally friendly processes, equipment, materials and methods should be given priority.
2) The remanufactured cylinder parts after repair should not be lower than the original new products in
Dimensional accuracy, technical parameters, quality characteristics and safety performance requirements.
(2) Requirements before repair

1) Surface remanufacturing repair design and demonstration should be carried out according to the service conditions, failure modes and functional requirements of the hydraulic cylinder and its parts, comprehensively considering technical, environmental and economic feasibility, to determine the repair technology plan and process flow, and formulate repair operation guidance documents, determine the type, composition, structure and related physical and chemical properties and mechanical property indexes of the surface repair layer.

2) According to the requirements of surface repair technology on the surface state of materials, the remanufacturing blank should be cleaned, inspected and subjected to corresponding pretreatment and surface protection. Cleaning should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3280, and inspection should comply with the provisions of GB/T 3120.
(3) Requirements during repair process

1) The remanufactured cylinder parts and their surface repair layer should be inspected after repair, and the content, method, plan and results of inspection should comply with the provisions of relevant technical documents.

2) The remanufactured cylinder parts and their surface repair layer should be subjected to dimensional inspection and accuracy inspection to ensure that the overall and local dimensions and accuracy of the repair parts meet the requirements of process guidance documents.

3) Necessary hardness, bonding strength, residual stress or defect inspection should be carried out according to the quality requirements of the repair layer, giving priority to the use of non-destructive testing technology and conducting inspection according to relevant standards.
4) Necessary factory test should be carried out according to the test requirements of the hydraulic cylinder, such as sealing test, etc.
5) Measures should be taken to prevent the remanufactured cylinder parts from being contaminated, corroded, damaged or deformed during storage or transportation.

sections.text: The basic principle of applicable and promotable nanocomposite brush plating technology is similar to that of traditional (or ordinary) brush plating technology. The difference lies in: during the brush plating process, nanoscale particles (1-100 nm) in the composite plating solution deposit onto the workpiece surface under the action of electric field force or complex ion holding, etc., becoming the particle reinforcement phase of the composite coating, with nanoscale particles co-depositing with metal to form the composite brush coating.

The nanoscale particles in the composite plating solution are nanoscale particles with specific performance added to the brush plating solution, and different material (system) nanoscale particles can be added according to needs, with ceramic nanoscale particles being only one of the optional particle materials.

Nanocomposite brush plating technology is an emerging composite brush plating technology, which not only has the general characteristics of traditional (or ordinary) brush plating technology, but also has different characteristics from traditional (or ordinary) brush plating technology, mainly reflected in the brush plating solution, coating structure, and performance:

items: The nanocomposite brush plating solution contains nanoscale insoluble solid particles, and the presence of nanoscale particles does not significantly affect the properties of the solution (such as acidity, alkalinity, conductivity, power consumption, etc.) and deposition performance (such as coating deposition rate, coverage area, etc.).

The composite brush coating obtained through nanocomposite brush plating technology has a denser structure and finer grains. The characteristics of the composite coating (fiber) structure are: nanoscale particles are uniformly distributed in the metal matrix phase, and the matrix structure is mainly composed of micro-nanocrystals.

The wear resistance, high temperature resistance, and other comprehensive properties of the nanocomposite brush coating are superior to those of the same metal coating. Nanocomposite brush coating can work at higher temperatures.

Depending on the material system of the added nanoscale particles, composite coatings with various properties such as corrosion resistance, lubrication and wear reduction, and wear resistance, as well as functional coatings, can be obtained.

In the same base metal nanocomposite coating, the composition, size, mass fraction, purity, etc. of solid particles have different degrees of influence on the performance of the nanocomposite brush coating. Optimizing these influencing factors can obtain a nanocomposite brush coating with the best performance/price ratio. This is also a way to obtain metal-ceramic materials with nanoscale structures.

The key to nanocomposite brush plating technology is the preparation of nanocomposite brush plating solution. Different nanocomposite brush plating solutions have different nanocomposite brush plating processes, which can obtain nanocomposite brush coatings with different properties. Reference [31] introduces: the brush plating solution contains about 20 g/L of nanoscale particles, which need to be specially dispersed before use. There are also references and materials that introduce that due to the above characteristics, nanocomposite brush plating has become an important means of restoring the dimensions of remanufactured products, and is frequently used in the remanufacturing process of thin-walled parts, slender rods, and precision parts. The addition of nanoscale particles greatly improves the performance of the coating, which can solve many problems in the remanufacturing process.

sections.text: Nanocomposite brush plating technology is not only a new technology in surface engineering, but also a key technology for remanufacturing parts, as well as a new method for manufacturing metal-ceramic materials. Nanocomposite brush plating technology is a combination of nanotechnology and traditional technology, which not only retains all the functions of traditional technologies such as electroplating, brush plating, and chemical plating, but also expands their application range, achieving broader, better, and stronger application effects:
(1) Improve the wear resistance of part surfaces

Using brush plating solution with added nano-ceramic particles for nanocomposite brush plating, due to the dispersed distribution of nano-ceramic particles in the matrix metal of the plating layer, a metal-ceramic brush plating layer is formed. The countless nano-ceramic hard points in the matrix metal of the brush plating layer significantly improve the wear resistance of the brush plating layer. This type of brush plating layer can replace processes such as hard chromium plating, carburizing, nitriding, and phase transformation hardening for parts.
(2) Reduce the friction coefficient of part surfaces

Using brush plating solution with added nano-solid particles (such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite, etc.) with friction-reducing effects for nanocomposite brush plating can obtain a nanocomposite friction-reducing layer. This brush plating layer contains countless dispersed solid lubrication points, which can effectively reduce the friction coefficient of friction pairs, playing a role in solid friction reduction, thereby reducing wear on part surfaces and extending the service life of parts.
(3) Improve the high-temperature wear resistance of part surfaces

Using brush plating solution with added nano-ceramic particles for nanocomposite brush plating, the ceramic phase in the formed metal-ceramic plating layer has excellent high-temperature resistance. When the brush plating layer works at higher temperatures, the ceramic phase can maintain excellent high-temperature stability, providing overall support for the brush plating layer and effectively improving the high-temperature wear resistance of the brush plating layer.
(4) Improve the fatigue resistance of part surfaces

The plating layers and coating layers obtained by many surface engineering technologies can quickly restore the dimensional accuracy and geometric accuracy of damaged parts, improving the surface hardness, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance of parts, but they are difficult to withstand alternating loads and have low fatigue resistance. Nanocomposite brush plating layers have higher fatigue resistance because countless nano-solid particles are deposited at defect sites in the nanocomposite brush plating, equivalent to placing countless "limiting piles" on many dislocation lines. These "limiting piles" can effectively prevent lattice slip. Dislocations are an internal stress source in crystals, and the existence of "limiting piles" also changes the stress state of the crystal. Therefore, the fatigue resistance of nanocomposite brush plating layers is significantly higher than that of ordinary brush plating layers.
(5) Improve the performance of non-ferrous metal surfaces

Many parts or part surfaces are manufactured using non-ferrous metals, mainly to utilize the electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, friction reduction, and corrosion resistance of non-ferrous metals. However, due to their low hardness and poor strength, non-ferrous metals often have short service life and are prone to damage. Preparing nanocomposite brush plating layers can not only maintain the inherent excellent properties of non-ferrous metals but also improve their wear resistance, friction reduction, corrosion resistance, and heat resistance. For example, treating various lead bronze and tin bronze bearing bushes (hydraulic cylinder guide sleeves) with nanocomposite brush plating can effectively improve their performance.
(6) Realize part remanufacturing and enhance their performance

The remanufacturing of hydraulic cylinders is based on used cylinder parts as blanks, with the first step being to restore the dimensional accuracy and geometric accuracy of damaged cylinder parts. Therefore, traditional electroplating and brush plating methods can be used first to quickly restore worn dimensions, and then nanocomposite brush plating technology can be used to brush plate a nanocomposite plating layer on the size plating layer as the working layer to improve the surface performance of parts, making their performance superior to prototype new products.

Using brush plating or brush plating + brush plating nanocomposite plating to repair scratches, grooves, and dents on cylinder parts (such as cylinder barrels and piston rods) is a fast and effective process method.
Since brush plating technology is already a traditional or ordinary technology, and there is abundant relevant literature and information, it will not be introduced here.

sections.text: When selecting important process parameters for nanocomposite brush plating, attention should be paid to: 1) Brush plating voltage. Since the nanocomposite brush plating solution contains a large amount of nanoparticles, to ensure good deposition of these particles in the brush plating layer, the brush plating voltage is generally slightly higher than that of the substrate metal plating solution. Typically, when the workpiece is small, the workpiece temperature is low, or the relative movement speed between the plating pen and the workpiece is slow, the brush plating voltage should be lower. During the nanocomposite brush plating process, the initial plating voltage should be slightly higher, and after a period of time (e.g., 10-20 s), it should be reduced to the normal brush plating voltage.

2) Brush plating temperature. Throughout the entire nanocomposite brush plating process, the ideal plating temperature for the workpiece is room temperature. This helps maintain the physicochemical properties of the plating solution stable, ensuring that the brush plating effect (deposition rate, uniform plating ability, current efficiency, etc.) remains in the best state, which is beneficial for nanoparticle deposition. The resulting nanocomposite plating layer has low internal stress and high bonding strength.

According to reference literature, during the entire nanocomposite brush plating process, the brush plating temperature should not be lower than 15°C and should not exceed 50°C. 3) During the nanocomposite brush plating process, the relative movement speed between the workpiece and the plating pen is generally 6-10 m/min. If the relative movement speed is too fast, it is not conducive to nanoparticle deposition and can easily cause excessive stress in the nanocomposite plating layer. If the speed is too slow, the local heat generation is high, which can easily cause the surface of the nanocomposite plating layer to turn black, and can also lead to loose structure and rough surface.

sections.text: 1. Micro Pulse Resistance Welding Repair Technology

Micro pulse resistance welding repair technology is represented by "GM-3450 series mold repair machine and its process". This technology is also developed according to the needs of mechanical parts maintenance practice.

GM-3450 series mold repair machine is a sequence controllable electric pulse output device, which is essentially a storage point welding machine. There are three models, and its main technical parameters are shown in Table 6-10.

sections.caption: Table 6-10  Main Technical Parameters of GM-3450 Series Mold Repair Machine

sections.text: The repair process of GM-3450 series mold repair machine is to melt the repair material onto the parent material through the action of electric pulse. Three types of repair materials can be used: powder materials, wire materials and sheet materials. Place the repair material close to the parent material to be repaired, connect the negative pole of the repair machine power supply to the parent material, and connect the positive pole of the repair machine power supply to the welding electrode. Hold the welding electrode and press it against the parent material through the repair material to form a contact resistance R between the repair material and the parent material. At this time, if the pulse current I passes through the positive pole→welding electrode→repair material→contact resistance R→parent material→negative pole, then the Joule heat generated on R is proportional to I²RΔt (where Δt is the duration of the electric pulse). This heat can cause the temperature of a micro area at the interface between the repair material and the parent material to rise rapidly until metal melting occurs. The melting zone is between the repair material and the parent material, and there is a very short metallurgical reaction, after which the electric pulse disappears, and due to rapid heat conduction, a micro-zone welding point is obtained. A large number of such welding points constitute the construction process of GM-3450 series mold repair machine.

Since the time without electric pulse is long enough, this cooling process is very sufficient. From a macro perspective, during the welding process, the overall temperature rise of the workpiece (parent material) in the repair area is very small. Therefore, micro pulse resistance welding is a "cold welding" technology.

According to the material, structure, status, failure mode, etc. of the workpiece to be repaired, selecting appropriate repair materials and process parameters can achieve no damage to the parent material, firm bonding between the repair material and the parent material, and surface metal repair with modification effect.

Cladding. Micro-pulse resistance welding repair technology realized by GM-3450 series die and mold repair machine has the following characteristics: (1) Wide selection of cladding materials: Different cladding materials can be selected to obtain cladding layers with different properties such as hardness, wear resistance, impact resistance, high temperature resistance or corrosion resistance. (2) Strong adaptability to repaired workpieces: This technology can be used to repair both the dimensions and shapes of workpieces, and is especially suitable for repairing various defects of parts such as pores, sand holes, scratches, broken edges, blunt edges, raised edges, and peeling wear of grooves; for parts with machining size out of tolerance or machining defects, this technology can also be used for repair. (3) Good machinability of cladding layer: The cladding layer obtained by this technology can be machined by turning, milling, planing, grinding and various finishing processes, and can also be finely ground to achieve very low surface roughness values. All the above machining processes will not cause the cladding layer to fall off, and the cladding and machining can be performed alternately until a satisfactory cladding effect is obtained. (4) Wide range of cladding dimensions:

This technology can be used to obtain cladding layers ranging from several micrometers to several millimeters. Therefore, this technology can be used to repair small workpieces as well as large workpieces. (5) Simple implementation and operation: The equipment is small in size, easy to carry, and easy to approach large workpieces to complete operations. The equipment is simple and easy to operate, and skilled operators can also be easily trained. According to the literature, this technology has been successfully applied to the repair of hydraulic cylinder bodies, piston rods, etc.
2. Laser-like High-energy Pulse Precision Cold Cladding Repair Technology

Laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold cladding repair technology is a new type of cladding welding technology that uses a high-energy pulse arc generated between a tungsten electrode and a workpiece to rapidly melt the base material and filler welding material (such as welding wire) under inert gas protection to achieve precision cold cladding. The cold cladding quality and cladding welding precision of this technology can reach the effect of laser cladding welding, and can be used for precision cold cladding of surface defects such as scratches, pitting, and cracks of parts, as well as special-shaped surfaces.

The diagram shows: AC 220V/50Hz power source → Isolation → Rectifier → Precision pulse control circuit → Capacitor discharge pulse circuit. Below this main path: High-energy pulse → High-frequency high-voltage → Tungsten electrode → Electrode → Workpiece. At the bottom: Inert gas protection.

sections.text: The 220V/50Hz AC power is stepped down and rectified to charge the storage capacitor, and then the energy stored in the capacitor is released to the tungsten electrode and the workpiece through the arc generated by the high-energy pulse, and the arc with extremely high temperature quickly melts the welding wire and the workpiece to weld them together. The main technical indicators of the laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold cladding equipment are shown in Table 6-11.

sections.caption: Table 6-11 Main Technical Indicators

sections.text: The process parameters of laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold cladding mainly include the type and size of pulse current, the diameter and tip cone angle of tungsten electrode, the flow rate of protective gas, etc. Generally, process parameters are selected according to the following items. 1) Type and size of pulse current. The laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold cladding process is different from the general argon arc welding process, and the required pulse current is very concentrated and short in time. The size of pulse current and pulse time are related to each other, and the pulse time and current size are generally selected according to the specification of cladding wire. The size of pulse current is the most important parameter that determines the depth of the cladding layer, which mainly depends on factors such as cladding material, specification, and cladding position. Table 6-12 lists the planar cladding parameters of 45 steel. 2) Diameter and tip cone angle of tungsten electrode. The tip cone angle of tungsten electrode is an important process parameter. Different tip cone angles of tungsten electrode are selected according to the type of cladding current used. The size of the tip cone angle of tungsten electrode will affect the allowable current, arc initiation and arc stability of the tungsten electrode. When using small current cladding, a small diameter

Tungsten electrode with a small pointed tip angle can easily ignite and stabilize the arc; when performing large current repair welding, increasing the pointed tip angle can prevent the tungsten electrode tip from overheating and melting, reducing loss, and preventing the arc from expanding upward and affecting the stability of the cathode spot.

sections.caption: Table 6-12  Plane Repair Parameters for 45 Steel

sections.text: The pointed tip angle of the tungsten electrode also has a certain influence on the penetration depth and width of the weld. Reducing the pointed tip angle decreases the penetration depth and increases the width, while increasing it does the opposite.

3) Under certain conditions, there is an optimal range for the flow rate of the protective inert gas and the nozzle diameter, where the protection effect of the inert gas is optimal and the effective protection area is maximized. If the inert gas flow rate is too low, the airflow is poor and the ability to exclude surrounding air is weak, resulting in poor protection; if the inert gas flow rate is too high, it easily becomes turbulent, drawing in air, which also reduces the protection effect. Therefore, the inert gas flow rate and nozzle diameter must be properly matched.
The general repair process for laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold repair welding is as follows:

items: Select the pulse current size and pulse time according to the wire diameter.
Hold the welding gun, with the tungsten electrode at a 70° angle to the workpiece, and place the wire at a 15° angle to the workpiece.
Step on the foot pedal (or hand control) switch to produce a weld point, and operate sequentially to produce continuous weld lines.
After reaching the required repair dimensions, perform surface finishing.

sections.text: Laser-like high-energy pulse precision cold repair welding has the following performance characteristics:

items: It has high repair welding accuracy. Since this technology can precisely control the output current and time, adjusting within a certain range, and running stably, even using φ0.2 mm wire can achieve perfect repair welding, reaching the accuracy of laser repair welding.

It has small repair welding impact. Since this technology uses pulse current, concentrated energy, low arc initiation current, and short action time, it overcomes the impact of the repair welding process on the workpiece, allowing for the repair of thin-walled parts, with small repair welding stress and post-welding deformation.

It has a small heat-affected zone. Since this technology can precisely control the output current and time, the input energy can be precisely controlled, ensuring that the input energy is only sufficient for the fusion between the workpiece and the filler material, with small heat input to the base metal, small heat-affected zone, no degradation of base metal performance, and no macroscopic thermal deformation.

It has high joint strength. This technology can achieve metallurgical bonding between the base metal and the filler material, with high joint strength after welding, suitable for various machining methods, and will not have problems such as weak bonding or falling off.

It has a wide repair range. Except for materials with very low melting points such as zinc and tin, and cemented carbide, other various metal workpiece materials can be repaired using this technology.
This technology has no special requirements for repair welding materials, and ordinary TIG welding rods can be used as repair welding materials.

sections.text: Surface Coating Repair Technology (referred to as surface coating technology) is a surface engineering technology that involves mixing high molecular polymers with special fillers (such as graphite, molybdenum disulfide, metal powders, ceramic powders, and fibers) to form composite adhesives, which are then applied to the damaged surfaces of remanufactured blanks to achieve specific purposes (such as sealing, leak plugging, wear resistance, corrosion resistance, insulation, conductivity, heat preservation, radiation protection, defect repair, dimensional restoration, and their combinations).

Surface coating technology has a simple process, adjustable coating thickness, and does not produce a heat-affected zone or deformation in the substrate. It is suitable not only for repairing cracks, scratches, dimensional tolerances, and casting defects, as well as surface repair of temperature-sensitive metal components in remanufacturing, but also for repairing failed components with explosion hazards (such as underground equipment and oil and gas equipment). This technology is safe and reliable, requires no special equipment, can be performed on-site, has a short remanufacturing cycle, saves labor hours, and effectively improves productivity. It is a fast and economical remanufacturing technology with very broad application prospects.
The surface coating process includes the following steps:

items: Initial cleaning. Initial cleaning mainly involves removing oil and rust from the surface to be restored, in order to measure, formulate the coating repair process, and perform pre-processing. Initial cleaning of parts can be done by rough washing in gasoline, kerosene, or diesel, followed by final cleaning with acetone.

Pre-processing. To ensure that the repair layer has a certain thickness, the parts must be mechanically processed before applying the adhesive. The pre-processing depth for the surfaces to be repaired is generally 0.5 to 3 mm. To prevent edge damage to the coating, a margin of 1 to 2 mm should be left on both sides when processing the coating surface. To enhance the bonding strength between the coating and the substrate, the surface to be coated should be processed into a "zigzag" shape. A rough surface with zigzags can increase the coating area and improve the coating strength.

Final cleaning and activation treatment. Final cleaning can be done using acetone; if conditions permit, sandblasting can be used on the coating surface for coarse activation treatment to thoroughly remove the surface oxide layer; flame treatment or chemical treatment can also be used to improve the surface activity of the coating.

Mixing the adhesive. The coating material is usually composed of two components. To achieve the best results, it must be mixed in the correct proportions. After the coating material is thoroughly mixed, it should be used immediately.
Applying the coating. Coating construction methods include scraping, coating stamping, mold forming, etc.

Curing. The curing speed of the coating is related to the ambient temperature, with higher temperatures leading to faster curing. Generally, room temperature curing takes 24 hours, and the coating reaches its maximum performance after 7 days; if cured at 80°C, it takes 2 to 3 hours. For coatings that do not require subsequent processing, excess coating material on the edges of parts can be trimmed using saw (knife) blades or files. If there are pores larger than 1 mm on the coating surface, they should be cleaned with acetone first, then repaired with adhesive, and polished after curing.
For coatings that require subsequent processing, turning or grinding methods can be used for processing to restore dimensions and precision.

sections.text: Over the past few decades, with the continuous emergence of new coating adhesives, surface coating technology has developed significantly and is widely used in equipment maintenance and remanufacturing, such as restoring worn parts and dimensional tolerances. After parts are worn, wear-resistant repair adhesive can be directly applied to the worn surface, and then mechanical processing or grinding can be used to restore the part dimensions to the design dimensions. Compared with methods such as build-up welding, thermal spraying, electroplating, and brush plating, this method has the advantages of being able to repair temperature-sensitive metal components and having adjustable coating thickness. The two major series of cold-bonded wear-resistant coatings developed by Germany, SKC (SKC) and DIAMANT (DIAMANT), were used earlier on heavy gantry milling machine worktable guide rails, beam guide rails, hydraulic cylinder pistons, and other components, with very good results. The HNT epoxy wear-resistant coating material developed by Guangzhou Machine Tool Research Institute is one of the earliest products developed domestically, used for machine tool guide rails or other friction surfaces (repair); the AR-4 and AR-5 developed by Xiangfan City Adhesive Technology Research Institute, and the TG series super metal repair agents developed by Armored Engineering Academy are widely used in the fields of wear and corrosion repair and pre-protection treatment of mechanical components, achieving very good results.

In addition, solid lubricant films can be used to solve the lubrication problems of friction pairs in rockets, spacecraft, and other machinery; surface coating layers can be used to restore and pre-protect chemical pipelines, ship hulls and propellers; repair scratches on hydraulic cylinder bodies and machine tool guide rails, restore worn and oversized parts to design dimensions; and solve sealing and corrosion resistance issues.
However, due to the limitations of adhesive performance, its application is currently subject to the following restrictions:

items: The surface coating layer has a limited lifespan when working under conditions of moisture, heat, alternating cold and heat, impact, and other complex environments.

The high-temperature resistance of organic adhesive-based surface coating layers is not high, generally not exceeding 350°C. Inorganic adhesives can withstand high temperatures of 1000°C, and ceramic adhesives can withstand temperatures above 2000°C, but they are more brittle.
The surface coating has high tensile and shear strength but low peel strength.
The use of organic adhesives, especially solvent-based adhesives, involves safety issues such as flammability and toxicity.

sections.text: With the development of materials science, the performance of adhesives is also being greatly improved. Improving the bonding strength and rapid curing performance of coatings, developing new environmentally friendly, high-temperature resistant, long-life, high-strength, and functional nano-adhesives are the main development directions of adhesive technology.

It is an important process technology to realize the long life of parts, greatly saving the consumption of parts. At the same time, it enables the reuse of scrapped parts, with obvious economic and social benefits.

Compared with the conventional manual surfacing method, the plasma spray welding remanufacturing technology obtains excellent weld layer quality, and can obtain sealing surfaces that meet quality requirements with less powder consumption, saving a large amount of precious cobalt-based alloys. 1. Introduction to Thermal Spraying Repair Technology
(1) Basic Concept and Characteristics of Thermal Spraying

Thermal spraying repair technology (abbreviated as thermal spraying technology) refers to heating powder or wire materials to a molten or semi-molten state using a heat source (flame, arc, plasma arc), atomizing and spraying them onto the surface of the remanufacturing blank under the action of high-pressure airflow, forming a lamellar structure and accumulating into a coating, which is a remanufacturing surface repair technology.

Thermal spraying is an important means of product remanufacturing. It can not only restore the dimensions of product parts but also improve the surface performance of parts, and has been widely used in the remanufacturing and maintenance of equipment parts, producing significant comprehensive benefits. Thermal spraying has the following characteristics:
1) The selection range of thermal spraying materials is extensive, including almost all metals, alloys, ceramics, plastics, and organic polymer materials.

2) The functions of the repair layer are diverse, including wear resistance, corrosion resistance, high temperature resistance, oxidation resistance, heat insulation, conductivity, insulation, sealing, friction reduction, lubrication, and radiation protection.
3) It is suitable for various substrate materials, such as metals, ceramics, glass, and other inorganic materials, as well as plastics, wood, paper, and other organic materials.
4) The thermal influence on the substrate is small, and the thickness of the repair layer is easily controlled, but the surface roughness value is large.
5) The repair layer and substrate are mechanically bonded or semi-metallurgical/semi-mechanical bonded, with low bonding strength, and the tensile bonding strength is only 30-40 MPa.
6) The thermal spray coating usually has a layered structure, with pores, incompletely melted particles, oxide films, and residual stress.

Reference [110] points out that when using the spraying method to repair internal holes, due to the cooling shrinkage of the internal hole substrate after repair, cracks, peeling, or even falling off of the repair layer often occur. Therefore, this method is not suitable for repairing internal hole parts such as hydraulic cylinders.

(2) Basic Principles and Classification of Thermal Spraying. Taking powder spraying as an example, during the thermal spraying process, the spraying material roughly goes through the following processes: heating → acceleration → melting → re-acceleration → impact on the substrate → cooling and solidification → formation of the coating. The overall process can be approximately divided into three stages:

items: The spraying material is heated, accelerated, and melted.
The melted material is atomized by the hot gas flow, further accelerated to form a particle flow; the melted particles interact with the surrounding medium.
The particles collide, deform, solidify, and accumulate on the substrate surface.

sections.text: The spraying material is related to many factors such as the heating temperature, speed, material type, powder particle size, energy type, spray gun structure, and powder feeding method. According to the type of heat source (or principle) used, thermal spraying can be classified as follows: 1) Using combustion flame as the heat source, including flame spraying, explosion spraying, supersonic flame spraying, plastic spraying, etc. 2) Using electric arc as the heat source, including arc spraying, high-speed arc spraying, etc. 3) Using plasma as the heat source, including atmospheric plasma spraying, supersonic plasma spraying, low-pressure plasma spraying (vacuum plasma spraying), water-stabilized plasma spraying, etc. 4) Using other heat sources, including wire explosion spraying, laser spraying, cold spraying, etc. Thermal spraying materials are classified by shape, including powder, wire, strip, rod; by composition, including metal, ceramic, organic, composite materials; by function, including wear-resistant, heat-resistant, oxidation-resistant, corrosion-resistant, etc.

(3) Thermal Spraying Process and Characteristics. The thermal spraying process is as follows: substrate surface pretreatment, including surface purification, pre-processing, roughening, etc.; applying various spraying methods for spraying; coating post-treatment, including pore sealing treatment, mechanical processing, heat treatment, etc.

2. Plasma Spraying Repair Technology
(1) Plasma Spraying Equipment. Plasma spraying equipment mainly includes the following parts:

1) Plasma spray gun. It is actually a non-transfer arc plasma generator and is the core device of plasma spraying equipment. It concentrates water, electricity, gas, powder, etc. of the entire system, and the most critical components are the nozzle and cathode. Among them, the nozzle is made of high thermal conductivity pure copper, and the cathode mostly uses cerium tungsten electrode (tungsten oxide mass fraction is 2%-3%).

2) Power supply. It is used to supply direct current to the spray gun, which is usually a full-wave silicon rectifier device. Commonly available are three specifications with rated power of 40 kW, 50 kW and 80 kW.

3) Powder feeder. It is a device used to store spray coating powder and feed the powder to the spray gun according to the process requirements. Its main technical requirements are high powder feeding accuracy, convenient powder feeding adjustment, and wide adaptability to powder particle size.

4) Heat exchanger. It is mainly used to enable the spray gun to obtain effective cooling, so as to achieve the purpose of prolonging the service life of the spray gun, usually adopting water cooling system.
5) Gas supply system. It includes the supply system of working gas and powder feeding gas.
6) Control equipment. It is used to regulate and control water, electricity, gas and powder, and can adjust and control the action program and process parameters of the spraying process.
(2) Plasma spraying process parameters
In the plasma spraying process, there are many factors affecting the quality of the coating, but the main process parameters are:

1) Plasma gas. Common gases include nitrogen and argon, and the purity of the gas is required to be no less than 99.9%. The selection of gas is mainly based on its availability and economy. Nitrogen is cheap, has high plasma flame enthalpy, fast heat transfer, and is conducive to powder heating and melting, but it cannot be used for powders or substrates that are prone to nitriding reactions; argon has a lower ionization potential, stable plasma arc and easy ignition, and a shorter arc flame, which is suitable for spraying small parts or thin parts. Argon also has a good protective effect, but argon has low thermal enthalpy and high price.

The size of gas flow directly affects the thermal enthalpy and flow rate of the plasma flame flow, thereby affecting the spraying efficiency, coating porosity and bonding force. If the gas flow rate is too large, the gas will take away useful heat from the plasma jet and accelerate the speed of the sprayed particles, reducing the "retention" time of the sprayed particles in the plasma flame, resulting in the sprayed particles not reaching the semi-melting or plastic state necessary for deformation, resulting in poor tensile bonding strength, density and hardness of the coating, and a significant decrease in deposition rate; on the contrary, if the gas flow rate is too small, it will cause the arc voltage value to be inappropriate and greatly reduce the speed of the sprayed particles. In extreme cases, it may cause the sprayed particles to overheat, causing the sprayed particles to be excessively melted or vaporized, causing the molten powder particles to accumulate at the nozzle or powder spray port, and then deposit in the coating in larger spherical particles, forming large holes.

2) Plasma arc power. If the plasma arc power is too high, more gas will be converted into plasma, and under the condition of high power and low working gas flow rate, almost all working gas will be transformed into active plasma flow, and the plasma flame temperature is also very high, which may cause some sprayed particles to vaporize and cause the coating composition to change, and the vapor of the sprayed particles melted between the substrate and the coating or inside the coating will condense, resulting in poor bonding. In addition, it may also cause the nozzle and electrode to be burned. If the plasma arc power is too low, the obtained is partial plasma gas and a plasma flame with lower temperature, which will cause insufficient heating of the sprayed particles, and the tensile bonding strength, hardness and deposition efficiency of the coating will be low.

3) Powder feeding. The powder feeding speed must be adapted to the input power. If the powder feeding speed is too fast, raw powder (unmelted) will appear, resulting in a decrease in spraying efficiency; if the powder feeding speed is too slow, the sprayed particles will be severely oxidized, and the substrate will be overheated. The powder feeding position will also affect the coating structure and spraying efficiency. Generally speaking, the powder must be fed to the flame core to obtain the best heating effect and the highest spraying speed.

4) Spraying distance and spraying angle. The coating material and coating characteristics are very sensitive to the spraying distance. The distance between the spray gun and the workpiece will affect the speed and temperature of the sprayed particles when they impact the substrate. If the spraying distance is too large, the speed and temperature of the sprayed particles will decrease, and the tensile bonding strength and spraying efficiency of the coating will decrease significantly, and the porosity will increase; if the spraying distance is too small, the substrate temperature will be too high, and the substrate and coating will be oxidized, affecting the bonding of the coating. However, under the condition that the substrate temperature rise is allowed, it is better to have a slightly smaller spraying distance.

The spraying angle refers to the angle between the flame flow axis and the surface of the sprayed part. When this angle is less than 45°, due to the influence of the "shadow benefit", the coating structure will deteriorate and form holes, resulting in a loose coating.

5) Relative movement speed of spray gun and workpiece. The movement speed of the spray gun should ensure that the coating is flat and prevent the appearance of ridges. In other words, there should be sufficient overlap between the widths of each stroke. Under the premise of meeting the above requirements, a higher spray gun movement speed is generally used in the spraying operation, which can prevent local overheating and surface oxidation.

6) Substrate temperature control. The ideal process is to preheat the workpiece to the temperature to be reached during the spraying process before spraying, and then use air cooling to keep it at the original temperature during the spraying process.
3. Plasma spraying and welding repair technology
(1) Plasma spraying and welding equipment

Plasma spraying and welding or plasma arc surfacing is a new surfacing process, which has the advantages of shallow melting depth, high surfacing rate, and low dilution rate. According to the filling material used during surfacing, plasma arc surfacing machines can be hot wire plasma arc surfacing machines, cold wire plasma arc surfacing machines, powder plasma arc surfacing machines, and melting pole plasma arc surfacing machines. Among them, the powder plasma arc surfacing machine is the most commonly used one.

The powder plasma arc surfacing machine uses the high temperature generated by the plasma arc to melt specific wear-resistant, corrosion-resistant or high-temperature alloy powder, and is a surfacing equipment that melts it onto the surface of the workpiece. By adjusting the plasma arc parameters, the thickness, width, and hardness of the surfacing layer can be conveniently adjusted within a certain range, and a surfacing layer with excellent performance can be obtained. Therefore, this equipment is widely used in the surfacing of bearings, bearing necks, valve plates, valve seats, worm gear blades and other parts, as well as the repair of wear after oil drill rods, bearings, shafts, and rolling mill rolls. Of course, this equipment can also be used for the repair of hydraulic cylinders and metal cylinder parts.
The powder plasma arc surfacing machine is roughly the same as the general plasma welding machine.

This is achieved by using a powder welding gun instead of the welding gun in the plasma welding machine. The powder welding gun generally uses direct water cooling and has a powder delivery channel, with the compression channel of the nozzle used being generally no more than 1. During plasma arc surfacing, a transferred arc or a mixed arc is generally used. In addition to the plasma gas and shielding gas, a powder delivery gas is also required. The powder delivery gas is generally argon.
