(2) Plasma spraying welding or plasma arc overlaying process. According to the introduction in reference [116], powder plasma arc overlaying is a method of overlaying by automatically sending alloy powder into the plasma arc area, also known as spraying welding. Powder plasma arc overlaying uses argon as the ionization gas. By adjusting various welding parameters and controlling the heat transferred to the workpiece, a high-quality coating with shallow melting depth, low dilution rate, and flat and smooth forming can be obtained.

In powder plasma arc overlaying, two DC arc welding machines with steep drop external characteristics are generally used as the power source. The negative poles of the two welding machines are connected in parallel to a high-frequency oscillator, and then connected to the cerium tungsten electrode of the spray gun through a cable. Among them, the positive pole of one welding machine is connected to the spray nozzle of the spray gun to generate a non-transfer arc; the positive pole of the other welding machine is connected to the workpiece to generate a transfer arc. Argon is used as the ionization gas, which enters the spray gun through an electromagnetic valve and a rotor flowmeter. After the power is turned on, a non-transfer arc is ignited by a high-frequency spark, and then a conductive channel between the electrode and the workpiece is formed by the jet of the non-transfer arc, thereby igniting the transfer arc. Before or simultaneously with the establishment of the transfer arc, the powder feeder sends powder to the spray gun, blows it into the arc, and sprays it onto the workpiece. Once the transfer arc is established, an alloy molten pool is formed on the workpiece, so that the alloy powder "melts" on the workpiece. As the spray gun or workpiece moves, the liquid alloy gradually solidifies, eventually forming an alloy overlay layer.

The characteristics of powder plasma arc overlaying are low dilution rate, generally controlled at 5%～15%, which is beneficial to fully guarantee the performance of the alloy material. For example, if 5mm overlay is required by stick electrode arc overlaying, only 2mm overlay is needed by plasma arc overlaying. The plasma arc has high temperature and concentrated energy, stable process, strong directionality, and is less disturbed by external factors. The alloy powder is fully melted and has little spatter. The slag and gas in the molten pool are easily excluded, so that the obtained overlay layer has excellent quality, is flat and smooth, and has a wide and precisely controllable size range. The width of one overlay can be controlled at 1～150mm, and the thickness can be 0.25～8mm, which is difficult to achieve by other overlaying methods. In addition, powder plasma arc overlaying has high productivity, is easy to mechanize and automate, and can reduce labor intensity.

According to the different results of the laser beam acting on the part material, laser remanufacturing technology can be mainly divided into two categories: laser surface modification technology and laser processing forming technology. Laser remanufacturing technology mainly aims at the damage of parts such as surface wear, corrosion, erosion, defects and dimensional changes, and restores the structural dimensions, while improving the service performance of parts. It is an important part of advanced remanufacturing technology, and plays an important role in restoring the core parts of waste products and improving the performance of parts. sections.text: 1. Laser Cladding Repair Technology

Laser cladding is a laser processing technology that uses a high-energy density laser beam to heat and melt cladding material, forming a molten pool on the substrate surface. After cooling and solidification, a metallurgical bonding layer is formed on the substrate surface, which is the laser cladding repair technology. This technology can restore the shape and dimensions of damaged parts and enable the metallurgical bonding layer formed on the substrate surface to have properties such as wear resistance, corrosion resistance, heat resistance, and oxidation resistance. Furthermore, it can prepare high-performance alloy surfaces on low-performance, inexpensive steel materials. It is a surface modification technology and waste parts repair and remanufacturing technology with high economic efficiency.

According to different methods of supplying cladding material to the workpiece surface, it can be divided into powder feeding laser cladding, wire feeding laser cladding, and pre-placed laser cladding. According to different working modes of the laser beam, it can be divided into pulsed laser cladding and continuous laser cladding. Pulsed laser cladding generally uses YAG (solid-state laser medium is Nd:YAG) pulsed laser, while continuous laser cladding mostly uses continuous wave CO₂ laser. The laser cladding process includes two aspects: optimizing and controlling laser heating process parameters; determining the cladding material and its supply method to the workpiece surface. For the CO₂ laser cladding process widely used in industry, the main process parameters that need to be optimized and controlled include laser output power, spot size, and scanning speed.
The laser repair process design specified in GB/T 29796-2013 includes two contents: laser cladding material selection and laser and process parameter selection.

Laser cladding material refers to the material added during the laser cladding process. It can be powder, wire, tape, or foil, among which powder material is the most widely used. At present, the powder materials for laser cladding are generally borrowed from thermal spray powders and self-designed and developed powder materials, mainly including self-fluxing alloy powders, metal-ceramic composite (mixed) powders, and metal powders independently designed and developed by various application units.

To ensure that the laser cladding layer has excellent quality, mechanical properties, and forming process performance, and to reduce its crack sensitivity, it is necessary to reasonably design or select the cladding material. Based on the principles of similar thermal expansion coefficients, similar melting points, and wettability between the cladding material and substrate, the laser cladding process also needs to be optimized. The quality control of the laser cladding layer mainly focuses on reducing component contamination, cracks, and pores in the laser cladding layer, as well as preventing oxidation and burn-through.
The evaluation of the laser cladding process and the quality inspection of repaired parts should follow the standards specified in GB/T 29796-2013.

2. Laser Forming and Cladding Repair Technology

According to the literature [86], laser cladding usually uses pre-placed coating or powder feeding methods to add cladding metal. Utilizing the characteristics of laser beam focusing with extremely high energy, only a slight melting of the substrate surface occurs in an instant, while the metal powder with the same or similar material to the substrate is completely melted. After the laser leaves, rapid solidification occurs, obtaining a dense (melted) cladding layer surface that is metallurgically bonded with the substrate, restoring the geometric dimensions of the part surface, and also strengthening the surface coating. The basic principle and technical essence of laser forming and cladding remanufacturing (repair) technology are the same as those of laser cladding rapid forming remanufacturing technology.

Laser forming and cladding repair technology solves the problems of material selection limitations, process heat stress, thermal deformation, coarse material grains, and difficult to guarantee the bonding strength between the substrate material that cannot be solved by repair processes such as vibration welding, argon arc welding, spraying, and plating. This technology has the following characteristics:

items: The laser cladding layer is metallurgically bonded with the substrate, and the bonding strength is not lower than 90% of the original substrate material.

Only the surface of the substrate material slightly melts during laser processing, with a micro-melting layer of 0.05～0.1 mm, and the heat-affected zone of the substrate is extremely small, generally 0.1～0.2 mm.
The temperature rise of the substrate does not exceed 80°C during laser processing, and there is no thermal deformation after laser processing.
The controllability of laser cladding technology is good and it is easy to achieve automation.

There is no coarse casting structure in the cladding layer and the substrate, and the structure of the cladding layer and the interface layer is dense, with fine crystals, and no defects such as pores, inclusions, and cracks.

sections.text: 6) The laser cladding layer is a gradient functional material composed of a bottom layer, a middle layer, and a surface layer, each with its own characteristics. The bottom layer has good wettability with the substrate and high bonding strength; the middle layer has high strength and hardness, and good crack resistance; the surface layer has properties such as erosion resistance, wear resistance, and corrosion resistance. This makes the repaired or remanufactured parts perform better and safer when used in equipment.
According to relevant information, laser forming and cladding is also known as laser profile following cladding, which needs to solve two problems:

items: How to imitate the prototype to repair the damaged part of the part, that is, profile following cladding repair or profile following cladding repair.
How to ensure that the repair layer is metallurgically bonded with the substrate and has a small heat-affected zone, and at the same time, the repair layer can grow outward in a single pass.

sections.text: To this end, relevant proprietary technologies can be referred to (for a fee) to solve the above problems. In the application of laser forming and cladding repair technology, the different irradiation characteristics of CO₂ laser and Nd-YAG laser should also be considered, and they can be used alternately during the repair process to adapt to the processing of cladding layers in different areas.
6.6 Mechanical Processing Technology for Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts
6.6.1 Basic Requirements for Mechanical Processing of Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts

The mechanical processing of the surface repair layer of cylinder parts refers to the mechanical processing of the remanufacturing coating and cladding layer on the surface of cylinder parts. There are some basic requirements for the mechanical processing of the surface repair layer of cylinder parts.
1. Requirements before processing

items: First, the processing area, range, and process plan should be determined.
The absence of defects that affect performance should also be determined.
The residual repair layer outside the processing area should be removed to prevent affecting subsequent processing.

sections.text: 2. Requirements during processing

items: Processing needs to consider geometric tolerances to determine its positioning and process.
Different processes should be selected according to the characteristics of different cylinder parts.

The positioning datum should be checked and trimmed to ensure that the dimensional tolerance and geometric tolerance can meet the drawing and technical requirements. Processing should be carried out according to the process regulations.

When mechanically processing the remanufacturing repair layer, suitable cutting tools, cutting parameters, or special processing methods should be used. The cutting tools should have sufficient strength, rigidity, toughness, and wear resistance.

During processing, a smaller cutting feed rate, depth of cut, and lower speed should be used, and the cooling of the cutting tool and repair layer should be strengthened to prevent the repair layer from falling off, cracking, burning, etc.
For remanufacturing coating, grinding is recommended; for remanufacturing cladding layer, turning, milling, or grinding can be used.
The mechanical processing of cylinder parts should be inspected and accepted according to the process, and only after the previous process is qualified can it be transferred to the next process.
During the handling, processing, and storage of cylinder parts, damage such as bumps, scratches, corrosion, and deformation should be prevented.

sections.text: 3. Requirements after processing

items: After processing, the surface performance, dimensional accuracy, geometric accuracy, and surface roughness of the cylinder parts should meet the requirements of the drawing and technical requirements.
Except for special requirements, the sharp corners of the processed cylinder parts should be dulled.

sections.text: 6.6.2 Turning Processing of Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts

Turning is one of the most commonly used mechanical processing methods for surface repair layers of cylinder parts. However, due to some characteristics of the surface repair layer of the parts, this turning processing often has the following problems:

items: Large impact and vibration during processing. Due to the uneven surface of the thermal spray coating and metal surfacing layer, as well as the uneven hardness inside and the presence of hard points (carbides, borides

sections.text: and gaps, etc., these will cause the cutting force to fluctuate during turning, resulting in large impacts and vibrations during the machining process. Therefore, the process system composed of the lathe, fixture, workpiece, and tool is required to have good rigidity, and higher requirements are also put forward for the strength of the tool.
(2) The tool is prone to chipping and abnormal wear

Due to the hard outer skin, sand holes, pores, etc. of the metal surfacing layer, the hard points inside the thermal spray coating, coupled with the vibration and impact during cutting, it is easy to cause chipping and abnormal wear of the cutting edge, resulting in loss of cutting ability.
(3) Short tool life

Since the metal surfacing layer and thermal spray coating generally have high hardness and wear resistance, especially the high-hardness metal surfacing layer and thermal spray coating, therefore, during machining, large cutting force and cutting heat are generated, which accelerates the wear of the cutting edge and causes it to become dull quickly. This brings great difficulties to cutting processing, and even makes it difficult to carry out cutting processing. Due to the short tool life, the improvement of cutting dosage is limited, and the productivity is reduced.
(4) The thermal spray coating is prone to peeling

The bonding strength between the thermal spray coating and the substrate is not high. The coating obtained by the spray process has a mechanical or semi-mechanical bonding with the substrate, and the tensile bonding strength is generally 30-50 MPa. In addition, the coating is generally thin, so during cutting processing, when the cutting force exceeds a certain limit, the coating is prone to peeling. This is something that should be prevented during cutting processing.
6.6.2.1 Turning of Surfacing Layer

Using the surfacing method to obtain the dimensional restoration layer of the wear surface of parts is a commonly used remanufacturing method. Although the metallurgical properties of the surfacing restoration layer mainly depend on the material of the surfacing electrode, due to the large and uneven thickness of the restoration layer caused by the surfacing method, surface hardening and changes in the organization within the layer, etc., the machinability of the surfacing layer will become poor, and it needs to be fully considered and noted during cutting processing.
1. Turning of low-alloy steel surfacing layer

Due to the different carbon content of the surfacing electrode, the hardness of the obtained surfacing layer is also different, which can be divided into medium-hardness surfacing layer and high-hardness surfacing layer from the perspective of hardness. The medium-hardness surfacing layer is the most widely used in the remanufacturing of mechanical parts. The medium-hardness surfacing layer is formed under normal cooling speed during surfacing, and the organization of the surfacing layer is pearlite plus a small amount of ferrite; when the cooling speed is faster, martensite will appear. In order to avoid the appearance of martensite and facilitate cutting processing, attention should be paid to reducing the cooling speed, such as adopting heat preservation and cooling.

The hardness of the medium-hardness surfacing layer is 200-350 HBW (such as surfacing layer with electrode 107, the hardness is about 250 HBW; with electrode 127, the hardness of the surfacing layer is about 350 HBW). The alloy elements such as Cr and Mn in the surfacing metal will dissolve in ferrite, playing a role in solid solution strengthening, and can also make the carbide alloy, so that the surfacing layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance, as well as good impact resistance.

The surfacing layer has a certain hardness and wear resistance, and when it is cut, the vibration and impact generated are large. In order to ensure that the tool is not damaged during processing and that the tool has a certain life, according to the commonly used tool materials and cutting performance and characteristics at present, tools such as carbide YG8, YT5, and YW1 can be selected for rough machining. These tool materials have good toughness and high bending strength, and are not prone to chipping during processing. For finishing, in addition to requiring the tool to have good wear resistance, it is also required to withstand the impact and vibration of hard points, pores, and sand holes left over from rough machining. At this time, tools such as carbide YT15 with higher hardness and better wear resistance can be selected.
2. Turning of stainless steel surfacing layer

The stainless steel surfacing layer is mostly obtained by surfacing with austenitic electrodes, and the metallographic organization is austenite. The austenitic organization has large plasticity and is prone to work hardening. In addition, the thermal conductivity is also very low (about 1/3 of that of 45 steel), so the austenitic stainless steel surfacing layer is also difficult to process.

For the stainless steel surfacing layer, YT-class carbide tools are not suitable for processing the stainless steel surfacing layer, because the titanium element in YT-class carbide steel is prone to cold welding with the titanium element in the workpiece material, which aggravates tool wear. Therefore, YG-class, YH-class, or YW-class carbide tools are generally used, and high-performance high-speed steel tools can also be used. Tool geometric parameters: the front angle is -5° to 0°; the back angle is 4° to 6°; the edge inclination angle is -5° to 0°; the main deflection angle should be appropriately reduced, and the tool tip arc radius should be increased. The cutting dosage is selected as ap=1.5-2mm, f=0.3-0.4mm/r, vc=14-18m/min.
6.6.2.2 Turning of Thermal Spray Coating

The biggest feature of thermal spray coating is its high hardness and high wear resistance, and its hardness can reach 50-70 HRC. Such thermal spray coatings can be called high-hardness thermal spray coatings, which are difficult to process. When cutting these coatings, there are special requirements for the selection of tool materials, tool geometric parameters, and cutting dosage.
1. Selection of tool materials

The general requirements for thermal spray coating on tool materials are high hardness, high wear resistance, sufficient bending strength and toughness. General carbide grades cannot be used for processing high-hardness thermal spray coatings. At present, the following three tool materials are better for processing thermal spray coatings:
1) Ultrafine-grained carbide with added tantalum carbide and niobium carbide.

The main functions of tantalum carbide (TaC) and niobium carbide (NbC) in carbide are as follows: they improve the hardness of carbide at normal and high temperatures, because their melting point is as high as 3500-3880°C, thereby improving the wear resistance of carbide; they prevent the growth of WC grains during the sintering process, thereby playing a role in refining grains, improving the bending strength, impact toughness and wear resistance of YT-class carbide; they improve the bonding temperature of carbide and steel, because their bonding temperature is higher than that of WC and TiC, reducing the diffusion of alloy components into steel, thereby reducing tool bonding wear and extending tool life. In ultrafine-grained carbide, due to the high dispersion of WC and cobalt,

Increasing the bonding area improves bonding strength, thereby increasing hardness by 1.5 to 2 HRA, and significantly improving bending strength. Therefore, ultra-fine grain cemented carbide with added tantalum carbide and niobium carbide exhibits better performance in terms of hardness, wear resistance, bending strength, and toughness, and can be used for low-speed cutting without chipping, adapting to the cutting processing of high-hardness thermal spray coatings. 2) Ceramic tool materials. Ceramics used as tool materials include pure Al₂O₃ ceramics, Al₂O₃-TiC mixed ceramics, and Si₃N₄-based ceramics. The domestic grades are SG5 (94 HRA, bending strength greater than 0.7 GPa) and AG2 (93.5 to 95 HRA, bending strength greater than 0.8 GPa). Using them for cutting thermal spray coatings yields good results, but their bending strength still needs further improvement. For example, using an SG5 blade to cut a nickel-based 102 spray coating (55 to 60 HRC), with cutting parameters aₚ=0.1 mm, f=0.3 mm/r, v=29 m/min, to machine an outer diameter of 50 mm and a length of 650 mm, the tool travels a cutting distance of 150 mm, and the wear VB behind the tool is 0.15 mm, with a surface roughness value of 10 to 2.5 μm. 3) Cubic boron nitride. Cubic boron nitride (CBN) is obtained by transforming hexagonal boron nitride under high temperature and high pressure with the addition of a catalyst. It is divided

into polycrystalline cubic boron nitride and cubic boron nitride composite blades. The advantages of cubic boron nitride are obvious: it has very high hardness and wear resistance, with a microhardness of 8000 to 9000 HV, second only to diamond; it has very high thermal stability (heat resistance can reach 1400 to 1500°C), much higher than diamond (heat resistance 700 to 800°C); it has great chemical inertness, and does not easily react chemically with iron group metals at 1200 to 1300°C. The overall bending strength is currently still at a relatively low level, with some blades reaching above 0.5 GPa. Cubic boron nitride tools can be used for cutting difficult-to-machine materials such as cemented carbide, quenched steel, chilled cast iron, and high-temperature alloys, with processing effects comparable to grinding. Currently, for high-hardness thermal spray coatings, it is the tool material with the highest cutting efficiency, and the cutting speed can be 4 to 5 times higher than that of YC09 cemented carbide blades.
2. Selection of Tool Geometry Parameters

The general requirements for tool geometry parameters for thermal spray coatings are to ensure the strength of the cutting edge (or insert) and good heat dissipation conditions, which are the principles for selecting tool geometric parameters. Additionally, attention should be paid to the rigidity of the system, and the radial component force should not be too large to avoid causing vibration. sections.text: 3. Selection of Cutting Parameters for Thermal Spray Coatings

The cutting parameters for thermal spray coatings are also limited by tool life. For the cutting processing of thermal spray coatings, the tool wear criterion can be determined by the method of testing to obtain the curve of tool wear amount versus cutting time. The influence of cutting speed on tool life is the greatest, followed by feed rate, while the influence of depth of cut is the smallest. Therefore, when prioritizing cutting parameters, the selection order is as follows: first, use the maximum depth of cut aₚ as much as possible, then select the allowable feed rate according to the machining conditions and requirements, and finally, select the maximum cutting speed under the conditions of allowable tool life or machine power. 6.6.3 Grinding of Repair Layers on Cylinder Parts

Grinding is mainly used for precision machining of outer circles, inner circles, planes, and various formed surfaces (gears, threads, splines, etc.). It can be used to machine difficult-to-machine thermal spray coatings, but its productivity is lower compared to grinding other difficult-to-machine metal materials. Generally, grinding accuracy can reach IT6-IT5 grade, and surface roughness can reach 0.08-0.20μm.
1. Characteristics of Grinding Thermal Spray Coatings

Higher accuracy and smaller surface roughness values can be obtained through grinding, so it is usually used for precision machining of thermal spray coatings. For high-hardness spray coatings, grinding is relatively difficult, mainly due to the following two reasons:

1) Grinding wheels tend to become dull rapidly and lose their grinding ability. The main reasons for the rapid dulling of grinding wheels are the dulling and breaking of the abrasive grains, and the "loading" of the grinding wheel. This is particularly prominent when grinding inner holes, as the diameter of the grinding wheel for inner holes is restricted by the hole size, unlike when grinding outer circles where larger diameter grinding wheels can be used. Therefore, the number of times the abrasive grains are engaged in grinding increases relatively within the same time period, leading to intensified wear and shortened wheel life.

2) Large radial cutting forces can cause vibration during the machining process, as well as make it easy for grinding heat to burn the surface and cause cracks in the machined surface, all of which affect the quality of the machined surface and the improvement of grinding parameters. Therefore, for grinding high-hardness thermal spray coatings, artificial diamond grinding wheels and cubic boron nitride grinding wheels are mostly used.

At present, domestic comparative test data for grinding nickel-based thermal spray coating outer circles using artificial diamond grinding wheels, green silicon carbide grinding wheels, and white corundum grinding wheels show that the performance of artificial diamond grinding wheels is far superior to that of green silicon carbide grinding wheels and white corundum grinding wheels.

sections.text: 6.6.4 Special Processing Techniques for Surface Repair Layers of Cylinder Parts
1. Electrolytic Grinding

Electrolytic grinding utilizes the electrochemical effect of electrolyte on the metal being processed (electrolytic action) and the mechanical grinding action of the conductive grinding wheel on the processing surface to remove the surface layer of metal. Electrolytic grinding of thermal spray coatings features high productivity, good processing quality, good economy, strong adaptability, and wide processing range, making it a new processing technology for difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings.

The electrolyte is an extremely important factor affecting productivity and processing quality in the electrolytic grinding process. During actual production, the optimal electrolyte for electrolytic grinding should be selected based on the technical requirements of different products and different materials. Tests show that for electrolytic grinding of difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings, electrolytes with sodium dihydrogen phosphate as the main component have better grinding performance.

The machine tools for electrolytic grinding can be either specialized electrolytic grinding machines or ordinary grinding machines and lathes that have been modified. The DC power supply for electrolytic grinding requires adjustable voltage (5-20V) and relatively stiff external characteristics. The maximum working current can be selected from 10-1000A depending on the processing area and required productivity. The circulating pump for supplying electrolyte generally uses a small centrifugal pump, equipped with devices for filtering and settling impurities in the electrolyte. Electrolyte is typically sprayed using pipes and flat nozzles, with the nozzle attached to the pipe and spraying electrolyte toward the working area. The internal grinding head consists of a high-speed grinding wheel shaft and a three-phase AC motor. The process parameters for electrolytic grinding can be formulated based on the following factors:

items: Process parameters of the grinding wheel. The grinding wheel can use conductive grinding wheels with diamond-bronze binder or graphite and silver-impregnated conductive grinding wheels. The peripheral speed of the grinding wheel vs=15-20m/s, axial feed speed vfa=0.5-1m/min (internal and external grinding), vfa=10-15m/min (surface grinding), workpiece peripheral speed vw=10-20m/s, radial feed speed vfr=0.05-0.15m/min (double stroke).
Voltage and current specifications. During rough machining, voltage is 8-12V, current density is 20-30A/cm²; during finish machining, voltage is 6-8V, current density is 10-15A/cm².

sections.text: If blackening of the grinding surface is observed when applying the above process parameters, the voltage should be reduced or the radial feed speed decreased while increasing the axial feed speed.
2. Ultrasonic Vibration Turning

Ultrasonic vibration turning is a processing method that uses a cutting tool to produce high-frequency vibration along the cutting speed direction for turning. The fundamental difference between ultrasonic vibration turning and ordinary turning is that in ultrasonic vibration turning, the cutting edge and the metal being cut form separated cutting, meaning the tool completes one cutting and separation cycle in an extremely short time during each vibration. In ordinary turning, the cutting edge and the metal being cut undergo continuous cutting without separation. Therefore, the mechanism of ultrasonic vibration turning is different from that of ordinary turning.

The main features of ultrasonic vibration turning are that both cutting force and cutting heat are much lower than in ordinary turning. The cutting force is approximately 1/3 to 1/20 of that in ordinary turning, and the cutting heat is approximately 1/5 to 1/10 of that in ordinary turning. This is the fundamental reason why ultrasonic vibration turning can achieve high processing accuracy and good surface quality. Tests show that for ultrasonic vibration turning of difficult-to-process thermal spray coatings, the cutting edge and tip of the tool must have high strength and wear resistance. The selection of tool material and tool geometric parameters should meet the following requirements:

items: Tool material. Tool materials such as YC09 and YW2 have good cutting performance when machining difficult-to-process Ni60 thermal spray coatings. For Al₂O₃ ceramic spray coatings, cubic boron nitride blades must be used. The tool life for both reaches a good practical level and is longer than in ordinary turning.

Tool geometric parameters. To ensure high strength of the cutting edge, the rake angle is generally selected as γo=0°; to reduce friction, the clearance angle is generally selected as αo=8°-12°; to enhance tip strength, both the principal cutting edge angle κr and auxiliary cutting edge angle κ'r can take small values, and the tip arc radius rε can take a large value to enhance tip strength, generally selected as rε=2-3mm.

sections.text: Ultrasonic vibration turning of thermal spray coatings has been well applied in engineering practice. After engine piston pins of certain construction machinery became worn and were scrapped in large quantities, they were remanufactured by thermal spraying (spray coating material was Ni60 with hardness of 60HRC). Mechanical processing was difficult after coating. The dimensional tolerance for the outer diameter of the piston pin was 0.011mm, and the surface roughness value was 0.32-0.04μm. Ordinary turning could not meet these requirements. Using ultrasonic vibration turning with the following process parameters: vibration frequency 20kHz, amplitude a=15μm, workpiece speed vw=4.8m/min, feed rate f=0.08mm/rev, depth of cut ap=0.1mm. After processing, the outer circle of the piston pin was measured with a dimensional error of 0.009mm and surface roughness value of 0.16μm, meeting assembly and usage requirements.
3. Magnetic Abrasive Polishing

Magnetic abrasive polishing involves placing magnetic abrasive materials in a magnetic field, where the abrasive particles arrange themselves along magnetic force lines to form a magnetic brush. The workpiece is placed between the N-S magnetic poles, maintaining a certain gap between the workpiece and the poles. When the workpiece rotates relative to the magnetic poles, the magnetic abrasive particles polish the workpiece surface. If an ultrasonic vibration device is placed axially on the workpiece, each point on the workpiece will vibrate longitudinally at 18000-25000Hz, producing an excellent ultrasonic-magnetic composite polishing effect. Let magnetic abrasive particle A be a particle close to the workpiece surface. Under the influence of the magnetic field, point A will generate a force fx pressing against the workpiece along the magnetic force line direction. Due to workpiece rotation, a tangential cutting reaction force fy is applied to point A by the workpiece surface. Also, because the magnetic field of the magnetic pole is non-uniform, point A also experiences a magnetic force Fm in the tangential direction due to the gradient change in magnetic field strength. This force is opposite to the fy direction and can prevent the magnetic field force on abrasive particle A (the resultant of fx and Fm) from being greater than the cutting reaction force fy. At this time, magnetic abrasive particle A is in a normal cutting state. When the magnetic field force on particle A is less than the cutting reaction force fy, particle A will slide or roll. The magnitude of the magnetic force is proportional to the square of the magnetic field strength, and the magnetic field strength increases with increasing DC power supply voltage. Therefore, as long as the

The magnitude of the applied voltage can be adjusted to control the size of the magnetic field strength. Magnetic abrasive finishing is mainly used for surface finishing and deburring of precision parts. The height of burrs should not exceed 0.1 mm, such as bearings, bearing bushes, oil pump gears, valve body cavities, and polishing and deburring after precision coupling repair. Using this method, the efficiency is high, the quality is good, and the chamfer of the edges can be controlled below 0.01 mm. For example, when using magnetic abrasive finishing to polish cylindrical stepped parts, this method can remove burrs with a height of 20-30 μm on the edges within a few minutes, and the radius of the rounded edges after grinding is 0.01 mm. This is something that cannot be achieved or is very difficult to achieve by other methods.
6.7 Hydraulic Cylinder and Its Parts Remanufacturing Quality Inspection Method
6.7.1 Quality Inspection Method for Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Parts Before Remanufacturing
According to the provisions of GB/T28619-2012, hydraulic cylinders and their parts before remanufacturing can be called remanufacturing blanks.

The purpose of quality inspection of hydraulic cylinders and their parts before remanufacturing is to make a remanufacturing evaluation of the remanufacturing blanks based on the results of appearance quality, internal defect, and special performance inspection of the remanufacturing blanks. Remanufacturing enterprises with conditions can conduct residual life assessment. Based on the designed life of the blanks in the manufacturing stage, fault statistics and failure analysis results in the service stage, using non-destructive testing technology, determine the life degradation law and degradation rate of remanufacturing blanks, extract characteristic parameters representing the damage degree of remanufacturing blanks, and evaluate the damage degree of remanufacturing blanks.

For remanufacturing blanks where cracks are not allowed to exist, find the potential dangerous parts of the remanufacturing blanks, select the early damage detection methods in Table 6-23, diagnose the degree of early damage based on the characteristic signal change law in the life degradation process of non-destructive testing, and predict the remaining life.
1. General Provisions

items: 1) The remanufacturing blanks and remanufacturing mode should comply with the definitions specified in GB/T28619-2012.

2) The quality inspection of remanufacturing blanks includes the inspection methods for the appearance quality, internal defects, and special performance of remanufacturing blanks. The appearance quality of remanufacturing blanks refers to the ability of the blank's appearance to meet the requirements of remanufacturing; internal defects refer to unreasonable or unsafe deficiencies existing inside the remanufacturing blanks; the inspection of special performance of remanufacturing blanks refers to the relevant performance related to environmental protection and electrical safety.
3) The technical requirements of the selected inspection method should be met before the quality inspection of remanufacturing blanks.
4) When inspecting the quality of remanufacturing blanks, a quality inspection specification and operation instruction manual for remanufacturing blanks should be compiled.
5) When inspecting the quality of remanufacturing blanks, non-destructive testing technology should be given priority.

6) The selection of non-destructive testing technology should fully consider factors such as the material, structure, manufacturing process, service conditions, and maturity of non-destructive testing technology of remanufacturing blanks.

sections.text: 2. Appearance Quality Inspection Method for Remanufacturing Blanks

6.7.2 Inspection Methods for Remanufactured Hydraulic Cylinders and Their Parts
According to the provisions of GB/T 28619—2012, remanufactured hydraulic cylinders and their parts can be called remanufactured products.

Inspection is divided into component inspection and assembly inspection; according to inspection items, it can be classified into mechanical processing inspection, surface repair layer inspection, assembly inspection, performance inspection, coating inspection, and packaging inspection.
1. General Provisions

items: Products of the same type and same model produced using the same remanufacturing process belong to the same inspection batch. The sampling quantity for the same inspection batch of remanufactured products should be at least 10% higher than that for sampling of original new products. For products with single batch quantity less than 10 pieces, inspection should be conducted at a ratio of not less than 50%. Other requirements should follow the provisions of GB/T 2828.1.

Before inspection, clear inspection procedures should be formulated. Appropriate selection should be made for measuring equipment, testing equipment, instruments, gauges, and special tools required for inspection to meet inspection requirements.
During inspection, clear requirements should be proposed for the controlled inspection environment, especially for precision measurements sensitive to environmental factors.
The inspection process should be protected as required to prevent injuries that may be caused by high-pressure and/or high-temperature hydraulic oil splashing or spraying during inspection.
Waste generated during the inspection process should be treated in an environmentally harmless manner.

sections.text: 2. Component Inspection
(1) Mechanical Processing Inspection

items: During the processing of remanufactured components, force-bearing parts and important working surfaces should not have defects such as sand holes, scratches, bruises, and rust spots that reduce component strength, lifespan, or affect appearance.
The heat treatment of the processed surface of components should not have oxide scale. The mating surfaces after processing should not require annealing treatment.

Workpieces with residual magnetism caused by processing or inspection should be demagnetized. Burrs on the surface of components (including keyways) should be removed, and sharp edges and corners should be chamfered.

After mechanical processing of the surface repair layer, geometric dimensions, geometric tolerances, and surface quality should be inspected, and they should meet the requirements of drawings and technical specifications.

sections.text: (2) Repair Layer Inspection

items: Coating Layer: ① Use a tensile strength tester to inspect the tensile bond strength and hardness of the coating layer. ② The coating surface should have no cracks, peeling, or flaking, and the surface roughness should meet design requirements.

Brush Plating Layer: ① The brush plating layer can be inspected using a hardness tester. ② After mechanical processing, the plating layer should have no defects such as peeling or flaking that affect usage.
Welding Layer: ① Through fatigue, wear resistance, and other tests, as well as metallographic analysis, determine whether the welding layer meets mechanical performance requirements.

sections.text: ② Through tensile tests, pressure tests (strength inspection), and non-destructive testing, determine whether the tensile bond strength and air tightness meet the repair process requirements.
③ The surface of the welding layer should be uniform, without peeling or delamination. The dimensions and standard quality should meet the repair process requirements.
④ Other Repair Layers. For components with special inspection requirements, they can be executed according to the requirements agreed upon by both parties.
3. Assembly Inspection

items: Before assembling the hydraulic cylinder assembly, each component should be cleaned or washed, and there should be no burrs, flash, oxide scale, rust, chips, sand particles, dust, or oil stains, and they should meet the corresponding cleanliness requirements. Except for special requirements, sharp edges and corners of components should be chamfered before assembly.
For components assembled using repair methods, the main mating dimensions after repair should meet the requirements of drawings and technical specifications.

sections.text: 4. Performance Inspection

According to the quality characteristics and safety performance of remanufactured products, they should not be lower than the relevant provisions of original new products. The inspection methods for hydraulic cylinder assemblies should follow the relevant sections of Chapter 5.
Hydraulic cylinders should undergo type inspection in any of the following situations:

items: For new remanufactured products or old products transferred to a new manufacturer.
Once every three years after formal production.
After being out of production for more than two years and resuming production.
When there is a significant difference between the factory inspection results and the previous type inspection.

items: Before coating, there should be no burrs, oxide scale, sand adhesion, oil stains, or other contaminants.
Special parts should be protected.

6.8 Application Examples of Repairing Cylinder Components Using Several Remanufacturing Technologies

Hydraulic cylinders have various failure modes. Some of them can be repaired through on-site maintenance, such as damage to seals. In addition to reasons such as bumps, scratches, plating layer peeling, and rust, the main reason for hydraulic cylinders becoming scrap is various types of wear, including abrasive wear, corrosive wear, and fatigue wear. For cases caused by overloading or external impacts, etc.

6.8.1 Remanufacturing Repair Examples of Hydraulic Cylinder Body (Barrel)

The remanufacturing of hydraulic cylinder body (barrel) should adopt corresponding remanufacturing technologies according to the detection results, as listed in some specific methods in reference [121]:

items: For rust on the outer wall of the cylinder body (barrel), a comprehensive method of chemical agents and mechanical shot blasting is used for rust removal and residual paint removal.

For wear and scratches on the inner hole of the cylinder body (barrel), scraping and rolling light or honing methods are used, combined with structural adjustment of parts or re-selection of sealing components, to meet the requirements of performance.

For some impact and sealing surface damage, cold welding machine surfacing is used, and then a method combining mechanical processing and manual repair can be adopted to meet the installation and sealing requirements.

sections.text: 1. Application of Honing Technology in Repairing Hydraulic Cylinder Body of Construction Machinery

According to the introduction in reference [122], as one of the core components of construction machinery, hydraulic cylinders have huge consumables, high processing difficulty, but high concentration of hydraulic cylinders, mainly composed of cylinder barrel, piston rod, piston, cylinder head, etc. Hydraulic cylinder remanufacturing uses less equipment, the process is relatively simple, and the added value of hydraulic cylinders is high, so it is very necessary and important to remanufacture construction machinery hydraulic cylinders.
(1) Failure Mode Analysis of Hydraulic Cylinders

The working environment of construction machinery (used) hydraulic cylinders is harsh, leading to the largest number of scrapped hydraulic cylinders. The main failure modes are abrasive wear, fatigue wear, adhesive wear, and deformation.
After disassembling and inspecting 100 hydraulic cylinders, a factory conducted data statistics on the damage forms of their main components, as shown in Table 6-25.

sections.caption: Table 6-25 Statistical Data of Cylinder Parts Detection Results (Unit: pieces)

sections.text: According to the statistical data, the main failure form of hydraulic cylinder barrel is abrasive wear. For this form of surface wear, honing technology is used to repair the size of the barrel for remanufacturing.
(2) Honing Process

The cylinder barrel is an important part of the hydraulic cylinder. Most cylinder barrels are scrapped due to internal particles causing scratches on the inner wall of the barrel, leading to excessive internal leakage, failure to meet the required working pressure and cylinder output force. Therefore, using honing technology to repair scratches on the inner wall of the barrel has become the main method. The honing process of the honing machine can be divided into three steps: rough honing, fine honing, and polishing.

During rough honing, at the initial stage, since there are scratches or peeling on the inner wall of the barrel and the oil stone on the honing head also has edges and burrs, the stroke speed and spindle load should be smaller, and after running smoothly, they should be gradually increased. Observe the change of the pressure gauge reading, and manually correct the taper of the barrel as needed; during fine honing, the spindle speed should be increased by about 10%, and the spindle load should also be increased accordingly, and the short stroke switch should be turned off; during polishing, the spindle speed and spindle load should remain the same as during fine honing. At this time, first turn off the spindle rotation, use the manual button to reduce the honing head, and add a special polishing emery cloth pad under the oil stone to continue honing. This is to improve the surface quality of the inner wall of the barrel. Observe whether the scratches, peeling, and other damage on the inner wall of the barrel have been completely honed to meet the requirements, then clean the cylinder body to remove the residual honing oil inside; after cleaning, apply a layer of protective oil to protect the inner wall of the barrel.
Setting of Honing Parameters:

items: Spindle Speed. Set the correct inner diameter size of the cylinder on the setting screen, and adjust the position of the hand wheel on the spindle box according to the spindle box speed value displayed on the screen. The reasonable spindle speed can be calculated by formula (6-11): ne = 17500/D (6-11). In the formula: ne—the reasonable spindle speed, in r/min; D—the inner diameter of the cylinder, in mm.

Stroke Speed. Press the stroke speed key to set. For a part that has not been honed in the previous process and when the part starts honing, the stroke speed can be set to about 15 m/min; after several strokes, set the stroke speed to the required value. The stroke speed v1 can be set by formula (6-12), i.e.: v1 = πDntan30°/1000 (6-12). In the formula: v1—the stroke speed, in m/min; D—the inner diameter of the cylinder, in mm; n—the spindle speed.

2. Experiment and Application of Cold Welding Technology in Hydraulic Support Bottom Cylinder Repair and Remanufacturing

According to the introduction in reference [123], cold welding technology is a new cold arc welding process that has emerged in recent years, which is a major improvement on the traditional melting pole gas shielded welding process. This technology uses advanced electronic technology to control the welding current waveform and voltage, and cooperates with the short-circuit transition of the molten droplet, thereby realizing the control of welding heat input. It can not only greatly reduce welding heat input, reduce the dilution rate of the cladding layer, but also improve the quality of the cladding layer.

Cold welding technology has the following main characteristics:
1) Low welding heat input. During cold welding, its heat input is only 1/3 of that of traditional melting pole gas shielded welding, or even lower. Therefore, the heat affected zone is small and the workpiece deformation is small.
2) Low dilution rate of the cladding layer. The dilution rate of the cladding layer after cold welding is less than 2%, which is comparable to laser cladding, and a cladding layer with higher quality and performance can be obtained.
3) Wide range of applicable welding materials and base materials. Cold welding equipment can basically be used for all carbon steel, stainless steel, Al, Cu, Ni and other types of flux-cored, solid wire and base materials on the market.

4) Less spatter. During cold welding, there is very little spatter, which can basically achieve spatter-free welding.
(1) Test Materials and Equipment
The test selected a hydraulic support bottom cylinder with a specification of φ530mm, and the test equipment selected the IG cold welding equipment produced by Henan Coal Science and Technology Institute Wear-resistant Technology Co., Ltd. The welding material directly affects the structure and performance of the cladding layer after cold welding. The welding material used in this test is aluminum bronze wire, and its main components are shown in Table 6-27.
(2) Cold Welding Process of Inner Wall of Hydraulic Support Bottom Cylinder
The main process flow of cold welding of the inner wall of the hydraulic support bottom cylinder is shown in Figure 6-6.

1) Cleaning before cold welding. In order to ensure the quality of the repair of the inner wall of the hydraulic support bottom cylinder, the generation of welding defects during cold welding should be minimized as much as possible. Therefore, before cold welding, the inner wall of the hydraulic support bottom cylinder to be welded must be thoroughly cleaned (such as high-pressure washing, ethanol wiping, etc.) to remove impurities such as oil stains and rust spots on the inner wall surface.
2) Cold welding process. According to the production experience of cold welding repair of the inner wall of the hydraulic support bottom cylinder, the main welding parameters for cold welding are shown in Table 6-28.

sections.caption: Table 6-27 Main Components of Test Welding Materials
Figure 6-6 Main Process Flow of Cold Welding of Inner Wall of Hydraulic Support Bottom Cylinder
sections.description: Process flow diagram showing the following steps in sequence: Feed/Inspection → Dimensional Inspection → Special Inner Wall Cleaning → Cold Welding → (branches to) Quality Inspection, Packaging, Inner Wall Mechanical Processing, Defect Repair, Weld Layer Quality Inspection

sections.text: Compared with traditional welding processes, cold welding produces minimal spatter, thereby reducing the formation of welding defects and improving welding quality. After cold welding, the cladding layer on the inner wall has a smooth and uniform appearance with no obvious welding defects. Measurements show that the single-sided thickness of the cladding layer after cold welding is approximately 3 mm, with a height difference of less than 0.5 mm, with values primarily depending on the welding parameters during cold welding.

To ensure the performance requirements of the hydraulic support base cylinder after repair, quality inspection of the cladding layer must be conducted before mechanical processing. After identifying and repairing defects, subsequent mechanical processing can proceed.

3) Mechanical processing of the inner wall. After the welded cylinder is completely cooled to room temperature, a deep-hole boring machine is used for boring. After rough boring and finish boring, a machining allowance of 0.5 mm is retained for the inner diameter of the cylinder. After boring is completed, a honing machine is used to hone the inner wall to the required dimensions. The surface roughness value of the finished inner wall does not exceed Ra0.4μm. After passing inspection, the repair of the hydraulic support base cylinder inner wall can be realized.
(3) Analysis of the application effects of cold welding technology

To test the application effects of cold welding repair on the inner wall of the hydraulic support base cylinder, wear testing and salt spray corrosion testing were conducted. Due to the difficulty of sampling from the hydraulic support base cylinder, steel plates of the same material as the hydraulic support base cylinder were selected for testing. Using the same welding material and cold welding parameters, cladding was performed on the steel plates. Standard samples were taken according to test requirements for testing, with their relative wear resistance and relative corrosion resistance shown in Figure 6-7.

sections.caption: Figure 6-7 Relative Wear Resistance and Relative Corrosion Resistance
sections.description: A bar chart showing comparison of wear resistance and corrosion resistance. The chart has a vertical axis labeled with values 0-7 and horizontal axis showing four categories: Base Material, Cladding Layer, Base Material, and Relative Corrosion Resistance. The cladding layer shows the highest value at approximately 6, while base materials show lower values around 1-2.

sections.text: As can be seen from Figure 6-7, the application effects of cold welding technology are significant. After repair using cold welding technology, the wear resistance and corrosion resistance of the inner wall of the hydraulic support base cylinder have been improved to varying degrees. Compared to the base material, the relative wear resistance of the cladding layer is approximately 1.8 times, and the relative corrosion resistance is approximately 6.2 times, significantly enhancing the performance of the surface cladding layer. The improved wear resistance makes the inner wall of the hydraulic support base cylinder less susceptible to wear during operation, and the significantly improved corrosion resistance extends the service life of the hydraulic support base cylinder. Additionally, according to the performance requirements of the hydraulic support base cylinder, different welding materials can be used to achieve cladding layers with different properties, obtaining various strengthening effects.
3. Application of Surface Adhesive Coating Technology in Repairing Large Hydraulic Cylinder Bodies

According to the introduction in reference [60], a 500t hydraulic press at a certain factory had a large hydraulic cylinder body with scratches and bulging on the inner wall, with the following specific conditions:

items: The length of scratches on the upper part of the cylinder inner wall is 450 mm.
The length of bulging on the lower part of the cylinder body is 350 mm, with the bulged size being φ502+0.021 mm (the original cylinder inner diameter was φ500+0.155 mm).

items: AK02-3 self-lubricating wear-resistant repair agent was applied to the scratched and bulged areas of the cylinder body after surface pretreatment and roughening, leaving machining allowance.
Curing was carried out using infrared heating.
Grinding tools with dimensions close to the cylinder inner diameter were used for machining to meet dimensional requirements and cylindricity and straightness requirements.

6.8.2 Repair Examples of Hydraulic Cylinder Piston Rod Remanufacturing
Hydraulic cylinder piston rod remanufacturing should use corresponding remanufacturing technologies according to inspection results, as some specific methods listed in reference [121]:

items: For piston rod surface plating layer peeling, local (minor) rust, bumps, and scratches, use a special stripping process to strip the hard chrome plating layer, repair local damage, and then re-chrome plate.

For cases where the piston rod diameter must be reduced, such as large-area rust, adjust the piston rod diameter by a certain amount, customize corresponding seals and end caps; simultaneously perform heat treatment strengthening on the piston rod to improve its mechanical strength and reduce remanufacturing costs.

For piston rods with severe surface bumps and scratches, use a cold welder for local welding to repair defects; plasma laser quenching can also be used to change the dimensions of the piston rod body, then overall reprocessing. Plasma laser quenching can also improve the mechanical properties of components and extend service life.

sections.text: For piston rods with severe surface damage or those requiring improved quality characteristics, advanced remanufacturing technologies such as plasma spraying and laser cladding should be used.
