1. Application of Laser Cladding Remanufacturing Technology for Columns and Jacks of Hydraulic Supports in Coal Mines

The laser cladding remanufacturing technology for columns and jacks of hydraulic supports in coal mines is a remanufacturing technology that uses laser cladding of stainless steel powder to restore the quality characteristics of columns and jacks that have failed due to internal leakage, peeling of the chrome plating layer, severe scratches, etc., to a level equal to or better than that of new products.

According to reference [124], the service life of columns repaired by electroplating and remanufactured by laser cladding under the same working conditions in the same coal mine is as follows: the service life of columns repaired by electroplating is 1 to 1.5 years; after 4.5 years of use, columns remanufactured by laser cladding do not show problems such as rusting and decreased sealing performance. According to the results of simulated tests, the actual service life of columns remanufactured by laser cladding should be 6 times that of columns repaired by electroplating.

According to the provisions of DB37/T1932-2011, columns and jacks should undergo thorough cleaning, degreasing, etc., and defect evaluation to determine whether they are suitable for remanufacturing. If any of the following conditions occur, they should be judged as unsuitable for remanufacturing:

items: a) The axial scratch depth on the sealing mating surface of the middle cylinder body and small column is greater than 2 mm.
b) The radial scratch depth on the sealing mating surface of the middle cylinder body and small column is greater than 2 mm.
c) There are cracks in the cylinder body, and the threads, annular grooves, or other connecting parts at the end of the cylinder body are incomplete.
d) The linearity error of the inner hole of the cylinder body is greater than 0.05%; the roundness and cylindricity errors are greater than 0.2% of the nominal size.
e) The linearity error of the live column is greater than 0.1%.

sections.text: For part evaluation, please refer to standards such as DB37/T2688.2-2015.
DB37/T1932-2011 also stipulates the requirements for main parts before cladding and the requirements for laser-clad stainless steel remanufactured columns.
Requirements for main parts before cladding:
a) The welds of the outer cylinder body, middle cylinder body, and piston rod should be subjected to ultrasonic testing according to the requirements of GB/T6402 and GB/T5777.

b) Check the damage, dimensions, and linearity of the outer cylinder body and middle cylinder body. If necessary, use laser cladding or electroplating technology to repair the inner hole to meet the technical requirements.
Requirements for laser-clad stainless steel remanufactured columns:
a) The thickness of the laser cladding layer should not be less than 0.5 mm.
b) After laser cladding, the surface hardness should not be lower than 40 HRC. After rolling treatment, it should not be lower than 42 HRC.
c) The cladding layer should be uniform and firm, without peeling, falling off, or blistering. There should be no burning, cracks, or dense pitting and other appearance defects.
(1) Application of Laser Cladding Technology in Hydraulic Supports of Coal Mines

1) Necessity of Laser Cladding for Hydraulic Support Columns. According to reference [125], the Shanxi Fenxi Mining Group uses electroplating technology for the overhaul of hydraulic supports and the repair of various jacks. According to environmental protection requirements, the number of hard chrome plating manufacturers is decreasing year by year, while the price of hard chrome plating is increasing, becoming a bottleneck in the repair of hydraulic support columns and jacks. Moreover, the quality of hard chrome plating is difficult to meet the requirements of coal mine users, especially in mines with corrosive gases or liquids, where H₂S corrosion has the greatest impact on hard chrome plating layers.

The service life of laser cladding layers is more than 5 times that of hard chrome plating layers. At present, most high-end hydraulic support remanufacturing in China adopts laser cladding. After laser cladding, the next overhaul of the column is particularly simple. Because when the column with hard chrome plating has a rust spot or scratch, during overhaul, the hard chrome plating layer must go through the complex process of complete stripping, repair, and re-hard chrome plating, which is time-consuming, laborious, and cumbersome, and pollutes the environment. For columns that have undergone laser cladding, during the next support overhaul, under the premise of ensuring sealing, most columns do not need to be disassembled and processed. Individual damaged areas only need micro-processing (repairing the damaged points by argon arc welding, then polishing and polishing with oilstone), which is inexpensive, time-saving, labor-saving, and environmentally friendly.

2) Comparison of Electroplating Layer and Laser Cladding Layer Performance of Columns. Electroplating is a surface treatment technology that uses an electrolytic process to deposit chromium on the substrate surface to form a chromium plating layer. The bonding between the plating layer and the substrate is chemical bonding, with weak bonding force, which is prone to blistering, cracking, and falling off. The electroplating process of columns and jacks generally adopts composite plating layer technology of copper-tin alloy plus hard chromium. The thickness of the electroplating layer is generally 0.05 to 0.06 mm. The chrome plating layer has high brittleness. When it is locally subjected to compression or impact, the plating layer is prone to cracks, and moisture in humid air will seep through the gaps to the substrate surface to form rust spots. With the passage of time, the spots continue to expand and increase, and connect into large areas. In severe cases, it will cause the support to fail.

Taking the laser cladding of high mining height column middle cylinder as an example, laser cladding technology uses a high-power laser beam to gather extremely high energy to instantly melt the surface of the workpiece to be processed. At the same time, the alloy powder pre-placed on the surface of the part is completely melted to obtain a dense cladding layer with metallurgical bonding with the substrate. After finishing, the single-sided thickness of the cladding layer is maintained at 0.50 to 0.60 mm, which is 8 to 10 times that of the electroplating layer, and it has a firm metallurgical bond with the substrate. Due to the concentrated and dense characteristics of the laser beam energy, most of the light energy is used for melting the powder, only slightly melting the substrate surface, and the heat-affected zone of the substrate is extremely small, generally 0.1 to 0.2 mm, effectively ensuring that the performance and shape of the base material do not change.

There are two types of mechanical processing technology after cladding: one is rough turning → fine turning → polishing; the other is rough turning → grinding → polishing. After fine turning, the surface roughness value after polishing by a special polishing machine can reach Ra0.4 μm or below.
3) Economic Analysis. According to research and calculation, the cost of using laser cladding technology is 3189.5 yuan/m², and the cost of using electroplating technology is 1450

yuan/m². The electroplating process requires removing the chrome plating and re-plating with chrome during each major overhaul, while the laser cladding process only requires repair during major overhaul, so the subsequent maintenance cost of the laser cladding process is significantly reduced. From a comprehensive benefit perspective, the laser cladding process is superior to the electroplating process and effectively solves the bottleneck problems in the electroplating process during bracket overhaul and jack repair.
(2) Application of stainless steel cladding remanufacturing technology in repairing hydraulic cylinder piston rods

According to the introduction in reference [126], investigations have shown that due to the long-term use of comprehensive support in harsh underground natural environments, under high load conditions, the hydraulic cylinder piston rod extends about 2/3 out of the hydraulic cylinder during operation, making it prone to corrosion and bending. This results in poor dust seal performance, creating a vicious cycle that brings dust and impurities into the hydraulic cylinder along with the extension and retraction of the piston rod. At the same time, due to most being used beyond their service life, pits appear on the rod surface. When the hydraulic cylinder piston rod extends, the seal ring at the pit position will cause seal failure, and the hydraulic cylinder cannot maintain pressure. For the above situations, methods such as re-copper plating or spraying wear-resistant plastic powder on the rod surface can be used. However, if the clearance exceeds the tolerance too much, copper plating cannot solve this problem, while spraying processes are often affected by various factors, causing the sprayed layer to easily fall off, and the hardness and impact resistance of the plastic powder are also poor. Through research, using stainless steel cladding technology for piston rod remanufacturing repair can increase surface hardness, reduce surface roughness values, and improve wear resistance and corrosion resistance, thereby improving the overall service life of the hydraulic cylinder. Therefore, using stainless steel cladding technology for remanufacturing repair of comprehensive support hydraulic cylinder piston rods can achieve good economic benefits.

Hydraulic cylinder piston rod stainless steel powder cladding repair is a technology that uses high-energy laser beam scanning to melt the stainless steel powder in the scanned area to achieve surface hardening. Its basic principle is to use a laser with a certain energy density (10³-10⁵ W/cm²) to irradiate the hydraulic cylinder piston rod, rapidly heating the worn surface layer area to above the phase transition point; below the melting point, the temperature at this time causes the stainless steel powder coated on the workpiece surface to reach the melting point and start melting, while the workpiece substrate remains in a cold state, with a large temperature gradient between the heating area and the substrate; when the laser beam stops irradiating, due to the effect of heat conduction, the heating area will rapidly cool (10⁶-10⁸ °C/s) and undergo stainless steel powder solution cooling, melting the stainless steel powder onto the metal hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface, achieving repair of the workpiece surface layer.
Using stainless steel cladding remanufacturing technology to repair hydraulic cylinder piston rods has the following characteristics:

items: 1) The laser beam provides rapid heating and self-cooling, without the need for insulation and cooling liquid cooling, making it a non-polluting green heat treatment process that can easily achieve cladding repair of the hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface.

2) Due to the fast laser heating speed, small heat-affected zone, and surface scanning heating, i.e., instantaneous local heating, the deformation of the repaired hydraulic cylinder piston rod is very small.
3) Due to the very small laser scattering angle and good directionality, it can accurately perform local melting repair on the hydraulic cylinder piston rod surface through a light guide system.

sections.text: 4) The cladding layer thickness of laser surface cladding is generally 0.7-1.5 mm. This repair technology can repair hydraulic cylinder piston rods with surface scratch and wear depths exceeding 1.5 mm.

In summary, using stainless steel powder cladding technology to repair various mining comprehensive support hydraulic cylinder piston rods is both economically and technically feasible. Multiple batches of experiments have been completed in Xinxin Mining Group with good results.
2. Application of high-frequency welding and brush plating remanufacturing technology in repairing the piston rod of the slewing hydraulic cylinder on ship-mounted pile driving machines

According to the introduction in reference [60], high-frequency welding multi-metal defect repair is a technology that uses a high-frequency welding multi-metal defect repair machine (referred to as the multi-metal defect repair machine, which is a patented product of Beijing Aoyukexin Group) to repair defects on the surface of various metal component surfaces (such as pores and sand holes in castings, peeling and wear marks generated during the use of different metal components). The working principle of the multi-metal defect repair machine is that when the equipment is working, it can charge the capacitor in a cycle of 10⁻³-10⁻¹s, and in an ultra-short time of 10⁻⁶-10⁻⁵s, high-frequency discharge can be performed. Using various metal filler materials as electrodes of the repair machine, when they contact the defect part of the metal substrate to be repaired, the high-frequency discharge voltage will break down the gas to form plasma, thereby generating electric sparks with temperatures above 6000°C, instantly melting the electrode (metal filler material) and the contact part (position) with the metal material of the substrate to be repaired, and then transitioning to the surface layer of the part to be repaired. Since an alloying effect is generated between the filler material and the substrate, it diffuses and infiltrates into the interior of the part to be repaired, forming a diffusion layer, obtaining a high-strength metallurgical bond.

Since during the welding process, the time between each discharge and the next discharge is extremely short, the repair machine has enough relative stopping time, so the heat will quickly diffuse to the outside through the substrate, and the repaired part of the substrate will not accumulate heat. Although the temperature rise of the substrate is almost maintained at room temperature, due to the instantaneous melting, the temperature of the electrode filler material can reach about 1000°C.

A certain shipping engineering bureau's pile driving ship's mast slewing is driven by a large slewing hydraulic cylinder. Due to the frequent operation of the slewing hydraulic cylinder, heavy loads, and severe corrosion during offshore operations, as well as flying sand and stones on the construction site shore and harsh environment, the chrome plating layer on the piston rod surface peels off and scratches, the piston rod seal is damaged, and oil leakage occurs.
According to the above situation, the slewing hydraulic cylinder of this pile driving ship has the following problems that need to be solved during repair:
1) Oil leakage from the hydraulic oil seal of the piston rod at the upper end cover.

2) Peeling and scratching of the chrome plating layer on the piston rod surface.
3) Local spot corrosion and scratching on the inner surface of the cylinder liner.
After research, it was decided to use a repair scheme combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating.
(1) Disassembly and decomposition of the hydraulic cylinder

1) Overall disassembly of the hydraulic cylinder. This ship-mounted pile driver's variable amplitude hydraulic cylinder has a maximum outer diameter of 1.27 m, a total length of 11.66 m, and a net weight of about 28 t. Among these, the piston rod, piston, and piston rod hinge head weigh 12 t, the upper end cover weighs 1.0 t, the bottom end cover weighs 3.0 t, and the cylinder barrel weighs 12 t. Before disassembling the hydraulic cylinder, the piston rod must be retracted to the limit position, the hoses removed, and the joints sealed. Use lifting equipment to lift the hydraulic cylinder, remove the hinge pin, then load the hydraulic cylinder onto a truck, transport it, and bring it into the factory.
2) Decomposition of the hydraulic cylinder. Remove the vent screw, take out the steel ball, connect a prepared pipe joint to the vent hole, connect the pipe, and inject compressed air into the lower cylinder (pressure is 0.6-0.8 MPa). Discharge the hydraulic oil in the upper cylinder into a clean oil drum (20 empty oil drums should be prepared). Place a prepared support trolley (or use sleepers) under the piston rod, and use compressed air to push out the piston and piston rod assembly (stroke is 8.25 m), trying to move the piston to the limit position to drain as much hydraulic oil as possible from the hydraulic cylinder; at the same time, during this process, ensure the concentricity of the cylinder barrel with the piston and piston rod.
a) Remove the upper end cover. Use a trolley to support the bottom of the upper end cover, clean the screws on the upper end cover and its surroundings, and use a special wrench to remove the screws. Weld two top rod nuts symmetrically on the end cover, and use threaded top rods to push out the upper end cover.
b) Remove the bottom end cover. Clean the screws on the bottom end cover and its surroundings, and use a special wrench to remove the screws.
c) Pull out the piston and piston rod. When the piston is about to be pulled out, the trolley should move closer to the piston.
Because this time a repair process combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating was adopted, the piston and piston rod do not need to be further decomposed, which reduces the amount of disassembly work and difficulty.
(2) Inspection of the hydraulic cylinder

items: Clean the cylinder barrel (inner wall), piston, and piston rod, etc. with light diesel, using tools such as silk cloth.
Check and measure the dimensions and tolerances of each mating surface, as well as the straightness, roundness, and cylindricity of the cylinder barrel, piston rod, etc.

Check whether there is eccentric wear on the guide sleeve of the upper end cover.
After inspection, the results are as follows:
a) The piston rod is severely worn and rusted. The original chrome plating layer on the surface is worn and rusted for a length of 4.6 m, with a depth of 1.0 mm.
b) The wear on the inner wall of the cylinder barrel has expanded from the original three scratch grooves to a wear surface with a width of 300-500 mm, a length of 5.1 m, and a depth of 1.0 mm.
c) The guide sleeve of the upper end cover is severely worn, and the V-shaped seal ring is severely deformed.

sections.text: (3) Repair of the piston rod

1) Repair requirements. Achieve the purposes of wear resistance and corrosion resistance, with a hardness above 55 HRC and a surface roughness value not higher than Ra0.2μm.
2) Process flow. Use a repair process combining high-frequency fusion welding and brush plating. The process flow is: trimming and grinding the base surface → cleaning and washing → high-frequency fusion welding → trimming and grinding the high-frequency fusion welding surface → brush plating → restoring the dimensions of the worn and corroded surfaces → mechanical polishing of the repaired surfaces.
3) Repair process.
① Cleaning and determining the repair reference. Hang the piston rod to be repaired onto a walking trolley (the distance between trolleys should not be less than 5 m). Since it has not been decomposed from the piston, pay attention to protecting the seals on the piston. Use a cleaning agent to clean the oil stains on the surface of the piston rod, then use an external diameter vernier caliper to measure the dimensions of the reference surface (measure the unworn surface of the lower end of the piston rod near the piston), and use this surface dimension as the reference for repair.
② Grinding of the surface to be repaired. Use a grinding machine to grind off the remaining chrome plating layer on the worn and corroded surface. For the worn surface, where the wear is more severe, first use a grinding machine for rough grinding, then use a grinding machine for grinding. For areas with deep corrosion, first use an angle grinder for grinding, then use a high-frequency fusion welding repair machine to weld the corroded areas flat, and then use a special grinding tool to grind (polish) the welded areas flat.
③ Use brush plating technology to brush plate the surface to be repaired. Use reverse pulse brush plating to brush plate the surface to be repaired. The process is as follows: electrolytic cleaning → activation with activating solution No. 1 → activation with activating solution No. 2 → activation with activating solution No. 3 → activation with activating solution No. 4 → activation with activating solution No. 5 → activation with activating solution No. 6 → activation with chrome surface activating solution → special nickel → nickel-chromium alloy. For areas with more corrosion or pitting, activation with copper activating solution can be used.

During the brush plating process, the quality of the brush plating layer is determined by the controlled temperature and current, as well as the technical level of the operator. Especially for the brush plating of transition surfaces, whether two materials can be well contacted, and the dimensional control of the transition surfaces, etc. are difficult points. During the brush plating process, using the stress-relief interlayer process can ensure that the brush plating layer has no cracks, no pitting, etc.

④ Mechanical polishing and inspection. The thickness of the brush plating layer should leave a certain amount of allowance for polishing and machining. After brush plating, mechanical polishing should be performed. On the 4600 mm long repaired surface of the piston rod, 17 inspection points were selected at equal distances to inspect the dimensional deviation of the piston rod diameter ф370. The inspection results are shown in Table 6-29. After inspection, the outer diameter dimensions of the repaired surface of the piston rod are controlled within the range of ф(370 ± 0.01) mm, achieving the predetermined reference dimensions and meeting the requirements of the new product; there are no repair marks, cracks, pitting, or peeling on the repaired piston rod surface, and the surface roughness meets the requirements; the hardness is tested with a hardness tester, and the value is above 55 HRC.

sections.text: (4) Assembly and Debugging of Hydraulic Cylinder
The assembly sequence of the hydraulic cylinder is exactly the opposite of the disassembly sequence and should be carried out according to the new product assembly technical requirements.

When this hydraulic cylinder drives the pile frame to swing from 30° forward to 30° backward, it should be completed within 18-20 minutes. The maximum working pressure of the hydraulic cylinder is 14 MPa.
1) No-load Test

The no-load test is conducted according to the new product test method, but attention should be paid to checking the oil level in the tank. If new hydraulic oil needs to be added, it must be filtered before being added. Air exhausting from both chambers of the hydraulic cylinder is necessary, but care should be taken to prevent spraying and environmental pollution. If too much air is mixed into the hydraulic oil in the tank, sufficient settling time should be left for the hydraulic oil in the tank to exhaust air by itself.
During the no-load test, check whether there is external leakage in the hydraulic cylinder and pipelines.
2) Load Test
Connect the piston rod head of the hydraulic cylinder to the pile frame and check the air exhausting condition again through the air release valve.

Control the hydraulic cylinder to drive the pile frame to swing from 30° forward to 30° backward. Specifically, perform the operations in the sequence of 0°→30° forward→0°→30° backward→0°, and check whether there is external leakage in the hydraulic cylinder and pipelines. Record the working pressure of the hydraulic cylinder and the time of swinging in each stage.
Keep the pile frame at 15° forward for 2 hours and observe whether the pile frame moves on its own.
After the test, this hydraulic cylinder has neither external nor internal leakage.
Note: It should be expressed as "The internal and external leakage of this hydraulic cylinder is not out of specification."

7.1.2 Cleanliness indicators required for hydraulic systems and components

The cleanliness indicators for hydraulic systems and their components should follow the regulations in the corresponding product standards. For main hydraulic components and accessories not specified in product standards, the cleanliness indicators should follow the regulations in JB/T 7858-2006 "Hydraulic Component Cleanliness Evaluation Method and Cleanliness Indicators for Hydraulic Components". The contamination level of hydraulic oil (expressed according to GB/T 14039) should be suitable for hydraulic system control elements such as high reliability or the most sensitive components in the hydraulic system, such as proportional valves, servo valves, proportional/servo controlled hydraulic cylinders, etc. However, the cleanliness or contamination level requirements for some hydraulic systems are classified according to system (working) pressure.

Cleanliness is a quantitative indicator that corresponds to contamination and measures the cleanliness level of a hydraulic system or component. The quantitative term commonly used to describe the degree of oil contamination - contamination level - refers to the content of contaminants related to a controlled environment. In forging machinery hydraulic systems, the JB/T 9954-1999 standard specifies that the cleanliness of a hydraulic system is expressed using two codes in fractional form. The first code represents the total number of particles larger than 5μm per milliliter of oil (in the numerator position), and the second code represents the total number of particles larger than 15μm per milliliter of oil (in the denominator position). For example: 18/15.

The cleanliness of forging machinery hydraulic systems is classified according to the working pressure of the system. The cleanliness of heavy machinery hydraulic systems should comply with the provisions in Table 7-10. 7.1.3 Flushing and Filtering of Pipelines and Working Medium in Hydraulic System

The initial cleanliness level of hydraulic system will affect the performance and service life of hydraulic system. If the solid particle pollutants generated during the assembly and manufacturing process of hydraulic system are not removed, the solid particle pollutants will circulate in the hydraulic system and damage the components of hydraulic system. In order to reduce the probability of such damage, the hydraulic oil and the inner surface of hydraulic system need to be filtered and flushed to reach the specified cleanliness level.

Flushing the pipelines of hydraulic system is a method to remove the solid particle pollutants inside the hydraulic system, but it is not the only method. The flushing and filtering of pipelines and working medium in hydraulic system should be carried out according to the following methods.
1. Preparation
1) From the perspective of pipeline flushing of hydraulic system, the following inspections should be done on hydraulic system and components:

items: Whether the most pollution sensitive components in hydraulic system, such as proportional valves and servo valves, have been removed and replaced by flushing plates or other valves.
Whether there are blind ends that cannot be flushed in the design of hydraulic system.
Whether there are parallel connected pipelines in the design of hydraulic system, and it is impossible to make each pipeline have sufficient flow.
Whether there are flow limiting components or internal filters in the hydraulic system.
Whether there are components that are vulnerable to damage by high flow rate or solid particle pollutants in the hydraulic system.
Whether all pipelines in the hydraulic system can be connected to each other for flushing.

sections.text: The problem of pipeline flushing in hydraulic system should be fully considered at the design stage, otherwise, changing the hydraulic circuit or removing some components for flushing will cause trouble or adverse consequences to pipeline flushing. However, bypassing or isolating some components is a conventional practice during pipeline flushing.
2) In order to enable the pipeline flushing of hydraulic system to reach the specified cleanliness level, the following influencing factors also need to be considered:

items: The components, pipes and oil tank in the hydraulic system must be cleaned and comply with the cleanliness index specified in the relevant standards.
The initial cleanliness of the hydraulic oil in the oil tank or newly injected should comply with the requirements of hydraulic pump.
If the hydraulic system is designed with an independent cooling and filtering system, it is necessary to make it run for a sufficient long time first.
It is necessary to design a proper flushing program.
It is necessary to establish a turbulent state in the pipeline.
Select a filter with a suitable filtering ratio to ensure that the specified cleanliness level can be reached within the allowed time period.
Both parties should confirm the relevant standards (or methods) for extracting oil samples and the standards based on which the oil sample inspection is carried out before pipeline flushing.

sections.text: Inspection report on oil sample issued by qualified inspection unit is one of the necessary technical documents provided by Party B to Party A, so it is also necessary for both parties to determine the inspection unit before pipeline flushing.
2. Pipeline Flushing

items: Establish special files for the pipelines to be flushed and record their achieved cleanliness levels.

The flushing method should be adapted to the actual conditions. However, in order to obtain satisfactory flushing results, the following main criteria should be met before flushing: ① The initial cleanliness of the hydraulic oil in the oil tank should meet the requirements of the hydraulic pump and be comparable to the cleanliness level specified in the hydraulic system. ② Do not introduce air into the hydraulic system. If necessary, the hydraulic oil can be filled to overflow state (design upper limit), or necessary air separation measures can be taken, such as heating and degassing. ③ If a flushing filter is installed on the hydraulic system, it should be installed on the return pipeline and close to the return port. ④ A coarse filter can also be installed at the suction port of the hydraulic pump. ⑤ The installed flow and temperature measuring devices should be as close as possible to the return port.

sections.text: The filtering characteristics of the flushing filter should be selected according to the cleanliness level required by the hydraulic system, for example, the allowable cleanliness level (ACL) of the hydraulic system. ACL represents an acceptable contamination level, and ACL should be coordinated with the contamination level that the most sensitive hydraulic component (such as proportional valve, servo valve) can accept and the allowable service life of the filter. If ACL is not specified, the classification specified in ISO 4406 can be used as a guide for selecting filter accuracy, as shown in Table 7-14.

7.1.4 Detection and Maintenance of Hydraulic System Working Medium

Detection and maintenance of the working medium of the hydraulic system are to ensure that the cleanliness level of the hydraulic oil required by the hydraulic system and components (hydraulic cylinder) is not inferior to the specified value and to extend the service life of the working medium.

Contaminants in hydraulic systems and components, especially solid particle contaminants, are the most common and harmful type of contaminants in hydraulic systems. They may be contaminants originally present (or remaining) in the hydraulic system and components (including piping), or contaminants that invade from the outside or are generated internally.
Contaminants that invade from the outside may be generated and invade the system as follows:

items: Inappropriate cleaning, installation, or maintenance allows solid particles, fibers, seal fragments, and other contaminants to invade the system.
Dust in the air invades the system through a tank with poor sealing or an air filter with low precision.
The hydraulic oil is contaminated during storage and transportation, or unqualified hydraulic oil is added to the system without fine filtration.
Dust is sucked in from the air when adding hydraulic oil in an open manner.

sections.text: It should be emphasized that inappropriate cleaning of hydraulic components and piping during the manufacturing process of hydraulic systems may be a major source of contaminant invasion into the system. Inappropriate cleaning means that on the one hand, contaminants such as chips and sand particles that should be removed by cleaning are not removed from the hydraulic components and piping; on the other hand, new contaminants such as fabric fibers and dust are allowed to invade the hydraulic components and piping during cleaning.
Internal self-generated contaminants may be generated as follows:

items: Metal particles generated by normal mechanical wear of friction pairs of pumps, cylinders, and valves, or rubber particles generated by seal wear.
Debris from hoses or filter elements falling off.
Degradation products of the oil.

sections.text: The types of these contaminant substances are generally as follows:

items: Particulate contaminants: rust, metal shavings, weld slag, sand, dust, etc.
Fiber contaminants: fibers, cotton yarn, seal tape pieces, paint coating layers, etc.
Chemical contaminants: hydraulic oil degradation caused by oxidation of the hydraulic oil or residual cleaning solvents and their products such as gels and sludge.
Water or air: water is brought in from the oil tank or the piston rod of the hydraulic cylinder, water leaks into the heat exchanger, air is mixed into the hydraulic oil, etc.

sections.text: There is also a type of contaminant - energy contaminants. In a broad sense, static electricity, magnetic fields, thermal energy, and radiation in hydraulic systems are contaminants in the form of energy.
1. Hydraulic Oil Sampling

To check the contamination status of the hydraulic oil, it is advisable to provide a method for extracting representative oil samples that complies with the provisions of GB/T 17489-1998 "Hydraulic Particle Contamination Analysis - Extraction of Liquid Samples from Working System Piping". If a sampling valve is provided in the high-pressure piping, a warning sign for high-pressure spray hazard should be placed so that it is clearly visible at the sampling point, and the sampling valve should be protected.

3. Hydraulic Oil Moisture Content Detection Method

JB/T 12920-2016 "Hydraulic Transmission - Hydraulic Oil Moisture Content Detection Method" stipulates the method of detecting hydraulic oil moisture content by Karl Fischer titration, which is suitable for detecting moisture content in hydraulic oil. (1) Working Condition Requirements for Karl Fischer Titrator

When detecting moisture content in hydraulic oil, the following working condition requirements should be met:
1) Ambient temperature: 3~30°C.

4. Monitoring of particulate contamination in hydraulic oil

GB/T 37162.1—2018 'Monitoring of particulate contamination of hydraulic fluid - Part 1: General rules' specifies methods and techniques for monitoring particulate contamination of hydraulic systems, and describes the advantages and disadvantages of various methods to correctly select monitoring methods under given conditions. The methods described in this standard are applicable to monitoring: cleanliness of hydraulic systems; flushing process; auxiliary equipment and test benches.
This standard is also applicable to monitoring other liquids (such as lubricants, fuels, processing liquids).

Instruments used to monitor particulate contamination cannot be used or called particle counters, even if they use the same physical principles as particle counters. For health and safety requirements, see GB/T 37162.1—2018.
(1) General rules
The selection of monitoring instruments or methods depends on, but is not limited to:

items: Use of the instrument, i.e. working method
Purpose of analysis

(1) Overview
Laser diffraction is a particle analysis method based on light scattering principle, which can be used to measure wide distribution of particle size and concentration. This method works by expanding a low-power transmitted laser beam into a parallel beam, which is then laterally irradiated onto the sensing channel. When particles pass through the parallel beam, the light is scattered and diffracted at different angles according to the particle size. The diffracted beams are focused on a multi-element solid-state detector, and by calculating the measured diffracted beams or calibrating with specific test powders, the particle size distribution of the measured sample can be finally determined.

(2) Main Features
1) Can be used for both offline and online analysis, and can also be used for mainline analysis with glass measurement windows
2) Wide particle size measurement range (0.2-2000μm)
3) Can analyze high concentration particle samples, such as those with contamination worse than 20/18/15 (see GB/T 14039-2002)
4) Analysis time is usually 5 minutes

(3) Limitations
1) Accurate detection requires high particle concentration, with contamination around 19/17/14 (see GB/T 14039-2002)
2) Particle size distribution is based on particle volume
3) Not commonly used in fluid power industry
4) Measurement device is bulky
5) Not suitable for multiphase liquids

(1) Overview
Let a conductive liquid pass through an insulating orifice with electrodes on both sides. When there are no particles, the impedance between the electrodes is constant; when there are particles, the conductivity of the liquid passing through the orifice will change, producing an electrical pulse proportional to the particle volume.

This method is not commonly used for monitoring oil-based liquid systems because the analysis process involves many other steps, such as separating particles and redispersing them in an electrolyte solution, or preparing a series of chemicals to make the oil conductive. Instead, it is used for monitoring water-based liquid systems.
See GB/T 29025-2012 "Particle Size Analysis - Electrical Resistance Method"

(2) Main Features
1) Wide particle size range can be measured by using different analysis orifices (0.5-1500μm)
2) Accurate volume measurement method
3) Can provide particle size distribution
4) Analysis time is usually 5 minutes if the liquid sample can be directly analyzed

(3) Limitations
1) Only used for offline analysis
2) Requires the measured liquid to be conductive
3) The electrical conductivity of particle contaminants in the liquid sample cannot be the same as that of the carrier liquid
4) Analysis time will be extended (usually 20-40 minutes) if the liquid sample is a non-conductive liquid
5) Less application in the fluid power industry

(1) Outline
The mesh blockage method is a detection method that measures the change in the characteristics of a mesh when a liquid sample passes through a mesh with uniform and known openings (or micropores).
When the liquid sample passes through the mesh, particles larger than the pore size of the micropores are filtered out, and the mesh gradually becomes blocked, resulting in an increase in the pressure difference across the mesh (constant flow principle) or a decrease in the flow rate through the mesh (constant pressure difference principle).
By analyzing the number of micropore blockages (blockage condition) and the volume of liquid flowing through the mesh, or by using calibration methods, the concentration of particles in the liquid sample larger than the mesh pore size can be estimated, and then the detection results can be converted to contamination level codes (GB/T 14039-2002).
Since the pressure drop across the mesh is proportional to viscosity, for constant flow detection instruments, the influence of viscosity changes must be corrected during the analysis, and the degree of correction depends on the instrument used. Changes in the density of the liquid sample during the analysis have little effect on the detection results.
See ISO 21018-3.
(2) Main Features
1) It can be used for various analysis methods:
   - Online analysis of high and low pressure pipelines
   - Analysis of oil tanks and container suction
   - Offline analysis of sample bottles
2) It can detect various liquids (such as mineral oil, synthetic liquids, emulsions, solvents, fuels, cleaning liquids, and water-based liquids)
3) As long as the state of the liquid does not change during the analysis, liquids with optical interfaces can be detected (such as water in oil, gas in liquid, and incompatible liquids)
4) A wide range of contamination levels can be detected using a single instrument
5) Depending on the type of instrument, the analysis time is usually 3 to 6 minutes.
(3) Limitations
1) The particle size range is limited (currently available instruments usually have only one or two meshes)
2) Constant pressure difference instruments cannot detect liquid samples with low particle contamination levels (such as contamination levels better than /13/11)
3) Constant flow instruments take a long time (about 8 minutes) to detect liquid samples with low particle contamination levels (such as contamination levels better than /10/8)
4) Individual particle sizes cannot be measured because this method is only limited to monitoring the general level of particle contamination in the system
According to Table A.7 in GB/T 37162.1-2018, the measured size is 6 to 14 μm.

(1) Outline
The weight analysis method is a detection method that separates and collects particles in a liquid sample on a pre-weighed filter membrane (pore size ≤1.0μm) by vacuum filtration, and then reweighs the filter membrane after removing oil and drying to calculate the mass of particles.
See GB/T 27613-2011 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Determination of Particle Contamination Level by Weighing Method"
(2) Main Features
1) It can measure a large amount of contaminants
2) Contaminants on the filter membrane can be analyzed by other methods
(3) Limitations
1) The error is very large when detecting liquid samples with low contamination levels
2) Unless the volume of the analysis liquid is increased, it is not suitable for systems that are too clean (contamination level better than 17/15/12, see GB/T 14039-2002)
3) The analysis time for liquid samples is usually 35 minutes
4) Particle size distribution cannot be measured
5) Auxiliary equipment (such as ovens and balances) is required

(1) Outline
The magnetic detection method is a detection method that measures the change in the radiated magnetic field when a test liquid containing magnetic and paramagnetic particles passes through the sensing area. This type of instrument has various configurations:
1) Some instruments can place the sample (liquid containing particles, filter membrane containing particles, or substrate containing magnetic separation particles) into the detector to measure the content of magnetic particles. Through calibration, this content can be given as a dimensionless index or in the form of mass fraction. Such instruments have a wide range of particle sizes that can be measured and can detect submicron particles (<0.5μm).

2) Some instruments can install magnetic detectors on the system pipelines to detect individual particles passing through. Such instruments can only detect large particles (>75μm) and provide particle count measurements based on volume.
3) Some instruments collect particles through magnets, and as the collected particle concentration gradually increases, the capacitance of the sensors will change. The collected particles can be removed by turning off the magnetic field or using high-voltage vaporization methods. Such instruments are called wear debris detectors.

(2) Main Features
1) Fast analysis of magnetic particles (wear debris analysis only takes 5 seconds)
2) Simple operation
3) Instruments are usually low-priced

(3) Limitations
1) Only used for detecting magnetic and paramagnetic particles
2) Detection results cannot provide particle size distribution or contamination degree grade codes
3) Unless the analysis liquid volume is increased, the detection effect is limited for overly clean samples (contamination degree better than 17/15/13, see GB/T 14039-2002)
4) Confusion in the units of detection results

(1) Overview
In this type of instrument, the liquid sample to be detected passes through a narrow channel illuminated by light (such as a low-power laser) of the sensor. When a single particle passes through the light beam, the amount of light received by the detector (usually located on the opposite side of the liquid flow) is reduced, and the amount of reduction is proportional to the projected surface area of the particle. Thus, when a particle passes through the light beam, it will generate a voltage pulse, which is then detected and recorded by the instrument. The correspondence between the particle size of the instrument/sensor and the pulse voltage can be obtained through calibration according to GB/T 18854-2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Calibration of Liquid Automatic Particle Counters" or GB/T 21540-2008 "Hydraulic Transmission - On-line Automatic Particle Counting System Calibration and Verification Methods". A certain volume of liquid sample needs to pass through the sensor during the detection process. See ISO 11500 and ISO 21018-4

(2) Main Features
1) Can be used for various analysis methods:
   —High and low pressure on-line analysis
   —Fixed installation in the main line of the system for analysis
   —Suction analysis from tanks and containers
   —Off-line analysis using sampling bottles
2) Wide particle size measurement range, up to 1.0~3000μm (depending on the design, the dynamic range of such instruments is usually 50~100)
3) Depending on the working method, the analysis time is usually 2~15 minutes
4) With automatic detection function, on-line instruments do not require operators
5) Wide particle concentration range can be detected without dilution
6) If the measurement volume is increased to improve the statistical quantity of particles, this method has very high accuracy in detecting ultra-clean liquids
7) Relatively simple operation, but requires data understanding ability

(3) Limitations
1) The liquid to be measured must be clear and homogeneous
2) Detection of liquids with optical interfaces (such as water in oil, gas in liquid, immiscible liquid mixtures, emulsions) will produce erroneous particle counts
3) Heavily contaminated liquids need to be diluted before detection, otherwise incorrect results will be produced
4) When there are a large number of small particles smaller than the minimum set size of the instrument in the liquid sample, it will affect the accuracy of the count
5) High environmental requirements for off-line analysis
6) Large particles (>200μm) can block the sensor
7) Detection results are easily affected by the state of the liquid (such as gels and opacity)

(1) Overview
Particles in the liquid sample are separated and collected on a filter membrane through vacuum filtration. The pore size of the filter membrane depends on the state of the liquid sample and the minimum particle size to be counted, but is typically 1.2 μm. For ease of manual counting, the filter membrane usually has 3.1 mm grids printed on it, but when using image analysis, there is no need to use a filter membrane with grids.
After the filter membrane is dried, it can be directly placed under an optical microscope for analysis using incident light, or it can be treated to become transparent and analyzed using transmitted light. Using a calibrated eyepiece reticle (manual counting) or by analyzing the number of pixels occupied by the particles (image analysis), the particle size is measured by the longest chord of the particles. Both methods are calibrated using traceable micrometers.
When performing manual counting, statistical techniques can be used to reduce measurement time. First, the size and count of individual particles in a selected number of grids are measured to obtain the values for any given size, and then these values are corrected to obtain the results for the entire volume of the liquid sample that passed through the filter membrane. When using image analysis for automatic counting, the entire surface of the filter membrane can be measured and analyzed. When measuring different particle sizes, different microscope magnifications need to be used.
Image analysis can also use a camera to convert the particles collected on the filter membrane or the particles in the liquid flow directly into images, and then use a computer or electronic device for image analysis.
See GB/T 20082-2006 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Method for Determining Particle Contamination Degree Using Optical Microscope"
(2) Main Features
1) Considered a standard method, most international and national standards that specify counting methods involve this method
2) Wide range of particle sizes that can be measured (≥2 μm)
3) Particles are visible, allowing timely detection of potential counting problems
4) Low equipment cost for manual counting
5) Information about particle types can be obtained when needed
6) If the liquid is filterable, the test results are independent of the state of the liquid
7) Image analysis can be used for automatic detection, reducing human error and improving measurement accuracy
8) Image analysis can be performed both offline and online
(3) Limitations of Manual Counting Method
1) High skill level required
2) Counting 6 particle sizes takes 30 minutes
3) High environmental requirements
4) Only used for offline analysis
5) Particles are easily obscured by sludge or gel
(4) Limitations of Image Analysis Method
1) When particles overlap or are not in focus, manual processing is required, resulting in increased testing time
2) To make the results more representative, retesting and verification at other magnifications are required

(1) Overview
A small piece of the filter membrane containing particles (usually 1 cm²) is fixed on an aluminum base, a conductive layer (gold, silver, or carbon) is sputtered on it, and then it is placed in the vacuum chamber of a scanning electron microscope for electron bombardment. The electron beam irradiates the sample (similar to the role of photons in an optical microscope), and the image is displayed on a monitor. Finally, the image is electronically processed and the corresponding results are output in a manner similar to image analysis (see the optical microscope counting method above).
When the electron beam is focused on the surface of the sample, it causes ionization of the atoms, producing characteristic X-rays of the material. By analyzing the spectrum of the characteristic X-rays, the elemental composition and content of the particles can be obtained.
See ISO 16232-7 and ISO 16232-8
(2) Main Features
1) High resolution (detection lower limit for particles is 0.01 μm)
2) When using image analysis, both particle size and quantity can be provided simultaneously
3) Elemental composition of particles can be provided
4) High-definition images that are almost unaffected by depth of field can be provided
5) Software can be used to create particle maps based on type and size
(3) Limitations
1) Only used for laboratory analysis
2) High cost and long time consumption (analysis time is usually 1-3 hours)
3) Requires skilled operators
4) Limited depth of electron penetration into the material (about 5 μm)

Film Erosion Method

items: (1) Summary: Install the monitoring instrument on a branch line of the hydraulic system (online analysis), using a nozzle to direct the fluid flow at a relatively high velocity (25 m/s) to spray onto one of two metal strips in the sensor. The second metal strip in the sensor is positioned directly opposite the first, with both strips vacuum-coated with a thin conductive film that, when electrically connected, forms a bridge network. Particles colliding with the active sensor will erode part of the conductive film, changing the metal strip's resistance. The amount of resistance change is proportional to the particle's concentration, hardness, and erosive characteristics. The instrument records the resistance change over time and frequency, expressing it as erosion rate. This method can detect individual particles of larger sizes.

(2) Main Features: 1) Can provide particle hardness and erosion characteristics; 2) Used for online/main line analysis; (3) Limitations: 1) Cannot detect particle size, quantity, or contamination level; 2) Not commonly used in the fluid power industry; 3) Detection results are related to fluid viscosity; 4) Detection results vary with particle hardness

7. Thermal Pollution's Effect on Hydraulic Oil

Understanding excessive heat in hydraulic working media as a form of energy pollution is itself a scientific advancement, because "contaminants" as defined in GB/T 17446-2012 do not include energy-based pollutants. Although this energy pollutant is determined under given conditions, when conditions change, it may no longer be considered a pollutant.

Based on practical experience, when a hydraulic system experiences systemic failures such as multiple component and pipeline external leaks, accelerated wear of multiple components, or jamming/clogging of various components, it may have been operating for an extended period at high temperatures or for a shorter period at even higher temperatures. In such cases, the most obvious manifestation should be the deterioration of the hydraulic oil in the original system.

The greatest danger of high hydraulic oil temperature is the final decomposition of the hydraulic oil itself, accompanied by the loss of viscosity and lubricity of the hydraulic oil. Decomposition will lead to the formation of varnish (oxide ions) substances, acidic substances, and sediment substances in the hydraulic oil. Varnish and sediment substances will cause valve sticking and eventually cause blockage, and also cause throttle orifice blockage; acidic substances will corrode metal surfaces and accelerate the wear of pumps, cylinders, and valves.

In most cases, high temperature will cause severe loss of viscosity and lubricity of hydraulic oil. Thin hydraulic oil may cause greater impact and vibration, increase the possibility of component damage, and even cause loosening of assemblies and connections with the base. If lubricity is lost and the lubricating oil film disappears, metal-to-metal direct contact will occur, leaving scratch marks on the surface.

Temperature is the main accelerator of hydraulic oil oxidation. For every 10°C increase in temperature, the oxidation reaction will double. When the temperature is below 60°C, the oxidation rate will be very low; when the temperature is above 60°C, the service life of mineral-based oil will be halved for every 10°C increase in temperature, and the service life loss rate will be as high as 97% at 100°C.

Based on these facts, a lower working temperature of the hydraulic system is beneficial to minimize oxidation reaction and hydraulic oil degradation. However, the oil temperature in the oil tank is not the actual oil temperature, and the temperature at the pump outlet can represent the actual temperature. In this way, the area where local oxidation is very severe will be hotter.

The thermal stability of oil refers to its ability to resist decomposition caused by temperature. If its use is not damaged within a specific range, then the upper limit of the hydraulic oil's extreme temperature is determined. Some literature introduces that most failures of hydraulic systems, especially electro-hydraulic servo valve-servo hydraulic cylinder control systems, are caused by hydraulic oil contamination, especially solid particle contaminants. When the system exhibits intermittent characteristics or other unreasonable characteristics, and unexplained failures occur, it should be suspected that it is caused by solid particle contaminants in the hydraulic oil.
7.2 Selection and Use of Hydraulic Cylinders
7.2.1 Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Guidelines for Selecting Hydraulic Cylinders

Guidelines for selecting hydraulic cylinders are given in Reference [54]. Improper selection of hydraulic cylinders will not only cause economic losses to users, but may also lead to accidents. When selecting, the working conditions of the hydraulic cylinder should be carefully analyzed, appropriate structural and installation types should be selected, and reasonable parameters should be determined.
The selection of hydraulic cylinders should mainly consider the following points:

items: 1) Structure type of hydraulic cylinder
2) Cylinder forward stroke output force or cylinder return stroke output force
3) Nominal (maximum rated or rated) pressure and working pressure range
4) Cylinder diameter and piston rod diameter
5) Maximum stroke of the cylinder and working stroke range of the cylinder
6) Reciprocating speed
7) Installation type
8) Environmental conditions (such as ambient temperature, environmental pollutants, etc.)
9) Usage conditions
10) Working medium
11) Sealing device
12) Other devices (such as buffering devices, exhaust (discharge) devices, etc.)

sections.text: When selecting hydraulic cylinders, priority should be given to using standard hydraulic cylinders from related series, which has many advantages: first, it can greatly shorten the design and manufacturing cycle; second, it is convenient for spare parts, and has greater interchangeability and versatility. In addition, standard hydraulic cylinders have been carefully analyzed and calculated during design, have undergone bench tests and field tests, and professional manufacturers have dedicated equipment, jigs, and relatively complete testing equipment, and the quality is guaranteed.

Inspection conditions can guarantee quality, so they are relatively reliable to use. Various series of hydraulic cylinders in our country have been standardized. At present, heavy machinery, construction machinery, agricultural machinery, automobiles, metallurgical equipment, combination machine tools, marine hydraulic cylinders, etc. have formed standards or series. The selection guide for hydraulic cylinders given in reference [54] is shown in Table 7-20.

sections.caption: Table 7-20  Selection Guide for Hydraulic Cylinders
rows: Selection of Main Parameters for Hydraulic Cylinders

When selecting hydraulic cylinders, according to the requirements of the motion mechanism, not only must the hydraulic cylinder have sufficient acting (output) force, speed, and stroke, but also sufficient strength and rigidity. However, in some special cases, to use standard hydraulic cylinders or to utilize existing hydraulic cylinders, such as the rated pressure of hydraulic cylinders, it is permissible to slightly exceed their rated working range. For example, if the rated working pressure of a hydraulic cylinder is 6.3 MPa, to increase its acting (output) force to push mechanical motion exceeding the rated load, it is allowed to increase its working pressure to 6.5 MPa or slightly higher. This is because when designing hydraulic cylinder parts, there is a certain safety margin. However, the following issues should be noted: ①The rated values of hydraulic cylinders should not be exceeded too much, otherwise the safety factor will be excessively reduced, making accidents prone to occur. ②The working conditions of hydraulic cylinders should be relatively stable, and the hydraulic system should not have unexpected impact pressure. ③The strength of certain parts of the hydraulic cylinder should be recalculated. In particular, the strength of the cylinder barrel, the connection strength of the cylinder head, and the longitudinal bending strength of the piston rod should be checked. Note: It is not recommended to select hydraulic cylinders beyond the nominal pressure, maximum rated pressure, or rated pressure of hydraulic cylinders, especially for hydraulic cylinders that have been used for a period of time.

There are many types of hydraulic cylinder installations, each with different characteristics. When selecting the installation type for a hydraulic cylinder, it is necessary to ensure that the machinery and hydraulic cylinder can move freely, make the hydraulic cylinder work stably, and place the installation part in a favorable stress state. In order to obtain greater freedom of movement, the hydraulic cylinders of construction machinery and agricultural machinery mostly use swing axis types, such as clevis hinge shafts or ball heads, such as telescopic cylinders, luffing cylinders, dump cylinders, boom cylinders, and lifting cylinders; However, the hydraulic cylinders for the worktable of metal cutting machine tools all use fixed axis type hydraulic cylinders, such as bracket and flange installation types.

Installation components must have sufficient strength. For example, if the bracket of a bracket type hydraulic cylinder is very thin and lacks rigidity, even if the installation is correct, the cylinder barrel will warp upward under pressure, causing the piston to not move normally, and even accidents such as bending and breaking of the piston rod may occur. Note: The installation components here should be considered as accessories of the cylinder; The bracket should be a bracket; However, there is no bracket type hydraulic cylinder, and the following is the same.

When selecting the installation type of hydraulic cylinders, try to use a type with better stability, such as the stability of the head hinge axis of a hinge axis type hydraulic cylinder is the best, and the stability of the tail hinge axis is the worst. Note: "Hinge axis" should be "hinge pin".

The same installation type, with different installation directions, will experience different forces. For example, the flange type hydraulic cylinder has four types: external flange at the head, internal flange at the head, external flange at the tail, and internal flange at the tail. Moreover, due to the different directions of the thrust and pull forces of the hydraulic cylinder, it constitutes eight working states of the flange. Among these eight working states, only two states are the best. For hydraulic cylinders that work in the direction of piston rod retraction, using an external flange at the head is most advantageous. When the working direction is to push out the piston rod, using an external flange at the tail is most advantageous. This is because only in these two cases will the flange not produce bending moments, while the other six working states will produce bending effects. In bracket type hydraulic cylinders, the overturning moment received by the radial bracket is the smallest, the tangential bracket is larger, and the axial bracket is the largest, all of which should be considered. Note: The author does not agree with some views in the above text, such as "only in these two cases will the flange not produce bending moments". The author believes that regardless of the installation type of the flange type hydraulic cylinder, the flange is subjected to bending moment. The reason why these two cases are considered reasonable is that the fastening screws do not bear tension. In addition, the descriptions of various installation types of flange type do not comply with the provisions of GB/T 9094-2006.

Influence of Speed on Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder

Low Speed Movement

When the hydraulic cylinder moves at low speed, special attention should be paid to the crawling problem. There are many reasons for the crawling of hydraulic cylinders, but they can be summarized into the following three aspects:
①The friction force between the relative moving parts of the mechanism pushed by the hydraulic cylinder is too large, the friction resistance changes, and there are contaminants on the mutual friction surfaces, such as the guide rails of the machine tool table being adjusted too tightly, poor lubrication conditions, etc.
②The internal causes of the hydraulic system. Such as poor flow stability of the speed control valve, compressibility of the oil, water hammer effect (water hammer phenomenon) in the system, air entrainment, unclean oil, pulsation of hydraulic pressure, unreasonable circuit design, no back pressure in the return oil, etc.
③Internal causes of the hydraulic cylinder. Such as excessive friction force of the seal, unreasonable clearance between sliding surfaces, low machining accuracy and surface finish (large surface roughness value), air entrainment in the hydraulic cylinder, poor rigidity of the piston rod, etc.
Therefore, when solving the crawling problem of the hydraulic cylinder at low speed, in addition to solving the external problems of the hydraulic cylinder, the internal problems of the hydraulic cylinder should also be solved, that is, corresponding technical measures should be taken in the structure. The main points to note are as follows:
①Select sealing parts with small sliding resistance, such as sliding seal, clearance seal, piston ring seal, plastic seal parts, etc.
②The piston rod should be subjected to stability verification.
③Make the clearance between sliding surfaces as large as possible within the allowable range, so that even if there are assembly errors, it will not cause large unilateral friction between sliding surfaces and affect the sliding of the hydraulic cylinder.
④The surface roughness value Ra of the sliding surface should be controlled between 0.05～0.2μm.
⑤The guide sleeve should be made of materials that can be immersed in oil, such as gray cast iron, aluminum bronze, tin bronze, etc.
⑥Adopt a reasonable exhaust device to remove the residual air in the hydraulic cylinder.
Note: The term "low speed" is not based on any standard; "sliding seal" is not clear what it refers to (sliding seal, plastic seal, etc. are not included in the sealing parts of piston and piston rod in Table 20-6-21 of reference [54]); the surface roughness value Ra of the sliding surface should be controlled between 0.05～0.2μm does not comply with the relevant standards and is impossible in practice.

The main problems of the high-speed hydraulic cylinder are the wear resistance of the sealing parts and the buffering problem.
①The maximum working speed of general rubber sealing parts is 60m/min. But from the perspective of service life, the working speed is best not to exceed 20m/min. Because when the sealing parts are rubbed at high speed, frictional heat will be generated, which is easy to cause burning, sticking, damage the sealing performance, and shorten the service life. In addition, high-speed hydraulic cylinders should use sealing parts that are not easy to twist, or take appropriate anti-twisting measures.
②When necessary, high-speed moving hydraulic cylinders should be equipped with buffering devices. To determine whether to use a buffering device, not only should the high speed of the hydraulic cylinder movement and the total mass and inertia force of the moving parts be considered, but also the working requirements of the hydraulic cylinder. Generally, when the speed of the hydraulic cylinder is in the range of 10～25m/min, it is necessary to consider using a buffering device. If it is less than 10m/min, it is not necessary to use a buffering structure. However, when the speed is greater than 25m/min, only taking buffering measures on the hydraulic cylinder is often not enough, and buffering measures should also be considered in the return circuit.
Note: High-speed reciprocating hydraulic cylinders also have a problem, that is, the external leakage will be very large, and even cause the piston rod seal to fail.
Influence of Stroke on Selection of Hydraulic Cylinder

When using a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder, the following two issues should be noted:
①Floating measures for the cylinder barrel. The cylinder barrel of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is very long, and the oil temperature in the hydraulic system is prone to rise during work, which may cause the expansion and elongation of the cylinder body. If both ends of the cylinder barrel are fixed, the cylinder body cannot elongate, and internal stress or deformation will inevitably occur, affecting the normal operation of the hydraulic cylinder. Using one end fixed and the other end floating can avoid thermal stress in the cylinder barrel.
②Supporting measures for the piston rod. The piston rod (or plunger) of a long-stroke hydraulic cylinder is very long, and it is prone to sag when fully extended, causing unilateral wear on the guide sleeve, sealing parts, and piston rod. Therefore, it should be considered to use a support bracket to support the piston rod or plunger as much as possible.
Note: Long-stroke hydraulic cylinders may also have the problem of radial expansion of the cylinder barrel. Therefore, some hydraulic cylinders (such as those with a stroke exceeding 1m) require the hydraulic cylinder to be stopped at half the stroke for internal leakage testing.

sections.caption: (Continued)
rows:
Generally, hydraulic cylinders are suitable for operation within the temperature range of -10 to 80°C, with a maximum limit not exceeding -20 to 105°C. Since most hydraulic cylinders use nitrile rubber as sealing elements, their operating temperature cannot naturally exceed the working temperature range of nitrile rubber. Therefore, the working temperature of hydraulic cylinders is limited by the performance of the sealing elements.

Additionally, the working of hydraulic cylinders at different temperatures should also have different considerations for the selection of component materials and determination of dimensions.

① When working at high temperatures, sealing elements should use fluororubber, which can work for a long time at high temperatures of 200 to 250°C, and its durability is also significantly superior to that of nitrile rubber.

In addition to solving the heat resistance of sealing elements, heat insulation and cooling measures can also be taken on the hydraulic cylinder. For example, the cylinder barrel and piston rod can be covered with heat insulation materials such as asbestos to reduce the influence of the heat source on the hydraulic cylinder.

The piston rod can be made hollow to allow the introduction of circulating cooling air or cooling water. The cooling of the guide sleeve is to introduce cooling air or cooling water from the cylinder barrel to take away the heat of the guide sleeve sealing element and piston rod.

For hydraulic cylinders working at high temperatures, due to the different coefficients of linear expansion of various materials, the dimensions of sliding surfaces should be properly adjusted. For example, the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is 10.6×10⁻⁶/°C, while that of oil-resistant rubber is 10 to 20 times that of steel. Undoubtedly, the expansion of sealing elements will increase the friction between sliding surfaces, so it is necessary to properly adjust the dimensions of sealing elements. To reduce the thermal influence of high temperature on the dust ring, in addition to using an asbestos heat insulation device, an aluminum bronze plate can also be added to the outside of the dust ring.

If the hydraulic cylinder works at a temperature higher than the recrystallization temperature of the materials used, the changes of hydraulic cylinder components should also be considered, especially the creep and strength changes of fasteners.

② When working at low temperatures, such as hydraulic cylinders working below -20°C, it is best to also use fluororubber or nitrile rubber with a plasticizer of 0259 mixed grease to make sealing elements and dust rings. Since the piston rod is prone to ice formation when working below 0°C, to protect the dust ring from damage, an aluminum bronze alloy scraper is often added outside the dust ring.

Special attention should be paid to the low-temperature brittle fracture of the metal materials of hydraulic cylinders when they work at -40°C or below. The tensile strength and fatigue limit of steel increase with decreasing temperature (except for carbon steel with a carbon mass fraction of 0.6%, whose fatigue limit drops sharply at -40°C). However, the impact performance starts to decrease significantly at -40°C, resulting in poor toughness of the steel. When subjected to strong external impact, it is prone to fracture and damage. Therefore, for hydraulic cylinders working at -40°C or below, high-carbon steel, ordinary structural steel and other materials with low impact values should be avoided as much as possible, and nickel-based stainless steel, chromium-molybdenum steel and other alloy steels with high impact performance should be used.

If the hydraulic cylinder has welded parts, the strength and reliability of the weld seam under low-temperature conditions should also be carefully checked.

Note: Many contents in the above text are inaccurate, so be sure to pay attention when referring to them, such as the working temperature range of general hydraulic cylinders, the working temperature range of sealing elements and sealing materials, etc., which do not conform to the current relevant standards.

Many hydraulic cylinders often work under harsh conditions. For example, excavators often work in wind and rain and constantly collide with dust, sand and stones; hydraulic cylinders working on the sea or seashore are easily eroded by seawater or humid air; hydraulic cylinders in chemical machinery often come into contact with acid and alkali solutions, etc. Therefore, corresponding measures should also be taken according to the working environment of hydraulic cylinders.
Working Environment Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders and Dust Prevention Measures

In occasions with a lot of dust, such as foundry workshops and ore crushing sites, special attention should be paid to the dust prevention of hydraulic cylinders. The entry of dust into the hydraulic cylinder will not only cause faults but also increase the wear of the sliding surfaces of the hydraulic cylinder. At the same time, powdery metal will be precipitated, and this powdery metal will further accelerate the wear of the hydraulic cylinder, forming a vicious cycle.

In addition, the dust mixed into the hydraulic cylinder can also easily be carried into other hydraulic devices by the circulating hydraulic oil, causing faults or aggravating wear. Therefore, dust prevention is very important.

The external dust prevention measures for hydraulic cylinders mainly involve adding dust rings or dust covers. When selecting dust telescopic sleeves, attention should be paid to their durability during high-frequency actions, as well as whether the air holes of the telescopic sleeves can timely introduce sufficient air during high-speed movement. However, the installation of telescopic sleeves will bring some difficulties to the assembly and adjustment of hydraulic cylinders.

Note: After checking, the so-called "dust cover", "dust telescopic sleeve", "telescopic sleeve", etc. in reference [54] lightweight rod-type hydraulic cylinder and other references are called "protective cover".
