sections.caption: Selection Methods for Hydraulic Cylinder Working Conditions (continued)
rows: Work environment impact on hydraulic cylinder selection - Rust prevention measures

In humid air environments, particularly in marine, underwater, or coastal operations, hydraulic cylinders are very susceptible to corrosion and rust. Therefore, rust prevention measures are crucial. One effective rust prevention method is chrome plating. After metal is chrome plated, its chemical stability resists corrosion from humid air and other gases, as well as from alkalis, nitric acid, organic acids, etc. Additionally, chrome plating increases hardness and reduces the friction coefficient, greatly enhancing wear resistance. However, it cannot resist corrosion from hydrochloric acid, hot sulfuric acid, etc. For general rust prevention or merely for wear resistance, a chrome plating layer of only 0.02-0.03 mm is sufficient. For hydraulic cylinders operating in wind, rain, or humid air, the chrome plating layer should be above 0.05 mm, or nickel plating may be used. For hydraulic cylinders operating in seawater, it is best to use materials like stainless steel. Additionally, bolts, nuts, and other components of the hydraulic cylinder should also consider using stainless steel or chromium-molybdenum steel.
Surface hardening of the piston rod

Some hydraulic cylinders operate under very harsh external conditions. For example, the piston rod of an excavator's hydraulic cylinder frequently collides with sand and gravel, while the piston rod or plunger of a press's hydraulic cylinder must directly press workpieces. Therefore, the surface hardness of the piston rod must be increased. The main method is high-frequency induction hardening, with a depth of 1-3 mm and a hardness of 40-50 HRC.
Force conditions impact on hydraulic cylinder selection - Overview

The force conditions on hydraulic cylinders are relatively complex. During alternating loads and frequent direction changes, hydraulic cylinders experience significant vibration; during heavy-load high-speed motion, they bear substantial inertial forces; under certain conditions, hydraulic cylinders must also bear lateral loads. Therefore, when designing and selecting hydraulic cylinders, appropriate measures should be taken according to the force conditions.

There are many causes of vibration in hydraulic cylinders. In addition to reasons from pumps, valves, and the system, certain reasons from the cylinder itself can also cause vibration, such as improper part processing and assembly, excessive sealing resistance, direction change impact, etc. Vibration can easily cause the connecting screws of hydraulic cylinders to loosen, which can lead to cylinder head separation, causing O-ring extrusion and damage, resulting in oil leakage. There are many methods to prevent screws and nuts from loosening, such as using fine thread, installing spring washers, lock washers, lock nuts, pins, set screws, etc. Additionally, tightening screws with stress greater than 50-60% above the yield strength can also prevent loosening. For hydraulic cylinders with significant vibration, attention should not only be paid to whether the connecting threads and screws of the cylinder head are prone to loosening, but also to the loosening problem of the threads connecting the piston and piston rod. Note: Based on the author's experience, the method of 'tightening screws with stress greater than 50-60% above the yield strength to prevent loosening' has not been seen applied to hydraulic cylinders.

When a hydraulic cylinder has a large load and high speed, it will be subjected to great inertial force, causing oil pressure to rise sharply, cylinder expansion, and the fastening parts to suddenly bear increased stress, which may even lead to cracking. Therefore, buffer structures need to be adopted.

When a hydraulic cylinder bears a large lateral load, it is easy to squeeze out the oil film on one side of the sliding surface of the hydraulic cylinder, causing excessive wear, burning, or even seizure. When selecting materials for hydraulic cylinder sliding parts, the following measures should be considered: ① Bronze surfacing on the outside of the piston or installation of a wear-resistant ring ② High-frequency induction hardening of the piston rod, with guide sleeves made of bronze, cast iron, or nitrided steel
Impact of seals and working oil on hydraulic cylinder selection

When the friction force of seals is large, crawling and vibration are likely to occur. To reduce sliding resistance, seals with low friction are often used, such as sliding seals. Additionally, the high-temperature resistance, low-temperature resistance, hardness, and elasticity of seals have a significant impact on the operation of hydraulic cylinders. Seals with poor high-temperature resistance are prone to sticking and adhesion when working at high temperatures; after the hardness of seals decreases, the phenomenon of being squeezed into gaps becomes more severe, further accelerating their damage and destroying the sealing effect; seals with poor low-temperature resistance are prone to permanent deformation in compression when working below -10°C, also affecting the sealing effect; seals with low hardness and poor elasticity are easily squeezed into the sealing gap and destroyed. Polyurethane seals are easily decomposed in aqueous solutions and should be given special attention. The selection of working oil should consider the pump, valve, hydraulic cylinder, and the entire hydraulic system, as well as analyze the working conditions and temperature of the hydraulic device to select appropriate working oil. When working under high temperature, high pressure, and low speed conditions, working oil with higher viscosity should generally be selected. When working under low temperature, low pressure, and high speed conditions, working oil with lower viscosity should be selected. Non-flammable oil should be used under hot and high-temperature conditions. However, it should be noted that when using water-based non-flammable oil, polyurethane rubber seals cannot be used; when using phosphate ester-based non-flammable oil, nitrile rubber seals cannot be used, otherwise hydrolysis and erosion will occur. High viscosity index oil should be used in precision machinery.

2. Selection Method for Multi-stage Hydraulic Cylinders

The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder belongs to a single-acting telescopic sleeve hydraulic cylinder, with advantages such as small size and large stroke. The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder has three installation types: cylinder bottom universal joint bearing clevis, cylinder body hinge shaft, and flange. The cylinder head first stage is equipped with a universal joint bearing clevis. The UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder has seven types of plunger diameters, which can be combined into six types of secondary cylinders, five types of tertiary cylinders, four types of quaternary cylinders, and three types of five-stage cylinders. Under the premise of allowing stability, the hydraulic cylinder manufacturer can provide UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinders with strokes exceeding 20m.

Since the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is composed of cylinders with various plunger diameters, each stage of the cylinder has different speeds when the system flow rate is constant. During the lifting load process, under normal circumstances, the plunger with the largest diameter extends first and at a slower speed; when the stroke of the large plunger ends, the next stage large diameter plunger extends again, and its speed will become faster; the plunger with the smallest diameter extends last, but its extension speed is the fastest. When retracting under external force, the plunger with the smallest diameter retracts first, at the fastest speed; then it retracts in sequence; the plunger with the largest diameter retracts last, and the retraction speed is also the slowest. For the speed requirements of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder, generally the time required for the full stroke is specified, or the operating speed of a certain stage.
Taking the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder as an example, the selection method for multi-stage cylinders is given below:

Usage method:
1) Working pressure. The rated pressure of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is 16MPa (factory test pressure is 24MPa). The user system should be adjusted within the range of 16MPa. For short-stroke UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinders with a stroke of less than or equal to 500mm per stage, the rated pressure can reach 21MPa, but it must be marked on the order model.
2) Determine the cylinder diameter of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder. If a constant thrust output is required for the full stroke, the thrust generated by the first stage (the stage with the smallest diameter) plunger under the provided medium pressure must be greater than the required constant thrust. For example, if the required constant thrust is 30kN and the system pressure is 12MPa, then the selected first stage plunger diameter is 56.4mm, and at this time, a cylinder with a diameter of approximately φ60mm for the first stage should be selected from the specifications. If the system pressure is 16MPa, then the φ60mm first stage cylinder can be directly selected according to Table 7-21. If the required thrust is a variable, then the variable force-stroke curve and the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder stroke thrust curve should be made to determine the optimal cylinder diameter selection. Since the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is a single-acting cylinder, it must rely on gravity load or other external forces to drive the return stroke. The minimum starting pressure of the UDZ type multi-stage hydraulic cylinder is less than or equal to 0.3MPa, from which the minimum return force of each plunger cylinder can be calculated.

7.2.2 Working Conditions for Hydraulic Cylinders

The working conditions for hydraulic cylinders generally refer to a set of characteristic values such as environmental conditions, nominal pressure or rated pressure, speed, and working medium determined by the purpose of the hydraulic cylinder. Generally, the rated working conditions are given during hydraulic cylinder design.

The environmental conditions during the use of hydraulic cylinders should include environmental temperature and its variation range, inclination or swaying conditions, vibration, air humidity (including icing), salt spray, environmental pollution, radiation (including thermal radiation), etc.; rated pressure includes minimum rated pressure (i.e., starting pressure) and maximum rated pressure (i.e., pressure resistance pressure), speed includes minimum (stable) speed and maximum speed, and working medium includes the type, cleanliness, and temperature of the working medium.
rated conditions; the working medium includes the viscosity and contamination of the hydraulic oil, etc.

The rated operating conditions are conditions that must be given or determined when designing a hydraulic cylinder, and the hydraulic cylinder can only guarantee sufficient service life if it is designed according to these conditions.

The extreme operating conditions are a special condition. Under these conditions, the hydraulic cylinder can only operate for a given time; otherwise, irreparable damage will be caused to the hydraulic cylinder, such as over-running during pressure resistance or high-temperature testing.
1. Temperature Range
Rated Operating Conditions: Generally, the ambient temperature for the operation of a hydraulic cylinder should be -20 to 50°C.

Extreme Operating Conditions: According to standards, when the ambient temperature is 65°C ± 5°C and the working medium temperature is 70°C ± 2°C, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to continuously reciprocate at the specified speed for 1 hour.
When the ambient temperature is -25°C ± 2°C and the working medium temperature is -15°C, the hydraulic cylinder should be able to continuously reciprocate at the specified speed for 5 minutes.
Therefore, the extreme ambient temperature range is temporarily set at: -25 to 65°C.
2. Maximum Rated Pressure

Because the maximum rated pressure is the pressure resistance pressure, the pressure resistance pressure is theoretically determined by the structural strength of the hydraulic cylinder, mainly by the structural strength of the generalized cylinder body. Therefore, if the structure of the hydraulic cylinder is already determined, then the pressure resistance pressure of the hydraulic cylinder can also be determined.

Although the maximum rated pressure can be determined by analogy, reverse design, etc., according to the above method in hydraulic cylinder design, it is usually determined to be 1.5 times the nominal pressure, i.e., the pressure resistance pressure.

JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard applies to single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with a nominal pressure below 31.5 MPa, using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.

According to GB/T 2346—2003 "Fluid Transmission and Components Nominal Pressure Series", where 31.5 MPa is below 25 MPa, the standard stipulates that the maximum rated pressure (pressure resistance pressure) is 1.5×25 MPa=37.5 MPa for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.

It is recommended to determine the pressure resistance test pressure of the hydraulic cylinder through negotiation between the manufacturer and the user: when the nominal pressure is greater than or equal to 20 MPa, the pressure resistance test pressure should be 1.25 times the nominal pressure.

If this is the case, then JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard stipulates that the maximum rated pressure (pressure resistance pressure) is 1.25×25 MPa=31.25 MPa for single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders using hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium.
It is also important to emphasize a few points:

items: The maximum rated pressure or pressure resistance test pressure should be combined with the corresponding temperature to form a combined condition.
The maximum rated pressure or pressure resistance test pressure should be a static pressure and can be verified.
The maximum rated pressure is the pressure immediately below the burst pressure.

sections.text: 3. Speed Range

In hydraulic cylinder testing, the starting pressure corresponding to the lowest (minimum) speed is generally not the lowest speed, because at this time the hydraulic cylinder is only starting, rather than having a stable speed.

The lowest speed of hydraulic cylinders specified in current standards, including seal standards, is generally not lower than 4.0 mm/s, usually the lowest speed is 8.0 mm/s; the lowest stable speed of marine digital hydraulic cylinders should not be greater than 20 pulse equivalents per second.

The highest speed of a hydraulic cylinder is closely related to the design of seals and sealing systems. Nitrile rubber seals generally limit the speed to below 500 mm/s, usually the highest speed is below 300 mm/s; the highest speed of marine digital hydraulic cylinders can reach 2000 pulse equivalents per second.
Hydraulic cylinders with speeds higher than 200 mm/s must be equipped with a cushioning device.
4. Working Medium

JB/T 10205—2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder" Standard stipulates that single and double-acting hydraulic cylinders use hydraulic oil or other mineral oils with comparable performance as the working medium. The working medium must be compatible with the materials, mainly the sealing materials.

Except for special requirements, during other hydraulic cylinder tests, the kinematic viscosity of the hydraulic oil at 40°C on the test bench should be 29 to 74 mm²/s, and it is best to coordinate with the user.

GB/T 7935—2005 "Hydraulic Components General Technical Conditions" stipulates that the kinematic viscosity of the test hydraulic oil at 40°C should be 42 to 74 mm²/s (special requirements are subject to separate regulations).
JB/T 6134—2006 "Hydraulic Cylinders for Metallurgical Equipment (PN≤25 MPa)" stipulates that the test oil viscosity grade should be VG32 or VG46.

JB/T 9834—2014 "Agricultural Double-Acting Hydraulic Cylinder Technical Conditions" stipulates that the test oil should use N100D tractor transmission and hydraulic dual-purpose oil or mineral oil with comparable viscosity, and its kinematic viscosity at 40°C should be 90 to 110 mm²/s.

JB/T 13141—2017 "Tractor Steering Hydraulic Cylinder" stipulates that the viscosity of the test oil: the kinematic viscosity of the oil at 40°C should be 90 to 110 mm²/s, or the kinematic viscosity at 65°C should be 25 to 35 mm²/s.

JB/T 3818—2014 "Hydraulic Press Technical Conditions" stipulates that the oil temperature in the oil tank (or the oil temperature at the inlet of the hydraulic pump) should not exceed 60°C, and the oil temperature should not be lower than 15°C.
The user and manufacturer negotiate to determine the high-temperature performance requirements of the hydraulic cylinder.

894.page_header: Chapter 7 Hydraulic Cylinder Use and Maintenance 883

sections.text: The working medium temperature of hydraulic cylinders generally should not exceed 90°C and should be limited in high-temperature operation time.

The solid particle contamination level of the test oil for general hydraulic cylinders (including marine digital cylinders) should not exceed -/19/15 specified in GB/T 14039-2002; the solid contamination level of the test oil for servo hydraulic cylinders specified in DB44/T 1169-2013 should not exceed 13/12/10 specified in GB/T 14039-2002.
7.2.3 Technical Requirements for Hydraulic Cylinders
1. General Requirements

items: JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinders" specifies the technical requirements for single-acting and double-acting hydraulic cylinders with nominal pressure below 31.5 MPa and using hydraulic oil or other mineral oil with comparable performance as working medium. For hydraulic cylinders with nominal pressure higher than 31.5 MPa, this standard may be referred to.
Generally, the ambient temperature for hydraulic cylinder operation should be within -20~50°C, and the working medium temperature should be within -20~80°C, preferably limited to 15~60°C.
The cleanliness of the hydraulic system should comply with the provisions of JB/T 9954-1999 "Cleanliness of Hydraulic Systems for Forging Machinery".

Generally, hydraulic cylinders should be lifted and installed using the lifting holes or hooks provided, avoiding bumps and scratches on the hydraulic cylinder, protecting the nameplate, and preventing corrosion of the hydraulic cylinder.
Installation and connection of hydraulic cylinders should minimize lateral forces on the piston and piston rod, ensure safety and reliability, and maintain accuracy.

Avoid using the hydraulic cylinder as a limit device. When the hydraulic cylinder is used as a limit device, the size and installation type of the hydraulic cylinder should be determined based on the maximum load caused by the restricted components.

Hydraulic systems with hydraulic cylinders must be equipped with safety valves to prevent the hydraulic cylinder from being subjected to overpressure exceeding 1.1 times the nominal pressure, especially to avoid overpressure caused by pressure increase due to piston area difference. The safety valve pressure can be set according to the overload test pressure of the main machine, and should not exceed 1.1 times the rated pressure for overload test pressure.

sections.text: 2. Performance Requirements

items: The hydraulic cylinder should be able to conveniently discharge air from all chambers during test operation.

The hydraulic cylinder should be able to start normally at the specified (minimum) starting pressure, and should run smoothly and uniformly at low pressure, without vibration, crawling, and sticking phenomena.

Except for the piston rod seal, other parts should not have external leakage (seepage); after stopping operation, the piston rod seal should not have external leakage; the external leakage of the piston rod seal during operation (including under low pressure) should comply with relevant standard specifications.
The internal leakage of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with relevant standard specifications.
At nominal pressure and below, hydraulic cylinders with load efficiency of 90% or above should be able to normally drive the load.
The stroke and tolerance of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with relevant standard specifications or design requirements.
For hydraulic cylinders with stroke positioning performance, their positioning accuracy and repeat positioning accuracy should comply with relevant specifications.
The pressure resistance, durability, cushioning performance, high temperature performance, etc. of the hydraulic cylinder should comply with relevant standard specifications.

sections.text: 3. Safety Technical Requirements

items: When using hydraulic cylinders, risk assessment should be conducted according to the failure modes given during hydraulic cylinder design, and protective measures should be taken.
Safety precautions should be taken for sliders (or moving parts) connected to piston rods that have the risk of accidental falling.
When hydraulic cylinders have explosion risk due to accidental overpressure, it is best to install protective covers outside the hydraulic cylinder.
Installation and connection of hydraulic cylinders must be firm and reliable, avoiding tilting, falling off, and disconnection.

Fasteners for installing and connecting hydraulic cylinders should avoid bearing shear forces as much as possible, and anti-loosening measures should be taken. GB/T 3766-2015 specifies: "Trunnion-mounted hydraulic cylinders may apply shear forces to their mounting bolts. If shear loads are involved, consideration should be given to using hydraulic cylinders with mechanisms capable of bearing shear loads. Fasteners for installation should be sufficient to bear overturning moments."

Use hydraulic cylinders within their design strength and stiffness, avoiding excessive deformation of hydraulic cylinder structure due to pushing or pulling loads. When hydraulic cylinders push loads, piston rods may bend or become unstable, which should be avoided from exceeding design specified values. GB/T 3766-2015 specifies: "To avoid bending or instability of hydraulic cylinder piston rods at any position, attention should be paid to cylinder stroke, load, and installation type."
When hydraulic cylinder piston (piston rod) movement speed exceeds 200mm/s, the piston must contact the cylinder bottom or cylinder head (guide sleeve) after cushioning.
Generally, when working medium temperature exceeds 90°C, ambient temperature exceeds 65°C or is below -25°C, the machine must be stopped.

Hydraulic cylinder leakage can cause environmental pollution, especially when hydraulic oil spraying may cause greater harm, protective measures should be taken to eliminate personal injury and fire hazards.
Hydraulic cylinders in use should not be inspected or disassembled.

sections.text: 7.3 Maintenance of Hydraulic Cylinders
7.3.1 Evaluation and Control of Hydraulic Oil Contamination
The hydraulic oil used in hydraulic systems should be compatible with all system components, accessories, synthetic rubber, and filter elements.
1. Evaluation of Hydraulic Oil Contamination
In hydraulic systems and components, contaminants exist to a greater or lesser extent.
The quantitative index for evaluating this degree of pollution is the pollution degree or cleanliness, with the antonym of pollution degree being cleanliness.

Solid particle contaminants present in hydraulic oil may cause serious consequences, thus requiring their measurement. GB/T 14039-2002 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fluid - Solid Particle Contamination Level Codes" stipulates the codes used to determine the level of solid particle contaminants in the fluid of hydraulic systems.

GB/Z 20423-2006 "Hydraulic System Assembly - Cleanliness Inspection" stipulates the procedures for determining and inspecting the cleanliness level that must be achieved before the hydraulic system is shipped after assembly.

GB/T 27613-2011 "Hydraulic Transmission - Liquid Contamination - Determination of Particle Contamination Degree by Weighing Method" stipulates two weighing methods for determining the particle contamination degree of the working medium of hydraulic systems, namely the double membrane and single membrane methods. This standard is applicable for detecting particle contamination degrees greater than 0.2 mg/L of the working medium of hydraulic systems.

JB/T 9954-1999 "Press Machinery - Hydraulic System Cleanliness" stipulates the representation method, limits, and measurement method for the cleanliness of hydraulic systems in press machinery. GB/T 14039-2002 is normatively referenced by JB/T 10205-2010 "Hydraulic Cylinder".
2. Control of Hydraulic Fluid Contamination Degree

Hydraulic systems include various hydraulic components, accessories, pipelines (oil blocks), oil tanks, and working media. As a type of hydraulic component, hydraulic cylinders may contain contaminants that can cause a decrease in the performance and reliability of the hydraulic system. Controlling the contamination degree (cleanliness) of hydraulic cylinders during the manufacturing and installation process can achieve and control the expected cleanliness level of the hydraulic fluid. However, the cleanliness of the hydraulic fluid should be controlled first.
(1) Control of Hydraulic Fluid Cleanliness

The requirements for hydraulic fluid cleanliness in hydraulic systems can be determined based on the sensitivity of the main hydraulic components to contamination and the system's control precision requirements, or according to the requirements specified in the manuals of the main hydraulic components to determine the acceptable cleanliness of the hydraulic fluid.

The cleanliness of newly purchased hydraulic fluid can be 1-2 levels lower than the system requirements. The oil can be filtered during installation to meet the system's cleanliness requirements. During the normal use of the hydraulic system, filter elements should be replaced regularly or in a timely manner according to the pressure difference alarm signal of the filter to ensure the filtering accuracy and meet the specified cleanliness requirements of the hydraulic fluid. Additionally, preventing water contamination is an important aspect of controlling the cleanliness of hydraulic fluid. After water mixes with hydraulic fluid, it can reduce the lubricating properties of the hydraulic fluid, causing corrosion of hydraulic components and emulsification of the oil. Under low-temperature working conditions, water droplets in the oil can condense into ice particles, blocking the gaps or small holes of control components and causing system malfunctions. When necessary, the water content in new oil should be tested according to the method given in JB/T 12920-2016 "Hydraulic Transmission - Hydraulic Oil - Water Content Test Method".
(2) Control of Hydraulic Cylinder Cleanliness

Since the cleanliness (contamination degree) of hydraulic cylinders can be evaluated based on the mass of residual contaminants inside the hydraulic cylinder (see JB/T 7858-2006 "Hydraulic Component Cleanliness Evaluation Method and Hydraulic Component Cleanliness Index") or by using the method of counting solid particles in a unit volume of oil to determine the contamination level (see GB/T 14039-2002 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fluid - Solid Particle Contamination Level Codes"), controlling the cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders means ensuring that their cleanliness (contamination degree) complies with the relevant standard requirements.

In JB/T 11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", the cleanliness test of hydraulic cylinders uses one chamber to pressurize and another to discharge oil, using an oil contamination detector to inspect the discharged oil.

In CB/T 3812-2013 "Ship Hatch Cover Hydraulic Cylinders", the cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders is determined by cleaning the internal cavity of the hydraulic cylinder, then slowly pouring the cleaning liquid onto a filter membrane (with an accuracy of 0.8μm) placed on the funnel outlet for filtration. After filtration, the membrane is dried and weighed. The difference in mass between the membrane before and after filtration is the mass of contaminants in the internal cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.
The control method for hydraulic cylinder cleanliness should generally follow these regulations:

items: The cleanliness of hydraulic cylinders is controlled and maintained through appropriate procedures (processes), so a set of procedures needs to be established.
Since each process and procedure requires human operation and execution, employees should be educated on the basics of contamination control.
Control the pollution of the workshop environment and eliminate dirty environments.
Control the cleanliness of cylinder parts through the cleaning process, but seals generally should not be cleaned.
After testing, the hydraulic fluid in each cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should be drained and each oil port should be promptly sealed.
Avoid paint contamination inside the hydraulic cylinder and protect the surface of the piston rod from paint contamination.
Packaging, storage, and transportation should ensure that the hydraulic cylinder is protected from contamination.

sections.text: For further control of contamination in hydraulic cylinders, refer to GB/Z 19848-2005 "Guide for Achieving and Controlling Cleanliness of Hydraulic Components from Manufacturing to Installation".
(3) Control of Hydraulic System Cleanliness

There may be a large amount of contaminants in hydraulic systems, which may be residual substances from various parts that make up the hydraulic system, such as chips, sand, filings, dust, welding spatter, welding slag, rubber, sealant, water, water-containing impurities, chlorine, acid, and descaling agents. During the use of hydraulic systems, some contaminants may also be generated or increased, such as water, acid, worn metal (mechanical impurities), (n-pentane) insoluble matter, etc.
The control method for hydraulic system cleanliness should generally follow these regulations:

items: Manufacturers should inform buyers through effective information about the harmful effects of contaminants entering the internal components.
Provide components that comply with GB/T 17489-1998 "Hydraulic Particle Contamination"

896.page_header: Chapter 7 Hydraulic Cylinder Use and Maintenance 885

sections.text: Analysis of contamination - take representative oil samples from the working system pipeline to check the cleanliness level of the hydraulic oil and other conditions.

items: The cleanliness level of hydraulic oil must be the same as or higher than that of hydraulic cylinder and other components.
The hydraulic system should be equipped with appropriate filtering devices to quickly remove contaminants generated during use.

Use the oil tank specified in GB/T 3766-2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - General Rules and Safety Requirements for Systems and Their Components" to ensure that the hydraulic oil is within the specified temperature range, especially not exceeding the high temperature.

Generally speaking, the buyer is not allowed to disassemble hydraulic components and hydraulic systems, even as part of the quality assurance program and based on the sampling of a certain percentage.
Establish oil change indicators, check in time, and change oil in time.

sections.text: 7.3.2 Hydraulic Cylinder Failure Modes and Risk Assessment

The failure of hydraulic cylinders is the loss of the ability to execute requirements. The causes of failure may come from product specifications, design, manufacturing, installation, operation, or maintenance, etc. According to the severity of the consequences, they can be classified as catastrophic, fatal, serious, mild, minor, and insignificant, and the selection and definition of severity depend on the field of application.

The failure of hydraulic cylinders is an event that leads to the failure of hydraulic cylinders, and the failure of hydraulic cylinders is the loss of the inherent ability to execute according to requirements. The failure of hydraulic cylinders is caused by the failure of the product itself, or by the failure caused by the insufficient product specifications, design, manufacturing, or maintenance in the early stage of the life cycle. Adjectives such as product specifications, design, manufacturing, maintenance, or misuse can be used to indicate the cause of the failure.

The type of failure can be associated with the corresponding type of failure, such as the failure of consumption and the failure of consumption; the adjective "faulty" indicates that the hydraulic cylinder has one or more faults.

A fault is a characteristic state in which a specified function cannot be executed as required. It does not include the inability to perform a specified function during preventive maintenance and other planned actions, as well as due to lack of external resources.

Failure analysis is an emerging and developing discipline, which has important practical significance in improving product quality, technology development and improvement, product repair, and arbitration of failure accidents.
1. Cylinder Failure Mode
(1) Failure Modes under Rated Static Pressure

items: Structural fracture, material separation.
Any cracks caused by the action of internal static pressure.
Excessive leakage at the seal due to deformation.
Permanent deformation that hinders the normal operation of the pressure cavity.

sections.text: Criteria for verification of rated static pressure: The tested pressure cavity must not exhibit any of the above failure modes.
(2) Failure Modes under Rated Fatigue Pressure

items: Structural fracture, material separation.
Any cracks caused by fatigue under the action of cyclic test pressure.

sections.text: Excessive leakage at the seal due to deformation.
Criteria for verification of rated fatigue pressure: The tested pressure cavity must not exhibit any of the above failure modes.
2. Piston Rod Failure Mode
Under normal circumstances, the failure modes of the piston rod are:

items: Impact damage.
Damage such as depression, bumping, scratching, and corrosion.
Bending or instability.
Damage to the coating on the surface of the piston rod due to deformation.

sections.text: Criteria for judging the failure of the piston rod: The piston rod must not exhibit any of the above failure modes.
3. Hydraulic Cylinder Sealing System Failure Mode

In order to cooperate with the implementation of GB/T 35023-2018 standard, the types of failures of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system should be clearly specified. The following are the types of failures of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system for readers' reference.
(1) Static Leakage of Hydraulic Cylinder

items: The internal static leakage, including low pressure, rated or nominal pressure, high temperature, and during pressure resistance test and after durability test, exceeds the specified value.

The external static leakage, including the oil port, including low pressure, rated or nominal pressure, high temperature, and during pressure resistance test and after durability test, exceeds the specified value.

sections.text: (2) Dynamic Leakage of Hydraulic Cylinder

items: The internal dynamic leakage is large.
The external dynamic leakage, including the oil port, is large or exceeds the specified value.

sections.text: (3) Changes in Sealing Performance of Hydraulic Cylinder

items: Vibration, abnormal noise, sudden rush, jamming or crawling occurs during trial operation and under low pressure and high temperature.
The starting pressure exceeds the specified value.
The dynamic friction force or the dynamic friction force with load exceeds the specified value.
The dynamic characteristics of the proportional or servo hydraulic cylinder exceed the specified value.
The output force efficiency of the hydraulic cylinder exceeds the specified value.
The pollution degree of the hydraulic oil in the wet volume of the hydraulic cylinder exceeds the specified value.

sections.text: Of course, the damage of the sealing surface of the sealing coupling, the sealing element and its groove
Failure is also a failure mode of the hydraulic cylinder sealing system.

In addition, as a failure mode of the hydraulic cylinder sealing (system), there is currently no standard for detecting dynamic leakage inside the hydraulic cylinder (such as piston seal). The causes (modes) of failure of reciprocating rubber lip seals are given in reference [102], including extrusion, breakage, tearing, wear, hardening, softening and swelling, deformation, scratching, indentation, burn, and aging. Among them, wear can be divided into excessive wear, fatigue wear, and adhesive wear. These failure modes can also be referred to when determining the failure mode of coaxial seals; however, these failure modes are generally expressed as damage to the sealing components.
4. General failure modes of hydraulic cylinders
In addition to the above-mentioned failure modes of the hydraulic cylinder barrel and piston rod, the main failure modes of general hydraulic cylinders are:

items: Deformation or fracture of the installation or connection structure of the hydraulic cylinder.
Deformation or fracture of the accessory structure of the hydraulic cylinder.
Bending or instability.
Damage such as indentation, bumping, scratching, and corrosion of cylinder parts.
External leakage or seepage other than at the piston rod seal.
Large internal leakage and large external leakage at the piston rod seal.
Large internal leakage or external leakage under specified high or low temperature and low pressure.
External contaminants (including air) entering the inside of the hydraulic cylinder.
High starting pressure.
Abnormal phenomena such as vibration, abnormal noise, crawling, deviation, or jamming occur when the piston and piston rod move.
Abnormal wear of cylinder parts made of metal, rubber, plastic, etc., and severe contamination of the working medium.
Loose connection and separation of mating surfaces between cylinder parts.
Change in maximum cylinder stroke or inaccurate positioning of the stroke.
The exhaust device cannot discharge or completely remove air from the various cavities inside the hydraulic cylinder.
Cavitation of the cylinder parts that form the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder.
Excessive impact between the piston or piston head and other cylinder parts.
Damage to the port.

sections.text: 5. Risk assessment

Risk is a combination of the probability of injury occurrence and the severity of the injury. However, in all cases, hydraulic cylinders should be designed, selected, applied, installed, and adjusted in such a way that when a failure occurs, personnel safety should be considered first, and damage to the hydraulic system and the environment should be prevented.

When designing hydraulic cylinders, all possible failures (including failures of the control part) should be considered. Risk assessment is the entire process including risk analysis and risk evaluation. It is a series of logical steps to analyze and evaluate risks related to machinery using systematic methods. The purpose is to eliminate hazards or reduce risks. For example, through risk assessment, hydraulic cylinders with fire hazards should consider using flame-retardant hydraulic fluids.
Risk evaluation is based on risk analysis and is the basis and premise for making a final judgment on whether risk reduction is necessary. Risk analysis includes:

items: Determination of mechanical limitations.
Hazard identification.
Risk assessment. Information on risk evaluation includes:
Description of the machinery.
Relevant regulations, standards, and other applicable documents.
Relevant usage experience.
Relevant human engineering principles.

sections.text: Among them, the user's hydraulic cylinder usage (technical) specification, the expected service life description of the hydraulic cylinder, failure modes, relevant standards, etc., are very important for the design and manufacturing of hydraulic cylinders. In addition, the pressure that a single hydraulic cylinder can normally withstand has a certain relationship with its rated fatigue pressure and rated static pressure. This relationship can be estimated and can serve as the basis for evaluating the expected service life of the hydraulic cylinder in standalone applications. This evaluation must be made by the user, and the user must also make judgments about factors such as impact, heat, and misuse during use.

It is stipulated in JB/T8779-2014: "The buyer should establish a system for regular maintenance, replacement of high-pressure components, and scrapping of the press to ensure the safe operation of the press."
6. Fatigue pressure test method for hydraulic cylinders

Since the fatigue failure mode is closely related to the safety function and service life of the hydraulic cylinder, it is very important for both the manufacturer and the customer of the hydraulic cylinder to master the reliability data of the hydraulic cylinder.

GB/T19934.1-xxxx/ISO10771-1:2015 "Hydraulic Transmission - Fatigue Pressure Test of Metal Pressure Vessels - Part 1: Test Method" stipulates the method for conducting fatigue tests on the metal pressure vessels of hydraulic components under continuous stable and periodically changing internal pressure loads.

This test method is only applicable to hydraulic components whose pressure vessels are made of metal, work at temperatures where creep and low-temperature embrittlement do not occur, are subjected only to stresses caused by (internal) pressure, and do not experience strength reduction due to corrosion or other chemical effects. The pressure vessel may include gaskets, seals, and other non-metallic parts, but these parts are not considered part of the pressure vessel of the hydraulic component being tested during the test.

This test method is not applicable to pipeline components (such as pipe fittings, hoses, rigid pipes, etc.) specified in ISO4413. For fatigue test methods for pipeline components, see ISO6803 and ISO6605.
The test pressure is determined by the user, and the evaluation method is given in ISO/TR10771-2.
(1) Test conditions

items: Before the test begins, the tested hydraulic cylinder and circuit should be vented.
The oil temperature in the tested hydraulic cylinder should be between 15 and 80°C. The temperature of the tested component should not be lower than 15°C.

sections.text: (2) Test Procedure

items: Cyclic pressure test. The number of test cycles should be in the range of 10⁵-10⁷.
General Requirements

sections.text: ① Use non-destructive testing methods to verify the consistency of the tested hydraulic cylinder with the manufacturing specification. ② If necessary, metal balls or other similar equivalent loose fillers can be placed inside the tested hydraulic cylinder to reduce the volume of pressurized oil, but ensure that the placed objects do not prevent pressure from reaching all test areas and do not affect the fatigue life of the hydraulic cylinder (such as shot peening strengthening). ③ When the hydraulic cylinder has multiple chambers with different pressure-bearing capacities due to design, the isolating part between the chambers should be tested for mechanical fatigue as part of the pressure-bearing shell.
(3) Failure Criteria
The following situations are considered as failures:

items: Any external leakage caused by fatigue.
Any internal leakage caused by fatigue.
Material rupture (such as cracks, etc.).

sections.text: 3) Application of Test Pressure

The front and rear ends of the hydraulic cylinder should preferably have two sets of oil ports, one connected to the pressure source and the other connected to the pressure measuring device. First, apply a test pressure with the lower limit of high pressure in the cyclic test (pU) to one side of the piston, and apply a test pressure lower than the upper limit of low pressure in the cyclic test (pL) to the other side of the piston. Then exchange these two pressures to generate a pressure cycle, as shown in Figure 7-4. For the pressure-boosting side of the piston, the time period T2 should be longer than T1. For this reason, the time period T1 on both sides of the piston should not start before the pressure on the other side drops below pL. The time period T1 on either side of the piston should end before the pressure on the other side rises above pU. The pressurization waveform can be of any shape.

7.3.3 Online State Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis of Hydraulic Systems and Hydraulic Cylinders

The online monitoring of hydraulic cylinders mainly uses instruments or devices installed on machines or hydraulic cylinders, and on hydraulic systems to monitor the pressure, temperature, input and output flow rate, contamination degree (cleanliness) of the working medium, piston rod movement speed, position, etc. in each chamber of the hydraulic cylinder.
The hydraulic cylinders on general hydraulic presses mainly monitor pressure, temperature, and the extreme positions of piston rod movement.
1. Pressure Monitoring

Pressure monitoring of hydraulic cylinders online often uses general pressure gauges, electric contact pressure gauges, digital pressure gauges, and other instruments. Among them, digital pressure gauges must be used together with pressure sensors or pressure modules and other pressure-sensitive elements.

General pressure gauges can only monitor visually. Permanent installed pressure gauges should use pressure limiters (pressure gauge dampers) or pressure gauge switches for protection, and the pressure gauge switches must be able to completely cut off when closed. The upper limit of the pressure gauge range should be at least about 1.75 times the nominal pressure of the hydraulic cylinder (hydraulic system).

Electric contact pressure gauges and digital pressure gauges can further control other components through the detected pressure, limiting or regulating the pressure of the entire hydraulic cylinder (hydraulic system).

The measurement point of the pressure gauge (or pressure sensor) used to detect the pressure of hydraulic cylinders should be located at 2-4 times the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline away from the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder.
2. Temperature Monitoring

The online temperature monitoring device of hydraulic cylinders should generally be installed in the oil tank. In order to control the temperature range of the working medium, cooling or heating devices (collectively referred to as heat exchangers) are generally designed on hydraulic systems.
The simplest temperature monitoring device is a liquid level and liquid temperature gauge installed on the oil tank, which can only be used for visual monitoring.
Hydraulic thermometers or controllers can be used for both oil tank temperature monitoring and heat exchanger control.

When conducting factory inspection of hydraulic cylinders, the measurement point used to detect the temperature of hydraulic cylinders is generally required to be located at 4-8 times the inner diameter of the connecting pipeline away from the oil port of the hydraulic cylinder.
3. Monitoring of Contamination Degree of Working Medium

Except for large, precise, and expensive hydraulic equipment, online monitoring devices (such as online particle counters) for the contamination degree of working medium are not installed on general hydraulic systems or hydraulic equipment.

In order to monitor the contamination degree of the working medium in the chambers of hydraulic cylinders more accurately, oil sampling ports should be set according to the requirements of relevant standards.
The most difficult thing in practice is whether it is possible to persist in regular monitoring and timely handle problems when they are detected.
In JB/T11588-2013 "Large Hydraulic Cylinders", it is stipulated to use an oil contamination detector to detect the oil discharged from hydraulic cylinders.
4. Monitoring of Extreme Positions of Piston Rod Movement

For general hydraulic cylinders that do not use hydraulic cylinders as the actual limiters, monitoring the position of the piston or piston rod is mainly to prevent the piston from directly contacting (colliding) with the cylinder bottom or cylinder head (guide sleeve), that is, limiting the extreme positions of the piston and piston rod stroke. The methods often used are travel switches and proximity switches or setting soft limits in numerical control systems.

For hydraulic cylinders with requirements for stroke positioning and repeated positioning accuracy, displacement sensors (such as magnetostrictive displacement sensors) are generally set inside or outside the hydraulic cylinder, or displacement sensors (such as rod-type, slider-type displacement sensors) are installed or connected on the piston rod (or its connecting parts, such as sliders) of the hydraulic cylinder. Among them, the most used on hydraulic presses is the grating linear displacement sensor, that is, the grating ruler.
5. Fault Diagnosis of Hydraulic Cylinders

Because after the hydraulic cylinder fails, one or several functional items of the hydraulic cylinder have faults, so according to the failure mode of the hydraulic cylinder, the faults of the hydraulic cylinder are diagnosed.

The faults of hydraulic cylinders are not only manifested in the inability to complete the specified functions under the specified conditions and within the specified time, but may also be manifested in the specified conditions and within the specified time, with one or several performance indicators exceeding the standard, or damage to hydraulic cylinder components (including jamming or seizure).
The faults listed in this section do not include those caused by hydraulic control systems or hydraulic cylinder drive systems.

sections.text: 7.3.4 On-site maintenance and servicing of hydraulic cylinders
1. Maintenance regulations for hydraulic cylinders
(1) Preparation

items: Hydraulic cylinders should be maintained by technically trained personnel when undergoing regular maintenance or malfunction.
There should be a maintenance plan, fault investigation, availability of drawings, spare parts, disassembly and assembly tools, and scheduled work period.
Prepare maintenance site, handle external oil leakage, ensure clean and pollution-free operation.
Before disassembling hydraulic cylinder, be sure to support and secure connected parts (such as sliders), and use lifting tools for hoisting.
When necessary, pre-evaluate the restoration of performance (including accuracy), safety, and reliability of maintained hydraulic cylinder.
Hydraulic cylinder must be maintained after shutdown, including disconnecting main power (power source).
After removing fittings at port, take immediate blocking measures to avoid and reduce environmental pollution.

908.page_header: Chapter 7  Hydraulic Cylinder Use and Maintenance  897

sections.text: 8) Generally, the disassembly of hydraulic cylinders should be completed by the manufacturer. When the manufacturer agrees with the user to allow the user to disassemble it themselves, the manufacturer should generally provide an operation guidance document.

Warning: Before disassembling the connectors and piping at the hydraulic cylinder ports, the connection between the hydraulic cylinder and the driven component (such as the slide block) must be disconnected, and the pressure in each chamber of the hydraulic cylinder must be relieved to zero. Otherwise, disassembling the hydraulic cylinder may result in danger.
(2) Disassembly

items: Disassemble the hydraulic cylinder according to the drawing and process (operation guidance document), and avoid rough disassembly, such as directly hammering cylinder parts.

Before disassembly and inspection, if there is no online monitoring device for the contamination degree of the working medium installed, the working medium in the cavity of the hydraulic cylinder should be sampled first, and then the surface of the hydraulic cylinder should be cleaned. The offline analysis of the working medium should be carried out synchronously with the maintenance of the hydraulic cylinder.
After cleaning, the installation and connection parts of the hydraulic cylinder should be inspected first, and records should be made.

The seals on the piston seal (system) and piston rod seal (system) must be inspected and recorded before disassembly. During disassembly, their integrity should be maintained as much as possible, and other parts should not be damaged. The disassembled seals (including retaining rings, support rings, etc.) must be scrapped, but should be kept for a certain period of time as required for reference.

In addition to checking the external dimensions of the hydraulic cylinder, the inner diameter of the cylinder, the diameter of the piston rod, the outer diameter of the piston, the matching hole of the guide sleeve (cylinder head), the shaft (mainly the inner hole of the guide sleeve), and the surface quality and dimensions of the grooves of each seal, the focus should be on checking and analyzing the parts involved in the failure.

Finding the cause of the failure, i.e., failure analysis, is a science and should be completed jointly by engineering technicians with professional knowledge. According to the "Failure Analysis Report" made by engineering technicians, specific measures should be taken for each component of the hydraulic cylinder, including reuse, repair, replacement, redesign and remanufacturing, scrapping, or returning the whole machine (scrapping).

During regular maintenance, there should also be a "Failure Analysis Report". For hydraulic cylinders and their parts whose functions are degraded or have serious damage or hidden dangers, and whose continued use will result in the loss of reliability and safety, specific explanations should be made for the parts or the whole machine.

sections.text: 8) Hydraulic cylinders that have been disassembled without making a "Failure Analysis Report" are not allowed to be reassembled.
(3) Maintenance

items: Parts that need maintenance should be transported out of the disassembly and assembly workshop.
Welded hydraulic cylinders that have not been disassembled are not allowed.
Maintenance should not damage the datum of the original hydraulic cylinder and its parts, especially the center holes at both ends of the piston rod.

sections.text: 4) The maintained hydraulic cylinder should comply with relevant standards as much as possible, such as the inner diameter of the cylinder, the diameter of the piston rod, the thread of the piston rod, the oil port, and the groove of the seal.

5) Specific problems should be analyzed specifically, and safe, reliable, fast, and cost-effective maintenance methods should be adopted for repair. Generally speaking, except for replacing all seals including retaining rings, support rings, etc., the repairability of hydraulic cylinders and their parts is poor.
6) Cylinder parts that are deformed or broken due to strength and stiffness problems are generally not allowed to be repaired and reused, i.e., they have "no repairability".
(4) Assembly

items: The assembly of hydraulic cylinders should be carried out according to the assembly process of hydraulic cylinders.

All parts used for the assembly of hydraulic cylinders must be qualified parts, including outsourced parts and purchased parts. If worn-out parts that exceed the tolerance are used for assembly, they must be approved.
All original seals must be replaced, including retaining rings, support rings, etc.
The cleanliness requirements of hydraulic cylinders must be guaranteed.

sections.text: (5) Testing

items: The maintained hydraulic cylinder should be inspected and qualified on the test bench before being used for installation on the host machine.
There are dangers in inspecting the hydraulic cylinder using the hydraulic system of the host machine. The possible dangers include:
① Unexpected misoperation or misaction.
② Hydraulic oil spraying and splashing.
③ Overpressure and bursting.
④ Squeezing of other parts, etc.
At least a sealing performance test should be passed before the hydraulic cylinder can be connected to the driven component (such as the slide block).
The hydraulic cylinder should be run several times under no-load and low-speed conditions until the air in the cylinder is exhausted before being connected to the driven component.
The leakage inside the hydraulic cylinder can be checked by measuring the settlement.

sections.text: 2. Maintenance of Hydraulic Cylinders

The maintenance of hydraulic cylinders is of great significance for ensuring the safety and reliability of hydraulic cylinders and extending their service life. The maintenance of hydraulic cylinders should focus on the hydraulic system and even the whole machine, and the most important content of daily maintenance is to ensure the cleanliness of the working medium and to work at the specified temperature. Specifically, it should include the following contents:

items: Clean and replace the filter element of the filter in time.
Ensure that there is sufficient heat exchange medium in the heat exchanger.
Regularly monitor and inspect the quality of the oil, and change the oil according to the oil change cycle and in time.
Inspect or spot-check the oil tank temperature as required, and ensure that the hydraulic machine works within the specified temperature range.
Regularly inspect the installation and connection of the hydraulic cylinder.
Replace the protective cover of the piston rod in time after it is damaged.
Repair according to the specified time, and replace all seals (including retaining rings, support rings) etc.
Generally, hydraulic cylinders that have experienced severe vibration, tilting, and swaying should be disassembled and inspected.

sections.text: After that, a trial run should be conducted before starting work.

items.text: Hydraulic cylinders that have malfunctioned should be repaired promptly and must not be operated while faulty.
For long-term idle hydraulic cylinders, the pressure in each chamber should be released, but the hydraulic oil should not be drained.
Protect the outer surface of the hydraulic cylinder from corrosion, and it can be repainted.
Protect the nameplate and warning signs.
When lifting the entire machine, do not use the lifting holes or hooks of the hydraulic cylinders that are components.
Hydraulic cylinders that have reached their expected service life should generally be scrapped. If the user continues to use them, special protection is required.

sections.text: The hydraulic cylinder is a major component of a hydraulic press. Once a malfunction occurs, the hydraulic press may be forced to shut down. The hydraulic cylinder is also a relatively precise hydraulic component that requires skilled personnel to carefully maintain and service it. The maintenance and servicing of hydraulic cylinders should be included in the technical documents of the hydraulic press and be implemented in practice.

Standard, New, and Accurate
Comprehensively and systematically cites standards related to hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing in recent years
Practical and Reliable Content

Comprehensively and systematically introduces commonly used formulas and materials for hydraulic cylinder design, technical requirements for hydraulic cylinders and their components, taboos in hydraulic cylinder design and manufacturing, test methods for hydraulic cylinders, and a large number of hydraulic cylinder product drawings that have been verified through actual machine testing (or empirical testing)
Innovation and Pursuit of Advancement
Screens out new technologies for hydraulic cylinder design and remanufacturing that have practical value or engineering application prospects
